abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: Tutor profiles here list the Cambridge components each person has taught and the hours they hold on Gulf Standard Time. Both matter. A specialist who cannot make a weekday evening in Abu Dhabi is not available to you, however good the subject match looks on paper.

intro.heading: The question is not whether online works. It is how the hour is built.
paragraphs: Online tuition stopped being an experiment some years ago, and the argument about whether it works has been replaced by a more useful one about how a particular hour is constructed. A session where a tutor talks over slides for fifty minutes is weak in any format. A session where a Cambridge candidate sits a timed question, shares the page, watches it marked in a second colour and leaves with the annotated script saved and one named task is strong in any format, and it happens to be easier to run on a screen than across a kitchen table. This page describes the second kind in detail, because the detail is what a parent is actually buying.

The practical starting point is that Cambridge IGCSE is a written qualification. Almost everything that decides a grade exists on paper: structured mathematics questions with method marks, extended theory answers judged against specific scheme wording, experimental reasoning on the Alternative to Practical, data response diagrams in 0455, directed writing in 0500. Teaching something written is a matter of putting the writing where both people can see it and annotate it, which a shared screen does well and a saved file does better than any face-to-face arrangement, because the annotation survives the session.

The constraint that genuinely matters in Abu Dhabi is the clock rather than the camera. A family in Khalifa City or Al Reef gets a child home from a long bus run after four, needs homework done, and has a workable window between five and eight in the evening. Gulf Standard Time sits at UTC+4, which means that window maps onto early afternoon in the United Kingdom and mid-evening in India. Every session IB Gram schedules is pinned to Gulf Standard Time and the tutor works around it, not the other way round. The question we ask a specialist is not where they live but which Abu Dhabi evening hours they can hold for two years.

What online delivery changes most is who is available. In-home tuition in this emirate is chosen from the people who can reach a particular community before six, which is a reasonable pool for Core-tier mathematics and a thin one for Extended 0620 chemistry in April or for 0606 Additional Mathematics at any point in the year. Remove the drive and the shortlist is everyone who has taught that component and can hold a Gulf Standard Time slot. That is the substantive advantage, and it is worth more than any software feature.

IB Gram delivers every UAE lesson one-to-one over live video. We do not make home visits in Abu Dhabi or elsewhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. The page below is written so a parent can test the claim rather than take it: what the hour contains, which subjects need something the screen cannot supply, what the market charges for the same hour, and the situations in which online is the wrong answer and we say so.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-online-tutor.programmesIntro: The stage a student is at changes what a screen can and cannot carry. Below are the four Cambridge and IB stages Abu Dhabi families most often ask about, described by what online delivery handles well and what still has to happen somewhere else.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The years before the IGCSE course, with Checkpoint tests in English, mathematics and science reporting a scaled score. Online sessions work well from about Year 8 onward, where a student can hold attention for an hour with a task in front of them. Below that age the honest answer is that a person in the room often does more, and we do not sell that service here.
programmes.countryNote: Checkpoint sits in March, May and October, so an Abu Dhabi school on an August start normally uses the May window. A short block of online work in Year 9 on algebra, rearranging formulae and drawing results tables is the cheapest possible insurance against needing Extended-tier rescue two years later.

programmes.name: Cambridge Upper Secondary (IGCSE)
programmes.description: The stage online delivery suits best, because nearly every mark is awarded for something written. Structured mathematics, extended theory, data response and the written practical alternative all consist of reading a question, writing an answer and having it marked against a published scheme. All three of those steps happen on a shared screen without loss.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools normally enter the June series, with November available for resits and single subjects. The tier decision in maths and the separate sciences closes months ahead of the papers, and an online tutor can gather the timed evidence for it from September without a single journey being made.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Post-16 work rewards sustained written argument and long multi-step problems, both of which are better handled on a saved shared document than on a sheet of paper that goes home in a bag. Students at this stage also schedule themselves, which removes most of the practical friction that makes online hard for younger children.
programmes.countryNote: For a UAE university place, Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five IGCSE or GCSE passes. Verify the current wording on the ministry's own site; IB Gram performs no part of that process.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Where an Abu Dhabi school runs IGCSE to Year 11 and the Diploma afterwards, the work becomes draft-based: an Internal Assessment in every subject, plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. Reviewing a draft against published criteria on a shared screen is the natural format for it, and the student writes every word of what is submitted.
programmes.countryNote: Students bridging from Cambridge IGCSE to Higher Level sciences on Al Reem Island or at a Saadiyat campus benefit most from an Extended-tier diagnostic before the Diploma starts. Core-tier content does not reach the point those courses begin from, and that gap is easier to close in Year 11 than in DP1.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is described by what the screen handles and what it does not. Ask the school for the four-digit code and the paper numbers before any of this is scheduled, because the component decides the session design.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Teaches unusually well on screen because the working must be visible to be marked at all. The student writes on paper and shares the page, or writes directly on a shared whiteboard, and the tutor annotates each method mark in a second colour. The saved page can be revisited weeks later, which a kitchen-table session never allows.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (0607)
subjects.description: A different code with a graphic display calculator used throughout and an investigative component. Screen sharing is an advantage here rather than a compromise, because the tutor can watch the calculator sequence being entered and see the misuse that a finished answer hides completely.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Calculus and trigonometry for students heading to A Level. The scarcest specialism on this list in Abu Dhabi, and therefore the subject where removing the drive changes the outcome most. Long multi-step solutions work better on a shared document that both people can scroll back through.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Paper 5 or Paper 6
subjects.description: Extended theory is reading and writing, so it transfers completely. Mechanisms and bonding diagrams are drawn on the shared surface and corrected live. Bench technique for a Paper 5 candidate belongs to the school laboratory; what a session can do is make sure the student knows what to watch for when they are standing there.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Paper 5 or Paper 6
subjects.description: Circuit reasoning is the usual problem and the screen suits it: a circuit redrawn step by step, with the current and potential difference annotated at each stage, is clearer than the same thing sketched upside down across a table. Graph work and gradient calculations annotate cleanly on a shared image.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Paper 5 or Paper 6
subjects.description: The highest content load and the subject where command terms decide most marks. Sorting a student's own past questions by command term is a document exercise, which is exactly what a shared screen is for. Diagrams are labelled live and the labelled version is kept.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences, Double Award (0654)
subjects.description: Three sciences in less depth across four theory papers plus the practical component. Online scheduling makes it practical to put two different science specialists on the same student in the same week, which is almost impossible to arrange with travelling tutors in this emirate.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and composition marked on a shared document, with the plan visible above the response. Watching a student plan in real time, rather than reading a finished piece, is where the teaching happens, and a screen share makes that observable in a way a notebook does not.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Accuracy and register carry the marks. Where the variant includes listening and speaking components, the audio quality of a live session is a genuine consideration and a headset stops being optional. Error-type counting across a term is straightforward when every draft is saved.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Diagram marks decide the grade, and drawing is the one place where a screen needs a little thought. A graphics tablet or a camera over paper both work; what does not work is describing a diagram in words. Expect the tutor to draw, and expect the student to redraw it immediately afterwards.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Case-study application is the lost-mark category, and highlighting an unused case-study line on a shared document is the fastest way to show a student what they did. The habit changes quickly once they see their own paragraph next to the material it ignored.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478) and ICT (0417)
subjects.description: The subjects best suited to a screen, for obvious reasons. Pseudocode and trace tables are written and checked live, and practical ICT tasks can be watched as they are performed, which catches the specification detail that costs marks far more often than any lack of capability does.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-online-tutor.regionsIntro: Online delivery removes the drive, which leaves scheduling as the real local variable. The notes below are about when a session can actually start in each part of the emirate, because that is the constraint families run into first.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Long bus routes mean a child is rarely free before half past four, and homework takes the next hour. A five-thirty or six o'clock start holds well here, and a Friday morning slot is the calmer choice during an exam term.

regions.name: Al Reef
regions.note: Among the longest school runs in the emirate, with children home late. Families here most often use a later evening slot midweek plus a weekend morning, which is also when a specialist in another time zone is easiest to secure.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Established school corridor with a short run but heavy after-school activity schedules. The practical problem here is competition for the hour rather than the commute, so slots are usually fixed for the full term and protected.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Schools on the island and towers within walking distance, so children are home early and a four-thirty start is realistic. That makes it the easiest area to pair with a tutor working from the United Kingdom in the early afternoon.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: A single bridge connection that adds significantly to any travelling arrangement. Removing it returns around forty minutes to the evening, which families typically spend on the timed paper the session is built around.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Bateen
regions.note: Central island communities with the shortest runs. The binding constraint is specialist availability for narrow codes at popular hours rather than geography, so booking the slot early in the academic year matters more than it does elsewhere.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Al Shamkha
regions.note: Mainland communities where travelling tutors quote at the top of the market band. Online scheduling makes the choice of tutor independent of that distance, which matters most for Extended sciences in the exam year.

regions.name: Yas Island and Masdar City
regions.note: Smaller residential populations with campuses nearby. Weekend sessions carry a larger share of the work here, and a predictable weekend hour is easier to hold for two years than a weekday one.

schoolClusters.note: Early finishes and short runs, so weekday afternoon slots are viable. Board usage varies by subject inside one school, so the exams officer is the source of truth about whether a subject is Cambridge or Pearson. Students we support attend schools across this area.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-online-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways an online Cambridge session is commonly structured in this emirate. The difference between them is what the hour is built around, which matters considerably more than the platform it runs on.

modes.title: Paper-first weekly session
modes.description: The default build. The student sits a timed question or section at the start, shares the page, and the remaining time is spent marking it and teaching from what went wrong. Content is taught in response to evidence rather than in a planned sequence, which is why it fits alongside school teaching instead of competing with it.

Annotated script saved and dated for comparison later

modes.title: Shared-document course for written subjects
modes.description: For 0500, 0450, 0460 and 0470, the session lives in one document that grows across the term: plans, drafts, annotations and the levels descriptors in the margin. The student can see their own writing from eight weeks earlier beside this week's, which is the clearest evidence of movement available in an essay subject.

modes.title: Small online group for one level and board
modes.description: Two to four candidates at the same tier on the same code, usually in the weeks before a series. Cheaper per hour, and genuinely useful for mark-scheme language and timing drills where hearing another student's wrong answer teaches something. Not the right format for a diagnosed individual component problem.

sections.heading: What actually happens in the sixty minutes
paragraphs: A good online Cambridge session has a shape, and the shape is the product. It opens with work rather than conversation: a timed question or a section of a past paper, done while the tutor watches and says nothing. Those first minutes are diagnostic, and the silence is deliberate, because a tutor who helps during the attempt destroys the only clean evidence the hour was going to produce. The student then photographs or shares the page, and the marking begins with the published scheme open beside it.

The middle of the session is annotation and argument. Each lost mark is identified, named and categorised out loud: method mark, scheme wording, command term, timing. Where the loss is content, that content is taught immediately and then tested with a second question. Where the loss is habit, the student rewrites the same question to scheme standard while the tutor watches. Rewriting under observation is the part families most often leave out and the part that changes behaviour, because it is the only moment when the new habit is actually practised rather than described.

The last few minutes are administrative and they are not optional. The annotated script is saved with a date. The tutor writes two or three lines naming what was lost and why. One specific task is set before the next session, specific enough to be checked. That record is what makes session nine comparable with session one, and it is produced automatically by this format while being almost impossible to extract from a tutoring arrangement that leaves no file behind.

sections.heading: Teaching the practical papers without a laboratory
paragraphs: This is the objection parents raise first and it deserves a precise answer rather than reassurance. Cambridge assesses practical skills in the separate sciences by one of two routes: Paper 5, a laboratory test with apparatus, or Paper 6, the Alternative to Practical, a written paper. The statement of entry says which your child sits. The component is worth around a fifth of the grade either way, which makes it as valuable as a large piece of the theory paper and gives it a fraction of the revision time in most households.

For a Paper 6 candidate there is no limitation at all, and the honest position is that the written alternative teaches better on a screen than across a table. The paper describes an unfamiliar experiment and asks which variable was controlled, why a reading is unreliable, how the method could be improved and what an anomalous result implies. That is reading, annotation and argument. A shared document with the question on one side and the mark scheme wording on the other is the ideal surface for it, and the annotated page is saved for the student to revisit.

For a Paper 5 candidate the split is clear and we state it rather than blur it. Apparatus handling, reading a burette, setting up a circuit and timing a reaction belong in the school laboratory, and a tutor cannot supply them. What a tutor can supply is everything the paper tests around the apparatus: identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables, drawing a results table with units in the headings, choosing a sensible scale, plotting accurately, spotting an anomalous point and writing a source of error in the narrow language the scheme credits. A student who arrives at the laboratory knowing what to pay attention to gets considerably more out of the school's practical time than one who does not.
bullets: Check the statement of entry for Paper 5 or Paper 6 before planning practical revision
Paper 6 is reading and reasoning, which transfers to a screen without loss
Bench technique belongs to the school; the reasoning around it does not

sections.heading: The tools that matter, and the ones that do not
paragraphs: Families worry about software and should worry about paper. The single most important piece of equipment in an online Cambridge session is a way of getting handwritten working onto the shared screen quickly. A phone or tablet propped above the desk on a small stand, or a cheap document camera, does this for very little money and solves most of what people imagine is wrong with online mathematics. A graphics tablet is better again for a tutor who draws constantly, and unnecessary for a student.

Audio matters more than video quality, and a wired headset with a microphone outperforms every laptop speaker. This is most obvious in 0510 and 0511 English as a Second Language where listening components are assessed, and it also prevents the small delays that make a student stop volunteering answers. Camera resolution, virtual backgrounds and screen effects contribute nothing. A stable connection, a headset and a way to show paper is the whole equipment list.

The other requirement is a place to work that is not a bedroom floor. A desk, a surface for paper, the textbook and calculator within reach, and an hour without a sibling walking through. That sounds trivial and is the most common cause of a session going badly in practice. It is also, incidentally, the thing an in-home tutor arriving at the door enforces by their presence, and the one genuine advantage of that format that online delivery asks a parent to replicate deliberately.
bullets: A phone or tablet on a stand above the desk solves handwritten working
A wired headset beats laptop speakers, and matters most in listening components

sections.heading: Scheduling against Gulf Standard Time and the Abu Dhabi school week
paragraphs: Gulf Standard Time sits at UTC+4 with no daylight saving, which makes Abu Dhabi an unusually convenient place to schedule from. A five o'clock evening session here is early afternoon in the United Kingdom and mid-evening in India, so both tutor pools are reachable inside the window an Abu Dhabi family actually has. Pages that quietly route UAE parents to a tutor on a European evening schedule are asking a Year 11 student to work at eleven at night; we pin the slot to Gulf Standard Time and ask the tutor to fit it.

The local week matters as much as the clock. Schools in the emirate run Monday to Friday with Friday finishing early, and weekends are Saturday and Sunday. That makes Friday afternoon and Saturday morning the two most underused tutoring windows in Abu Dhabi, and the easiest slots to hold for a full term because nothing competes with them. Weekday evenings between five and seven are the opposite: every family wants them, and a popular specialist's Tuesday hour is gone by late September.

Term rhythm then decides how many hours are useful. September to November is the window where tier evidence can still change an entry and where one session a week is plenty. From the mocks to about six weeks out, two sessions a week on a diagnosed component is the normal shape. In the final six weeks the work changes entirely and nothing new should be introduced. Booking a slot that can survive all three phases, including a pause during mock week, is worth more than finding a marginally better tutor for a slot that collapses in February.

sections.heading: Which Cambridge subjects suit a screen, and which need something else
paragraphs: Not every subject transfers equally and pretending otherwise is how providers lose credibility in the second month. The subjects that transfer completely are the written ones, which is most of the Cambridge IGCSE list: mathematics in all three codes, extended theory in the sciences, the Alternative to Practical, business studies, economics, geography, history, both English qualifications and computer science. In those subjects the screen is neutral at worst and an improvement at best, because the work is saved.

Two categories need something the session cannot supply. Laboratory technique for a Paper 5 candidate belongs to the school. Practical coursework in subjects such as art and design, or the performance elements of music and drama where the school has chosen them, require facilities and supervision a tutor is not part of. In both cases the useful framing for a parent is that the tutor teaches the thinking and the school provides the setting, and anyone claiming otherwise is overselling.

A third category is about the student rather than the subject. A child who genuinely cannot stay on task without an adult beside them will get less from a screen, and that is more common at primary age than at IGCSE. Where that is the situation, the right advice is in-home tuition with a local tutor, and we give that advice knowing we do not sell the service in this country. A provider whose recommendation is identical regardless of the child is not making a recommendation.

sections.heading: What online Cambridge tuition costs here, and what the rate excludes
paragraphs: Market rates for online one-to-one IGCSE tuition in this emirate run roughly from AED 45 an hour at the budget end, where tutoring is often done by university students, up to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor and AED 450 or more for an exam-year specialist. Premium or examiner-marketed tutors are advertised considerably higher again. Those figures come from published UAE provider pages and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, read in October 2026, and they describe the market rather than an IB Gram price list.

The more useful question is what sits inside the rate. An hour of teaching is the obvious part. Whether the tutor marks work against the published scheme, writes a session note, keeps a running log of error types and reviews it with you at four weeks is the part that varies enormously between providers at identical prices. Two tutors at AED 250 can be selling very different products, and the difference is not visible until January. Ask what arrives after the session before you compare any two numbers.

What an online rate does not include is a journey, which is the whole of the gap between it and the AED 180 to 500 band quoted by travelling tutors in this market. It also does not include apparatus, a laboratory or supervision of practical work, and a provider who implies otherwise should be asked how. Being explicit about the exclusions is not a weakness of the format; it is the thing that lets a parent work out whether the number in front of them is good value for what their child actually needs.

sections.heading: Ramadan, exam terms and the shape of the UAE year
paragraphs: A tutoring plan written without the UAE calendar in it falls apart twice a year. Ramadan shortens the school day and moves family routines substantially, and the hours that worked in January stop working. The arrangement most Abu Dhabi families settle on is a later session after Iftar, or a shift to a morning slot at the weekend, with the session length sometimes reduced. Both are easy to arrange with a tutor whose availability is a calendar entry rather than a drive across the city.

Because Ramadan moves earlier each year by roughly eleven days, it drifts across the examination calendar, and some years it lands close to a series or close to the mocks. That is worth checking a term ahead rather than discovering in the week it begins. A short planning conversation in January about which weeks will be affected, and what the session will look like in them, protects the continuity that makes the whole record worth keeping.

The rest of the year has its own rhythm. Summer is long and is the single most wasted opportunity in this market: a Year 10 student who spends four weeks of July on the foundations that Extended-tier work assumes arrives in Year 11 in a different position, and nobody competes for tutoring slots in July. Eid breaks interrupt sequences and are a good moment to re-baseline rather than to push on. And the winter break sits immediately before or after the mocks at most Abu Dhabi schools, which makes it either the most valuable fortnight of the year or a complete write-off, depending entirely on whether anyone planned it.

sections.heading: Regulation, permits and what an online tutor can honestly claim
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi are supervised by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK publishes its own inspection ratings, and a parent should read a school's standing there rather than on any tutoring company's page. Across the rest of the country the picture differs: Dubai has KHDA, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

Private tutoring is regulated federally. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers applicants including teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The official route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, applied for through its app, website and e-services system. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published, so any figure quoted to you is unsourced.

What that means for claims is simple and worth stating because this market breaks the rule constantly. IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA, MoHRE, Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation, approval or partnership, and does not claim any. There is no IB Gram office in the UAE. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai would need a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific thing issued to training institutes; describing an online matching service as regulator-approved is both wrong and the single most common misrepresentation in this search result.

The MoHRE private tuition work permit is free and valid for two years; ask to see it
No fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted amount as unverified
IB Gram claims no regulator or board approval and has no UAE office

sections.heading: When an online tutor is the wrong answer
paragraphs: A page selling online tuition should be able to say when not to buy it, and there are four situations where we would not. The first is a young child who cannot hold a task without an adult beside them. That is a developmental fact rather than a motivation problem, and an in-home tutor is the better answer; we do not provide one in this country and we will say so rather than take the booking.

The second is a problem that is not academic. A student whose marks fell away in one term while everything else changed too is usually telling you something that more mathematics will not address. The diagnostic session often surfaces it, and the right recommendation is the school's pastoral team or a specialist, not another hour a week. The third is a request for help with work that must be the student's own: we teach the skill, explain the criteria and mark the draft, and we do not supply coursework, Internal Assessments or essays, whatever the deadline.

The fourth is a timetable with nothing left in it. A Year 11 student carrying nine IGCSEs plus the mandatory UAE subjects, three activities and a long bus run may need something taken away rather than added. Two tutoring sessions bolted onto that week produce fatigue and worse marks, which is a result nobody attributes to the tutoring. Honest advice there is to drop something first, and we would rather give it in the first conversation than three months into a schedule that was never going to work.
bullets: A young child needing an adult in the room is better served in person, which we do not offer here
A sudden fall in marks alongside other changes is rarely fixed by more teaching
We never supply coursework or assessed work; the student writes it
An overloaded week needs something removed before anything is added

process.title: Send the code, the board, the tier and the paper numbers
process.description: Four facts off the statement of entry. They determine which syllabus applies, whether the practical component is Paper 5 or Paper 6, and therefore how the session is designed. Most matches are made from this alone, usually the same day.

process.title: Name the Gulf Standard Time hours that genuinely work
process.description: Not the hours you hope will work. Account for the bus run, homework and activities, and give two or three real windows. The slot has to survive three phases of the year, including mock week, which is why we ask about it before matching rather than after.

process.title: Check the equipment, which takes five minutes
process.description: A way to show handwritten working, a wired headset, a desk with the calculator and textbook on it. That is the whole list. Doing this before the first lesson is the difference between a diagnostic hour and an hour spent on technology.

process.title: Diagnostic first session at no charge
process.description: Taught by the tutor who would take the course. Timed work in the first fifteen minutes, marked against the published scheme, every loss categorised, and a written baseline at the end. Nothing is payable until you decide to continue.

process.title: Weekly sessions, with the record arriving each time
process.description: Annotated script saved and dated, two or three lines on what was lost and why, one named task before the next lesson. At four weeks, fifteen minutes with you on what the pattern now shows and what the next block should target.

whyPoints.title: The hour has a published shape
whyPoints.description: Timed work first, marking against the scheme second, rewriting under observation third, record last. You can hold a session against that structure and ask why if it drifts. Most providers describe outcomes instead, which cannot be checked.

whyPoints.title: Slots are pinned to Gulf Standard Time
whyPoints.description: The tutor fits the Abu Dhabi evening, not the reverse. UTC+4 with no daylight saving puts both the UK and India tutor pools inside a workable window, which is how a narrow-code specialist becomes reachable at six on a Tuesday.

whyPoints.title: The practical limitation is stated, not glossed
whyPoints.description: Paper 6 teaches completely on screen. Paper 5 bench technique belongs to the school laboratory and we say so. What a session adds is the variables, tables, graphs and error wording the paper actually credits around the apparatus.

whyPoints.title: Every session leaves a file behind
whyPoints.description: Annotated scripts are saved and dated, so week nine is comparable with week one. That record is produced automatically by this format and is almost impossible to extract from an arrangement that leaves nothing written down.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their source and date
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page were read in October 2026 from published provider pages and a public rate table, with the exclusions listed beside them. Three of the six pages ranking for this search publish no price at all.

whyPoints.title: We say when online is the wrong choice
whyPoints.description: Young children who need an adult present, non-academic problems, and timetables with nothing left in them are all situations where more tutoring is not the answer. A provider whose advice never changes is not giving advice.

faqs.question: How does a tutor see my daughter's maths working during a video lesson?
faqs.answer: She writes on paper as normal and the page is shared, either by a phone or tablet propped on a small stand above the desk or by photographing it and dropping it into the session. Some students prefer writing straight onto a shared whiteboard. The tutor then annotates in a second colour exactly as they would across a table, naming each method mark that went missing. The advantage over a kitchen table is that the annotated page is saved with a date, so the same marked question can be looked at again three weeks later.

faqs.question: What equipment do we actually need before the first online session?
faqs.answer: Less than most families expect. A stable connection, a wired headset with a microphone, a desk with the calculator and textbook within reach, and some way of getting handwritten work onto the screen: a phone or tablet on a cheap stand is enough. Camera resolution and software features contribute nothing. The item people forget is the room: an hour without a sibling walking through matters more than any hardware, and it is the one thing a tutor arriving in person enforces simply by being there.

faqs.question: Can the Paper 6 Alternative to Practical really be taught without apparatus?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the paper has no apparatus in it. It describes an experiment the student has usually never performed and asks which variable was controlled, why a particular reading is unreliable, how the method could be improved, how to tabulate the results and what an anomalous point means. All of that is reading, annotating and arguing, which a shared document handles well. The productive practice is criticising unfamiliar methods rather than rereading experiments done in class, and students who revise the second way prepare for the wrong paper.

faqs.question: My son sits the Paper 5 practical test. What can an online session do for that?
faqs.answer: Everything except the apparatus, which is a real limitation and worth stating. Handling a burette, setting up a circuit and timing a reaction belong to the school laboratory. What a session can teach is the reasoning the paper credits around the practical: identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables, drawing a results table with units in the headings, choosing a sensible scale, plotting accurately, spotting anomalies and writing a source of error in the narrow wording the scheme accepts. A student who knows what to watch for gets far more from the school's laboratory time.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start if we live in Al Reef?
faqs.answer: Usually six or later. The bus run from the outlying communities is long, and homework takes the hour after that, so families in Al Reef and the southern mainland tend to settle on a later weekday evening slot plus a weekend morning. That pattern happens to pair well with specialists working from other time zones, because Gulf Standard Time sits at UTC+4 and a six o'clock Abu Dhabi session is early afternoon in the United Kingdom. The slot is pinned to your clock, and the tutor works around it.

faqs.question: Will my child end up with a tutor awake at midnight somewhere else?
faqs.answer: Not in a schedule we build. Gulf Standard Time is UTC+4 with no daylight saving, which puts an Abu Dhabi evening session in the early afternoon in the United Kingdom and the mid evening in India. Both are sustainable for a tutor over two years, which matters because continuity is worth more than any single session. Where a requested hour would land badly for every available specialist, we say so and offer a different window rather than booking something that quietly degrades by November.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge subjects do not work well over video?
faqs.answer: Two groups. Practical components needing facilities and supervision, such as the laboratory element of Paper 5 or studio and performance work in art, design, music and drama, require the school and a tutor can only teach around them. And any subject for a student who genuinely cannot stay on task without an adult beside them, which is more common at primary age than at IGCSE. Everything written transfers fully: all three maths codes, extended theory, the written practical alternative, the English qualifications, the applied subjects and computer science.

faqs.question: What does online IGCSE tuition cost in Abu Dhabi compared with a tutor who travels?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 put online one-to-one tuition roughly between AED 45 and 150 at the budget end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor and AED 200 to 450 for an exam-year specialist, with premium tutors advertised higher. Travelling in-home tuition in this market is quoted around AED 180 to 500 an hour, with the journey inside the rate. The gap is the car, not the teaching. Those are market figures from published provider pages and a public rate table, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Two tutors quote the same hourly rate. How do I tell them apart?
faqs.answer: Ask what arrives after the session. At an identical price, one tutor delivers an hour of explanation and another delivers timed work marked against the published scheme, an annotated script saved with a date, two or three lines naming the lost marks and a four-week review with you. Those are very different products and the difference does not become visible until the mocks. The question also separates people quickly: a tutor who already works this way answers in one sentence, and one who does not will talk about rapport.

faqs.question: How should we handle sessions during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Plan it a term ahead rather than in the week it starts. School days shorten and routines shift substantially, so most Abu Dhabi families move to a later session after Iftar or to a weekend morning, sometimes with a shorter lesson. Because Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year it drifts across the examination calendar, and in some years it lands close to the mocks or close to a series. A short conversation in January about which weeks are affected protects the continuity that makes the whole record worth keeping.

faqs.question: Is a small online group worth considering instead of one-to-one?
faqs.answer: For some purposes, yes. A group of two to four candidates on the same code, same tier and same board, working through timed papers and comparing mark-scheme wording, is good value and genuinely useful, because hearing another student's wrong answer teaches something a textbook cannot. Market rates for small groups run around AED 90 to 200 an hour each. It is the wrong format for a diagnosed individual component problem, where the whole value is in one student's own script being read closely every week.

faqs.question: Can a tutor in another country legally teach my child in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 applies to individuals providing private lessons here, issued free of charge for two years. Ask any tutor working with a UAE family about their permit position and ask them to show it where it applies. IB Gram holds no regulator or examination-board approval of any kind and claims none; what we can do is be specific about who holds what and point you to MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service.

faqs.question: My daughter is shy and will not speak up in a video lesson. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: Less than in a classroom, and often less than with a tutor in the room. A session built around her own written work does not depend on volunteering answers: she writes, the tutor marks, and the conversation is about marks that are already on the page. Several families report the opposite of what they feared, because the student is in a familiar room with no audience. Use the free first lesson to test it. If she is visibly worse on screen, that is useful information and we will say so rather than talk you into a term.

faqs.question: How many online sessions a week should a Year 11 student have?
faqs.answer: One a week from September is normally right, which is also the window where tier evidence can still change an entry. After the mocks, two a week on a diagnosed component is the usual shape for six to ten weeks. In the final six weeks the work changes rather than increases: nothing new is introduced and every session is timing and scheme language. Adding a third weekly session to a timetable already carrying nine subjects plus the mandatory UAE subjects usually produces fatigue and worse marks, which nobody attributes to the tutoring.

faqs.question: Do you send past paper packs and mark schemes for us to keep?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody honest will. Syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes are the property of Cambridge and Pearson, and distributing copied packs is a copyright problem rather than a service. What a tutor should do is reference the official documents, point you to cambridgeinternational.org and the Pearson qualifications site, and build the session around a paper the student sits to time and then has marked against the official scheme. That achieves everything a bundle of photocopies pretends to and leaves your family holding nothing it should not have.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-online-tutor.closingHeading: Test the mechanics, not the promise
abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-online-tutor.closingBody: Book one session and watch the hour. Does it open with timed work or with conversation. Is the published mark scheme actually on the screen. Does an annotated script arrive afterwards with a date on it and one named task. Those three checks tell you more about a Cambridge IGCSE online tutor in Abu Dhabi than any profile will. Send the syllabus code, the board, the tier and the paper numbers, plus two Gulf Standard Time windows that genuinely work, and the first session is at no charge with nothing payable until you have seen it run.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-physical-scien.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the chemistry and physics halves of Cambridge IGCSE Physical Science 0652 to Abu Dhabi students over live video. Each one marks to the Cambridge mark scheme rather than to a feeling about the work, and each keeps a per-topic record you can read.

intro.heading: 0652 is two subjects reporting into one grade, which is why progress is hard to see
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Physical Science 0652 puts chemistry and physics into a single qualification. A student sits one set of papers, receives one grade, and that grade averages two bodies of content that behave nothing like each other. Chemistry in 0652 rewards recall with precision: the test for sulfate, the colour of a precipitate, the correct ionic equation. Physics in 0652 rewards transferable method: rearrange, substitute, state the unit, check the magnitude. A student can be comfortable in one half and badly exposed in the other, and the school report will still read as a single science grade in the middle of the range.

That averaging is the practical problem an Abu Dhabi parent is usually trying to solve when they search for a Cambridge IGCSE Physical Science 0652 tutor in Abu Dhabi. The mock came back as a 5 or a C. Nobody in the house can say which half produced it. A general science tutor will revise everything at the same depth, use up twenty weeks, and the grade will move by roughly the amount the student would have moved anyway. The useful first step is not more teaching. It is a split diagnostic that produces two numbers instead of one.

This page is built around that evidence. Every claim a tutor makes about a 0652 student should be traceable to a marked script with a date on it. In the first week your child sits a short Core or Extended question set drawn from past Cambridge material, taken under timed conditions on camera, and it is marked against the published mark scheme. The output is a table: chemistry topics with marks earned over marks available, physics topics the same. From that table a session plan writes itself, because the weakest three rows are the plan.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For 0652 that constraint turns out to help. The specialist you want is someone who has marked hundreds of Paper 4 scripts and knows that candidates lose more marks to unit errors and significant figures than to not knowing the physics. There are not many of those people, and the chance that one lives a twenty-minute drive from Al Reem Island is low. Over video the pool is the whole roster rather than the neighbourhood.

The second thing online delivery gives a 0652 student is the screen itself. Paper 6, the alternative to practical, is a written paper about apparatus, method, sources of error and data tables. It is taught far better on a shared screen, where a tutor can put a real results table in front of the student, let them plot it, and then annotate the line of best fit live, than it is across a kitchen table with a textbook between two people. Paper 5 candidates still do their laboratory work at the school centre, and the tutor's job there is the method and the data handling that surrounds it.
bullets: Week one produces two separate mark profiles: chemistry and physics
Core and Extended are taught to different ceilings, not the same content slower
Marked scripts are dated and kept, so grade movement is checkable
Paper 6 data handling drilled with live annotation on a shared screen
Sessions scheduled after the Abu Dhabi school run, Gulf Standard Time

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-physical-scien.programmesIntro: 0652 students in Abu Dhabi arrive from several places and leave for several more. These are the programme stages where Physical Science support actually changes an outcome, and what the work looks like at each one.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary into the IGCSE option block
programmes.description: The year the science route is chosen. A student heading for 0652 rather than separate Biology, Chemistry and Physics is usually either short of option slots or stronger in the humanities. The work at this stage is closing the arithmetic gap that will otherwise surface in Year 11: rearranging a formula with the unknown on the bottom, converting between grams and kilograms without a calculator, and reading a scale between two marked divisions.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools licensed by ADEK run option evenings in the spring term, and the Physical Science route is often presented as the lighter choice. It is lighter in content and not in method, so a Year 9 student who cannot yet handle standard form should be given that work before the option is locked rather than after.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 10 — the first half of the syllabus
programmes.description: Teaching order varies by school, but most Abu Dhabi centres cover the particulate model, atoms and bonding, electricity and the basics of energy during Year 10. This is the cheapest year to fix anything, because a topic revisited eight months later costs one session rather than four. Year 10 work is weekly, short and consolidating: one topic taught, one past-paper question set marked, one list of errors carried into the next week.
programmes.countryNote: Year 10 in the emirate runs through two long holiday breaks and a Ramadan term with shortened days. Families who keep a single short session running across those weeks lose far less ground than families who stop in April and restart in September, and the marked-script record makes that visible rather than theoretical.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 11 — mocks, tier confirmation and the June series
programmes.description: The year the tier decision becomes final and the papers stop being abstract. Work shifts from learning content to producing marks under time pressure: full Paper 3 or Paper 4 attempts, marked strictly, with the lost marks sorted into categories — content not known, method known but botched, question misread, time ran out. Those four categories need four different responses, and treating them all as revision is why some Year 11s plateau.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi centres sit the June series alongside the rest of the Cambridge world, with final entries submitted months earlier. If your child's tier is still unresolved after the January mock, that is a conversation for the school's exams officer, not something a tutor can change later in the year.

programmes.name: Resit and the November series
programmes.description: A 0652 grade that blocks a sixth-form or A-Level route can be re-sat in the November series. A resit is a different job from a first attempt: the content is mostly there, the marks are not, and the diagnostic work is narrower and more surgical. Six to ten weeks of targeted paper practice on the three weakest topic clusters usually does more than a full re-teach of the syllabus.
programmes.countryNote: Resit candidates in Abu Dhabi may sit as private candidates at an approved Cambridge exam centre if their school does not enter them. Entry windows close well before the exam, so the first call is to a centre and the second is about teaching.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-physical-scien.subjectsIntro: 0652 rarely travels alone. These are the other Cambridge IGCSE subjects Abu Dhabi students most often pair with Physical Science, with the part of each that interacts with the 0652 workload.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: The single strongest predictor of a 0652 physics mark. Rearranging equations, standard form, significant figures and gradient from a graph appear in both papers. Students who are secure in Extended maths tend to lose 0652 marks on recall; students on Core maths tend to lose them on calculation.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Often taken alongside 0652 to give a second science without the full triple load. Biology rewards sustained written recall and command-word discipline, so it competes for the same revision hours as 0652 chemistry rather than the physics half.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: The alternative combined route, worth two IGCSEs and covering biology as well. Families sometimes discover after the option deadline that the school offers one and not the other. The content overlap with 0652 is large, the grading and paper count are not.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: The separate award. A 0652 student moving to 0620 inherits most of the particulate and bonding content and must add organic chemistry, moles in depth and a fuller qualitative analysis set. Useful to know if a school change is likely mid-course.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics (0625)
subjects.description: The separate award on the physics side. The step up from 0652 is depth in waves, electromagnetism and nuclear physics rather than a new way of thinking. A student who enjoys the physics half of 0652 is often a candidate for A-Level Physics regardless of the combined grade.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics — Additional (0606)
subjects.description: Taken by stronger mathematicians in some Abu Dhabi schools. It has no direct 0652 content, but students carrying it almost never lose Physical Science marks to algebra, which changes where tutoring hours should go.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: Relevant to 0652 because the theory papers are read before they are answered. Students who misread 'describe' as 'explain', or who lose the thread of a three-clause question stem, are losing science marks to reading speed.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: A common pairing in the Khalifa City and Al Raha schools. It shares with 0652 physics the habit of working through a defined method step by step, and students who do well at one often respond to the same style of session structure.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Shares the data-response skill set with Paper 6: read the table, describe the trend, quote figures with units. Geography students usually bring that skill to 0652 already and need less time on the alternative-to-practical paper.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Paired with 0652 by students heading for business or engineering management rather than pure science. Both reward precise use of a defined term, which is a transferable habit worth naming out loud in a session.

regions.note: Dense towers, short school runs, and a cluster of British-curriculum students. Sessions here routinely start at 16:00 Gulf Standard Time because nobody is sitting on Mussafah Road. The constraint is usually a sibling's activity schedule rather than traffic.

regions.note: Villa and low-rise community with a long commute off the island for some schools. A 17:00 start is realistic; a 16:00 one often is not. Saadiyat Island IGCSE science tuition tends to settle into a fixed weekday slot plus a longer weekend paper session.

regions.note: Established mainland neighbourhoods close to some of the oldest British-curriculum schools in the emirate. Students here are often in large, settled cohorts where the school's own teaching order is predictable and a tutor can run slightly ahead of it.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Al Reef
regions.note: Spread-out communities where the drive to a tuition centre can take longer than a session. Online delivery removes that entirely, which is the main reason enquiries from here are growing faster than from the island.

schoolClusters.note: Where most 0652 enquiries in the emirate originate. These are large cohorts with wide ability spread, which is exactly the setting where the Core and Extended tier decision gets made late and sometimes gets made wrong.

sections.heading: What a Cambridge IGCSE Physical Science 0652 tutor is actually for
paragraphs: A 0652 tutor exists to separate two sciences that the grade has merged. The job is to produce a per-topic mark profile for the chemistry half and the physics half, teach to whichever is weaker, and show you the evidence each week. Lessons are one-to-one and delivered online over live video to Abu Dhabi families, with a trial lesson first.

That is a narrower description than most tutoring pages offer, and deliberately so. Physical Science is the syllabus where good general teaching produces the least movement, because the average of two scores hides which score is the problem. A student who is at 70 per cent in chemistry questions and 35 per cent in physics questions looks identical on a report card to a student who is at 52 and 53. The first student needs eight weeks of physics method. The second needs a different conversation entirely, probably about tier and about how much time the subject is getting at all.

In practice the opening fortnight looks like this. One short Core or Extended chemistry set, timed, camera on, marked to the published scheme. One short physics set the same way. The marks are written into a two-column table by topic. Then a plan that names three topic clusters and nothing else, with a re-test date already in it. If the diagnostic says the issue is reading the question rather than knowing the science, the plan says that instead, and the work becomes command words and question-stem decomposition.

What a tutor will not do is promise a grade. No tutor can see the paper, the boundaries or the day, and anyone offering you a number is selling something other than teaching. What a tutor can do is show you a dated script from week two and a dated script from week ten and let you read the difference yourself.

sections.heading: Inside 0652: six components, two routes, one grade
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Physical Science is assessed by multiple choice, a theory paper and a practical component. A candidate sits three of the six components: a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and either the practical test or the alternative to practical. Which multiple-choice and theory paper depends entirely on the tier the school has entered them for.

The practical requirement is the part Abu Dhabi parents ask about most, because it is the part that sounds incompatible with online tutoring. It is not. Paper 5 is laboratory work carried out at the registered exam centre, which is the school; no tutor of any kind sits in that room. Paper 6 is a written paper about practical work — identifying apparatus, spotting the controlled variable, finishing a results table, plotting and reading a graph, naming a source of error and saying how to reduce it. Paper 6 is a reasoning paper wearing a lab coat, and it is taught on a screen.

Weightings matter when you are deciding where an hour goes. The theory paper carries the largest single share of the grade, the multiple-choice paper a smaller one, and the practical component the rest. That means a student losing marks across the theory paper is losing them from the biggest pool, and a student who is strong in theory but careless in multiple choice is leaving a smaller but much cheaper set of marks on the table — multiple-choice marks are usually recoverable with technique rather than content.

Always confirm the component structure against the syllabus for your child's exam year. Cambridge revises syllabuses on a cycle, and the version a school is teaching to is the version on the Cambridge International site, not the one in a two-year-old revision guide.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the ceiling
paragraphs: The tier decision is the highest-leverage conversation in the whole of 0652, and it is usually made in a school office in Year 10 without the family in the room. Core candidates sit the Core multiple-choice and theory papers and are assessed across the lower part of the grade range. Extended candidates sit the harder pair and are assessed across the upper part. A student entered for Core cannot reach the top grades however well they perform on the day. A student entered for Extended can, and can also fall further.

This is why an unexplained middling mock grade needs unpicking before the tier is confirmed rather than after. A Core-entered student scoring near the top of the Core range is a student whose ceiling, not whose ability, is the limiting factor. A borderline Extended student scoring poorly on the Extended theory paper may be losing most of their marks to the supplement content, which is a specific and teachable set of topics rather than a general weakness.

The maths load is the clearest practical difference between the two routes. Core questions tend to ask for one operation on a formula given in the question. Extended questions chain two or three steps, expect standard form, and expect a unit at the end. A student who is comfortable with Extended Mathematics 0580 rarely struggles with this; a student on Core maths who has been entered for Extended science almost always does, and the fix is algebra practice rather than more physics.

Only the school can change an entry, and only inside Cambridge's entry windows. A tutor's useful contribution is evidence: a marked Extended paper with a mark on it, handed to the family before the conversation with the school, is worth more than an opinion about potential.

sections.heading: Where 0652 marks actually go missing, half by half
paragraphs: On the chemistry side, the losses are concentrated and predictable. Qualitative analysis is memorised loosely, so a flame colour or a precipitate colour is almost right. Ionic equations are written with the charges omitted or the state symbols missing. The particulate model is described in terms of what the student remembers of the diagram rather than in terms of energy and spacing. Mole calculations, where the syllabus asks for them, are attempted without first writing the balanced equation, which guarantees the ratio is wrong even when the arithmetic is fine.

On the physics side, the losses are almost all method. The formula is recalled correctly and then rearranged incorrectly. The substitution is right and the unit is left off, which costs a mark on a question worth four. Graph questions ask for a gradient and the student reads a single point instead of a triangle. Questions about energy transfer get answered with the word 'energy' repeated rather than named forms, and the mark scheme wants the names. None of this is a knowledge problem, which is why re-teaching the topic does nothing and drilling the method does a lot.

There is a third category that belongs to neither half: reading. 0652 theory questions are written in layered stems, and a candidate who answers the question they expected rather than the one printed loses marks they could already have earned. Command words are the diagnostic here. 'State' wants a fact and no reason. 'Describe' wants what happens. 'Explain' wants why. 'Suggest' invites a sensible answer not necessarily in the syllabus. Students who learn to underline the command word before writing recover marks in both halves at once.

A marked script sorts every lost mark into one of these buckets within about twenty minutes. That sorting is the part most revision skips, and it is the part that decides what the next eight sessions should contain.

sections.heading: Paper 6 and the practical marks you can still teach online
paragraphs: Parents reasonably assume that a practical component rules out a tutor who is not in the room. For the alternative to practical it is the reverse. Paper 6 asks a candidate to look at a described experiment and reason about it: which variable was controlled, why the readings were repeated, what the anomalous point suggests, how the method could be improved. Every one of those is a thinking task performed on paper, and a shared screen is a better surface for it than a table, because the tutor and the student are looking at the same results table at the same time and the annotations are visible to both.

The highest-yield drill is the data table. Candidates lose marks for inconsistent decimal places, for headings without units, for a column order that does not follow the method, and for calculating a mean before checking for an outlier. These are habits, and habits are built by repetition with immediate correction, which is exactly what a 90-minute online session with live marking provides.

Graph work is the second cluster. A sensible scale that uses most of the grid, points plotted to the right precision, a line of best fit that is a line rather than a join-the-dots, and a gradient taken from a large triangle with the working shown. Students who can do these four things reliably pick up marks on almost every data question in the paper, including the ones about topics they found difficult in theory.

For candidates sitting the practical test rather than the alternative, the tutoring job is the surrounding method: planning a fair test, recording to the precision of the instrument, and writing conclusions that quote the data. The laboratory work itself happens at the school, under the centre's supervision, and no tutor is part of it.

sections.heading: The evidence trail: what you receive, week by week
paragraphs: The reason this page talks about marked scripts rather than about enthusiasm is that a 0652 grade moves slowly and invisibly unless somebody is counting. A parent who is paying by the hour deserves to see the count. Below is the shape of a twelve-week block for a Year 11 Extended candidate who arrived with an unexplained grade in the middle of the range.

The pattern is deliberate. Diagnostics first, so the plan is built on data. Repair work in the middle, on three clusters only, with the rest of the syllabus explicitly left alone. Re-testing of the same question types at the end, because a topic that was repaired and never re-tested has not been shown to be repaired. The final weeks go to full papers under time, which tests something different again: stamina and allocation.

You are not asked to take any of this on trust. Each marked script carries a date, a mark, the mark scheme reference and a one-line cause for every lost mark. Put week two and week twelve side by side and the trend is either there or it is not. If it is not, that is a reason to change tutor or change approach, and a family should have the evidence to make that call rather than a feeling at the end of a term.

Progress on Physical Science 0652 past paper marking is rarely linear, and the record usually shows one half moving before the other. That is normal and worth knowing in advance, because a flat chemistry column in week six does not mean the block is failing when the physics column has moved eleven marks.

sections.heading: The Cambridge calendar, counted backwards from the exam
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. That single sentence resolves most of the confusion in a UAE household, because the deadlines that actually constrain a family sit months before the paper itself.

Cambridge publishes key dates per series, and the March series is the clearest worked example of how far ahead the administration runs: for the March 2027 series the examination period is 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027, results are issued on Cambridge International Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. The gap between the entry deadline and the exam is roughly ten weeks, and the gap between the exam and the certificate is months.

There is a logistical trap worth knowing about. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone's timetable. A UAE centre and a UK centre are not necessarily in the same zone. Take the timetable from your child's own exams officer rather than from a revision forum.

For planning purposes, work backwards. A November series 0652 retake means an entry conversation with a centre in the summer, a diagnostic in September, and paper production through October. A June first attempt means the tier is settled by the January mock, repair work in the spring term, and full timed papers from the Easter break onwards. Confirm every date on cambridgeinternational.org, since series dates and deadlines are revised.

sections.heading: ADEK, the mandatory subjects, and what 0652 counts towards
paragraphs: In Abu Dhabi the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, which is the equivalent role to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority in Dubai, the Sharjah Private Education Authority in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. That map matters for a practical reason: inspection reports, curriculum approval and the rules a school must follow all come from the emirate's own authority, so an Abu Dhabi parent reading Dubai guidance is reading the wrong document.

Privately, the federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. This is the rule behind every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement, and it is why a 0652 candidate is also carrying Arabic and, where applicable, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside their Cambridge options. Those subjects take real timetable space, and a revision plan that ignores them is a plan the student cannot actually follow.

On university equivalency, the Ministry of Education's British-track requirement is published and specific: students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. Whether a combined-science award such as 0652 is counted as one subject or two in that tally is a question for the attestation authority rather than for a tutor, and it is worth asking before the option block is chosen rather than in Year 13.

IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International or any UAE authority. It is a tutor-matching platform. Equivalency and attestation are processes families complete through the official channels, and nobody should tell you that tutoring is required for either of them.

If the tier is still undecided, say so — that changes which diagnostic is sent first and what the trial lesson is spent on.

It is used as a working lesson rather than a sales call: the tutor teaches one topic and sets a short timed question set so that there is already a marked script before any money changes hands.
