faqs.question: What is Cambridge IGCSE Physical Science 0652 and how is it different from Co-ordinated Sciences?
faqs.answer: 0652 Physical Science combines chemistry and physics into a single IGCSE award. Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 covers biology as well and is a double award worth two IGCSEs. Both are alternatives to taking the three separate sciences. The practical consequence for a family is the grade count on the certificate and the amount of content carried: 0652 is one grade from two sciences, which is lighter on content than triple science but concentrates two very different skill sets behind one number. Check which route your child's school actually enters candidates for, because schools rarely offer both.

faqs.question: My child's 0652 mock came back as a middling grade and nobody can say why. What is the first step?
faqs.answer: Split the grade. A single Physical Science mark averages a chemistry score and a physics score that can be twenty marks apart, and until they are separated any revision plan is guesswork. The first fortnight should be two short timed question sets, one per half, taken under exam conditions and marked against the published mark scheme, producing a topic-by-topic table of marks earned over marks available. The weakest three rows become the plan. That diagnostic takes two sessions and usually changes what the next two months contain.

faqs.question: Can my child's practical marks be improved if the tutor is not in the laboratory?
faqs.answer: For the alternative-to-practical paper, yes, and the screen helps. That paper asks the candidate to reason about a described experiment: identify the controlled variable, finish a results table, choose a sensible graph scale, read a gradient from a triangle, name a source of error and say how to reduce it. All of that is paper-based reasoning that a shared screen suits well, with live annotation of the same table both people are looking at. For the practical test itself, the laboratory work happens at the school exam centre and no tutor of any kind is present.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child is entered for Core or Extended 0652?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's exams officer or head of science directly, and ask for it in writing. The tier sets the grade ceiling and determines which papers your child sits, so it changes what tutoring should target. Core candidates are assessed across the lower part of the grade range and cannot reach the top grades however well they perform. Extended candidates can, and can also lose more. If the entry is still open, a marked Extended paper with a real mark on it is far more useful in that conversation than an opinion about potential.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring a reasonable format for a science subject like 0652?
faqs.answer: For this syllabus it is a good fit rather than a compromise. The marks in 0652 are won through method: rearranging formulae, writing balanced equations with state symbols, handling units, plotting data and reading gradients. All of that is done on paper or on screen, and screen sharing lets a tutor annotate the student's own working in real time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, since home visits are a service offered only in India, so every Abu Dhabi session runs one-to-one over live video.

faqs.question: What does the market charge for IGCSE science tutoring in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market rates across the UAE run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget or university-student online tutoring, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit once travel is priced in, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IGCSE or A-Level specialist, with premium named tutors quoted above that. Those are figures providers publish about themselves, gathered in October 2026, not IB Gram's price list. Ask about our own model on the trial lesson.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Year 11 Physical Science candidate usually need?
faqs.answer: One session a week is the normal starting point through Year 10 and most of Year 11, moving to two in the final run-in if the paper marks say the work is not consolidating fast enough. More than two rarely helps, because the limiting factor is usually how much independent question practice a student does between sessions rather than how much teaching they receive. A good tutor reduces frequency when the marked scripts show the student can now self-correct, and says so rather than keeping the slot.

faqs.question: We are in Khalifa City and the drive home takes 40 minutes. When can sessions realistically start?
faqs.answer: For most Khalifa City and Al Reef families, a 17:00 or 17:30 start in Gulf Standard Time works better than a 16:00 one, and two shorter weekday sessions often produce more than one long evening block. Families on Al Reem Island or in the Al Raha corridor can usually hold a 16:00 or 16:30 slot because the school run is shorter. Because delivery is online, the drive to a tuition centre disappears from the calculation entirely, which is the main reason mainland enquiries have grown fastest.

faqs.question: Does a 0652 grade count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. Whether a combined award is treated as one subject or two in that count is a question for the Ministry or the attestation authority, and the answer should be obtained in writing before the Year 9 option block is finalised rather than afterwards.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with revision for the Arabic and Islamic Education my child also has to take?
faqs.answer: Those subjects sit alongside the Cambridge options because private schools must cover Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed to teach. They take real timetable space and real revision time. Support for them is a separate stream from 0652 work, with its own tutors, and the mandatory-subject content itself is prescribed, so any material used has to be the school's. The honest point for planning is simply that a Year 11 revision timetable has to include them.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need a private tuition work permit in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The official route is the MoHRE service 'Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through the ministry's app, website or e-services. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can my child's own science teacher at school tutor them privately instead?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi, no. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the code of conduct attached to the MoHRE private tuition permit also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Teachers tutoring outside school hours need that permit. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it, and treat any offer of your child's own classroom teacher privately as a problem rather than a perk.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legitimately do with practical write-ups and assessed work?
faqs.answer: A tutor teaches the method, asks questions about the reasoning, reviews what the student has produced and gives feedback on it. Everything that is assessed has to be the candidate's own. That means no supplied answers, no finished write-ups and no editing a piece until it is no longer the student's work. Some sites in this market sell completed assessed work outright; that is an academic-integrity breach that puts the student's qualification at risk, and it is worth asking any prospective tutor where they draw the line.

faqs.question: Can we see proof that the tutoring is working before committing to a full year?
faqs.answer: That is what the marked-script record is for. Week two produces a dated diagnostic with a mark on it; week ten produces a comparable set of question types with another mark. Put them side by side and the movement is either visible or it is not. A six to eight-week diagnostic and repair block exists precisely so a family can test the approach before buying a year of it, and a flat trend after that block is a reason to change tutor or change approach rather than to extend it.

faqs.question: My child needs to retake 0652 in the November series. Is there enough time?
faqs.answer: Usually, because a retake is a narrower job than a first attempt. The content is largely known and the marks are not, so the work is diagnostic, then surgical repair of the two or three weakest topic clusters, then full timed papers. Six to ten weeks is a realistic block. The constraint is administrative rather than academic: entries close well before the exam, so the first call is to the school or to a Cambridge exam centre that accepts private candidates, and the second is about teaching.

faqs.question: What happens if no 0652 specialist is available when we need one?
faqs.answer: You get told. Physical Science is a narrower roster than Mathematics or Biology, and there are weeks in the run-up to a series when the specialists who mark Extended theory scripts are fully booked. The alternatives are a waiting slot, a different session time, or a tutor whose strength is one half of the syllabus rather than both, which can be the right answer when the diagnostic has already shown the problem sits in one half. What will not happen is a match made quietly with whoever happens to be free.

Sessions run one-to-one over live video to Abu Dhabi, timed to Gulf Standard Time around your school run. If the evidence after six weeks says the approach is not working, change it — you will have the scripts to see that for yourself.

The first thing each one does is count the lost marks by topic area and by question type, because those two numbers almost always disagree with what the student thinks is wrong.

intro.heading: Where 0625 marks actually go, and why nobody notices
paragraphs: Ask a Year 11 student in Abu Dhabi what they find hardest in Cambridge IGCSE Physics and almost all of them say electricity. Ask the same question of a stack of marked scripts and the answer is different. Electricity is the largest topic area and the one teachers warn about, so students revise it hardest and lose a proportionate share of marks there. The disproportionate losses sit elsewhere: in thermal physics, which is taught early and revised late; in waves, where several marks are attached to the quality of a drawing; and in written description questions across every topic, where the physics is understood and the answer earns nothing.

The current 0625 syllabus is organised into six topic areas, covering motion, forces and energy; thermal physics; waves; electricity and magnetism; nuclear physics; and space physics. Candidates sit a multiple-choice paper, a written theory paper at their tier, and a practical component which carries a fifth of the grade. The exact components, durations and weightings for a given series are set out in the current syllabus on cambridgeinternational.org, and that is the document to check rather than a revision guide bought two years ago.

What makes the quiet losses quiet is that they do not look like failures. A student who writes that the metal gets hotter because heat travels through it has produced a sentence their parent would accept and an examiner will not, because the mark required the mechanism: free electrons gaining kinetic energy and transferring it through collisions. A student who draws a ray diagram with correct refraction and no arrows, no normal and no labels loses marks on a drawing that is physically right. Neither student knows anything is wrong until a script comes back.

Abu Dhabi adds a specific constraint on how much time is available to fix any of this. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a particular curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, provided they adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. In practice that means a Year 11 in this emirate is carrying the mandated subjects alongside nine or ten examined ones, and the evening is shorter than a revision timetable assumes. A plan that does not count those hours honestly falls apart in November.

IB Gram matches Abu Dhabi families to a 0625 specialist and teaches one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For separate physics that is the arrangement that works in your favour, because the person who can mark a six-mark description question properly is not necessarily within driving distance of Saadiyat, Khalifa City or Al Shamkha.

The practical component carries roughly a fifth of the total grade
Thermal physics and waves lose more marks than their size suggests
Description questions need a mechanism, not a restatement of the observation
Core and Extended candidates sit different papers at different ceilings
Mandated Arabic, Islamic education and social studies sit in the same week

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-t.programmesIntro: A 0625 entry is a decision about what comes after it as much as about Year 11. The programmes below are the ones that come up when an Abu Dhabi family asks whether separate physics is the right route for their child.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics
programmes.description: Separate physics as a single IGCSE, examined by multiple choice, a written theory paper at Core or Extended tier, and a practical component. The content covers motion, forces and energy, thermal physics, waves, electricity and magnetism, nuclear physics and space physics. Extended candidates meet additional depth in most areas and can reach the full range of grades.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi, separate sciences are typically offered by the larger British-curriculum departments, with the coordinated or combined route used where a student is carrying a heavy option block. Which route a school uses is a departmental decision, and the head of science is the person who can explain why a particular set was chosen for your child.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences
programmes.description: A double award covering biology, chemistry and physics in one course with two grades. The physics inside it is narrower than 0625 and uses the same command vocabulary, so a student who struggles with description questions in one will struggle in the other. Families comparing the two should look at the time on the timetable rather than only at the content list.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools put most of a year group on the coordinated route and reserve separate sciences for students intending to continue them. If your child is in a coordinated set and wants A Level physics, the question for the department is what the sixth form expects, not whether the switch is theoretically possible.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level Physics
programmes.description: The sixth-form continuation, with substantially more mathematics, formal treatment of uncertainty, and extended practical work assessed in its own papers. Students arriving from Extended 0625 find the topic names familiar and the level of algebra new, which is why maths fluency is often the real prerequisite rather than physics knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi sixth forms set their own entry requirements, and they usually ask for a specific Extended grade in physics and a comparable grade in mathematics. A published requirement at your child's school is the one that matters; a figure quoted on a tutoring site is not.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Offered at Standard and Higher Level, with a strong emphasis on experimental work and a written internal assessment that is the student's own from the first draft to the last. The conceptual overlap with 0625 is real, and the shift is in how much explanation each answer is expected to carry.
programmes.countryNote: The emirate has a substantial IB sector, and students frequently move from a Cambridge Year 11 into a Diploma Year 12 at a different school. The useful preparation in that gap is description and explanation practice rather than new content, because that is the skill the Diploma assumes from day one.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-t.subjectsIntro: The grid below breaks the six 0625 topic areas into the units a tutor actually plans sessions around. Each entry names the specific place marks tend to disappear, which is more useful than a list of topic titles.

subjects.name: Kinematics and motion graphs
subjects.description: Speed, velocity, acceleration and the reading of distance-time and speed-time graphs. Most losses come from describing a graph rather than interpreting it, and from calculating a gradient without stating the units it carries.

subjects.name: Forces, moments and momentum
subjects.description: Resultant forces, Hooke's law, turning effects and the principle of moments, with momentum for Extended candidates. Students lose marks by omitting the pivot in a moments calculation and by treating weight and mass as interchangeable in a written answer.

subjects.name: Energy, work and power
subjects.description: Energy stores and transfers, efficiency, work done and power. The phrase energy is lost scores nothing: the mark requires naming where the energy went, usually as thermal energy to the surroundings by heating or by sound.

subjects.name: Pressure and density
subjects.description: Pressure in solids, liquids and gases, pressure with depth, and the gas laws for Extended candidates. The recurring error is substituting a depth measured from the wrong reference point, or forgetting that pressure in a liquid does not depend on the shape of the container.

subjects.name: Thermal properties and temperature
subjects.description: Thermal expansion, specific heat capacity, melting and boiling, and latent heat. This unit carries a reliable supply of calculation marks and is routinely revised last, which is the main reason it costs Abu Dhabi candidates more than it should.

subjects.name: Transfer of thermal energy
subjects.description: Conduction, convection, radiation and the experiments that distinguish them. Nearly every mark here is awarded for a mechanism in particle terms, so an answer that says heat rises or heat travels through the metal collects nothing at all.

subjects.name: General properties of waves
subjects.description: Wavelength, frequency, amplitude, the wave equation, reflection, refraction and diffraction. Marks attach to the diagram as much as the description: wavefronts drawn with the correct spacing and direction earn credit that a written sentence cannot replace.

subjects.name: Light, lenses and ray diagrams
subjects.description: Reflection, refraction, critical angle, total internal reflection and thin converging lenses. A ray diagram without the normal drawn, without arrows on the rays, or without labels loses marks even when the geometry is entirely correct.

subjects.name: Sound and the electromagnetic spectrum
subjects.description: Longitudinal waves, the audible range, echoes, and the ordering and uses of electromagnetic radiation. A short unit with predictable question types, which makes it one of the cheapest places to recover marks in the final fortnight.

subjects.name: Electrical quantities and circuits
subjects.description: Charge, current, potential difference, resistance, series and parallel circuits, and circuit calculation. The largest topic area and the one most heavily revised, so the losses here are usually arithmetic and circuit reading rather than misunderstanding.

subjects.name: Electromagnetic effects
subjects.description: Magnetic fields, the motor effect, electromagnetic induction and transformers. Students lose marks by describing what happens without naming the change in magnetic flux linkage or the relative motion that caused it.

subjects.name: Nuclear physics and radioactivity
subjects.description: Atomic structure, isotopes, alpha, beta and gamma radiation, half-life and safety. A short, self-contained area with highly predictable question types, which makes it the most reliable late revision in the whole syllabus.

subjects.name: Space physics
subjects.description: The solar system, orbits, stellar life cycles and the expanding universe. Often the last unit taught and the first abandoned under pressure, yet it asks for description rather than calculation, which suits students who are weak on the mathematics.

sections.heading: Thermal physics: the area Abu Dhabi candidates under-revise
paragraphs: Thermal physics is taught early in most schemes of work, which means it is a year old by the time a student revises for a final paper. It is also the area where the question types are most predictable and the marking is least forgiving, because almost every description mark is awarded for a mechanism expressed in terms of particles. An answer that reaches the right conclusion by the wrong route scores nothing, and an answer that restates the observation in different words scores nothing either.

The calculation side is kinder. Specific heat capacity and latent heat questions follow a small number of shapes, and a student who can lay out a substitution clearly will collect most of those marks. What trips candidates is a change of state hidden inside a question: a quantity of ice warmed, melted and then heated as water requires three separate calculations, and students who have only ever practised one-step problems do the first and stop.

The experiments matter too, because the practical component draws on them. Measuring specific heat capacity with an immersion heater, investigating cooling, demonstrating convection in water and comparing conduction in different metals all appear as contexts for questions about method, sources of error and improvements. Those questions are answerable from understanding rather than from having stood in a laboratory, which is why the area is workable over video.

In a session the fix is mechanical. The student writes an answer, the mark scheme wording is put beside it, and the gap is named. After a dozen of these the sentence structure changes: particles, energy, transfer, consequence. It is unglamorous work and it is where a measurable number of marks lives on this syllabus.

sections.heading: Waves, light and the marks attached to a drawing
paragraphs: Waves is the area where students are most likely to understand the physics and least likely to be paid for it. A substantial share of the available marks sits on diagrams, and the diagram conventions are specific: the normal drawn as a dashed line at the point of incidence, arrows on every ray showing direction, angles measured from the normal rather than the surface, and labels where the question asks for them. A ray diagram can be geometrically perfect and lose half its marks on those four points.

The wave equation questions cause a different problem, which is unit handling. Frequency in kilohertz, wavelength in centimetres and a speed required in metres per second is a routine combination, and students who convert at the end rather than the beginning produce answers out by a factor of a thousand with working that otherwise deserves credit. The method mark often survives; the accuracy mark does not.

Total internal reflection and critical angle questions reward precision in language. Light travelling from a denser to a less dense medium, an angle of incidence greater than the critical angle, and the consequence stated as all the light being reflected inside the material: each of those clauses can carry a mark. Students who say the light bounces back have the physics and none of the vocabulary, which is a fixable problem and a common one.

Sound and the electromagnetic spectrum sit alongside this as short, highly predictable units. The audible range, the ordering of the spectrum, a use and a danger for each region, and the echo calculation with the factor of two for the return journey: this is the cheapest list of marks on the whole syllabus, and it is frequently the first thing dropped when a student runs short of revision time.

sections.heading: Nuclear physics: the short area with the most reliable marks
paragraphs: Radioactivity is the smallest of the six topic areas and the most predictable. Atomic structure, isotopes, the three types of emission with their properties, nuclear equations, half-life and safety precautions cover almost every question that has ever been asked on it. There is very little room for an unfamiliar context, which makes it the single best use of a final fortnight for a student who has run out of time.

The properties of alpha, beta and gamma radiation are examined through comparison: ionising ability, penetrating power, deflection in fields, and what stops each one. Students who learn these as a table answer confidently; students who learn them as prose confuse beta and gamma under pressure. Nuclear equations require balancing mass number and proton number, which is arithmetic rather than physics, and once shown it rarely goes wrong again.

Half-life is where the marks are lost, and the cause is usually reading rather than understanding. A question gives an initial count rate and asks for the time to fall to a stated level, or gives a time and asks what fraction remains. Students halve the wrong quantity, or count the number of half-lives and forget to multiply by the half-life itself. Three or four worked examples with the steps written out explicitly closes this.

Safety and handling questions are worth separating out, because they reward sensible specifics: distance, shielding, time of exposure, tongs rather than fingers, and storage in a labelled lead container. These are description marks of exactly the kind this syllabus loves, and they are available to a student who has never been near a radioactive source, which every candidate in Abu Dhabi can safely be assumed not to have been.

sections.heading: How a longer 0625 answer is split, line by line
paragraphs: The number of marks beside a question is an instruction about length and structure. A four-mark explanation needs four separate creditable statements, not one good one expressed at length. Students who have never been shown this write a dense paragraph containing two marks' worth of physics and conclude that they are bad at written answers, when the problem is that nobody told them to count.

The command word sets the type of each statement. State wants a fact with no reasoning. Describe wants what happens, in sequence, without why. Explain wants the mechanism and the because. Suggest invites a reasonable answer in an unfamiliar context and is marked generously. Calculate wants working and a unit. Determine usually implies reading a value from a graph or diagram first. Mixing these up is the most expensive single habit on this syllabus, and it is also the quickest to change.

Abu Dhabi students in schools where English is the language of instruction but not the language of the home are affected by this more than most, and not for the reason people assume. The limitation is rarely vocabulary. It is that the physics register is unfamiliar to everybody, so a student already working in a second language has two unfamiliar things at once. Practising the sentence shapes directly helps considerably, and it helps faster than general language work would.

The table below sets out the command words with what each line of a full answer has to contain. We give students a version of it to keep beside their revision, and we mark every written answer against it. Within three or four sessions most students stop writing paragraphs and start writing numbered points, which is exactly what the mark scheme is built to reward.

sections.heading: The mandated UAE subjects that sit beside 0625 in an Abu Dhabi week
paragraphs: Any realistic physics plan for an Abu Dhabi student has to start from the real timetable, and the real timetable includes subjects that a British revision guide knows nothing about. The federal position is that private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, provided they adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Those subjects carry lesson time and homework, and they land on the same evenings as everything else.

The detail of how they are organised varies by emirate and by school. In Dubai, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority has published requirements setting out mandatory subject provision, including separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic education and social studies, with combined classes for the two groups prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Abu Dhabi families should ask their own school and check adek.gov.ae rather than assume the Dubai documentation applies unchanged.

Why this belongs on a physics page is simple arithmetic. A Year 11 carrying nine or ten examined subjects plus mandated subjects has perhaps two evenings a week that can hold an hour of concentrated work, and a tutoring plan that assumes four will be abandoned by the middle of term. We would rather schedule one protected hour that survives to the series than two that collapse in November, and we schedule around the mandated subjects rather than pretending they are optional.

Ramadan shifts this again. School hours shorten, family routines change, and the hour that works in February is not the hour that works during the month. Timed papers are better moved out of that window entirely, so that nothing measured happens under conditions that do not represent a normal week. Those are scheduling decisions taken in advance, in writing, rather than improvised when a session is cancelled.

sections.heading: The alternative to practical paper, read as a set of question types
paragraphs: The practical component carries roughly a fifth of the 0625 grade, and which paper your child sits is decided by the centre rather than the family. One version is a laboratory test; the other assesses the same skills on paper. In either case the skills examined are a short and repeated list: reading an instrument, recording to a consistent precision, tabulating with units in the heading, plotting, drawing a line of best fit, taking a gradient, identifying an anomaly, naming a source of error and suggesting an improvement.

That list is why this component is the most tutorable part of the syllabus and the least often tutored. A student who has never been taught that units belong in the table heading rather than beside each value loses marks in every practical question they ever attempt. A student who draws a line through the origin because lines should go through the origin loses the gradient marks that follow. These are conventions, and conventions can be taught over video as well as in a laboratory.

Error questions reward specificity above everything. Parallax when reading a scale, heat loss to the surroundings, the reaction time in a manual timing, a ruler not held vertically, a thermometer touching the side of a beaker: each of these is a creditable answer. Human error is not, and neither is the equipment was faulty. Improvements have to address the error actually named, which is where most of the remaining marks go missing.

Where a student is sitting the laboratory test, a tutor's honest role is the written and analytical half: the tabulation, the plotting, the analysis and the error reasoning. The handling of apparatus belongs to the school, and we say so plainly rather than implying that a video call substitutes for a bench. That division is worth stating to any provider who claims otherwise.

sections.heading: What separate physics support costs around Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: The published market for tutoring in the UAE spreads across bands that are wide but reasonably well documented, because several providers publish their own numbers. The figures below are theirs, stated as at October 2026, together with the ranges from a 2026 Dubai cost survey. They are market context, not our price list, and Abu Dhabi tracks Dubai closely for online specialist teaching because the tutor pool is national rather than local.

Separate physics sits towards the specialist end of those bands for a reason that has nothing to do with marketing. A tutor who can mark a six-mark explanation against the scheme, correct a ray diagram properly and teach the practical conventions is doing something different from a general science tutor covering three subjects at once. There are fewer such people, and in an emirate where many students are on the coordinated route the local demand for them is thin, which is exactly why online matching changes the arithmetic.

In-home rates in this market include travel, and that travel is bought at the teaching rate. Crossing from the mainland to the island at five in the afternoon is not a small amount of time, and a two-hour booking that contains forty minutes of driving is being charged as two hours of teaching. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. The comparison below exists because families are quoted both and deserve to see the difference stated.

The question worth asking of any quote, from us or anybody else, is what sits inside the hour. Is written work set between sessions. Is it marked against the published scheme, and do you receive the marked script. Is there a record of which topic areas have been tested. Those three answers distinguish products that look identical on a price list.

sections.heading: From 0625 into an Abu Dhabi sixth form
paragraphs: The usual reason a family invests in separate physics is what comes next, and the honest picture of that is more specific than most sites admit. Cambridge AS and A Level Physics introduces substantially more algebra, formal treatment of uncertainty, and practical papers of its own. The students who struggle in the first term are rarely the ones who found 0625 content hard. They are the ones whose mathematics was weak, because the physics now arrives wrapped in manipulation they cannot do quickly.

That has a practical consequence for a Year 11 plan. If a student intends to continue physics, the highest-value work alongside it is often algebraic fluency: rearranging, indices, standard form and the handling of units in a calculation. A tutor who notices that the physics losses are arithmetic rather than conceptual should say so, and the right purchase in that case may be maths support rather than more physics hours.

For the IB Diploma route the shift is different again. Explanation carries more weight, experimental work runs across the whole course, and the internal assessment is the student's own from the first draft to the last. A student moving from a Cambridge Year 11 into a Diploma Year 12 benefits most from written explanation practice, which is also the thing that improves a 0625 grade. The two goals point in the same direction, which makes that work unusually good value.

What a sixth form actually requires is set by the school, and published requirements differ across the emirate. The head of sixth form or the head of science can tell you the grade and the subject combination they expect, and that answer is worth more than any general guidance. No tutoring provider can tell you what a particular Abu Dhabi school will accept, and one that offers to is guessing.

process.title: Send a marked script, not a report
process.description: The useful first message carries your child's most recent marked physics paper, a note of whether the entry is Core or Extended if you know, and the evenings that are genuinely free. The script lets a specialist count lost marks by topic area, which is where the plan comes from.

process.title: A free first lesson that counts the losses
process.description: The trial session is a working hour. Marks from the script are counted by topic area and by question type, your child writes one longer answer, and that answer is marked against the scheme wording in front of them. You receive the written count whether or not you continue.

process.title: Agree the target and the hour
process.description: Topic-area repair, description practice, or weekly support across the course. The slot is fixed in Gulf Standard Time around the school week, with timed papers moved to a weekend where the commute from the mainland corridor is long.

process.title: Written work, marked before the next session
process.description: Each session sets written answers, which come back marked line by line against the published scheme. Diagrams are drawn by the student and corrected to the conventions. This is the mechanism that moves description marks, and it is what the cheaper bands leave out.

process.title: Recount at the halfway point
process.description: After several weeks the lost marks are counted again on a comparable paper. If the targeted area has not moved, the plan changes or we say that further sessions are not the right purchase. That conversation is built in rather than avoided.

whyPoints.title: A separate-physics specialist
whyPoints.description: 0625 is taught by the larger science departments in this emirate and by a minority of tutors. Matching online rather than by driving distance is how a family in Al Shamkha or on Hudayriyat reaches somebody who marks explanation questions properly.

whyPoints.title: The plan comes from a mark count
whyPoints.description: Topic choice is decided by counting losses on a real script, not by asking a fifteen-year-old what feels difficult. The count almost always disagrees with the impression, and thermal physics and waves are where it usually points.

whyPoints.title: Answer writing treated as a skill
whyPoints.description: Command words, mechanisms in particle terms and answers built to the number of marks on offer. This is the most transferable thing a 0625 student can be taught, and it improves every topic area at the same time.

whyPoints.title: Practical conventions taught honestly
whyPoints.description: Tabulation, plotting, gradients, anomalies and specific error reasoning can all be taught over video. Handling apparatus cannot, and we say so rather than implying that a video call replaces a laboratory bench.

whyPoints.title: A timetable that includes the mandated subjects
whyPoints.description: Arabic, Islamic education and social studies carry real hours in an Abu Dhabi week. We schedule one protected slot that survives the term rather than a plan built on evenings that are already taken.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot stand behind
whyPoints.description: No grade promises, no implied approval from ADEK or any examination board, no IB dates we cannot source, and no board material redistributed as downloads. What has been checked is named; nothing beyond it is implied.

faqs.question: Which thermal physics questions come up most often in 0625?
faqs.answer: A small and predictable set. Explaining conduction in a metal in terms of free electrons, explaining convection through density change, calculating energy with specific heat capacity and latent heat, describing an experiment to measure specific heat capacity, and suggesting why a measured value came out high or low. Radiation questions about shiny and dull surfaces recur as well. Because the set is this stable, the area rewards targeted work more than almost anything else on the syllabus, and it is usually revised last because it was taught first.

faqs.question: My daughter can describe an experiment but scores two out of four. Why?
faqs.answer: Because a four-mark answer needs four separate creditable statements, and a good description often contains two expressed at length. For a practical method the marks are usually spread across named apparatus, the quantities actually measured, how they are measured, and the calculation that follows. A student who writes fluently about setting up the equipment and never states which values are recorded has written half an answer. Counting the marks and planning one point each is a change that takes a few sessions and affects every topic area.

faqs.question: Does 0625 still include radioactivity, and is it worth revising?
faqs.answer: Nuclear physics is one of the six topic areas in the current syllabus, and it is the best value in the final fortnight. The question types barely vary: comparing the three emissions, balancing nuclear equations, half-life from a count rate or a graph, safety and handling, and background radiation. There is very little scope for an unfamiliar context, so a student who has run short of time will recover more marks here per hour than in electricity. Confirm the content for your child's series on cambridgeinternational.org, since syllabuses are revised periodically.

faqs.question: What does a six-mark 0625 question actually need in each line?
faqs.answer: Six separate creditable points, with the command word setting the type of each. If the question says explain, each line should carry a mechanism and a consequence rather than a restatement. If it says describe, the lines should be a sequence of what happens with no why attached. The practical habit is to write the number of marks at the top of the answer space and plan that many short statements before starting. Students who do this stop writing paragraphs and start collecting marks, usually within three or four sessions.

faqs.question: How do ray diagrams get marked in 0625?
faqs.answer: Largely on convention, which is why a geometrically correct diagram can still lose half its marks. The normal should be drawn as a dashed line at the point of incidence, every ray should carry an arrow showing direction, angles should be measured from the normal rather than from the surface, and labels should appear where the question asks for them. For lenses, the construction rays themselves carry marks. These are all teachable over video, because the student draws and the tutor corrects against the scheme in real time.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does the mandated subject load leave for physics?
faqs.answer: Less than most revision timetables assume. Private schools in the UAE teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their own curriculum as part of the federal baseline, and those subjects carry homework that lands on the same evenings as everything else. A Year 11 with nine or ten examined subjects realistically has two evenings that can hold an hour of concentrated work. We would rather fix one protected physics hour that lasts until the series than agree to three that quietly disappear after November.

faqs.question: Which Abu Dhabi schools enter candidates for separate Cambridge physics?
faqs.answer: Typically the larger British-curriculum departments, several of which sit on the island and in the Khalifa City corridor, while a good number of schools put most of a year group on the coordinated route and reserve separate sciences for students intending to continue them. The decision belongs to the department rather than to the regulator. The question to ask a head of science is how many students are entered for separate physics this year, at which tier, and what the sixth form expects from those who want to continue.

faqs.question: Are sound and the electromagnetic spectrum worth separate revision time?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they are among the cheapest marks available. The question types are narrow: the audible range, how sound travels as a longitudinal wave, the echo calculation with its factor of two for the return journey, the order of the spectrum, and a use and a danger for each region. A couple of hours covers the lot. Students under time pressure usually drop this first because it feels like general knowledge, and then meet two or three questions on it in the papers they actually sit.

faqs.question: What does a 0625 physics tutor charge an hour around Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300 and separate-science specialists at AED 200 to 450 or above, with one provider publishing AED 650 at the premium end. In-home rates in the UAE run from about AED 180 to 500, and that band includes travel bought at the teaching rate. Those are other providers' own published numbers as at October 2026 rather than our price list. For physics the thing to check inside any rate is whether written work is marked against the scheme between sessions.

faqs.question: Will you send a physics tutor to our home on Saadiyat Island?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons for Abu Dhabi families run one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For separate physics that works in your favour: the constraint is not distance but the number of people who can mark an explanation question properly and correct a ray diagram to the conventions, and matching online rather than by postcode is what makes one of them available to a family on Saadiyat.

faqs.question: Do tutors need a UAE permit to teach my child physics online?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the country is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and federal guidance states it is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Those without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. We check a tutor's permit position before a match and describe it as nothing more than that.

faqs.question: How does 0625 compare with the physics inside Co-ordinated Sciences?
faqs.answer: The separate syllabus goes further in most areas and produces a single physics grade, while the coordinated double award covers all three sciences and produces two grades across them. The physics content inside the coordinated course is narrower, and it uses the same command vocabulary and the same practical conventions, so a student who loses marks on explanation questions in one will lose them in the other. If your child is on the coordinated route and wants to continue physics, the question belongs to the sixth form rather than to a comparison of content lists.

faqs.question: My son has four weeks before the paper. What is realistic for 0625?
faqs.answer: Four weeks can move a grade, and it cannot cover a syllabus. The honest plan prioritises by marks per hour: nuclear physics first because the question types are the most predictable, then sound and the electromagnetic spectrum, then thermal physics description answers, then command word practice across whatever topics the script shows as weak. New content in electricity is a poor use of the last fortnight. If the script shows large content gaps across several areas, we would say that plainly rather than sell four weeks of sessions that cannot close them.

faqs.question: What does an Abu Dhabi sixth form expect from a 0625 grade?
faqs.answer: Each school sets its own entry requirements, so the published requirement at your child's school is the only reliable answer, and the head of sixth form can give it to you directly. What is consistent across them is that Cambridge AS and A Level Physics assumes considerably more algebra than 0625 does, and the students who struggle in the first term are usually the ones whose mathematics was weak rather than their physics. Where a Year 11 script shows arithmetic losses rather than conceptual ones, maths support can be the better purchase.

faqs.question: Is a weekend morning better than a weekday evening for physics?
faqs.answer: For timed papers and long written answers, yes, and most Abu Dhabi families settle on a mix. A weekday session after a long bus journey from the island to Al Shamkha or Al Reef is useful for review and poor for anything that needs an uninterrupted hour, while a weekend morning holds a full theory paper comfortably. The arrangement we most often end up with is a short midweek review and the measured work at the weekend, with the timings agreed in advance rather than rearranged each week.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-t.closingHeading: Count the lost marks before buying any hours
abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-t.closingBody: If your child is sitting Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 at a school in Abu Dhabi and the school has said electricity is the problem, the first useful step is to count the lost marks by topic area on a real script. Send the most recent marked paper, note whether the entry is Core or Extended, and say which evenings are genuinely free. The free first session does the count, marks one longer written answer against the scheme in front of your child, and gives you the result in writing. Lessons run one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-psychology-026.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Cambridge IGCSE Psychology to Abu Dhabi students in Years 10 and 11. The arrangement is deliberately evidence-led: a timed answer set every week, marked against the published criteria, returned with the specific missing element named, and kept so that progress can be read rather than described.

intro.heading: How to tell whether Psychology tutoring is working, in week six rather than in August
paragraphs: Most tutoring arrangements are judged on feel. The student says the sessions are helpful, the tutor says they are making progress, and nobody finds out whether that was true until a mock result arrives months later. Psychology is unusually well suited to a better method, because everything it assesses is written down. A marked answer shows exactly what a student can and cannot do, in a form a parent can read without any subject knowledge at all, and a folder of them in date order is a progress record rather than an opinion about one.

That is the organising idea of this page. Rather than listing qualifications, it sets out what evidence a 0266 arrangement should produce, when, and what it means when the evidence does not appear. By the end of week two there should be a marked script with the lost marks named specifically. By week six there should be five or six of them and a visible direction. If there is nothing to read by week six, the arrangement is not working, whatever anybody says about engagement.

The subject itself cooperates. Cambridge IGCSE Psychology is assessed by written examination, with nothing submitted from home, so there is no internal assessment and no coursework to supervise. Students who have heard about the Internal Assessment in IB Psychology sometimes expect one here; there is none at IGCSE. The paper structure, durations and mark totals are set out in the syllabus for each exam series, and a revision plan should be built from the version that matches your child's series rather than from an older copy.

Where marks are lost is consistent enough to predict. Students describe a study when the question asked them to evaluate it. They name an ethical issue without saying what it requires or how a researcher would deal with it. They confuse the independent and dependent variables under time pressure. They read a graph without saying what it implies. None of these is a knowledge gap, which is why they are visible on a marked script and invisible in conversation, and why marking is the mechanism that moves this grade rather than extra explanation.

Delivery in the UAE is online, one-to-one, over live video with screens shared, and IB Gram does not make home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tutoring is offered only in India. For a subject taught by reading a script together, the shared screen is the right tool. Private schools in this emirate are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools here, and Psychology is a minority option in most of them, usually one class with one teacher and no second set to move into.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-psychology-026.programmesIntro: 0266 sits at the start of a pathway that gets considerably more demanding, and the habits built at IGCSE are the ones the later courses assess twice as hard. Knowing the intended destination changes what a first term should prioritise.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Psychology
programmes.description: Introduces psychological approaches, a set of core studies, and research methods: variables, experimental design, sampling, reliability, validity, data handling and research ethics. Assessed by written examination with no coursework component, and the topic list, paper structure and mark totals for your child's series are set out in the current syllabus document.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi, 0266 is usually a Year 10 option taken by a small self-selected group, frequently timetabled against a second humanity or a third science. Because the class is small there is no parallel set, so a student who loses three weeks to illness or to a mid-year move has no internal route back and that is the usual trigger for an outside booking in this subject.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Psychology
programmes.description: The continuation route, with research methods treated at far greater depth, named studies examined in detail, and extended answers that must evaluate rather than describe. Students who reached a good IGCSE grade by learning study summaries find the first AS term difficult, because the summaries stop being enough and the methodological critique starts carrying the marks.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools offer 9990 in their sixth form, and some admit students to it without IGCSE Psychology at all. Where a student is continuing, the IGCSE year is best spent building methods fluency rather than memorising more studies, because methods is the component that scales and recall is the one that does not.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Psychology
programmes.description: The alternative post-sixteen route for students moving into an IB Diploma school. It adds an Internal Assessment, a written report on a simple replicated experiment, which is the first time these students meet assessed work produced outside an exam hall. The IGCSE methods material is the direct preparation for it, which is one more reason to take that part seriously at sixteen.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has a substantial IB sector alongside its Cambridge schools, and movement between them at sixteen is routine here. A student heading for DP Psychology benefits from a short bridging block over the summer on experimental design and report conventions, since nothing at IGCSE required them to write up a study of their own.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Sociology
programmes.description: The neighbour subject, sharing most of the research-methods content including sampling, reliability, validity and research ethics. The difference is the level of explanation: psychology explains individual behaviour, sociology explains group patterns. Students taking both learn the methods once and are examined on them twice, which is a genuine efficiency.
programmes.countryNote: Where an Abu Dhabi school offers the pair, taking both is efficient rather than duplicative. The risk is answer style under exam pressure: a psychology answer reaches for a study and a mechanism, a sociology answer reaches for a concept and a social pattern, and candidates occasionally produce the wrong one in the wrong paper.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-psychology-026.subjectsIntro: Psychology is often one half of a booking. The subjects below are the usual companions in an Abu Dhabi option block, mostly because they share either the methods content or the extended-answer demand.

subjects.name: Psychology (0266)
subjects.description: The subject of this page. Sessions build research-methods fluency, turn described studies into evaluated ones, drill the data and graph questions that recur every series, and produce a marked script every week as the progress record.

subjects.name: Sociology (0495)
subjects.description: Shares most of the methods content, including sampling, reliability, validity and ethics, so a student taking both covers that material once. The separation to maintain is the level of explanation: individual behaviour against group patterns.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Supports the biological approach directly: the nervous system, hormones, the brain and the physiological basis of behaviour. Students carrying Biology can explain a mechanism where others assert an outcome, which is worth marks in any question about biological explanations.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Behind the data-handling questions that catch candidates out. Mean, median, mode and range, percentage change, reading values off a graph accurately and choosing an appropriate chart all appear, and losing those marks has nothing to do with psychology.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500)
subjects.description: Relevant because the longer psychology answers are extended prose under timing. Students who can control a paragraph convert their knowledge into marks; students who cannot lose marks on material they genuinely understand.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: Many Abu Dhabi candidates sit 0510 alongside 0266. The useful transfer is precision in short written answers, where a psychology definition has to be exact rather than approximate to score.

subjects.name: Global Perspectives (0457)
subjects.description: Shares the evaluation demand and the habit of asking how a claim was produced. Students who have done 0457 research work handle study critique more readily, because they have already been made to ask who produced evidence and why.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Contributes the structure of a supported judgement: a position taken, the alternative addressed, and a reason given. That is the shape the longer psychology questions want when they ask a candidate to evaluate rather than describe.

subjects.name: History (0470)
subjects.description: Brings source evaluation, which maps onto study critique: who conducted this, when, on whom, and what does that do to the conclusion. It is the single most transferable humanities skill into 0266 evaluation questions.

sections.heading: What progress in 0266 looks like on paper, week by week
paragraphs: A tutoring arrangement should be falsifiable. If nothing it produces could show that it was not working, then its claim to be working means nothing either. In a written-exam subject that is easy to arrange: the student produces a timed answer every week, somebody marks it against the published criteria, and the marked scripts are kept. A parent who can read five scripts in date order does not need to ask anybody whether progress is happening.

The sequence below is what a reasonable six weeks produces. It is deliberately unambitious in the early weeks, because a first marked answer is a diagnostic rather than an achievement, and because a student whose first script is good was probably not the student who needed the booking. What matters is the direction across the set and the disappearance of specific named faults rather than a rising percentage, since the questions are not of equal difficulty.

Two things should change in that window. The named faults from week one should stop recurring: if the week-one script lost marks for describing a study instead of evaluating it, the week-five script should not. And the student's own ability to predict their marks should improve, which is the clearest sign that the criteria have been internalised rather than merely explained. A student who can read their own answer and say where it will lose marks has acquired something that lasts past the exam.

What should also be visible is what has not changed. An honest marked set shows persistent faults as well as corrected ones, and a tutor should name them at the six-week review rather than letting a general impression of progress cover them. Where the evidence shows no movement, the right answer is to change the plan or stop, and a family is entitled to be told that rather than invited to buy another term.

sections.heading: Research methods is the examinable spine of the subject
paragraphs: Of everything in 0266, research methods is the most predictable and the most reliably under-taught. It appears in every series because it is the part of psychology that does not change, and it is taught quickly in many schools because students find core studies more interesting than operationalisation. The consequence is a cohort that can recount experiments in detail and cannot say what the independent variable was, which is a strange and very fixable position to be in.

The content divides into four blocks. The first is variables and operationalisation: what was manipulated, what was measured, what else might have affected the result, and how an abstract idea such as aggression or memory was turned into something countable. Candidates who cannot operationalise lose marks on questions that are otherwise straightforward, because the question asks how the researcher measured it and the student answers what the researcher was interested in.

The second block is design and sampling. Independent measures, repeated measures and matched pairs each solve a problem and create one, and the examinable skill is choosing for a described study and saying why. Sampling works the same way: random, opportunity, volunteer and stratified samples differ in who they reach and what they distort, and a question gives a scenario rather than asking for a list. The third is reliability, validity and the things that threaten them, including demand characteristics and researcher effects, where candidates routinely use reliability and validity as synonyms and lose the mark that the distinction was the whole point of.

The fourth is data. Mean, median, mode and range, choosing an appropriate graph, reading values accurately off an axis and saying what a pattern implies rather than restating it. These marks are available to any careful student and are lost for reasons unrelated to psychology, which makes them the cheapest marks on the paper to recover. sections.heading: Core studies: knowing one well enough to criticise it
paragraphs: Students arrive at Psychology expecting to learn studies and they are right, but they usually learn the wrong half. A study can be recounted in detail, with the procedure in order and the findings accurate, and still produce a mid-band answer, because most of the marks above description sit in the critique. The useful target is not more studies; it is each study held firmly enough to be taken apart.

A critique framework makes that teachable rather than a matter of flair. Five headings cover almost everything an IGCSE question can ask. Who the participants were, how many, and what that does to the conclusion. Which method was used and what it cannot show. Where it was conducted and whether behaviour there resembles behaviour elsewhere. Which ethical issues arose and how the researcher dealt with them. And what the findings actually support, as distinct from what they are often said to support. A student who applies those five headings to any study will have something to write.

The framework also prevents the most common evaluation failure, which is a criticism that could be made of any study ever conducted. Small sample is not a criticism unless the student says what the small sample makes unsafe. Lacks ecological validity is not a criticism unless the student says what about that setting differs from the one the conclusion is about. The difference between a generic objection and a specific one is exactly the difference between a lower and an upper band.

Practically this means fewer studies, held better. For most candidates two or three secure studies per topic area, each with its five-heading critique available from memory, beats a longer list of summaries. It also makes retrieval easier under exam pressure, which is where the real losses happen: a student who has over-revised breadth and under-revised depth freezes when asked to evaluate rather than to describe.
bullets: Sample: how many, who, and what that makes unsafe to conclude
Method: what it was, and specifically what it cannot show
Setting: whether behaviour there resembles behaviour elsewhere
Ethics: which issue arose, and how the researcher handled it
Conclusion: what the findings support, as opposed to what is claimed

sections.heading: Where psychology answers lose marks
paragraphs: Marked scripts from Abu Dhabi candidates show the same handful of faults with striking consistency, which is good news for a family deciding whether tutoring is worth buying. The faults are specific, nameable and short-lived once named. They are not caused by weak effort and they are rarely caused by weak understanding, which is why more explanation does not fix them and marking does.

The largest is description where evaluation was asked for. A student retells the study and stops, because retelling is what they practised. The second is the generic criticism, where a real objection is replaced by a sentence that would fit any study. The third is the variable confusion, which surfaces under time pressure even in students who can explain the distinction calmly in a lesson, and which responds only to repetition on real scenarios.

The fourth is ethics as a list. A student names informed consent, deception and protection from harm without saying what any of them requires or how a researcher would address them, and the marks sit in the second half. The fifth is data questions answered with a restatement: the graph shows that the score went up, with nothing said about what that implies for the hypothesis. The sixth is the undecided answer, where a question asking for a judgement receives a balanced summary and no position.

A seventh deserves its own mention because it is purely administrative: misreading the command word. Describe, explain, suggest and evaluate ask for different things, and a correct answer to the wrong command scores badly. Fifteen minutes a week spent sorting real questions by command word, rather than discussing command words in the abstract, generally removes this category inside a month and costs nothing.

Criticisms that would apply equally to any study ever run

sections.heading: Ethics in the syllabus, and ethics in the tutoring room
paragraphs: Research ethics is examinable content in 0266 rather than background reading, and it is also the part of the syllabus where a student's answer most often stops halfway. Naming an issue is the first mark. Saying what it requires of the researcher is the second. Saying how a particular study breached it or handled it is the third, and that is where candidates stop writing. Teaching it as a three-step move rather than as a vocabulary list changes the score on every ethics question.

The table below sets out the main issues in that three-step form. It is worth a student's time to be able to produce the right-hand column from memory for any study they have learned, because questions tend to arrive as a scenario rather than as a definition request. A study in which participants were not told the real aim is a deception question; the marks are in what the researcher should have done afterwards, and debriefing is the answer the weaker scripts never reach.

There is a second kind of ethics on this page, and it belongs in the open. 0266 has no coursework, so nothing a student submits to Cambridge could be improperly authored by anybody. School-set assignments and mocks still exist and still feed predicted grades, which feed sixth-form and university applications, and on those the boundary is the usual one: a tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on work the student has written. No sentences are supplied for submission, and no draft is edited to the point where the authorship becomes unclear.

Published exam material gets the same treatment. Syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are referenced and obtained through the school from cambridgeinternational.org rather than circulated as downloads. Reproducing board material is a copyright matter, and with unreleased papers it becomes a malpractice exposure that lands on the candidate rather than on the provider. A tutor marking against the published criteria does not need to distribute anything to do the job properly.

sections.heading: Marking a script together, line by line
paragraphs: The most useful twenty minutes in a Psychology session is not teaching. It is the marked script on a shared screen with the cursor moving through it, the tutor stopping at each place a mark was available, and the student saying what should have been written there. That order matters. A tutor who explains the correction produces a student who agrees; a tutor who asks the question produces a student who can do it next week without help.

The process has a rhythm. Read the question aloud and identify the command word before looking at the answer. Go through the answer marking where credit was earned, which matters as much as finding faults because students systematically underestimate what they did right. Stop at each gap and ask what the criteria wanted there. Then set the same question again, to be answered cold, and compare the two scripts side by side. The gain between attempt one and attempt two is attributable to one change rather than to general improvement, which makes it genuinely informative.

This is where the online format earns its place rather than merely coping. Two scripts can sit side by side on screen, annotated live, with the student taking control to rewrite a paragraph while the tutor watches. Doing the same thing on paper across a table means one person holding the sheet and the other reading upside down. Screen sharing is not a compromise for this task; it is the better tool, and it is also why the marked work is easy to keep and easy for a parent to open.

The output is what the family receives. A marked script, a short note naming the faults in plain language, and a line on what changed since the last one. Over six weeks that becomes a folder nobody has to interpret. It also makes the honest conversation possible: if the faults named in week one are still there in week five, that is visible to everybody and the plan needs changing rather than defending.

sections.heading: What counts outside the exam hall: equivalency and next steps
paragraphs: Two practical questions sit behind most 0266 bookings and neither is about teaching. The first is whether the subject counts. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, the published requirement is a pass in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Psychology counts as an accredited subject like any other.

The detail that catches families out is the exclusion: Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE total. A student taking those two plus four academic IGCSEs therefore has four counting subjects rather than six, which changes option-block planning in Year 9 and is worth checking before it is too late to adjust. At least one competing tutoring site publishes a six-subject requirement, which is not what the published rule says.

No IB equivalency figure appears anywhere on this page, because none has been confirmed from the Ministry's own pages for this project. If your planning depends on an IB points number, read it at moe.gov.ae or ask the attestation authority in your emirate directly rather than trusting a tutoring site, this one included. Equivalency is also not a process a tutor performs, accelerates or influences, and no tutoring is required for it; any provider implying otherwise is building urgency around a regulatory process.

The second question is where Psychology leads. Cambridge AS and A Level Psychology is the direct continuation and some Abu Dhabi schools admit students to it without the IGCSE. IB Diploma Psychology is the route in an IB sixth form and introduces an Internal Assessment, a written report on a replicated experiment, which is the first assessed work these students produce outside an exam hall. Neither route requires IGCSE Psychology, and a student who enjoys the subject should take it for that reason rather than for a prerequisite that does not exist.

sections.heading: Scheduling in Abu Dhabi, and what starting actually involves
paragraphs: A written-work arrangement needs two things from the calendar: a session slot and time afterwards for the student to write. Families who book a session at the only free moment in the week, with activities either side of it, end up with a tutor teaching and nobody writing, which removes the mechanism the whole plan depends on. The practical advice is to protect a forty-minute writing window somewhere in the following two days before fixing the lesson time.

Abu Dhabi sorts into the usual three windows. Short-commute communities in the central districts and Khalifa City can manage a late-afternoon start. The 5.30pm to 7pm band is the most contested in the emirate. After 7pm is what mainland families use, and for a minority subject like Psychology it is where specialist availability is genuinely better, so a family able to take a later slot gets a real choice of tutor. Mocks cluster in January and February, which is when demand peaks and choice disappears; an October start costs the same per hour.

Ramadan is worth agreeing in advance rather than improvising. Sessions commonly move to post-Iftar timing, and written tasks are better set shorter and more frequently through that month than paused entirely, because a four-week gap in a marking cycle is hard to recover from with a June series approaching. Travel is the other recurring factor: an online slot can follow a family to another time zone during the holidays if the time difference is agreed before the trip rather than after it.

Starting is short and specific. Send one marked script, a list of the topic areas the class has covered, and the series the student is entered for. A free trial lesson follows, one session and no charge, spent marking a real answer with the student rather than interviewing them. What comes back is a written note naming the faults and a realistic week count. If no 0266 specialist is free in the slot you need, you will be told that rather than offered a general science or humanities tutor, and no grade is promised by anybody, because a subject marked by examiners reading extended prose does not allow it.
