sections.heading: How sessions run in Abu Dhabi, and where the line sits on homework
paragraphs: Lessons are one-to-one and delivered over live video, booked in Gulf Standard Time so they sit after the school day rather than inside it. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; those visits are a service we run only in India. For a second foreign language the online format is also what makes a syllabus-specific match possible: a tutor who has marked Cambridge 0530 and the Edexcel Spanish paper is not reliably living within driving distance of Al Reef, Al Shamkha or Al Ain.

Sessions have a fixed shape. The tutor opens the running error list, takes the category at the top, teaches or revises it, and sets a short task that tests that category and nothing else. The task is marked with a count rather than a score and the count goes back into the list. Once a term there is a full timed paper with every lost mark attributed to a component and a category, plus two lines comparing it with the previous one.

The boundary on school work is firm. A tutor may teach a structure, model a task on a different prompt, mark something your child has already submitted, name the category a mark came off, and set a parallel task. A tutor may not supply sentences for a piece going to school, polish a draft into a finished state, or hand over material to be copied. Boards treat submitted work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student. The working test is whether your child could reproduce a correction unaided tomorrow.

If no 0530 specialist is free in the slot you need, we say so and give the next realistic time rather than putting a general Spanish speaker in front of an exam class. Spanish is a smaller subject than maths in this emirate and availability is genuinely tighter in the spring term, which is one more reason the autumn is the cheaper place to start.

process.title: Confirm the board and the code
process.description: Send the syllabus code from the entry sheet, Cambridge 0530 or the Pearson Edexcel equivalent, with the series and the centre. Schools in this emirate use both boards, and a term spent on the wrong board's past papers is the most avoidable loss available in this subject.

process.title: Build the error list from real work
process.description: In the free trial the tutor marks a recent piece of your child's Spanish and sorts the mistakes into the six categories, with counts. That list, not a syllabus checklist, is what the plan is built from, and you get a copy of it whether or not you book anything further.

process.title: Separate the knowledge gaps from the habits
process.description: Some categories close in one session and some need a term of short practice. We split the list in two and tell you which half the time available can realistically reach, especially where there are only a few weeks before a series.

process.title: One category per session, counted every time
process.description: Each session takes the top category, teaches it, and ends with a task that tests only that. Marking returns a count that goes back into the list, so the same category can be compared across weeks. Nothing is written for your child at any point in the term.

process.title: Timed paper once a term, attributed
process.description: A full paper under timed conditions, with every lost mark attributed to a component and a category, and a short written comparison against the previous paper. The comparison drives the next six weeks. No predicted grade is attached, because boundaries are set after the series.

whyPoints.title: Errors named as categories
whyPoints.description: Marked work comes back with counted categories rather than red corrections and a comment about care. A parent who speaks no Spanish can still see whether the ser and estar count fell from eleven to three, which is the only independent check available in this subject.

whyPoints.title: The fix is costed honestly
whyPoints.description: Each category carries a realistic timescale, including the two that will not move inside eight weeks. Selling an exam-term intensive aimed at a habit problem is the standard move in this market and it is why families feel the hours did nothing.

whyPoints.title: Accents and the keyboard sorted in week one
whyPoints.description: A ten-minute fix that removes a two-year habit. Spanish accents change meaning and sometimes tense, and a student who practised without them because typing was awkward will omit them by reflex in a handwritten paper.

whyPoints.title: Both accents practised deliberately
whyPoints.description: Peninsular and Latin American listening are labelled and alternated rather than mixed at random, and capture is recorded on the permitted plays only. Practice with unlimited replays rehearses a skill the paper does not test.

whyPoints.title: Straight about taking two languages
whyPoints.description: We mark French and Spanish cross-contamination as its own category, recommend different evenings for each, and will tell you when three languages in one exam year is more than the week can hold. That conversation costs us bookings and saves families terms.

whyPoints.title: Delivered online, with nothing implied
whyPoints.description: Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with later starts during Ramadan. We hold no accreditation from any regulator or exam board and claim none, and we do not write any part of what your child hands in.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge IGCSE Spanish 0530 easier than French 0520?
faqs.answer: Easier at the start and not easier overall. Spanish spelling is phonetically regular, so listening and reading feel approachable in the first year, which is why it is chosen as the lighter option at fourteen. It then asks for things English never does: two verbs for to be, a past-tense choice based on whether an action was completed, and an early brush with the subjunctive. Students who coasted through Year 9 plateau in Year 10 when the preterite and imperfect arrive. Ask the department for a marked written task in each language rather than asking which is easier.

faqs.question: What is the difference between ser and estar, and why does it cost marks?
faqs.answer: English gives one verb for to be and Spanish gives two, with the choice resting on categories rather than on the permanent-against-temporary rule most students are taught. Location, states resulting from a change, and a handful of adjectives that shift meaning with each verb all break the simple version. It costs marks in writing and speaking, and occasionally wrong-foots a reading question. The categories can be taught in one session; making the choice automatic under time pressure takes four to six weeks of short forced-practice tasks, counted each week so you can see it landing.

faqs.question: My son mixes up Spanish and French verb endings. Is taking both a mistake?
faqs.answer: Not a mistake, but it has a cost that nobody warns families about. The two languages interfere with each other far more than either interferes with English: past-tense endings bleed across, and false friends slip through proofreading because the result looks like a word. We mark that interference as its own error category so it gets counted rather than hiding inside the tense and agreement totals. The structural fixes matter more than the linguistic ones: different evenings for each language, separate notebooks, and no back-to-back sessions, which guarantee the problem.

faqs.question: Does my child need the subjunctive to get a good grade in 0530?
faqs.answer: At this level the sensible position is to control a small number of triggers properly and otherwise write accurate indicative Spanish. Which triggers the specification expects is a question for the published syllabus for your child's series and for their teacher. What costs marks is ambition: a mangled subjunctive in a sentence that did not need one scores below a clean indicative, and the student usually leaves the exam thinking they wrote something impressive. Four accurate sentences beat eight attempted ones. At IB Spanish B HL or A Level, avoidance stops working and it has to be taught properly.

faqs.question: How do written accents and the letter n with a tilde work in an online Spanish lesson?
faqs.answer: We sort out the keyboard in the first week, either by adding a Spanish input layout or by learning the dead-key sequences, whichever your child will actually use. This matters because accents are not decoration: some distinguish otherwise identical words and some mark a tense, so an omitted accent can turn a correct sentence into an error. Then handwriting gets separate attention, since the paper is written by hand and the accent must be placed deliberately. Work is photographed and marked on a shared screen, so the tutor sees the handwritten page rather than a typed version.

faqs.question: My daughter learned Latin American Spanish and the listening used a Peninsular accent. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It is a real and fixable one. Practice material reflects the full range of spoken Spanish, and a student trained mostly on one variety can stall on the other. The usual symptom is a listening mark that swings by a band between practice papers for no reason the student can explain. We stop mixing recordings at random: each one is labelled, the two varieties are alternated, and capture is recorded separately. Improvement on one variety while the other stays flat tells you the issue is accent familiarity rather than vocabulary, which is the quicker fix.

faqs.question: What can a single Spanish session realistically fix?
faqs.answer: Knowledge gaps, not habits. One session is enough to teach the ser and estar categories, teach por and para, sort out accents and the keyboard, explain when not to attempt a subjunctive, and teach the paraphrase patterns that cost marks on the reading paper. What no run of consecutive sessions will fix is agreement under time pressure, the automatic past-tense choice, or listening across an unfamiliar accent, because those are habits needing ten focused minutes several times a week across a term. A short plan should buy the knowledge gaps first.

faqs.question: Which 0530 component do Abu Dhabi students lose the most marks on?
faqs.answer: Writing, and mostly to the same handful of categories rather than to a shortage of ideas. Ser and estar errors, one past tense used where a choice was required, inconsistent agreement and missing accents account for the bulk of what we mark in this emirate. Speaking loses marks for the same reasons, more visibly, because hesitation is audible as well as recorded. Reading losses are narrower and more teachable: students scan for the word the text used when the question has paraphrased it, which explicit pattern work changes within a few sessions.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start Spanish tutoring in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Not too late to gain marks, too late for some of them. Eight to ten weeks will move the knowledge gaps, reading paraphrase patterns, listening technique and the accent habit, and those convert into marks quickly. It will not make agreement automatic or embed the preterite-imperfect choice, because both are habits built over months. The honest plan aims the available hours at what can move and says plainly what cannot, rather than selling a full-course intensive. If the student will also do ten minutes a day between sessions, the ceiling rises noticeably.

faqs.question: Should my child choose Spanish in Year 9 if they already study Arabic?
faqs.answer: It is a workload question rather than a language one. Arabic provision is part of the deal in UAE private schools, so Spanish would be the second language rather than the first, and two languages means two sets of written accuracy practice in the same week. That is manageable for a student with genuinely spare evenings and punishing for one who has them only in theory. Ask how many timetabled Arabic minutes a week your school runs before deciding. We would rather give you a straight view of the week than take the booking and watch one language go unpractised.

faqs.question: Do you cover the Edexcel International GCSE in Spanish as well as Cambridge 0530?
faqs.answer: Yes, and establishing which one your child sits is the first thing we do. Cambridge IGCSE Spanish is 0530; the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE in Spanish is a separate qualification usually carrying the code 4SP1, with different papers, past material and timetables. Schools in this emirate use both. Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, while Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series. The code is on the entry sheet and one email to the school confirms it.

faqs.question: How many Spanish sessions a week does a Year 10 student need?
faqs.answer: One weekly session plus short practice between them covers most Year 10 students, and the practice matters more than the session count. The category work that moves written accuracy needs frequency rather than duration: ten focused minutes several times a week beats a second hour at the weekend. Where the bottleneck is listening or speaking we sometimes run two short sessions instead of one long one, because both respond to frequency. Starting in Year 10 rather than Year 11 is also simply cheaper, since habit items have time to automate before the exam term.

faqs.question: Can the 0530 speaking test be prepared if nobody at home speaks Spanish?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the format helps. Spoken attempts are recorded with your consent and the same task is repeated a month later, so progress can be heard rather than described, which is the only honest check available to a family that does not speak the language. We train recovery rather than scripted answers: what the student does in the few seconds after meeting a word they do not have. Response length is tracked too, since very short correct answers leave developable marks unclaimed. A fixed twice-weekly slot does more than an occasional conversation group.

faqs.question: How do you check whether the Spanish grammar work is actually sticking?
faqs.answer: By counting, not by asking. Each marked task returns the number of errors in each category rather than a score out of ten, and the counts carry forward week to week. If ser and estar were taught in week one and the count is unchanged in week six, the teaching was explanation rather than practice, which is a problem with us and not with your child. Once a term a full timed paper has every lost mark attributed to a component and a category, so you can see whether the lesson work survived exam conditions.

faqs.question: What does a Cambridge IGCSE Spanish tutor cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Market rates rather than ours: qualified subject tutors working online in the UAE advertise between roughly AED 150 and AED 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE support from AED 150, and in-home visits are put at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour in Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table. Specialist exam-year rates run higher. The bigger variable is plan length, and that depends on how much of your child's error list is knowledge gaps rather than habits, which is what the free trial establishes before anybody quotes you a package.

Send the syllabus code off the entry sheet and one recent marked piece of Spanish, and the free trial will produce a counted error list sorted into the six categories, split between the gaps one session can close and the habits that need a term. You keep that list either way. Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, counts are carried forward every week, and nothing is ever written for your child.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-travel-and-tou.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Cambridge IGCSE Travel and Tourism and the humanities subjects it sits beside in an Abu Dhabi option block. Each has marked 0471-style responses against a published mark scheme and can show a parent, on screen, why a long answer scored short.

intro.heading: Why 0471 candidates write plenty and still miss the grade
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Travel and Tourism 0471 is a content-light, technique-heavy syllabus. A student opening it for the first time assumes it rewards knowing things about airlines, hotels and resorts. The marks sit somewhere else. They go to candidates who can read the insert they are given, recognise which command term is being used, and answer at the tariff printed beside the question. A candidate who knows the industry well and writes freely about it will still be capped, because the examiner is marking a specific instruction and not general enthusiasm.

In Abu Dhabi this plays out in a particular way. Travel and Tourism is a minority entry in most private schools in the emirate. It usually runs in one option block beside Business Studies and Geography, and it is often taught by a specialist in one of those subjects rather than by someone whose career has been spent on 0471. That is a timetabling reality, not a criticism of the teacher, but it has a consequence a parent can see: the class tends to receive less syllabus-specific past-paper marking than the Maths or Science sets do, and the feedback it does receive is more general.

A tutoring session can fix three things, in this order. First, the reading habit: teaching a candidate to annotate the insert before writing a word, because the marks for application come from the source and nowhere else. Second, the tariff discipline: four lines for a four-mark question, a judgement and a conclusion for an evaluate question, one noun for a one-mark state question. Third, the evidence bank: a small set of destinations and operators the candidate knows in real detail, rather than a long list they know shallowly.

That third point is where an Abu Dhabi student has an advantage almost nobody uses. The syllabus wants destination examples, visitor-management examples, sustainability examples and event-tourism examples. Abu Dhabi supplies all of them. Louvre Abu Dhabi and the Saadiyat Cultural District, the Etihad Airways hub at Zayed International Airport, the co-located theme parks on Yas Island, the UNESCO-listed Cultural Sites of Al Ain, the controlled visitor numbers on Sir Bani Yas Island, and the hotel-occupancy spike around the Grand Prix weekend are all checkable, all local, and all more persuasive on paper than a recycled textbook paragraph about a European resort.

On delivery, the position is plain. Tutoring for UAE families runs one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For a source-based subject that is not a compromise, because the insert, the mark scheme and the destination data all live on a shared screen where tutor and student annotate the same document at the same time. Everything priced on this page is the market, attributed to whoever published it, and every Cambridge date is cited rather than restated.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-travel-and-tou.programmesIntro: 0471 sits inside a wider Cambridge route, and Abu Dhabi families usually want to know what comes after it. These are the programmes most relevant to a Travel and Tourism candidate in the emirate, with what each one assumes on entry.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE (Upper Secondary)
programmes.description: The two-year upper-secondary stage where 0471 is taught and examined. Candidates typically carry seven to nine subjects, of which Travel and Tourism is one option choice. Assessment is by written examination in a published series, entered by the school's Cambridge exams officer, and the grade is reported on the Cambridge statement of results before the certificate itself is issued.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi, Cambridge IGCSE runs across the British-curriculum schools licensed by the Department of Education and Knowledge. Alongside it, Arabic, Islamic education and social or moral studies are required for the relevant student groups under the federal rule that private schools must follow those subjects regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed to teach, so a Year 10 timetable in the emirate is fuller than the Cambridge subject list alone suggests.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level
programmes.description: The post-16 Cambridge route. Travel and Tourism continues at this level, and a student who enjoyed 0471 often takes it with Business or Geography. The step up is in evaluation: answers are longer, the sources are denser, and a judgement that is merely asserted no longer scores. Candidates also meet quantitative material such as occupancy and spend data in a form 0471 only hints at.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, the reported requirement is one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade no lower than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. An Abu Dhabi family planning a UAE university application should read that requirement on moe.gov.ae for the current cycle rather than relying on a tutoring page, including this one.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: There is no direct IB equivalent of 0471. Students who want the same territory inside the Diploma usually take Business Management or Geography, where tourism appears as a case-study context rather than a subject in its own right. The transferable skill is the one 0471 teaches badly when untaught: reading a source pack under time pressure and answering the instruction given.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools offer the Diploma alongside or instead of a British route, and families on the island and in the Al Raha corridor often choose between the two at the end of Year 11. A 0471 candidate moving into the Diploma should expect the command-term vocabulary to change, because the IB marks against assessment criteria rather than a question-by-question tariff.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-travel-and-tou.subjectsIntro: Travel and Tourism is rarely the only subject a family is thinking about. These are the Cambridge IGCSE subjects most often requested alongside 0471 by Abu Dhabi families, with what each one is actually assessing.

subjects.name: Travel and Tourism (0471)
subjects.description: Written assessment across the industry, worldwide destinations, customer care and working procedures, products and services, marketing and promotion, and destination management. The grade turns on command-term discipline and on applying a given insert rather than on breadth of general knowledge.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: The subject most often timetabled against 0471. Candidates lose marks by defining terms correctly and then failing to apply them to the named business in the case study. The analysis-and-evaluation habit transfers directly into Travel and Tourism answers.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Shares the tourism, sustainability and settlement content with 0471 but assesses it through map, graph and fieldwork skills. Students who can read a resource in Geography usually read a Travel and Tourism insert well too; the reverse is less reliable.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Supplies the vocabulary a strong 0471 evaluation answer leans on: demand, price elasticity, seasonality, multiplier effects. Marks are lost on diagram labelling and on conclusions that restate the question instead of weighing the two sides.

subjects.name: Enterprise (0454)
subjects.description: Project-based and increasingly chosen in Abu Dhabi option blocks. Useful beside 0471 because both reward applied reasoning about a real organisation, though Enterprise assesses the process of planning rather than recall of industry structure.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500)
subjects.description: The hidden constraint on 0471. A candidate who cannot write a tight explanatory paragraph in English will be capped on the extended-response questions regardless of how well they know the industry. Directed-writing practice pays twice.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Common across Abu Dhabi's international cohort. The reading-for-detail skill assessed here is the same skill 0471 inserts demand, and timed summary practice transfers almost one for one into source-based tourism questions.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Relevant to 0471 because tourism data arrives as percentages, index numbers and occupancy rates. A candidate comfortable with proportional reasoning reads a visitor-arrivals table correctly; one who is not misreads the trend and builds an answer on it.

subjects.name: Information and Communication Technology (0417)
subjects.description: Chosen alongside 0471 by students interested in travel distribution and online booking. The practical components are assessed under supervised conditions, which makes the revision rhythm different from a written-only subject and worth planning separately.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.description: Frequently on the same Abu Dhabi timetable, because Arabic is required for the relevant student groups in private schools in the emirate. Worth noting that an Arabic grade is excluded from the five subjects counted in the reported Ministry of Education equivalency rule.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-travel-and-tou.regionsIntro: Abu Dhabi is not one commute. The emirate runs from the island out through Saadiyat and Yas to the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor and on to the newer mainland communities, and where a family lives changes what time a session can realistically start.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Home to Louvre Abu Dhabi and the Saadiyat Cultural District, which makes it the most useful postcode in the emirate for a 0471 candidate gathering first-hand destination evidence. Families here usually run sessions between 4.30pm and 7pm.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: The co-located theme-park cluster and Yas Marina Circuit sit here, giving a candidate visitor-management and event-tourism material within a short drive. Grand Prix week reshapes the family calendar and is worth planning revision around.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Dense residential towers with a young school-age population and a short bridge commute to the island. Evening slots fill early here, and families tend to prefer two shorter weekly sessions over one long one.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Villa communities with a large British-curriculum cohort and a long school run. A 4pm start is rarely achievable by car; online sessions from 4.30pm are, which is the practical argument for the format in this part of the emirate.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: A corridor of international schools and family villas between the island and the airport. Parents here often ask for one session a week in term time and a tighter block in the weeks before the series.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Older island neighbourhoods with established British-curriculum schools and shorter commutes. Useful for 0471 because the Corniche, Qasr Al Hosn and the marina sit close enough for a candidate to collect their own observations.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Al Falah
regions.note: Newer mainland communities where school runs are long and tutor travel time is real money. These are the areas where the in-home market rate quietly absorbs forty minutes of driving each way.

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat, Al Bateen and the island
schoolClusters.note: The island and its nearest bridge communities hold most of the emirate's established British-curriculum provision. Option blocks here are wide enough that Travel and Tourism appears as a genuine choice rather than a filler, which is also why 0471 candidates in this cluster tend to be the ones who chose it deliberately.

sections.heading: The written papers, and what each one is really marking
paragraphs: 0471 is assessed by written examination. There is no practical component and no portfolio to build, which makes it unusual among the option subjects an Abu Dhabi student might pick in Year 9. One paper covers the syllabus broadly; the other pushes the same material into applied, source-based questions where the candidate is handed material and expected to use it. The exact duration, mark total and weighting of each component are set in the syllabus for the series your child is entered for, and that document is the first thing a parent should read. This page does not restate figures Cambridge can revise between series.

What matters more than the weighting split is the behaviour each component rewards. The broad paper punishes vagueness: a question asking a candidate to identify two types of tour operator wants two nouns, and a paragraph of context around them earns nothing extra while costing minutes that the longer questions needed. The applied paper punishes the opposite habit. A candidate who has memorised a strong answer about a destination and reproduces it regardless of the insert provided will lose the application marks entirely, because those marks are tied to the source on the desk.

The table below sets out the syllabus areas as the Cambridge material groups them, what the questions in each area actually demand, and the failure pattern we see most often in Abu Dhabi scripts. It is organised the way a tutor would work through a diagnostic, not the way a textbook contents page is ordered. Read the right-hand column first if you are trying to work out whether tutoring would help: if two or three of those failures describe your child, the gap is technique rather than content, and technique is the faster thing to fix.

One practical note on entry. The option, the tier where one exists, and the series are chosen by the school's Cambridge exams officer months before revision begins. A family who disagrees with the entry has to raise it early, not in the spring. That is covered further down, in the section that counts the year backwards.

sections.heading: The case-study trap: why a full page can still score three marks
paragraphs: The single most common script we see in this subject is fluent, confident, well organised and under-marked. The candidate has written a page. The content is accurate. The grade is a C. The reason is almost always the same: the answer is about tourism in general when the question was about the material supplied. Examiners cannot award credit for knowledge that is not applied to the given context, and a candidate who has not been taught that explicitly will keep writing the same essay and keep receiving the same mark.

The trap has a second layer. Schools, reasonably, teach case studies. A class spends two lessons on a destination, the students take notes, and those notes become the answer to every destination question thereafter. In a question that happens to suit the taught example, the result is excellent. In a question that specifies a different visitor type, a different season or a different kind of resort, the same paragraph arrives unchanged and most of its marks evaporate. The candidate experiences this as bad luck. It is not luck; it is a technique that works intermittently.

Breaking the habit takes an unglamorous drill. The student is given an insert and a question and is not allowed to write prose for the first four minutes. Instead they underline the visitor type, the location, the time frame and the command term, and write three bullet points, each one quoting or paraphrasing something from the source. Only then do they write. Most students resist this for two or three sessions and then notice their marks have moved, because the application credit they were missing is now there to be awarded.

The same drill fixes a related problem in evaluation questions. Asked to assess whether a development benefits a host community, a candidate will produce three advantages, three disadvantages and then stop, as though balance alone were the answer. The mark scheme wants a judgement. Teaching a student to finish with a sentence that decides something, and gives one reason for deciding it, is a small change that moves extended answers more reliably than any amount of extra content revision.
bullets: Four minutes of annotation before writing is the highest-return habit in the subject
A pre-learned destination paragraph scores well only when the question happens to fit it

sections.heading: Abu Dhabi as the case study your child already lives in
paragraphs: Candidates everywhere are told to use examples. Most reach for whatever the textbook used, which means an examiner reads the same European resort hundreds of times. An Abu Dhabi student has an alternative that is both more interesting and easier to defend, because they can check it. The emirate contains a purpose-built cultural district, a hub carrier, a cluster of co-located theme parks, a UNESCO-listed oasis landscape, a protected island reserve with controlled visitor numbers and an annual motorsport event that visibly moves hotel pricing. Those are the exact categories the syllabus asks about.

Using local material well is not a matter of mentioning the place. It means being able to state something specific and sourced: who funds an attraction, which visitor markets it targets, what constrains its capacity, how its season behaves. A candidate who can write two sentences of that quality about Louvre Abu Dhabi will out-mark one who writes six vague sentences about a destination they have only read about. The research is also genuinely short: the Department of Culture and Tourism publishes material on the emirate's attractions, and each operator publishes its own.

There is a discipline to this. A local example must still answer the question asked. If the question specifies a mass-market beach destination and the candidate supplies a high-value cultural one, the example is wrong no matter how well known it is. The useful approach is to build a small portfolio covering different visitor types and different management problems, so that whatever the paper specifies, something in the portfolio fits. Four or five well-understood examples beat a dozen half-remembered ones, and the portfolio is one of the first things a session builds.

The table below is a starting grid rather than a finished answer. Each row pairs an Abu Dhabi asset with the syllabus territory it illustrates, the kind of statement a candidate should be able to make about it, and where the underlying information can be verified. Nothing here should go into an exam answer until the student has checked it themselves; that checking is part of what makes the example theirs.

sections.heading: Command terms, tariffs and the shape of a six-mark answer
paragraphs: Every mark in this subject is allocated against an instruction. Cambridge publishes what its command terms mean, and the mark scheme for each paper shows how credit is split. Most candidates have never read either document. They write what feels like a good answer and hope the examiner agrees. Teaching a student to read the command term and the tariff together, before writing, is the single change that moves scripts fastest, and it takes about three sessions to become automatic.

The tariff tells a candidate how much to write. A one-mark question wants one creditable item. A four-mark question usually wants either four separate points or two points developed once each; the mark scheme shows which. A question worth eight or ten marks is asking for structure, not volume: points on both sides, each developed, then a judgement. Students who write to length rather than to tariff run out of time on the questions that pay most, which is why a good script often looks less impressive than a weak one at first glance.

The command term tells a candidate what kind of sentence to write. Describe wants an accurate account; explain wants a reason linked to a consequence; analyse wants the parts of a situation and how they interact; evaluate wants a weighed judgement. A candidate who answers explain with a description has written something true that cannot be credited. This is the most frequent cause of the gap between a student's apparent subject knowledge and their actual mark, and it is entirely teachable.

The table below gives the working version we use in sessions. The tariffs shown are the ranges these terms commonly carry rather than fixed values, because the allocation varies by paper and series; the mark scheme for your child's paper is the authority. What does not vary is the kind of sentence each term expects, and that is the part worth drilling.

sections.heading: The 0471 year counted backwards from the entry deadline
paragraphs: Families plan forwards from today. Cambridge works backwards from a series. The gap between those two habits is where most avoidable damage happens, because the decisions that constrain a grade are taken months before anyone feels urgency. Entries close, forecast grades are submitted, and timetables are issued by zone, all while a Year 11 student still thinks of the exam as something in the distant future.

Two facts from the Cambridge exam administration guidance are worth a parent's attention. The first is that IGCSE exams run in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, so the series your child sits is a choice the school has already made. The second is sharper: every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Download the timetable through the school, not from a search result.

The table below uses the published key dates for the March 2027 series as a worked example. Abu Dhabi centres do not generally enter that series, so the dates themselves are not your child's dates. What they show is the shape of the calendar: entries closing more than two months before the first paper, forecast grades submitted before the papers are sat, results reaching the centre well after the exam period, and certificates arriving later still. Apply that shape to whichever series your child is entered for, and read the live dates from Cambridge rather than from any page that restates them.

There is one IB-adjacent caution worth stating plainly, because Abu Dhabi families often have children in both systems. No IB exam or results date appears anywhere on this page. The IB's own site is not reliably reachable for automated checking, so any IB date here would be second-hand. Confirm IB dates with the school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org directly.

sections.heading: What 0471 tutoring costs in the Abu Dhabi market
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible providers in this market publish no price at all, and two of the ones that do quote in US dollars, a currency no Abu Dhabi family transacts in. That is the gap this section fills. Every figure below is the market, attributed to the provider that published it, with the month it was read. None of it is an IB Gram price list, and a page that quoted one without the session length, subject and tutor profile attached would be telling you very little anyway.

Two things specific to Travel and Tourism push a quote upwards, and a parent should know both before negotiating. The first is scarcity: 0471 is a minority entry, so the pool of tutors who have actually marked it against a published scheme is small, and scarce subjects sit at the top of any band rather than the middle. The second is that a generalist humanities tutor can be perfectly competent at the content and still not know the command-term tariffs, which is precisely the thing a 0471 candidate is paying to fix. Ask directly whether the tutor has marked 0471 responses against the scheme, and ask to see that happen in the first session.

On what a family actually needs, the honest answer is fewer hours than most quotes assume. Where the problem is technique rather than content, the change tends to arrive inside six to ten sessions, because the student is learning a small number of habits rather than a syllabus. Where content really is missing, the number rises and the right conversation is about whether the entry itself still makes sense. Any provider quoting a long fixed block before seeing a marked script is selling a package, not a diagnosis.

One pricing note that is easy to miss. Market in-home rates look higher than online rates partly because travel sits inside the hourly figure. A tutor driving from the island to Khalifa City at 5pm is spending time that someone pays for, and it is not the tutor. Comparing an online rate with an in-home rate without accounting for that is comparing two different products.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home visit for a source-based subject
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi parents searching for help with this subject are usually picturing someone at the dining table. It is worth testing that picture against what the subject actually requires, because 0471 is unusually well suited to a shared screen. Nearly everything a session needs is a document: an insert, a question paper, a mark scheme, a visitor-arrivals table, a destination's own published information. Annotating those together, with both people seeing the same cursor, is a better lesson than passing printed sheets across a table.

The travel economics matter too. An in-home tutor covering the island, Khalifa City and Al Raha in the same week is pricing forty to ninety minutes of driving into every visit, and at 5pm on Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Street that estimate is optimistic. The family pays for it either in the hourly rate or in a session that starts late and finishes early. Removing the drive is what makes a 4.30pm start realistic on a weekday in Khalifa City rather than aspirational.

The decisive argument is the tutor pool. In-home tutoring narrows the choice to people willing to drive to your community on your evening. For Maths that is a manageable constraint, because the local pool is deep. For a minority option subject it can mean the difference between a specialist who has marked 0471 scripts and a competent generalist who has not. Online removes the geography from the matching problem, which is exactly what a scarce subject needs.

Being plain about what is on offer: IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE, and home visits are a service offered only in India. The comparison below is therefore between what we provide and what the local market provides, set out so a family can decide rather than discover. If an in-home tutor is genuinely the better fit for your child, that is a reasonable conclusion to reach from this table.

sections.heading: ADEK, the tutor permit, equivalency and where honest help stops
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi are overseen by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which according to the federal government's own information service supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. That is worth knowing for two reasons. It is the body whose published inspection outcomes describe your child's school, and it is the body whose professional-ethics expectations shape what a serving teacher may do outside school hours. Press reporting indicates that Abu Dhabi rules prohibit school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school; a family should verify the current policy wording with ADEK directly before relying on it.

Individual tutoring in the UAE is permitted but regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced through Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The federal government's own pages state that the permit is granted free of charge for two years, and that eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. They also state that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no figure should be quoted to you, including by us. IB Gram makes no claim to any regulator or examination board accreditation, and any provider that does should be asked to show the permit or centre number.

On equivalency: a 0471 grade can count towards the Ministry of Education's British-track requirement, because the two subjects reported as excluded from the count of five are Arabic and Islamic education. The reported requirement is five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at that grade or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. A page currently ranking for these searches states six subjects rather than five, which is why a family should read the requirement on moe.gov.ae for the current cycle. No tutor performs equivalency, and nobody should present it as something they can secure for you.

Finally, the boundary on what help means. A tutor teaches, questions, explains a mark scheme and gives feedback on what the student has produced. A tutor does not supply assessed material to be handed in as the student's own, and no provider should offer to. For 0471 this is straightforward, since the subject is examined by written paper under supervised conditions, but the same principle governs how we handle practice answers: the student writes, the tutor marks, and the words that reach the examiner are the student's.

process.title: Tell us the series and the symptom
process.description: The two facts that shape everything else are which series your child is entered for and what the problem looks like on paper. A low mark with fluent writing is a different job from a low mark with thin content. If you have a marked script or a mock paper, send it; it saves a session.

process.title: A no-charge first lesson with a marked answer
process.description: The first session is free, one per family, with no card details taken. Your child answers a section of a past paper and the tutor marks it against the published scheme while you watch if you want to. You finish with a marked script and a plain statement of where the marks went.

process.title: Agree the format and the slot
process.description: Weekly through the course, an intensive block before the series, or a single diagnostic. We propose one and say why. The slot is fixed to Gulf Standard Time and chosen around the school run, which in Khalifa City and Al Raha usually means 4.30pm or later.

process.title: Build the evidence bank alongside the technique
process.description: Each session pairs a technique drill with one addition to the student's own case-study portfolio, drawn where possible from the emirate so the student can check it. By the pre-series block the candidate has four or five examples they understand properly rather than a long list they half-remember.

process.title: Review against the backward calendar
process.description: We check progress against the series calendar rather than against the term, because entries, forecast grades and the zone timetable all fall earlier than families expect. If the sensible conclusion is to reduce sessions or stop, we will say so rather than extend a block.

whyPoints.title: Marking, not talking
whyPoints.description: The lesson a 0471 candidate needs is somebody marking their writing against the published scheme and showing them the gap. Every session includes written work marked live on screen, which is also how a parent can judge whether the tutoring is working without taking anyone's word for it.

whyPoints.title: Figures that carry a source
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page names the kind of provider that published it and the month it was read. Nothing is presented as an IB Gram price list, and nothing is a statistic without a source. A page that cannot show where a number came from should not be used to plan a budget.

whyPoints.title: A scarce subject matched without geography
whyPoints.description: Travel and Tourism is a minority entry in Abu Dhabi, so the constraint on quality is the size of the pool, not the distance. Online one-to-one matching removes the drive from the equation and makes a genuine 0471 specialist possible for a family in Al Shamkha as much as on Saadiyat.

whyPoints.title: Local evidence a candidate can verify
whyPoints.description: The emirate supplies real material for destinations, visitor management, heritage constraints and event seasonality. Sessions build a portfolio from it and insist the student checks each claim themselves, which is what turns a mentioned place into a usable example.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits, stated first
whyPoints.description: Lessons are online, one-to-one and over live video; home visits are not part of what we do in the UAE. We hold no regulator or board accreditation and do not claim any. A tutor marks and teaches, and the work that reaches an examiner is written by the student.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge IGCSE Travel and Tourism 0471 an easy option for a Year 10 student in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: It is accessible in content and demanding in technique, which is a different thing from easy. The industry material is readable and most students pick it up quickly. The marks, though, are awarded against command terms and tariffs, and a candidate who writes well but answers the wrong instruction will sit in the middle of the grade range regardless of effort. Students who struggle with timed extended writing in English often find 0471 harder than expected. The fair summary is that it rewards disciplined readers and punishes fluent waffle, so the right question is not whether it is easy but whether your child reads questions carefully.

faqs.question: Which written components does a 0471 candidate sit, and how do they differ?
faqs.answer: The syllabus is assessed by written examination only, with one paper covering the subject content broadly and another pushing the same material into applied, source-based questions where candidates are given material to use. The durations, mark totals and weightings are set in the syllabus for the series your child is entered for, so read that document rather than relying on any figure restated on a tutoring page. The behavioural difference matters more than the split: the broad paper punishes vagueness and rewards precision on short questions, while the applied paper punishes pre-learned answers that ignore the insert supplied.

faqs.question: Why does my child write a full page and still only score three marks?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the answer is about tourism in general when the question was about the material supplied. Application marks are attached to the insert, so knowledge that is never connected to the given visitor type, location or season cannot be credited however accurate it is. The second common cause is a mismatch between the command term and the sentence written: an explain question answered with a description produces something true that earns nothing. Both are technique faults rather than knowledge gaps, which is good news, because technique moves faster than content. Four minutes of annotation before writing fixes more of this than extra revision does.

faqs.question: Can a 0471 candidate use Abu Dhabi attractions as their case-study examples?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is usually a better choice than a textbook example, provided the example fits the question. The emirate offers a purpose-built cultural district on Saadiyat, a hub carrier at Zayed International Airport, a co-located park cluster on Yas Island, a World Heritage oasis landscape at Al Ain, a controlled-access island reserve and an annual motorsport weekend that visibly moves hotel pricing. Those cover most of the syllabus categories. The discipline is to match the example to the visitor type the question names, and to be able to state something specific and checkable rather than simply naming the place.

faqs.question: Does a Travel and Tourism grade count towards the five subjects the Ministry of Education requires?
faqs.answer: On the British track as reported in July 2026, the requirement is five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and the two subjects reported as excluded from that count are Arabic and Islamic education. Travel and Tourism is not excluded, so it can count as one of the five. A page currently ranking for these searches states six subjects rather than five, so read the requirement on moe.gov.ae for the current cycle before planning a subject list around it. No tutoring provider carries out equivalency or can secure an outcome from it.

faqs.question: What does a Cambridge 0471 tutor charge per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: The UAE market, read in October 2026, runs from about AED 45 to AED 150 an hour for budget or university-student online tutors, AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to AED 500 for an in-home visit with travel inside the figure, and AED 200 to AED 450 or more for a declared IGCSE or IB specialist. One premium provider publishes AED 650. Each of those bands comes from the provider that published it. A minority option subject such as 0471 tends to sit at the upper end of whichever band applies, because the pool of tutors who have actually marked it is small.

faqs.question: When do Abu Dhabi schools enter candidates for Cambridge Travel and Tourism, and when do entries close?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series, and the series your child sits is chosen by the school. Entries close well before the papers: the published key dates for the March 2027 series, useful as a worked example of the calendar shape, show final entries due on 27 November 2026 for an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. Your child's dates will differ. Get the timetable through the school, because each centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who uses the wrong zone version.

faqs.question: Are 0471 lessons delivered at our villa in Abu Dhabi, or online?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India, and we would rather say that plainly than let a family discover it at booking. For this subject the format is a genuine advantage rather than a compromise, because almost everything a session uses is a document. The insert, the mark scheme and a destination's published data all sit on a shared screen where tutor and student annotate the same page together, which is difficult to replicate with printed sheets.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a 0471 student usually need before the June papers?
faqs.answer: Where the problem is technique rather than content, the shift usually appears inside six to ten sessions, because the student is learning a small number of habits: annotate before writing, answer to the tariff, match the sentence to the command term, finish an evaluation with a judgement. Where real content is missing the number rises, and the honest conversation at that point is about whether the entry still makes sense. Any provider quoting a long fixed block before seeing a marked script is selling a package rather than making a diagnosis, and a parent is entitled to ask what the diagnosis is.

faqs.question: My child is strong in Geography but weak in Travel and Tourism. Why the gap?
faqs.answer: Usually because Geography trains resource interpretation explicitly while Travel and Tourism assumes it. A Geography student is taught to read a map, a graph and a photograph and to answer from them, and that habit is examined directly. In 0471 the same skill is required but less visibly taught, so a capable student can slip into writing from memory. The other common factor is vocabulary precision: Travel and Tourism distinguishes products from services and operators from intermediaries, and a candidate who blurs those categories loses the discrimination marks even when the underlying understanding is sound.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child prepare the destination data they need to quote?
faqs.answer: A tutor can show your child where to find it, how to judge whether it is reliable, and how to turn it into a sentence that earns marks. What a tutor should not do is hand over a ready-made paragraph to memorise, because that is how pre-learned answers get written into papers they do not fit. In practice a session looks like this: the student finds the figure from the attraction's own published information or from the emirate's tourism body, the tutor questions whether it answers the question asked, and the student rewrites until it does. The example ends up theirs.

faqs.question: Does Travel and Tourism help with admission to a hospitality or tourism degree in the UAE?
faqs.answer: It is relevant preparation and it demonstrates interest, but admission requirements are set by each university and should be read from the institution's own published entry criteria rather than inferred from a subject choice. For UAE universities, certificate equivalency through the Ministry of Education is a separate process from admission, and the British-track requirement is about the number and grade of accredited subjects rather than which subjects they are. Tutoring is not required for any of this, and any page implying that a qualification cannot be achieved without it should be read with caution.

faqs.question: Must a tutor hold a MoHRE permit to teach Abu Dhabi families privately?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced through Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the federal government's own pages state that it is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those offering private tutoring without a permit are stated to be subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you. Press reporting also indicates Abu Dhabi school staff may not tutor students enrolled at their own school.

faqs.question: Can 0471 sessions move to a later evening slot during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families ask for it. School timings compress during the month, energy levels shift, and a 4.30pm session that worked in January often does not work in the holy month. Sessions can move to a post-Iftar slot, shorten to 45 minutes, or pause entirely and resume afterwards with the block extended rather than lost. Because this subject rewards short, frequent technique practice rather than long content sessions, it adapts to a compressed month better than most. Tell us early so the slot can be reserved before the evening hours fill up across the emirate.

faqs.question: What happens if no Cambridge 0471 specialist is free when we enquire?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substitute quietly. Travel and Tourism is a minority entry and the pool of tutors who have marked it against a published scheme is genuinely small, so there are weeks when the honest answer is that nothing suitable is open in your preferred slot. The options we will put to you are a different time, a short wait for a named tutor, or a humanities specialist who will be introduced as exactly that rather than as a 0471 expert. If none of those works for your family, we will tell you that too.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-travel-and-tou.closingHeading: Start with one marked answer, not a package
abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-travel-and-tou.closingBody: The quickest way to find out whether a 0471 problem is technique or content is to have one answer marked against the published scheme and explained. That is what the no-charge first lesson is for: your child writes, the tutor marks it live, and you keep the script and a plain statement of where the marks went. From there the sensible format is usually a weekly slot through the course or a short block before the series, timed to Gulf Standard Time and set around your school run. If the conclusion is that tutoring is not what your child needs, we will say that instead.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach named Cambridge IGCSE syllabuses to Abu Dhabi students. Each profile lists the syllabus numbers the tutor works on and the components they mark, because a tutor who knows 0620 is not automatically the right person for 0654.

intro.heading: Cambridge grades a syllabus, not a subject
paragraphs: There is a difference between a tutor who teaches chemistry and a tutor who teaches Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620, and the difference shows up in marks. Cambridge publishes a numbered syllabus for every course it examines. That document states which topics are assessable, which components a candidate sits, how the marks divide between them, and which command words the questions will use. A student who has been taught the subject well but has never been taught the syllabus loses marks in a pattern that is entirely predictable from the document itself.

Abu Dhabi families meet this problem more often than most, because the emirate's British-curriculum schools draw students in from several systems. A child who arrived from an American school in Year 9, or from a national curriculum elsewhere in the Gulf, can be two years into a Cambridge course without anyone having explained what the papers look like. They know the content. They answer a six-mark question in three lines because nobody told them a six-mark question is an instruction about length as well as about content. That is the most common diagnosis in a first session with a Cambridge IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi, and it is one of the quickest to fix.

The syllabus number itself is the thing to get straight first. Mathematics is 0580 and Additional Mathematics is 0606; the sciences run as Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, or as Coordinated Sciences 0654 and Combined Science 0653; English runs as First Language 0500 or Second Language 0510; Arabic appears as First Language 0508 and as a foreign language 0544. Business Studies is 0450, Economics 0455, Computer Science 0478, Accounting 0452. Those numbers appear on the entry the school submits and on the statement of results, and confirming them against the current list on cambridgeinternational.org is the first ten minutes of a sensible tuition plan. Syllabuses are revised, so the year matters as much as the number.

From there the machinery is learnable. Every question carries a command word that tells the examiner what to accept: state wants a fact, describe wants observable detail, explain wants a causal chain, suggest wants applied reasoning about an unfamiliar context, and a candidate who treats all four the same scores inconsistently and cannot work out why. Every paper has a mark allocation that implies a structure. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and must use the matching version of the timetable. None of that is secret. It is published, and almost no competing page in this search mentions any of it.

On delivery, plainly: IB Gram does not send a tutor to an Abu Dhabi address, because home visits are a service we run only in India. Cambridge support for UAE families is one-to-one over live video at a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot, with past-paper work marked between sessions and returned annotated. That format suits this particular job unusually well, since most of the work is two people looking at the same marked script and the same mark allocation at the same time.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Cambridge runs a continuous route from lower secondary to pre-university, and the IGCSE years sit in the middle of it. These are the stages Abu Dhabi families ask about, with what each one actually examines.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The years before the numbered IGCSE syllabuses begin, ending in Checkpoint tests that Cambridge runs in March, May and October. Checkpoint is diagnostic rather than certificated, which makes it the most useful and least used piece of evidence a parent gets: it shows where a student sits against international expectations two years before anything counts.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools vary in how much weight they put on Checkpoint results, and many families never see them broken down by strand. Asking for the strand-level breakdown before Year 10 begins is the cheapest piece of diagnosis available, and it usually predicts which IGCSE subjects will need support.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Core tier
programmes.description: On tiered syllabuses such as 0580, 0610, 0620 and 0625, the Core route examines a defined subset of the content and makes the upper grades unavailable. The teaching job is to secure the full Core content rather than to extend it, and the honest conversation is about whether the tier was the right entry in the first place.
programmes.countryNote: Core entries appear most often in Abu Dhabi where a student joined a Cambridge school part-way through Key Stage 4. A tier review in the first term of Year 10 is realistic; one in the spring of Year 11 usually is not, because the school has already submitted the entry.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Extended tier
programmes.description: The full syllabus content, the full grade range, and the papers that post-16 courses expect. Extended papers carry more multi-step questions, more questions set in unfamiliar contexts, and a heavier reliance on command words beyond state and describe. Most Cambridge IGCSE tuition in this emirate is Extended work.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi sixth forms and Diploma programmes routinely set subject-specific IGCSE entry grades, which is why an Extended grade in Mathematics or a science carries weight beyond the certificate itself. The grade gates a choice, and the choice is made before results arrive.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Where Cambridge IGCSE leads for most students who stay in the British system. The step up is less about new content than about sustained argument and unfamiliar application, and students who learned to read command words properly at IGCSE arrive able to do that. Students who did not spend Year 12 learning it late.
programmes.countryNote: The Ministry of Education's equivalency route for British-curriculum students requires one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae.

abu-dhabi/cambridge-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Each Cambridge syllabus loses marks in its own way. These are the numbered syllabuses Abu Dhabi families most often ask for, with the specific failure a session is usually bought to fix.

subjects.name: Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Marks are lost on method rather than on answers. Candidates who write only a final figure forfeit the working marks available when the figure is wrong, and candidates who round early lose accuracy marks on multi-step questions. The fix is mechanical and fast: write the method, keep full precision until the last line.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: A genuine step beyond 0580, with calculus and more demanding trigonometry and functions work. Students arrive able to execute procedures and unable to choose between them, so sessions concentrate on recognising which tool an unfamiliar question is asking for before any algebra starts.

subjects.name: Biology 0610
subjects.description: The highest-content syllabus of the three sciences and the one where strong students underperform most often, because knowing the material is not the same as answering the command word. Describe and explain questions on the same diagram want different answers, and the marks go to whoever noticed.

subjects.name: Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Two reliable problem areas: the quantitative work around moles and concentrations, where arithmetic discipline decides the mark, and organic chemistry, where students memorise reactions without the functional-group logic that makes unfamiliar examples answerable.

subjects.name: Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity and circuit analysis generate more enquiries in Abu Dhabi than any other physics topic, followed by anything requiring unit manipulation. Candidates lose marks for stating relationships qualitatively when the question wanted a calculation with units carried through.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: Three disciplines, one grade, less content per discipline than the separate syllabuses. The tuition risk is uneven coverage: a tutor strong in chemistry and weak in physics produces a student who is strong in a third of the paper. Confirm all three disciplines before booking.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language 0510
subjects.description: Reading and writing marks turn on task fulfilment, register and the number of distinct points made, not on vocabulary display. Students who write elaborately and address half the prompt score below students who write plainly and address all of it.

subjects.name: English First Language 0500
subjects.description: The directed writing and analysis components reward structural control. The commonest loss is a response that narrates the passage instead of analysing how it works, which is a planning habit rather than a knowledge gap and moves within a few sessions.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language 0508
subjects.description: Sits alongside the licensed international curriculum because private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic regardless of the programme they run. Tutors able to teach it to IGCSE standard are scarce relative to demand across the emirate, so continuity matters more than it does elsewhere.

subjects.name: Business Studies 0450 and Economics 0455
subjects.description: Definitions are the cheapest marks and the ceiling. Grades above the middle depend on application to the stimulus material and on evaluation that reaches a judgement, which is a writing discipline that can be taught directly from marked answers.

subjects.name: Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: Theory and practical problem solving reward different habits, and students are usually strong in one. Algorithm questions want pseudocode that someone else could execute, and marks are lost on unstated assumptions rather than on logic errors.

subjects.name: Accounting 0452
subjects.description: Format carries marks. Candidates who understand double entry but present statements loosely lose presentation and consistency marks across a whole paper, which is why drilling layout against marked answers moves a grade faster than more theory does.

sections.heading: The syllabus number is the first thing a Cambridge tutor should ask for
paragraphs: Cambridge examines syllabuses, and each one has a number. That number, with the year of the version, determines what is assessable, which components a candidate sits and how the marks divide. It is printed on the entry the school submits and on the statement of results, and it is the one piece of information that makes a tuition plan accurate rather than approximate. A tutor who starts teaching before establishing it is guessing, politely.

The practical reason this matters in Abu Dhabi is the spread of provision. One school in the Khalifa City corridor offers three separate sciences; a school a few minutes away offers Coordinated Sciences 0654 and nothing else. One offers English as a First Language 0500; another enters almost everyone for English as a Second Language 0510. A parent who buys tuition for the wrong one has bought practice on a paper their child will never sit, and the first anyone notices is usually a mock result that makes no sense.

Syllabuses are also revised. A past paper from several years ago may examine content that has since moved or been removed, and a revision plan built on old material wastes weeks. The fix is to confirm the current version on cambridgeinternational.org at the start, and then to work from the material the school has issued plus official practice. Nobody should be sending you a private library of syllabus documents, mark schemes or past papers: those are Cambridge copyright, and a provider distributing them is telling you how they operate. sections.heading: Command words are mark instructions, and most lost marks live here
paragraphs: Cambridge questions begin with a command word, and the word is not decoration. It states what the examiner will accept. A student who answers a describe question with an explanation has written something true and scored nothing, and a student who answers an explain question with a description has done the same. This is the single most common diagnosis in a first Cambridge session with an Abu Dhabi student, and it cuts across every subject.

The confusion is understandable, because in ordinary speech these words overlap. In Cambridge usage they do not. State wants a fact with no reasoning attached. Describe wants what happens or what is observed, in sequence, without causes. Explain wants the causal chain, and a response with no because in it rarely earns the marks. Suggest signals an unfamiliar context where the candidate must apply principles rather than recall an answer, and it is the command word strong students fear most because there is nothing to remember. Compare wants both sides addressed in the same sentence, not two paragraphs side by side. Calculate wants working, because the working carries marks even when the final figure is wrong.

The mark allocation is the second half of the instruction. A two-mark question wants two distinct creditable points, and padding wastes time that a later question needed. A six-mark question is telling a candidate that six separate things are available, and a three-line answer cannot contain them. Teaching a student to count the marks and plan that many points before writing is a technique fix rather than a content fix, which is why it moves grades inside a handful of sessions rather than a term.

sections.heading: Coordinated 0654, Combined 0653 or three separate sciences
paragraphs: This is the Cambridge decision that most changes a student's post-16 options in Abu Dhabi, and it is frequently made by timetable rather than by choice. Three separate syllabuses award three grades and cover the most content. Coordinated Sciences 0654 awards a double grade across all three disciplines with less content in each. Combined Science 0653 awards a single grade with lighter content again. All three are legitimate Cambridge routes; they open different doors.

Where it matters is the step into Year 12. A student intending to take a science at Advanced Level or Higher Level in the Diploma is usually better served by the separate syllabus in that discipline, because the content gap at the start of Year 12 is smaller and the habits of working are closer to what is coming. A student taking sciences to a sound pass and then moving towards humanities or business is often better served by Coordinated, which frees timetable space for another subject. Neither is a lesser choice in the abstract.

For tuition the decision has one concrete consequence. A combined route is taught by one teacher covering three disciplines, and a tutor booked for it must genuinely cover all three. Families routinely book a tutor whose strength is chemistry for a 0654 entry and discover in March that the physics third of the paper was never properly addressed. Ask the question directly before the first session, and if the honest answer is two disciplines out of three, book accordingly rather than hoping.
