abu-dhabi/certified-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: What a tutor needs to know differs by qualification, and so does the evidence worth asking for. These are the four routes Abu Dhabi families are hiring for, with the competence each one actually demands.

programmes.name: Cambridge International GCSE
programmes.description: Terminal papers against four-digit codes, with assessment objectives published per syllabus and weighted differently across subjects. Several syllabuses are tiered: Core papers and Extended papers lead to different grade ceilings. The competence test for a tutor is whether they can state the paper structure and the objective weightings for the specific code without looking them up.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge provision is the most widespread across Abu Dhabi's British curriculum schools, so most families here are hiring against a Cambridge code. Ask the school which code and which tier in writing, then ask a prospective tutor to describe the papers for it. A tutor who answers in general terms about the subject rather than specifically about the code is not yet qualified for the job you are hiring for.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4MB1 Mathematics B, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology and 4EA1 English Language A. Exams are available in May/June and November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. Paper structures and assessment wording differ from Cambridge even where the content overlaps.
programmes.countryNote: The specialist pool per subject is thinner inside Abu Dhabi than for Cambridge, which is where a credential claim deserves the most scrutiny. A tutor who has taught 0620 Chemistry for a decade is well qualified for 0620 and has to learn 4CH1's structure. Both facts can be true, and an honest tutor will say so rather than treat the two as interchangeable.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The usual continuation route, where subject depth narrows the credible tutor pool sharply. At this level a subject degree carries more weight than it does at IGCSE, because the content genuinely reaches undergraduate foundations in Further Mathematics, Physics and Economics. Teaching training still decides whether that knowledge reaches a seventeen-year-old.
programmes.countryNote: This is also the qualification UAE Ministry of Education equivalency asks for on the British track. The published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the five, plus one A-Level at no less than E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. Verify the current wording through the Ministry's own channel before planning around it.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across two levels plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, with an internally assessed component in every subject. The credential question is sharper here, because internal assessment criteria are detailed and subject-specific, and a tutor who has not worked with a particular subject's criteria will give plausible but unhelpful feedback.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools sit the May session. IB session and results dates are not published on these pages: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so nothing in this project has been confirmed from the board. Ask your school's IB coordinator or read ibo.org directly for any date. The academic-honesty boundary is also strictest here, and a tutor who offers to write any part of an internal assessment is a risk to the student, not a resource.

abu-dhabi/certified-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: A credential is only meaningful against a specific paper. These are the subjects Abu Dhabi families hire for, with what the assessment actually rewards and the question that tests whether a tutor knows it.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580, 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Marks split between method and accuracy, so unshown working forfeits credit even for a right answer. The test question for a tutor: what does the Core entry cap the grade at, and which topics appear only on the Extended papers? A tutor who cannot answer that will prepare a student for papers they will not sit.

subjects.name: Physics (0625, 4PH1)
subjects.description: Quantitative answers need units and sensible significant figures, and graph questions carry marks for axes and gradients as well as conclusions. Ask a tutor how the practical or alternative-to-practical component is assessed on your child's code; the answer differs between boards and is the clearest competence test in this subject.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620, 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations, organic mechanisms, state symbols and balanced equations. The presentation marks here are dense and cheap to recover, which is why chemistry responds well to a short block. Ask a tutor which equation conventions the mark scheme credits; a vague answer means the mark scheme has not been read recently.

subjects.name: Biology (0610, 4BI1)
subjects.description: The most command-word sensitive of the sciences. Describe and explain are marked differently, and a student who confuses them loses marks regardless of knowledge. A competent tutor will talk about assessment objectives and command words before talking about topics, because that is where the recoverable marks sit.

subjects.name: English First and Second Language (0500, 0510, 4EA1)
subjects.description: Two different qualifications often conflated by providers. First Language is directed writing and analysis against band descriptors; Second Language includes accuracy, range and the listening and speaking components. Hiring the wrong specialist is the most common credential mismatch in this subject across the market.

subjects.name: English Literature (0475, 4ET1)
subjects.description: Set-text dependent, so the only credential that matters is whether the tutor has taught your child's actual texts and the option papers the school entered. Essay argument and quotation use carry the marks. A tutor who asks for the text list before quoting a rate is demonstrating the right instinct.

subjects.name: Economics and Business (0455, 0450, 4EC1)
subjects.description: Evaluation marks are the largest recoverable block and the most frequently abandoned. Diagrams need labels, shifts and a stated direction of change. Ask a tutor how many marks a typical evaluation question carries on your child's paper and what distinguishes a top band response from a middle one.

subjects.name: History and Geography (0470, 0460)
subjects.description: Source utility and case-study specificity. A paragraph with a named example outscores a well-written generalisation every time. These are option-led papers, so a tutor must know which options the school entered before any preparation has value, and should ask you for that at the first contact.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences (0654, 0653)
subjects.description: Three strands in one qualification, and the credential question is whether one tutor can genuinely cover all three at the depth required. Many cannot, and the honest ones say so. Ask which strand they are strongest in and plan the hours accordingly rather than assuming equal coverage.

subjects.name: Additional and International Mathematics (0606, 0607)
subjects.description: A scarce specialism locally. 0607 carries its own structure and a graphic display calculator expectation, which is a specific technical competence rather than general maths ability. Ask which calculator model the tutor teaches with and how calculator-method marks are awarded on that paper.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (0478, 0417)
subjects.description: Pseudocode notation, trace tables and the practical component, where the mark scheme is particular about form. A professional developer who has not taught the syllabus will write better code and lose more marks than a trained teacher who has. This is the subject where a teaching credential matters most relative to industry experience.

subjects.name: Arabic (0508, 0544)
subjects.description: Taught alongside the licensed curriculum in every UAE private school. First Language and Foreign Language are separate syllabuses with separate expectations, and matching the wrong one is common. Arabic and Islamic Education are excluded from the five subjects counted for British-track Ministry equivalency.

sections.heading: What "certified" can legitimately mean in UAE tutoring
paragraphs: A certified IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi can hold three sorts of credential, and only one of them is a legal requirement. The MoHRE private tuition work permit is the requirement. A teaching qualification is a professional credential. Examiner experience is a claim about a past role. No exam board certifies private tutors, and no UAE authority maintains a register of approved individual tutors for parents to search.

The distinction matters because each one answers a different question and families routinely accept one as an answer to another. A tutor with a doctorate in chemistry has proved they understand chemistry; they have not proved they know what a 0620 mark scheme credits. A tutor with QTS has proved they were trained to teach a class of thirty; they have not proved they have taught your child's board. A tutor with a permit has proved they may lawfully charge for tutoring in the UAE, which says nothing about quality but a great deal about whether the arrangement is above board.

The table below is the version worth keeping. For each credential it sets out who issues it, what it genuinely demonstrates, what it does not, and the one thing a parent can do to check it. Most of those checks take minutes, and almost nobody performs them, which is why the claim is so freely made. Asking is not rude; a tutor who is irritated by a verification question has told you something useful.

A final note on how to read any provider's claims, including this page's. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or endorsement from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, operates no UAE centre or office, and delivers every UAE lesson one-to-one over live video. Any provider stating otherwise about itself should be asked to produce the permit or centre number, because those are specific documents issued to specific entities and either exist or do not.

sections.heading: The one certification that is actually required: the MoHRE work permit
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, it is granted free of charge for two years, and it carries a code of conduct. MoHRE's own service is listed as private tutor licensing, with no fee stated and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

The eligibility list is broader than most parents expect, and knowing it prevents two different mistakes. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. So a university student tutoring maths in Abu Dhabi is not operating outside the system by definition; they are eligible for the same permit a school teacher is. The question is whether they hold it.

What happens without one is stated plainly by the authorities and should not be embellished. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anyone, including by pages like this one. A figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source, and a provider who quotes one is making it up or repeating someone who did.

A business is a different legal animal from an individual. A tutoring operation with premises and staff needs an educational services permit for a training institute from the relevant authority, with initial approval first, a limited window to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested ahead of expiry. That is a specific document issued to a specific entity. IB Gram holds no such permit and operates no premises in the UAE, which is why it describes itself as an online tutor-matching platform and not as a centre.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE paper actually assesses, and where the marks go
paragraphs: A credential check tells you whom to hire. The rest of this page is about what they should then do. An IGCSE grade is the sum of marks awarded against published assessment objectives, and those objectives are weighted differently across subjects. Knowledge and recall is one objective; applying it to an unfamiliar context is another; analysing, evaluating and handling data is a third. A student can be strong on the first and lose most of the available marks on the others.

This is why content revision so often fails to move a grade. A student who has read the textbook twice has worked on one objective. The question that asks them to suggest why a result was unexpected, or to evaluate whether a policy achieved its aim, is testing something the textbook does not practise. The repair is not more content but a specific drill on the objective the marks are being lost against, which is a short piece of work with an outsized effect.

The table maps the component types a student will meet, what each is testing, where the marks typically go and what a session actually fixes. It is written generically across subjects because the objective weightings differ per syllabus; for your child's code, the published syllabus document states the exact split, and a tutor should be working from that document rather than from memory. The boards publish them, and so should any tutor be able to point you to the right one.

One boundary worth stating here. This page publishes no past papers, no mark schemes, no grade boundary tables and no syllabus documents, and it will not supply them. Those materials belong to Cambridge and Pearson, reproducing them is not ours to do, and a provider offering a library of them as a download is taking a risk with somebody else's copyright. The correct route is the board's own site or your child's school, and a good tutor works from the official current version because syllabuses are revised.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the entry that quietly caps the grade
paragraphs: Several Cambridge syllabuses are tiered, and the tier is the single most consequential administrative fact about a student's entry. Core papers and Extended papers cover different content and lead to different grade ceilings, so a student entered for Core cannot reach the top grades however well they perform. Families discover this at various points, and the later the discovery the more expensive it is.

The sequence that goes wrong looks like this. A student is placed in a Core set in Year 10 on the basis of Year 9 performance. The family hires a tutor in Year 11, the student improves substantially, and everyone assumes the improvement will show in the result. It cannot, beyond the ceiling. And by the time anyone checks, the entry deadline may have passed: Cambridge's March 2027 series, for example, has final entries due on 27 November 2026 for an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027.

So the first conversation with a school is not about tutoring at all. It is a request in writing for the syllabus code and the tier for every subject, and a question about what evidence the department would need to move a student from Core to Extended and by when. That conversation costs nothing in October. Having it in February means the answer no longer matters. A tutor who does not ask about the tier in the first session is not paying attention to the thing most likely to determine the outcome.

The parallel point on the Pearson side is the series choice rather than the tier, since tiering varies by subject. Pearson International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, so a resit is a visible option on a known timetable rather than a year's wait. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is a reminder that any date, including the ones on this page, should be confirmed against the live official timetable before anyone plans around it.

sections.heading: Which credential matters for which subject
paragraphs: The credential that helps most is subject-dependent, and this is where a generic certified claim is least useful. In Computer Science and ICT, a trained teacher who knows the pseudocode notation the mark scheme credits will outperform a professional developer, because the marks are awarded for form as much as function. In Further Mathematics or A-Level Physics, depth of subject knowledge genuinely matters, and a strong degree is worth more than it is at IGCSE.

In the sciences at IGCSE, the useful credential is specific experience of the practical or alternative-to-practical component on the relevant code, because that component is assessed differently between boards and is where unprepared students lose a concentrated block of marks. In English, the division is between First Language and Second Language, and a tutor fluent in the band descriptors for one is not automatically useful for the other. In Literature and the humanities, the only credential that counts is having taught the specific texts and option papers.

Examiner experience deserves its own paragraph because of how it is used. Where it is real, recent and in the relevant subject, it means someone has applied a mark scheme to hundreds of scripts and knows what the middle of a band looks like. That is genuinely valuable. What it does not mean, and must never be implied to mean, is access to unreleased papers, to grade boundaries before publication, or to any information not available to a school. We do not describe a tutor as an examiner unless the board, subject, series and year can be stated, and we would suggest you apply the same test to anybody else.

The practical shortcut, for a parent with limited time, is to ignore the list of credentials and ask three subject questions instead. What are the papers for my child's code, and what are they each worth? Where do most students lose marks on that paper? What would you do in the first three sessions? A tutor who answers those precisely has demonstrated more than any certificate does. A tutor who answers them in general terms about the subject has told you they have not yet looked at the syllabus.

sections.heading: Verifying a tutor without taking anybody's word for it
paragraphs: Verification in this market is unusually easy and unusually rare. Nothing on the list below requires a lawyer, a fee or more than a short exchange of messages, and together they eliminate the great majority of mismatches families later regret. The reason to do it before the first payment rather than after the first month is that a wrong match costs a term, and a term in Year 11 is not replaceable.

Start with the permit, because it is binary. Ask the tutor directly whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit and ask to see it. There is no awkwardness in the question: the permit is free, it takes a stated two working days to issue, and the eligibility categories are broad, so a willing tutor has no reason not to hold one. A refusal, or a long explanation about why it is not needed, is the answer to a different question.

Then test the subject claim with the three questions in the previous section, and ask for a marked example of a student script with the identifying details removed. A tutor who marks against the published mark scheme will have one. Next, confirm the practical arrangements in writing: the weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, what happens to a session cancelled at short notice, what you receive after each lesson, and what the replacement process is if the match does not work.

Finally, use the trial lesson as the real test, because it is the only one that observes teaching. Ask for a past-paper question to be attempted and marked inside it. Watch for three things: does the tutor let your child work, do they mark against the scheme rather than their own view, and can they name the specific mark-scheme point that was missed. Our trial is a full session on a real question, no card details are taken to book it, and nothing is owed if you stop there.

sections.heading: Abu Dhabi specifics: ADEK, school staff and the conflict nobody mentions
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi's private schools are overseen by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes inspection outcomes per school. Of the competitor tutoring pages reviewed for this project, not one named ADEK at all, which is a strange omission on pages aimed at Abu Dhabi parents. ADEK governs schools; it does not certify private tutors, and no tutoring provider can hold a tutor accreditation from it because no such instrument exists.

The Abu Dhabi fact that bears directly on hiring is the professional-ethics position for school staff. Press reporting on the emirate's rules describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and notes that teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. That is secondary reporting rather than a quotation from the current policy document, so verify it against ADEK's own published policy before relying on the exact wording.

The principle behind it is sound regardless of the precise drafting, and it is worth a parent's attention because the offer is made often. The person who sets and marks your child's school assessments should not also be paid to prepare them for those assessments. It compromises the assessment, it puts the teacher at professional risk, and it leaves the family holding an arrangement that may breach a code of conduct. If your child's own teacher offers private lessons, the right response is a question to the school rather than a transaction.

What this means for how we describe ourselves is simple and worth repeating once more. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, certified, licensed or endorsed by ADEK or by any other UAE authority or exam board, holds no educational services permit, operates no office or centre in the emirate, and does not offer home visits in the UAE. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. Where we name a regulator on this page, it is to explain what that body governs, nothing more.

sections.heading: What no certificate can tell you, and how to find it out in one session
paragraphs: Every credential on this page is a statement about the past. None of them predicts the thing that actually determines whether tutoring works, which is the fit between one adult and one teenager at 5pm on a Tuesday. A tutor can hold a permit, a PGCE, a first-class degree and genuine examiner experience, and still be the wrong person for a particular fifteen-year-old who needs to be asked questions rather than told answers.

What a single well-run session reveals is more diagnostic than a page of qualifications. Does the tutor spend the first ten minutes finding out what the student can already do, or does the lesson begin with an explanation? Does the student spend more of the session working than listening? When a mistake appears, does the tutor correct it or get the student to find it? Is the session's objective something the student could state afterwards in one sentence?

There is a specific test for honesty too, and it is worth watching for. Ask what the tutor thinks the realistic outcome is. The honest answer involves the marks-to-boundary distance from the school's own mock, a note that grade boundaries are set per series after papers are sat, and a description of what should visibly change in six sessions. A promised grade is the answer of someone selling rather than teaching, and it should end the conversation rather than reassure you.

So the recommendation this page ends on is a sequence rather than a credential. Confirm the syllabus code and tier with the school in writing. Ask any provider the five verification questions. Then take one trial lesson that contains a real past-paper question, marked, with the lost mark explained. Ours is free, takes no card details, and ends with the marked script in your hands. If the fit is wrong you will know within the hour, which is considerably faster than a certificate would have told you.

faqs.question: What does it mean for an IGCSE tutor to be certified in the UAE?
faqs.answer: It can mean three different things, and only one is a legal requirement. The requirement is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. The second is a teaching qualification such as QTS or a PGCE, which proves training in classroom teaching rather than knowledge of your child's board. The third is examiner experience, which is a claim about a past role. Ask which of the three is being claimed, because providers use the single word to cover all of them.

faqs.question: Is there an official IGCSE tutor certification anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge International does not issue a certificate to private tutors and neither does Pearson. There is no IGCSE tutoring qualification, no public register of approved individual tutors, and no authority that inspects a one-to-one lesson. What exists is the UAE work permit, generic teaching qualifications, and subject degrees. So the only useful test of subject competence available to a parent is to ask what the papers are for your child's syllabus code and what each one is worth, then listen to how precisely the question is answered.

faqs.question: How do I check a tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit?
faqs.answer: Ask the tutor directly and ask to see it. MoHRE's own service is listed as private tutor licensing, with a two-working-day completion time and no fee stated, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system. Because the permit is free, quick to obtain and open to a broad set of categories including school teachers, employees, unemployed residents and university students, a willing tutor has little reason not to hold one. A long explanation of why it is unnecessary is itself informative.

faqs.question: Does the private tutor permit cost anything in the UAE?
faqs.answer: No. The private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page for it lists no fees alongside a two-working-day completion time. That is consistent across every official source checked for this page. Anyone telling you the permit is expensive, or using its cost to justify a higher rate, is mistaken. On the other side of it, individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted as unverified.

faqs.question: Can a university student legally tutor IGCSE in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the permit. University students are expressly named among the eligible applicants for the MoHRE private tuition work permit, alongside registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals and school students aged 15 to 18. So the legal question is answered by whether they hold the permit, not by their age or occupation. The separate question is competence: a strong undergraduate may be excellent for Year 10 content and poor at paper technique, which is what the three subject questions on this page are designed to expose.

faqs.question: Should I insist on a tutor with QTS or a PGCE?
faqs.answer: Insist on it where the problem is how your child answers rather than what they know. Teacher training is specifically about explanation, sequencing and assessment, and those are the skills that fix command-word failure, unshown working and abandoned evaluation. Where the problem is genuine content depth at A-Level in Physics or Further Mathematics, a strong subject degree may matter more. In Computer Science and ICT, a trained teacher usually beats a professional developer, because the mark scheme credits notation as well as working code.

faqs.question: Are examiner-trained tutors worth the higher rate?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and only when the claim is specific. Where someone has genuinely marked a board's scripts recently in the relevant subject, they know what the middle of a band looks like, which is hard to learn any other way. Ask for the board, the subject, the series and the year. What examiner experience never means is access to unreleased papers, to boundaries before publication, or to anything a school cannot see, and any provider implying otherwise should be treated with scepticism. We do not describe a tutor as an examiner unless those four details can be stated.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a separate permit to teach online?
faqs.answer: The permit framework covers paid private tuition rather than a particular medium, so a tutor providing lessons to a family in the UAE should hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit regardless of whether the lesson happens over video. The permit carries a code of conduct that applies either way. Where a tutor is based outside the UAE entirely, the position is different and depends on their own jurisdiction, which is one reason we disclose where a tutor is based before you book rather than leaving the delivery location vague.

faqs.question: What qualification should an IGCSE science tutor hold?
faqs.answer: Subject knowledge at the level is a given; the differentiator is specific experience of the practical or alternative-to-practical component on your child's syllabus code, because that component is assessed differently between Cambridge and Pearson and is where unprepared students lose a concentrated block of marks. Ask how it is assessed on that code and what the common errors are. A tutor who answers with variable control, specific sources of error and the exact conventions the mark scheme credits has the relevant competence, whatever the certificate says.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a tutor really knows my child's syllabus code?
faqs.answer: Three questions, asked before any payment. What are the papers for this code and what is each one worth? Where do most students lose marks on that paper? What would you cover in the first three sessions? Precise answers that reference objective weightings, command words and specific question types show the syllabus has been read. General answers about the subject show it has not. A fourth question helps for tiered subjects: what does the Core entry cap the grade at, and which topics appear only on Extended papers?

faqs.question: What are the assessment objectives in an IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: They are the published categories a subject's marks are allocated against, typically covering knowledge and recall, applying knowledge to unfamiliar situations, and analysing, evaluating or handling data, with weightings that differ per syllabus. This is why reading the textbook twice often fails to move a grade: it practises one objective while the lost marks sit in another. The exact split for your child's code is stated in the board's published syllabus document, which is where a tutor should be working from rather than from memory.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Core and Extended entry?
faqs.answer: On several Cambridge syllabuses the papers are tiered, and the tier decides the highest grade available. Core papers cover less content and cap the grade; Extended papers carry additional topics and the full range. A student entered for Core cannot reach the top grades however well they are taught, which makes the tier the most consequential administrative fact about an entry. Ask the school in writing which tier applies per subject, and ask what evidence would support a move and by when, because entry deadlines close months before the papers.

faqs.question: Can a tutoring company hold a KHDA or ADEK licence?
faqs.answer: A business with premises and staff can hold an educational services permit for a training institute from the relevant emirate authority, which involves initial approval, a limited window to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal ahead of expiry. That is a document issued to a specific entity with a specific address. It is not a tutor accreditation and it says nothing about an individual online tutor. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE premises, and is not approved or endorsed by any UAE authority or exam board.

faqs.question: What should the first session show me about a tutor's competence?
faqs.answer: Four things. Whether the opening ten minutes are spent finding out what your child can already do rather than explaining. Whether your child works more than they listen. Whether a mistake gets corrected by the tutor or found by the student with a question. And whether the session had one objective your child could state afterwards in a sentence. Add one test of honesty: ask what the realistic outcome is. A marks-to-boundary estimate with a note that boundaries move per series is the right answer; a promised grade is not.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who teaches at my child's school allowed to tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: Press reporting on Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules describes a prohibition on school staff providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and notes that teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. That reporting is secondary, so check ADEK's current published policy rather than treating this as authoritative. The underlying principle holds either way: the person who sets and marks your child's assessments should not be paid to prepare them for them.

intro.heading: What the timetable covers, and what it quietly leaves to the student
paragraphs: The Corniche is apartment living along the island's north-western waterfront, and the households here are compact, mixed in nationality, and often within a fifteen-minute drive of school. Children walk or take a short ride to school, and parents are rarely negotiating with the traffic the outer communities contend with. Logistics are rarely the reason a family here looks for a tutor. The reason is almost always a gap in coverage: a component nobody has taught, a criterion nobody has explained, a paper the student has never sat under timed conditions.

That gap is structural rather than anyone's fault. A Diploma Programme subject typically gets four taught hours a week. In those hours a teacher has to cover the syllabus, set and review assessments, and manage thirty students. The Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the habit of writing a full paper in the time allowed all sit largely outside taught time. Schools set deadlines for them. Very few can afford to teach them line by line, and the ones that try do it with a lunchtime clinic rather than a lesson. The result is that the largest controllable block of marks in the Diploma is produced in whatever time a sixteen-year-old can find after everything else.

The same pattern runs through IGCSE. Content coverage is thorough. What tends to be thin is exam technique at the level of individual command terms, and the practice of sitting a complete paper to time rather than a set of questions over a week. Students who know the content and score below their ability are almost always losing marks in that second category, and the fix is a fortnight of marked papers rather than another pass through the syllabus.

So the useful question for a Corniche family is not whether the school is good. It is which specific pieces of work sit in the gap this term, and what each of them is marked out of. A student who knows that a sciences investigation is marked out of twenty-four across four named criteria, and that the evaluation criterion is where most of their class will lose marks, behaves differently from one who has been told to write up an experiment. That single sheet of information is free, it comes from the school, and asking for it costs one email.

This page is organised around that. There are tables on what class time covers and what it does not, on criterion letters and their mark allocations, on paper weightings at Higher and Standard Level, on a realistic week of independent study, on what filling the gap costs in AED, and on the formats available. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, which are a service we run only in India.

abu-dhabi/corniche.programmesIntro: Three programme routes appear in Corniche enquiries, and in each one the question is the same: which assessed component is nobody covering, and what is it worth. The answers differ sharply between them.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. The core carries up to three points on top of the subject grades. Internal Assessments are worth between twenty and thirty per cent of a subject grade depending on the course, which makes them the largest single block of marks a student controls directly.
programmes.countryNote: Corniche DP students mostly travel a short distance across the island or over a bridge to Al Reem or Saadiyat. Because the commute is manageable, the requests here are about components rather than scheduling: a sciences investigation that has stalled at the data-analysis stage, or a Paper 3 that has never been practised.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked from 0 to 8, with no terminal exam unless the school enters students for eAssessment. Reports show criterion letters, so a child can appear to be doing well on three criteria and be losing marks consistently on the fourth without that ever being named at home.
programmes.countryNote: The practical use of MYP for a Corniche family is as preparation. A student who has learned to read criterion descriptors in MYP 4 arrives in DP1 already able to work out what a task is marked on. That skill transfers directly, and it is the cheapest advantage available in the whole programme.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Assessed by terminal papers, with tiered entry in many Cambridge subjects. Syllabus codes decide what a tutor needs to know: Cambridge Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, Mathematics 0580, against Pearson International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 and Physics 4PH1. The command terms and the mark-scheme style differ between the two boards.
programmes.countryNote: The gap at IGCSE is almost always timed full-paper practice. Students in this district typically have thorough content coverage and no habit of writing for ninety minutes without stopping. Four complete papers, marked against the official scheme, usually move a grade more than four more topic lessons.

abu-dhabi/corniche.subjectsIntro: Each note below names the component where the marks sit, rather than describing the subject. That is the information a Corniche parent needs in order to ask the school a precise question at the next parents' evening.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The scientific investigation is marked out of twenty-four across four criteria, and the evaluation criterion is where whole classes lose marks together because it requires naming specific weaknesses in a method the student designed. Written papers punish imprecise language more than gaps in knowledge.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics and organic mechanisms carry the grade. In the investigation, the data-analysis criterion rewards honest uncertainty treatment, which costs planning time rather than equipment. A clear research question with a measurable variable scores more than an ambitious experiment with no quantifiable outcome.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · Cambridge 0625 · Pearson 4PH1
subjects.description: Electricity and fields are the recurring difficulty at every level. Students who can state the relationships still misread a circuit with a parallel pair inside a series loop. At Higher Level, induction demands sign conventions that are rarely enforced in class and always enforced in marking.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Standard Level, Papers 1 and 2 carry forty per cent each with the exploration at twenty. At Higher Level, Papers 1 and 2 drop to thirty each, Paper 3 takes twenty, and the exploration keeps twenty. Paper 3 supplies no method, which is why it is the component most often left unpractised.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Same weighting structure as the other route, different content. Marks are lost in the written interpretation rather than in the computation: a correct regression followed by a sentence that misstates what the gradient represents earns the calculation mark and nothing else.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The Internal Assessment is marked out of twenty-five, with fifteen of those marks in the investigation itself and six in source evaluation. Students narrate when they should argue. The Higher Level Paper 3 regional option is a large block of content that rewards early, systematic note-building.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries at eight hundred words each, each marked against a short set of criteria that explicitly rewards diagram accuracy and the use of a key concept. An unlabelled axis costs marks that no amount of evaluation recovers. Higher Level adds a quantitative paper worth a fifth of the grade.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: At Standard Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 carry thirty-five per cent each with the individual oral at thirty. Higher Level keeps Paper 1 at thirty-five, reduces Paper 2 to twenty-five, and adds the Higher Level essay at twenty. Paper 1 is where timing failures show up most clearly.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE)
subjects.description: The Extended tier reaches the top grades and includes functions, vectors and harder trigonometry. The hidden weakness in this district is non-calculator arithmetic, because students who have always had a device do not notice the gap until a paper forbids it.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay marked against a single global descriptor out of ten, capped at one thousand six hundred words, plus an exhibition with a commentary of nine hundred and fifty words across three objects. Almost nobody is taught how to structure either, which makes it one of the most recoverable parts of the Diploma.

abu-dhabi/corniche.regionsIntro: The Corniche sits at the top of the island, and its neighbours matter mainly because of where the schools are and how long the run takes. Each note is written from the point of view of a family living in a Corniche tower.

regions.name: Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Directly inland from the western end of the Corniche and effectively continuous with it. Many Corniche families use its services daily and share the same schools, so the two districts produce very similar component-level requests, mostly around timed paper practice.

regions.name: Al Markaziyah
regions.note: The central business district immediately behind the eastern Corniche, with a dense population in older towers. Students here walk or take a short ride to school, which means afternoon slots from 16:00 Gulf Standard Time are genuinely workable rather than theoretical.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: South along the island's western shore, ten to fifteen minutes from the Corniche. A more established and more bilingual district, which is why Arabic as a first language appears far more often in its requests than in those from the Corniche towers.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Across the island to the east and home to The British International School Abu Dhabi and Repton Abu Dhabi. For a Corniche family this is a twenty-five to thirty-five minute afternoon run, which puts lesson slots at 17:30 or later for students at those schools.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Reached by bridge from the island's northern side, home to Cranleigh Abu Dhabi. The run is manageable in the morning and slower at pick-up, so Diploma Programme students at that school tend to prefer later evening sessions for component work.

regions.name: Al Mushrif
regions.note: Inland and south, where The British School Al Khubairat sits. One of the shorter runs from the Corniche, which is why a reasonable number of Corniche families use it and why their enquiries concentrate on IGCSE technique rather than on scheduling.

regions.name: Al Zahiyah
regions.note: East along the waterfront from the Corniche, a dense older district of apartment blocks. Students there sit the same papers and share the same component gaps, and the shared bus routes mean afternoon timings run almost in parallel with the Corniche.

schoolClusters.city: Schools within a short run of the Corniche
schoolClusters.note: These are the campuses Corniche families reach most easily, and they cover British, American and IB Diploma provision. Because the commute is short, enquiries from this group are about specific assessed components rather than about fitting a lesson into the evening at all.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Bridge and cross-island schools
schoolClusters.note: A substantial group of Corniche Diploma students travels to Al Reem or Saadiyat. Those schools set their own internal deadline calendars for Internal Assessments and the Extended Essay, and component support has to be planned from that calendar rather than from the board's final dates.

abu-dhabi/corniche.modesIntro: Because Corniche requests are component-shaped rather than open-ended, these formats are defined by what is being produced and when it is due rather than by a weekly habit.

modes.title: Component block
modes.description: A fixed run of sessions aimed at one assessed component: a sciences investigation, a Paper 3, a Theory of Knowledge essay. The block starts with the criteria and the mark allocation, works through the student's own material, and ends when the component is submitted or the paper is sat.

modes.title: Timed paper programme
modes.description: Weekly sessions built around sitting complete past papers to time and marking them against the official scheme. The teaching happens in the marking, where a student sees exactly which words earned a mark and which did not. This is the format that moves IGCSE grades fastest in this district.

modes.description: One or two sixty-minute sessions a week running alongside the school's scheme of work, for a student who is coping but drifting. sections.heading: The coverage gap, measured rather than asserted
paragraphs: The direct answer first: in a typical Diploma Programme timetable a subject receives about four taught hours a week, and the assessed work a student must produce outside those hours includes an Internal Assessment worth a fifth to a quarter of the subject grade, a four-thousand-word Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, and enough timed paper practice to be fluent in three different paper formats.

No school can teach all of that inside contact time, and the better ones do not pretend to. What they do is set deadlines, provide a supervisor, and expect the student to manage the work. For a self-organised student that is fine. For most sixteen-year-olds it means the largest controllable block of marks in the Diploma gets produced in the last available fortnight.

At IGCSE the gap is narrower but sharper. Content coverage is usually complete. What is missing is the skill of writing a full paper in the time allowed and of answering the command term that was actually used. A student who writes everything they know in response to a question asking them to explain one factor has demonstrated knowledge and scored two marks out of six.

The table below splits the work into what class time reliably covers and what it does not. Use it to ask the school a specific question, which is more useful than asking whether your child needs a tutor. The honest answer to that second question is often no, as long as somebody is covering the right-hand column.

sections.heading: Criterion letters and what each one is actually worth
paragraphs: This is the most useful page of information a Diploma student can be given, and almost nobody gives it to them. Internally assessed work is marked against named criteria with published mark allocations. A student who knows that a sciences investigation carries twenty-four marks split evenly across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation will spend their time differently from one who thinks the experiment is the point.

The pattern repeats with different shapes in different subjects. A Mathematics exploration is marked out of twenty, with six of those marks for the use of mathematics and only three each for personal engagement and reflection, which is why a beautifully written exploration with thin mathematics underperforms. A History Internal Assessment puts fifteen of its twenty-five marks in the investigation itself. The Extended Essay carries thirty-four marks, twelve of them for critical thinking alone.

Two practical consequences follow. First, read the criteria before choosing the question, because some questions cannot score well on the heaviest criterion no matter how carefully they are executed. Second, when a draft comes back with a mark, ask which criterion lost the marks rather than how to improve generally. Teachers answer the specific question readily and the general one vaguely, because the general one has no answer.

Confirm every figure below against the current subject guide through your school's IB coordinator. Subject guides are revised on a cycle, this page does not republish board documents, and a mark allocation that was right two years ago may not be right now.

sections.heading: Paper weightings at Higher and Standard Level
paragraphs: Weightings decide where revision time should go, and students consistently guess them wrong. A Higher Level Mathematics candidate who spends equal time on all three papers has over-invested in two of them and under-invested in the one that supplies no method. A Standard Level English candidate who neglects the individual oral has neglected thirty per cent of the grade.

The structure also changes between levels in ways that surprise families. In Mathematics, moving from Standard to Higher Level does not just add content: Papers 1 and 2 fall from forty per cent each to thirty, and a new Paper 3 takes twenty. In History, the Higher Level Paper 3 regional option takes thirty-five per cent, which is the largest single component in the course and the one most often started late.

Internal Assessment weight is the other number worth knowing. In most Diploma sciences the investigation is twenty per cent of the final grade, and in History the Internal Assessment is a quarter at Standard Level. That is a fifth to a quarter of the result produced under no time pressure, with the criteria published in advance. Treating it as a side project is the most common avoidable loss in the whole programme.

sections.heading: A week of independent study that survives a Corniche evening
paragraphs: Most study plans fail because they assume a student has four clear evenings. In practice a Corniche household has a short commute, a flat with one quiet surface, siblings, and a Diploma student who is tired by 21:00. A plan that ignores that produces guilt rather than work.

The version that holds is built from short, named blocks with a deliverable at the end of each. Ninety minutes is the longest useful block for most sixteen-year-olds, and forty-five is enough to produce something. The deliverable matters more than the duration: a block that ends with three marked exam questions is work, while a block that ends with reading over notes is a feeling.

The weekend is where the heavy components fit. A full paper to time needs an unbroken two hours and a mood nobody has on a Tuesday, so Saturday morning is where it belongs. Internal Assessment work is the same: data analysis and drafting need continuity, and twenty-minute fragments across a week produce a document that reads as though it was written by five people.

One more constraint is specific to apartment living. A flat usually has one quiet working surface, and it is often the same table the family eats at, so a block has to start and finish rather than sprawl. Students who agree a start time with the household get more done than students who intend to work all evening.

The table is a template rather than a prescription. Change the days to fit the household. Keep two features: every block names a deliverable, and the heavy timed work sits at the weekend rather than at the end of a school day.

sections.heading: Past papers: using them so they teach something
paragraphs: Past papers are the most powerful revision tool available and the most commonly wasted. The standard failure is to work through a paper with the mark scheme open, score most of it, feel reassured, and learn nothing. That is reading, not practice, and it predicts an exam result poorly.

The version that works has three rules. Sit the paper to time, in one sitting, with nothing open. Mark it yourself against the official scheme afterwards, writing the reason next to every lost mark rather than the correct answer. Then record the reason in a running list, because almost every student has three recurring errors and does not know what they are.

The reasons cluster predictably. Misreading the command term. Running out of time on the last long question. Omitting units. Answering a question about one factor by writing about three. None of those are knowledge problems, and all of them are fixable in a fortnight once they have been named. This is the whole content of what a good tutor does in a timed paper programme.

On sourcing, work from official material through the school. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards that publish them, and the right approach is to use the official source and cite it rather than to circulate copies. IB Gram does not host or supply board documents as downloads, and a provider offering a library of them is a signal rather than a convenience.

sections.heading: What filling the gap costs in AED, and how many sessions it takes
paragraphs: The figures here are market rates in the UAE, taken from providers' own published pricing and from a published 2026 Dubai tutoring rate survey by Bestimate. They are the market, not an IB Gram price list. The reason to show them on a page about coverage gaps is that component work is finite: a Theory of Knowledge essay block is four sessions, not a year, and the cost should be judged that way.

The published hourly spread is wide enough to be worth reading carefully. At the budget online end the figures run roughly AED 45 to 65, with one platform entering at AED 33 to 52. An agency that publishes its rates lists AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB; a UK-based agency quotes AED 270; survey data puts specialist exam-year work at AED 200 to 450 and above; and the premium named end reaches AED 650. In-home visits in the emirate are published between roughly AED 180 and AED 500, travel included inside the hour.

Converting those hourly figures into the monthly commitment a Corniche family actually signs is the more useful exercise. Eight online sessions appear at around AED 799 a month, against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. A weekly one-hour slot comes to roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at budget level, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or beyond for specialist exam-year support.

The second column of the table is the one worth arguing about with a provider. A component block has a defensible length. If a quote for Theory of Knowledge support runs to twenty sessions, ask what happens in sessions nine to twenty, because the essay is one thousand six hundred words long.

sections.heading: An in-home tutor on the Corniche compared with online delivery
paragraphs: Families searching for a home tutor along the Corniche have a reasonable case to consider. The district is central, the roads are short, and a tutor based on the island can reach most Corniche addresses quickly. Unlike the outer communities, travel time is not the main objection here.

The objection that does apply is matching. The work described on this page is component-shaped: Criterion D in a sciences investigation, Paper 3 in Analysis and Approaches, the structure of a Theory of Knowledge essay. Those are taught well by a relatively small number of people. Restricting the choice to those willing to visit a Corniche tower at 18:00 on a Wednesday narrows it for no academic reason.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE, and does not run a centre in the emirate. Delivery is one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for marking a paper line by line. For this kind of work the shared screen is a genuine advantage rather than a compromise, because both people annotate the same document and the student keeps the annotated copy.

There is also a continuity argument that matters in a district of rented apartments. Households here move between buildings and between emirates more often than villa families do, and an online tutor does not change when the address does. In the term before a terminal paper, that is worth more than any other form of stability.

The table sets out where each format wins. In-home provision has a real advantage for younger children who need an adult present to stay on task, and that is worth saying plainly on a page that recommends something else.

sections.heading: When the gap feels too wide: the academic honesty line
paragraphs: The pressure described on this page is exactly the pressure that produces academic misconduct, and it is worth naming directly. A student three weeks from an Internal Assessment deadline with no data is in the situation where an offer to supply a finished document becomes tempting. Providers in this market do sell that, and one researched competitor sells completed Internal Assessments outright.

The consequence falls on the student. Assessed coursework must be the student's own, and a malpractice finding can cost a diploma rather than a grade. No provider shares that risk, and none of them carries it after the fact. The boundary is therefore not a matter of taste.

What a tutor can do is substantial. Explain how each criterion is awarded and what the marks reward. Ask the questions a supervisor asks about scope, method and evidence. Read a draft the student has written and say precisely why a section will not score. Teach the referencing convention. None of that involves supplying text, data or analysis that enters a submission, and all of it moves marks.

There is a second practical protection, which is to involve the supervisor early. Schools deal with an honest problem, including an experiment that produced nothing usable, far better than they deal with a late one. A student who reports a failed method six weeks out gets help; a student who reports it the night before a deadline gets a deadline.

The real protection is the calendar. An Internal Assessment planned across three months is a manageable project with room for a failed experiment. The same work compressed into three weeks is the situation this section is about. Booking component support early is a cheaper form of integrity insurance than any policy.
bullets: A tutor explains criteria, questions the method, and feeds back on existing drafts
A tutor supplies no text, data or analysis for a submission
A malpractice finding costs the student, not the provider
Early planning removes most of the pressure that creates the problem

process.title: Name the component, not the subject
process.description: The fastest first message says which piece of work is the problem: the sciences investigation at the data-analysis stage, Paper 3 in Analysis and Approaches, the Theory of Knowledge essay. A component request can be matched in a day or two. A request for help with chemistry generally takes a diagnostic session to turn into the same thing.

process.title: Send the criteria and the internal deadline
process.description: Ask the school for the criterion descriptors the work will be marked against and the internal deadline, which is often weeks before the board's. Those two documents let a tutor plan the block backwards and tell you how many sessions it should take before you commit to any of them.

process.title: Sit one full paper before the first session
process.description: A complete past paper written to time, unmarked, is the single most informative thing a Corniche student can bring to a first session. It shows whether the problem is content, timing or command terms, which are three different jobs. A predicted grade shows none of that.

process.title: Agree the deliverable for each session
process.description: Every session should end with something that exists: a marked set of questions, a redrafted section, a recorded error pattern. Agreeing that at the start prevents the drift into general revision that makes a block of ten sessions feel like nothing happened.

process.title: Stop when the component is done
process.description: A component block has an end. When the investigation is submitted or the paper is sat, stop, review whether anything else sits in the gap, and start a new block only if it does. Rolling support that nobody evaluates is how tutoring becomes a standing cost rather than a fix.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the component, not the subject label
whyPoints.description: A tutor who teaches Paper 2 well is not automatically useful on a sciences evaluation criterion. Matching names the component, which is why a request from a Corniche family usually turns into teaching within a couple of working days rather than after a diagnostic month.

whyPoints.title: Criteria and weightings explained in the first session
whyPoints.description: Students are told what their work is marked out of, criterion by criterion, with the mark allocation. That single piece of information changes how they spend their own study time, which is worth more over two years than the sessions themselves.

whyPoints.title: Marking on a shared screen, not a verdict
whyPoints.description: Papers are marked line by line against the official scheme with the reason written next to each lost mark, and the student keeps the annotated copy. The teaching is in the marking, which is the part most revision programmes skip.

whyPoints.title: Blocks with an end date
whyPoints.description: Component work is finite and is quoted that way. A Theory of Knowledge essay is a short block, not a term. Being told how many sessions something should take is a reasonable thing to expect before paying for any of them.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: This page says exactly what a tutor may and may not do with assessed coursework, because the pressure described here is the pressure that produces misconduct. Official papers and mark schemes are cited and linked rather than redistributed.

faqs.question: How much of a Diploma subject is taught in class, and how much is left to my child?
faqs.answer: A Diploma subject typically gets around four taught hours a week, which covers the syllabus, some assessment review and class management. Outside that sit the Internal Assessment, worth a fifth to a quarter of the subject grade, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, and the timed full-paper practice that builds exam fluency. Schools set deadlines for these and provide supervision, but very few can teach them line by line. For a Corniche family the useful question is which of those pieces is unsupported this term, not whether the school is good.

faqs.question: What is my child's Internal Assessment actually marked out of?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject, and knowing the number changes behaviour. A Diploma sciences investigation carries twenty-four marks split evenly across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. A Mathematics exploration carries twenty, six of them for the use of mathematics. A History Internal Assessment carries twenty-five, fifteen of those in the investigation itself. Ask the school for the criterion descriptors and confirm the allocation against the current subject guide, because guides are revised on a cycle and this page does not republish board documents.

faqs.question: Why do whole classes lose marks on the evaluation criterion?
faqs.answer: Because it asks for something uncomfortable: naming the specific weaknesses in a method the student designed themselves. Most students write a general paragraph about human error and more repeats. That scores poorly. What scores is identifying a named limitation in the actual procedure, explaining how it affected the data in a stated direction, and proposing a concrete improvement. It is a teachable skill and a short piece of work, which is why it is one of the most recoverable blocks of marks in the whole Diploma.

faqs.question: How are the papers weighted at Higher Level compared with Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Not just by adding content. In Mathematics, Standard Level splits forty per cent to Paper 1, forty to Paper 2 and twenty to the exploration, while Higher Level drops the first two to thirty each and adds Paper 3 at twenty. In History, the Higher Level Paper 3 regional option carries thirty-five per cent and is the largest single component in the course. In English A, the Higher Level essay takes twenty per cent that Standard Level does not have. Confirm current weightings against the subject guide before building a revision timetable from them.

faqs.question: Which component do Higher Level Mathematics students most often leave unpractised?
faqs.answer: Paper 3, almost without exception. It is worth a fifth of the Higher Level grade and it supplies no method, so a student has to choose the route through an extended problem themselves. Papers 1 and 2 ask questions whose shape hints at the technique. Paper 3 does not, which exposes anyone who has learned procedures without the reasoning underneath. Practice means unfamiliar extended problems with the solution withheld, which is slow and unsatisfying work and the reason this is usually an eight to twelve session block rather than a quick fix.

faqs.question: What does a workable study week look like for a student in a Corniche apartment?
faqs.answer: Short named blocks on weekdays and the heavy work at the weekend. Forty-five to sixty minutes is the realistic weekday block, and each one should end with something that exists: three marked questions, one advanced Internal Assessment section, two corrected answers with the reason noted. A full past paper to time needs an unbroken two hours and belongs on a Saturday morning, with Sunday used to mark it and record the error pattern. Plans that assume four clear evenings produce guilt rather than work.

faqs.question: How should past papers be used so they actually help?
faqs.answer: Three rules. Sit the paper to time, in one sitting, with nothing open, because working through a paper with the mark scheme visible is reading rather than practice. Mark it yourself afterwards against the official scheme, writing the reason next to each lost mark instead of the correct answer. Then keep a running list of those reasons, because almost every student has three recurring errors and does not know what they are. Misread command terms, missing units and running out of time account for most of them.

faqs.question: Can we get past papers and mark schemes from a tutoring provider?
faqs.answer: You should not need to, and a provider offering a library of them is a warning rather than a convenience. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards that publish them, so the correct route is through your child's school, which holds proper access, and through the boards' own official pages. IB Gram does not host or supply board documents as downloads. Sessions work from material the student brings from school, cited to its official source.

faqs.question: Does a tutor on the Corniche need to visit our apartment to mark a paper?
faqs.answer: No, and for this particular job a shared screen is arguably better. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, so Corniche lessons are one-to-one over live video. Both people annotate the same paper, the reason for each lost mark is typed next to it, and the student keeps the annotated copy to work from afterwards. In-home tutoring does exist in Abu Dhabi, with published market rates from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, and it suits younger children who need an adult physically present.

faqs.question: How many sessions should a Theory of Knowledge essay block take?
faqs.answer: Usually three to five. The essay is capped at one thousand six hundred words and is marked against a single global descriptor out of ten, so the work is structural: identifying two or three defensible knowledge claims, finding real examples, and building an argument that does not merely restate the prompt. If a provider quotes twenty sessions for this component, ask what happens in sessions nine to twenty. A block with a defensible length is a reasonable thing to ask for before paying.

faqs.question: What does component work cost in Abu Dhabi, in AED?
faqs.answer: Published market rates run from roughly AED 45 to 65 an hour at the budget online end, AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB from an agency that publishes its rates, AED 270 from a UK-based agency, and a survey band of AED 200 to 450 and above for specialist exam-year work, with AED 650 at the premium named end. In-home visits in the emirate are published between AED 180 and AED 500 with travel inside the hour. Those are market figures, not an IB Gram price list, and they are worth judging per block rather than per hour.

faqs.question: My child knows the content but keeps scoring below expectation. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Almost always technique rather than knowledge. The pattern in this district is a student with thorough content coverage and no habit of writing a complete paper in the time allowed. The three usual causes are misreading the command term, so a question asking for one factor gets an essay on three; running out of time on the final long question; and omitting units or working. All three are visible in one marked paper and fixable in a fortnight once named. Sitting a full paper before any tutoring starts identifies which applies.

faqs.question: Is a mock exam result a reliable prediction?
faqs.answer: It is reliable evidence about the paper the student sat and much weaker evidence about the one they will sit. A mock is usually a past paper, often sat in a different order from the real series, sometimes with a narrower content range because the course is unfinished. What a mock tells you accurately is the error pattern: timing, command terms, which topics collapse under pressure. Read it for that rather than for the grade, and ask the subject teacher which criteria or questions the marks were lost on.

faqs.question: My child is three weeks from an Internal Assessment deadline with no data. What now?
faqs.answer: Triage, honestly, and avoid the obvious trap. Providers in this market do sell finished coursework, and a malpractice finding falls on the student and can cost a diploma rather than a grade. What works instead is narrowing the investigation to something answerable with available data, accepting a weaker research design mark in exchange for a complete conclusion and evaluation, and spending the remaining time on the criteria that can still be earned. Then talk to the supervisor early rather than the night before. Schools handle an honest problem far better than a late one.

abu-dhabi/corniche.closingHeading: Name the component and the deadline, and the rest is schedulable
abu-dhabi/corniche.closingBody: Enquiries from the Corniche are rarely about logistics, because the commute here is short. They are about a specific piece of assessed work that nobody has had time to teach: a criterion, a paper, an essay with a word limit. Those have defined lengths and defined criteria, which makes them schedulable and makes the cost judgeable per block rather than per term. Send the component, the criterion descriptors and the school's internal deadline, and lessons start one-to-one over live video with a shared screen for marking.

abu-dhabi/eastern-mangroves.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are matched for transfer work: establishing what a new arrival has actually covered, bridging the gap to the cohort they have joined, and holding the first coursework deadline that lands before they have settled. Subject and board are confirmed before a single lesson is booked.

intro.heading: A residence district, a shorter tenancy and a school year already in progress
paragraphs: Eastern Mangroves sits on the north-eastern edge of Abu Dhabi island, on the channel facing the mangrove reserve, close to Al Salam Street and the Al Zahiyah and Al Nahyan districts behind it. It is apartments, serviced residences and hotel apartments rather than villa compounds, and that housing stock selects for a particular kind of household: professionals on project contracts, consular and institutional staff, newly arrived families waiting on a longer lease, and families deliberately keeping their commitments short while they work out where to settle.

The academic consequence is arrival timing. In a villa community most children start in September with everybody else. Here a meaningful share of students join in November, February or April, into a cohort that has already covered a term or two of a two-year course. The school absorbs them well enough. What the school cannot do is reconstruct, subject by subject, what that particular child was taught at their previous school and what they therefore missed, because nobody has the hours for that work across every new arrival.

That reconstruction is the single most valuable thing an outside tutor does for a household in this district, and it is cheap. One diagnostic hour per subject, built around the last work the previous school marked, produces a list of named topics rather than a vague sense that the child is behind. Families who skip it buy a term of lessons and spend half of it re-teaching material the child already knew.

Transfers also raise questions no settled family ever asks. Whether an IGCSE taken at a school in Singapore counts towards the Ministry of Education's equivalency file. Whether a student who did two years of the Middle Years Programme can enter a British Year 11 and sit IGCSEs in nine months. What happens when a family arrives after the entry deadline for a session has closed, which is a date that sits months before the exam rather than weeks. Those questions have answers, and they are published on this page because the market does not publish them anywhere.

There is a second pattern worth naming, because it changes what a family should buy. Mobile households tend to under-invest in the first weeks and over-invest in the third month, once a poor set of grades has arrived. The grades are usually a reporting artefact rather than a verdict: a student assessed in January on material covered in October will score badly whatever their ability, and the honest response is a topic map, not four subjects of tuition. Families who understand that sequence spend less and get further.

Tuition itself is delivered as one-to-one online lessons over live video. For a household in a serviced apartment with no study and a possible move in six months, a format that needs no travel, no fixed address and no notice period is the practical one as well as the one we offer. It also means the same tutor and the same weekly hour survive a change of building, a month in a hotel between leases, and in many cases a move to another country entirely.

Mid-year arrivals are normal here rather than exceptional
The first task is a topic-level map of what was missed, not a general catch-up block
Entry deadlines for a session sit months before the papers, and transfers miss them
