abu-dhabi/eastern-mangroves.programmesIntro: Arrivals here come from every direction, so the programme notes below are written from the point of view of a student joining part-way rather than one who started with the cohort.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups marked against four criteria lettered A to D, each out of eight, assessing process as much as content. A student arriving from a content-and-exams system finds the marking unfamiliar before they find the material difficult, and their first reports look worse than their understanding warrants.
programmes.countryNote: A student joining the MYP mid-year from a British or Indian system typically has stronger content and weaker criterion literacy. The quickest win is teaching them what criterion B actually asks for in their new school's rubric, which is usually a two-session job rather than a term of subject tuition.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Entry part-way into the first year is possible; entry part-way into the second is extremely difficult, because the internal assessments and the core are already in progress with school deadlines attached.
programmes.countryNote: For an Eastern Mangroves family arriving in the Diploma, the urgent items are not lessons. They are the internal assessment timetable the new school has already set, the Extended Essay supervisor allocation and the subject combination, since a Higher Level subject the previous school did not offer cannot simply be picked up in February.

programmes.name: IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both run here and their papers differ even where the subject matches. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 has a Core tier on papers 1 and 3 capped at grade C and an Extended tier on papers 2 and 4 reaching A*; Pearson 4MA1 tiers as Foundation and Higher.
programmes.countryNote: A transfer between boards mid-course is the trap. The same subject name conceals different papers, different tiering and sometimes different content emphasis, and a student who revises the wrong board's material for three months has lost the term. Confirming the board and tier in writing is the first thing to do on arrival.

programmes.name: A Level
programmes.description: Linear qualifications with all assessment at the end of the course and almost no coursework in most subjects. A narrow, deep route in three or four subjects, which makes it easier to join late than the Diploma, since there is no core and fewer internally assessed components already under way.
programmes.countryNote: For families expecting another relocation within two years, the A Level route is often the more portable choice, and it is accepted on the Ministry's British track alongside the IGCSE requirement. The Ministry asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

abu-dhabi/eastern-mangroves.subjectsIntro: New arrivals ask for help in a predictable set of subjects, usually because the previous school sequenced the content differently rather than because the child is weak.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Standard Level sits two papers at 40% each with a 20% exploration; Higher Level adds Paper 3. Transfer students most often arrive missing the proof and complex-number material, because different systems place it in different years, and it compounds quickly if unnoticed.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with the graphic display calculator in constant use. Students arriving from a system that banned calculators for most of the course are at a technical disadvantage that is purely mechanical and closes in a few focused sessions.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE)
subjects.description: The decision that matters for an arrival is the tier, because Core caps at grade C. That decision belongs to the school but should be informed by marked evidence from the previous one, not by a first impression formed in week two.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Papers 1 and 2 carry 36% and 44% in the Diploma with a 20% investigation. Transfers typically have the mechanics and lack the written explanation discipline, since many systems reward the numerical answer alone.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are where Higher Level marks sit, and they are also where curricula diverge most in sequencing. An arriving student often knows a later topic and not an earlier one, which looks like confusion and is actually a gap in order.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Built on unifying themes with heavy use of unseen contexts in Paper 2. Students from recall-based systems lose marks by describing rather than explaining, which is a technique issue a tutor can address in weeks rather than months.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis in Paper 1, comparative essay in Paper 2, the Individual Oral at 30% of Standard Level. Arrivals often have to pick up set texts the cohort read last term, and prioritising which ones matter for Paper 2 saves considerable wasted reading.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Reading, writing and listening with register control carrying more weight than vocabulary range. For a mid-year arrival from a non-English-medium system this is often the subject where an outside hour has the quickest visible effect.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Both carry internally assessed components, the Economics portfolio of three commentaries and the Business project, with school deadlines that do not pause for an arrival. These are the components a transfer student most often finds already half-elapsed.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the international programme under the federal curriculum rules, and a genuine surprise to most arrivals. The gap for a newcomer is script fluency rather than vocabulary, and starting at the right level matters more than starting fast.

abu-dhabi/eastern-mangroves.regionsIntro: This part of the island runs into several adjoining districts, and a new family's school options are shaped by which of them they can reach in the morning.

regions.name: Al Zahiyah
regions.note: The district immediately behind Eastern Mangroves, dense and central, with a mix of apartment housing and older school provision. Short school runs are possible here, which is one reason arriving families often place children locally before reassessing.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: Across the island to the west, with Al Bateen Academy and the American Community School. The drive crosses the city rather than the corniche, so it is manageable at school times and slower in the late afternoon.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Reached by bridge from the eastern side, with its own apartment-based school provision. A frequent choice for arriving families because leases are plentiful and several schools sit inside the development itself.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: North across the channel, anchored by Cranleigh Abu Dhabi. Strong Diploma provision and a realistic commute from here, which makes it one of the two districts arriving Diploma families most often look at first.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: The deepest school cluster in the emirate, out along the highway. Families arriving mid-year often find availability here when island schools are full, at the cost of a long daily run.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Villa community built around a full IB continuum school. Relevant to arriving families who want PYP, MYP and DP under one roof, which reduces the number of transitions a mobile household has to manage.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Mainland district with substantial Indian and Pakistani curriculum provision. The usual destination for households arriving from South Asia who want to keep a national board for a year before moving to IGCSE.

regions.name: the Corniche
regions.note: The western waterfront route most Eastern Mangroves families use for cross-island school runs. Useful to know that the late afternoon stretch is where the evening disappears, which decides the earliest honest session time.

schoolClusters.city: Central and eastern Abu Dhabi island
schoolClusters.note: The schools within a short run of Eastern Mangroves, covering British, American, IB and Indian-board routes. For an arriving family this is where immediate availability is usually found, since island capacity turns over with the expatriate cycle.

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat, Al Raha and Khalifa City
schoolClusters.note: The wider set an arriving family considers once the immediate placement is settled, and the one with the deepest Higher Level Diploma provision in the emirate. These are the schools most often named when a transfer student needs a specific subject combination.

abu-dhabi/eastern-mangroves.modesIntro: Transfer work has a shape: diagnose, bridge, then settle into something sustainable. The three patterns below follow that sequence rather than offering a menu.

modes.title: Diagnostic hour per subject
modes.description: One session per subject, built around the last work the previous school marked, producing a named list of topics covered and topics missed. This is the purchase that should come before any block of lessons, and for some families it turns out to be the only purchase needed.

modes.title: Bridging block
modes.description: A short, dense sequence targeting only the named gaps, usually six to ten sessions across one or two subjects. The aim is to bring the student level with the cohort on specific topics, then stop, rather than to run an open-ended arrangement that outlives its purpose.

Continuity of tutor matters more for a mobile student than for a settled one, because they have already lost it at school.

sections.heading: What the first six weeks after an arrival should actually do
paragraphs: The instinct on arrival is to book lessons in everything, and it is the wrong first move. A new student is simultaneously managing an unfamiliar curriculum, an unfamiliar marking system, a new social group and often a new language of instruction at the margins. Loading four subjects of tuition onto that produces exhaustion and very little measurable change.

A better six weeks looks like this. Week one: collect the paperwork. Previous school reports, the last marked work in every subject, the syllabus or scheme of work from the old school if obtainable, and the new school's confirmation of board and tier per subject. Weeks two and three: one diagnostic session per subject that matters, producing a topic-level list of what was and was not covered. Weeks four to six: a bridging block on the one or two subjects where the gaps are real, while the student settles into everything else unaided.

That sequence has a built-in economy. Most arrivals turn out to have genuine gaps in one or two subjects rather than across the board, and the diagnostic identifies which. Families who skip to lessons immediately pay to re-teach material the child already knows, and they usually discover it around the point where they were going to stop anyway.

One thing deserves to be pulled forward out of that sequence. If the student is in the Diploma or in Year 11, any internally assessed component with a school deadline inside the next term gets attention immediately, before the diagnostic work is finished. Those deadlines do not wait for a settling-in period, and a missed investigation window is a much harder problem to solve than a content gap.
bullets: Collect reports, marked work and written confirmation of board and tier first
One diagnostic session per subject before any block is booked

sections.heading: A curriculum transition map, subject by subject
paragraphs: Transitions are talked about generally and experienced specifically. A student is not behind in science; they have not met the mole concept, or they have met it and never used it in a calculation. The table below is the version of that map we work from, and the column that matters is the third one, because that is where a tutor actually spends time.

Several patterns in it are counter-intuitive. A strong Middle Years Programme student entering the Diploma often finds the written examinations harder than the coursework, because the MYP trained them in process and the Diploma also tests timed recall and technique. A strong Indian-board student entering IGCSE usually has more content than they need and less examination-style written explanation, so the work is about answer construction rather than about teaching new material. And a British Year 11 student entering the Diploma rather than A Levels has to add breadth, a second language and the core, which is a workload shock rather than a difficulty shock.

The timings in the final column are indicative and assume one weekly hour plus the student doing the set work. They are deliberately modest. A bridge that is sold as a fortnight is usually a bridge nobody measured, and the ones that genuinely take two or three months are the maths route changes, where missing foundations cannot be skipped.

Use the map as a conversation with the new school rather than instead of one. The head of year will know what previous arrivals from that system found hard, and that local knowledge is worth more than any table.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency: what each curriculum has to show
paragraphs: Families who move often ask the same question eventually: will these qualifications be accepted here. Equivalency is the Ministry of Education process that recognises a foreign secondary certificate for use in the UAE, and it matters for university applications and for some employment routes. It is also the area where this market publishes the least reliable information, including at least one ranking competitor page that states the wrong number of required subjects.

On the British track the requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which is the detail that catches families out, because a student counting them can finish Year 11 a subject short.

On the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL internet-based test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT; mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Maths test before applying. For the IB we deliberately publish no points threshold, because the source we can cite does not state one and an unsourced figure on a page like this would be worse than silence.

Two further points of principle. Equivalency is a Ministry process, not something a tutoring service performs, guarantees or accelerates, and no amount of tutoring is required for it. And requirements are revised, so verify the current rule on the Ministry's own site or with the attestation authority before building a university plan on it. What a tutor can usefully do is make sure the subject spread and the grade floor are on track two years early, rather than discovered in the final term.

sections.heading: Arriving after the entry deadline has already closed
paragraphs: This is the problem nobody warns transferring families about. Examination entries close months before the examinations themselves, and a student arriving in January may already be too late for a session they assumed was available. Cambridge's own key dates for the March 2027 series illustrate the gap precisely: the examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, but final entries were due on 27 November 2026, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results released on Direct on 13 May and certificates issued in late June.

There is a second trap specific to this region. Every Cambridge examination centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after consulting the wrong zone's timetable. A family that downloads a timetable found through a search engine, rather than the one the school provides, has created a real risk of missing a paper.

Pearson Edexcel runs its International GCSEs in May and June and again in November, and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those dates come from Pearson's own pages and are the right kind of anchor for a plan, but always open the live official timetable rather than relying on a figure restated on any website, including this one.

For the IB we publish no session or results dates. The organisation blocks automated verification, so nothing in this project is confirmed from the IB itself, and a date on a tutoring page that turns out to be wrong is worse than no date at all. UAE schools sit the May session; confirm every specific date with your child's diploma coordinator or on the IB's own site.

If an entry has genuinely been missed, the usual options are the next available series, a private-candidate entry through a centre that accepts external candidates, or in some cases a different board with a different session pattern. All three are real and all three have deadlines of their own, which is why this conversation belongs in the first week after arrival rather than the first month.

sections.heading: What a bridging term costs in this market, and who published the figure
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages examined for this project publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars rather than dirhams. So here are the market bands, attributed, as of October 2026. Budget online tutoring, generally university students or non-specialists, runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at its entry tiers. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits run AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate, on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table and comparable listings. Subject specialists at IB, IGCSE or A Level are AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and premium named tutors reaching AED 650.

A bridging block is a defined purchase rather than an open commitment, which makes it easy to budget. Two diagnostic hours plus eight bridging sessions in one subject, at the qualified-tutor band, is a known number before you start. Compare that with an open-ended weekly arrangement across four subjects, which is the arrangement arriving families most often agree to and most often regret.

The relocation context matters too. A household on a project contract may be paying school fees mid-year, a relocation agent, a short-let premium on the apartment and shipping, all in the same quarter. Scoped tuition that ends when the gap closes fits that reality considerably better than a monthly package, and anyone selling a twelve-month commitment to a family on a six-month lease is not paying attention.

None of those figures is an IB Gram price list. They are the market, published so a newly arrived family with no local reference points can tell whether a quote is normal. Where our own pricing is concerned, the free trial session and the consultation are the honest route, because the cost depends on subject, level and how many hours the diagnostic actually justifies.

sections.heading: The home tutor question in a serviced apartment
paragraphs: Households here search for a home tutor, and in a serviced apartment the logic is slightly different from a villa. There may be no study, no second table and a living room that is also the dining room. A visiting tutor and a sixteen-year-old working through a mock script occupy the only shared space in the home for ninety minutes, which in a household of four is a real cost nobody prices.

The money is also different from what parents expect. In-home rates in this market run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a comparably qualified tutor working online. And for a transferring family the deeper issue is choice: the pool of people who will drive to a specific building on a weekday evening is small and skews generalist, which is exactly the wrong pool when the task is reconstructing an IGCSE Chemistry sequence taught on a different board.

IB Gram does not make home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Abu Dhabi families are taught one-to-one over live video, and for a mobile household that is an advantage rather than a concession. The same tutor and the same slot survive a change of apartment, a month in a hotel between leases and in many cases a move to another country.

The format does need a workable corner: a laptop, headphones and a door that closes for an hour. In a small apartment that often means agreeing the hour with the whole household rather than just with the student, and families who settle that in advance lose far fewer sessions than those who improvise it weekly.

sections.heading: Arabic and the mandatory subjects arrivals never expect
paragraphs: Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific national curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That federal rule is why a child arriving from London or Houston into an international school here picks up subjects that were not on the brochure, and the discovery usually happens in the first set of reports rather than at enrolment.

The organisational detail is specific. Expectations and language of instruction differ between Arab and non-Arab students for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and Dubai's regulator publishes the most detailed public guidance on how schools must separate those groups, down to minimum lesson lengths. Abu Dhabi families are under the Department of Education and Knowledge rather than KHDA, but the federal requirement underneath is the same, which makes that published guidance a useful reference for understanding what your child's timetable is doing.

Two consequences for an arriving household. The first is timetable arithmetic: these subjects take real hours, so a Diploma student carrying six subjects and the core is doing so in a week that also includes mandatory Arabic, and parents who cannot see where the study time went have part of their answer. The second is the equivalency point made earlier, and it is worth repeating because it costs families real grades: Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five accredited subjects the Ministry requires on the British track.

Support is available as an additional-language Arabic stream focused on script fluency and the specific assessment the school uses. We do not supply or reproduce approved content for the mandatory subjects, because using different or additional material without prior Ministry permission is not permitted, and an arriving family is better served by a tutor who respects that boundary than by one who ignores it.

sections.heading: Where a tutor stops when a student is new to the IB
paragraphs: A student who arrives into the Diploma part-way is the most vulnerable kind of student in an academic-honesty sense, and not because they are dishonest. They have joined a system with unfamiliar rules, they are behind on an internal assessment with a school deadline attached, and they are under pressure from a household that has just spent a great deal of money on a relocation. That is the exact situation in which a family starts asking a tutor for things nobody should supply.

So the line is worth stating before it is tested. A tutor interrogates the research question until it can be answered inside the word limit. A tutor says that a planned method will not generate data capable of supporting a conclusion, before the data exists. A tutor reads a draft against the published criteria and names the criterion that is unevidenced, teaches the missing skill, and returns the work. A tutor asks the student to justify a paragraph aloud.

A tutor does not supply text to be pasted, does not rewrite a section into something the student could not have produced, does not edit a draft to completion, and does not hand over a topic, a structure or a data set ready-made. Nothing is bought in. One operation in this market openly sells finished Diploma internal assessments; a new arrival is precisely the customer that product is aimed at, and the malpractice finding would fall on the student rather than on the seller.

The practical protection is sequencing. Get the coursework conversation into the first fortnight after arrival, when there is still room to choose a question and design a method. Families who wait until the deadline is visible end up with only cosmetic options, and that is where the pressure comes from. We flag those dates in the first session for exactly this reason.

sections.heading: Starting from the previous school's paperwork
paragraphs: The first request we make of an Eastern Mangroves family is unglamorous: send the paperwork. The final report from the previous school, the last marked work in each subject, the previous school's scheme of work if it can be obtained, and the new school's written confirmation of the board and tier for every examined subject. That package, read by a specialist, produces a plan in an hour. Without it, the first three sessions become an expensive version of the same exercise.

Then a diagnostic session per subject that matters, which is rarely all of them. The output is a named topic list, split into covered, partly covered and not met. Parents find this document more useful than any report, because it is specific enough to act on and short enough to read. You keep it whether or not you continue with us.

From there the plan is scoped rather than open-ended: a bridging block on the subjects with real gaps, a date by which the gaps should have closed, and a measurement against the school's own next assessment rather than against how the sessions felt. If the school's assessment says the gap has closed, the block ends. Arrangements that quietly continue past their purpose are a feature of this market and not a good one.

Two honest limits. Coverage for the rarer Diploma languages and some Higher Level combinations is thin in this time zone, and a mid-year arrival asking for a specific weekday slot in a rare subject may find nothing behind the request; we say so rather than substituting a generalist. And in this market generally, it is worth asking any tutor whether they hold the private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Working without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so be sceptical of any figure quoted to you.

process.title: Send the previous school's paperwork
process.description: Final report, last marked work per subject, and the old scheme of work if you can get it. Add the new school's written confirmation of board and tier for each examined subject. A specialist reading that package produces a plan in about an hour; without it the first sessions do the same job far more slowly.

process.title: Diagnose subject by subject
process.description: One session per subject that matters, producing a topic-level list split into covered, partly covered and not met. Most arrivals have real gaps in one or two subjects rather than across the board, and this is what identifies which. You keep the list whether or not you continue.

process.title: Deal with any live coursework deadline
process.description: If an internal assessment, exploration or Extended Essay milestone falls inside the next term, it is handled before the diagnostic work finishes. Content gaps can be closed later. A missed investigation window cannot, and that is the item most often overlooked during a settling-in period.

process.title: Run a scoped bridging block
process.description: Six to ten sessions on the named gaps, with the scope fixed at the start and a date by which it should be done. Progress is measured against the school's own next assessment rather than against how the sessions felt. The block ends when the gap closes, by design.

process.title: Decide whether to keep a weekly slot
process.description: Some students need nothing further once the bridge is complete. Others, particularly in the Diploma, benefit from a continuing hour that supervises coursework and timed practice. For households expecting another move, the slot and the tutor travel with you rather than being rebuilt in the next city.

whyPoints.title: Built for transfers, not for settled cohorts
whyPoints.description: The first deliverable is a topic-level map of what a new arrival actually missed, produced from the previous school's marked work. Most tutoring here starts by selling lessons; starting with a diagnosis is both cheaper for the family and the only way to avoid paying to re-teach known material.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency explained with its source
whyPoints.description: Five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3 with Arabic and Islamic education excluded, plus an A Level at E or two AS Levels. We publish no IB points threshold because no citable source states one. A ranking competitor publishes a wrong subject count; we would rather say verify at source.

whyPoints.title: Deadlines published, with the board named
whyPoints.description: Cambridge's March 2027 entries closed on 27 November 2026 for examinations starting 3 February. Pearson's November 2026 window ran to 19 November. We name the board, link the live official timetable and publish no IB dates at all, because the IB's own site is the only acceptable source for those.

whyPoints.title: Scoped purchases rather than open commitments
whyPoints.description: A diagnostic is one or two hours. A bridging block is six to ten sessions with a defined end. For a household managing school fees, a short lease and a relocation in the same quarter, a known cost that finishes is worth more than a monthly package that quietly renews.

whyPoints.title: The tutor travels with the family
whyPoints.description: A mobile student has already lost continuity at school. Keeping the same tutor and the same slot through a change of apartment, a month in a hotel or a move to another country is one of the few stabilities available, and live video is what makes it possible.

whyPoints.title: No borrowed authority
whyPoints.description: We explain what the Department of Education and Knowledge does and point you to the Ministry for equivalency. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, operates no UAE office, and does not imply otherwise anywhere on this page.

faqs.question: We are moving to Eastern Mangroves in February. Can my child still join an IB Diploma cohort?
faqs.answer: Joining part-way through the first Diploma year is usually workable. Joining part-way through the second is very difficult, because internal assessments and the core are already in progress against school deadlines, and a Higher Level subject the previous school did not offer cannot be picked up in the final months. The questions to ask the new school before accepting a place are which subjects are available in your child's combination, what internal assessment deadlines have already passed, and who will supervise the Extended Essay. Those answers matter more than the tutoring plan.

faqs.question: How do we find out exactly what my child missed by changing school mid-year?
faqs.answer: One diagnostic session per subject, built around the last work the previous school marked, produces a named topic list split into covered, partly covered and not met. It takes an hour or two per subject and it is the cheapest useful thing a transferring family can buy. Most arrivals turn out to have genuine gaps in one or two subjects rather than everywhere, which is why booking a term of lessons across four subjects before the diagnosis is how families end up paying to re-teach material their child already knows.

faqs.question: Do IGCSEs taken at a school in another country count for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. Accreditation of the awarding body is the operative word, so verify the current requirement on the Ministry's own site or with the attestation authority rather than relying on any tutoring page, including this one.

faqs.question: What happens if we arrive after the examination entry deadline has closed?
faqs.answer: Entries close months before papers, so this happens regularly. Cambridge's March 2027 series shows the gap: examinations from 3 February to 4 March 2027, but final entries due 27 November 2026. The options are the next available series, a private-candidate entry through a centre that accepts external candidates, or in some cases a board with a different session pattern, since Pearson runs May and June plus November. All three carry deadlines of their own, which is why this belongs in the first week after arrival rather than the first month.

faqs.question: Why does Cambridge publish different timetables for different zones?
faqs.answer: Every Cambridge examination centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs between them. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. The practical rule for a newly arrived family is simple: use the timetable your child's school provides, not one found through a search engine, and confirm the zone with the examinations officer rather than assuming it from the country.

faqs.question: Why will you not publish the IB examination dates?
faqs.answer: Because we cannot verify them from the IB itself. The organisation's site blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed at source, and a wrong date on a page a parent plans around is worse than no date at all. UAE schools sit the May session, and your child's diploma coordinator holds the current calendar including the internal deadlines that actually bind. Cambridge and Pearson dates we do publish, because those boards publish them openly and we can cite the page.

faqs.question: Is there any tutoring my child needs in order to get equivalency?
faqs.answer: No. Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process applied to certificates and transcripts, and no tutoring is required for it. Anyone implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a regulatory procedure. What a tutor can usefully do is make sure the subject spread and the grade floor are on track early: five accredited subjects at no less than E or grade 3 on the British track, with Arabic and Islamic education outside that count. Discovering a subject shortfall in the final term is the avoidable failure.

faqs.question: Does a Middle Years Programme student find the Diploma harder than an IGCSE student does?
faqs.answer: Differently hard. An MYP student usually arrives with strong process skills, research habits and criterion literacy, and less practice at timed written examinations under real pressure, which is where the Diploma also tests them. An IGCSE student arrives with the opposite profile: examination technique in place, less experience of extended independent projects. The MYP gap tends to close in six to eight weeks of deliberate timed practice. The IGCSE gap is a workload adjustment across the first term, and it is mostly about the core.

faqs.question: How much does a bridging block of tutoring cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Market rates as of October 2026 run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for a budget or university-student tutor, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel inside the figure, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB or A Level specialist. Those bands come from published competitor pricing and Bestimate's 2026 rate table, not from us. A scoped block of two diagnostics plus eight sessions is therefore a known number before you commit to anything.

faqs.question: Do your tutors come to apartments at Eastern Mangroves?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not make home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Abu Dhabi lessons run one-to-one over live video. Independent in-home tutors do work in this district and their rates carry the travel, which is part of why in-home figures run from about AED 180 to AED 500 an hour. In a serviced apartment there is also a space cost that nobody prices: a visiting tutor occupies the only shared room in the home for the duration of the session.

faqs.question: My child has never used a graphic display calculator. Is that a problem in IB maths?
faqs.answer: It is a real but short-lived problem, and it is mechanical rather than mathematical. Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation assumes calculator fluency throughout, and students arriving from systems that restricted calculators lose marks on operations they could do by hand but cannot do quickly on the device. Three or four focused sessions on the specific functions the course uses, regression, distributions, numerical solving and graphing, closes it. It is worth doing immediately on arrival rather than discovering it in a first assessment.

faqs.question: Why did Arabic appear on my child's timetable without warning?
faqs.answer: Because private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed international curriculum, under the federal requirement. Expectations and language of instruction differ between Arab and non-Arab students, and schools organise those groups separately. For most arriving families the practical issues are timetable time, which explains part of the missing study hours, and the equivalency point that Arabic and Islamic education do not count among the five subjects the Ministry requires on the British track.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child catch up on an internal assessment that is already late?
faqs.answer: Up to a clear point. The tutor can test whether the research question is answerable inside the word limit, check that the method will produce usable data, read what exists against the published criteria and name the criterion that is unevidenced, then teach the missing skill. What cannot happen is text being supplied, a section being rewritten, a draft edited to completion, or a topic or data set handed over ready-made. A malpractice finding falls on your child, not on the tutor, which is why lateness is a reason to start sooner rather than to cross the line.

faqs.question: We may relocate again within two years. Does that change what we should buy?
faqs.answer: Yes, in two ways. Prefer scoped purchases that finish, a diagnostic and a defined bridging block, over monthly packages that renew past their usefulness. And weigh portability in the curriculum decision itself: A Level is linear, narrow and relatively easy to resume elsewhere, while the Diploma's internal assessments and core are harder to transfer mid-course. Keeping the same tutor across a move is one of the few continuities a mobile student can have, and live video is what makes that practical.

faqs.question: What if you have nobody available for the subject we need?
faqs.answer: We say so before you plan around us. Coverage for the rarer Diploma languages and some Higher Level combinations is genuinely thin in this time zone, and a specific weekday slot in a rare subject may have nothing behind it. In that case we offer the nearest honest alternative, a different day, a different session length, or a tutor in another time zone, and if there is no real match we tell you rather than putting a generalist in front of a Higher Level paper. For a transferring family, a clear no is more useful than an optimistic yes.

abu-dhabi/eastern-mangroves.closingHeading: Send the old school's paperwork first
abu-dhabi/eastern-mangroves.closingBody: If you have just arrived at Eastern Mangroves, the most useful hour available to you is not a lesson. It is a specialist reading the previous school's final report, the last marked work in each subject and the new school's confirmation of board and tier, then writing down exactly which topics your child has not met. That document is what a bridging plan is built from, and it is also what stops you buying a term of lessons in material your child already knows. From there the plan is scoped, measured against the school's own next assessment, and delivered one-to-one over live video, which means it starts this week and travels with you if you move again.

Each profile names the boards taught and the hours held in Gulf Standard Time, so you can see before any conversation whether an Abu Dhabi evening slot exists.

intro.heading: Why 4AC1 quotes in Abu Dhabi arrive hundreds of dirhams apart
paragraphs: Ask three providers in Abu Dhabi what an accounting tutor costs and you will get three numbers that barely overlap. A university student advertising on a community board may quote AED 60 an hour. An agency with a subject specialist will quote AED 250. A named specialist with a waiting list may quote beyond AED 500. None of them is lying. They are selling different things, and the differences stay invisible until the first invoice arrives: marking, preparation, travel, replacement cover, and whether anybody reads your child's school scheme of work before the first lesson.

Abu Dhabi adds its own pressure to that range. ADEK professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from taking paid private work with students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that says the same thing. This has been reported in the Gulf press and should be checked against the current ADEK policy document before anyone treats the wording as exact. The practical effect on a parent is simple enough: the cheapest and most obvious option, the person already teaching the class, is off the table, and the local market prices accordingly.

Accounting is also a thin subject here. Most Abu Dhabi private schools entering candidates for Pearson Edexcel International GCSE run large groups in Mathematics A and English Language A and a single small group in Accounting, sometimes taught by a business studies teacher covering a second specialism. That scarcity shows up in the hourly rate, in how long a match takes, and in how often a family is offered a business studies tutor for an accounting paper. The two subjects share vocabulary and almost none of the mark scheme.

Then there is the drive. An in-home tutor crossing from Al Khalidiyah to Khalifa City at four in the afternoon is paid for the hour taught and the hour lost, which is why Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one work at AED 180-350 against AED 45-150 at the budget online end. Families in Al Reef, Al Shamkha and Mohammed Bin Zayed City feel it most. The pool of people willing to drive out and back for a single hour is small, and the ones who will do it charge for it.

This page gives the numbers rather than hiding them, then says plainly what IB Gram sells. Lessons for Abu Dhabi families run one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. Home visits in Abu Dhabi are not something IB Gram offers anywhere in the UAE, because that is an India-only service, so the travel premium disappears and the choice of tutor stops being a function of who lives within a twenty-minute drive of your building. What replaces it is an accounting specialist and a weekly record of marked work.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-accounting-4ac1-.programmesIntro: Accounting sits inside a bigger decision about option blocks and the post-16 route. These are the four programmes an Abu Dhabi family choosing or already sitting 4AC1 is usually weighing, with what each one changes about the cost and the shape of tutoring in this emirate.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Accounting
programmes.description: Two written papers, each carrying half the marks, with no coursework or controlled assessment. The content runs from the double-entry framework and books of prime entry through control accounts, correction of errors and the suspense account, to final accounts for sole traders, partnerships and limited companies, then ratio analysis and interpretation. Paper timings should be confirmed on the current Pearson specification, which is the only place they are authoritative.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi, 4AC1 is usually a single option-block group rather than a year-wide subject, so a student who falls behind rarely has a second class to move into. ADEK licenses and inspects the school, but the entry and the internal deadlines belong to the school's exams officer. Ask who that person is in September rather than in March.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Accounting 0452
programmes.description: The Cambridge route to the same qualification level, assessed by two papers with a multiple-choice and short-answer structure that differs from Pearson's. The accounting is broadly the same accounting; the command terms, the layout expected in a statement of financial position and the way marks are released for own-figure answers are not. A tutor who has taught only one board will cost you time on the other.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools split between the two boards, and some enter different subjects with different boards in the same year. Before paying for any accounting hours, get the exact syllabus code from the exams officer. A family that books 0452 help for a 4AC1 candidate pays twice, once for the lessons and once for the unlearning.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International A Level Accounting
programmes.description: The post-16 continuation, where Year 11 habits either pay off or become expensive. Published accounts, cash-flow statements, standard costing, budgeting and investment appraisal all assume the double-entry fluency that 4AC1 was supposed to build. Students who passed Accounting by memorising formats rather than understanding them usually meet the gap in the first term of Year 12, when there is far less room to fix it.
programmes.countryNote: Fewer Abu Dhabi schools offer Accounting at A Level than at International GCSE, so some families discover in Year 11 that continuing means changing school or sitting as a private candidate. That is worth knowing before option choices are signed, because it decides whether 4AC1 is a terminal qualification or the first half of a four-year run.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Business Management
programmes.description: The IB alternative for a student who preferred the commercial side of accounting to the ledgers. Business Management covers finance and accounts as one unit of five, with ratio work and cash-flow forecasting but no double-entry bookkeeping, and it carries an internal assessment that has to be the student's own from first idea to final submission.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run both the Diploma Programme and International GCSE, so the switch at sixteen happens inside one building. Students arriving from 4AC1 usually find the finance unit straightforward and the internal assessment unfamiliar, since nothing in Pearson Accounting asks for a research question or a tool-based analysis of a real organisation.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-accounting-4ac1-.subjectsIntro: Accounting is almost never tutored alone. These are the subjects Abu Dhabi families most often pair with 4AC1, with what each one assesses and where the marks tend to go missing. Rates for all of them sit inside the same market bands set out further down this page.

subjects.name: Accounting (4AC1)
subjects.description: Two written papers, half the marks each. The expensive topics are correction of errors, control accounts, partnership appropriation and limited company final accounts. Students lose marks on presentation conventions, such as missing dates, wrong narratives and totals that are not cast, long before they lose them on understanding.

subjects.name: Accounting (0452)
subjects.description: The same subject under Cambridge command terms, with a multiple-choice component Pearson does not use. Candidates trained on Pearson layouts often lose marks here for over-writing short answers and for ignoring the own-figure rule, which lets a wrong subtotal still earn the marks that follow it.

subjects.name: Business (4BS1)
subjects.description: The usual partner subject. It shares the finance vocabulary with Accounting and almost none of the mark scheme: 4BS1 rewards applied judgement and evaluation in extended answers, while 4AC1 rewards accurate records. A student who is strong in one is not automatically strong in the other.

subjects.name: Economics (4ET1)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is where this subject is won and lost. Labelled axes, a correct shift and a stated direction of change earn marks that prose cannot recover afterwards. Students arriving from Accounting often under-explain, assuming the number speaks for itself on the page.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.levels: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, Foundation and Higher tier
subjects.description: Accounting candidates rarely struggle with the arithmetic and often struggle with percentage change, ratio and reverse percentages under time pressure, which are exactly the skills ratio analysis depends on. Tier choice matters, because Foundation caps the grade available and the decision belongs to the school.

subjects.name: English Language A (4EA1)
subjects.description: Relevant to Accounting because the interpretation questions are written answers. A student who can calculate a current ratio and cannot say what it means in two sentences is losing marks that a language tutor, not an accounting one, usually fixes fastest.

subjects.name: ICT (4IT1)
subjects.description: A common option-block neighbour, assessed with a practical examination that rewards evidence discipline: file names, screenshots, test plans. Those habits transfer to accounting presentation, which is also marked on whether an examiner can follow what the candidate actually did.

subjects.name: Computer Science (4CP0)
subjects.description: The other technical neighbour, with an on-screen programming paper that sits oddly beside written subjects in the same study timetable. Families often ask whether one tutor can cover both subjects; in practice the specialisms rarely overlap enough for that to work well.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific national curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, which run alongside the international programme. They take timetable space that an accounting revision plan has to work around rather than ignore.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-accounting-4ac1-.regionsIntro: Where you live in Abu Dhabi changes the arithmetic of tutoring more than it changes the teaching. These notes cover the school clusters each district feeds, the realistic earliest start for a weekday session, and what an in-home tutor would have to drive to reach you.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi Island — Al Khalidiyah and the Corniche
regions.note: Dense, well served by schools, and the one part of the emirate where an in-home accounting tutor is genuinely findable. Parking and the afternoon school-run crawl still push a realistic first weekday slot back to about 4.45pm.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Nahyan
regions.note: A long-established British-curriculum catchment, with families often holding places across two or three island schools. Sessions here can start earlier than on the mainland because the drive home is short, which matters for a Year 11 candidate sitting a November entry.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Villa communities with long internal roads, so an in-home tutor loses time inside the compound as well as on the way to it. Accounting tuition in Khalifa City usually settles on a 5.30pm or 6pm online slot, keeping weekends free for timed paper practice.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Close to the eastern school corridor and to the airport road, which is the bottleneck. Accounting groups in this cluster are small, so a student who needs a second explanation of the suspense account rarely gets one in class.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: A short causeway from the island and a long way from the mainland tutor pool. Families here pay the top of the in-home band for anyone willing to make the trip, which is why online delivery changes the sum most sharply in this district.

regions.name: Yas Island

A UAE family does not transact in dollars, so here are the bands in dirhams with the source attached to each one. These are market figures and not an IB Gram price list. Our own position is a free trial lesson and a conversation about hours, because the right number depends on how many weeks are left and how much marking is involved.

Read the table as a map of what is included rather than as a quality ladder. A tutor at AED 60 an hour is usually teaching from a textbook and returning nothing in writing. A tutor at AED 250 is usually marking a timed question between sessions, which is where most of the grade movement in accounting actually happens. Above AED 500 you are paying for scarcity, a named specialist whose hours are already full, and for accounting in Abu Dhabi that scarcity is real rather than manufactured.

The monthly figures are the ones parents budget against. Packages seen in this market run from about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions to AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's 2026 estimates for a single weekly hour land at AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Accounting sits in the middle band for most Abu Dhabi families and at the top of it during Year 11.

Nothing in the table includes the examination entry fee. That is charged by the centre entering your child, not by the tutor, and a private candidate pays it separately. Ask the school for the figure in writing before building a budget around it, and ask at the same time whether the school will enter an external candidate at all.

sections.heading: Three things specific to this emirate that move the number
paragraphs: The first is the ethics rule. ADEK professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and a teacher tutoring outside school hours needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than quoted, and verify it against the current ADEK document. It matters commercially because it removes the one supplier a parent would otherwise approach first, and scarcity raises a price.

The second is subject depth. Accounting is an option, not a core, and an option group of a dozen students does not justify a second specialist teacher. A family in Al Raha or Khalifa City looking for an accounting tutor in Abu Dhabi is therefore competing with every other family in the same position for a very small number of people who have actually taught 4AC1 to a series. That is why match times for accounting run longer than for Mathematics A, and why a business studies tutor is so often offered instead.

The third is distance. Abu Dhabi is a long emirate. A tutor living on the island and teaching in Al Shamkha spends more time in the car than in the lesson, and the rate has to carry both. Online accounting tuition in Abu Dhabi deletes that line item, which is the single largest saving available to a family outside the island districts. sections.heading: What 4AC1 actually assesses, and which parts cost the most to fix
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Accounting is assessed by written papers alone, each carrying half the marks, and there is no coursework component anywhere in the qualification. That single structural fact shapes every sensible tutoring plan: the only thing being marked is what a candidate can produce on paper, under time, in a layout an examiner recognises. Confirm current paper durations on the Pearson specification page rather than relying on any third-party summary, this one included.

The content divides into three blocks of very different cost. The recording block, which covers double entry, books of prime entry, the ledgers and the trial balance, is cheap to teach and expensive to leave broken, because everything later depends on it. The adjustment block, which covers depreciation, accruals and prepayments, bad debts, control accounts and the correction of errors, is where most lost marks live. The interpretation block, ratio analysis and the written comment on it, is the one most often rushed in the final weeks.

The adjustment block is where tutoring hours earn their keep. Correction of errors and the suspense account reward a specific procedure, and a candidate who has not practised it will usually get the journal right and the suspense account wrong, or will fix the ledger and forget the statement of profit or loss. Partnership appropriation and limited company final accounts behave the same way: the marks sit in a sequence, and a sequence is teachable. Guesswork is not, and at AED 250 an hour guesswork is expensive.

sections.heading: Where Abu Dhabi candidates lose accounting marks
paragraphs: Most of the lost marks we see in marked 4AC1 scripts from this emirate are not conceptual. They are procedural, which is good news, because procedure is the fastest thing to teach. A candidate who understands depreciation can still lose three marks for omitting the date, mislabelling the account, failing to carry a balance down or leaving a total uncast. None of that requires a re-teach of the topic. It requires somebody to mark the work and name the habit.

The second pattern is narrative. Pearson expects a narrative on a journal entry, and a surprising number of candidates write the figures and skip the words. The third is the own-figure convention: when a candidate carries forward a wrong subtotal and the mark scheme allows the following marks to be earned anyway, a student who abandons the question loses everything that was still available. Students taught to keep going score better than equally able students taught to be careful.

The fourth pattern is specific to this market. Students in Abu Dhabi who moved into International GCSE from an American or Indian curriculum often arrive with correct accounting and the wrong presentation conventions, because the formats differ. That shows up as a strong candidate marked down repeatedly for the same thing. It takes two or three sessions to correct and it is almost never diagnosed in class, because the class is being taught content rather than having its scripts read line by line.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from a Pearson series
paragraphs: No competitor page researched for this project names an examination session at all. That is a strange omission, because the session is what the whole plan hangs from. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year, so a Year 11 candidate in Abu Dhabi has a real choice about which series to sit, and a resit candidate has a second chance within the same academic year rather than twelve months later.

The dates that matter are not only the exam dates. Pearson publishes a provisional timetable well ahead of each series, including one for International GCSE November 2027, and then confirms a final timetable; the November 2026 series ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Because provisional dates can be revised, any plan should be built against the live official timetable rather than against a figure copied onto a page like this one. The entry deadline sitting inside your child's school is earlier still, and it is the one families miss.

Results timing shapes the resit decision. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A family deciding in late August whether to resit in November has a few weeks to make the entry, which is why the conversation about a resit should happen before the result arrives rather than after it. Cambridge candidates sitting 0452 work to a different calendar, including a March series whose final entries fell on 27 November 2026 for an examination period of 3 February to 4 March 2027.
