sections.heading: Who is permitted to charge you for accounting lessons in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is a permitted activity, and it is permitted on conditions. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, through the smart app, the website and the e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no page should quote an amount, and any figure you see circulating should be treated as unverified. What a parent can usefully do is ask the question directly before paying anything: does this person hold the permit, and under which category. A tutor who treats that as an unreasonable question has answered it.

A business is a different matter from an individual. An operation with premises and staff needs an educational services permit from the relevant authority, which is a specific licence issued to training institutes, and nothing about holding a work permit makes a tutor regulator-endorsed. IB Gram does not hold a KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or Ministry of Education licence and does not describe itself as having one. We can explain the system, point you to the official channel, and tell you exactly what our own tutors are and are not.

sections.heading: Online delivery against an in-home accounting tutor in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: An in-home accounting tutor in Abu Dhabi is a real product that real families buy, and the honest case for it is supervision: a parent in the next room, a child who cannot close a laptop, a younger student who needs the structure of somebody physically present. The honest case against it is arithmetic. At AED 180-500 an hour you are funding a drive, and the tutor you get is drawn from whoever is willing to make that drive to your district on that evening.

Accounting is unusually well suited to a screen, which is not true of every subject. The work is written, sequential and visual: a shared document with a ledger on it, annotated live, is closer to how the subject is actually assessed than a notebook on a kitchen table. Screen-sharing a marked script and working through the examiner's deductions line by line is the core activity, and it loses nothing over video. A practical science subject would be a harder argument to make.

So the comparison for an Abu Dhabi family is not convenience against quality. IB Gram does not send a tutor to your address in this emirate, because home visits are a service offered only in India, and the saving is spent on specialism instead: a tutor who has taught 4AC1 to a series, at an hour that works in Gulf Standard Time, with a marked script between every session. For a family in Al Reef or on Yas Island, that is the difference between an accounting specialist and the nearest available tutor.

sections.heading: What 4AC1 is worth afterwards: the five-subject count and equivalency
paragraphs: Families in Abu Dhabi often ask whether Accounting counts for anything beyond the certificate, and the answer sits in the Ministry of Education equivalency rules for the British track. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also show either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Accounting is a subject like any other inside that count.

One detail saves families money and is widely got wrong. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. A page currently ranking for these searches tells UAE candidates they must take six International GCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five, excluding those two. That difference can change an option-block decision in Year 9, which is why it is worth checking the Ministry's own guidance rather than a tutoring company's summary, including this one.

IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency, and no points threshold for the IB route is published here because none has been verified on the Ministry's own pages. Nor is tutoring a requirement for equivalency, admission or progression; any page implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency. What tutoring can honestly do is make a grade more likely than it would otherwise be, and in a five-subject count a single borderline grade is sometimes the whole decision.

process.title: Send the marked work, not a description of it
process.description: Photographs of the last two marked accounting papers, the school's scheme of work if you have it, and the syllabus code. A description of the problem is a starting point; a marked script is evidence. Most of what a first session needs to know is already written on those pages in another teacher's handwriting.

process.title: A free trial lesson that produces a diagnosis
process.description: Sixty minutes over live video, in which the tutor works through one of those scripts with your child rather than delivering an introductory lecture. You get a short written note afterwards naming the topics, the procedural habits and the realistic number of hours. There is no card required and no obligation to continue.

process.title: A weekly plan with one named topic and one marked task
process.description: Each session has a single topic and ends with a timed question to be completed before the next one. The task comes back marked against the published mark scheme with the lost marks named. That written record is what lets you judge whether the money is doing anything, without taking our word for it.

process.title: A review at four sessions, against the scripts
process.description: After four sessions there is enough marked work to see a trend or the absence of one. We look at it with you and say which it is. If the match is wrong, changing tutor at that point costs four hours rather than a term, and that is the honest moment to make the decision.

whyPoints.title: Board-specific rather than subject-general
whyPoints.description: A 4AC1 candidate needs somebody who knows Pearson's layouts, narratives and own-figure conventions, not somebody who knows accounting in general. We say which board a tutor has actually taught to a series, and we will tell you when the honest answer is the other board.

whyPoints.title: Marked scripts rather than attendance
whyPoints.description: The deliverable between sessions is a marked piece of work with the lost marks named, not a report that lessons took place. It is the only evidence a parent can read without specialist knowledge, and it is the first thing to ask any provider in this market for.

whyPoints.title: Published rates and a map of the market
whyPoints.description: The table on this page quotes competitors' own published figures with the source attached, because three of six researched pages publish nothing at all. You should be able to see where any quote sits in the Abu Dhabi market before you accept it, including a quote from us.

whyPoints.title: Academic-honesty boundaries stated up front
whyPoints.description: 4AC1 carries no coursework, so the question is narrower here than on an IB page, but the principle holds across every subject we teach: a tutor teaches, marks and gives feedback on a student's own work. Assessed work remains the student's throughout, and we will not take it over.

whyPoints.title: Coverage disclosed, including the gaps
whyPoints.description: Accounting is a thin specialism in this emirate. If no 4AC1 specialist is free at the hour you need, we say so and set out the alternatives rather than filling the slot with a business studies tutor. A disclosed gap is cheaper for you than an undisclosed mismatch.

faqs.question: What does an Edexcel IGCSE Accounting 4AC1 tutor cost per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Abu Dhabi for a qualified subject tutor working online sit at roughly AED 150-300 an hour, with International GCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and named premium tutors above AED 500. Budget online options advertise from AED 45-150, and in-home visits run AED 180-500 because travel is funded inside the hour. Those are published market figures from EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase, Bestimate and BartyED as at October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. What we quote depends on hours, weeks remaining and how much marking is involved, and the first lesson is free.

faqs.question: Why can my child's own accounting teacher not tutor them privately in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: ADEK professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This has been reported in the Gulf press and the exact wording should be checked against the current ADEK policy document. The effect for you is that the most convenient supplier is unavailable, which is part of why specialist rates in this emirate sit where they do. Asking a teacher to breach it puts their position at risk.

faqs.question: Does living on Abu Dhabi island rather than Khalifa City change what we pay?
faqs.answer: For in-home tutoring, considerably. The island has the densest tutor pool in the emirate, so a family in Al Khalidiyah can usually find somebody at the lower end of the AED 180-500 in-home band. A family in Khalifa City, Al Reef or Al Shamkha is paying for a longer drive and a smaller pool, which pushes the rate up and the availability down. For online lessons the district changes nothing about the price. It changes only the realistic start time, because the school run still has to finish first.

faqs.question: Is a Cambridge 0452 accounting tutor interchangeable with a Pearson 4AC1 one?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. The underlying accounting is the same, but Cambridge IGCSE Accounting 0452 uses a multiple-choice component Pearson does not, the command terms differ, and the expected layouts and own-figure conventions are not identical. A tutor who has taught only 0452 will teach your child good accounting and some wrong habits, which then cost marks on a 4AC1 paper. Before booking anything, get the syllabus code from the school's exams officer in writing. Some Abu Dhabi schools enter different subjects with different boards in the same year, so one answer does not cover the timetable.

faqs.question: How many hours of 4AC1 support should an Abu Dhabi family budget for Year 11?
faqs.answer: A weekly sixty- to ninety-minute session across Year 11 is about thirty to thirty-five hours, which at mid-market rates lands somewhere near AED 600-1,200 a month on Bestimate's 2026 estimates. A family starting in January rather than September is usually buying twenty hours at a higher intensity, which costs less in total and delivers less. The variable nobody budgets for is marking time. Ask whether marking is inside the hourly rate or charged on top, because that single question changes the real cost of a term by a noticeable margin.

faqs.question: Do accounting tuition rates in Abu Dhabi rise before the November series?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens rather than headline rates. Accounting specialists in this emirate are few, their evening slots fill from about September, and by October the question is usually whether a slot exists rather than what it costs. Some providers do price short intensive blocks above their standard hourly rate because the preparation and marking load per session is higher. The practical consequence is that a family deciding in late October for a November entry is choosing from what is left. Booking against the entry deadline rather than the exam date avoids most of that.

faqs.question: Which 4AC1 topic areas swallow the most tutoring hours?
faqs.answer: The adjustment block, every time. Correction of errors and the suspense account, control accounts, depreciation, accruals and prepayments, and bad and doubtful debts between them account for most of the marks lost in the scripts we read. Partnership appropriation and limited company final accounts come next, because the marks sit in a sequence and a broken sequence loses several at once. Double entry itself is cheap to teach and expensive to leave broken. Ratio interpretation is usually the last thing to get attention and the easiest to improve in the final fortnight.

faqs.question: Are accounting lessons for Abu Dhabi families taught online or at an Abu Dhabi address?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The search term that brought you here is the phrase parents use, so we would rather answer it plainly than pretend. What you get instead of a visit is a wider choice of specialist, no travel premium inside the rate, and a marked script after each session that a parent can read without knowing any accounting.

faqs.question: What does an in-home accounting tutor in Abu Dhabi charge, and what is inside that number?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put in-home one-to-one work at AED 180-350 on Bestimate's 2026 table, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200-500 and monthly in-home packages at AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Inside that number is the lesson, the travel to your district and the travel back, and in most cases no written marking. The travel is the part worth examining, because you are paying for an hour the tutor spends in a car. It also narrows your choice to whoever will make that drive on that evening.

faqs.question: Does a quoted accounting tuition rate in Abu Dhabi include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, and ask for the answer in writing. The VAT treatment of tuition in the UAE depends on the provider and is not something a tutoring page should state as fact without a Federal Tax Authority citation, so treat any page that does with caution. What a parent can reasonably require is clarity on one point: is the figure you were quoted the figure you will be invoiced, and is a tax registration number shown. A provider that cannot answer that about its own pricing has told you something useful about its administration.

faqs.question: Is a group accounting class at an Abu Dhabi centre cheaper than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, and that is not the only question. A centre group runs to a fixed scheme at a fixed pace, which suits a student who is broadly on track and needs structure. It suits a student losing marks on a specific procedural habit far less, because nobody in a group is reading that student's scripts line by line. A paired session with one other candidate from the same school and board is often the better compromise: the rate splits, and each student still gets individual marked work back.

faqs.question: How do I check an accounting tutor is permitted to charge us in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Ask whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and under which eligibility category. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, so cost is no excuse for not having one, and the categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so distrust any page quoting an amount.

faqs.question: How does 4AC1 sit in the five-subject count for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: It counts as one of the five. The Ministry of Education's British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at E or better or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One page currently ranking for UAE searches states six subjects are needed; the sourced figure is five. Verify it on the Ministry's own pages, because an option-block decision in Year 9 can turn on it.

faqs.question: What happens if no 4AC1 specialist is free in our evening slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you, which sounds obvious and is not the norm in this market. Accounting is a thin specialism and a 5.30pm Gulf Standard Time slot in October is the most contested hour of the week. The realistic options are a different hour, a weekend session, a wait of a week or two for a slot to open, or a paired session with another candidate from the same cohort. What we will not do is put a business studies tutor in front of an accounting paper and describe it as a match.

faqs.question: Where does the money go if we only have AED 1,000 a month for accounting?
faqs.answer: At mid-market rates that is roughly four to six hours a month, so spend it on diagnosis and marking rather than on coverage. Four sessions that each take one marked script apart and fix one procedural habit will move more marks than six sessions re-teaching the syllabus from the start. Ask for the marking in writing and use it yourself between sessions. If the budget has to stretch further, a paired session with another candidate from the same school and board roughly halves the hourly cost.

intro.heading: What an Abu Dhabi family should have in writing by the end of week three
paragraphs: Most 4BI1 tuition begins the same way. A parent in Khalifa City or Al Mushrif sees a Year 11 mock grade of 5 against a school target of 7, and books someone who came recommended through a class group. Six weeks later the student reports that the sessions are useful, the next mock moves half a grade or does not move at all, and nobody involved can explain which part of the course was responsible. The missing ingredient is almost never effort. It is evidence: a written record of which of the five 4BI1 topics is leaking marks, which command terms are being misread, and what was done about each.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Biology is examined by two written papers and carries no coursework. Paper 1 is the longer sitting and holds 110 of the 180 marks available. Paper 2 holds the remaining 70 and is the only place Topic 5, the use of biological resources, can appear. Because nothing is internally assessed, every mark your child will ever be awarded comes from a script produced under timed conditions. That makes 4BI1 unusually easy to audit. A tutor can hand you marked sections of released past papers inside the first fortnight, with the marks attributed to topics rather than to adjectives.

The evidence pack we ask tutors to keep is deliberately boring. Session one sets a baseline: one Paper 2 section attempted cold, marked against the published mark scheme, then broken down by topic and by command term. Sessions two to four work the two weakest topics and nothing else. Session five repeats the exercise on an unseen section of comparable difficulty. The gap between those two scripts is the only honest answer to the question parents actually ask, and it arrives inside a month rather than after the next school mock in February.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared whiteboard and screen sharing, because that is how IB Gram works everywhere outside India. IB Gram does not run home visits in Abu Dhabi; visiting tuition is a service we offer only in India. In practice that is what lets an Al Raha Beach family work with a biology specialist who has taught the 4BI1 genetics and ecology topics for years, rather than whoever happens to be free to drive out to the compound at half past five. Sessions can be recorded on request, so a diagram drawn once is rewatchable the night before the paper.

None of this needs a long commitment. Market rates for International GCSE science tuition in Abu Dhabi are set out further down with their sources attached, the trial lesson costs nothing and takes no card details, and the first review point lands before most families have spent much at all. If after three weeks nobody can tell you which topic moved and by how many marks, that is a reason to change tutor. The page says so plainly because it is as true of us as of anyone else quoting for the same work.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-biology-4bi1-tut.programmesIntro: 4BI1 does not begin in Year 11. The sequence below is the one Abu Dhabi families actually move through, from Key Stage 3 science into a two-year International GCSE course and on to International A Level Biology or Diploma Biology. Each stage changes what a biology tutor is for, and the handover points between them are where marks go quietly missing.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 Science
programmes.description: Three years of combined science that most British-curriculum schools in Abu Dhabi teach as a carousel, with biology appearing for a term at a time. The content is light but the habits are not: labelled diagrams, variables named correctly, units written on every answer. A Year 9 student who cannot yet draw a set of axes without prompting will lose marks in 4BI1 for reasons that have nothing to do with biology.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools option students into single sciences or Double Award at the end of Year 9, and the decision is often made on a single internal test. A term of Year 9 support is the cheapest intervention available, because it changes which qualification your child is entered for rather than trying to rescue the grade two years later.

programmes.name: International GCSE Biology
programmes.description: The Pearson single-award specification, graded 9 to 1 and assessed by Paper 1 and Paper 2 with no coursework. Five topics run across the two years: the nature and variety of living organisms, structures and functions in living organisms, reproduction and inheritance, ecology and the environment, and the use of biological resources. Paper 1 covers the first four; Paper 2 reaches all five.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi centres enter candidates in the May/June series and, increasingly, in November. Pearson publishes the final timetable for each series on its own site, and the entry deadline falls months before the first paper. A family planning a November entry should be having the conversation with the exams officer in the summer, not in October.

programmes.name: International A Level Biology
programmes.description: The Pearson post-16 route many Abu Dhabi students take straight out of 4BI1, structured in units and examined in January, May/June and October windows depending on the centre. The jump is not in the biology so much as in the writing: answers lengthen, the data questions carry statistics, and marks start depending on whether a student can explain a mechanism in order rather than list its parts.
programmes.countryNote: Students aiming at medicine or dentistry through UAE or UK universities usually need biology and chemistry together at this level. Where that is the plan, it is worth treating the second half of Year 11 as the first half of the A Level course, because the 4BI1 topics on transport and homeostasis are the ones that reappear immediately.

programmes.name: November resit and private candidates
programmes.description: Pearson runs International GCSE in a May/June series and a November series, which gives a student who missed a grade one clean retry without losing a year. A resit plan is not a repeat of the course. It starts from the marked script, if the centre releases it, and it targets the specific components where the marks were lost rather than re-teaching the topics that already worked.
programmes.countryNote: A private candidate in Abu Dhabi has to find a centre willing to accept external entries, pay the centre's own fee on top of the Pearson entry fee, and meet the centre's internal deadline rather than Pearson's. Start the search at least a full term ahead, because the places go early and some centres take no external candidates at all.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-biology-4bi1-tut.subjectsIntro: Biology is rarely the only subject in play. The list below is what Abu Dhabi 4BI1 students most often pair it with, and what each pairing does to a weekly timetable. Where a sibling subject shares a skill with biology, such as graph work, percentage change or extended prose, the two can be taught inside one session instead of booked twice.

subjects.name: Biology (4BI1)
subjects.description: The subject of this page. Two written papers, 180 marks, no coursework, graded 9 to 1. Most of the marks that go missing sit in three places: genetic diagrams drawn without a key, osmosis and transport answers that describe rather than explain, and ecology questions where the student writes biology but not the biology the command term asked for.

subjects.name: Chemistry (4CH1)
subjects.description: The usual partner subject, and the one that most changes a biology plan. Moles, concentration and percentage yield recur in biology data questions in a different costume. A student who is secure with calculations in 4CH1 generally picks up the quantitative marks in 4BI1 Paper 2 without any extra teaching, which is why we check the chemistry before adding biology hours.

subjects.name: Physics (4PH1)
subjects.description: Taken alongside biology by students keeping engineering open as well as medicine. The overlap is skills rather than content: rearranging equations, reading a gradient, and writing a conclusion that refers to the data. Where a student is strong in biology and weak in physics, the diagnosis is almost always maths rather than science, and the session plan should say so.

subjects.name: Human Biology (4HB1)
subjects.description: Pearson's separate human biology specification, offered by a small number of Abu Dhabi centres and occasionally chosen by private candidates. It shares a great deal with 4BI1 on structures and functions but treats plants and ecology differently. Check which code your child's centre has entered before buying any resource, because the past papers are not interchangeable.

subjects.name: Science Double Award (4SD0)
subjects.description: The three-science alternative that reports two International GCSE grades rather than three. Students move between 4SD0 and single-award biology more often than schools advertise, usually at the end of Year 10. If that move is on the table, a tutor should be mapping the extra single-award content before the transfer, not after.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.description: The quiet determinant of a biology grade. Paper 2 of 4BI1 rewards students who handle magnification, scale bars, percentage change and rates without stalling. Where a biology mock shows marks lost on every calculation question, the cheaper fix is four sessions of targeted number work rather than another pass through the specification.

subjects.name: English Language A (4EA1)
subjects.description: Biology at this level is a writing subject in disguise. Six-mark explanation questions are marked on sequence and linkage, and a student who writes in fragments loses marks they have the knowledge to earn. Families often book 4EA1 and 4BI1 together for exactly this reason, and the explanation-writing work transfers both ways.

subjects.name: Geography (4GE1)
subjects.description: Shares the ecology and human-impact ground with 4BI1 Topic 4, and shares its command terms almost exactly. Students who can structure a geography case-study answer usually find the biology ecosystem questions straightforward once somebody points out that the two are the same exercise with different vocabulary.

subjects.name: Business (4BS1)
subjects.description: Common in the Abu Dhabi option blocks as a counterweight to three sciences, and worth naming here because it competes for the same revision evenings. Where a student carries biology, chemistry and business into Year 11, the timetable rather than the content is the problem, and a tutor should be helping triage it.

subjects.name: International A Level Biology
subjects.description: Where 4BI1 leads for most students who enjoyed it. The transition work that pays best is not new content but note-taking and the discipline of answering in mechanism order. Students who finish 4BI1 in June and start the A Level in September benefit more from four summer sessions on that than from pre-reading the first unit.

sections.heading: What a 4BI1 tutor can actually show you after three weeks
paragraphs: Three weeks is about four sessions. That is not long enough to raise a grade, and any page telling you otherwise is selling. It is long enough to produce four specific things, and if they are missing at the end of week three you are not buying tuition, you are buying company.

The first is a baseline script. A section of a released 4BI1 paper, attempted cold without notes, marked against the published mark scheme, with each lost mark attributed to a topic number and to a command term. The second is a ranked list: the two topics costing the most marks, with the figures beside them, not a general sense that genetics is weak. The third is a record of what was taught in each session, in one line each, so the teaching can be checked against the ranked list. The fourth is a second script on unseen material of comparable difficulty, so the first can be compared with something.

Those four artefacts let you ask a question that tuition rarely survives: did the sessions address the topics the baseline identified, and did the second script improve on the first in those topics specifically? A general improvement across everything is usually practice effect. An improvement concentrated in the two topics that were taught is evidence. A decline is information too, and it is better to have it in October than in March.

Parents sometimes worry this sounds clinical for a fifteen-year-old. In practice students prefer it. The vague version of tutoring, where nobody says what is wrong, is far more demoralising than a sheet saying that Topic 3 is costing nine marks and that nine marks is most of a grade boundary.

sections.heading: The two 4BI1 papers and where the 180 marks sit
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Biology is assessed entirely by written examination. There is no internally assessed component and no coursework folder, which means there is nothing to submit, nothing to supervise and nothing a tutor could improperly influence. It also means the whole grade rests on two sittings.

Paper 1 is the long paper and carries 110 of the 180 marks on offer, a little over three fifths of the qualification. It draws on the first four topics. Paper 2 carries the remaining 70 marks and is the only component in which Topic 5, the use of biological resources, can be examined, alongside material from the earlier topics. The practical content of the specification is examined through these written papers rather than in a separate practical exam, which is why so many 4BI1 questions describe an experiment and ask the student to interpret it.

The consequence for planning is simple and most families miss it. A student who is strong on cells, transport and inheritance but has never touched fermentation, selective breeding or fish farming has capped their Paper 2 before they sit down. Because Paper 2 is the shorter paper, a weak Topic 5 does less damage than a weak Topic 2 overall, but it is also the easiest gap to close, since the topic is finite and heavily factual.

Always confirm the current component structure, durations and mark totals on the live specification at qualifications.pearson.com before buying resources. Pearson revises specifications and publishes the authoritative version itself; a page like this one is a guide to what to look for, not a substitute for the document your child's centre is teaching from.

sections.heading: Reading a marked 4BI1 script when you are not a biologist
paragraphs: A marked script is the most useful document in this process and the one parents most often file away unread. You do not need the biology to read it. You need to know what the command term at the start of the question was asking for, because that single word sets the entire marking.

Edexcel questions are built from a small vocabulary of instructions, and each one has a price. State and name are one mark each and want nothing more than the word. Describe asks what happens and collects marks for observations. Explain asks why it happens and collects marks for mechanism, which is why a student who describes an explain question beautifully can score nothing. Calculate wants working shown, because method marks survive an arithmetic slip. Suggest signals that the context is unfamiliar and the examiner is accepting any scientifically sound reasoning.

Once you know that, the pattern in a script becomes visible without any subject knowledge. If the zeros cluster on explain questions, the problem is not revision, it is writing. If they cluster on calculate, the problem is maths. If they are spread evenly across a topic, the content genuinely is not known. Those three diagnoses lead to three completely different session plans, and guessing between them is how a term gets wasted.

This is also the quickest way to judge a tutor. Ask what the last script showed, by command term. A tutor working from evidence will answer in thirty seconds. A tutor working from impression will talk about confidence.

sections.heading: The 4BI1 topics that cost Abu Dhabi candidates the most marks
paragraphs: Across the 4BI1 scripts that reach us from Abu Dhabi centres, the losses are not evenly spread. Four areas account for a disproportionate share, and three of the four are fixable in a handful of sessions because the problem is technique rather than knowledge.

Transport in plants and animals is the first. Students learn the structures and then meet a question about water movement under a changed condition and describe the structure again. The mark scheme wants the mechanism in order: concentration gradient, movement, consequence. Inheritance is the second, and here the losses are almost entirely presentational. A genetic cross drawn without defining the allele symbols, or a Punnett square with no phenotype ratio stated, throws away marks the student has clearly earned in their head.

The third is Topic 5, the use of biological resources, which appears only in Paper 2 and is routinely the last thing taught and the first thing forgotten. Fermenters, selective breeding, fish farming and glasshouse production are finite, factual and quick to secure, which makes them the best value revision in the specification. The fourth is quantitative work: magnification, scale bars, rates and percentage change. These are maths marks wearing a biology costume, and they go missing in clusters.

Ecology sits slightly apart. The content is usually known, but the answers are written as general environmental comment rather than as biology. The repair is a vocabulary discipline: name the organism, name the process, state the effect on the population. It takes two sessions and it moves marks in both papers.

sections.heading: Practical biology with no practical exam, and what that means for online lessons
paragraphs: Parents reasonably ask how a subject with this much laboratory work can be tutored over video. The answer starts with how Pearson assesses it. Practical skills in this specification are examined inside the written papers, not in a separate practical examination, so what is actually being tested is a student's ability to read an experimental setup, identify variables, interpret results and write a conclusion the data supports.

Every one of those is a paper skill. A tutor sharing a screen can put an unfamiliar apparatus diagram in front of a student, ask what is being controlled and why, and work through the answer in the same way an examiner will read it. Where a diagram needs drawing, the student draws on the shared whiteboard or photographs their page and uploads it, which is in some ways better than a classroom, because the drawing survives the session and can be compared with the next one.

What online delivery cannot do is replace the hands. A student who has never set up a potometer or watched an enzyme reaction change with temperature holds the knowledge more loosely than one who has. That work belongs in the school laboratory, and the right move is to make sure your child is actually doing it there rather than watching a partner do it. A tutor can tell you which of the specification's practicals matter most for the written papers, so the limited lab time is spent on those.

This is the honest version of the online case for biology, and it is not a compromise. The marks live in interpretation and in writing. Those are exactly the parts that one-to-one teaching with a shared screen and a marked script does better than a room with twenty-four students in it.

sections.heading: What 4BI1 tuition costs in Abu Dhabi, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible tutoring sites in this market publish no price at all, and two of the remaining quote in US dollars, which UAE families do not transact in. The table below collects what the market actually charges in dirhams, with each band attributed to the provider or survey that published it. These are market rates, not IB Gram's price list. Our own quote follows the free trial lesson, once the tutor knows how much marking the plan involves.

The variables that move a science quote in Abu Dhabi are predictable. Format is the largest: a visiting hour includes travel the family pays for, which is why in-home bands sit well above online ones in every published survey. Specialism is next, because a tutor who teaches 4BI1 specifically rather than general science commands more, and reasonably so. Session length matters less than parents expect, since a 90-minute session is rarely half again the price of a 60-minute one. Marking between sessions is the hidden variable, and the one worth paying for in a subject assessed entirely by written paper.

Timing moves the number too. Quotes firm up as a series approaches and availability tightens in the four to six weeks before the first paper, which is also when the least useful work gets booked. A family that starts in October for a May/June entry pays the quieter rate and gets the better tutor. A family that starts in April pays the busy rate for crisis management.

Two figures worth holding beside the tutoring cost. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27 under Dubai's economic incentives package, which tells you something about the direction of education costs in the region generally. And the private tuition work permit itself is issued free of charge, so any quote presenting a licensing fee as a line item should be questioned.

sections.heading: Online, visiting and group tuition compared for an Abu Dhabi family
paragraphs: The question behind most searches for a biology tutor in Abu Dhabi is not really online or in-home. It is whether the person teaching your child knows 4BI1 well enough to read a mark scheme out loud and explain why an answer scored two out of four. Format matters because it decides how wide the pool of such people is.

A visiting tutor has to live within a tolerable drive. From Al Shamkha or Al Reef at five in the afternoon, that radius is small, and it shrinks further once you require a biology specialist rather than a general science tutor. Online delivery removes the radius entirely. A family in Al Falah can work with someone who has taught the inheritance and resources topics for a decade, at a time that does not depend on the Sheikh Zayed bridge.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tuition is a service we run only in India. That is a limit, and it belongs on the page rather than in the small print. What replaces it is one-to-one teaching over live video with screen sharing, a shared whiteboard, the option to record, and written marking between sessions. For a subject assessed by two written papers, that is not a lesser version of the service. The artefacts the papers reward are documents, and documents travel better than people do.

Group tuition deserves a straight answer too. For 4BI1 it works for content coverage and fails for diagnosis, because the whole value of the marked-script approach is that it is about one student's errors. A group class of six cannot do that, and should be priced and judged as revision, not as tuition.

sections.heading: The Pearson series counted backwards from the entry deadline
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a calendar, and it is the single most useful thing a page about an exam can contain. Pearson runs International GCSE in a May/June series and a November series each year. The deadlines that matter to a family sit months before the first paper, and they are set by the centre as often as by Pearson.

The published reference points are these. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. The November 2025 series results reached students on 22 January 2026, which is the right expectation to hold for a November entry rather than a date to rely on. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, and those are the documents to work from because dates can be revised.

Read backwards, that gives a usable plan. If the goal is a May/June entry, the content should be complete by the February half term, with the spring term spent on timed papers and marking. If the goal is a November entry, the serious work happens over the summer, because October is already inside the exam window. A resit decision after August results has to be made quickly, since the centre's internal deadline for a November entry may already have passed.

One caution that applies to every date on this page. Always take exam dates from the official timetable at qualifications.pearson.com, and confirm entry deadlines with your child's exams officer, because the centre's internal cut-off is usually earlier than the board's. Cambridge makes the same point more bluntly for its own series: centres are allocated to administrative zones, and it says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone's timetable.

sections.heading: ADEK, the permit, and the five-subject equivalency rule
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi private schools are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge. The federal portal u.ae states that ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, which is a different arrangement from Dubai, where KHDA oversees the quality of private education, and from Sharjah, where the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates it. ADEK is named by effectively none of the competing tutoring pages in this market, which is a strange gap given that it publishes the inspection ratings Abu Dhabi parents read.

Private tutoring itself sits with a different ministry. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and u.ae states that it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no figure should be quoted to you by anyone, including us. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing.

There is one Abu Dhabi-specific rule worth knowing before you ask a teacher for private help. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE permit's code of conduct making a similar point. We treat that as press-reported rather than as ADEK's exact wording, and the sensible step is to check the current ADEK policy document before arranging anything. Either way, asking your child's own biology teacher to tutor them for payment is the wrong first move.

Finally, what the grade is for. For the British track, Ministry of Education equivalency requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. A 4BI1 grade can be one of those five. One well-ranked competitor page tells UAE families they need six IGCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five, and it is worth checking the current requirement on moe.gov.ae yourself because this is a regulatory process, not a tutoring one. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency, and no tutoring is required for it.

process.title: Send the last marked script
process.description: The most useful thing you can send is not a description of the problem but the last marked biology paper or mock, however bad it looks. If the school has not released it, ask the exams officer or the head of science for it; most will share a mock script with a parent who asks directly. A screenshot of the mark breakdown is enough to start.

process.title: Free trial lesson, with a cold diagnostic
process.description: The trial lesson costs nothing and takes no card details. Most of it is the student attempting a short section of a released 4BI1 paper without notes while the tutor watches how they read the question. That is more informative than any conversation about confidence, and it produces the baseline the rest of the plan is measured against.

process.title: A two-page plan ranked by marks lost
process.description: Within a couple of days you receive a short written plan: the two topics costing the most marks with the figures beside them, the command terms being misread, the session shape proposed, and the date of the first re-test. If the plan does not name topics and numbers, say so and ask for one that does.

process.title: Weekly sessions with marking between them
process.description: Sessions run at a fixed time on Gulf Standard Time, one-to-one over live video. Between them the student attempts a short paper section, and the tutor marks it against the published scheme before the next session. The marking is the part that produces evidence, and it is the part worth paying for in a subject assessed only by written paper.

process.title: Week-five re-test and a decision point
process.description: In week five the student sits an unseen section of comparable difficulty and the two scripts are compared, topic by topic. That comparison decides whether the plan continues, changes shape or stops. Changing tutor at this point is a normal outcome, not a complaint, and it costs nothing.

whyPoints.title: Marks attributed to topics, not to adjectives
whyPoints.description: Every review point names a topic number and a figure. You should be able to read a one-page summary and know which part of 4BI1 cost the most marks last month and what was done about it, without knowing any biology yourself. Pages that promise progress without naming a component are describing a feeling.

whyPoints.title: A specialist rather than a radius
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means the filter on who teaches your child is whether they know this specification, not whether they can reach Al Shamkha before six. For a single-award science with five defined topics and two papers, that difference shows up in the first session, usually in how the tutor talks about Topic 5.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are attributed to the provider or survey that published them, with the format they apply to. Three of the most visible competing sites in this market publish no price at all. Knowing the bands lets you judge any quote, including ours, which arrives after the free trial lesson rather than before it.

whyPoints.title: A clear line around the student's own work
whyPoints.description: 4BI1 has no coursework, but school assignments, practical write-ups and investigation reports still get set. A tutor teaches, questions and marks. Nobody at IB Gram supplies a finished piece of work for submission or an answer to be copied across, and that boundary is stated here because competing pages in this market sell exactly that.

whyPoints.title: Permit and conduct questions answered before you book
whyPoints.description: The private tuition work permit route, who is eligible, and the position on a child's own school teacher are set out on this page with their sources. You should not have to ask a tutoring service whether what it is arranging is permitted in the emirate, and you should be suspicious of any page that avoids the subject.

whyPoints.title: Recordings and notes that stay with you
whyPoints.description: Sessions can be recorded on request and the marked scripts remain yours. If the arrangement ends, the evidence does not. That matters most when a family moves school or emirate mid-course, which happens often enough in Abu Dhabi that the next tutor should never have to start the diagnosis from nothing.

faqs.question: How much does an Edexcel IGCSE Biology 4BI1 tutor cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in this emirate run roughly AED 45-150 an hour for budget online help, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 200-450 or more for an International GCSE specialist. Visiting tutors sit higher, at AED 180-500, because travel is inside the price. Those figures come from the providers and rate surveys named in the cost table above, not from us. IB Gram quotes after the free trial lesson, once the tutor knows how much marking between sessions the plan needs, which in a subject assessed by two written papers is the part that actually changes the price.

faqs.question: Does Edexcel IGCSE Biology 4BI1 include a practical exam my child has to sit?
faqs.answer: No. The specification is assessed by two written papers with no separately examined practical and no coursework. Practical skills are tested inside those papers, which is why so many questions describe an apparatus or a set of results and ask the student to identify the variables, interpret the data or write a conclusion. That has a direct consequence for tutoring: the skills worth practising are reading an unfamiliar experiment and writing about it precisely. The hands-on work still matters for understanding and belongs in the school laboratory, so make sure your child is doing it there rather than watching a lab partner.

faqs.question: How are Paper 1 and Paper 2 weighted in 4BI1?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries 110 of the 180 marks available and draws on the first four topics of the specification. Paper 2 carries the remaining 70 marks and is the only place Topic 5, the use of biological resources, can be examined, though it can also reach back into earlier material. Confirm the current durations and totals on the live specification at qualifications.pearson.com, since Pearson revises its own documents. The planning point is that a student who has never revised Topic 5 has limited their shorter paper before they start, and that topic is finite and quick to secure.

faqs.question: Which 4BI1 topics do Abu Dhabi students lose the most marks on?
faqs.answer: Four areas account for most of the losses in the scripts that reach us. Transport in plants and animals, where students describe structures when the question asked them to explain movement. Inheritance, where the biology is right but the genetic diagram has no defined symbols or no stated ratio. Topic 5, which is taught last and revised never. And quantitative work such as magnification, scale bars and percentage change, which is really maths. Three of those four are technique rather than knowledge, which is why they move quickly once a marked script shows which one is responsible.

faqs.question: Can a 4BI1 tutor help with the practical write-ups my child's school sets?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the skills the write-up is testing, mark a draft the student has produced, and ask the questions that make the student find their own weak paragraph. What nobody at IB Gram will do is supply text for submission, rewrite a report to a finished state, or provide an answer to be copied across. There is no coursework component in 4BI1 itself, so the submitted work here is internal to the school, but the principle is the same one that applies to assessed coursework and it is worth being explicit about, because competing pages in this market sell the opposite.

faqs.question: My child sits 4BI1 in the November series. Is six weeks of tutoring enough?
faqs.answer: Six weeks changes paper technique reliably and content coverage only partially. If the specification has been taught and the marks are going missing on command terms, timing and calculation, six weeks of twice-weekly sessions with marking in between is a sensible plan and usually shows in a timed paper by week three. If whole topics have never been covered, six weeks is triage, and the honest conversation is about which components to protect. Either way, the first session should be a cold paper section rather than a revision lecture, because the plan depends on knowing which of the two situations you are in.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 4BI1 and taking biology inside Science Double Award?
faqs.answer: Single-award 4BI1 reports one International GCSE grade in biology and covers the subject in more depth, including Topic 5 on the use of biological resources. Science Double Award reports two grades across biology, chemistry and physics together and covers less of each. Students aiming at International A Level biology or at medicine generally want the single award. Abu Dhabi schools option students into one route or the other around the end of Year 9, often on one internal test, and movement between the two in Year 10 is more common than schools advertise. Ask which code your child is actually entered for.

faqs.question: Is Edexcel 4BI1 harder than Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610?
faqs.answer: They are different in structure rather than in difficulty. Pearson's 4BI1 uses two written papers with practical skills examined inside them. Cambridge's biology syllabus is tiered and includes an alternative-to-practical style component, and Cambridge runs June and November series with centres allocated to administrative zones, each with its own timetable. The practical consequence for a family is that past papers are not interchangeable, so buy nothing until you have confirmed the code on your child's statement of entry. A tutor who cannot tell you which board the school entered should not be marking the scripts.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child's Abu Dhabi school entered Edexcel or Cambridge for biology?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer for the statement of entry, which lists the specification code against each subject. It is the fastest and most reliable route, and the code matters: 4BI1 is Pearson's single-award biology, 4SD0 is its Double Award, and Cambridge uses an entirely different numbering. Schools in the same part of Abu Dhabi sometimes use different boards, and some centres enter different boards for different subjects within one student's timetable. Textbook covers and department habits from previous years are not evidence. Get the code in writing before buying resources or booking tuition.

faqs.question: Does a private biology tutor in Abu Dhabi need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, which states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted with suspicion. The application route is MoHRE's own service page for private tutor licensing.

faqs.question: How many 4BI1 sessions a week do Abu Dhabi families usually start with?
faqs.answer: One a week is the normal starting point for a Year 10 or early Year 11 student, with a short paper section marked between sessions. Two a week makes sense in the four to six weeks before a series, or where whole topics are missing rather than technique. A Year 10 student already holding a strong grade is often better served by one session a fortnight built around work they have already done. The deciding evidence is the week-five re-test rather than a parent's or tutor's instinct, which is why that date is set at the start.

faqs.question: Can my child's own biology teacher tutor them privately in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Treat that as the wrong starting point. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers giving paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct making a similar point. We treat that reporting as press-sourced rather than as ADEK's exact wording, so check the current ADEK policy document before arranging anything. A separate tutor who does not teach at the school avoids the question entirely, and also gives your child a second explanation of the same topic.

faqs.question: Does a 4BI1 grade count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: It can be one of the five subjects the British track requires. The sourced rule is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count of five. One well-ranked competing page tells UAE families they need six subjects. Check the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority yourself, because equivalency is a regulatory process that IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee.

faqs.question: How do online 4BI1 lessons handle diagrams, graphs and data tables?
faqs.answer: With a shared whiteboard and screen sharing, which for this subject is an advantage rather than a workaround. The tutor can put an apparatus diagram or a results table on screen, annotate it live, and ask the student to label or extend it. Where the student needs to draw, they either draw on the whiteboard or photograph their page and upload it, and that image stays in the record for comparison with the next attempt. Sessions can be recorded on request, so a mechanism drawn once in October is still rewatchable the night before the paper.

faqs.question: Can 4BI1 sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they usually should. School days shorten during Ramadan and concentration in the late afternoon is not what it is in February, so the useful hours shift. Families commonly move a 5pm slot to after Iftar, or switch to shorter and more frequent sessions. Because delivery is online there is no travel to rearrange, which makes the change a scheduling message rather than a renegotiation. The content plan matters here too: Ramadan is better spent on paper technique and consolidation than on introducing a new topic for the first time.

faqs.question: What happens if the first 4BI1 tutor is not the right fit?
faqs.answer: You say so and we change the tutor at no extra charge. Nobody should spend a term on a mismatch, and a subject-specialist match is not an exact science, particularly for a fifteen-year-old who has to be willing to be wrong out loud. The week-five review exists partly for this: if the re-test shows no movement in the topics that were taught, that is evidence about the match rather than about your child. Marked scripts and session notes stay with you, so the next tutor starts from the diagnosis rather than from the beginning.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-biology-4bi1-tut.closingHeading: Start with the script you already have
abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-biology-4bi1-tut.closingBody: You almost certainly have the most useful document in this process already: your child's last marked biology paper. Send it, book the free trial lesson, and let the first session be a cold attempt at a section of a released 4BI1 paper rather than a conversation about confidence. What comes back is a short written plan naming the two topics costing the most marks, the command terms being misread, and a date in week five when the whole thing gets re-tested. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. If the evidence does not move, you will know in a month, and so will we.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-business-4bs1-tu.tutorsIntro: The tutors below currently take Edexcel IGCSE Business 4BS1 students across Abu Dhabi. Each works from the Pearson specification and from past stimulus material, because a Business answer that ignores the firm in the source loses application marks regardless of how good the theory is.

intro.heading: Why 4BS1 trips up students who understand business perfectly well
paragraphs: Business is the option subject most often chosen because it sounds manageable, and most often misjudged for the same reason. The content genuinely is accessible: a bright Year 10 can read about cash flow, marketing mix and economies of scale and feel entirely on top of it. Then the mock arrives and the marks are thin in places that make no sense to the family. The student knew the material. What they did not do was answer the question about the business in front of them, which is the thing Pearson is paying marks for.

Application is the whole game in 4BS1. The paper hands the student a short account of a specific firm, with figures, a sector, a location and a problem. A general answer about why marketing matters earns knowledge marks and stalls. An answer that names what this firm sells, uses the numbers given, and explains the consequence for this firm's cash position keeps climbing. Students almost never fail because they do not know what break-even means. They fail because they explain break-even instead of calculating it for the company in the extract and then saying what the result implies.

The second weakness is numerical, and it surprises parents who chose Business partly to avoid maths. Edexcel International GCSE Business expects calculation: break-even output and margin of safety, cash-flow forecasts, revenue, costs and profit, and a set of ratios used to judge performance. None of it is hard arithmetic. All of it is easy to lose marks on, because the follow-up question asks what the figure means for the business, and a student who has only memorised the formula has nothing to say at that point.

Then there is the writing. The longest questions ask for a recommendation or a judgement about a course of action for the named firm, and the mark scheme rewards a decision supported by the evidence in the extract, with a stated condition or risk. Students instinctively write a balanced list of advantages and disadvantages and leave the examiner to choose, which is precisely the structure that caps a script below the top band. It is fixable in a handful of marked attempts, and almost impossible to fix without any.

For Abu Dhabi families there is a practical layer on top. Business departments in the emirate's British-curriculum schools are often small, with one teacher covering several year groups, so line-by-line feedback on long answers is scarce. Add Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies alongside the licensed curriculum and a Year 11 week has very little slack in it. Lessons here run online over live video, which removes travel at both ends and keeps a weekly slot alive through a term that gets progressively busier.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-business-4bs1-tu.programmesIntro: Business sits inside a longer commercial route, and the sensible tutoring plan depends on where your child is in it. These are the stages at which families in Abu Dhabi most often ask for help, and what changes at each.

programmes.name: Year 9 option choice
programmes.description: The point at which Business, Economics, Accounting and sometimes Commerce compete for the same slot. Choosing badly costs two years, and the usual mistake is picking on perceived difficulty rather than on how the student writes. A single session using one past extract from each subject shows a family more than a school options evening can.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools vary in which commerce subjects they can staff, so the real option list is narrower than the specification catalogue suggests. Ask the head of department which codes were entered last year rather than which subjects appear in the prospectus; small departments drop and add options between cohorts.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Business
programmes.description: The qualification on this page. Content spans business activity and external influences, people in business, finance, marketing and operations. Assessment is written only, with stimulus material about real or realistic firms, calculation questions, and extended questions asking for a justified recommendation. Grades are reported on the 9-1 scale under the current specification.
programmes.countryNote: In the emirate, 4BS1 is frequently taken alongside Mathematics A and English Language A, with Economics or ICT filling the final option. Students who later move to an IB sixth form find Business Management familiar in content and completely different in assessment, so the writing habits built now are the part that transfers.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level Business
programmes.description: The direct continuation. The step up is in the length of evaluation and the expectation that a student handles unfamiliar quantitative data without prompting. Students who scored well at IGCSE through recall alone struggle in the first term, because A Level marks reward the reasoning rather than the terminology.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi sixth forms run International A Level Business or Economics, and UAE universities publish their own subject requirements for business and finance degrees. Check the current entry criteria on the university's admissions pages directly, since requirements change year to year and a tutor's summary is not a source.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Business Management
programmes.description: The alternative route at the emirate's IB schools. It adds an internal assessment based on a real organisation, which means research and referencing become part of the grade. Strong 4BS1 students adapt quickly on content and need specific help with the internal assessment format, which has no IGCSE equivalent.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has a well-established group of IB schools alongside its British-curriculum sector, and moving between the two at sixteen is common. Where that move is planned, a Business tutor can start building research and source-handling habits in Year 11 so the first DP term is not spent learning how to reference.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-business-4bs1-tu.subjectsIntro: These are the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects most often paired with Business in Abu Dhabi, with the code schools enter and the part of each course that generates tutoring requests.

subjects.name: Business (4BS1)
subjects.description: Written assessment only, covering business activity and influences, people, finance, marketing and operations. The pressure points are application to the firm in the extract, the calculation set, and extended questions that want a justified recommendation rather than a balanced list of points.

subjects.name: Accounting (4AC1)
subjects.description: The closest companion subject and the one most often underestimated. Accounting marks are awarded for format, labelling, dates and workings as well as for the final figure, so a student used to writing explanations in Business has to learn a far more exact style of answer.

subjects.name: Economics (4EC1)
subjects.description: Shares vocabulary with Business and rewards the opposite instinct: generalisable theory and traced chains of reasoning rather than application to one named firm. Students taking both need the two answer shapes kept deliberately distinct, which is a recurring job in sessions.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.description: Supplies the arithmetic Business assumes: percentages, ratio, averages and reading graphs. Foundation-tier students often need ratio and percentage change secured before Business ratio analysis stops costing marks, which is a short, well-defined piece of work.

subjects.name: ICT (4IT1)
subjects.description: Half of the qualification is a practical examination worked on provided files, including spreadsheet modelling that mirrors the cash-flow and break-even work in Business. The two reinforce each other usefully, though the practical paper needs its own timed rehearsal under exam conditions.

subjects.name: English Language A (4EA1)
subjects.description: Business long answers and 4EA1 extended writing reward the same discipline: a clear claim, evidence used rather than mentioned, and a developed consequence. Where Business scripts show knowledge in disorganised paragraphs, work on structure tends to lift both subjects at once.

subjects.name: Geography (4GE1)
subjects.description: Overlaps with Business on data response, case studies and writing about change over time, including industrial location and development. Students taking both can be taught one method for handling an unseen source, which saves time in the Year 11 revision period.

subjects.name: Computer Science (4CP0)
subjects.description: A frequent fourth option, with a written principles paper and a practical programming examination. It is the least self-teachable subject in the option block, and families often ask about it in the same enquiry as Business because both receive limited timetabled support.

subjects.name: History (4HI1)
subjects.description: The other extended-writing option in most Abu Dhabi option blocks. History rewards weighted argument about causation; Business rewards a decision about what a firm should do next. Keeping the two conclusions styles separate is worth one explicit session for students taking both.

sections.heading: What a 4BS1 tutor in Abu Dhabi spends the first three sessions doing
paragraphs: The first three sessions of Edexcel IGCSE Business tutoring are diagnostic, and they are not spent teaching content. Session one takes a past stimulus extract and asks the student to read it aloud and say what is usable: what the firm sells, who it sells to, what has changed, what the figures show, and what problem the extract is setting up. Most students have never been asked to do this deliberately, and the answer reveals immediately whether the application weakness is a reading habit or a writing habit.

Session two is a short timed set of questions across different mark tariffs, marked afterwards against the published mark scheme. The purpose is to separate three things that look identical on a report card: not knowing the content, knowing it but not applying it to the firm, and knowing and applying it but running out of time. Those three problems need completely different plans, and guessing between them wastes a term.

Session three is the first rewrite. The student receives their marked script with the mark-scheme wording beside their own, and rewrites the two weakest answers in the session rather than at home. Doing it live matters, because the tutor can see where the student stalls: often at the point where a general statement needs to become a specific consequence for the named firm, which is exactly the sentence the marks are attached to.

By the end of three sessions a family should have a written diagnosis they can read, not a reassurance they have to trust. That diagnosis names the problem, the target and the evidence that will show movement. If it turns out the student's issue is something tutoring cannot fix on its own, such as unmanaged exam anxiety or a timetable with no study time in it, that is worth saying early rather than after four months of invoices.

sections.heading: The 4BS1 content map, and where each topic area actually surfaces
paragraphs: Pearson organises International GCSE Business content into several topic areas covering business activity and the influences on it, people in business, business finance, marketing, and business operations. Assessment is written only. What matters for revision planning is that the topic areas do not arrive in neat blocks on the paper: a single extract about one firm can pull in marketing, operations and finance in consecutive questions, so revising in isolated silos leaves students unable to switch.

The practical consequence is that late revision should be organised around firm types rather than around chapter headings. A student who has worked through extracts about a manufacturer, a service business, a retailer and a start-up has met the same theory in four different contexts and can recognise which part of the specification a question is reaching for. A student who has revised chapter by chapter knows more and retrieves less.

External influences deserve particular attention for students in the Gulf, because the examples that come naturally to them are often better than the textbook ones. Exchange-rate movement, fuel and utility costs, import dependence, labour mobility and government policy are all live realities for firms operating here, and a student who can use a genuine local example with confidence writes more convincingly than one reciting a generic case. The caution is that the extract always wins: a local example supports the point, it never replaces the firm given.

Confirm the current topic structure, paper codes and timings against the live 4BS1 specification and sample assessment materials on qualifications.pearson.com, and confirm with the school which series and code your child is entered for. Schools occasionally run a transitional cohort on a legacy code, and a tutor working from the wrong version will drill the wrong answer shapes.

sections.heading: Application: the sentence where most 4BS1 marks are won or lost
paragraphs: Application in Business has a recognisable sentence shape, and once a student can produce it reliably their marks move. The shape is: because this firm does something specific named in the extract, the consequence is a particular effect on a stated measure. Both halves are necessary. Students routinely produce the second half on its own, which reads as theory, or the first half on its own, which reads as a summary of the extract. The mark is attached to the join.

The reason this is hard has nothing to do with intelligence. Students are taught business concepts in class, and concepts are general by nature, so the instinct under exam pressure is to reach for the general version. Overriding that instinct requires practice with a pen in hand, not an explanation. This is why sessions are built around attempting and rewriting rather than around being taught: the student has to produce the specific sentence often enough that it becomes the default.

A second habit worth building is figure discipline. If the extract gives a cost, a price, a number of staff or a growth rate, the examiner has put it there to be used. Answers that ignore every number provided have told the marker that the student did not read carefully. Answers that quote a figure and then draw a consequence from it look exactly like the top band of the mark scheme, because that is what the top band describes.

Finally, recommendation questions need a decision. The mark scheme rewards a choice, justified by evidence from the extract, with an acknowledged risk or a condition under which the answer would change. A student who writes three paragraphs of balanced discussion and then declines to decide has written a good essay and a mediocre exam answer. Teaching that distinction explicitly, and then marking against it, is usually the single highest-value intervention available in this subject.
bullets: Name the firm, its sector and what it actually sells in the first line of a long answer
Use at least one figure from the extract whenever figures are provided
Trace one consequence properly rather than listing four undeveloped ones
On recommendation questions, decide, justify from the extract, then state the risk
Keep local Gulf examples as support for the extract, never as a substitute for it

sections.heading: The quantitative half of Business that students skip until February
paragraphs: Business calculation is where confident students lose marks quietly. The arithmetic is simple enough that nobody treats it as a revision priority, and the questions are structured so that the calculation is worth a few marks and the interpretation that follows is worth more. A student who can compute break-even but cannot say what a thin margin of safety means for a firm facing a rent increase has banked the small half of the marks and left the large half on the table.

The recurring errors are consistent and therefore trainable. Mixing per-unit and total figures. Using monthly data in an annual formula. Forgetting that a cash-flow forecast carries a closing balance forward as the next month's opening balance. Treating profit and cash as interchangeable, which is the conceptual error most likely to wreck an otherwise strong answer about a firm's survival. Each of these takes minutes to diagnose from a marked script and a session or two to fix properly.

The method we use is deliberately boring: each calculation is practised in the exam's own question format, then immediately paired with an interpretation prompt, so the student never learns the formula in isolation. After a few weeks the calculation stops being the obstacle and the interpretation becomes the thing being taught, which is the right order. Spreadsheet work helps here, and students taking ICT 4IT1 alongside Business often find the two subjects reinforcing each other.
