sections.heading: Business 4BS1 or Economics 4EC1? A straight comparison for Abu Dhabi option blocks
paragraphs: This is the most common question we get from Year 9 families in the emirate, and the honest answer is that the subjects reward different students rather than one being easier. Business is concrete: a named firm, a decision to make, numbers to use, a recommendation to justify. Economics is abstract: a market, a mechanism, a diagram used as evidence, a chain of reasoning traced to a consequence. A student who likes deciding things prefers Business. A student who likes explaining why things happen prefers Economics.

There is a writing difference too. Business long answers are short and decisive, built around the extract. Economics extended answers are longer and more argumentative, and reward a weighed judgement with conditions. Students who write fluently but struggle to commit to a position often do better in Economics, where the discussion itself earns marks for longer. Students who write briskly and dislike open-endedness usually score higher in Business.

Taking both is a reasonable choice and plenty of students in the emirate do. The risk is cross-contamination: writing a Business-style answer in an Economics paper, which skips the mechanism, or an Economics-style answer in Business, which never mentions the firm. If both are taken, the two answer shapes should be taught side by side and deliberately contrasted early, rather than left for the student to separate under exam pressure in Year 11.

Neither subject is a prerequisite for a business or economics degree at most universities, and neither closes a door. Check the published entry requirements for the courses your child has in mind, including those at UAE universities, rather than relying on staffroom received wisdom. Where a student is undecided, one session with a past extract from each paper is the cheapest way to find out which style of thinking they actually enjoy.

sections.heading: The evidence pack: what a parent should receive, and how often
paragraphs: Business tutoring is easy to deliver badly and hard to audit, because an hour spent discussing a company is pleasant and feels useful. The only defence is a short, fixed cycle of documented evidence. Our default is a marked script every fortnight, a one-line target after every session, and a mark trend on repeated question types reviewed at week six. None of that is impressive on its own. Collectively it is the difference between knowing whether something is working and hoping it is.

What we deliberately do not supply is a predicted grade. A prediction from a handful of papers on a 9-1 scale is statistically meaningless, and it invites exactly the wrong conversation. What is meaningful is movement on a particular question type: application marks on long answers, or the interpretation marks that follow a calculation. Those are the figures in the tracker, and they move or they do not.

We also do not supply reproductions of board material. Pearson publishes the specification, sample assessment materials, past papers and mark schemes under its own terms; those are referenced and linked from the official site rather than copied into handouts. Besides the copyright position, working from the live site means the version is current, which matters in a subject where specifications are periodically revised.

At week six, the review is a decision point rather than a progress report. If the marks on the targeted question type have not moved, the honest options are a different tutor, a different plan, or an acknowledgement that the obstacle is outside the session. Carrying on unchanged because everyone is being polite is the most expensive outcome available, and it is also the most common.

sections.heading: What Business tutoring costs in Abu Dhabi, and how to compare two quotes
paragraphs: Most providers in this market will not publish a number, so here is the market as it stood in October 2026. Advertised online rates from low-cost platforms start around AED 33 to 52 an hour at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik, with the broader budget band running to about AED 150. Qualified subject tutors working online advertise from roughly AED 150, which is where Unitors lists IGCSE, rising to about AED 300. Specialist IGCSE and A Level tutors are quoted between AED 200 and AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing around AED 270 and premium examiner-led provision reaching AED 650 at BartyED.

In-home provision is priced differently because somebody has to pay for the driving. Bestimate's rate table for the market puts home visits around AED 180 to 350, independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500, and monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions appear at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Online monthly packages advertise around AED 799 for eight sessions. These figures belong to the providers named and were read in October 2026; they are not IB Gram prices.

Comparing two quotes sensibly means comparing what the hour contains. An hour of conversation, an hour of teaching with homework set, and an hour that includes a marked script with mark-scheme comparison cost different amounts to supply and produce different results. Ask any provider three questions: who marks the extended answers, against what, and what document the parent receives. The answers separate the market faster than the headline rate does.

For context on the wider cost picture, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. School fees are the dominant education cost in most households, and tutoring is a small fraction of it, which is worth keeping in view when deciding between one well-evidenced session a week and three cheap ones nobody follows up.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and why an option subject makes it relevant
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai's equivalent is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. ADEK is named by almost none of the tutoring content written for this emirate, which says a good deal about how much of it was actually written for Abu Dhabi.

This matters to a Business family in a specific way. Inspection reporting is public, and it is the only external account of a school's performance that is not written by the school. For a small option department, the inspection commentary on teaching quality in the subject area is more informative than a prospectus. Where a department is thin, outside support is not a criticism of the school; it is a sensible response to a staffing reality.

Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not merely inspection sits with the emirate regulator. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That federal baseline is the reason your child carries mandatory UAE subjects alongside the Edexcel timetable, and it is a real constraint on how many tutoring hours a week make sense.

On the tutor's own legal position, the rule is straightforward and worth asking about. Private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by any UAE regulator or examination board, and no page of ours should suggest otherwise.

sections.heading: Scheduling, Ramadan, and the honest position on home visits
paragraphs: A tutoring arrangement in Abu Dhabi usually fails on logistics rather than on teaching. British-curriculum schools in the emirate typically finish between 14:30 and 15:30. Add the drive from the island to Mohammed Bin Zayed City or Al Falah, add a sibling's activity, and the window for a Business session that is not conducted on an exhausted teenager is narrow. Sessions are therefore scheduled around the household rather than around the tutor, and because delivery is online over live video there is no travel on either side to accommodate.

Ramadan is planned for in advance rather than improvised. School hours shorten, family routines move later, and a weekly afternoon slot will not survive the month. The usual arrangement moves sessions to a post-Iftar time or shortens and reduces them for a few weeks, with an agreed catch-up pattern afterwards. Families who plan this in January keep their momentum. Families who do not tend to lose four weeks and start the summer run behind.

The summer break has its own effect for a student entered in a summer series: Abu Dhabi schools finish early enough that timetabled teaching can end before the last papers are sat, leaving a stretch where tutoring is the only structured teaching in the week. That period should be planned deliberately rather than discovered, and it is usually when the full timed papers get done properly.

On delivery, the position is stated plainly because vagueness here wastes a parent's time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Tutoring at a student's address is a service we run only in India, and no tutor will be sent to an Abu Dhabi address. UAE lessons are one to one over live video, with stimulus material annotated on a shared screen and written work returned marked. For a written, case-based subject like 4BS1 that costs nothing in teaching quality and gains a great deal in tutor choice, because the match is made on specification knowledge rather than on who happens to live nearby.

process.title: Send the code, the series and the last script
process.description: The three things that make a first session useful are the specification code the school entered, which series your child is sitting, and the most recent marked paper or mock. For 4BS1 the script matters most: the distribution of lost marks across tariffs is the diagnosis, and it saves a session of guesswork.

process.title: Take the free trial session
process.description: Sixty minutes with a specification-matched tutor at no cost and with no card details taken. It includes a short timed question so there is something real to mark, and you receive the marked work plus a written note on whether the issue is knowledge, application or pacing.

process.title: Fix the slot and the evidence cycle in writing
process.description: Before weekly sessions begin we confirm the time in Gulf Standard Time, the school's topic order, the Ramadan arrangement, and what you receive and when. The default is a marked script every fortnight and a one-line target after each session.

process.title: Work the application discipline weekly
process.description: Each session uses a different firm and sector in the stimulus material so the student meets the same theory in varied contexts. Calculation is drilled in short bursts and always paired with an interpretation prompt, never taught as an isolated formula.

process.title: Review at six weeks and change something if nothing moved
process.description: Six weeks gives enough marked scripts to see a trend on a targeted question type. A flat trend triggers a change of tutor or plan rather than a request for patience, because discovering in April that nothing moved is the expensive version of this conversation.

whyPoints.title: Specification-matched, not subject-matched
whyPoints.description: A tutor who knows business and a tutor who knows what 4BS1 rewards on a recommendation question are different people. Application and judgement marks are where Business grades are decided, and board-specific technique is what earns them.

whyPoints.title: Application taught by attempting, not explaining
whyPoints.description: Sessions are built around attempting questions and rewriting them after marking, because the instinct to answer generally can only be overridden with a pen in hand. Explanation alone leaves the habit untouched.

whyPoints.title: The numbers are taken seriously
whyPoints.description: Break-even, cash flow, profit and ratio work are examinable and routinely under-revised. Each is practised in the exam's own format and then paired with an interpretation prompt, so the larger half of the marks is not left behind.

whyPoints.title: Evidence rather than reassurance
whyPoints.description: A marked script every fortnight, a one-line target each session and a mark trend reviewed at six weeks. No predicted grades from small samples, no invented statistics, and no claim that cannot be shown to you on paper.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated honestly
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families run online over live video. IB Gram holds no UAE regulator or examination-board approval, operates no UAE office, and does not send tutors to Abu Dhabi addresses. All of that is said before anyone pays.

whyPoints.title: Built around the Abu Dhabi week
whyPoints.description: Slots are set to real commutes from the island, Khalifa City and the mainland communities, with the Ramadan pattern and the early summer break planned in advance rather than handled as emergencies.

faqs.question: How much does an Edexcel IGCSE Business 4BS1 tutor cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 show low-cost online platforms advertising from about AED 33 to 65 an hour, with the budget band reaching roughly AED 150. Qualified online subject tutors advertise from around AED 150 to AED 300, and IGCSE specialists between AED 200 and AED 450 and above. In-home visits run about AED 180 to 500 because travel is priced into the rate. Monthly packages appear at around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four in-home visits. Those are the providers' own advertised figures, not ours. What changes value most is whether the hour includes a marked script with mark-scheme comparison.

faqs.question: Is Edexcel IGCSE Business the same qualification as the old Business Studies course?
faqs.answer: It is the current Pearson Edexcel International GCSE in Business, and schools and students still often call it Business Studies out of habit. The content will look familiar to anyone who studied the older course: ownership and objectives, people, finance, marketing and operations. What has changed in recent specifications across the board is the weight given to applying theory to the specific firm in the stimulus material and to handling quantitative data. If you are buying revision material second-hand or using an older textbook, check it against the current 4BS1 specification on qualifications.pearson.com, because practice questions written for a previous version can drill the wrong answer shape.

faqs.question: Does 4BS1 include any coursework or controlled assessment?
faqs.answer: No. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Business is assessed entirely by written examination, with entries available in the May and June series and again in November. There is no portfolio, no controlled assessment and no practical component. The planning consequence is that every mark depends on exam-day performance, so timed practice under proper conditions is not optional preparation; it is the only rehearsal available. It also means a weak run of school assignments cannot drag the final grade down, and a strong run cannot lift it. Families sometimes find this reassuring and sometimes find it alarming. Either way it should shape how tutoring hours are spent.

faqs.question: How much maths does Edexcel IGCSE Business actually involve?
faqs.answer: More than most families expect when they choose it as the less mathematical option. Students need break-even output and margin of safety, cash-flow forecasting with balances carried forward, revenue, costs and profit, percentage change, and a set of performance ratios. The arithmetic itself is straightforward and well within Foundation-tier Mathematics A. The marks, though, usually sit in what comes after the calculation: explaining what the figure means for the firm in the extract. A student who has memorised formulas without practising interpretation will reliably bank the smaller half of the available marks on those questions.

faqs.question: My child writes general answers instead of using the case study. How do you fix that?
faqs.answer: By making them attempt and rewrite, not by explaining it again. The target is a specific sentence shape: because this firm does something named in the extract, the consequence is a particular effect on a stated measure. We start by having the student read an extract aloud and identify what is usable, then set timed questions, mark them against the published mark scheme, and have the two weakest answers rewritten live in the next session. Doing the rewrite in front of the tutor matters, because the stall almost always happens at the exact point where a general statement needs to become a consequence for the named business.

faqs.question: Which is the stronger option at Abu Dhabi schools, Business or Economics?
faqs.answer: Neither is stronger in the abstract; they suit different students. Business gives a named firm, figures and a decision to justify, and rewards concrete, decisive writing. Economics gives a market and a mechanism, and rewards abstraction, diagrams used as evidence and a weighed judgement. Students who dislike committing to a position often score better in Economics, where the discussion earns marks for longer. Taking both works well, provided the two answer shapes are taught side by side early, since writing a Business-style answer in an Economics paper quietly costs development marks. One session with a past extract from each paper is the cheapest way to decide.

faqs.question: Can my child take Business 4BS1 and Accounting 4AC1 together?
faqs.answer: Yes, and schools in the emirate do run both, but they are less similar than the names suggest. Business rewards explanation and judgement about a firm. Accounting rewards exactness: ledger formats, labelling, dates and workings all carry marks, and a beautifully argued answer earns nothing if the statement is laid out wrongly. Students who move between the two without adjusting style tend to under-perform in Accounting. If both subjects need support, we would usually rather provide two specialists than stretch one tutor across both, and we will say so rather than quietly bundling them into one match.

faqs.question: What evidence should I receive from a Business tutor each month?
faqs.answer: At minimum: two marked scripts with the mark-scheme wording set beside your child's own answers, a one-line target after each session, and a log of recurring calculation errors. At six weeks you should also see a mark trend on a repeated question type, because that is the only thing that shows whether the plan is working. What you should not receive is a predicted grade from a handful of papers, which is statistically meaningless on a 9-1 scale, or a verbal assurance that sessions are going well. If a provider cannot name the document you will receive and how often, that is the answer to your question.

faqs.question: Do Abu Dhabi schools use Edexcel or Cambridge for Business?
faqs.answer: Both are used across the emirate, and schools frequently choose board by subject rather than adopting one across the whole option block. The only reliable way to know is to ask the head of department which specification code was entered for the current cohort. It matters more than parents expect: the two boards cover comparable content but structure their questions differently, particularly on the longest answers, so a tutor drilling the wrong board's technique can leave a student well prepared for a paper they are not sitting. Confirm the code before the first session rather than after the first mock.

faqs.question: Do universities in the UAE take IGCSE Business seriously as a subject?
faqs.answer: Admissions decisions at this level rest on the overall profile rather than on one option subject, and Business is a perfectly respectable IGCSE. For the British track, reported UAE equivalency requirements refer to five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus Advanced Level or Advanced Subsidiary results. Specific degree entry requirements are set by each university and change, so check the admissions pages of the institutions your child is considering directly. Equivalency itself is a Ministry process that no tutoring provider performs, guarantees or speeds up.

faqs.question: What happens to our weekly Business session during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: It gets planned, not cancelled. School hours shorten during the month and family routines move later, so an afternoon slot that works in January will not hold. The usual arrangement is to move sessions to a post-Iftar time, or to shorten and reduce them for a few weeks with an agreed catch-up pattern afterwards. We set this out in advance with families who start in the autumn term, because the alternative is losing four weeks of momentum just as a summer-series cohort should be moving into timed-paper work. Online delivery makes the shift straightforward, since no travel has to be rearranged.

faqs.question: My child keeps confusing profit and cash flow. Is that a common problem?
faqs.answer: It is one of the most common conceptual errors in the subject, and it is worth fixing properly because it damages answers about whether a firm will survive. Profit is revenue less costs over a period. Cash is what is actually in the account when a bill falls due. A firm can be profitable and still run out of cash, which is exactly the scenario examiners build extracts around. We teach it with a short cash-flow forecast where a profitable month still produces a negative balance, because seeing it happen on a grid fixes it far more reliably than a definition does.

faqs.question: How long before the exam should Business revision switch to timed papers?
faqs.answer: About ten weeks before the first paper, and the date should be set at the start from the official Pearson timetable rather than chosen when someone starts worrying. Before that point, sessions teach and build the application habit. After it, sessions are built around complete papers and question-by-question mark breakdowns, with the full paper sat to the clock at least three times before the series. Pacing is the reason: students who work front to back routinely arrive at the longest, most valuable question with a few minutes left, which looks like weak understanding and is actually a timing failure.

faqs.question: Do you support students resitting Business in the November series?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a resit is the one situation where the diagnosis already exists. The previous script, or the breakdown the school can provide, shows exactly which question types lost marks, so the plan starts from evidence rather than from a fresh assessment. We review the paper question by question before teaching anything, rebuild only the topics that actually cost marks, and move to full timed papers early, because resit candidates very often ran out of time on their first attempt. Pearson's November International GCSE series and its published timetable are the fixed points to plan backwards from; confirm the entry route with the school.

faqs.question: Does ADEK publish anything useful about a school's Business department?
faqs.answer: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and publishes inspection outcomes, which is the only external account of a school's performance not written by the school itself. For a small option department the inspection commentary on teaching and progress in the relevant subject area is more informative than a prospectus page. Read it as context rather than as a verdict: a thin Business department often reflects staffing and cohort size rather than quality. Check the current reports on ADEK's own site, and treat anything a tutoring provider tells you about a named school's inspection result as secondhand until you have.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-business-4bs1-tu.closingBody: The useful first step for a 4BS1 student is not a block of lessons. It is one session with a past extract and a short timed question, marked properly against the published mark scheme, so you can see whether the marks are going on knowledge, application or the clock. That session is free, takes sixty minutes, needs no card details, and is run by a tutor matched to the Edexcel specification rather than to business in general. Lessons are delivered online over live video in Gulf Standard Time around an Abu Dhabi school week. If the evidence points somewhere tutoring cannot help, we will say so.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-chemistry-4ch1-t.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1 to Abu Dhabi students, from a Year 10 start through to a November resit, working from released papers and the board's published mark schemes rather than from a generic worksheet pack.

intro.heading: Why a chemistry student who understands the reaction still loses the marks
paragraphs: Chemistry is the subject where a parent is most likely to be told that the child understands it. Teachers say so, the child says so, and the evidence in the exercise book agrees. Then a mock comes back at 94 out of 180 and nobody can explain the distance between the two. The explanation is almost always the same, and it is not about understanding. Chemistry papers award marks in steps, and a student who arrives at the right conclusion by a route the scheme does not recognise collects the final mark and loses the three before it.

That is a diagnosable problem rather than a vague one. Take a standard five-mark calculation: convert a mass to moles, use the equation to find a mole ratio, convert back to a mass or a volume, apply a concentration or a gas-volume relationship, then round and attach a unit. Each of those is a credited step. A student who does the whole thing on a calculator and writes a single number has told the marker nothing and can only score for the answer. The same student, shown a mark scheme and asked to lay out five lines, will often score four of the five on a question they previously scored one on. No new chemistry has been learned.

So the argument of this page is narrow. What a chemistry tutor should be doing in week one is not re-teaching bonding. It is taking a marked 4CH1 script and sorting every lost mark into one of four bins: a step never written down, a step written wrongly, a unit or significant-figure error at the end, and genuine content that is not known. Those four bins lead to four different plans, and three of them are much faster than the fourth. A family that pays for content re-teaching when the real problem is step presentation pays for a term of work that was never needed.

There is a second reason chemistry rewards this approach more than its sibling sciences. The 4CH1 specification splits into four sections, and the first one, principles of chemistry, contains the quantitative spine that the other three keep borrowing. Moles, equations, concentration, gas volumes, relative formula mass and percentage yield all live there. A weakness in that section does not stay in that section; it reappears in every titration question in physical chemistry and every yield question in organic chemistry. Fix it once and the marks move in three places at the same time, which is why it is the one part of the course worth buying hours for twice.

Lessons for Abu Dhabi families run online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; a tutor arriving at a residence is a service we operate only in India. For a step-marked subject this is a straightforward advantage rather than a compromise, because the shared screen is where the steps get written, marked and rewritten in the same hour, and the student can see the scheme's wording beside their own.

What follows is the detail: where the steps sit in a 4CH1 calculation, what each specification section actually tests, the ion and gas tests that are lost in the wording rather than the chemistry, the fortnightly record a parent receives, what this costs in Abu Dhabi against published market figures, what ADEK and the MoHRE permit mean for whoever teaches your child, and the firm limit on what a tutor may do with work a school will assess.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-chemistry-4ch1-t.programmesIntro: Chemistry is a two-year course where the damage is usually done in one term and discovered in another. The stages below are the points at which an Abu Dhabi family can act, and what evidence exists at each one.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 Science
programmes.description: Chemistry at this stage is particle diagrams, simple word equations and a first encounter with the periodic table. The content barely matters later; two habits do. Writing a balanced equation before attempting any number, and carrying units through a calculation rather than adding them at the end. A Year 9 student who has never been required to show a step will not start showing one in Year 10 unaided.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools decide between separate sciences and Science Double Award at the end of Year 9, often on a single internal paper. Chemistry is the subject where that decision bites hardest, because single-award 4CH1 goes considerably deeper into quantitative work than the double-award route. Ask the head of science which route the current Year 9 cohort was placed into and what the placement was based on.

programmes.name: International GCSE Chemistry, first year
programmes.description: Principles of chemistry and most of inorganic chemistry are normally taught in Year 10, which puts the mole arithmetic in front of a student who has not yet met Higher tier maths rearrangement. This is the cheapest moment in the whole course to intervene, and the one families almost never use, because Year 10 reports rarely look alarming enough to prompt it.
programmes.countryNote: Most Abu Dhabi schools set an end-of-Year-10 internal paper from released Pearson questions. That script is the single most useful document available before the examination year, and it is far easier to obtain in June than in January when departments are marking mocks. Ask for it by name rather than asking for a progress update.

programmes.name: International GCSE Chemistry, examination year
programmes.description: Physical chemistry and organic chemistry arrive in Year 11, with organic frequently taught in the final term before the series. The predictable result in marked scripts is competent inorganic work, patchy physical chemistry where the arithmetic is reused, and organic answers that name a functional group correctly and then describe the reaction in words a scheme does not credit.
programmes.countryNote: Mock windows in Abu Dhabi cluster in November and January, and Pearson entry deadlines sit months ahead of the exam window itself. A January mock script is the last complete evidence available before entries are confirmed, which makes it the right document for deciding between a full push and a targeted repair of two sections.

programmes.name: November series and private candidates
programmes.description: Pearson International GCSE runs a May/June series and a November series, so a chemistry grade can be improved without repeating a school year. A resit is a different job from a first attempt because the component marks already form a diagnosis, and the work is to rebuild one or two specification sections properly rather than to revisit all four at speed.
programmes.countryNote: A resit candidate needs an entry through a centre, and the entry deadline governs everything that follows. Published Pearson milestones place final entries months before the exam window, so the resit decision gets made long before revision begins. Confirm live dates on qualifications.pearson.com and with the exams officer at the centre taking the entry.

subjects.name: Chemistry (4CH1)
subjects.description: The subject of this page. Four specification sections, two written papers, 180 marks, untiered and graded 9 to 1, with no coursework. Marked scripts lose most heavily on unwritten calculation steps, on test questions where observation and conclusion are merged into one sentence, and on organic reactions described rather than named.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.description: The arithmetic chemistry runs on. Ratio, rearrangement, standard form, percentage change and significant figures all appear in both subjects. A student losing chemistry marks on the mole almost always has a matching gap in Higher tier maths, and one repair fixes two subjects.

subjects.name: Biology (4BI1)
subjects.description: Shares the science option block and competes for the same revision hours. Biology rewards precise written explanation and chemistry rewards precise quantity, so a strong biologist weak in chemistry usually has the vocabulary and lacks the habit of showing a numerical route.

subjects.name: Physics (4PH1)
subjects.description: The third separate science and the closest in arithmetic demand. Unit conversion, standard form and formula rearrangement recur in both. Students who treat the two as unrelated pay twice for one weakness, and a shared drill on units usually lifts both sets of marks.

subjects.name: Science Double Award (4SD0)
subjects.description: The alternative route, covering all three sciences for two grades. Chemistry content is reduced and the quantitative demand is lighter. Confirming which route your child is on is the first question we ask, because in Abu Dhabi households with two children the answer is sometimes different for each.

subjects.name: Further Pure Mathematics (4PM1)
subjects.description: Taken by students heading towards A-Level sciences. A 4PM1 student finds chemistry calculation easy, which hides a different weakness: the written explanation marks in inorganic and organic questions, where a precise answer in words is worth as much as a number.

subjects.name: English Language A (4EA1)
subjects.description: Relevant to chemistry through the extended-response marks. A student who writes loosely writes loosely in a six-mark chemistry explanation, and markers pay for sequence and precision in both subjects. Command-word work transfers between them more than most families expect.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Required in UAE private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and timetabled inside the school day. Its relevance to a chemistry plan is scheduling arithmetic: it occupies periods that might otherwise be free and shapes where a weekly session can sit.

subjects.name: Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: Also required in UAE private schools, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students under published guidance. Again the chemistry relevance is timetable rather than content: these are fixed periods and a realistic weekly slot has to work around them.

subjects.name: Business (4BS1)
subjects.description: A common pairing for students who intend to leave science after Year 11. sections.heading: Where the steps go in a 4CH1 calculation, and what each one is worth
paragraphs: A chemistry calculation is not marked as right or wrong. It is marked as a sequence, and the scheme releases credit at each point where a candidate demonstrates a specific move. This is why two students with the same final answer can score two marks apart, and why a student who gets the answer wrong can still collect most of the marks available. Families find this counter-intuitive, and students find it worse: a child who has been told all year that chemistry is about understanding reactions is being assessed, in a large part of the paper, on whether they wrote four lines in a recognisable order.

The moves themselves are finite. Convert a given mass or volume into moles. Read the balanced equation for a ratio. Apply the ratio. Convert back into the quantity the question asked for. Handle a concentration, a gas volume at room conditions, a percentage yield or a limiting reagent where one is involved. Round sensibly and write the unit. Any one of those can be the single missing line that costs three marks, and in a marked script the missing line is visible immediately to someone who knows where to look.

The practical consequence for tutoring is a change of order. The first session with a new 4CH1 student does not start with bonding or with the periodic table; it starts with three calculations from a released paper, worked on a shared screen with every line written out, and then marked against the scheme while the student watches. That hour usually tells a parent more than a term of school reports, because it separates the student who cannot do the chemistry from the far more common student who can do it and is not being paid for it.

The table below sets out the step sequence and the marks at risk at each stage. The figures describe where credit typically sits in a multi-mark quantitative question rather than any particular paper, and the mark schemes themselves are published on qualifications.pearson.com after each series.

sections.heading: The four sections of 4CH1 and what each one actually tests
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry is assessed by two written papers with no coursework and no separately assessed practical. Paper 1C runs for two hours and Paper 2C for one hour fifteen minutes, with 180 marks between them, and the qualification is untiered and graded 9 to 1. Paper 2C assesses the content the specification flags as examined only on the second paper, which is why a candidate who revises evenly across the whole course without checking the split arrives under-prepared for the shorter sitting. Confirm component details for your child's series against the specification on qualifications.pearson.com.

The more useful division for planning is the specification's own: four sections, each with a distinct failure mode. Principles of chemistry holds states of matter, atomic structure, the periodic table, bonding, and the entire quantitative apparatus of moles, equations, concentration and gas volumes. Inorganic chemistry covers groups, reactivity, gases, and the tests whose marks live in precise wording. Physical chemistry covers rates, energetics, reversible reactions and equilibrium, and reuses the arithmetic from section one. Organic chemistry covers homologous series, reaction types, polymers and the naming conventions that students approximate and schemes do not.

Read that way, a marked script tells you which section to buy hours for. Loss concentrated in principles means the spine is weak and the loss is also quietly present in the other three sections, which makes it the most valuable repair in the course. Loss in inorganic usually means the chemistry is known and the wording is not. Loss in physical chemistry is frequently just the principles weakness showing up again in a titration or a rate calculation. Loss in organic almost always reflects teaching order rather than ability, because organic tends to be taught last and revised least.

sections.heading: The mole is one skill, and it is most of the quantitative grade
paragraphs: If a single idea decides a 4CH1 grade it is the mole, and the reason is structural rather than conceptual. A mole question is not one question type. It is the gateway to titration calculations, to percentage yield, to gas volumes at room temperature and pressure, to empirical formula work, to concentration conversions between grams per cubic decimetre and moles per cubic decimetre, and to limiting reagent reasoning. A student who is shaky here is not shaky in one topic. They are shaky in a diagonal line that cuts through three of the four specification sections.

What makes the diagnosis tricky is that the symptom looks like carelessness. A student divides when they should multiply, or converts cubic centimetres to cubic decimetres by the wrong factor, and the result reads like a slip. Seen across six marked questions, the same slip is a structure problem: the student is pattern-matching to a remembered example instead of reasoning from the quantity they have to the quantity they want. The cure is unglamorous. Every calculation starts by writing down what is given with its unit, what is wanted with its unit, and the route between them, until the route is written without prompting.

This is also where the honest version of session arithmetic matters. Rebuilding mole reasoning properly takes more than one hour and fewer than a term. In practice it tends to absorb a handful of sessions, with a five-minute drill attached to every subsequent lesson until the error stops recurring in marked work. We would rather tell a family that than sell a package on the promise that one lesson fixes it, and the marked record is what shows whether it worked. A student whose unit errors have disappeared from three consecutive marked sets has genuinely fixed something.

The section also explains why we resist starting a new 4CH1 student on whichever topic the school is currently teaching. Following the school's sequence feels responsive and usually spends the hour on content the student will meet again in class anyway. Starting on the quantitative spine spends the hour on something nobody in the school day has time to rebuild.

sections.heading: Observation, conclusion, and the inorganic marks lost in the wording
paragraphs: Inorganic chemistry is where 4CH1 candidates lose the marks they are most annoyed about, because they knew the answer. A test question typically asks what a candidate would see and what that tells them, and those are two separate credits. A student who writes that the solution turns blue so copper is present has not written the two-part answer; a student who writes a pale blue precipitate forms with sodium hydroxide solution, indicating copper two ions, has. The chemistry is identical. One version collects both marks and the other collects one.

The pattern repeats across the familiar tests. Flame tests, where a colour has to be named precisely rather than approximately. Precipitate tests with sodium hydroxide, where the colour and the word precipitate both matter, and where a precipitate that redissolves in excess is a separate observation. Halide tests with silver nitrate, where cream and pale yellow are distinguishable answers. Gas tests, where limewater turning milky, a splint relighting, or damp red litmus turning blue are the observations and the gas identity is the conclusion. Sulfate tests with barium chloride and acid. In every case the mark scheme separates what is seen from what is deduced.

Teaching this online is efficient because the examined skill is written. The student types or writes the two-part answer, the scheme's wording goes on the screen beside it, and the difference is visible rather than explained. A session can work through eight test questions in half an hour, and in marked work the improvement shows up quickly, which makes inorganic a sensible place to start a block when a family needs early evidence that the arrangement is doing something. It is the least glamorous section of the course and the cheapest per mark recovered.

sections.heading: The fortnightly review, and the decision it is supposed to force
paragraphs: Weekly marking produces data. A review is what turns it into a decision. Every fortnight on a continuing arrangement, the tutor sends a short note built on the marked work rather than on impressions, and the note exists to force one of four choices: continue as planned, change the section being worked on, change the format, or stop. A review that recommends continuing every time is not a review, and a parent should be suspicious of one.

What the note contains is deliberately plain. The marked sets attached, the raw marks on each, the proportion of loss sitting in each of the four bins, and one sentence on what changed. A parent who knows no chemistry should be able to read it in two minutes and tell whether step marks are being earned. The usual trajectory is that step and unit losses fall first, within three or four marked sets, because they are presentation problems; content gains arrive more slowly because a section genuinely has to be rebuilt.

The reason to write the review as a decision point rather than a summary is that tutoring arrangements drift. A family books because of a mock, the mock passes, the sessions continue, and nobody revisits whether the original brief still applies. Six weeks later the student is being taught whatever the school taught that week, which is a service but not the one that was bought. A fortnightly note that names the section being worked on makes that drift visible to everyone, including the tutor.

sections.heading: What a 4CH1 plan costs in Abu Dhabi, in context
paragraphs: Parents in Abu Dhabi searching for a chemistry tutor usually mean someone who will arrive at the door, and the market for that is real. Published UAE figures put in-home one-to-one tuition at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, and advertised in-home monthly packages run around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Bestimate's 2026 rate table gives AED 180 to 350 for in-home visits; independent home tutors are quoted up to AED 500.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, and nothing here should be read as an offer to send anyone to a residence in the emirate. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; visiting a UAE address is a service we run only in India. In a step-marked subject the online format does specific work rather than merely saving travel. The scheme and the student's own lines sit side by side on a shared screen, the marking happens where the student can watch it, and the time a visiting tutor would spend in a car is the time this arrangement spends marking.

The figures below are published market rates from the named sources, quoted as the market and dated to October 2026, not as an IB Gram price list. Three of the six competitor pages reviewed for this project publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. Our own arrangement starts with one free trial lesson, with no card details taken; what a weekly plan costs after that depends on session length and frequency, which is a conversation rather than a published table.

The context column is the part families find most useful. A chemistry grade is one component of a school year that already costs a great deal, and KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27 under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Abu Dhabi fee approvals sit with ADEK rather than KHDA, so the comparison is indicative rather than transferable, but the scale is the point: tutoring is usually a small fraction of the annual cost of the schooling it is protecting.

sections.heading: ADEK, the permit, and what a parent can verify without taking anyone's word
paragraphs: Most pages written for UAE parents mention a regulator once and move on. The useful version tells you what you can check yourself. Private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which the UAE government's own guidance describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and which publishes its own inspection ratings. That means a school's rating is a matter of public record, and so is the question of whether a school exists, which is worth knowing because at least one competitor page reviewed for this project lists a school that appears not to exist.

Private tuition is governed separately. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page for the permit lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the ministry's app, website and e-services system. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule has been published, any specific figure quoted to you is unverified.

There is an Abu Dhabi-specific point families should know. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school; verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it. The practical reading is to avoid hiring your child's own chemistry teacher, which also removes any awkwardness about who marks internal assessments.

IB Gram holds no permit, licence, accreditation or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, Pearson or any examination board, and makes no claim to any. We are a matching platform. The two questions worth asking any tutor, whether found through us or elsewhere, are whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition permit and whether their current employment permits private tutoring. A tutor who cannot answer those has answered them.

sections.heading: What a chemistry tutor may not do, including with a chatbot in the room
paragraphs: 4CH1 carries no coursework, which removes the most common academic-honesty trap in international qualifications. It leaves others. A tutor may teach, demonstrate, set work and mark it against a published scheme. A tutor may not complete a piece of work that the school will treat as the student's own, and that includes collected homework, internal mock papers taken home and any task feeding a predicted grade. The line is clear and the consequence of crossing it falls on the student, not the tutor. One essay mill in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright; that is an integrity breach we will not imitate in any subject.

A second limit covers materials. Pearson's past papers, mark schemes, examiner reports and specifications are the board's copyright and are published on the board's own site, with recent series released to centres under conditions. A tutor may reference them, work from them live and point you to the official page. A tutor should not be handing over a drive folder of reproduced papers, and anyone offering unreleased material is offering something that would make your child a malpractice case. Every reference on this page points at qualifications.pearson.com for that reason.

The newest version of this problem arrives as a chatbot. A chemistry explanation generated in thirty seconds reads plausibly, uses the right vocabulary and is frequently wrong in a way a Year 11 student cannot detect, particularly on mechanisms, equilibrium reasoning and anything involving a mole ratio. Where a student has clearly submitted generated text, the useful response is not a lecture; it is to put the generated answer and the mark scheme side by side and let the student find the two sentences that would score nothing. That is a lesson worth having, and it is one of the better uses of a marked-script hour.

The last limit is about claims. No tutor, however many 4CH1 scripts they have marked, can guarantee a grade, and a page promising a 9 is selling something it cannot deliver. What can be committed to is process: marking against the published scheme, an honest record including when it is flat, and being told when the arrangement is not working rather than invoiced through another term.

sections.heading: Joining in January, and what happens when no 4CH1 specialist is free
paragraphs: The most common moment a chemistry enquiry arrives in Abu Dhabi is the week after January mocks, which is also the week every other family in the emirate has the same idea. Two things follow. The evening slots between 5pm and 8pm Gulf Standard Time fill first, and chemistry specialists are a narrower pool than maths tutors. So here is the position before you enquire rather than after.

When the specialist who matches the specification has nothing in the window you want, there are three honest answers. A different time, usually a weekend morning, which for timed calculation work is better than a Tuesday at 7pm anyway. A different tutor, meaning a strong general science tutor who covers 4CH1 alongside 4BI1 and 4PH1, which fits a student who needs step presentation and arithmetic rather than organic depth. Or a wait with a date attached, which is occasionally the right answer and is always better than a placement that does not fit. What we will not do is say yes and then quietly drop the marking by week three.

A January start also changes the plan itself. There is no time to rebuild four sections, so the work becomes triage: the mock script names the section with the heaviest loss, the block takes that section and the step presentation problem together, and everything else is protected rather than improved. That is a smaller promise than families want to hear in January and it is the one that survives contact with the exam timetable.

Getting started is short. Send the last marked chemistry script and the series your child is entered for, we confirm the specification code and which paper carries the Paper-2-only content, and a free trial lesson follows with no card details taken. If the match is wrong after the trial or after the fourth session, we move the student at no extra charge and the marked record goes with them. Changing tutor once is common and is not a failure of the process.

process.title: Send the last marked chemistry script
process.description: Not a description of the problem and not the report, but the paper itself, however poor the mark. If the school has not released it, ask the exams officer or head of science; most Abu Dhabi departments share mock scripts on request. Where nothing exists, the trial lesson generates one from three released calculations.

process.title: Sort the loss into the four bins
process.description: Every lost mark goes into one of four categories: step never written, step written wrongly, unit or significant-figure error, or genuine content gap. Three of those four are faster to repair than families expect, and knowing the split before paying for a term is the difference between a plan and a hope.

process.title: Name one section in writing
process.description: Before the first paid session the block names one of the four specification sections and the question types it will target, together with what you receive each fortnight. A plan naming principles of chemistry and titration calculations is checkable; a plan promising to improve chemistry is not.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One live session, no card details taken, with the tutor we think fits. It is working time rather than a sales call: three released calculations worked on a shared screen and marked step by step, which produces the audit whether or not you continue afterwards.

process.title: Read the fortnightly review and decide
process.description: Every two weeks a short note arrives with the marked sets attached, the raw marks, the split across the four bins and one sentence on what changed. It exists to force a decision: continue, change section, change format, or stop. We will say stop when the record says so.

whyPoints.title: Marking at the level of the step, not the paper
whyPoints.description: A chemistry mark scheme releases credit line by line, so the useful unit of feedback is the line rather than the score. Every marked set comes back with the missing lines identified, which is what turns a vague instruction to show your working into something a student can actually do next week.

whyPoints.title: The quantitative spine before the current topic
whyPoints.description: We start on moles, equations and units rather than on whatever the school taught that week, because the school will teach that topic again and nobody in the school day has an hour to rebuild the arithmetic. It is the one repair that moves marks in three specification sections at once.

whyPoints.title: The specification code confirmed first
whyPoints.description: 4CH1 is not Cambridge 0620, and single-award chemistry is not Science Double Award 4SD0. The paper structure, the Paper-2-only content and the entry deadline all follow from the code, and in Abu Dhabi households with two science students the answer is sometimes different for each child.

whyPoints.title: A review that can recommend stopping
whyPoints.description: The fortnightly note exists to force a decision, and one of the available decisions is to stop. A record that recommends continuing every single time is a record nobody is reading. Two flat sets early are normal; six are a signal, and you should hear it from us.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before you enquire
whyPoints.description: Evening slots in Abu Dhabi fill in the weeks after January mocks, and chemistry specialists are a narrower pool than maths tutors. When the honest answer is a weekend morning or a two-week wait, that is the answer, rather than a placement with whoever happens to be free.

faqs.question: What does an Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry 4CH1 tutor charge in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market rates run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online help, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an International GCSE specialist. Bestimate's 2026 table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and TutorChase publishes AED 270, with independent home tutors quoted to AED 500. Advertised packages include about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' figures as published in October 2026, not ours; IB Gram starts with a free trial lesson and no card details.

faqs.question: Why does my child get part marks on chemistry calculations but never full marks?
faqs.answer: Because the scheme credits steps and your child is probably writing only the answer. A multi-mark calculation releases marks for converting a mass to moles, reading the ratio from a balanced equation, applying the ratio, converting back to the quantity asked for, and rounding with a unit. A single number on the line collects at most the answer mark. This is the most common finding in a first 4CH1 script audit and one of the fastest to repair, because no new chemistry has to be learned, only written down in a recognisable order.

faqs.question: Which of the four 4CH1 sections is worth tutoring first?
faqs.answer: Usually principles of chemistry, because it holds the moles, equations, concentration and gas-volume work that the other three sections keep borrowing. Loss there is never confined there: it reappears in titration questions in physical chemistry and yield questions in organic chemistry, so a family that repairs it sees marks move in three places. Inorganic chemistry is the exception worth taking first when a script shows the chemistry known and the wording imprecise, since those marks come back quickly and give early evidence that the arrangement is working.

faqs.question: How are practical skills assessed in 4CH1 when there is no practical exam?
faqs.answer: Through written questions on the two papers. There is no coursework and no separately assessed practical in Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry, so the whole grade comes from written work, but candidates are still asked to describe methods, identify variables, explain why a step was repeated, read a value from an apparatus diagram, or suggest an improvement. Those marks appear every series and are routinely dropped by students who have performed the experiments at school and never written about them in the form a scheme rewards. The experiments stay the school's job.

faqs.question: My child can describe a flame test but still loses the mark. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always imprecision rather than ignorance. A flame test question separates the observation from the conclusion, and the observation has to name the colour exactly: lilac rather than purple, crimson rather than red, and so on. A student who writes that the flame changes colour so potassium is present has collapsed two credits into one sentence and will score one of them. The repair is wording practice against released schemes, which is quick work and some of the cheapest marks in the paper to recover.

faqs.question: When should an Abu Dhabi student start revising organic chemistry?
faqs.answer: Earlier than the school teaches it, if the goal is a high grade. Organic chemistry is commonly delivered in the final term of Year 11, which leaves little time between the teaching and the series. In marked scripts it shows up as correct chemistry written in approximate language: a reaction described rather than named, a homologous series pattern recognised but not stated. Because the content volume is modest and the losses are linguistic, organic responds well to a short block, and it is often the most recoverable section in a plan starting after January mocks.

faqs.question: Which chemistry specification is my child's Abu Dhabi school actually using?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer, or look at the top of any past paper the department has issued, where the code is printed. Pearson 4CH1 and Cambridge 0620 differ in paper structure, in how practical skills are examined and in entry deadlines, so revision aimed at the wrong one wastes real time. There is a second question inside the first: whether your child sits single-award chemistry or chemistry inside Science Double Award 4SD0, which examines reduced content with a lighter quantitative load. Check per child, since siblings are sometimes on different routes.

faqs.question: What does a fortnightly chemistry review actually contain?
faqs.answer: The marked question sets, the raw mark on each, the split of lost marks across the four bins we use, and one sentence on what changed. It should take a parent who knows no chemistry about two minutes to read and should end with a decision: continue on this section, move to the next, change the format, or stop. A review that recommends continuing on every occasion is not functioning as a review, and that is a reasonable thing to say to a tutor.

faqs.question: Does splitting a 4CH1 session between two students work?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking about because the cost per student drops. It works when both students are on the same specification and series, within about a grade of each other, and both bring marked work to each session. It stops working when one needs mole arithmetic rebuilt while the other needs organic naming, because the step audit that makes the session useful is individual. We would rather say that before the first session than discover it in week five, and marking is returned separately in any case.

faqs.question: Can an online lesson teach titration properly?
faqs.answer: It can teach the examined part of titration, which is the calculation and the method description rather than the manual technique. The marks in a titration question come from reading a burette value correctly, identifying concordant results, averaging them properly, converting volumes to cubic decimetres, applying the mole ratio from the balanced equation and reporting with a unit. All of that is written work and all of it sits better on a shared screen than on a bench. Handling the glassware remains the school laboratory's job, and the school does it.

faqs.question: How late is too late to start chemistry tutoring before the series?
faqs.answer: Six weeks is enough to repair one specification section and a step-presentation habit. Three weeks is enough to drill units, rounding and the two-part test answers, which is a real if modest number of marks. Under two weeks the useful work is exam-paper logistics rather than chemistry. What no block of any length can do is rebuild two years, and a tutor who implies otherwise has not read the script. A short block should name what it will not cover as clearly as what it will.

faqs.question: How can I check that a chemistry tutor is permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask directly whether they hold the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and whether their current employment allows private tutoring. The permit is granted free of charge for two years and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, so cost is no excuse for not holding one. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount quoted to you as unverified.

faqs.question: My child used a chatbot for a chemistry homework answer. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It is a problem in two ways. Where a school will assess the work, submitting generated text is misrepresentation and the consequences land on the student. The quieter problem is accuracy: generated chemistry reads fluently and is frequently wrong on mechanisms, equilibrium reasoning and anything involving a mole ratio, in ways a Year 11 student cannot detect. A useful session puts the generated answer beside the published mark scheme and asks the student to find the sentences that would score nothing. That tends to settle the question better than a warning.

faqs.question: Which five subjects does the Ministry of Education count for British-track equivalency?
faqs.answer: The published rule asks for five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or grade 3, and states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. The British track also requires one subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Chemistry counts as an ordinary subject within the five. One ranking competitor states six IGCSE subjects are needed, which does not match the published rule. Verify current requirements on moe.gov.ae before making decisions.

faqs.question: Can we start in January after a disappointing mock?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most common starting point in Abu Dhabi, which is why evening slots fill in that fortnight. A January start changes the plan rather than the method: there is no time to rebuild four sections, so the mock script names the heaviest-loss section, the block takes that plus the step-presentation problem, and the rest of the course is protected rather than improved. If the specialist who fits has no evening slot, the honest options are a weekend morning, a general science tutor, or a short wait with a date on it.

faqs.question: How soon should a tutor tell us the chemistry plan is not working?
faqs.answer: By the week-six review at the latest, and in writing. Two flat marked sets early on are normal, because timed conditions and honest marking both pull a score down before lifting it. Six sets with no movement in either step marks or raw score mean the arrangement is wrong, and the record makes that visible without anyone needing to interpret it. At that point the tutor changes at no extra charge and the marked work transfers. Stopping is also a legitimate outcome and we would rather say so than invoice another term.
