sections.heading: Is the person you are letting in permitted to teach privately?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is not an unregulated activity, and this is the part of the decision most households skip. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

The official route is MoHRE's own service, listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days and no fee listed. That is the page to send anybody who tells you a permit is expensive, slow or optional.

There is an Abu Dhabi-specific point that matters more here than anywhere else in the country. Press reporting of ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's own code of conduct is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the holder's school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it. The practical advice is unambiguous either way: however convenient it looks, your child's own subject teacher is the wrong person to pay privately.

A separate thing entirely is an organisation with premises and staff. A tuition centre operating in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal. IB Gram is not a centre, holds no such permit, and should never be described as approved by any regulator. We can tell you what each body does; none of them endorses us.

sections.heading: The supervision problem, and the part online delivery does not solve
paragraphs: An adult in the room is a real service and online tuition does not provide it. Saying otherwise would be the sort of claim this page spends most of its length pushing back against, so here is the honest version: if what you need is somebody to make a fourteen-year-old sit down, a video link is a weaker tool than a person at the table, and you should solve that part separately.

What works in practice in Abu Dhabi households is a small set of arrangements that cost nothing. The session happens at a desk in a shared part of the home rather than in a bedroom, with the door open. A parent is within earshot for the first two or three lessons and then stops being, because the point is for the student to own the hour. The device is on a table, not on a lap, with a second screen or a printed paper beside it so the student can write by hand while the tutor can see the page.

That last detail does more work than people expect. Edexcel maths and science are written subjects: students have to produce working on paper under timing. A session where everything happens on a screen trains the wrong motor habit. The households that get most from online tuition print the paper, work in pen, and hold it up to the camera or photograph it afterwards. The tutor annotates the scan, and now there is a dated artefact that a visiting arrangement would have left as a conversation.

The other half of supervision is attention, and attention is a schedule problem more than a presence problem. A student who is being tutored at 19:30 after football is not going to produce evidence of anything. In Abu Dhabi, where bus arrivals cluster between 15:15 and 16:00 in the Khalifa City corridor and later on the island, the single most effective change most families can make is moving the session half an hour earlier.
bullets: Desk in a shared room, door open, device on a table rather than a lap
Paper and pen in use during the session; the screen is for the tutor, not the working
Parent within earshot for the first two or three lessons, then deliberately not
Session scheduled before co-curriculars, not after them

sections.heading: What a visiting tutor cannot easily leave behind
paragraphs: A good visiting tutor produces exactly the same teaching as a good online one. Where the formats genuinely diverge is in the record. A session in your sitting room leaves a conversation at the door and some writing in an exercise book. A session on a shared screen leaves an annotated document, and that difference compounds over a term.

Consider the question every parent asks in month two: is this working. Answering it requires two comparable pieces of evidence. The baseline paper from week one and a similar paper from week five, both marked against the published Pearson scheme, with the lost marks grouped by topic and by assessment objective. Those documents are trivially easy to produce when the marking happened on a screen and almost always absent when it happened in pencil on a sheet that went back into a school bag.

This is also the difference between a tutor's opinion and a second opinion. If you want to show somebody else what is going on - the school, a different tutor, a relative who teaches maths - you need artefacts that leave the house. A dated folder of marked scripts does that. A positive impression does not, and when a family decides to change tutor after two terms, the absence of that folder is usually what makes the next tutor start from scratch at your expense.

None of this makes a visiting tutor the wrong choice for a household whose main problem is a thirteen-year-old who will not sit down. It does mean that if your problem is eleven missing marks on 4PH1 Paper 1, the format that produces the evidence is the one worth paying for.

sections.heading: Recordings, forms and a minor's data
paragraphs: Online delivery creates records, and records about a child need a stated purpose. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs how personal data is handled, and a tutoring arrangement involving a minor should be explicit about what is collected and why rather than leaving it to a privacy page nobody opens.

The practical questions to ask any provider, including us, are short. Is the session recorded, and if so who can watch it and for how long is it kept. Where do the marked scripts live, and can you take a copy if you leave. What does the enquiry form collect, and why does it need that field. Is the child's school name being collected for matching, for marketing, or for neither. A provider who cannot answer those in plain language has not thought about it.

Our position is that a lesson is recorded only when the family asks for it, that marked scripts belong to you and are shareable on request, and that an enquiry needs the specification codes, the year group and a contact - not a photograph, not a report card, and not a list of grades. If a form asks a UAE family for a child's school, grades and photograph without saying what each is for, that is a reason to be careful rather than a sign of thoroughness.

One more thing worth checking on any UAE page, ours included: the contact route. Two sites ranking for Abu Dhabi tutoring queries route parents to Indian mobile numbers, and one shows a Dubai address on an Abu Dhabi page. Neither is illegal and both tell you something about how carefully the page was built.

sections.heading: Ramadan, travel and the weeks the plan has to survive
paragraphs: A tutoring plan in Abu Dhabi has to survive the UAE calendar, and the calendar is not the same as a northern-hemisphere school year. Ramadan shortens school days and shifts the usable study hours into the evening, and for many households the workable slot during that month is after Iftar rather than at half past five. A visiting arrangement in that window is harder to sustain for everybody involved; an online slot moves by agreement.

Long summer and winter breaks spent outside the country are the other recurring disruption. Abu Dhabi families travel, often for several weeks, and a visiting tutor cannot follow. A video link can, subject to the time difference being workable, which it usually is for the UK, Europe, India and East Africa. The students who lose least over a summer are the ones who keep a reduced schedule of one session a fortnight rather than stopping entirely and restarting cold in September.

There are also weeks when stopping is the right call. Internal mock fortnights, the days immediately before a paper, and the week a family moves house are all periods where an extra hour of tuition subtracts rather than adds. A plan that names its pauses in advance is more likely to be kept than one that treats every missed week as a failure.

Where this lands practically: agree the slot, agree what happens during Ramadan, agree what happens in July, and agree the two or three weeks you will deliberately skip. Doing that at the start costs one conversation and prevents the slow erosion that ends most tutoring arrangements in this market before they produce any evidence.
bullets: Ramadan: a post-Iftar slot by agreement, with shorter sessions and the same cadence
Travel weeks: one session a fortnight beats stopping and restarting cold
Mock fortnights: often the right week to pause rather than add
Name the planned pauses at the start, in writing

sections.heading: Comparing two quotes that describe different things
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi parents routinely compare an AED 200 online hour with an AED 320 visiting hour and conclude that one is better value. The numbers are not comparable until you know what each includes, and in this market they rarely include the same things.

Six questions make two quotes describe the same product. Is the price per hour or per session, and is a session sixty minutes or fifty. Is marking against the published mark scheme included, or is it extra, or does it simply not happen. Who provides the papers, and are they the official Pearson versions for the entered specification. Is there a written review at any point, and how often. What happens if the tutor is unavailable for a fortnight - replacement, credit, or nothing. And what is the notice period for stopping.

Ask those six and the apparently cheaper quote often turns out to be the dearer one. A fifty-minute session with no marking and no written review, at AED 200, costs more per recovered mark than a sixty-minute session with same-day marking at AED 250. Cost per hour is the wrong unit; cost per mark actually moved is the right one, and nobody can tell you that number in advance - which is exactly why the four-week evidence point matters.

One caution on figures you will be shown. If a provider quotes you a success statistic - a percentage, an average grade, a number of students helped - ask for the sample size, the date and the method. Figures on tutoring sites in this market frequently contradict themselves on the same page, and a number that cannot be sourced should not move a buying decision.

process.title: Say where you are and which codes
process.description: The community, the school, the specification codes and the hour you want. Abu Dhabi geography genuinely matters to scheduling even in an online arrangement, because bus arrival times differ by twenty-five minutes or more between the island and the Khalifa City corridor, and the slot has to fit the real evening.

process.title: Hear the coverage position first
process.description: Before any trial we tell you whether a specialist in that exact code is free at that hour, what the realistic wait is if not, and what the alternative looks like. On thinner codes such as Further Pure Mathematics or Computer Science that answer is sometimes no, and you get it before you have invested anything.

process.title: Free trial lesson, with the format tested
process.description: The trial is a working session that deliberately tests the online format: a timed question attempted alone, written by hand, photographed and annotated. That is the part families are unsure about, so it is the part the trial should answer rather than postpone.

process.title: Set the household arrangement, then start
process.description: Desk in a shared room, door open, paper and pen, and a slot that sits before co-curriculars rather than after them. Five minutes of planning here changes more about the outcome than the choice of tutor does, and it costs nothing.

process.title: Review at four weeks and decide
process.description: A dated written review with the baseline mark, the current mark, lost marks grouped by topic and assessment objective, and three targets. Then a decision: continue, move the hours, change tutor, or stop. If the evidence does not support continuing we will say so in writing.

whyPoints.title: The position is stated before the form
whyPoints.description: IB Gram does not sell visiting tuition in the UAE, and this page says so in its third paragraph rather than in a footnote. You can decide whether the online format suits your household before you have given anybody a phone number, which is how it should work.

whyPoints.title: Figures carry their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to whoever published it and dated to October 2026. They are market rates, not our prices. Three of the most visible sites in this market publish no figure at all, and two quote in dollars, which is not the currency Abu Dhabi families pay in.

whyPoints.title: The whole specialist pool, not the drivable one
whyPoints.description: A household in Al Shamkha gets a tutor who has taught the exact Edexcel code many times, rather than the best available person within a twenty-minute drive. On thin codes such as 4PM1 and 4CP0 that is the difference between a specialist and a willing generalist.

whyPoints.title: The hour is the hour
whyPoints.description: No part of the slot goes into a car, in either direction, and no session ends early to protect a booking across a bridge. Over a school year the recovered time is substantial, and it is time that produces marked work rather than apologies.

whyPoints.title: Records you can take with you
whyPoints.description: Annotated papers, mark-scheme feedback and the four-week review are yours to keep and to show to anybody: the school, a second tutor, a relative who teaches the subject. Evidence that lives only in a provider's account is not evidence you can act on.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what we do not do
whyPoints.description: Online delivery does not put an adult at the table, and we do not pretend it does. Where that is the thing you are buying, the section above sets out household arrangements that work instead. A disclosed limitation is more useful than a discovered one.

faqs.question: Do tutors travel to villas in Khalifa City or Al Raha for Edexcel lessons?
faqs.answer: Not through us. IB Gram does not sell home visits in Abu Dhabi; visiting tuition is a service we run only in India. In the UAE every lesson is one-to-one and live over video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. Independent visiting tutors do serve both communities, and the published market band for an in-home hour including travel runs from roughly AED 180 to AED 500. If you want the visiting option, that is the band to negotiate within, and the questions to ask are about the permit, the travel buffer and whether marking is included.

faqs.question: What does a visiting IGCSE tutor charge per hour in Abu Dhabi right now?
faqs.answer: Published market rates gathered in October 2026 put an in-home one-to-one hour between about AED 180 and AED 500 once travel is priced in. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table gives a common range of AED 180 to AED 350, independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to AED 500, and named examiner-level tutors are quoted up to AED 650 and above. Monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions appear around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799. Those are other people's figures with their sources named, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: How much of a paid hour does an Abu Dhabi home tutor actually spend teaching?
faqs.answer: Families here typically describe forty-five to fifty teaching minutes inside a sixty-minute booking. Arrival and settling takes five to eight minutes, and a tutor with a second booking across a bridge often finishes five to ten minutes early to protect it. Nobody is behaving badly; it is arithmetic about traffic. Across a thirty-week year, ten lost minutes a week is roughly five hours of teaching, which at mid-market rates is a real sum for something that produced no marks. An online slot does not carry that deduction at either end.

faqs.question: Is a home tutor better for a child who gets distracted in front of a screen?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends what the distraction is. If the issue is that a fourteen-year-old will not start without an adult present, a person at the table is a stronger tool than a video link, and that is worth saying plainly. If the issue is a device with notifications on it, the fix is the household arrangement rather than the format: desk in a shared room, door open, phone in another room, paper and pen for the working. Try two or three online sessions set up that way before concluding the format is the problem.

faqs.question: Can my son's own class teacher at his Abu Dhabi school tutor him privately?
faqs.answer: Treat it as ruled out. Press reporting of ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit's code of conduct is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the holder's school. Confirm the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on the detail. Beyond the rules there is a practical reason: the person who sets your son's internal assessments should not also be paid to prepare him for them.

faqs.question: What equipment does a household in Al Reem Island need for online Edexcel lessons?
faqs.answer: Less than people expect. A laptop or tablet on a table rather than a lap, a reliable connection, headphones, and a printed past paper with a pen. The screen is for the tutor's annotation and explanation; the working should still happen by hand, because Edexcel maths and science are written subjects assessed on paper under timing. A second small screen or a propped phone camera showing the page helps but is not essential. Nothing needs to be bought before a trial lesson tells you whether the arrangement suits your household.

faqs.question: Who else can be in the room while an online Edexcel lesson is running?
faqs.answer: Anyone you like, and we encourage a parent to be within earshot for the first two or three sessions. After that it is usually better to step back, because the student needs to own the hour and a watched teenager performs rather than works. What matters more than presence is the layout: a desk in a shared part of the home with the door open, rather than a laptop in a bedroom. That arrangement is also the sensible safeguarding default for any one-to-one teaching, in any format.

faqs.question: Are lesson recordings kept, and what happens to my daughter's data?
faqs.answer: Sessions are recorded only when a family asks for it. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs personal data here, and a minor's data deserves an explicit answer rather than a buried policy. Ask any provider three things: is the session recorded and who can watch it, where do the marked scripts live and can you take copies, and what does the enquiry form collect and why. Our enquiries need the specification codes, the year group and a contact; not a photograph, a report card or a list of grades.

faqs.question: We have two children on Edexcel courses. Does a visiting tutor work out cheaper?
faqs.answer: Only if both children need the same subject at the same level, which is unusual. One travel cost spread across two consecutive hours does reduce the premium, so a visiting arrangement is at its most economic in exactly this case. The catch is specialism: a tutor strong in 4MA1 Higher is not automatically the right person for 4ET1, and two consecutive hours with a generalist can cost more per recovered mark than two separate specialists. Price it per mark moved rather than per visit, and run a diagnostic paper for each child first.

faqs.question: Does an online tutor charge less than a visiting tutor for the same Edexcel paper?
faqs.answer: On the published figures, yes, and by a meaningful margin. A qualified subject tutor working online sits in a band of roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour in this market, while the in-home band runs AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included. The difference is not teaching quality; it is a car and the opportunity cost of the driver's evening. Those are market rates with their sources named, gathered in October 2026. Whether the premium is worth paying depends on whether you are buying expertise or an adult in the room.

faqs.question: Our Wi-Fi drops in the evening. What happens to a lesson that cuts out?
faqs.answer: Tell us before the first session so the plan accounts for it. Practical mitigations work: a wired connection or a position closer to the router, a phone hotspot as the agreed fallback, and a rule that anything lost to a genuine technical failure is made up rather than billed. Because the materials are a printed paper and a shared document, a two-minute dropout costs two minutes rather than the session. Households in older island apartment stock and in some high-rise buildings report this most, so it is a normal conversation rather than an awkward one.

faqs.question: How do we get the marked papers if the tutor is not in the house?
faqs.answer: The student works on a printed paper by hand, photographs or scans it, and the tutor annotates the scan against the published Pearson mark scheme. You receive the annotated version, dated, and it stays yours. Over a term that folder becomes the only reliable answer to whether the tuition is working, because it lets you compare a week-one paper with a week-five paper on the same scheme. It is also what you hand to the school, or to a different tutor, without anybody starting again from nothing.

faqs.question: What should we ask a visiting tutor before letting them into the house?
faqs.answer: Four things, in this order. Do you hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit, and may I see it. Do you currently teach at my child's school, because in this emirate that should rule you out. Is the price per sixty minutes, and does it include marking against the published mark scheme. And what written record will exist after a month. A tutor who answers all four without hesitation is probably the right sort of person regardless of format; one who deflects on the permit question has told you something important.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to after Iftar during Ramadan in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families do. School days shorten and the usable study hours shift into the evening, so a post-Iftar slot often works better than the usual half past five. The sensible pattern is to keep the same weekly cadence but shorten sessions, because concentration rather than willingness is the limiting factor that month. Agree the Ramadan arrangement at the start of the year rather than in the week before it begins; plans that are renegotiated under pressure are the ones that quietly stop.

faqs.question: What happens if we need to reschedule a session at short notice?
faqs.answer: Ask for the notice period in writing before you book anything, from us or anybody. Our working rule is that a slot moved with reasonable notice is moved, a slot missed without notice is used, and anything lost to a technical failure on our side is made up. The reason to settle this early is that rescheduling is the most common friction point in a year-long arrangement in this market, and an unstated policy becomes an argument in week nine rather than a line in a message in week one.

faqs.question: Is group tuition at a centre in Abu Dhabi a cheaper option than either?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes; per recovered mark, often not. A group class costs less per student and delivers less individual talk time and far less marking, which is where most of the value sits for an Edexcel candidate with eleven specific missing marks. It also adds a second school run at the end of an already long day. Groups work well for broad revision across a cohort and for students who are broadly secure and need pace. They work poorly when the problem is one topic, one method chain or one paper's timing.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-home-tutor.closingHeading: Decide what you are actually buying
abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-home-tutor.closingBody: If the thing your household needs is an adult at the table, a visiting tutor is a real answer and the band to negotiate within is roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour. If what you need is somebody who has taught 4CH1 or 4PM1 to Year 11 many times, at full value for every minute you pay for, with marked papers you keep, then online one-to-one is the stronger purchase and it is what we deliver in Abu Dhabi. Tell us the codes, the community and the hour, take the free trial, and test the format on a real timed question before deciding anything.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-ict-4it1-tutor.tutorsIntro: The teachers below work on Pearson Edexcel International GCSE ICT and the office-and-data skills it assesses. Each one works in the software with the candidate rather than describing it, because a 4IT1 practical mark is earned by what ends up in the file, not by what the student can explain about it.

intro.heading: The one IGCSE where a parent can audit the work without the specification
paragraphs: Most subjects leave a parent dependent on somebody else's judgement. You cannot mark a chemistry answer or check a Python program, so you buy hours on trust and wait for a mock. ICT is different, and almost nobody says so out loud. The output of a 4IT1 session is a file: a spreadsheet, a database, a document, a presentation, a web page. You can open it on your own laptop. You can click a cell and read the formula bar. You can sort a column and see whether the data moves as a block or breaks apart. That makes ICT the one qualification on your child's timetable where you can check the work yourself in about four minutes.

This page is written around that fact, because it changes what tutoring in Abu Dhabi should look like. Instead of a progress report, the end of each session produces a file and a short note naming what in that file would score and what would not. You keep both. After a month you have a set of files and a version trail, and the comparison between the first spreadsheet and the fourth is something you can see rather than something you are told about. A tutor who cannot produce that in a software subject is selling conversation, and in ICT conversation is unusually easy to sell, because the subject sounds familiar to adults who use the same software at work.

The two 4IT1 components fail in different ways. The written paper examines ICT systems, networks, data and the social, legal and ethical issues around them, and it rewards evaluation against a stated purpose rather than description of features. The practical paper puts a candidate in front of a computer with provided data files and a task brief, and marks what the file shows: the formula that calculates rather than the number typed in, the query that answers the question actually asked, the document that follows the house style it was given. A candidate can be comfortable with software and still lose heavily on the practical paper by not reading the brief twice.

Abu Dhabi adds its own conditions. Private schools in the emirate are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, so there is a published inspection outcome you can read before buying anything. Schools must also deliver Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies alongside the licensed curriculum, which compresses the option blocks; in several Abu Dhabi schools ICT and Computer Science are timetabled against each other, so a Year 9 choice becomes irreversible. And because practical work depends on a computer room, access to practice time at school varies more between Abu Dhabi schools than any other variable in this subject.

One honest note before the detail. Nobody can guarantee a 4IT1 grade, and a tutor who offers one is telling you something about their marketing rather than their teaching. What this page offers instead is auditability: files you can open, a note you can read, a version trail you can compare, and a specification checklist that says what has been practised and what has not. The sections below show you exactly what to click, what good looks like in each task area, what the Abu Dhabi market charges, and what to ask your child's school before you spend anything at all.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-ict-4it1-tutor.programmesIntro: 4IT1 sits inside a route, and the decision made at option time shapes what comes after it. These are the qualifications an Abu Dhabi ICT candidate moves between, and what each one assumes the student can already do with software and data.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE ICT
programmes.description: The qualification on this page. Two components: a written paper on ICT systems, data, networks and the social, legal and ethical issues around them, and a practical examination completed on a computer using provided data files. The practical work draws on document production, spreadsheet modelling, database work, presentation and web authoring. Confirm current paper structure, timings and software guidance on the Pearson specification, because Pearson revises its documents between series.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi, 4IT1 is usually taught in British-curriculum schools that also offer Computer Science, and the two often occupy the same option block. Because practical lessons need a computer room, the amount of hands-on time a candidate gets differs sharply between schools in the same emirate, and that difference is the single most common reason a family ends up buying ICT hours.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Computer Science
programmes.description: The subject 4IT1 is most often confused with. Computer Science examines the principles of computing in a written paper and problem solving through code in an onscreen paper. It is not a harder version of ICT and ICT is not a lighter version of it; they assess different things, and a student who enjoys building usable documents and models frequently scores better in ICT than in a programming paper.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi families moving in from CBSE or American schools mid-cycle sometimes find their child has studied neither in any depth. The first job is then to decide which of the two the remaining time can realistically carry, and for a candidate with one year left the practical, file-based nature of ICT is usually the more recoverable of the two.

programmes.name: Pearson International A Level and post-16 routes
programmes.description: Where ICT candidates go next. Some continue into applied computing or business-and-information courses; others move to subjects that use the data-handling skills rather than examining them. The practical habits built in 4IT1, particularly modelling in a spreadsheet and designing a query, transfer directly into business, economics and any post-16 course with a research component.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi students planning on UAE universities should check the Ministry of Education equivalency requirements for the British track: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at grade E or two AS Levels. Whether a particular ICT grade is accepted for a particular degree is a question for the university and the attestation authority rather than a tutor.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 computing and ICT, before the option choice
programmes.description: The stage where the real gap opens. Key Stage 3 computing in Abu Dhabi schools ranges from a structured course with proper software teaching to a few lessons a term shared with another subject. A candidate arriving in Year 10 without touching a spreadsheet formula is starting 4IT1 from behind, and that is a diagnosis rather than a judgement.
programmes.countryNote: Families choosing options in Year 9 in Abu Dhabi should ask two concrete questions: how many timetabled periods a week does ICT get, and does the practical teaching happen in a computer room or on personal devices. The answers predict how much outside support a candidate will need more reliably than any inspection grade does.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-ict-4it1-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Pearson International GCSE codes that most often share an Abu Dhabi timetable with 4IT1, and what each one assesses. The pattern worth noticing is how many of them reward the same skill ICT rewards: a judgement made against a stated purpose.

subjects.name: ICT (4IT1)
subjects.description: Written theory on systems, data, networks and the issues around them, plus a practical examination on a computer with provided files. Marks are lost on practical tasks that look finished but typed a value where a formula was wanted, and on written answers that describe a feature without judging it against a purpose.

subjects.name: Computer Science (4CP0)
subjects.description: Principles of computer science in a written paper and problem solving with code in an onscreen paper. A different subject from ICT with different marks available; the overlap is in data representation and networks, which is why candidates sometimes revise the two together.

subjects.name: Business (4BS1)
subjects.description: The closest companion subject in skill terms. Its evaluation questions want a judgement, a reason and a consequence in a named context, which is exactly what the ICT written paper wants. Students who learn the structure in one subject transfer it quickly to the other.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.description: Underpins the spreadsheet modelling tasks more than families expect. Percentage change, rounding and the difference between a displayed value and a stored value all appear in practical work, and a candidate shaky on those will produce models that look right and calculate wrong.

subjects.name: Economics (4EC1)
subjects.description: Shares the data-interpretation demand. Reading a chart for what it actually shows, rather than what the title suggests, is marked in both subjects, and both punish an answer that stops at description before reaching a judgement.

subjects.name: English Language A (4EA1)
subjects.description: Decides whether a technically competent ICT candidate can write an answer the examiner can credit. Evaluation questions need controlled sentences with a clear subject, and in a second or third language that is a skill to practise rather than assume.

subjects.name: Physics (4PH1)
subjects.description: Overlaps on hardware, signals and networks, and shares the habit of showing working. A diagram or screenshot without stated reasoning collects little in either subject, because the reasoning is what the mark scheme pays for.

subjects.name: Chemistry (4CH1)
subjects.description: Taken alongside ICT by students heading towards applied science. Its extended answers train the sequencing discipline the ICT written paper rewards: linked statements in the right order, each one doing work rather than restating the last.

subjects.name: Biology (4BI1)
subjects.description: Useful as a reference point for command terms. Describe, explain, compare and evaluate mean the same things in 4BI1 as in 4IT1, and a student who has learned them in a science can apply them to an ICT scenario question in one session.

subjects.name: Further Pure Mathematics (4PM1)
subjects.description: A smaller overlap, but relevant for candidates taking ICT alongside a strong maths route. The shared habit is defining a process precisely before executing it, which is what designing a spreadsheet model actually is.

sections.heading: How to open your child's 4IT1 file and read it like a marker
paragraphs: This takes four minutes and needs no knowledge of the specification. Open the spreadsheet your child produced and click on a cell that holds a result. If the formula bar shows a number, the mark is gone: the task wanted a calculation and received a typed answer. If it shows a formula, read whether it refers to cells or has numbers buried inside it, because a model with a tax rate typed into twelve formulas cannot be updated and loses the point of modelling. Then widen a column that shows hashes, because a printed output a marker cannot read scores nothing.

Do the same with a document. Look at whether headings are consistent, whether the font changes halfway down, whether the brief asked for a particular style and the file follows it. Open a presentation and check that the text is readable at a distance rather than pasted in at nine points. For a database, sort a column and watch what happens: if the rest of the row travels with it, the structure is sound, and if the data breaks apart, there is a structural problem no query will fix.

None of this makes you an ICT teacher. It makes you able to tell, in minutes, whether an hour you paid for produced work that would score. That is a reasonable thing to want in a subject where the output is a file sitting on a laptop you own. The table below is the audit we give Abu Dhabi parents at the start, written so it can be used by somebody who has never seen the specification and does not intend to.

sections.heading: What 4IT1 actually assesses, and how it differs from Computer Science
paragraphs: The written component covers ICT systems and their components, networks and the internet, data and its organisation, the software used to produce documents and models, and the social, legal and ethical issues that come with digital systems. The practical component is a task brief completed on a computer using provided data files, drawing on document production, spreadsheet modelling, database work, presentation and web authoring. Both carry substantial weight, so a candidate strong in one still needs the other; confirm the current structure and timings on the Pearson specification rather than from memory.

The difference from Computer Science is not difficulty, it is what is being examined. Computer Science asks a candidate to produce an algorithm and express it in code. ICT asks a candidate to use existing tools correctly to meet a stated purpose, and to judge whether a system suits that purpose. Those are different skills with different failure modes, and a student who is methodical about following instructions but dislikes abstraction will usually find ICT the better fit. The reverse is also true, and option evenings in Abu Dhabi frequently get this backwards by presenting ICT as the easier route.

What ICT is not is a subject where familiarity with software is sufficient. Every year candidates who have used spreadsheets since Year 7 lose practical marks because they did not read the brief twice, did not save with the file name specified, or typed a result rather than calculating it. The written paper punishes the same casualness in a different register: an answer listing features of a system when the question asked whether the system suited a named purpose. The decision table below is what we put in front of Abu Dhabi families choosing between the two subjects in Year 9.

sections.heading: Answering the legal and ethical questions with UAE examples
paragraphs: The written paper's issues questions are the part Abu Dhabi candidates most often answer with borrowed British examples, and they are also the easiest part of the paper to make locally concrete. The UAE has its own personal data protection law, Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021, which gives individuals rights over their personal data and places duties on organisations that process it. A candidate who can name a real legal framework from the country they live in, and describe what it requires of an organisation, is doing exactly what an evaluation question asks: applying a principle to a named context.

The same localisation works across the issues topics. Private tutoring itself is a usable example: individuals providing private lessons in the UAE need a work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the permit is granted free of charge for two years. That is a digital-services application process, a licensing regime and a data-collection exercise in one, and it gives a candidate a concrete example when a question asks about the use of online government services. School data is another: a student can discuss what their own school holds about them and why.

Two cautions belong here, and they are the kind of thing a tutor should be teaching rather than a page asserting. First, a candidate should never state a penalty figure they cannot source; the UAE authorities have not published a fine schedule for unlicensed private tutoring, so an answer that invents one is weaker than one that says penalties apply under the applicable laws. Second, a law should be named and described, not paraphrased into something it does not say. Precision is what the marks are for, and a scenario answer grounded in a real UAE framework is harder to fault than one built on a half-remembered foreign statute.
bullets: Name Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 for UAE personal data protection

sections.heading: Spreadsheet tasks: the formula bar test and what it exposes
paragraphs: Spreadsheet work carries more recoverable marks than any other practical area, because its failures are habits rather than gaps in understanding. The first habit is typing results. A candidate who works out a total mentally and types it has produced a correct-looking file with nothing creditable in the cell. The second is burying constants: a commission rate written into every formula instead of referenced from one cell, so the model cannot be changed and the point of a model is lost. The third is formatting that hides errors, including columns too narrow to read and rounding that makes a wrong figure look right.

Absolute and relative references are the technical skill underneath. A formula copied down a column has to know which part of it should move and which should stay, and a candidate who has never been shown the distinction will fill a column with plausible nonsense. This is a thirty-minute teaching job and a two-week habit job, which is why it belongs early in a plan rather than in the fortnight before a series. Charts are the other reliable loss: axes unlabelled, a title that repeats the sheet name, a chart type that cannot show what was asked.

The useful thing for a parent is that every one of those failures is visible in the file. You do not need to know the task brief to see a typed number in a results cell or an unlabelled axis. That is why the weekly artefact in a spreadsheet block is the file itself plus a note listing which of these habits appeared and whether it appeared again the following week. Repetition in that list is the real finding; a single occurrence is just a mistake.

sections.heading: Database tasks: three questions that reveal whether the query was understood
paragraphs: Database work is where 4IT1 candidates lose marks quietly, because a wrong answer here looks as tidy as a right one. The first question to ask about any query is what the brief asked for in its own words. Briefs are specific: records above a value and before a date, sorted one way, showing named fields only. A query that returns the right records with every field included has not followed the instruction, and the instruction was the mark. Reading the brief aloud and underlining each condition takes a minute and recovers more than any amount of software practice.

The second question is whether the structure can support the query at all. If the table was built with a single field holding a name and a department together, no query can separate them cleanly, and the candidate will produce a workaround that costs time and marks. Structure first, then queries: fields with one piece of data each, sensible data types, and validation where the brief asks for it. A parent can test this without knowing anything about databases by sorting a column and watching whether the rows stay intact.

The third question is what the output actually shows. A query that is correct but displays every field, or sorts the wrong way, or includes the heading row in the sort, presents as finished work and marks as incomplete. Reports have the same trap: data correct, layout unreadable, fields truncated. The teaching move is to finish every database task by re-reading the brief against the output, condition by condition, which is a discipline rather than a skill and so transfers to every other task area in the paper.
bullets: Underline every condition in the brief before touching the software
One piece of data per field, decided before any query is written
Check the sort direction and whether headings were included
Show only the fields the brief named, not everything available

sections.heading: Documents, presentations and web authoring: following a brief you did not write
paragraphs: The production tasks look like the easy part of the paper and routinely are not. A brief specifies a purpose, an audience, a house style and often a file name, and each of those is checkable. Marks go on consistency: the same heading style throughout, images placed and sized rather than dropped in, text that fits its frame, a file saved where and how the brief said. These are not aesthetic judgements, which is why a candidate who insists on their own design choices loses marks for work that looks better than the specification wanted.

Presentation tasks fail on readability and on audience. Nine-point text pasted from a document is unreadable on a screen, and a slide dense with paragraphs ignores what a presentation is for. The brief usually names the audience, and that name is the criterion the examiner uses. Web authoring tasks fail on structure: navigation that does not work, headings that are formatted text rather than actual headings, images without alternative text where the brief asked for accessibility.

The common thread across all three is that the brief is the mark scheme, and reading it twice is worth more than any software shortcut. In teaching this we spend the first part of a task reading the brief and listing its conditions as a checklist, then build, then check the file against the list before saving. That produces the artefact a parent can audit and, more usefully, a habit that survives into the examination room, where nobody will be there to ask whether the brief was read.
bullets: List every condition in the brief as a checklist before building

sections.heading: The weekly file trail, and what a month of it shows
paragraphs: A single marked file tells you very little. A sequence of them, dated and kept, tells you whether anything is changing. That is the whole method on this page: every session saves a file, the note names which habits appeared, and the following week's note says whether they appeared again. After four weeks you have a list that reads like a diagnosis rather than an opinion, and you can see which problems are closing and which are being talked about rather than fixed.

The trail also protects against a particular kind of waste. ICT is a subject where sessions can feel productive while circling the same comfortable software, because building a neat document is more pleasant than practising a database query under time. A dated list of task areas practised makes that visible immediately: four weeks of spreadsheets and no database work is not a plan, it is a preference. The checklist is the only reliable guard against it, and it costs nothing to maintain.

The table below is the shape most Abu Dhabi families settle into with one session a week. A school practical mock replaces whatever was scheduled, because the school's own timed task is better evidence than anything set at home. The right-hand column is the question the week's file answers, so you can check the trail without reading the specification or asking anyone to interpret it.

Keep the files somewhere you control rather than inside a school platform or a tutor's account. Two reasons: a platform login disappears when a term or a provider ends, and a trail you cannot open is not evidence. A dated folder on a home machine, one file per session, is enough. It also makes the handover painless if a family changes tutor mid-year, which happens often enough in this subject to plan for, and it gives the next teacher a diagnosis in ten minutes rather than a session.

sections.heading: What 4IT1 support costs in Abu Dhabi, and what the hour is spent on
paragraphs: Published rates in this market, read in October 2026, cover a wide range: Tutopiya advertises online sessions from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65; Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150; TutorChase lists AED 270 for specialist support; Bestimate's rate table puts agency-arranged in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500; BartyED publishes AED 650. Those are each provider's own published figures, not ours. IB Gram does not publish a rate card on these pages; the first lesson is free, one per family, and a continuing rate is agreed after the diagnostic.

What matters more in ICT than the band is what the hour is spent doing, because the subject offers an unusually easy way to spend money badly. An hour of someone talking about spreadsheets is worth very little; an hour in which the student drives the software while a teacher watches and corrects is worth a great deal, and the two cost the same. The file you are left with distinguishes them better than any description of teaching method. If an hour produces no file, you have bought the first kind.

sections.heading: ADEK, your school's computer room, and what to ask before buying hours
paragraphs: In Abu Dhabi the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools, and publishes inspection outcomes. Read your child's before buying anything: it will not grade ICT separately, but judgements on teaching and progress in the relevant phase, plus any comment on provision or staffing, usually tell you whether the gap is the department's or your child's. Those are different problems and the second one is the only one tutoring fixes efficiently.

Then ask the school three questions that matter more in this subject than in any other. How many timetabled periods a week does ICT get. Is practical teaching done in a computer room or on personal devices. Which software versions does the school use, since a candidate practising at home on something different will meet small interface differences at exactly the wrong moment. The answers tell you how much practice time your child has actually had, which is the real variable behind most 4IT1 marks in the emirate.

One rule is worth knowing before you ask a teacher for private lessons. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for school staff have been reported to prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and a teacher tutoring outside school hours is expected to hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Treat that as press-reported and check the current ADEK document before acting on it. The permit route itself is official: free of charge, valid for two years, applied for through MoHRE's own channels, and tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule to quote.

sections.heading: Teaching a software subject over live video, and the equipment check
paragraphs: Tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is an India-only service and nobody will arrive at an Abu Dhabi address. For ICT the online format is the natural one. The work is software, the student needs to be the one holding the mouse, and a shared screen lets a teacher watch the technique rather than the result. Sessions can also be paused on the file and resumed next week exactly where they stopped.

The equipment check is short and worth doing before the first lesson rather than during it. The student needs a laptop or desktop with the office-type software their school uses, a browser, and a headset if the household is busy. A tablet is adequate for written-paper work and poor for practical tasks, because the paper rewards comfortable editing rather than reading. The most common Abu Dhabi obstacle is a school-issued device with locked software or restricted screen sharing, which is solvable only by using a home machine, so it is better discovered early.

There are honest trade-offs. A student who will not stay on task without an adult nearby needs one for the first few weeks. A shared apartment on Al Reem Island needs an agreed quiet hour. Set against that, the teaching pool stops being limited to specialists who can reach your community before dinner, which in ICT matters: the local market in the outer mainland communities offers generalists, and a generalist can teach the theory respectably while struggling to coach a timed practical brief.

process.title: Send the brief, not just the subject
process.description: The most useful first message says which component is the problem and attaches something concrete: a practical task the school returned, a mock script, or even a photograph of a marked sheet. In a file-based subject the artefact tells us in minutes what a conversation would take a session to uncover.

process.title: A free diagnostic, inside the software
process.description: One free lesson per family, no card details collected. The student completes a short task brief while the teacher watches the technique, then answers two scenario questions. You receive the file and a note naming the habits present. You can open the file and check the note against it yourself.

process.title: A plan with a task-area checklist
process.description: The plan names which practical areas will be practised and in what order, how the written paper is handled, and the weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time. The checklist is dated, because the question that matters after a month is which areas have still not been touched.

process.title: Weekly sessions that end with a saved file
process.description: The student drives the software; the teacher corrects live. Each session saves a dated file and a short note on what would score and what would not. Those two things are the whole record, and they are designed to be read by a parent rather than by another teacher.

process.title: A timed brief, then an honest review
process.description: Around week four a full task brief is done under exam-length conditions, and the note records which habits reappeared under time. That is the point to decide whether to continue, change the focus or stop, based on the file trail rather than on how the sessions felt.

whyPoints.title: You can audit the work in four minutes
whyPoints.description: Open the file, click a result cell, read the formula bar, sort a database column, check the axis labels. In ICT the output is a file you own, so you can verify what an hour produced without knowing the specification or trusting anyone's summary of it.

whyPoints.title: The student holds the mouse
whyPoints.description: Practical marks are earned by technique under time, and technique only improves when the student does the work while someone watches. A session where the teacher demonstrates and the student observes produces an understanding of software and no marks.

whyPoints.title: Both components tracked separately
whyPoints.description: Written scenario technique and practical task technique move at different speeds and fail for different reasons. Keeping separate records stops the enjoyable practical work from absorbing hours that the written paper needed.

whyPoints.title: UAE examples in the issues answers
whyPoints.description: Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on personal data protection and the MoHRE private tuition permit are real local frameworks a candidate can name and describe. A scenario answer grounded in the country the student lives in is harder to fault than a borrowed one.

whyPoints.description: ADEK rather than KHDA, mainland and island commute patterns that decide session timing, and the practical-access question that varies more between Abu Dhabi schools than anything else in this subject. A page that would fit any city would help nobody.

faqs.question: How can I check my child's 4IT1 spreadsheet work myself?
faqs.answer: Open it and click on a cell that holds a result. If the formula bar shows a number, the task wanted a calculation and got a typed answer, and the mark is gone. If it shows a formula, check whether rates and constants are referenced from their own cells or buried inside the formula, because a buried value defeats the purpose of a model. Widen any column that prints as hash marks, and read the axis labels on any chart. That audit takes about four minutes, needs no knowledge of the specification, and tells you whether the hour you paid for produced creditable work.

faqs.question: What should the formula bar show after a 4IT1 modelling task?
faqs.answer: A formula that refers to other cells, with any rate or constant held in one cell and referenced rather than repeated. If the same percentage appears typed inside eight formulas, the model cannot be updated and the examiner can see that the candidate did not understand what a model is for. You should also be able to copy a formula down a column and have it stay correct, which is what absolute and relative references are for. A candidate who has not been taught that distinction will produce a column of plausible, wrong numbers.

faqs.question: Is ICT a softer option than Computer Science for an Abu Dhabi student?
faqs.answer: No, and option evenings often imply otherwise. The two subjects assess different things. Computer Science asks a student to produce an algorithm and express it in code. ICT asks them to use existing tools correctly for a stated purpose and to judge whether a system suits that purpose. A methodical student who dislikes abstraction usually scores better in ICT; a student who enjoys building logic from nothing usually scores better in Computer Science. Choose on how your child prefers to work. In many Abu Dhabi schools the two sit in the same option block, so the decision is effectively made once.

faqs.question: Which software will my child need for the 4IT1 practical component?
faqs.answer: Office-type applications covering documents, spreadsheets, databases, presentations and web authoring, and the practical component is sat on a computer with data files provided. The important thing is to practise in the same software family the school uses, because small interface differences cost time under exam conditions. Ask the school which versions it runs before setting up anything at home. The common Abu Dhabi complication is a school-issued laptop with locked software or restricted screen sharing, which usually means practice has to happen on a home machine instead.

faqs.question: Can my child use UAE data protection law in a written ICT answer?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a stronger answer than a borrowed foreign example. The UAE has its own personal data protection law, Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021, which gives individuals rights over their personal data and places duties on the organisations processing it. Naming a real framework from the country the student lives in, then describing what it requires of an organisation in the scenario, is exactly what an evaluation question rewards. The rule is to name and describe accurately rather than paraphrase, and never to state a penalty figure the student cannot source.

faqs.question: Why do 4IT1 candidates lose marks on work that looks finished?
faqs.answer: Because the brief is the mark scheme and tidy work is not the same as compliant work. Briefs specify a purpose, an audience, a house style, which fields to show, how to sort, and often a file name. A document in the student's preferred style, a query showing every field, a report that truncates data, a file saved under the wrong name: each loses marks while looking complete. The fix is a habit rather than a skill. Read the brief, list its conditions, build, then check the file against the list before saving. It survives into the exam room, where nobody will prompt them.

faqs.question: What does a dated file trail show that a single mark cannot?
faqs.answer: Whether anything is changing, and whether the same mistake keeps returning. One marked file is a snapshot and a mistake in it might be nothing. Four dated files with notes make a pattern: the typed-result habit appeared in week one, was absent in week two, came back under time in week four. That is a finding you can act on. The trail also exposes a particular waste in ICT, where sessions drift towards comfortable software work, so four weeks of spreadsheets and no database practice becomes visible immediately rather than at the mock.

faqs.question: How much does an Edexcel IGCSE ICT 4it1 tutor cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market rates read in October 2026 range from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour at the student-tutor end, through AED 150 to 300 for qualified subject tutors online, to AED 270 for specialist support and AED 650 at the premium end; agency-arranged in-home visits are published at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate. Those are other providers' own figures. IB Gram publishes no rate card here: the first lesson is free, one per family, and a continuing rate follows the diagnostic, because an hour of software basics and an hour of timed practical work are different products.

faqs.question: Does an ICT grade count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: The British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at grade E or two AS Levels at the same grade. Whether a specific subject is accepted for a specific programme is a question for the Ministry and for the university's own admissions office, not for a tutor, and equivalency rules are administrative and do change. Verify the current wording on moe.gov.ae before relying on it. No tutoring is required for equivalency, and anyone suggesting otherwise is misdescribing a government process.

faqs.question: What should I ask our Abu Dhabi school about its ICT provision?
faqs.answer: Three questions, and they are more useful than any inspection grade. How many timetabled periods a week does ICT actually get. Is practical teaching delivered in a computer room or on personal devices. Which software versions does the school use. The answers tell you how many genuine hands-on hours your child has had, which is the variable behind most practical marks in this emirate. Add a fourth if staffing has changed mid-cohort: ask which task areas have been covered so far, because the school's own record is sometimes incomplete after a handover.

faqs.question: How many 4IT1 sessions does a Year 11 in Abu Dhabi usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends which problem the diagnostic finds, and the honest answer waits for it. Habit problems, such as typing results or ignoring the brief, often change within three or four sessions because the student already has the skill. Technical gaps like absolute references or database structure need teaching plus a fortnight of practice. Written-paper technique moves at the speed of command-term work, usually a few sessions. Most exam-year families settle on one weekly hour plus a denser timed block before the series, then review against the file trail rather than renewing automatically.

faqs.question: Are 4IT1 lessons for Abu Dhabi families taught online or at our address?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India, and nobody will arrive at an Abu Dhabi address. For a software subject the online format is the stronger one: the student holds the mouse, the teacher watches technique on a shared screen, and the file is saved and resumed next week. Published in-home rates in this market, AED 180 to 500 an hour, also carry the travel cost inside them.

faqs.question: Who is allowed to touch the file my child will be assessed on?
faqs.answer: Only your child. A tutor teaches, demonstrates on a separate example, reviews the student's own file and marks it, and sets a harder version of the same task. A tutor does not operate the keyboard on work that will be presented as the student's, and no tutor should produce assessed work for a student in any subject. In 4IT1 the practical component is sat under examination conditions, so the deeper point is practical: a candidate whose practice files were built by somebody else arrives with no technique and a folder suggesting otherwise.

faqs.question: What happens to ICT sessions during Ramadan in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: They move. Abu Dhabi schools shorten the day during Ramadan and household routines change substantially, so a fixed late-afternoon slot usually stops working for a month. Sessions commonly move to after Iftar, which is simpler online because no journey has to be rebuilt around the new time. Practical work also suits that period reasonably well: a shorter, task-focused session inside the software is more productive when concentration is limited than a long written-technique session would be. The file trail continues through it, which keeps the month from becoming a gap in the record.

faqs.question: Does my child need Microsoft Office at home, or will free software do?
faqs.answer: What matters is practising in the same software family the school and the examination use, because the practical component is marked on what the file shows and small interface differences cost time under pressure. Free alternatives are usable for learning concepts such as absolute references or query conditions, and they differ enough in menus and functions to be a poor choice in the final weeks. Ask the school which versions it runs, and if the school device is locked down, set up a home machine instead. This is worth sorting before the first session rather than mid-task.

faqs.question: What does ADEK's inspection outcome tell me about ICT teaching?
faqs.answer: Not a subject grade, but enough to be worth reading first. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and publishes inspection outcomes, and the useful parts for this subject are the judgements on teaching quality and progress in the relevant phase, plus any comment on provision or staffing. Read alongside your child's school reports, it usually tells you whether the department has been stable. If it changed hands mid-cohort, ask which task areas were actually covered, because the handover is where coverage gaps in this subject normally come from.

Send the component, the school, the software your child uses, and a workable hour in Gulf Standard Time.

Rates are quoted after a diagnostic rather than from a tariff, because a Higher tier candidate twelve weeks from the November series and a Year 10 Foundation candidate need different hours for different money.

intro.heading: Why nobody will quote you a 4MA1 price
paragraphs: Search for maths tutoring in this emirate and you will find page after page that discusses value, quality and outcomes without printing a single number. In the competitor set researched for these queries, three of six published no price at all, one published a rate in its schema that contradicted the figure in its own body copy, and the two that did quote money quoted US dollars, which is not the currency a family in Al Reef pays anyone in. One agency page asks the price question in its own FAQ list and then declines to answer it.

So here is the structure of the market in AED, taken from providers' own published pages and from a dated rate survey, with every figure attributed. Budget online tutoring, usually a university student, sits at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour. A qualified subject tutor online runs about AED 150 to 300. An in-home visit with travel inside the rate runs about AED 180 to 500. A declared IGCSE or A Level specialist runs about AED 200 to 450 or more, and a premium named tutor has been published at AED 650. Those are market rates and not an IB Gram tariff.

The reason a tutor cannot sensibly quote you before looking at the work is that 4MA1 hides two completely different jobs behind one syllabus code. A Year 10 candidate who needs the Foundation tier content secured over eighteen months needs a steady weekly hour and very little marking. A Year 11 Higher tier candidate ten weeks from the series needs fewer sessions and far more between-session labour: papers marked question by question, a topic ranking by marks dropped, and a revision order built from that ranking. The second job costs more per hour and fewer hours in total.

The third variable is tier, and it is a money question as much as an academic one. Pearson offers 4MA1 at Foundation tier, where the grade range tops out well below the top of the scale, and at Higher tier, which reaches the top grades. A candidate entered at the wrong tier either loses access to grades they could have earned or spends a year failing to answer questions pitched above them. Getting that decision right in Year 10 saves more money than any hourly discount, and it is a decision the school makes on evidence the tutor can help produce.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared whiteboard. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to an address is a service we run only in India. For a 4MA1 candidate that is mostly a pricing fact rather than a pedagogical one: an online hour is an hour of maths, while an in-home hour in Abu Dhabi has somebody's drive from the island to Shakhbout City priced into it, which is why the two market ranges differ by roughly the cost of the car.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-maths-a-4ma1-tut.programmesIntro: 4MA1 sits in the middle of a route, and the cost of support depends heavily on which end of that route a family is planning from. These are the stages Abu Dhabi schools actually run around it.

programmes.name: Year 9 preparation for the International GCSE route
programmes.description: The cheapest point in the whole sequence to intervene. Most 4MA1 grades are decided by whether fractions, negative indices, rearranging and basic algebraic manipulation are automatic before the course starts. An hour a fortnight in Year 9 costs a fraction of a Year 11 rescue block and removes most of the reason one is ever needed.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools set their tier recommendations during Year 10, using internal assessment evidence from late Year 9 onwards. A family that waits for the first formal tier conversation is reacting to data rather than shaping it, and in an emirate where option and tier letters go out before the winter break that timing matters.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1)
programmes.description: Two written papers, each two hours, each worth one hundred marks and half the qualification, with a calculator permitted in both and no coursework component. Content runs across number and the number system, equations, formulae and identities, sequences, functions and graphs, geometry and trigonometry, vectors and transformation geometry, and statistics and probability.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE exams in May/June and November each year, which gives Abu Dhabi candidates a genuine second window rather than a full year's wait. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Centres differ in whether they will enter a candidate in November, so ask the maths department before building a plan around it.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International AS and A Level Mathematics
programmes.description: The usual destination for a strong Higher tier 4MA1 candidate. The step up is in algebraic fluency rather than new topics, which is why candidates who scraped a grade through heavy calculator use at IGCSE struggle in the first term. Pure content assumes the 4MA1 Higher algebra is already automatic.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run the Pearson post-16 route alongside the IB Diploma, and families choosing between them at the end of Year 11 are usually choosing on breadth rather than on maths difficulty. The maths-only comparison is narrower than the marketing on either side suggests.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: The other common destination, and the one where the 4MA1 tier decision comes back. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes confident algebraic manipulation from day one; Applications and Interpretation leans on modelling and technology. A Foundation tier 4MA1 candidate entering Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is taking on a very steep first term.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has a long-established Diploma cohort across the island and the mainland corridor, and university requirements in the UAE and abroad differ on which maths course they accept for engineering, economics and medicine. Check the specific course page rather than the general admissions page, in Year 11 rather than Year 13.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-maths-a-4ma1-tut.subjectsIntro: The 4MA1 specification is organised into content areas, and marks are dropped unevenly across them. These are the areas a tutor works through, plus the adjacent maths qualifications Abu Dhabi families most often ask about in the same conversation.

subjects.name: Numbers and the number system
subjects.description: Standard form, surds at Higher, percentage reverse problems, bounds and ratio. The cheapest marks on either paper and the most commonly dropped, because candidates meet this content in Year 9 and never revisit it. A single session on reverse percentages and bounds usually recovers more marks than one on trigonometry.

subjects.name: Equations, formulae and identities
subjects.description: Rearranging, simultaneous equations, quadratics by factorising, formula and completing the square at Higher, algebraic fractions and proof. This is the area that decides whether post-16 maths is realistic, and it is where a Higher tier candidate either has automatic manipulation or spends the paper fighting the algebra instead of the question.

subjects.name: Sequences, functions and graphs
subjects.description: Arithmetic and geometric sequences, nth term, function notation, inverse and composite functions at Higher, transformations of graphs, and differentiation on the Higher papers. Graph sketching is where method marks are most often available and least often claimed, because candidates plot points instead of describing shape.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, circle theorems, Pythagoras, right-angled and non-right-angled trigonometry, three-dimensional work and circle measure. The marks here are overwhelmingly in written reasoning: a correct answer with no stated angle fact scores less than a wrong answer with a correct chain of reasoning.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformation geometry
subjects.description: Column vectors, vector geometry proofs, and the transformation work that runs through both tiers. Vector proof questions are routinely abandoned by candidates who can do every step individually, which makes them one of the highest-yield topics for a short, targeted block of sessions.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Averages from tables, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals, tree diagrams and conditional probability. Histogram frequency density is the single most reliable source of dropped marks on the Higher papers, and it takes one session to fix permanently.

subjects.name: Calculator technique for both papers
subjects.description: A calculator is permitted in both 4MA1 papers, which changes what examiners reward. Candidates lose marks by rounding mid-calculation, by not showing the substitution a method mark depends on, and by not knowing their own model's statistical and fraction functions. Not a syllabus topic; routinely worth several marks.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Further Pure Mathematics (4PM1)
subjects.description: The extension qualification some Abu Dhabi schools run for strong mathematicians, covering calculus, series, logarithms and coordinate geometry. Families usually meet it as a surprise option letter in Year 10 and want to know whether it is worth the extra tutoring hours before committing.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics B (4MB1)
subjects.description: A different Edexcel maths specification with a different paper structure, sat by a smaller number of centres. Confirm with the maths department which code your child is entered against before buying any revision material, because past papers are not interchangeable between the two.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: The Cambridge equivalent, with Core and Extended tiers instead of Foundation and Higher and a different paper structure. Abu Dhabi families moving between schools sometimes change board mid-course, and the overlap is large but the question styles and the tiering rules are not identical.

These notes are about distance, evening timing and what the local tutoring market actually charges.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Dense, central, and the easiest part of the emirate for an in-home tutor to reach, which is why the local market quotes its lower in-home rates here. It is also the area where families most often compare an in-home quote against an online one and discover the gap is almost entirely travel.
