regions.note: A long villa corridor where school buses arrive late and in-home tutors quote a premium or a two-hour minimum to make the drive worthwhile. Online sessions here usually sit at 5.30pm or later, and a one-hour slot is genuinely one hour rather than fifty minutes of settling down.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Shamkha
regions.note: Further out again, and the point at which in-home quotes in this market start attracting a travel surcharge or simply a refusal. Families in these communities are the clearest beneficiaries of a rate with no car in it, and they tend to book later evening slots.

regions.name: Yas Island and Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Short commutes to the island schools and a high concentration of Higher tier candidates heading for competitive post-16 routes. The tutoring conversation here is usually about whether to add 4PM1 rather than whether 4MA1 is at risk, which changes the hours and the cost.

regions.name: Al Bateen, Al Mushrif and the Corniche
regions.note: Established inner-city neighbourhoods with large, experienced maths departments and strong internal cohorts. Local in-home supply is good here, so the honest comparison is specialist quality rather than availability, and that is the comparison online delivery wins.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: Mainland communities where a weekday evening is compressed by distance from the island schools. Friday and Saturday morning blocks work better than weekday hours for a paper-marking session that needs more than sixty minutes.

regions.name: Masdar City and Between the Bridges
regions.note: Smaller residential pockets with very thin local tutoring supply for a specific syllabus code. A family here asking for a 4MA1 Higher specialist rather than a generic maths tutor will usually be offered the generic one locally, which is the substitution an online match avoids.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, two hours inland, and the part of the emirate where in-home rates for a named-specification specialist are least competitive simply because the pool is small. Online delivery removes the premium entirely rather than discounting it.

schoolClusters.city: The island British-curriculum schools
schoolClusters.note: Students we support attend long-established British-curriculum schools on and around Abu Dhabi island, where Higher tier entry is the default and the tutoring request is usually about the top grades rather than a pass. Fee levels here also set family expectations about what an hour of tutoring should cost.

schoolClusters.city: The Khalifa City, Al Raha and mainland corridor
schoolClusters.note: Students we support also attend the mainland corridor schools serving the villa communities east of the island. Cohorts here are large and mixed-tier, so the tier decision is a live conversation in Year 10 and the cost of getting it wrong is a year of mispitched teaching.

schoolClusters.note: A smaller, more widely spread cohort where local supply of a named-specification maths specialist is genuinely limited. Families here are the most likely to be quoted a travel premium or told nobody is available, which is the market condition online delivery exists to answer.

sections.heading: What the Abu Dhabi market charges for 4MA1 support
paragraphs: Below is the rate structure in AED, with each band attributed to the provider or survey that published it as of October 2026. These are market figures, not an IB Gram price list, and they are published here because the cluster this page competes in is almost entirely silent on money. Our own model is a free trial lesson first and a quote after the diagnostic, for the reason set out above: the same syllabus code hides a steady two-year job and a ten-week rescue, and those do not cost the same.

Read the table with two questions in mind. First, what is inside the hour. A rate that covers live contact only is not comparable with one that covers marking a two-hour paper against the published scheme, which is real labour and routinely an hour of it. Second, what the exit looks like. Monthly packages in this market have been published at around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, and a package is harder to leave mid-term than a weekly slot.

The third thing to notice is the shape of the in-home premium. The published in-home band sits roughly AED 30 to AED 200 an hour above the equivalent online band, and that gap is not extra teaching. It is a car crossing Abu Dhabi in evening traffic, priced into your hour. For a family in Al Reem Island that premium is small; for one in Al Shamkha or Al Ain it is the largest single component of the bill. Whether that is worth paying is a judgement, but it should at least be a visible one.

sections.heading: The six things that actually change the number
paragraphs: Tier comes first. A Foundation tier candidate needs fewer, shorter, more repetitive sessions and almost no past-paper marking, because the content ceiling is lower and the question styles are narrower. A Higher tier candidate aiming at the top grades needs full papers marked and a diagnostic ranking, which is labour outside the lesson. Two candidates at the same school in the same year group can therefore sit at opposite ends of the market band without either being overcharged.

Proximity to the series comes second. Twelve weeks out, a tutor can plan a syllabus order and work calmly through it. Four weeks out the job becomes triage, which is harder, denser and usually delivered in longer sessions. Demand also peaks in the eight weeks before each window, which tightens availability for the specialists rather than the generalists. Booking in September for a May series costs the same per hour as booking in March and buys a materially better match.

The remaining four are session length, whether marking is billed, seniority, and format. Ninety-minute sessions cost less per usable minute than sixty, because the first ten minutes of any session are spent re-entering the problem. Marking a two-hour paper to the published scheme is roughly an hour of work and some providers absorb it while others bill it. Seniority is worth paying for in an exam year and often not in Year 10. And a small group at two to four students lowers the cost per family while removing the thing a one-to-one hour is for.

sections.heading: 4MA1 structure: two papers, one calculator, no coursework
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A is assessed by two written papers. Each runs two hours, carries one hundred marks and is worth half the qualification, a calculator is permitted in both, and there is no coursework or controlled assessment. That last point matters for cost planning: unlike a creative or practical subject, nothing accumulates across the two years that cannot be fixed in a concentrated block, which is why rescue tutoring works better in maths than in art.

Because both papers allow a calculator, the examiner is not testing arithmetic. Method marks are available for substitution, for a stated formula, for a correct chain of reasoning and for a sketch, and they are lost by candidates who write a single rounded answer from the calculator display with no working. A candidate who shows the substitution before pressing anything can score most of a question they ultimately get wrong, and this is the cheapest technique change available in the whole qualification.

The content spreads across six areas: numbers and the number system; equations, formulae and identities; sequences, functions and graphs; geometry and trigonometry; vectors and transformation geometry; and statistics and probability. Higher tier adds the heavier algebra, calculus, function notation, vector proof and histogram work. Confirm the paper structure and the content list against the current specification on qualifications.pearson.com for your child's cohort, and confirm with the maths department that the entry is 4MA1 rather than the Mathematics B specification, because the past papers are not interchangeable.

sections.heading: Foundation or Higher: the decision that costs or saves the most
paragraphs: No hourly discount matters as much as this choice. Pearson tiers 4MA1, and the two tiers sit different papers with different ceilings. A candidate entered at Foundation who was capable of Higher loses access to the upper grades, which can close a post-16 door that no amount of later tutoring reopens. A candidate entered at Higher who is not ready spends a year meeting questions pitched above them, loses confidence, and often ends up with a lower grade than the Foundation route would have produced.

The decision belongs to the school, and it is made on internal evidence. What a tutor can contribute is better evidence: a timed Foundation paper and a timed Higher paper, both marked to the published scheme, with the raw marks and the pattern of losses written down. That is a far stronger thing to take to a Year 10 parents' evening than a feeling. It also costs two sessions rather than a term, which is why we sell it as a bounded consultation rather than as a reason to start weekly tutoring.

The decision has a cost consequence afterwards too. A Higher tier candidate aiming at the top grades generates genuine marking labour across Year 11 and will sit nearer the specialist end of the market band. A Foundation candidate generally does not. Families who model this honestly in Year 10 often find that the cheaper total plan is a term of intensive work now to make Higher viable, rather than two years of steady tutoring inside a Foundation ceiling they never wanted.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in the context of what Abu Dhabi families already pay
paragraphs: A tutoring quote lands differently depending on what else is on the bill, and this is context the fees cluster never provides. Private school fees in this emirate are approved and overseen by the regulator rather than set freely, and the surrounding market has been stable: in Dubai, the regulator confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under an economic incentives package. Abu Dhabi fee decisions sit with ADEK rather than with Dubai's authority, so check your own school's published schedule rather than assuming the same.

Against a school fee, tutoring is a small and highly variable line. One session a week at the qualified-tutor band is roughly the published AED 600 to 1,200 a month. Two sessions a week in an exam year at the specialist band reaches the published AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more a month. A short paper-marking block of six sessions is a one-off cost rather than a standing one. And a private candidate entering an exam outside a school pays Pearson entry fees through a centre, which is a separate cost nobody includes in a tutoring comparison.

The planning point is that the total is controlled by duration, not by rate. A family paying the lower band for eighteen months spends more than a family paying the higher band for ten weeks. Most of the overspending we see in this emirate comes from starting late and then buying intensity, which is the most expensive combination available. Starting earlier at a lower intensity is both cheaper and, on the evidence of how 4MA1 marks are actually lost, more effective.

sections.heading: What you are actually buying in a 4MA1 hour
paragraphs: The honest breakdown of a specialist hour in an exam year is roughly this. Before the session, a timed paper has been marked question by question against the published mark scheme, and the losses have been sorted into careless, method and content. That is forty to sixty minutes of work on a two-hour paper. During the session, the content losses are taught, the method losses are drilled, and the careless losses are addressed as technique rather than as teaching. After it, the topic ranking is rewritten and the next paper is chosen to test what was just fixed.

That sequence is why two providers quoting the same number can be selling very different things. A rate covering live contact only, with homework self-marked at home, is a legitimate product at a lower price. A rate covering the marking and the diagnostic is a different product. Neither is dishonest; quoting the first and describing the second is. Ask any provider in this market a direct question: is the time spent marking my child's paper inside the hour I am paying for, or additional.

There is a second thing inside the hour that families rarely ask about, which is the written record. A session that produces a dated topic ranking, a marked paper your child can re-read and a short note on what to do next is checkable. A session that produces a verbal summary is not. Over a term, the difference is whether a parent can tell that the money moved something, or whether they are reliant on everybody feeling positive about it in April.

sections.heading: Online against in-home for 4MA1, priced honestly
paragraphs: An in-home maths tutor has real advantages and this page is not going to pretend otherwise. A tutor in the room can see a candidate's working upside down on the page, catch the moment attention goes, and keep a reluctant fifteen-year-old at the table. Those are worth something. IB Gram does not sell home visits in Abu Dhabi, so the table below compares what the local market offers against what we actually deliver, and a family is entitled to weigh it in either direction.

What online buys for a named-specification subject is the match. A 4MA1 Higher specialist who has marked those papers is a different proposition from a competent general maths tutor who will drive to Al Reef on a Tuesday, and in most of this emirate you cannot have both. Removing geography from the match also removes the travel premium from the rate, which for outlying communities is the largest single saving available. Maths is also the subject where screen sharing genuinely loses nothing: a shared whiteboard and a document camera reproduce the page.

The practical mechanics are straightforward. The candidate works on paper, photographs it or writes on a shared tablet canvas, and the tutor annotates live. Timed papers are sat on paper under real conditions and uploaded for marking. Nothing in that loop requires anybody to be in the same room, and it produces a saved record that an in-home arrangement does not. The honest exception is the candidate whose problem is attention rather than mathematics, and for those families we say so rather than selling a slot that will not be used.

sections.heading: Permits, invoices and the questions to ask before you pay
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and permitted, and it is also licensed. The private tuition work permit arrived with Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. The eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page for it lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website or e-services system.

Two consequences for a family comparing quotes. A tutor who tells you no permit exists, or that one is optional, is either uninformed or hoping you are. And because individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no fine schedule published, any specific amount quoted at you as a scare tactic is unverifiable. Ask instead whether the person teaching your child holds the permit, and treat an evasive answer as the answer.

On invoicing, keep the questions narrow and factual. Ask what the hourly figure covers, whether marking is inside it, what notice ends the arrangement, and what the quoted figure includes or excludes in tax terms for that provider. Nothing on this page states the tax treatment of tuition fees in the UAE, because that is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority and not for a tutoring website to assert. Ask the provider directly and get the answer in writing on the invoice rather than in a chat message.

sections.heading: The free trial, the diagnostic and the quote
paragraphs: Here is the sequence, with the conditions stated rather than buried. You tell us the school, the year group, the tier if one has been set, and the series your child is working towards. The candidate sits one timed past paper at home, on paper, under real conditions. We mark it against the published mark scheme before the trial lesson, which means the free hour is spent on the results of the diagnostic rather than on gathering it. The trial is one lesson per family and is booked without card details.

After the trial you receive a topic ranking by marks dropped, a recommended mode, and a quote. Sometimes the recommendation is nothing: a Year 10 candidate on track at the right tier with a competent department does not need paid tutoring, and saying so costs us an hour and keeps a family's trust for the two years when they might. We would rather lose a sale in October than be the reason a family stops believing anything a tutoring website tells them.

If no 4MA1 specialist has a slot in the window you need, you hear that at enquiry. Demand concentrates in the eight weeks before each Pearson series, so a May-series enquiry made in March competes with everybody else's. Where a UAE-based specialist is not available, the match may be a specialist teaching into Gulf Standard Time from elsewhere, and that is disclosed before booking rather than after. None of the competitor pages researched for this cluster discloses a coverage limit at all.

process.title: Send the school, the year and the tier
process.description: Those three facts decide almost everything about the plan and the price. If the tier has not been set yet, say so, because that becomes the first piece of work rather than something to assume. Confirm the entry is 4MA1 and not the Mathematics B specification.

process.title: Sit one timed paper before anything is paid for
process.description: A full past paper at home, on paper, to time, with no help. We mark it against the published mark scheme and sort the losses into careless, method and content. The free hour is then spent on the diagnosis rather than on producing it.

process.title: Take the trial lesson and the written ranking
process.description: One lesson per family, booked without card details. You leave with a topic ranking by marks dropped and an honest recommendation, which is sometimes that no paid tutoring is needed. A quote follows the diagnosis rather than preceding it.

process.title: Choose the mode, not just the rate
process.description: Weekly through the course, a paper-marking block before a series, or a bounded tier consultation. The mode sets the total cost far more than the hourly figure does, and the cheapest total is almost always the earliest start at the lowest intensity.

process.title: Work from the ranking and re-rank every cycle
process.description: Each cycle is a timed paper, marking, a session on the real losses, and a rewritten ranking. The next paper is chosen to test what was just fixed, which is how you find out whether the money moved anything rather than hoping it did.

process.title: Stop when the ranking stops moving
process.description: When the top of the ranking is stable and the losses are careless rather than content, the sessions have done their job. We say so. A provider who never reaches that conclusion is selling a subscription rather than a diagnosis.

whyPoints.title: The AED numbers are on the page, with sources
whyPoints.description: Market rates are published here with the provider or survey that quoted them and the date they were read. Three of six researched competitor pages print no price at all. A family that can see the market can argue with any quote, including ours.

whyPoints.title: The quote follows a marked paper
whyPoints.description: A rate quoted before anyone has seen your child's work is a guess dressed as a price. We mark a timed paper first, then quote against the actual job, which sometimes produces a smaller number than a family expected and occasionally none at all.

whyPoints.title: No travel is priced into the hour
whyPoints.description: Delivery is online one-to-one, so nobody is crossing the emirate in evening traffic on your money. For families in Al Reef, Al Shamkha and Al Ain that removes the single largest premium in the local market rather than discounting it.

whyPoints.title: Marking is stated, inside or outside
whyPoints.description: Marking a two-hour 4MA1 paper to the published scheme is about an hour of labour. We say whether it sits inside the quoted hour before you book, and we recommend asking every other provider in this market the same question in writing.

whyPoints.title: The tier decision is treated as a money decision
whyPoints.description: Foundation or Higher moves a family between market bands and decides which post-16 routes stay open. We support it with two timed papers marked to the scheme, as evidence for the school, rather than with an opinion offered for free.

whyPoints.title: Availability limits are disclosed at enquiry
whyPoints.description: Demand concentrates in the eight weeks before each Pearson series. If no 4MA1 specialist is free in your window you hear it immediately, and if the match teaches into Gulf Standard Time from outside the UAE you hear that before booking.

faqs.question: What does an Edexcel IGCSE Maths A 4MA1 tutor cost per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Market rates in the UAE run roughly AED 45 to 150 for a budget online tutor, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel inside the rate, and AED 200 to 450 or more for a declared IGCSE specialist. One premium provider publishes AED 650. Those are other providers' own published figures as of October 2026, not ours. We quote after a timed paper has been marked, because the same syllabus code covers a steady two-year job and a ten-week rescue and those do not cost the same.

faqs.question: Is the marking of past papers included in the hourly rate or charged separately?
faqs.answer: That depends entirely on the provider, and it is the most useful question a family in this market can ask. Marking a two-hour 4MA1 paper against the published mark scheme, sorting the losses into careless, method and content, is roughly forty to sixty minutes of work. Some providers absorb it and price the hour higher; others bill live contact only and expect the paper to be self-marked at home. Both are legitimate products at different prices. Ask for the answer in writing, because a rate quoted without that detail is not comparable with one quoted with it.

faqs.question: How many 4MA1 sessions does a Year 11 candidate in Abu Dhabi usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends far more on when you start than on the child. A candidate starting in September of Year 11 at one session a week is working through a planned order and typically needs that single weekly hour. A candidate starting eight weeks before the series needs a denser block built around timed papers, which is more total labour in less time and costs more per week. We size it after marking one timed paper and we re-size it every cycle, stopping when the topic ranking stops moving rather than running sessions to a predetermined number.

faqs.question: Should my child be entered for 4MA1 at Foundation or at Higher tier?
faqs.answer: That is the school's decision and it should be made on marked evidence rather than on impressions. Foundation tops out below the top of the grade scale while Higher reaches it, so a wrongly cautious entry can close post-16 routes that later tutoring cannot reopen, and a wrongly ambitious one wastes a year on questions pitched above the candidate. What a tutor can usefully add is a timed Foundation paper and a timed Higher paper, both marked to the published scheme, with the raw marks written down for the maths department. That is two sessions, not a term.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home maths tutor in Abu Dhabi more expensive than an online one?
faqs.answer: Because the drive is inside the rate. The published in-home band in this market sits roughly AED 30 to 200 an hour above the equivalent online band, and that gap is travel time rather than additional teaching. In-home arrangements also commonly carry a two-hour minimum so the journey is worth making, which doubles the smallest purchase available. For a family in Al Reem Island the premium is modest; for one in Al Shamkha or Al Ain it is the largest single component of the bill, which is the saving online delivery actually represents.

faqs.question: Do 4MA1 tutoring rates rise closer to the exam series?
faqs.answer: The published hourly bands do not move much, but the practical cost of starting late does. Demand concentrates in the eight weeks before each Pearson window, so the specialists fill first and a late enquiry competes for a smaller pool. Late starts also force a denser mode: triage built around timed papers rather than a planned syllabus order, delivered in longer sessions. The result is a higher weekly spend for fewer weeks, which usually totals more than an earlier, calmer start would have. Book for a May series in the autumn rather than in March.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover 4MA1 and Further Pure Maths 4PM1 for the same student?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and where a candidate is sitting both it is usually the better arrangement, because the two qualifications share algebraic machinery and a single tutor can stop the two folders blurring at deadline time. The practical constraint is that 4PM1 is a narrower specialism than 4MA1, so the pool of tutors genuinely comfortable with both is smaller. Ask at enquiry rather than assuming. If no single match exists we will say so and propose two tutors with a shared plan rather than stretching one across both.

faqs.question: Is a calculator allowed in both 4MA1 papers, and does that change how we revise?
faqs.answer: A calculator is permitted in both papers, and it changes revision considerably. The examiner is not testing arithmetic, so the marks sit in method: a stated formula, a visible substitution, a chain of reasoning, a sketch. Candidates lose marks by rounding mid-calculation and by writing a single display value with no working, which forfeits method marks on questions they nearly had. Revision should therefore include an audit of the candidate's own calculator model, its statistical and fraction functions, and the habit of writing the substitution before pressing anything.

faqs.question: Which Pearson exam series do Abu Dhabi schools enter for International GCSE maths?
faqs.answer: Pearson makes International GCSE exams available in May/June and November each year, so there is a genuine second window rather than a twelve-month wait after a disappointing result. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Whether your centre will enter a candidate in November is a school decision, so ask the maths department before planning around it, and use the live official timetable.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest way to support a 4MA1 candidate over two years?
faqs.answer: Start in Year 9 or early Year 10 at a low intensity. Most 4MA1 marks are decided by whether fractions, indices, rearranging and basic manipulation are automatic before the course begins, and an hour a fortnight at that stage costs a fraction of a Year 11 rescue block. The most expensive pattern in this market is the opposite: start late, then buy intensity. A family paying the specialist band for ten weeks of triage often spends more than one that paid the qualified-tutor band calmly for eighteen months.

faqs.question: Does a 4MA1 tutor working with Abu Dhabi families need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged fifteen to eighteen. The ministry's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so distrust any specific amount quoted at you. Verify on mohre.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Can we hire my child's own maths teacher from school for private sessions?
faqs.answer: That is the arrangement to avoid in this emirate. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the work permit's code of conduct is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it. The practical reading: a teacher who offers you that arrangement is telling you something about their judgement, and the risk falls on them and on the school.

faqs.question: Does your quoted figure include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask for that in writing on the invoice from any provider, including us, and keep the question narrow. Nothing on this page states the tax treatment of tuition fees in the UAE, because that is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority rather than something a tutoring website should assert. What a family can reasonably require is a clear statement of what the quoted figure includes, shown on the invoice rather than agreed in a chat message. A provider who cannot put that in writing has told you something useful about their bookkeeping.

faqs.question: What happens to our money if the 4MA1 match turns out to be wrong?
faqs.answer: Ask every provider this before paying anything, because the real cost of a bad match is the term it wastes rather than the hours it bills. Our arrangement is weekly rather than packaged, so a family can stop. We also replace a match on request after two sessions without requiring a reason, because a candidate who has decided they dislike the tutor will not work for them regardless of who is right. What we do not offer is any refund tied to a grade outcome, and nor should anybody else.

faqs.question: Is a small group class cheaper than one-to-one for 4MA1 in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Per family, yes, and tuition centres in this market price group classes per term rather than per hour, which makes direct comparison awkward. Ask for the per-hour equivalent before deciding. The trade-off is that the thing you are buying in a one-to-one 4MA1 hour is diagnosis: a paper marked against your child's specific pattern of losses and a session built from that pattern. In a group of four, that pattern is averaged. Groups work well for content coverage in Year 10 and poorly for exam-year triage.

faqs.question: We are in Al Ain - does that change the price of a 4MA1 tutor?
faqs.answer: With online delivery, no. The rate from Al Ain is the rate from Al Bateen, because no one is driving. In the local in-home market it changes a great deal: Al Ain sits roughly two hours inland, the pool of tutors familiar with a specific Pearson specification code is small, and families there are the most likely to be quoted a travel surcharge or told that nobody is available for that subject at all. That gap, rather than any discount, is what online one-to-one delivery actually removes for the western part of the emirate.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-maths-a-4ma1-tut.closingHeading: Get the paper marked, then talk about money
abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-maths-a-4ma1-tut.closingBody: Send the school, the year group and the tier if one has been set, and have your child sit one full past paper at home under timed conditions. We mark it against the published mark scheme before the free trial lesson, so the hour is spent on what the paper showed rather than on gathering it. You leave with a topic ranking by marks dropped, a recommended mode and a quote built against the actual job. The trial is one lesson per family, booked without card details, and if the honest answer is that no paid tutoring is needed yet, that is what you will hear.

intro.heading: Pearson Edexcel is not Cambridge with a different logo
paragraphs: The most common mistake made when hiring for International GCSE in Abu Dhabi is treating the board as a detail. It is not. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports grades on a 9 to 1 scale while Cambridge reports A* to G. Pearson tiers Mathematics A into Foundation and Higher, where Foundation reaches grade 5 at most and Higher runs from 9 down to 4 with an allowed 3 beneath it. Pearson permits a calculator in both of its maths papers; Cambridge sets one paper without one. Pearson International GCSE sciences carry no separate practical paper at all, assessing practical understanding inside the written papers instead. Four differences, each of which changes how a student should revise.

Abu Dhabi makes this harder than it needs to be, because board usage is mixed inside individual schools. A single British-curriculum school in this emirate may enter Pearson for mathematics and Cambridge for the three sciences, or the reverse, and the prospectus will say only that it follows the British curriculum. The only reliable source is the exams officer, subject by subject, and the statement of entry when it arrives. A tutor working from the wrong board teaches the right content in the wrong question style, and the mismatch usually surfaces at the mocks.

The second thing an Edexcel family needs to plan around is that Pearson runs two series a year. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May and June and again in November. That changes the shape of a two-year course meaningfully: a subject can be sat early, a weak grade can be resat in January rather than waiting a full year, and a private candidate has two entry points instead of one. It also means the revision calendar has two peaks, and families who plan only for the summer lose half of the flexibility they paid for.

Dates matter here and we publish only the ones Pearson has actually published. The final timetable for the November 2026 series runs to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also issues provisional timetables well ahead of each series, including for International GCSE in November 2027, and those can be revised, so any session table should send you to the live official timetable rather than restate dates that may change. The link to check is Pearson's own exam timetables page.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not make home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. For a Pearson candidate that is a practical gain rather than a concession, because the pool of tutors who have taught 4PM1 Further Pure Mathematics or 4CP0 Computer Science at Higher tier is small in any one city and reachable from anywhere once the drive is removed.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Four stages where Abu Dhabi families ask for Pearson support, with what each one assesses and what the two-series year means for planning it. The board changes more at each stage than parents expect, so each note is specific to Pearson rather than general.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Typically eight to ten subjects, each with a Pearson code beginning with a 4, graded 9 to 1. Mathematics A is tiered Foundation or Higher; most other subjects are single tier. The sciences are two written papers with practical understanding assessed inside them, which removes a separate practical component and raises the weight of experimental questions in the theory papers.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools entering Pearson usually use the summer series, with November available for resits, early entry and single subjects. The Ministry of Education equivalency route for British-curriculum students counts five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, which on the Pearson 9 to 1 scale means grade 3 is the number that matters.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The post-16 continuation, structured in units that can be sat across more than one series. Students arriving from 4MA1 Higher find the step manageable; those arriving from Foundation tier meet a gap, because Foundation never covered the algebra the A Level course begins from. That gap is visible in the first unit and is much cheaper to close in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: For a UAE university place, equivalency on the British track asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside the five International GCSE passes. Confirm the current wording on the ministry's own site; IB Gram performs no part of that process.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 and the years before the course
programmes.description: Pearson does not examine these years, so schools assess internally and the tier decision for 4MA1 is formed from that internal data. Work in Year 9 therefore has a direct consequence: it determines whether a student is put forward for Foundation or Higher, and Foundation caps the grade at 5 whatever happens afterwards.
programmes.countryNote: This is where an Abu Dhabi family has the most leverage and uses it least. A short block of work in Year 9 on algebra, proportion and graph interpretation changes the tier conversation in Year 10, and in July nobody in this emirate is competing for tutoring slots.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Several Abu Dhabi schools run International GCSE to Year 11 and then switch to the IB Diploma, which replaces unitised papers with six subjects at Higher or Standard Level plus an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and an Internal Assessment in each subject. The written-argument load and the coursework deadlines are new, and the student writes every word themselves.
programmes.countryNote: A student moving from 4MA1 Higher into Diploma mathematics at Higher Level should be diagnosed in Year 11 rather than in DP1. From Foundation tier the move to Higher Level mathematics is not realistic without a substantial bridging block, and saying so early is kinder than discovering it in October.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Each entry names the Pearson code, the tiering position and the component where Abu Dhabi students most often lose marks. Codes beginning with 4 are International GCSE; check them against the statement of entry rather than assuming from the subject name.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.description: Two papers, calculator permitted in both, which changes revision substantially compared with a board that sets a non-calculator paper. Foundation reaches grade 5; Higher runs 9 to 4 with an allowed 3. Most lost marks are method marks in multi-step questions where the working was compressed into a single line.

subjects.name: Further Pure Mathematics (4PM1)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 4MA1 Higher by students heading to A Level mathematics, covering calculus, series, logarithms and coordinate geometry the main course never reaches. The scarcest specialism on this list in Abu Dhabi, which is precisely why removing the drive from the hiring decision matters most here.

subjects.name: Physics (4PH1)
subjects.description: Two written papers with practical understanding examined inside them rather than in a separate practical component. That raises the weight of experimental questions in the theory papers, so method, variables and graph interpretation have to be revised as physics rather than as a separate practical topic.

subjects.name: Chemistry (4CH1)
subjects.description: Calculation-heavy, with moles, titration arithmetic and yield questions carrying marks that are lost to presentation as often as to understanding. Students who do not set out units and intermediate values lose method marks on questions they have effectively answered correctly.

subjects.name: Biology (4BI1)
subjects.description: High content load with extended-response marks that depend on command words. Experimental questions about unfamiliar investigations appear inside the written papers, and students who revise only the content tend to meet those questions for the first time in the hall.

subjects.name: Science Double Award (4SC0)
subjects.description: Two grades from a combined course across the three sciences in less depth than the separate codes. A sensible choice for a broad subject spread and a poor one for a student heading to A Level or Higher Level science, because the depth those courses assume sits in the separate syllabuses.

subjects.name: English Language A (4EA1)
subjects.description: Non-fiction reading and transactional writing on the main paper, with a second assessed route the school selects. Marks are lost to structure and to answering a slightly different question rather than to vocabulary. A short planning routine that survives time pressure is most of the remedy.

subjects.name: English Literature (4ET1)
subjects.description: Extended responses judged against levels descriptors, where evidence has to be used rather than mentioned. Marking two of a student's own responses side by side against the published descriptors makes the difference visible far faster than any amount of general advice about essay technique.

subjects.name: Economics (4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and data response decide the grade. An unlabelled axis or an unmarked new equilibrium scores nothing however sound the paragraph beneath it, so exam practice here is largely drawing practice done to the standard the mark scheme expects.

subjects.name: Business (4BS1)
subjects.description: Application to the given context carries the marks. Students write accurate general paragraphs that never touch the case material and lose the application and evaluation marks. Highlighting the unused lines on a student's own script changes the habit within a few sessions.

subjects.name: Geography (4GE1) and History (4HI1)
subjects.description: Source and case-study work with extended responses marked in levels. Abu Dhabi students frequently have strong knowledge and weak question discipline in these subjects, which is a structural fix rather than a content one and therefore faster to achieve than parents expect.

subjects.name: Computer Science (4CP0) and ICT (4IT1)
subjects.description: Written components ask for algorithms, pseudocode and trace tables in a particular form, and practical ICT work is lost to specification detail rather than capability. Students who code fluently in class still need to practise writing pseudocode by hand under time.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-online-tutor.regionsIntro: Board usage varies by school rather than by neighbourhood, so these notes cover what a Pearson family in each part of the emirate runs into practically: when a session can start, and which entry pattern the local schools tend to use.

regions.name: Al Mushrif
regions.note: Central island, short school runs, early finishes. Weekday afternoon sessions are realistic here, which makes it the easiest area to secure a Pearson specialist during the November series when demand concentrates on evenings.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: Dense cluster of international schools with mixed board usage inside single institutions. Families here most often need the subject-by-subject board check, because siblings at the same school can sit different boards for maths.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Schools on the island and short walks home, so a four-thirty start works. Useful during a November entry, when the final weeks of October demand slots that most families cannot otherwise offer until six.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Long bus runs push sessions past five-thirty. The two-series year helps here: an early entry in November frees the summer timetable, which is worth more in this area than in the shorter-commute communities.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Established school corridor with heavy after-school activity schedules. Competition is for the hour rather than the tutor, so Pearson families here tend to fix a weekend morning slot for the full two-year course.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: One bridge in and out, which prices any travelling arrangement heavily. Online scheduling returns that time, and in a November entry year those forty minutes a week are the difference between four and six timed papers.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Al Shamkha
regions.note: Mainland communities a long way from the island, where travelling rates sit at the top of the market band. Pearson resit candidates here benefit most from scheduling that ignores distance entirely.

regions.name: Al Reef and Masdar City
regions.note: Outlying residential pockets with late returns from long bus routes. Later weekday slots and weekend mornings carry most of the work, which also suits the January results window after a November entry.

schoolClusters.note: The emirate's longest-established British-curriculum provision, where Pearson and Cambridge entries frequently sit side by side within one school. The exams officer, not the prospectus, is the source of truth. Students we support attend schools across this area.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Al Reef
schoolClusters.note: Newer capacity with long bus routes and a wide spread of board usage. Several schools in this corridor enter Pearson for mathematics while using another board for sciences, which is exactly the split that catches families out at the mocks.

sections.heading: Find out which board the school entered, subject by subject
paragraphs: This is the first question and most families never ask it. A British-curriculum school in Abu Dhabi is not obliged to use one board across its whole subject list, and many do not. Mathematics with Pearson and the sciences with Cambridge is a common pattern; so is the reverse, and so is a change between one cohort and the next when a head of department moves. The prospectus will say the school follows the British curriculum, which tells you nothing about which papers your child will sit.

The consequences are concrete. A Cambridge maths candidate sits a paper with no calculator; a Pearson 4MA1 candidate may use one in both papers. A Cambridge science candidate sits a practical test or a written alternative worth around a fifth of the grade; a Pearson science candidate has practical understanding examined inside the two written papers and no separate component. A Cambridge grade is a letter; a Pearson International GCSE grade is a number from 9 to 1. A tutor working from the wrong assumption on any of those will teach competently and prepare for the wrong examination.

Getting the answer takes one email. Ask the exams officer for the board and the code for every examined subject, and the tier where one applies. When the statement of entry arrives, check it against what you were told, because late changes happen. Keep the list somewhere you can find it, because every subsequent decision, from which past papers to use to which timetable to read, depends on it. sections.heading: Foundation or Higher in 4MA1, and what the tier actually caps
paragraphs: Pearson Mathematics A is tiered, and the tier sets a ceiling before any revision happens. A Foundation entry is examined on a reduced content range and reaches grade 5 at most. A Higher entry covers the full range and reports 9 down to 4, with an allowed grade 3 beneath it for a candidate who falls short. Those are different papers with different question styles, not an easier and a harder version of the same examination, and a student entered at Foundation cannot reach a grade 6 however well they perform.

The decision is made at school from internal assessment data, usually during Year 10, and confirmed when entries are submitted. Schools are managing risk when they make it: a borderline student entered at Higher who falls below the allowed grade 3 walks away with nothing, which is a worse outcome than a secure Foundation 5. That is a reasonable institutional instinct and it is occasionally wrong for an individual child, particularly one who had a difficult Year 9 and has since caught up.

What changes a provisional Foundation entry is evidence, and the evidence has to be the right shape. A parent's view that their daughter is capable of more does not move a department. One full Higher-tier past paper, sat under real time conditions and marked against the published scheme, does, because it answers the question the school is actually asking. Produce that in the autumn term and the conversation is possible. Produce it in February and the entry has already gone.

sections.heading: The Pearson year, using only the dates Pearson has published
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May and June and again in November, which gives an Abu Dhabi family two usable peaks in the year rather than one. The published final timetable for the November 2026 series runs to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are Pearson's own figures and they are the ones worth planning around.

Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, including for International GCSE in November 2027, and states clearly that provisional dates can be revised. The practical rule that follows is one almost no competing page observes: a session plan should link the live official timetable on the Pearson qualifications site rather than reproduce dates that may change. A restated date on a web page is out of date the moment the board revises it, and a candidate who revises against it has a real problem rather than an inconvenience.

Counting backwards from a series is how the year becomes legible. Entries close months before the first paper, on an internal school deadline that precedes Pearson's. Mocks sit a few months out and are the first external-looking evidence anybody has. Six to ten weeks out is when a diagnosed component can still be fixed. The final fortnight is for pacing and nothing else. A family that knows which of those windows it is in makes different and better decisions than one working from the exam date alone.

sections.heading: What a Pearson paper rewards, and where that differs in practice
paragraphs: Two boards examining the same physics content still reward slightly different behaviour, and a student who has practised one style meets the other as a surprise. Pearson International GCSE science papers examine practical understanding inside the written components, which means experimental questions arrive mixed into theory questions rather than grouped in a paper of their own. A candidate who has revised the content thoroughly and never practised a question about an unfamiliar investigation loses marks that look like carelessness and are actually unpreparedness.

In 4MA1 the calculator changes the character of revision. With a calculator permitted in both papers, arithmetic fluency matters less and setting out matters more, because the questions that carry weight are multi-step and the marks sit in identifiable steps. The expensive habit is doing two operations at once and writing one line. That is worth saying plainly to a student: on this board the calculator does the arithmetic and your job is to make the reasoning visible, which is the opposite of what students assume a calculator paper means.

In the written subjects, Pearson's levels descriptors reward sustained engagement with the specific question and the specific material. Students who have been taught to write everything they know about a topic score in the middle band repeatedly, however much they know. Reading a student's own response beside the published descriptors, and marking where the band boundary actually sits, is the intervention that moves these subjects, and it works much faster than general advice about essay structure because it is specific to their writing.

sections.heading: Where 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 marks actually go missing
paragraphs: The science codes produce recognisable, repeatable losses, and a single marked paper is usually enough to identify which the student has. In 4CH1 the largest recoverable category is calculation presentation: moles, titration arithmetic and yield questions where the answer is right, the units are missing and the intermediate value was never written down. Those are method marks, they are worth several per paper, and they are recovered by habit rather than by teaching.

In 4PH1 the pattern is formula before understanding. A student recognises a question as a current question, selects the right equation and applies it to the wrong part of the circuit. The diagnostic is easy: ask the student to describe what is happening in words before touching an equation. Those who cannot have a reasoning gap that no amount of formula practice will close, and those who can were simply rushing, which is a different and much shorter fix.

In 4BI1 the content volume means losses spread thinly across the whole paper, which disguises them. The underlying cause is almost always command words: describe answered as explain, explain answered with a restatement of the data, and extended responses that list rather than develop. Sorting a student's own lost marks by command word, rather than by topic, is the hour of diagnosis that changes the next two months in this subject. Parents often find this counter-intuitive, because the student's biology knowledge is usually sound and the report says revision is the problem. A script showing eleven marks lost to one misread command word across a single paper settles that argument quickly, and it points at a fix that takes weeks rather than terms.

sections.heading: The two-session year: early entry, resits and private candidates
paragraphs: Having two series a year is Pearson's most practically useful feature and the one Abu Dhabi families exploit least. A student secure in one subject by the end of Year 10 can sit it in November of Year 11 and remove it from the summer timetable, which is worth more than a grade improvement in that subject because it frees attention across everything else. The decision has to be made with the school, which controls the entry, and it has to be made on evidence rather than optimism: a timed paper at the standard, in the autumn, not a feeling about confidence.

The second use is a resit. A grade that arrives in August can be re-sat in the November series, with results reaching students in the following January window, as the November 2025 results did on 22 January 2026. Whether that is worth doing depends on the mark breakdown rather than the grade. A candidate two marks below a boundary with one weak component has a strong case. A candidate thirty marks below across every component is being asked to repeat a year's learning in ten weeks, and an honest adviser says so.

The third situation is a private candidate: a student whose school does not offer a subject, or who is educated outside a school entering for them. That requires an examination centre willing to accept private candidates, and the entry deadlines and fees are the centre's business rather than a tutor's. We can teach the syllabus and tell you what the papers require. We cannot enter a candidate, and any provider implying they can arrange an entry on your behalf should be asked, in writing, exactly which centre.

sections.heading: What online Pearson tuition costs in Abu Dhabi, and when the price moves
paragraphs: Market rates for online one-to-one International GCSE tuition in this emirate run roughly from AED 45 an hour at the budget end up to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor, with exam-year specialists quoted from AED 200 to 450 and premium or examiner-marketed tutors advertised considerably higher. Travelling in-home tuition is quoted around AED 180 to 500 an hour, with the journey inside the rate. Those are market figures from published UAE provider pages and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

What moves the number in a Pearson household specifically is the two-session calendar. Demand peaks twice: in the weeks before the November papers and again in the spring before the summer series. A specialist's weekday evening hour in late October is the scarcest commodity in this market, and rates in the top half of the band are what a family pays for arriving late to it. Booking the same hour in September, before either peak, is the single largest saving available and it requires no negotiation at all.

The other variable is scarcity of code rather than scarcity of time. 4MA1 Foundation support is widely available in this emirate. 4PM1 Further Pure Mathematics, 4CP0 Computer Science and the less common language codes are not, and a family needing one of those is choosing from a short list at any price. That is also the case where online delivery changes the outcome rather than the cost, because a short national list becomes a workable international one once the drive stops being a constraint.

sections.heading: Grades 9 to 1, grade 3, and what Ministry of Education equivalency counts
paragraphs: Pearson International GCSE reports grades from 9 down to 1, which matters beyond school reports because the Ministry of Education equivalency requirement for British-curriculum students is expressed in both scales. The published rule is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. On the Pearson scale, grade 3 is therefore the number a family should know.

Two details are regularly got wrong in this market. The first is the subject count: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count, so those five have to come from elsewhere in the subject list. The second is the count itself, which one ranking competitor publishes as six. It is five. Reading the requirement correctly is not a detail when a family is choosing Year 9 options with a UAE university in mind.

Two cautions belong with that. No IB points threshold for equivalency should be quoted to you without a source on the ministry's own site, because the published British-track numbers are documented and the IB figure is not. And equivalency is a process the authorities run, not something a tutoring company performs, arranges or guarantees. Describe it, verify it on the official channel, and treat anyone offering to secure it on your behalf with considerable suspicion.

sections.heading: Switching board, school or country mid-course
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi has a mobile population and a mid-course move is common rather than exceptional. The hardest version is a change of board inside a subject, because content maps across reasonably well and assessment does not. A student arriving from a Cambridge 0580 Extended class into a Pearson 4MA1 Higher class has met most of the mathematics and none of the paper. The fix is narrow and quick if it is identified: four to six sessions on the new paper's question styles, the calculator position and the layout the scheme rewards.

A change of school within the same board is easier but carries a tier risk. Schools set internal thresholds differently, and a student placed at Higher in one school can be placed at Foundation in another on the same data. Where that happens, the timed paper marked against the published scheme is again the document that settles it, and a new school generally welcomes evidence it did not have to generate itself.

Arriving from a different curriculum entirely, which happens frequently in this emirate, needs a proper audit rather than a catch-up block. A student coming from an American or national-curriculum background into International GCSE in Year 10 may be ahead in some subjects and two years behind in the specific skills the papers assess. Mapping that subject by subject in the first fortnight, and being honest about which subjects cannot realistically be carried, saves a family far more than any amount of general support across everything.

sections.heading: What a Pearson tutor may and may not do with assessed work
paragraphs: Some Pearson International GCSE subjects include an assessed route the school selects, and schools also set substantial internal projects regardless of board. Wherever work is submitted under the student's name, the boundary is absolute rather than negotiable. The student produces the work. A tutor teaches the skill it assesses, explains the criteria in plain language, questions a draft the student has written, marks it against those criteria and says what would score more.

What a tutor does not do is supply sentences, restructure a draft into a submission, or hand over a finished piece. The line is easy to hold in practice: a student should leave a session with a list of changes and the understanding needed to make them, and should return with a version they wrote themselves. We state this openly because the alternative is sold openly in this market, and a parent buying it is transferring all of the risk to their own child.

The same applies to materials. Pearson's specifications, past papers and mark schemes belong to Pearson, and the right conduct is to reference them and send you to the official qualifications site rather than circulating copied packs. A session built on a paper the student sits to time, marked against the official scheme and then taught from, achieves everything a bundle of photocopies pretends to and leaves nobody holding material they should not have. Unreleased material is a separate and more serious matter: anyone offering access to papers that have not been published is describing a malpractice route, and the candidate rather than the seller carries the consequence of it.

process.title: Confirm the board and the Pearson code for every subject
process.description: One email to the exams officer, asking for the board, the code and the tier where one applies. Check it against the statement of entry when it arrives. Every later decision, from which past papers to use to which timetable to read, depends on this list being right.

process.title: Decide which series you are actually planning for
process.description: Pearson runs a May and June series and a November one. Whether a subject is being taken early, sat in the summer or resat changes the whole shape of the work, and it is a school decision that has to be made on evidence rather than on confidence.

process.title: Diagnostic first session at no charge
process.description: A timed paper from the correct board, marked against the published scheme by the tutor who would take the course, with every loss categorised. You end with a baseline number and a named problem. Nothing is payable until you decide to continue.

process.title: Weekly work with a written record each time
process.description: An annotated script saved and dated, two or three lines naming what was lost and why, and one specific task before the next session. At four weeks, a short review of what the pattern shows and what the next block should target.

process.title: Re-baseline at the mocks and after any results day
process.description: Mock scripts are classified the same way as the first session. After a November results day the component mark breakdown, not the grade, decides whether a resit is worth the entry and what the summer plan should be.

whyPoints.title: Matched by Pearson code and tier
whyPoints.description: 4MA1 Foundation and 4MA1 Higher are different papers, and 4PM1 is a different subject again. Asking for the code and the tier at the start is how a match becomes specific rather than plausible, and it takes one look at the statement of entry.

whyPoints.title: The board differences are set out, not blurred
whyPoints.description: A 9 to 1 grade scale, a calculator in both maths papers, practical understanding inside the science written papers, two series a year. A tutor who does not know those four things is preparing your child for a different examination.

whyPoints.title: The two-session year used deliberately
whyPoints.description: An early entry in November on a secure subject frees attention across the summer. A resit decision is made from the component breakdown. Both are planning conversations most families never have, and both are free to have in September.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my son sits Pearson Edexcel or another board for each subject?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer directly, subject by subject, and ask for the code as well as the board. Abu Dhabi schools commonly split boards across the subject list, so mathematics may be Pearson while the sciences are not, and the prospectus will only say the school follows the British curriculum. Check what you are told against the statement of entry when it arrives, because late changes do happen. Pearson International GCSE codes begin with a 4, such as 4MA1 for Mathematics A and 4PH1 for Physics.

faqs.question: What is the highest grade available on 4MA1 Foundation tier?
faqs.answer: Grade 5. Pearson Mathematics A is tiered: Foundation is examined on a reduced content range and reaches grade 5 at most, while Higher covers the full range and reports 9 down to 4, with an allowed grade 3 beneath it. They are different papers rather than easier and harder versions of one examination. The tier is confirmed when entries are submitted and cannot be changed for that series afterwards, so the conversation about it belongs in the autumn term rather than in the spring.

faqs.question: Is it true that a calculator is allowed in both Pearson maths papers?
faqs.answer: Yes, which is one of the more practically significant differences between the boards. Cambridge sets one of its mathematics papers without a calculator; Pearson permits one throughout Mathematics A. That shifts where the marks live. Arithmetic fluency matters less and visible reasoning matters more, because the weighty questions are multi-step and the method marks sit in identifiable steps. Students often assume a calculator paper means less writing, and the opposite is true: the calculator handles the arithmetic so the reasoning has to be on the page.

faqs.question: Do Pearson International GCSE sciences have a practical exam?
faqs.answer: No separate practical component. Pearson examines practical understanding inside the two written papers, so experimental questions about unfamiliar investigations arrive mixed into theory questions rather than grouped into a paper of their own. The consequence for revision is that method, variables, graph work and sources of error have to be practised as part of ordinary physics or chemistry revision rather than saved for a separate practical topic. Candidates who revise content thoroughly and never practise an unfamiliar investigation lose marks that look like carelessness.

faqs.question: When do November Pearson results reach students?
faqs.answer: In recent years in the January window: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. For the summer series, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. The published final timetable for the November 2026 series runs to 19 November 2026. Pearson issues provisional timetables ahead of each series and states that they can be revised, so check the live official timetable on the Pearson qualifications site rather than relying on a date restated on any web page, including this one.

faqs.question: Should my daughter sit one subject early in the November series?
faqs.answer: It is worth considering if she is genuinely secure in it, because removing a subject from the summer timetable frees attention across everything else, which is usually worth more than a grade improvement in that one subject. The decision belongs to the school, which controls the entry, and it should be made from a timed paper sat at the standard in the autumn rather than from confidence. An early entry on a subject that is not secure converts one comfortable summer grade into two anxious ones.

faqs.question: Is a November resit worth the entry after an August results day?
faqs.answer: That depends on the component mark breakdown rather than on the grade. A candidate two or three marks below a boundary, with the loss concentrated in one component, has a strong case and a short piece of work ahead of them. A candidate thirty marks below across every component is being asked to repeat a year's learning in roughly ten weeks, and an honest adviser will say so rather than sell the sessions. Ask the school for the breakdown first, then decide, and confirm the entry deadline before committing to anything.

faqs.question: My son is moving from a Cambridge class into a Pearson class. How much catching up is that?
faqs.answer: Less than it sounds, and it is a paper problem rather than a content problem. He has met most of the mathematics or science already; what he has not met is the question style, the grade scale, the calculator position and the layout the Pearson scheme rewards. Four to six focused sessions on past papers from the new board usually covers it, provided somebody actually identifies it as the issue. The expensive version is spending a term on content he already knows while the paper style remains unfamiliar.

faqs.question: Can IB Gram enter my child for a Pearson paper as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: No. Entering a candidate is done through an examination centre that accepts private entries, and the deadlines and fees are that centre's business. What we can do is teach the specification and make sure the student knows exactly what the papers require. Any provider implying it can arrange an entry on your behalf should be asked, in writing, which centre and under what arrangement. Pearson publishes the specifications and timetables openly, and the centre is the only route to an entry.

faqs.question: What does grade 3 mean for Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: It is the floor on the numeric scale. The published requirement for British-curriculum students is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among those five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor publishes six subjects, which is wrong. Verify the current wording on the ministry's own site, and note that no tutoring company performs or guarantees any part of this process.

faqs.question: Which Pearson codes are hardest to find a tutor for in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: 4PM1 Further Pure Mathematics, 4CP0 Computer Science and the less common language codes. Those have short candidate lists in any single city, and in the weeks before a series they have effectively none at a specific weekday evening hour. This is where online scheduling changes the outcome rather than the price, because a short local list becomes a workable one once the drive is no longer a constraint. If nothing is free at the hour you need, you will be told with a date attached rather than kept waiting.

faqs.question: How many timed papers should a Year 11 Pearson candidate actually sit?
faqs.answer: More than most do, and under real conditions rather than at the kitchen table with the answers nearby. A reasonable pattern is one timed component a fortnight from January, rising to one a week in the final six weeks, each marked against the published scheme and classified by loss type. The value is not in the practice itself but in the comparison: the same component, the same conditions, eight weeks apart, is the only honest measure of whether anything has moved. Unfinished papers score zero on what they did not reach.

faqs.question: Does the November series clash with the Abu Dhabi school term?
faqs.answer: It sits inside it, which is the practical difficulty. The published November 2026 final timetable runs to 19 November 2026, in the middle of a normal teaching term, so a candidate is revising for papers while classes continue in every other subject. Families who plan for this reduce other commitments for those three weeks rather than adding sessions, and they shift tutoring to pacing and mark-scheme language rather than new content. Those who do not plan for it usually report the term as the hardest of the two years.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover 4MA1 and 4PH1 for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. Mathematics and physics specialists overlap more than mathematics and biology ones, and a tutor who has taught both codes at the right tier is genuinely useful because the algebra in 4PH1 is the algebra in 4MA1. What does not work is a mathematics tutor covering physics because the timetable is convenient. Ask which codes they have taught, at which tier, and how recently, and treat a vague answer as a no.

faqs.question: Do you provide copies of Pearson specifications and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: We reference them and link to them rather than sending copies. Specifications, past papers and mark schemes are Pearson's property, and circulating copied packs is a copyright matter rather than a service. Everything a family needs is published openly on the Pearson qualifications site, including the specification for each code and the live examination timetables. A session built around a paper your child sits to time, then marked against the official scheme, does everything a bundle of photocopies pretends to do.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-online-tutor.closingHeading: Confirm the board, then the series, then book
abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-online-tutor.closingBody: Two emails settle most of this. One to the exams officer asking for the board, the Pearson code and the tier for every examined subject. One to us with that list, the series you are planning for and two Gulf Standard Time windows that genuinely work. The first session is at no charge, taught by the tutor who would take the course, built around a timed paper from the correct board and marked against the published scheme. Nothing is payable until you have seen how they mark, and every date we rely on points back to Pearson's own timetable.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-physics-4ph1-tut.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1 for Abu Dhabi students, from a Year 10 start through to a November resit. Each works from released papers and the published mark schemes rather than from a generic worksheet bank.

intro.heading: What you should be able to read after a month, and what no page can promise you
paragraphs: Physics tuition in Abu Dhabi usually starts from a single piece of paper. A Year 11 mock comes back with 52 out of 110 on Paper 1P, the comment at the bottom says the student needs to show more working, and the school target still says 7. Nothing in that document tells a parent which of the eight 4PH1 topics is responsible, whether the loss is physics or arithmetic, or how many hours it would take to close. The grade is visible and the diagnosis is not, which is exactly the gap a tutor is being hired to fill.

So the first thing to ask of any 4PH1 tutor is not what grade they expect. It is what they will hand you, and when. A session that produces nothing you can read leaves you back where you started, judging the tuition by how your child says it felt. Four weeks of lessons should produce four marked pieces of work, a list of topic numbers with mark losses next to them, and a short written note of what changed. None of that is a promise about the final grade. It is evidence that the work is being diagnosed rather than described.

Pearson makes this unusually easy to do honestly, because 4PH1 is a transparent qualification. There are two written papers and 180 marks between them. There is no coursework and no separately assessed practical, so every mark your child will ever earn in this subject is earned on paper, under timed conditions, against a mark scheme that is published after each series. A tutor who works from those documents can say precisely where a script lost marks and what kind of loss it was. A tutor who works from a textbook chapter cannot.

That is the whole of our argument on this page. We are not going to tell you that Abu Dhabi families get better results with us, because we cannot show you the data that would make that sentence true, and a figure without a sample size and a method is worth nothing to you. What we can describe is the record a weekly 4PH1 session produces: the paper section attempted, the raw mark, the topic that cost the most, the fix attempted, and the mark on the next attempt at the same question type. Over a term that record either shows movement or it does not, and you get to see which.

Lessons for Abu Dhabi families are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; sending a tutor to a residence is a service we run only in India. The practical effect in this subject is that your child is matched to someone who teaches 4PH1 specifically, rather than to whichever physics graduate can reach Khalifa City before 5pm. For a specification where the marks hinge on knowing that a velocity-time graph's area is displacement and its gradient is acceleration, that difference is the entire point.

What follows is the detail: how the two papers are built, which topics a marked script usually indicts, what the record looks like week by week, what the Abu Dhabi market charges for this kind of help, what ADEK and the MoHRE permit mean for anyone teaching your child, and the firm limit on what a tutor may do with your child's work.
