abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-physics-4ph1-tut.programmesIntro: 4PH1 is a two-year course, but the decisions that set its ceiling are made earlier and the consequences land later. The sequence below is the one Abu Dhabi families actually move through, and each stage leaves a different kind of evidence behind.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 Science
programmes.description: Three years of combined science in which physics appears a term at a time. The content is modest; the habits are not. Writing a unit after every number, rearranging a two-step formula without panic, plotting axes with a sensible scale and reading a gradient off a line are the four skills that decide how 4PH1 feels two years later. A Year 9 student who cannot yet do them will lose 4PH1 marks for reasons that are not about physics.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools option students into separate sciences or Science Double Award at the end of Year 9, usually on one internal test. A term of Year 9 support changes which qualification a child is entered for, which is a cheaper intervention than trying to rescue a single-award physics grade in Year 11. Ask the head of science which route the current cohort was placed into and on what evidence.

programmes.name: International GCSE Physics, first year
programmes.description: Forces and motion, electricity, waves and energy transfer are normally taught first, which means the topics with the heaviest calculation load arrive before exam technique has formed. Year 10 is when a mark log is worth most: the same arithmetic errors recur across topics, and a student who fixes significant figures and unit conversion in Year 10 stops paying for them in every paper afterwards.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools run internal end-of-year assessments in May or June using past Pearson questions, so a Year 10 report usually rests on a real script. Ask for it. It is the single most useful document for setting up a Year 11 plan, and it is far easier to obtain in June than in January, when departments are deep in mock marking.

programmes.name: International GCSE Physics, examination year
programmes.description: Magnetism and electromagnetism, radioactivity and particles, and the astrophysics content assessed only on Paper 2P tend to arrive late, often after the mock. That creates a predictable pattern in marked scripts: solid marks on topics taught in Year 10, scattered marks on topics taught weeks earlier, and heavy losses on the six-mark extended questions that cross topics.
programmes.countryNote: Mock windows in Abu Dhabi cluster in November and January, and the Pearson entry deadline for a summer series sits months before the exam itself. A mock script marked in January is the last complete piece of evidence available before entries are confirmed, which makes it the right moment to decide between a full-course push and a targeted repair of two topics.

programmes.name: November series and private candidates
programmes.description: Pearson International GCSE is examined in a May/June series and a November series, so a 4PH1 grade can be improved without repeating a school year. A resit plan works differently from a first attempt: the component marks from the first sitting are already a diagnosis, and the work is to rebuild two or three topics to a higher standard rather than to re-teach eight.
programmes.countryNote: A resit candidate in Abu Dhabi needs an entry through a centre, and the entry deadline is the constraint that decides everything else. Published Pearson milestones put final entries months ahead of the exam window, so the decision to resit is made long before revision starts. Confirm the live dates on qualifications.pearson.com and with the exams officer at the centre taking the entry.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-physics-4ph1-tut.subjectsIntro: Physics is rarely the only subject in play, and the pairing changes what a weekly hour has to do. The list below is what Abu Dhabi 4PH1 students most often sit alongside it, with the specific interference each pairing creates.

subjects.name: Physics (4PH1)
subjects.description: The subject of this page. Two written papers, 180 marks, untiered and graded 9 to 1. Marked scripts tend to bleed in three places: equations recalled but rearranged wrongly, graph questions answered without using the axes, and six-mark explanations that describe an effect without naming the quantity that causes it.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.description: The arithmetic physics depends on. Standard form, rearranging formulae, percentage change and gradient all appear in both. A student losing physics marks on calculation almost always has a matching gap in Higher tier maths, and fixing it once pays twice.

subjects.name: Chemistry (4CH1)
subjects.description: Sits in the same science option block and competes for the same revision hours. The overlap is quantitative: moles, significant figures and unit conversion. Students who treat the two subjects as unrelated repeat the same arithmetic mistakes in both and pay twice for one weakness.

subjects.name: Biology (4BI1)
subjects.description: The third separate science, and the one most often sacrificed in a crowded week. Biology rewards precise written explanation; physics rewards precise quantity. A student strong in biology and weak in physics usually has the vocabulary and lacks the habit of attaching a number to a claim.

subjects.name: Science Double Award (4SD0)
subjects.description: The alternative route, covering all three sciences for two grades rather than three. Physics content is reduced and astrophysics is not examined in the same way. Confirming which route a child is on is the first question we ask, because the answer sometimes differs between siblings in one household.

subjects.name: Further Pure Mathematics (4PM1)
subjects.description: Taken by students heading for A-Level maths or physics. Calculus and vectors appear here before they appear anywhere else, and a 4PM1 student usually finds 4PH1 calculation trivial, which masks weak written explanation until a six-mark question exposes it.

subjects.name: English Language A (4EA1)
subjects.description: Relevant to physics for one reason: the extended-response marks. A student who writes loosely in English writes loosely in a six-mark physics explanation, and markers pay for sequence and precision in both. Command-word work transfers between the two subjects more than most families expect.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Required in UAE private schools regardless of the international curriculum a school is licensed to teach, and timetabled in school hours. It matters to a physics plan only as a constraint: it occupies periods that might otherwise be free, which affects where a weekly session can realistically sit.

subjects.name: Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: Also required in UAE private schools, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students under published guidance. Again, the relevance to 4PH1 is timetable arithmetic rather than content: these are fixed periods, and a realistic weekly physics slot has to work around them.

subjects.name: Computer Science (4CP0)
subjects.description: A common pairing for students who intend to read engineering. The logic transfers; the exam habits do not. Computer science rewards a correct final answer, while a physics mark scheme pays for the method line even when the number is wrong, and students who move between them often stop showing working.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-physics-4ph1-tut.regionsIntro: Abu Dhabi spreads across the island, the mainland corridor towards Khalifa City and Al Raha, and the newer communities beyond. The school run and the sports timetable decide when physics can realistically be taught, so the notes below are about session timing rather than scenery.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Karamah
regions.note: Short runs from several long-established island schools, so a 4.30pm physics slot holds during term. Families here often have two children on different specifications, and a fixed weekly time protects the marked-work cycle better than a flexible one.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Tower living with lifts and parking between the car and the desk, which routinely eats the last fifteen minutes of a school run. Sessions after 6pm start on time; a 5pm slot in exam term tends to begin with the student still arriving.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: The largest concentration of Year 10 and 11 separate-science entries in the emirate. Bus runs are long, so the practical choice is a late session or a weekend morning, and weekend mornings are where a full past-paper section fits without being rushed.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Zeina
regions.note: Close to the Al Raha corridor schools, with short journeys but heavy after-school activity schedules. Physics sessions here are often pushed to Friday or Saturday, which suits timed paper work and suits marking turnaround less well.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: A short commute to the island schools and a long one to anywhere on the mainland. Students here frequently sit Paper 2P content taught late in Year 11, so plans tend to be built backwards from the mock rather than from the start of the course.

regions.name: Yas Island and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Mixed school destinations, some island and some mainland, which makes household timetables unpredictable from week to week. A recorded session matters more here than elsewhere: a missed slot can be caught up without losing the marked-work cycle.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Al Shamkha
regions.note: Longer mainland journeys and a wider spread of school destinations. Evening sessions from 7pm are normal, and a 60-minute slot with one marked paper section works better than a 90-minute slot that starts with a tired student.

regions.name: Al Bateen and the Corniche
regions.note: Dense school provision within a few minutes of home, so the limiting factor is activity scheduling rather than traffic. Early-evening physics works, and these are the households most likely to want two short sessions a week before a mock.

schoolClusters.city: Island and corniche schools
schoolClusters.note: The oldest British-curriculum provision in the emirate, where separate-science entries are long established and mock calendars run early. Students we support in this cluster usually arrive with a marked mock script in hand, which shortens the diagnostic to a single session.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City and the Al Raha corridor
schoolClusters.note: The heaviest concentration of Year 10 and 11 science entries in Abu Dhabi, and the cluster where single-award physics and Science Double Award students sit in the same families. Confirming the specification code before the first session is routine here because the answer varies within a household.

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat, Yas and the newer communities
schoolClusters.note: Newer schools with growing Year 11 cohorts and, in several cases, their first or second full cycle of International GCSE science entries. Mock scripts are available but historical grade patterns are thin, so plans here lean harder on released Pearson questions than on school precedent.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-physics-4ph1-tut.modesIntro: Three shapes of 4PH1 support cover almost every request that reaches us from Abu Dhabi. They differ mainly in how much marking happens between sessions, which is the part that produces the evidence a parent can actually read.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one with a marked paper section
modes.description: The default. One live session a week on Gulf Standard Time, with a section of a released 4PH1 paper attempted between sessions and marked against the published scheme before the next one. The session opens on the marking and spends the rest of the hour on the weakest topic it exposed. Over a term this produces a dated record of where marks moved and where they did not.

Session recording available on request

modes.title: Pre-mock repair block
modes.description: A short, dated block of four to eight sessions aimed at two named topics, booked after a mock script has been read. The scope is set in writing before the block starts and the block ends with a timed attempt at the same question types that failed in the mock. This is the format for a family who wants a defined piece of work rather than an open-ended arrangement.

sections.heading: What a marked 4PH1 script tells you that a progress report does not
paragraphs: A school progress report gives you a grade and an adjective. A marked script gives you four numbers, and those four numbers are the whole diagnosis. The first is the raw mark against the maximum for the section. The second is the share of marks lost on method lines rather than final answers, which separates a physics problem from an arithmetic one. The third is the number of questions left blank or abandoned, which is a pacing and confidence measure rather than a knowledge one. The fourth is the distribution of loss across topic numbers, which tells you whether the problem is one topic or eight.

Those four figures point at four completely different interventions. Heavy loss on method lines means the student knows the physics and is not writing it down in the order a mark scheme pays for, which is a technique repair measurable in a handful of sessions. Blanks in the second half of a paper mean the first half took too long, which is a pacing drill rather than a content one. Concentrated loss on topics 6 and 7 usually means magnetism and radioactivity were taught in the weeks before the mock and have not been revisited. Loss spread evenly across all eight topics is the hardest case and the one most likely to need a full course rebuild.

This is why the first request we make of an Abu Dhabi family is the last marked physics paper, however poor it looks. Not a description of the problem, not the report, not the target grade. If the school has not released the script, the exams officer or the head of science will usually share a mock paper on request, and most departments in the emirate do. Where nothing is available, the trial lesson becomes the diagnostic: a timed section of a released Pearson paper, marked against the published scheme, which produces the same four numbers an hour later.
The table below is what that audit looks like written down. It is a format, not a result; the figures a given student produces are their own.

sections.heading: Paper 1P and Paper 2P: 180 marks and the pace they set
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics is assessed by two written papers and nothing else. Paper 1P runs for two hours and carries 110 marks. Paper 2P runs for one hour fifteen minutes and carries 70. Together that is 180 marks, and the qualification is untiered and graded 9 to 1, so every candidate sits the same two papers. There is no coursework, no portfolio and no separately assessed practical examination, which means the entire grade is decided by what a student can write under timed conditions.

The division of content matters for revision order. Paper 1P assesses the specification's core content across forces and motion, electricity, waves, energy resources and energy transfer, solids, liquids and gases, magnetism and electromagnetism, and radioactivity and particles. Paper 2P assesses that same ground plus the content the specification flags as assessed only on the second paper, including the astrophysics material. A student who revises evenly across eight topics without checking which paper tests the extra depth will under-prepare for Paper 2P and over-prepare for Paper 1P.

The pacing arithmetic is the part most revision plans ignore. One hundred and ten marks in 120 minutes gives roughly 65 seconds per mark. Seventy marks in 75 minutes gives almost exactly the same figure. Both Pearson physics papers therefore run at about one mark a minute, which sounds comfortable and is not, because a six-mark explanation and a two-mark calculation do not consume time in proportion to their marks. Students lose far more to the clock on extended responses than they expect, and the blanks that show up in a marked script are usually paid for in the first forty minutes of the paper rather than the last ten.

Weightings and timings are given here as published for the current specification. Confirm them for your child's series against the specification and the live timetable on qualifications.pearson.com, because entry codes and component details are the kind of thing a board revises between series.

sections.heading: The eight topics read as a diagnosis rather than a syllabus list
paragraphs: Every 4PH1 topic fails in its own characteristic way, and after enough marked scripts the pattern becomes recognisable from the loss alone. Forces and motion loses marks on graph interpretation: a student reads a value off a velocity-time graph when the question wanted the gradient, or calculates the gradient when the question wanted the area. The physics is understood and the question is misread, and the fix is a drill on what each graph feature represents rather than a re-teach of motion.

Electricity loses marks on series and parallel reasoning and on rearrangement under pressure. A student who can state that current is the same throughout a series circuit will still divide when they should multiply once the question adds a second resistor and a voltmeter. Waves loses marks on diagram conventions, particularly on refraction, where a ray drawn without a normal line or bending the wrong way costs the mark regardless of the written explanation beside it. Energy resources and energy transfer loses marks to vagueness: an answer that says energy is lost rather than naming the store and the transfer earns nothing in a mark scheme that pays for named quantities.

Solids, liquids and gases is where unit conversion does the damage, because pressure, volume and temperature questions move between kilopascals and pascals, cubic centimetres and cubic metres, and degrees Celsius and kelvin within a single question. Magnetism and electromagnetism loses marks on the direction rules, which are learned as hand gestures and forgotten under pressure. Radioactivity and particles loses marks on nuclear equations where mass and atomic numbers do not balance, and on half-life questions answered by guessing rather than by halving systematically. Astrophysics, assessed in the Paper 2P content, is the topic most often taught last and revised least, and in marked scripts it is frequently the cleanest source of recoverable marks.

Reading loss this way changes what a session is for. A tutor who knows that three quarters of a student's electricity loss sits in rearrangement rather than in circuit theory spends the hour on algebra applied to physics, not on circuits. That is a different lesson from the one a revision guide would prescribe, and it is only available to someone holding the marked script.

sections.heading: Eight weeks of evidence, and what the record looks like
paragraphs: The question a parent paying for weekly tuition should be able to answer is simple: what changed last month, and how do you know? A record that answers it has four columns and takes a tutor two minutes a week to keep. Which paper section was attempted, what it scored, which topic the loss sat in, and what the next session did about it. Eight weeks of that is a document rather than an impression, and it is the thing we ask tutors to produce for every Abu Dhabi family on a weekly arrangement.

The shape of the record is predictable even though the numbers are not. The first two weeks almost always show a flat or falling score, because the student is now attempting sections under timed conditions rather than at leisure, and because the early marking is honest about things a school report has been gentle about. Weeks three to five usually show the technique marks arriving first: method lines appearing, units written, working shown even where the final answer is wrong. Content gains, where they come, come later, because a topic genuinely has to be rebuilt rather than reminded.

What the record also does is make failure visible early. If eight weeks of marked sections show no movement at all in either method marks or raw score, the arrangement is not working, and a parent holding the log can see that in a minute without knowing any physics. We would rather that conversation happened in week eight with evidence than in month five with a disappointing result. A tutor change at that point costs nothing, and the log transfers to whoever picks the work up.
The table sets out the structure of such a log. The entries are illustrative of the format, not a prediction for any student, and no tutor can commit in advance to a mark on a given week.

sections.heading: Why the search says tutor in Abu Dhabi and the lesson happens over video
paragraphs: Parents in Abu Dhabi search for a physics tutor in Abu Dhabi, and they usually mean someone who will arrive at the door. That is a reasonable thing to want and a real market: published figures for in-home one-to-one tuition in the UAE run from around AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, with monthly in-home packages advertised around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors are quoted up to AED 500.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, and nothing on this page should be read as an offer to send anybody to a residence in the emirate. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; a tutor arriving at a UAE address is a service we run only in India. The honest comparison is not between our online lesson and a hypothetical visit from us, but between an online specialist and the pool of tutors who can physically reach a given Abu Dhabi community on a weekday evening.

That pool is the real constraint. A family in Al Shamkha or Mohammed Bin Zayed City choosing in-home tuition is choosing from whoever will drive there between 5pm and 8pm, which in a specification like 4PH1 often means a general science tutor rather than a physics specialist who works from released Pearson papers. Online, the catchment is irrelevant and the selection criterion becomes the specification code. The second effect is quieter and matters more over a term: the travel time a visiting tutor bills is time not spent marking, and marking between sessions is what produces the evidence described above.

IB Gram's own arrangement starts with one free trial lesson, with no card details taken; what a weekly plan costs after that depends on session length and frequency, which is a conversation rather than a table.

sections.heading: Practical physics in a specification with no practical examination
paragraphs: 4PH1 has no assessed practical and no coursework, which leads some families to assume practical work can be skipped. The specification says otherwise in the most expensive possible way: practical skills are examined through written questions on both papers. A candidate can be asked to describe a method, identify the independent variable, explain why a reading was repeated, suggest an improvement to an apparatus setup, or read a measurement from a diagram of a scale. Those marks are available every series and they are lost by students who have done the experiments and never written about them.

The experiments themselves are the familiar ones: measuring the acceleration of a trolley down a ramp, finding the resistance of a wire by varying its length, investigating the refraction of light through a glass block, determining a specific heat capacity, measuring the extension of a spring against load. What a mark scheme pays for in each case is not the result but the procedural reasoning. Why that control variable. Why that number of repeats. Why a thermometer reading has an uncertainty of half a division. A student who has performed every one of these at school and never articulated the reasoning will still drop the marks.

Online lessons handle this well because the examined skill is written rather than manual. A session can put a diagram of an apparatus on a shared screen, ask the student to write the method in the form a mark scheme rewards, and mark that answer against a published scheme in the same hour. Graph work transfers the same way: the student plots on paper or on a shared whiteboard, photographs it, and the line of best fit, the gradient triangle and the labelled axes are reviewed point by point. None of that needs a tutor in the room, and screen sharing makes the marking visible to the student while it happens.

What an online session cannot do is give a student hands on a ripple tank. That is the school's job and the school does it. Our part is making sure the written marks attached to those experiments are earned, which is the part the marked scripts show being missed.

sections.heading: ADEK, the MoHRE permit, and who may legally tutor your child in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection ratings. The UAE government's own guidance sets out this division: KHDA covers Dubai, the Sharjah Private Education Authority covers Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages reviewed for this project, which is a strange gap on pages written for Abu Dhabi parents.

What matters for tutoring is a separate instrument. Private tuition in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the ministry's app, website and e-services. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anyone.

There is a second rule that catches Abu Dhabi families specifically. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it. The practical reading is clear enough: the convenient arrangement in which your child's own physics teacher tutors them privately for a fee is the one to avoid, however well meant the offer.

IB Gram holds no licence, permit, accreditation or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, Pearson or any examination board, and this page makes no such claim. We are a matching platform, and the question a parent should ask of any tutor, through us or otherwise, is whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition permit and whether their own employment allows private tutoring. That is a reasonable question and a tutor who cannot answer it is answering it.

sections.heading: What a physics tutor may not do, and why the limit protects your child
paragraphs: 4PH1 carries no coursework, which removes the most common academic-honesty trap in international qualifications. It does not remove all of them. A tutor may teach, explain, demonstrate a worked example, set work and mark it against a published scheme. A tutor may not complete a piece of work that a school will treat as the student's own, and that includes homework a department collects for assessment, internal mock papers taken home, and any task feeding into a predicted grade. The line is not subtle and the consequence of crossing it lands on the student rather than the tutor.

There is a related limit on materials. Pearson's past papers, mark schemes, examiner reports and specifications are the board's copyright, published on the board's own site and, for recent series, released to centres under conditions. A tutor may reference them, work from them in a live session and point you to the official page; a tutor should not be supplying you with a drive folder of reproduced papers, and a tutor offering unreleased material is offering something that would make your child a malpractice case. Every reference on this page points at qualifications.pearson.com for exactly that reason.

The third limit is about claims rather than conduct. No tutor, however many 4PH1 scripts they have marked, can guarantee a grade, and any page promising a 9 or a specific number of marks is selling something it cannot deliver. What can be promised is process: that work will be marked against the published scheme, that the mark log will be honest including when it is flat, and that you will be told when the arrangement is not working rather than invoiced through another term. Tutors described as examiners here would have to evidence current examiner status, and we do not use examiner status to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content.

Families sometimes read these limits as reluctance. They are the opposite. A tutor who will not do your child's assessed work is a tutor whose marked feedback means something, because the script in front of them is genuinely their student's.

sections.heading: When no 4PH1 specialist is free, and how matching actually works
paragraphs: Availability is where tutoring platforms are least honest, so here is the position plainly. Physics at International GCSE level is a narrower specialism than maths, and the Abu Dhabi evening slots between 5pm and 8pm Gulf Standard Time are the most requested hours in the week. In exam term those slots fill. When the specialist who matches your child's specification and level has no slot in the window you need, there are three possible answers and we would rather you knew all three before enquiring than discovered them afterwards.

The first is a different time. A weekend morning or an earlier weekday slot usually frees a specialist immediately, and for timed paper work a Saturday morning is better than a Tuesday at 7pm in any case. The second is a different tutor: a strong general science tutor who teaches 4PH1 alongside 4BI1 and 4CH1 rather than a physics-only specialist, which is a reasonable fit for a student who needs the arithmetic and technique work rather than Paper 2P astrophysics depth. The third is a wait with a date on it, which is sometimes the right answer and is always better than a placement that does not fit.

The matching process itself is short. You send the last marked physics script and tell us the series your child is entered for, we confirm the specification code and the paper structure, and a free trial lesson follows with the tutor we think fits. No card details are taken for the trial. If the match is wrong, say so after the trial or after the fourth session and we move the student, at no extra charge, with the mark log passed to whoever picks the work up. Changing tutor once is common and is not a failure of the process.

What we will not do is tell you that a tutor is available when the honest answer is Saturday at 9am, because the arrangement that follows a false yes is the one that quietly stops producing marked work by week three.

process.title: Send the last marked physics script
process.description: The most useful document is not a description of the problem but the last marked paper or mock, however poor the mark. If the school has not released it, ask the exams officer or the head of science; most Abu Dhabi departments will share a mock script on request. Where nothing exists, the trial lesson produces one.

process.title: Confirm the specification and the series
process.description: We check that your child is on Pearson 4PH1 rather than Cambridge 0625 or Science Double Award 4SD0, and which series the entry is for. The paper structure, the Paper-2-only content and the entry deadline all follow from that answer, and in some households the answer differs between siblings.

process.title: Agree the scope in writing
process.description: Before the first paid session, the two topics the block will cover are written down, along with the marked-work cycle and what you will receive each week. A plan that names two topics and a question type is checkable; a plan that says it will improve physics is not.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One lesson over live video, no card details taken, with the tutor we believe fits. It is a working session rather than a sales call: a timed section of a released paper, marked in the hour, which produces the script audit and the four numbers whether or not you continue.

process.title: Read the log at week four and week eight
process.description: Two review points, both built on the dated mark log rather than on a conversation. If method marks and raw scores are flat at week eight, the arrangement is not working and we change the tutor or tell you to stop. The log transfers to whoever picks the work up.

whyPoints.title: Mark losses attributed to topic numbers
whyPoints.description: Every review point names a 4PH1 topic and a figure. You should be able to read a one-page summary and know which part of the specification cost the most marks last month and what was done about it, without knowing any physics yourself. A page that cannot show you that is asking you to trust an adjective.

whyPoints.title: The specification code before the first lesson
whyPoints.description: 4PH1 is not 0625 and single-award physics is not Science Double Award. Confirming the code is the first thing we do, because the paper structure, the Paper-2-only content and the entry deadline all depend on it, and a term of revision aimed at the wrong specification is a term wasted.

whyPoints.title: Marking between sessions, not only inside them
whyPoints.description: The evidence a parent can read is produced by work marked against the published scheme in the gap between lessons. A tutor whose whole hour is explanation leaves nothing behind. The marked section is the deliverable; the live hour is where its findings get taught.

whyPoints.title: An honest log, including when it is flat
whyPoints.description: A record that only ever shows improvement is a record nobody is keeping. Two flat weeks are normal early, because timed conditions and honest marking both lower a score before they raise it. Eight flat weeks mean something is wrong, and you should hear that from us rather than work it out in results week.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before you enquire
whyPoints.description: Weekday evening slots in Abu Dhabi fill during exam term, and a physics specialist is a narrower pool than a maths one. When the honest answer is a weekend morning or a two-week wait, that is the answer you get, rather than a placement with whoever happens to be free.

whyPoints.title: No claim we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No guaranteed grades, no satisfaction percentages, no self-published star rating, and no suggestion of approval from ADEK, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education or Pearson, none of which IB Gram holds. Market rates on this page are quoted from the named source with its date, and our own pricing starts with a free trial.

faqs.question: How much does an Edexcel IGCSE Physics 4PH1 tutor cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in the UAE run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online help, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an International GCSE specialist. Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and TutorChase publishes AED 270; independent home tutors are quoted up to AED 500. Those are other providers' figures as published in October 2026, not ours. IB Gram starts with one free trial lesson, with no card details taken, and the weekly cost after that depends on session length and frequency.

faqs.question: What should I actually have in writing after a month of 4PH1 tutoring?
faqs.answer: Four marked pieces of work, a list of 4PH1 topic numbers with the marks lost against each, a count of method-line losses separated from final-answer losses, and a short dated note of what each session changed. That is the minimum a weekly arrangement should leave behind. It is not a grade prediction and it is not a guarantee of anything, but it lets you judge the tuition on evidence rather than on how your child says the lesson felt. If a month produces nothing you can read, ask why before booking a second month.

faqs.question: Which of the two 4PH1 papers carries more of the grade?
faqs.answer: Paper 1P does. It runs for two hours and carries 110 of the 180 marks, so about 61 per cent of the qualification, while Paper 2P runs for one hour fifteen minutes and carries 70 marks, or about 39 per cent. Paper 2P also assesses the content the specification flags as examined only on the second paper, including the astrophysics material, which is why revising evenly across topics without checking the paper split under-prepares a candidate for the shorter paper. Confirm component details for your child's series on qualifications.pearson.com, since boards do revise them.

faqs.question: My child's marked physics paper is covered in ticks but the grade is still a 5. How?
faqs.answer: Usually because the ticks are on method lines and the final answers are wrong, or because whole questions in the last third of the paper are blank. Both are visible in a script audit and neither is a knowledge problem. Method-line credit with wrong answers points at arithmetic and unit conversion rather than physics, which is a repair measurable in a few sessions. Blanks concentrated late in the paper point at pacing, since both 4PH1 papers run at roughly one mark a minute. Those two diagnoses lead to completely different lessons, which is why the script matters more than the grade.

faqs.question: Where do Abu Dhabi 4PH1 candidates most often lose marks they could have kept?
faqs.answer: In marked scripts the recurring losses sit in a few predictable places. Motion graphs answered with a gradient when the question wanted the area, or the reverse. Electricity questions where series and parallel reasoning collapses once rearrangement is needed. Refraction diagrams drawn without a normal line. Pressure and gas questions where kilopascals, cubic centimetres and degrees Celsius are not converted. Nuclear equations whose mass and atomic numbers do not balance. Each of those is a drill rather than a re-teach, which is why identifying them from a script is worth more than another pass through the textbook.

faqs.question: Does Edexcel IGCSE Physics 4PH1 include a practical exam my child has to sit?
faqs.answer: No. There is no assessed practical and no coursework in 4PH1; the whole grade comes from the two written papers. Practical skills are still examined, through written questions that ask a candidate to describe a method, identify variables, explain why readings were repeated, suggest improvements to an apparatus setup or read a value from a scale. Those marks appear every series and are routinely dropped by students who have done the experiments at school but never written about them in the form a mark scheme rewards. The experiments stay the school's job; the written marks are ours.

faqs.question: What happens to circuit and ray diagrams when the physics lesson is over video?
faqs.answer: They move to a shared screen, which usually makes them easier to teach than on paper. A circuit can be drawn, redrawn and annotated while the student watches, and the same diagram can be marked against the published scheme line by line in the same hour. Graph work goes the other way: the student plots on paper, photographs it, and the axes, scale, line of best fit and gradient triangle get reviewed point by point. Nothing in a 4PH1 diagram question needs a tutor in the room, and screen sharing makes the marking visible while it happens rather than afterwards.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child's Abu Dhabi school entered Pearson 4PH1 or Cambridge 0625?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer, or look at the top of any past paper the department has issued, where the code is printed. It matters more than families expect. Paper structures, the way practical skills are examined, and the entry deadlines differ between the two boards, so a term of revision aimed at the wrong specification wastes real time. Within Pearson there is a second question: whether your child sits single-award physics, 4PH1, or physics inside Science Double Award 4SD0, which examines reduced content. In some households the answer differs between siblings, so check per child.

faqs.question: Is a MoHRE permit required for whoever teaches my child 4PH1?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE is regulated by permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The MoHRE private tutor work permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you are quoted with suspicion.

faqs.question: Can my child's own physics teacher at their Abu Dhabi school tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: It is the arrangement to avoid. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on this summary. The safer route is a tutor with no relationship to the school, which also removes any question about predicted grades and internal assessment being marked by someone you are paying.

faqs.question: How does a physics International GCSE grade fit into a UAE equivalency file?
faqs.answer: On the British track, the published rule asks for five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among those five, plus one subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Physics is an ordinary subject for that count. One ranking competitor states six IGCSE subjects are required, which does not match the published rule. Equivalency is handled by the Ministry, not by us, and the requirements should be verified on moe.gov.ae before any decision.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do Abu Dhabi families usually start with for 4PH1?
faqs.answer: One, in a fixed weekly slot, with a marked paper section between sessions. One well-marked hour a week produces more evidence than two unmarked hours, because the marking is what identifies the topic and the error type. Families tend to move to two sessions a week in the six to eight weeks before a mock or a series, usually splitting them into one content session and one timed-paper session. Starting at three sessions a week is almost always a sign the diagnosis has been skipped, and it is the arrangement most likely to be abandoned by week four.

faqs.question: We have six weeks until the series. Is an evidence log still worth keeping?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it gets shorter and blunter. Six weeks is roughly six to twelve sessions, which is enough to repair two topics and a pacing problem but not enough to rebuild eight topics. The log for a short block names the two topics on day one, records a timed section each week, and tracks the blank count as closely as the raw mark, because late-paper blanks are the cheapest marks to recover in a short run. What a six-week block cannot do is make up two years, and a tutor who says otherwise is not reading the script.

faqs.question: Can 4PH1 sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most Abu Dhabi families do move them. School days shorten, energy in the late afternoon drops, and a timed physics paper attempted at 4pm during Ramadan is not a fair measure of anything. Sessions commonly shift to after Iftar, and the marked-work cycle usually drops to one shorter section a week rather than a full paper. Since lessons run over live video there is no travel to schedule around, which makes a late slot practical in a way an in-home arrangement would not be. Tell us before the month starts so the slot is held.

faqs.question: What happens if the marks have not moved after eight weeks?
faqs.answer: You tell us, or we tell you, and the tutor changes at no extra charge. Two flat weeks early on are normal, because timed conditions and honest marking both pull a score down before they lift it. Eight flat weeks across both method marks and raw score mean the arrangement is not working, and the mark log makes that visible without anyone needing to interpret it. The log goes to the next tutor so the diagnostic work is not repeated. Stopping is also a legitimate outcome, and we would rather say so in week eight than invoice another term.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-physics-4ph1-tut.closingHeading: Start with the script you already have
abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-physics-4ph1-tut.closingBody: The most useful document in this process is probably already in your house: your child's last marked physics paper, whatever the mark on it says. Send it, book the free trial lesson, and let the first hour produce the four numbers rather than another conversation about targets. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, the marked sections come back with topic numbers attached, and after four weeks you will have a dated log you can read in a minute. If it shows nothing moving, we will say so and change the tutor.

intro.heading: What a Double Award actually costs to support, and why the quotes vary so much
paragraphs: Science Double Award is the qualification that breaks tutoring arithmetic. A parent in Al Reef or Mohammed Bin Zayed City looks at a report with three science teachers' comments and two predicted grades on it, asks three tutoring services for a price, and gets three answers that are not comparable because each has silently assumed something different. One has quoted for biology. One has quoted for three subjects at the single-award rate. One has quoted a monthly package and not said how many sessions it contains.

The structure is worth stating plainly before any money is discussed. Pearson's 4SD0 is examined by three written papers, one in biology, one in chemistry and one in physics, and it reports two International GCSE grades rather than three. It covers less of each science than the three single awards do, which is the whole point of it: it buys two science grades for roughly the timetable cost of two subjects instead of three. Confirm the current paper structure, durations and mark totals on the live specification at qualifications.pearson.com, because Pearson revises its own documents and the centre teaches from that version, not from a summary.

That structure has a direct financial consequence. A Double Award student does not need three tutors. They need one science tutor who can read a mark scheme in all three papers and identify which of the three is actually costing the grade, plus occasional specialist cover for whichever science turns out to be the problem. The cheapest serious plan in this subject is diagnostic first and specialist second, and the most expensive mistake is booking three weekly hours in September because three sciences appear on the timetable.

Every dirham figure on this page is attributed. Three of the six most visible tutoring sites in this market publish no price at all, and two of the rest quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not pay in. The bands below come from providers and rate surveys that published them, with the format each applies to. They are the market, not IB Gram's price list. Our own number follows the free trial lesson, because until a tutor has seen a marked script nobody can honestly say how much marking the plan requires.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video with screen sharing and a shared whiteboard. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; visiting tuition is a service we run only in India. For a three-science qualification that turns out to matter financially as well as practically, because the published in-home bands in this emirate sit well above the online ones and the premium is travel the family funds. The comparison table further down costs both options over a term rather than per hour, which is the number that actually lands on a household budget.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-science-double-a.programmesIntro: Double Award sits in the middle of a route, and the money decisions are made at its edges. The three stages below are where Abu Dhabi families spend, and the earliest of them is by far the cheapest place to change an outcome.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 Science
programmes.description: Combined science taught as a rotation in most British-curriculum schools here, which means biology, chemistry and physics each appear for a term and then disappear. The Year 9 option decision, single awards or Double Award, is frequently made on one internal test taken at the end of that rotation. A term of support in Year 9 is the lowest-cost intervention available in the whole sequence.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi the option blocks are often set before the spring term, so a family wanting to influence the route has to act in the autumn. Changing which qualification a child is entered for costs a few sessions. Trying to compensate for the wrong route two years later costs a great deal more and rarely works.

programmes.name: Science Double Award
programmes.description: Three papers, two grades, graded on the 9 to 1 scale, with no coursework to submit. Students carry all three sciences through two years but at reduced depth compared with the single awards. The tuition spend concentrates in two windows: the first term of Year 10, when the habit of writing scientific answers is formed, and the final two terms of Year 11, when timed papers start producing real diagnostic information.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi centres enter candidates in the May/June series and increasingly in November as well. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers and are set by the centre, not by the family, so a plan that assumes a November entry is still available in October is usually wrong. Ask the exams officer for the internal deadline in writing.

programmes.name: Moving to single-award sciences
programmes.description: Some students start on Double Award and transfer to single-award biology, chemistry or physics, typically because a post-16 plan needs the depth. The transfer is not free in teaching terms: the single awards carry content the Double Award does not, including material that appears only in the single-award papers, and that gap has to be closed before the transfer rather than after it.
programmes.countryNote: Where a family is weighing this, the cost comparison to run is the handful of catch-up sessions now against two years of a post-16 course taken without the right prerequisite. Several Abu Dhabi schools will allow the move inside Year 10 but not later, so the question is time-limited and worth asking early.

programmes.name: What a Double Award opens and closes
programmes.description: Two science grades at 9 to 1 satisfy a great many post-16 and university entry requirements, and for a student heading into business, humanities or social sciences the Double Award is often the sensible and cheaper choice. Where the plan involves International A Level sciences, medicine or engineering, individual course entry requirements should be read directly rather than assumed.
programmes.countryNote: Check the published entry criteria of the specific sixth form or university in question, including UAE institutions, rather than relying on general advice. This is a prerequisite question with a documented answer, and no tutoring is required to resolve it; it costs one email to the admissions office.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-science-double-a.subjectsIntro: A Double Award plan is priced by what it has to cover, so the list below is written in those terms: what each strand demands, and what it typically costs in sessions rather than in dirhams. Several of these can be taught inside one booking because they share a skill rather than a syllabus.

subjects.name: Biology within 4SD0
subjects.description: Usually the cheapest strand to support, because the content is largely factual and the marks go missing on writing rather than on understanding. Explanation questions wanting a mechanism in order are the main leak. Two to four sessions on answer structure often moves this paper more than a term of content teaching would.

subjects.name: Chemistry within 4SD0
subjects.description: The strand that most often needs real teaching hours. Moles, equations and concentration either work or they do not, and a student who has lost the thread in Year 10 cannot patch it in Year 11. Where a Double Award grade is below target, chemistry is the first paper we ask to see.

subjects.name: Physics within 4SD0
subjects.description: Frequently a mathematics problem in a science costume. Rearranging equations, handling units and reading a gradient account for most of the lost marks. The cost-efficient fix is sessions on the numeracy rather than on the physics, which is cheaper because the same work pays off in the chemistry paper too.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.description: The highest-leverage subject on this list for a Double Award budget. Calculation marks appear in all three science papers, so four sessions of targeted number work can show up three times. Where a science mock shows blanks on every calculation, start here rather than with any science.

subjects.name: Single-award Biology (4BI1)
subjects.description: The destination for Double Award students who decide they need biology in depth, and the comparison point for families weighing the two routes. It adds content the Double Award does not cover, including a topic on the use of biological resources, and that extra material is the real cost of transferring.

subjects.name: Single-award Chemistry (4CH1)
subjects.description: The hardest of the three transfers to make late, because the single-award content builds rather than extends. Families considering it should get the content map before committing, and should price the catch-up honestly: this is usually six to ten sessions, not two.

subjects.name: Single-award Physics (4PH1)
subjects.description: Transferable with moderate catch-up for a student who is already comfortable with the mathematics, and effectively impossible for one who is not. The entry test for this conversation is not interest in physics; it is whether the student can rearrange an equation without a prompt.

subjects.name: English Language A (4EA1)
subjects.description: Named here because science marks depend on writing more than parents expect. Extended-answer questions in all three 4SD0 papers are marked on sequence and linkage. Families often find that work done for English shows up in the science grades at no additional science cost.

subjects.name: Geography (4GE1)
subjects.description: Shares data-handling and case-study structure with the science papers and uses nearly the same command terms. Where a student performs well here and poorly in science extended answers, the problem is confidence in the science vocabulary rather than in the skill itself, and that is a short and cheap fix.

subjects.name: Business (4BS1)
subjects.description: A common Abu Dhabi option pairing with Double Award and relevant to budgeting because it competes for the same revision evenings. When a family is choosing where limited tuition money goes, the subject with the clearest marking criteria usually gives the faster return, and that is often this one.

sections.heading: Why three sciences do not mean three tuition bills
paragraphs: The instinct is understandable. Three sciences appear on the report, so three hours a week get booked, and by half term the family is spending more on tuition than on any other part of the school year while the student is doing less of their own work than before. Double Award does not need that, and the structure of the qualification is the reason.

Two grades are reported from three papers. That means no single science carries a whole grade on its own, and a weakness in one paper is diluted in a way it would not be across three single awards. The practical effect is that the question worth paying to answer first is not how to teach three sciences but which of the three is actually costing the grades. That is a diagnostic question and it takes one session and one marked script, not three weekly bookings.

Once the diagnosis exists, the spend concentrates. In our experience of Abu Dhabi Double Award scripts, chemistry is most often the paper responsible, physics is most often a mathematics problem in disguise, and biology is most often a writing problem rather than a knowledge one. Each of those has a different and differently priced remedy, and two of the three are short. Booking all three sciences equally guarantees that at least two thirds of the money goes where it was not needed.

There is a second saving most families miss. One lead tutor across three papers sees patterns that three separate tutors cannot, because command-term errors and calculation failures repeat across the sciences. Fixing the pattern once pays three times. Three tutors each fix it in their own subject, and the family pays for the same lesson three times over.

sections.heading: The three 4SD0 papers and what they are worth to a plan
paragraphs: Pearson's Science Double Award is assessed by three written papers, one in each science, with no coursework component and nothing internally assessed. The two reported International GCSE grades are built from the combined performance across all three. There is no practical examination; practical skills are tested inside the written papers, which is why so many questions present an apparatus or a set of results and ask the student to interpret them.

For a tuition plan the important feature is that the papers are independent in content but not in grade. A student can be strong in two papers and weak in one and still see both reported grades dragged down, which is the mechanism behind the single most common Double Award complaint: the student says two of the three sciences are fine and the grades still disappoint. That is not a contradiction, it is arithmetic.

It also means the cheapest route to grade movement is almost always the weakest paper, not the favourite subject. Students revise what they enjoy, and in Double Award that is the least efficient possible allocation of their time. A tutor's first job, and the thing the first marked script buys, is to redirect that effort. It is worth saying to a fifteen-year-old explicitly, because the instruction to revise the subject you dislike makes no sense until somebody shows how the grades are calculated.

Confirm the current structure, paper durations and mark totals on the live specification at qualifications.pearson.com before buying any resource. The specification is the document the centre teaches from, and it is revised; a summary on any website, including this one, is a guide to what to look for rather than an authority.

sections.heading: What the Abu Dhabi market charges, and who published each figure
paragraphs: Here is the table nobody else in this market publishes. Each band is attributed to the provider or rate survey that put the number in public, with the format it applies to, because a dirham figure without a format attached is meaningless: an in-home hour and an online hour are different products at different costs.

Read it as a range, not a price list. The bottom band buys homework supervision and is often a university student working from a textbook, which for three sciences is rarely enough. The middle band buys a teacher who knows the board. The specialist band buys someone who can mark a 4SD0 chemistry paper against the published scheme and explain why an answer scored two out of four, which in a qualification assessed entirely by written paper is the thing actually being purchased.

IB Gram's own number is not in the table, deliberately. We quote after the free trial lesson, when the tutor has seen a marked script and knows how much marking between sessions the plan requires. Quoting before that would mean either guessing high or guessing low, and in a three-science qualification the honest answer genuinely depends on which paper turns out to be the problem.

One figure to subtract from any quote you receive. The private tuition work permit in the UAE is issued free of charge, so a licensing or registration fee presented as a line item on a tutoring invoice has no basis in the published rules. Ask what it is for.

sections.heading: Budgeting a two-year 4SD0 plan month by month
paragraphs: Hourly rates are the wrong unit for a decision that runs across two academic years. Families budget monthly, and the useful question is what a Double Award plan costs per month at three realistic intensities, and in which months the intensity should change.

Bestimate's published monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions give a usable frame: roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages seen in this market include an online offer at AED 799 a month for eight sessions and in-home arrangements at AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. Those are published market figures, not ours, and the in-home comparison shows where the travel premium lands.

The shape matters more than the level. A plan that runs at the same intensity for twenty-four months wastes money in the quiet terms and under-provides in the loud ones. The sensible curve is light fortnightly review through Year 10, one short specialist block whenever a marked script names a paper, and a concentrated run-up in the four to six weeks before the series. That curve costs less in total than steady weekly sessions and produces more, because the expensive hours are bought when they can change something.

Two pieces of context for the household budget. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. School fee policy in Abu Dhabi is a matter for ADEK rather than KHDA, but the direction of travel in regional education costs is worth knowing before committing to a two-year tutoring spend.

sections.heading: Costing online against a visiting tutor over a full term
paragraphs: Per-hour comparisons flatter visiting tuition because they hide the parts a family pays for in time rather than in dirhams. Costed over a term, the gap widens, and for a three-science qualification it widens further because the specialist you want is less likely to live within range.

Take a plan of one weekly session across twelve weeks. At the published online specialist band, that is twelve hours of teaching with marking between sessions and no travel for anyone. At the published in-home band, the same twelve weeks costs more per hour before travel is counted, and the travel is counted twice: once in the rate, and once in the slot's reliability, because a visiting arrangement that depends on a drive across Abu Dhabi at five in the afternoon loses sessions to traffic, rain and school events in a way a video call does not. A lost session is a full session's cost with none of the benefit.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Abu Dhabi; visiting tuition is a service we offer only in India. That limit belongs in plain sight rather than in the small print. What replaces it is one-to-one teaching over live video with screen sharing, a shared whiteboard, optional recording and written marking between sessions. For three written papers with no practical examination, the work the qualification rewards is documents, and documents move more cheaply than people.

Group tuition is the honest third option and deserves a straight assessment. For Double Award it covers content economically and cannot diagnose, because diagnosis is about one student's specific errors across three papers. Price it as revision, judge it as revision, and do not expect it to tell you which paper is costing the grades.
