sections.heading: Double Award, single awards, and the price of changing route
paragraphs: This is the decision with the largest financial consequence in the whole 4SD0 story, and it is usually made in a ten-minute options meeting at the end of Year 9. Double Award buys two science grades with less content than three single awards. For a student heading towards humanities, business or social sciences it is the right choice and the cheaper one in every sense, including the amount of tutoring the two years will need.

For a student who may want International A Level sciences, medicine or engineering, the calculation changes. The single awards carry content the Double Award does not, and post-16 courses are built on the assumption that it was taught. The fix is not impossible but it is not free: closing a single-award gap in chemistry is realistically six to ten sessions, biology rather fewer, physics dependent entirely on whether the mathematics is secure. Several Abu Dhabi schools allow the transfer during Year 10 and not afterwards, so the window is short.

The right way to price this is against the alternative. A handful of catch-up sessions in Year 10 is a small, bounded cost. Starting a two-year post-16 science course without the prerequisite content is an unbounded one, and it tends to be paid in the first year of the sixth form at the highest tuition rates in the market, under time pressure, at the point when nobody can afford the disruption.

What this does not require is guesswork. Read the published entry requirements of the specific sixth form or university the student has in mind, including UAE institutions, and ask the school directly which content the Double Award omits relative to the single award. Both answers exist in writing, and neither of them costs anything. No tutoring is needed to establish what a course requires, and any page implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency.

sections.heading: What is not a cost: permits, free school support and the fee position
paragraphs: Several things that look like costs in this market are not, and knowing which is which protects a budget better than negotiating an hourly rate. The clearest example is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, and the federal portal u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. A fee line on a tutoring invoice described as licensing or registration has nothing published behind it.

The second is school support. Abu Dhabi private schools sit under the Department of Education and Knowledge, which u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and most schools run their own intervention sessions for students below target. Those are free and they come from the teacher who wrote the specification scheme of work. Asking the head of science what is already available should precede any tutoring purchase, and a tutoring page that discourages the question is not acting in your interest.

The third is the part of the process nobody can sell you. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so nobody can quote you an amount. Separately, press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules describes a prohibition on school staff giving paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE permit's code of conduct making a similar point. We treat that as press-reported rather than ADEK's exact wording, and the safe step is to check the current ADEK policy document before arranging anything.

Finally, the regional fee context. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27 under Dubai's economic incentives package. Abu Dhabi fee policy is ADEK's rather than KHDA's, so read that as context for where education costs are heading in the region, not as a statement about your own school. For Ministry of Education equivalency, the sourced British-track rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3 with Arabic and Islamic education excluded, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Two Double Award grades can count towards that five. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae; IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees equivalency, and no tutoring is required for it.

sections.heading: Getting a comparable quote, and the questions that make quotes comparable
paragraphs: Most families in this market are not overpaying because they chose badly. They are overpaying because the three quotes they compared described three different products and only one of them said so. Six questions make quotes comparable, and they take one message to ask.

Ask which papers the quote covers, named: all three 4SD0 papers, or one science. Ask whether marking between sessions is included, and how much, because in a written-paper qualification that is the work. Ask what happens to a cancelled session on either side. Ask whether the rate changes closer to the series, since quotes do firm up as availability tightens in the final six weeks. Ask what the review point is and when it falls. And ask what it costs to change tutor, because the answer tells you how confident the provider is in the match.

Then ask the one question that separates a tutoring service from a lead-generation site: what will you show me in writing after a month? A provider working from marked scripts answers with a document. A provider working from impressions answers with a sentiment. In a qualification where every mark comes from a timed paper, there is no excuse for the second answer.

For completeness, here is our side of those answers. One free trial lesson, no card details. A written plan within a couple of days naming the paper responsible and the marks at stake. One lead tutor across all three sciences with specialist cover added only where the evidence calls for it. Marking between sessions included as standard. A re-test and a decision point in week five. A tutor change at no extra charge if the match is wrong. And a quote that arrives after the diagnostic, in dirhams, with what it includes written down.

process.title: Send the three science grades and one marked script
process.description: The predicted or mock grades for all three 4SD0 papers, plus the most recent marked script from whichever looks weakest. That pair of documents is enough to tell whether this is a chemistry problem, a mathematics problem or a writing problem, and those three have different price tags.

process.title: Free trial lesson used as a diagnostic
process.description: No charge and no card details. Most of the session is the student attempting a short section of a released paper from the weakest science while the tutor watches how the question is read. That is where the useful information is, and it costs nothing to collect.

process.title: A written plan with the cost attached
process.description: Within a couple of days you receive the paper responsible, the marks at stake, the plan shape proposed, what marking is included, and the quote in dirhams. If any of those five is missing from a quote you receive anywhere, including from us, ask for it before paying.

process.title: Sessions at the intensity the evidence supports
process.description: One lead tutor, a fixed weekly or fortnightly slot on Gulf Standard Time, and specialist cover bought only for the paper that needs it. The plan is designed to be cheap in the quiet terms so there is budget left for the four to six weeks when it matters.

process.title: Week-five re-test and a spending decision
process.description: An unseen section of comparable difficulty, marked and compared with the baseline. That comparison decides whether to continue, change shape, add a specialist block or stop. Stopping is a legitimate outcome and the page says so, because a plan that cannot be ended is a subscription rather than a service.

whyPoints.title: Every dirham figure carries its source
whyPoints.description: The bands on this page are attributed to the provider or survey that published them, with the format each applies to. Three of the most visible competing sites in this market publish no price at all and two quote in dollars. Knowing the published range is what lets you judge any quote, including the one we send after the trial.

whyPoints.title: One lead tutor across three papers
whyPoints.description: Command-term errors and calculation failures repeat across biology, chemistry and physics. One tutor who sees all three fixes the pattern once. Three separate tutors each fix it inside their own subject, and the family pays three times for the same lesson without ever being told that is what happened.

whyPoints.title: The quote comes after the diagnostic
whyPoints.description: We do not price a three-science plan before a tutor has seen a marked script, because the honest number depends on which paper is responsible and how much marking the plan needs. A provider who quotes a Double Award plan sight unseen is guessing, and the guess is not usually in your favour.

whyPoints.title: Free school support gets mentioned first
whyPoints.description: Most Abu Dhabi schools run intervention sessions for students below target, delivered by the teacher who knows the scheme of work, at no cost. We say so on the page. Any tutoring service that would rather you did not ask the head of science that question is optimising for its own revenue.

whyPoints.title: A clear line around the student's own work
whyPoints.description: 4SD0 has no coursework, but schools still set investigations and reports. A tutor teaches, questions and marks. Nobody at IB Gram supplies a finished piece for submission or an answer to be copied across, and that boundary is stated plainly because competing pages in this market sell precisely that.

whyPoints.title: A plan you can stop
whyPoints.description: The week-five review is a genuine decision point, including the decision to stop. Marked scripts and session notes stay with you either way, so if a family pauses for a term or moves emirate the next tutor starts from the diagnosis rather than from nothing, and does not have to be paid to repeat it.

faqs.question: How much does an Edexcel IGCSE Science Double Award 4SD0 tutor cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published bands in this market run roughly AED 45-150 an hour for budget online help, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200-450 or more for an International GCSE specialist, and AED 180-500 for a visiting tutor with travel inside the rate. Those figures belong to the providers and rate surveys named in the table above. Because 4SD0 spans three papers, the number that matters is the monthly one rather than the hourly: published monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240-600 at the budget end and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

faqs.question: Do I need to pay for three tutors to cover 4SD0?
faqs.answer: No, and it is usually the most expensive way to get the worst result. Two grades are reported from three papers, so the first question worth paying to answer is which paper is costing the grades, and that takes one marked script. From there a single lead tutor who can read mark schemes across all three sciences handles the weekly work, with a short specialist block bought only for the paper the evidence names. Three weekly bookings in September means at least two thirds of the money goes somewhere it was not needed.

faqs.question: How is Science Double Award 4SD0 different from taking three single sciences?
faqs.answer: 4SD0 is assessed by three written papers, one in each science, and reports two International GCSE grades rather than three. It covers less of each science than the single awards do. For a student heading towards humanities, business or social sciences that is the sensible and cheaper route, in timetable terms as well as in tuition. For a student who may want International A Level sciences, medicine or engineering, the single awards carry content the Double Award omits, and post-16 courses assume it was taught. Read the specific course entry requirements rather than general advice.

faqs.question: Which of the three 4SD0 papers usually needs the tutoring money?
faqs.answer: In the Abu Dhabi scripts that reach us, chemistry most often. Moles, equations and concentration either work or they do not, and a student who lost the thread in Year 10 cannot patch it under exam pressure. Physics is frequently a mathematics problem wearing a science costume, so the cheaper fix is numeracy work that also lifts the chemistry paper. Biology is usually a writing problem rather than a knowledge one, and moves in two to four sessions on answer structure. Three different diagnoses, three different prices, and only a marked script tells you which applies.

faqs.question: Does 4SD0 have a practical exam or any coursework to pay for?
faqs.answer: No. There is no separately examined practical and no coursework component, so nothing is submitted and nothing is internally assessed. Practical skills are tested inside the three written papers, which is why questions routinely describe an apparatus or present a set of results and ask the student to identify variables, interpret data or write a supported conclusion. That shapes what tuition should buy: practice at reading unfamiliar experiments on the page. Confirm the current component structure on the live specification at qualifications.pearson.com, because Pearson revises its own documents.

faqs.question: What should a monthly 4SD0 tutoring budget look like across two years?
faqs.answer: Not flat. A plan running at one intensity for twenty-four months wastes money in the quiet terms and under-provides in the loud ones. The shape that costs less in total is light fortnightly review through Year 10, one short specialist block whenever a marked script names a paper, and a concentrated run-up in the four to six weeks before the series. Published monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions in this market run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

faqs.question: Is a monthly package better value than paying by the hour for 4SD0?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the package includes, and packages in this market are not written to make that easy. Published examples include an online offer at AED 799 a month for eight sessions and in-home arrangements at AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. Before comparing either with an hourly rate, ask three things: how many of the three sciences it covers, how much marking between sessions is included, and what happens to unused sessions. A package that bundles eight hours of talking and no marking is cheaper per hour and worse value.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in Abu Dhabi rise closer to the exam series?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens and quotes firm up in the four to six weeks before the first paper, which is also when the least useful work tends to get booked. A family starting in October for a May or June entry pays the quieter rate and has a wider choice of specialist. A family starting in April is paying the busy rate for crisis management. If budget is the constraint, the single most effective saving in this subject is starting earlier at a lower intensity rather than negotiating harder later at a higher one.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Abu Dhabi have to hold a permit, and does it cost anything?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it is free. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no amount can legitimately be quoted to you.

faqs.question: Can my child get 4SD0 help from their school for free before I pay anyone?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it should be the first call. Most Abu Dhabi private schools run intervention or clinic sessions for students below target, delivered by the staff who wrote the scheme of work, at no cost. Ask the head of science what is already running and whether your child is in it. Separately, press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules describes a prohibition on school staff giving paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, so free school support and paid help from a different tutor are the two clean options.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do Abu Dhabi families usually book for Double Award?
faqs.answer: One a fortnight is the right starting point for a Year 10 student with stable grades, built around work the student has already done. One a week becomes sensible when a marked script names a paper or a transfer decision is pending. Two a week makes sense only in the final four to six weeks, or where whole topics are genuinely missing rather than technique. The week-five re-test rather than anyone's instinct decides which of the three applies, which is why that date gets set before the first session.

faqs.question: What does it cost to move from 4SD0 to a single-award science?
faqs.answer: Realistically six to ten sessions for chemistry, fewer for biology, and for physics it depends entirely on whether the student's mathematics is secure. The single awards carry content the Double Award does not, and that gap has to be closed before the transfer rather than after it. Several Abu Dhabi schools allow the move during Year 10 and not later, so the window is short. Price it against the alternative: a bounded catch-up cost now, or an unbounded one in the first year of a post-16 science course taken without the prerequisite content.

faqs.question: Do two Double Award grades count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: They can count towards the five subjects the British track requires. The sourced rule is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. One well-ranked competing page states six subjects are needed. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority, because equivalency is a regulatory process IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee, and no tutoring is required for it.

faqs.question: Can one booking cover two children, one on 4SD0 and a sibling on single awards?
faqs.answer: Often it can, and in Abu Dhabi households it frequently should. Where both children are inside the same Pearson science family, one lead tutor can hold both plans, which costs less than four separate bookings and means the diagnosis is not repeated twice. Live sessions still run one-to-one, because two students with different papers in one hour is a group class with a premium price attached. What is shared is the tutor, the marking approach and the record, not the session itself.

faqs.question: What happens to the cost if we need to pause during Ramadan or exam weeks?
faqs.answer: Nothing should be charged for sessions not taken, and any quote you accept should say so in writing before you pay. During Ramadan school days shorten and late-afternoon concentration drops, so the practical move is shifting slots to after Iftar or switching to shorter and more frequent sessions rather than pausing entirely. Because delivery is online there is no travel arrangement to renegotiate. Ramadan weeks are better spent on paper technique and consolidation than on meeting a new topic for the first time, which also makes them cheaper weeks.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-science-double-a.closingHeading: Get one comparable quote before you get three incomparable ones
abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-science-double-a.closingBody: Send the three 4SD0 grades and the most recent marked script from whichever science looks weakest. The trial lesson is free and takes no card details, and most of it is a cold attempt at a short paper section. What comes back is a written plan naming the paper responsible, the marks at stake, what marking is included and the quote in dirhams. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with one lead tutor across all three sciences and specialist cover only where the evidence asks for it. If the week-five re-test shows nothing moved, stopping is a legitimate answer and the scripts stay with you.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The profiles below cover Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects taken in Abu Dhabi schools, listed by specification code rather than by subject label. Each one states the papers taught, the tier prepared for, and the kind of written evidence produced after a month of lessons.

intro.heading: Evidence first: what a month of Edexcel tuition should leave behind
paragraphs: Most tuition decisions in Abu Dhabi are made on a feeling and reviewed on a feeling. A report card says inconsistent, a tutor is booked, and three months later the only new information is that the student seems less anxious about maths. That is worth something, but it is not evidence, and it cannot tell you whether to carry on, change tutor, or move the hours into a different subject entirely. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is unusually easy to audit. Past papers are published. Mark schemes are published. Assessment objectives are printed in the specification. Grades arrive on a 9 to 1 scale with published boundaries for past series. If a tutor cannot show movement against any of that, the movement is probably not there.

This page sets out the artefacts an Edexcel IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi should be able to put in front of you, when each one should exist, and what it means when one is missing. It also explains how to read a marked script yourself. You do not need to be a physicist to see that a child lost eleven marks on Paper 1 of 4PH1 and that nine of them came from questions asking for a calculation with a unit attached. You need the script, the mark scheme, and somebody willing to point at the pattern rather than talk around it.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in Abu Dhabi; visiting tuition is a service we run only in India. That matters here because it changes what the evidence looks like. A shared screen can be annotated and saved. A marked PDF can be stored and compared with the one from three weeks earlier. A specialist in 4CH1 organic chemistry can teach a student in Al Raha Gardens at 17:30 on a Tuesday without forty minutes of the hour disappearing into the drive from the island.

The order of the page is the order an audit would run in. What should exist by week four. How to read a marked 4MA1 script. Where Pearson actually puts the marks, code by code. What the 9 to 1 scale does to a single mark near a boundary. The November and May/June series counted backwards from the entry deadline. What your child's school report measures and what the emirate's inspection rating does not. The honesty line around coursework folders. And the five-subject equivalency rule that will still matter long after the tutoring stops.

Market rates appear where they are useful and are always attributed to whoever published them. Nothing here is a price list from us, and no figure here is a promise about a grade. A tutor who tells you a grade is certain has told you something useful about the tutor.
bullets: Marked past-paper scripts with the Pearson mark scheme beside them, dated and kept
An assessment objective breakdown: which AO lost the marks, not only how many
Specification codes on every plan, because 4MA1 and 4MB1 sit different papers
A four-week written review carrying the next three sessions' targets
Market AED rates attributed to their source, never presented as our own pricing

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Abu Dhabi families arrive at Edexcel from several directions: a British-curriculum school running it from Year 10, a transfer from a Cambridge centre, or a move from an Indian board mid-key-stage. The three routes below are the ones that generate most of the tutoring questions in this emirate, and each has its own evidence trail.

programmes.name: Lower secondary into Edexcel entry
programmes.description: The two years before a specification code appears on a timetable decide how much of Year 10 is spent catching up. Algebraic fluency, rearranging formulae, significant figures, unit conversion and reading a graph are the five skills that reappear in every Edexcel science and maths paper. Tuition at this stage is cheap to buy and expensive to skip, because the same gaps cost marks four years later in a 4PH1 calculation.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi British-curriculum schools differ on when they start the specification. Some begin 4MA1 content in Year 9, others hold to a separate lower-secondary scheme until Year 10. Ask your school's head of key stage which it is before you buy hours, because a Year 9 student already on 4MA1 content should be practising on real papers, not on worksheets.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Graded 9 to 1, assessed entirely by examination in most subjects, and available in a May/June and a November series. Mathematics Specification A is tiered: Foundation reaches grade 5 at the top, Higher runs 9 to 4. Most sciences sit two written papers of unequal length and weight. The specification document, not the textbook, is the authority on what is examinable.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi centres enter candidates through their own examinations officer, which means your child's entry deadlines are the school's deadlines, not Pearson's public ones. The practical consequence is that a decision to change tier or add a subject has to be made weeks earlier than parents expect. Ask the examinations officer for the internal cut-off date in writing.

programmes.name: International A Level, after the IGCSE year
programmes.description: The Edexcel International A Level is modular in structure, which is why Abu Dhabi families who have just finished a linear IGCSE find the vocabulary confusing. Units are examined separately and can in principle be sat across series. The IGCSE grade matters here mainly as a prerequisite and as a predictor of whether the student can carry the unit load.
programmes.countryNote: Ministry of Education equivalency for the British track asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3. That makes the IGCSE year and the sixth-form year one decision, not two, for any family planning on a UAE university.

programmes.name: November series and resit planning
programmes.description: Pearson International GCSE subjects are available in a November series as well as May/June, which gives a student who missed a grade one structured attempt before sixth-form offers firm up. A resit is a different tutoring job from a first sitting: the content is largely known, and the work is almost entirely about paper technique, timing and the two or three topics that produced the lost marks.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Abu Dhabi school enters candidates for the November series, and some will only do so for subjects they already teach. If your school does not, the alternative is a private candidate entry at a centre that accepts external candidates, which carries its own fee and its own earlier deadline. Confirm both before planning the autumn around it.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Edexcel subjects are listed here by specification code, because the code is what decides the papers, the tiering and the mark scheme. A tutor who cannot name the code your child is entered for cannot audit the marks. Weightings move between specification versions, so treat the figures below as the current shape and confirm on the Pearson subject page.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.description: Two written papers of equal weight, each two hours. Higher tier reaches grade 9; Foundation caps at 5. The marks that go missing are rarely in the hardest topics: they are in multi-step problems where a correct method is abandoned, in surds and indices, and in questions that ask for a reason as well as a number. A marked script shows this within one paper.

subjects.name: Mathematics B (4MB1)
subjects.description: A different course from Specification A, with two papers of unequal length and a reach up to grade 9 without tiering. Schools in Abu Dhabi that run B tend to do so for stronger cohorts. Students moving between the two specifications mid-course lose time on content that simply is not shared, which is why the code belongs on the first page of any tutoring plan.

subjects.name: Physics (4PH1)
subjects.description: Two written papers, the first substantially longer and heavier than the second. Practical skills are examined inside the written papers rather than in a separate practical exam. The reliable mark losses are units, significant figures, rearranging an equation under time pressure, and six-mark explanation questions where the physics is right and the sequence is not.

subjects.name: Chemistry (4CH1)
subjects.description: Two written papers following the same shape as Physics. The topic that separates grades in Abu Dhabi cohorts is organic chemistry: homologous series, functional groups and mechanisms are memorisable, which means they are also the fastest marks to recover with structured practice. Moles calculations are the other recurring leak, and they are a maths problem wearing a chemistry hat.

subjects.name: Biology (4BI1)
subjects.description: Two written papers, with data handling and experimental design running through both. Biology scripts lose marks to vocabulary rather than understanding: a student who writes that enzymes are killed instead of denatured has the idea and not the mark. Tutoring here is largely about command terms, named examples and the discipline of answering the question asked.

subjects.name: English Language A (4EA1)
subjects.description: Non-fiction reading and transactional writing in one paper, poetry and prose with imaginative writing in the other, and a coursework route available in place of the second paper at some centres. Marks move when a student stops summarising and starts analysing a writer's choices. The anthology is the single highest-return piece of preparation available in this subject.

subjects.name: English Literature (4ET1)
subjects.description: Set text work where the quotation bank matters more than the essay plan. Abu Dhabi students who read widely often underperform here because they write appreciation rather than argument. Tutoring works on the shape of a paragraph, the integration of short quotations, and timing across questions, which is the most common reason a strong candidate drops a grade.

subjects.name: Business (4BS1) and Economics (4EC1)
subjects.description: Both reward precise definitions and a developed chain of reasoning, and both punish lists. The highest-tariff questions ask for evaluation, and evaluation has a structure a student can be taught in two sessions. Data-response questions in Economics are where numerate students pick up marks that essay-led revision never reaches.

subjects.name: Further Pure Mathematics (4PM1)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 4MA1 or 4MB1 by students heading for maths-heavy sixth-form routes. Calculus, series and coordinate geometry arrive earlier than they would in a standard course, so the gap between a comfortable and an uncomfortable student is usually algebraic fluency rather than new content.

subjects.name: Computer Science (4CP0)
subjects.description: A written theory paper and a practical programming component make this the subject where tutoring has to switch register halfway through. Students lose marks on trace tables, on binary and hexadecimal conversion under time pressure, and on writing code that compiles but does not do what the question asked.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in Abu Dhabi changes the hour a lesson can realistically start far more than it changes the tutor available, because the tutor arrives over a video link. The notes below are about timetable reality: school finish times, the bridge crossings and the point in the evening after which a sixteen-year-old stops absorbing anything.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: A dense cluster of British-curriculum families with school buses arriving between 15:15 and 16:00. A 16:30 start works here on most weekdays, which is early enough to finish a full past paper before the evening fragments into dinner and younger siblings.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Villa households with the longest average school run in the emirate on the island-bound routes. Families here consistently report that a tutor driving from Al Bateen loses most of a 17:00 slot in traffic, which is exactly the cost a video link removes.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Short school runs and late-finishing co-curricular programmes. The practical consequence is a later start: 18:00 and 18:30 sessions fill first here, and a 90-minute block on a Thursday often does more than two weekday hours.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Apartment and older villa stock on the island with short runs to several long-established British schools. Midweek 17:00 slots are the norm, and the limiting factor is usually a shared study space rather than travel.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: Large mainland communities where several schools finish later than the island average. Families here benefit most from the November series conversation, because resit entries have to be planned around a school that may not offer them.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: High-rise living with a bridge dependency in both directions. A fixed, repeating slot matters more here than a flexible one: a session that always runs at 17:30 on Mondays survives the week better than one negotiated each time.

regions.name: Yas Island and Al Falah
regions.note: Newer communities with growing Year 10 and Year 11 cohorts and fewer local subject specialists. These are the postcodes where a parent searching for a Chemistry or Further Pure tutor within driving distance most often finds nobody, and where online coverage changes the answer.

schoolClusters.city: Island and Al Mushrif
schoolClusters.note: Long-established British-curriculum provision with sizeable Year 11 cohorts and internal mock calendars that run earlier than parents expect. Students here usually arrive at tuition with marked mock scripts already in hand, which makes the first diagnostic session faster and cheaper.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Yas
schoolClusters.note: The corridor where most of the emirate's newer British and American provision sits. Demand here concentrates on the sciences and on Mathematics A Higher tier, and the common request is a fixed weekday slot that survives the school bus timetable.

schoolClusters.city: Mainland communities
schoolClusters.note: Mohammed Bin Zayed City, Shakhbout City and Al Shamkha households, where the nearest specialist in a niche Edexcel subject is often in another emirate. These are the families for whom a stated coverage position matters more than a short drive.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-tutor.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every Edexcel request that reaches us from Abu Dhabi. They differ in what evidence they produce, which is the relevant difference on a page about evidence: a diagnostic produces a baseline, a weekly slot produces a trend, and an intensive block produces a before and an after.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one by specification code
modes.description: A fixed slot against one code, running from the diagnostic through to the series. The session shape stays stable so the evidence is comparable week to week: ten minutes reviewing last week's independent work, forty minutes on the targeted topic, and the last ten on a timed exam-style question marked against the real scheme.
bullets: One code per slot, so the mark trail stays attributable
Timed question every session, marked against the published scheme
Written four-week review with the next three targets named
Independent work set in paper format, not worksheet format

modes.title: Diagnostic and paper-audit block
modes.description: Two or three sessions whose only purpose is to find out where the marks go. The student sits a full past paper under timing, the tutor marks it against the scheme, and the output is a written breakdown by topic and assessment objective. Some families buy nothing else, take the breakdown to the school, and are right to.
bullets: Full paper under real timing, not a selection of questions
Mark-by-mark breakdown by topic and assessment objective
A written recommendation on tier, where tiering applies
No commitment to weekly hours afterwards

modes.title: Pre-series intensive
modes.description: A compressed block in the weeks before a May/June or November series, built around papers rather than content. The work is timing, question selection, command-term discipline and the two or three topics the diagnostic named. This is the format where a week of evidence looks dramatic and a term of it looks modest, so expectations are set in writing first.
bullets: Paper-led rather than topic-led, with marking turned around same day
Built around the published timetable for the live series
Targets stated as marks and components, never as a promised grade
Suited to resit candidates whose content knowledge is already in place

sections.heading: What should exist by week four, and what its absence means
paragraphs: Four weeks is the right review point for Edexcel tuition. It is long enough for a tutor to have seen a full paper and short enough that the money still feels recoverable. By the end of it, a set of specific artefacts should exist. If they do not, the problem is almost never that the tutor is unqualified. It is that nobody agreed at the start what the evidence would be, so nothing was collected.

The table below is the list we work to, and it is reproduced here so you can use it on anybody, including us. Notice that none of it requires subject knowledge on your part. You are checking that a document exists, that it is dated, and that it says something specific enough to be wrong. A review note reading good progress in algebra fails that test. A review note reading nine of the twelve lost marks on Paper 1 were in multi-step percentage problems passes it.

The absence column is the useful one. A missing marked script usually means no full paper has been sat, which means the diagnosis is based on the tutor's impression of the student in a lesson. That is a real signal but a weak one, because a student who follows an explanation competently can still be unable to start the question alone under timing. A missing assessment objective breakdown usually means the tutor is marking by feel rather than against the published scheme, which is the difference between tuition and homework help.

One more thing belongs in a four-week review and is almost always left out: a statement of what the tutor now thinks is not the problem. Ruling things out is as valuable as finding them, and it is the clearest sign that somebody has actually looked.

sections.heading: Reading a marked 4MA1 script without being a maths teacher
paragraphs: Open the script and the mark scheme side by side. Ignore the total. Work down the paper writing one of three letters next to each question where marks were lost: N for nothing written, S for started and stopped, or W for a complete answer that was wrong. The distribution of those three letters tells you more about what to buy than the grade does.

A paper full of N marks in the second half is a timing problem, and timing problems are cheap to fix. The student knows more than the mark suggests and is losing marks to pace, question selection and the decision to keep grinding at question nine instead of banking the easy marks on question seventeen. Three sessions of timed paper practice with a visible clock usually moves this, and a tutor who instead starts re-teaching topics has misread the script.

A paper full of S marks is a method problem. The student recognises the question type, begins correctly, and loses the thread at the second or third step. This is the most common pattern in Abu Dhabi Higher tier cohorts and the most responsive to one-to-one work, because the fix is specific: rehearse the full chain on eight similar questions until the sequence survives without prompting. Mark schemes help you see it, because they award method marks separately, and a script collecting method marks and dropping accuracy marks is a different child from one collecting neither.

A paper full of W marks is a knowledge problem, and it is the slowest and most expensive to fix. Confident wrong answers mean a misconception has been practised until it feels right. Expect weeks rather than sessions, and expect the first month of evidence to look flat while the misconception is unpicked. Tell the tutor which pattern you think you are looking at. If they disagree, you will learn something from the reason.
bullets: N marks clustered late in the paper point to pace, not knowledge
S marks mean method marks are landing and accuracy marks are not
W marks mean a misconception has been rehearsed and needs unpicking
Compare two scripts six weeks apart; the letter mix is the progress measure

sections.heading: Where Pearson puts the marks, specification by specification
paragraphs: Parents are told that a subject is hard. Specifications are more specific than that: they say which paper carries the weight, how long each one runs, and what proportion of the available marks sits in the component your child is weakest at. That is the information that should decide how the tutoring hours are split, and almost nobody looks it up.

The table sets out the current shape for the codes Abu Dhabi families ask about most. Treat the detail as a starting point and confirm it on the subject page at qualifications.pearson.com, because Pearson revises specifications and the version your child's centre entered them for is the only one that matters. Where a figure matters to a decision, ask the school's examinations officer to confirm the entry code in writing.

Two patterns are worth drawing out. First, in the sciences the longer first paper usually carries well over half the marks, which means a student who performs better on short-answer recall than on extended explanation is losing marks where the marks actually are. Second, in Mathematics A the two papers are equal, so a strong first paper does not buy any insurance. Students who treat Paper 2 as the easier sitting lose marks to that belief every series.

Tiering is the other decision hiding in the table. Foundation tier in Mathematics A caps the attainable grade at 5. That is sometimes the correct choice and it is always a choice with a ceiling, so it needs to be made on evidence from a sat paper rather than on a prediction from a term of classwork.

sections.heading: The 9 to 1 scale, and what one mark is worth near a boundary
paragraphs: The 9 to 1 scale compresses the top of the range. Grades 9, 8 and 7 occupy the territory that a single A star once covered, which means the distance between a good script and an outstanding one is now measured in a handful of marks. Abu Dhabi parents who remember letter grades consistently underestimate how close the top three grades sit to one another, and overestimate the amount of work needed to cross one boundary.

Boundaries move every series. They are set after the papers are marked, they reflect the difficulty of that particular paper, and they are published for past series rather than announced in advance. Anyone quoting a fixed mark total for a grade 7 is quoting history, not a target. What is stable is the relationship: a few marks reliably separate adjacent grades at the top of the scale, and a handful of recovered marks in one component is a realistic month of work.

This is why the evidence trail matters more than the grade trail. A student moving from 46 to 53 marks on a 4CH1 Paper 1 has done something real, and depending on that series it may or may not show as a grade change. If you only measure grades, you will cancel tuition that is working and continue tuition that is not. Component marks move first; grades follow when enough of them have moved.

The table below is a way of reading a script rather than a boundary table. It describes what each band usually looks like on paper and what the realistic next move is, which is the question a parent is actually asking when they ask what grade is achievable.

sections.heading: Four weeks, week by week: the review cycle that makes tuition auditable
paragraphs: A review cycle is not an administrative overhead; it is the only thing that converts hours into a decision. The shape below is deliberately short, because a twelve-week plan reviewed at week twelve is a twelve-week bet. Four weeks costs less to be wrong about and still produces comparable evidence.

Week one is diagnostic. A full past paper is sat under real timing, at home if necessary, and the tutor marks it against the published scheme rather than estimating. The output is a baseline mark and a topic list, and the student should be told the baseline. Students who are kept away from their own numbers cannot own the plan, and ownership is most of what separates a productive weekly slot from a supervised hour.

Weeks two and three are the work. Each session carries one targeted topic and one timed exam-style question from the real paper bank, marked the same day. Independent work is set in paper format, not as a worksheet, because the skill being built is starting a question alone. By the end of week three there should be three marked pieces to compare, and a visible answer to the question of whether the student can now begin unaided.

Week four is the review and the decision. A dated note states what moved, what did not, what has been ruled out, and the three targets for the next block. Then somebody decides: continue, change the subject allocation, change tutor, or stop. The decision is the point. A plan with no decision point is a subscription.
bullets: Week 1: full paper under timing, marked against the scheme, baseline shared with the student
Weeks 2-3: one topic and one timed question per session, marked same day
Week 4: dated written review naming what moved, what did not, and what was ruled out
Then a decision: continue, reallocate hours, change tutor, or stop

sections.heading: The Pearson series counted backwards from the entry deadline
paragraphs: The question Abu Dhabi families ask in February is whether there is still time. The honest answer depends less on the exam date than on the entry deadline, which sits months earlier and is administered by the school rather than by Pearson. Decisions about tier, about adding a subject, and about whether to sit at all have to be made before that internal cut-off, and parents routinely discover it a fortnight after it has passed.

Pearson publishes International GCSE exams in a May/June and a November series each year, and issues provisional timetables ahead of each one. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. For the preceding series, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are the published anchors; the live timetable at qualifications.pearson.com is the only version that should be planned against, because provisional dates can be revised.

Counted backwards, the pattern is consistent across series. The entry decision sits roughly three months before the first paper. The internal mock window sits six to ten weeks before. The last useful point to start a genuine content rebuild is around twelve weeks out, and after that the work is paper technique rather than new learning. This is not a reason to decline late help, but it is a reason to say plainly what late help can and cannot do.

The table lays this out as a sequence. The dates column deliberately points at the official timetable rather than restating it, because a page that hard-codes a date is wrong the moment Pearson revises one.

sections.heading: What the school report measures, and what an inspection rating does not
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which publishes inspection ratings for the emirate's schools. Those ratings describe a school: leadership, teaching quality, provision, outcomes at cohort level. They are genuinely useful when you are choosing a school, and they tell you almost nothing about whether your particular child is on course for a grade 7 in 4PH1.

The same gap exists inside the school report. A predicted grade is a professional judgement built from classwork, internal assessments and a teacher's experience of previous cohorts. It is not a measurement. Two teachers in the same department, looking at the same student, will sometimes predict a grade apart, and both will be defensible. When a parent brings a predicted grade to a first tutoring session as though it were a reading from an instrument, the conversation starts in the wrong place.

What a report does tell you, if you read it structurally rather than emotionally, is where the school thinks the variance is. Comments about inconsistency usually mean marks fluctuate between assessments, which is a timing or confidence pattern. Comments about effort in class alongside solid assessment marks usually mean a student who performs and does not participate, which is not a tutoring problem. Comments about understanding with poor assessment marks are the pattern most responsive to one-to-one work.

The practical move is to ask the school for the marked internal assessments rather than the summary grades. Those scripts are the same kind of evidence this page has been describing, they already exist, and they cost nothing. A tutor who is given them in session one can skip most of the diagnostic and start work a fortnight earlier.

sections.heading: Coursework folders, draft feedback and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Some Edexcel routes include a coursework component, most visibly the alternative to the second paper in English Language A at centres that offer it. Coursework changes the honesty question from theoretical to immediate, because there is a document sitting on a laptop with a deadline on it and a tutor in the room.

The boundary is not complicated, and it is worth stating in words a fifteen-year-old can repeat. A tutor may teach the skill the task assesses. A tutor may explain the criteria the piece will be marked against. A tutor may read a student's own draft and say which criterion is not being met and why. A tutor may model the technique on a different text entirely, so the student can see what the move looks like before trying it on their own.

A tutor may not supply sentences that end up in the submitted piece, restructure the student's work for them, or hand over material that is then presented as the student's own. The difference is authorship. If the finished piece contains thinking the student cannot explain back to you unprompted, something has gone wrong, and the risk sits with the student rather than the tutor. Centres are required to authenticate coursework, and a malpractice finding is a far worse outcome than a lower honest mark.

Ask any prospective tutor the question directly and listen for a precise answer. A tutor who says they help with coursework and leaves it there has not thought about it. A tutor who distinguishes between feedback on a student's draft and production of content has, and that distinction is the single most useful thing to test for in a first conversation with somebody in this market.
bullets: Teaching the skill, explaining criteria and marking a student's own draft: inside the line
Supplying sentences, restructuring the piece or providing content to submit: outside it
Modelling the technique on a different text is the safe way to demonstrate a move
If the student cannot explain a paragraph back unprompted, treat it as a warning

sections.heading: The five-subject equivalency rule, and why it outlasts the tutoring
paragraphs: Families planning on a UAE university eventually meet Ministry of Education equivalency, and it is better met in Year 10 than in Year 13. For the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Two details catch people out. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the IGCSE count, which means a student taking exactly five subjects including Arabic may find the count does not work. And a ranking tutoring site in this market publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong; the sourced figure is five. If a subject choice is being made partly for equivalency reasons, the arithmetic needs doing before the entries are submitted, not after the results arrive.

The American track has a different shape again, with English proficiency satisfied by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test. No International Baccalaureate points threshold is published in that source, so any figure you are given for IB equivalency should be checked on the Ministry's own pages before it is relied on.

IB Gram does not carry out equivalency or attestation, and no tutoring arrangement affects the outcome of that process. What tuition can do is make the subject-choice conversation an informed one: which five subjects will carry the count, whether a sixth is worth the hours, and whether a Foundation tier entry in Mathematics A still satisfies the grade floor. Those are planning questions, and they are cheaper to answer early. Verify the current rules with the Ministry of Education or the relevant attestation authority before acting on them.

process.title: Tell us the codes, not the subjects
process.description: The first message that helps is one naming the specification codes, the tier where tiering applies, the series your child is entered for and the school. Everything else can wait. With the codes we can tell you within a day whether a specialist in that exact paper is free at the hour you need, and what happens if one is not.

process.title: Free trial lesson, with a written diagnostic
process.description: The trial is a working session, not a sales call. The tutor sets a timed question from the real paper bank, marks it against the published scheme, and writes up what the script shows. You keep that write-up whether or not you book anything further, because it is useful on its own.

process.title: Baseline paper in week one
process.description: A full past paper is sat under real timing and marked against the scheme. The baseline mark, the topic breakdown and the assessment objective split are shared with you and with the student. This is the number every later claim about progress gets compared against, so it is established before the hours start.

process.title: Weekly slot with same-day marking
process.description: One code per slot, one targeted topic, one timed question marked the same day. Independent work arrives in paper format. The session shape stays constant on purpose, because a stable format is what makes week four comparable to week one rather than merely later than it.

process.title: Four-week review and a decision
process.description: A dated note sets out what moved in marks, what did not, what has been ruled out, and three targets for the next block. Then a decision gets made: continue, move hours to a different subject, change tutor, or stop. If the evidence does not support continuing, we say so.

process.title: Coverage stated honestly, including the gaps
process.description: Some Edexcel codes have thin specialist coverage at Abu Dhabi evening hours. Where that is true we say which code, what the realistic wait is, and what the alternative looks like, including a tutor in a different time zone if that is what covers the paper. You decide with the limitation in front of you.

whyPoints.title: The code is on the plan
whyPoints.description: Every plan names the specification code and the tier, because 4MA1 Higher and 4MB1 are different courses with different papers. A tutor working from the subject name rather than the code can be teaching content your child will never be examined on, and nobody finds out until a mock.

whyPoints.title: Marking against the published scheme
whyPoints.description: Work is marked against the real Pearson mark scheme rather than by impression. That is what makes method marks and accuracy marks visible separately, and it is the only way to tell a student who nearly had it from one who did not start.

whyPoints.title: Evidence you keep
whyPoints.description: Marked scripts, the assessment objective breakdown and the dated four-week review are yours. You can take them to the school, to a second opinion, or to a different tutor. Evidence that only lives in the provider's account is not evidence you can act on.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery, chosen on the merits
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. A family in Al Raha Gardens gets a specialist in the exact paper rather than whoever is within a twenty-minute drive, and the forty minutes a visiting tutor would spend in traffic stays in the lesson.

whyPoints.title: Stated coverage limits
whyPoints.description: Where no UAE-based specialist covers a code at the hour you want, we say so and name the alternative instead of quietly substituting a generalist. A disclosed limitation is cheaper for everyone than a discovered one, and it is the thing competitor pages in this market consistently leave out.

whyPoints.title: No grade promises, and attributed figures
whyPoints.description: No target is stated as a guaranteed outcome, and every AED figure on our pages is attributed to whoever published it. Market rates belong to the market. A tutor who is certain about a grade before seeing a script is telling you about their sales process.

faqs.question: How will I know after four weeks whether an Edexcel tutor is actually working?
faqs.answer: Ask for four things: the baseline paper mark from week one, the marked scripts since, the assessment objective breakdown, and a dated note naming three targets for the next block. Then compare the component marks, not the predicted grade. Grades move after enough component marks have moved, so a student going from 46 to 53 on a 4CH1 paper has made real progress even if the grade label has not changed yet. If none of those documents exists, the honest conclusion is not that the tutoring failed but that nobody agreed what success would look like.

faqs.question: My daughter's school in Khalifa City teaches 4MA1 Higher tier. Should she move down to Foundation?
faqs.answer: Decide it on a sat paper rather than on classwork. Foundation tier in Mathematics A caps the attainable grade at 5, which is sometimes exactly right and is always a ceiling. Have her sit a full Higher paper under timing and get it marked against the published scheme. If she is collecting method marks and dropping accuracy marks across the paper, Higher is usually still the better entry with targeted work. If most questions are blank in the second half, that is a pace problem and also fixable. If answers are confident and wrong throughout, the tier conversation becomes genuine. Ask the examinations officer for the internal cut-off date before deciding.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Edexcel Mathematics A and Mathematics B on my son's timetable?
faqs.answer: They are separate specifications, not two names for the same course. Mathematics A, code 4MA1, is tiered: Foundation reaches grade 5 and Higher runs from 9 to 4, with two equally weighted papers. Mathematics B, code 4MB1, is single tier to grade 9 with two papers of unequal length and some content that Specification A does not share. Schools in Abu Dhabi choose between them for cohort reasons. The practical point is that a tutor must know which code your son is entered for, because preparing for the wrong one wastes hours on content that will not appear.

faqs.question: Can a tutor show me exactly which assessment objective my child is losing marks on?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a reasonable thing to insist on. Every Edexcel specification sets out its assessment objectives and the share of marks each carries. A tutor marking against the published scheme can total the lost marks by objective rather than by topic, which answers a different and more useful question: is this a recall gap, an application gap, or an analysis gap. Recall gaps respond to drilling. Application gaps need rehearsed method chains. Analysis gaps need modelled answers and comparison. Topic-level feedback alone cannot tell you which of the three you are buying hours for.

faqs.question: Our Physics teacher says 4PH1 Paper 1 carries most of the marks. Is that right?
faqs.answer: In the current shape of the specification the first paper is substantially longer and heavier than the second, so the broad statement holds. Check the exact figures on the subject page at qualifications.pearson.com for the version your child's centre entered, because Pearson revises specifications and only the entered version matters. The useful consequence is strategic: a student who is stronger on short recall than on extended explanation is losing marks in the component where most of the marks live, and the hours should follow the weighting rather than the comfort.

faqs.question: A grade came back a single mark below the boundary. What can an Abu Dhabi family do about it?
faqs.answer: Go through the school, quickly. Post-results services, including a review of marking, are requested by the centre rather than by parents, and the windows are short and published by Pearson for each series. Ask the examinations officer the same day for the deadline and the fee position. Understand what a review does: it checks that the mark scheme was applied correctly, and it can move a mark down as well as up. In parallel, ask about the next series as a contingency, because a resit entry also has a deadline that sits months before the paper.

faqs.question: Does Pearson publish mark schemes a parent can read without a teacher account?
faqs.answer: Past papers and mark schemes for Edexcel International GCSE are published on the Pearson qualifications site, and a parent can read them. That matters because it makes tuition auditable by somebody with no subject training. Open the script and the scheme side by side and you can see where method marks were awarded and accuracy marks lost. We reference and link official material rather than reproducing it, since the papers and schemes are Pearson's copyright. Ask your tutor to work from the official version for the entered specification rather than from a third-party summary.

faqs.question: Is the November series a sensible place to resit one Edexcel subject?
faqs.answer: Often yes, provided the entry route exists. Pearson runs International GCSE in a November series as well as May and June, and the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Two practical conditions apply. First, your child's school has to enter candidates for that series in that subject, and not all Abu Dhabi centres do. Second, a resit is a technique job rather than a content job, so the preparation looks different: timed papers, question selection and the two or three topics the original script actually lost marks on.

faqs.question: My son is in Year 10 at a British school on Saadiyat Island. Is it too early for paper practice?
faqs.answer: No, and starting early is the cheapest intervention available. A Year 10 student can sit a full past paper on the content covered so far, and the point is not the mark. It is the pattern: whether questions are left blank, started and abandoned, or answered confidently and wrongly. That pattern is stable enough to plan against and it changes what you buy. Early paper work also removes the novelty shock that costs marks in a first mock. Ask your school whether the specification is already being taught, since some Abu Dhabi schools begin Edexcel content in Year 9.

faqs.question: What should a four-week written review from a tutor actually contain?
faqs.answer: Five things. The baseline mark and the current mark on comparable papers. A breakdown of lost marks by topic and by assessment objective. A statement of what has been ruled out, which is as useful as what has been found. Three named targets for the next block, phrased as components and marks rather than as a grade. And a recommendation, including the recommendation to stop or to move hours elsewhere if that is what the evidence says. A note saying good progress, keep going is not a review.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor in Abu Dhabi is permitted to teach privately?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a work permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask directly whether a permit is held, and apply through the official MoHRE route at mohre.gov.ae if you are the one tutoring.

faqs.question: What is a tutor allowed to do with my daughter's English coursework folder?
faqs.answer: Teach the skill the task assesses, explain the criteria it will be marked against, read her own draft and name which criterion is not yet met, and model the technique on a different text so she can see the move before attempting it. What a tutor must not do is supply sentences that end up in the submission, restructure the piece on her behalf, or provide material she then presents as her own. The test is authorship: if she cannot explain a paragraph back to you unprompted, treat that as a warning rather than a success.

faqs.question: Does ADEK's inspection rating for our school tell me anything about my child's grades?
faqs.answer: Not directly. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and publishes inspection outcomes, which describe leadership, teaching and provision at school level. That is the right information for choosing a school and the wrong information for predicting one student's 4PH1 result. For that you need marked scripts from your own child. A useful move is to ask the school for the marked internal assessments rather than the summary grades, since they already exist, cost nothing and let a tutor skip most of the diagnostic.

faqs.question: How many of my son's Edexcel subjects count towards UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, alongside one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. A site ranking in this market states six subjects, which does not match the sourced rule. Do the arithmetic before entries are submitted, and verify the current position with the Ministry of Education, since IB Gram neither performs nor influences equivalency.

faqs.question: Nobody local teaches Edexcel Accounting at the hour we need. What happens then?
faqs.answer: We tell you that, name the code, and set out the options rather than substituting a generalist. Usually there are three. Wait for a UAE-based specialist slot to open, which we can usually estimate within a day. Take a tutor in another time zone whose availability fits an Abu Dhabi evening, which works well for 4AC1 because the subject is highly structured. Or reallocate the hours to a subject where a specialist is free and the marks are more recoverable. Thin coverage on niche codes is real in this emirate, and a disclosed limit beats a discovered one.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both 4CH1 and 4BI1 for the same student in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth testing rather than assuming. A tutor with a strong background across the sciences can run both, and there is a real benefit in one person seeing the whole picture, particularly where the underlying problem is data handling or extended explanation rather than subject content. The risk is depth: organic chemistry and genetics reward specialists. The practical approach is to run a diagnostic paper in each, look at where the lost marks actually sit, and split the codes between two tutors only if the breakdowns point in different directions.

abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Start with one paper, then decide
abu-dhabi/edexcel-igcse-tutor.closingBody: The cheapest useful thing an Abu Dhabi family can do this week is have their child sit one full Edexcel past paper under real timing and get it marked against the published scheme. Everything on this page follows from that document: the tier decision, the topic list, the hours, and whether tuition is the right purchase at all. Tell us the specification codes and the series, take the free trial lesson, and keep the written diagnostic whichever way you decide. If the evidence says the hours should go somewhere else, we would rather say so in week four than in week twelve.

intro.heading: What experience actually buys in an IB course
paragraphs: Searches for an experienced IB tutor in Abu Dhabi almost always begin after a disappointing report. The parent has read the comments, seen a 4 where a 6 was predicted, and concluded that the missing ingredient is somebody who has done this before. That conclusion is usually right. What goes wrong next is the test applied to it: experience gets measured in years, because years are the only number anybody volunteers, and years are the weakest of the available signals.

A teacher who has delivered the same Standard Level course in the same school for twelve years has taught one syllabus twelve times to a fairly narrow intake. A tutor four years into private work, carrying three Higher Level subjects across six different schools and two curricula, has seen far more ways for a mark to disappear. Neither is automatically the better choice for your child. They are different kinds of experienced, and the difference is only visible if you ask a better question than how long.

There are four questions that separate the two. Which programme, which subject, which level, and how many cohorts carried through to a final examination series. A tutor who answers all four without hesitating has the experience you are paying for. One who answers with a decade and a list of school names has told you nothing you can check. The rest of this page turns those four questions into something you can run in ten minutes over a trial lesson, alongside the AED bands the Abu Dhabi market actually charges for each level of experience and who published those numbers.

The second half of the page covers ground that applies whoever you hire: the ADEK professional-ethics position on teachers tutoring their own students, the MoHRE private tuition work permit that private tutoring in the UAE now runs on, and the academic-honesty boundary around internal assessment work. An experienced tutor knows precisely how marks are awarded, which makes that boundary more tempting to cross, not less. A parent buying experience should know where the line sits before the first invoice rather than after a school has raised a question about authorship. The page also sets out the stopping condition, because the hardest decision in private tutoring is not who to hire but when to stop paying somebody pleasant who is not moving anything.

One practical note on delivery, because it changes who is available to you. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. The consequence is the point: your child is matched to somebody who has taught the exact subject at the exact level, rather than whoever has genuine Higher Level experience and happens to live within a twenty-minute drive of Khalifa City.
