process.title: Say which board, version and tier
process.description: Send the specification code from the statement of entry, the tier where the subject is tiered, and the practical route in any science. Matching then happens on who has prepared candidates for those exact papers rather than on who describes themselves as experienced, which is the only version of the word that means anything.

process.title: Test the experience in the free trial
process.description: Thirty minutes at no charge with the matched tutor, no card details taken, one trial per family. Hand them a marked script and ask what they see. Ask what changed in the current specification version. Ask them to mark one answer aloud and name the criterion. Three questions, four minutes, and a clear answer either way.

process.title: Commission a diagnosis, not a term
process.description: The first engagement is a script review or a four-session block, not an open-ended weekly slot. It ends with a written note naming the component, the habit behind the loss and the marks at stake. If that note is general, the experience was not what it was described as, and we match again.

process.title: Agree the calendar, including Ramadan
process.description: Settle the plan against the Abu Dhabi school year before the first paid session: when mocks fall, when the entry deadline closes, how timing changes during Ramadan, and when study leave begins. Experienced tutors raise this unprompted. A plan that assumes a fixed slot from September to June will not survive February.

process.title: Review on evidence, then narrow or stop
process.description: At four sessions you should hold a before and after on one question type. At eight, the error rate on that type should be falling. Hours then move off the component or the engagement ends. Open-ended tuition to the final day of the series is common in this market and is rarely what the evidence supports.

whyPoints.title: Experience is matched as a measurement
whyPoints.description: We match on series prepared for, specification version read, board worked, tier taught and practical route covered. Those five facts are what make long service useful, and they are checkable in a trial lesson, which a claim about years is not.

whyPoints.title: Annotation against criteria, every script
whyPoints.description: Marked work comes back with the criterion named, the line where a chain broke identified, and the command word the student actually answered flagged. That is what an experienced marker produces, and it is the difference between a diagnosis you can act on and marking you cannot.

whyPoints.title: No examiner claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: Current examiner status for an individual is not something we can verify, so we do not publish it. Several pages competing for this search do, in the past tense and without dates, and use it to imply access to boundaries and papers that nobody has. Omitting an unverifiable credential is the only honest option.

whyPoints.title: Process forecasts, not grade promises
whyPoints.description: You will be told which component is losing marks after session one and shown a scored repeat attempt by session four. You will not be promised a grade, because thresholds are set by the board after the papers are marked. A guarantee in this market is a claim about something the seller does not control.

whyPoints.title: Built around the Abu Dhabi year
whyPoints.description: Plans are set against mock season, the entry deadline for the entered series, Ramadan timing and study leave, because those are what actually break a schedule here. Families in Al Samha, Al Ghadeer and Al Jubail Island feel the timing constraints most, and an online slot is what makes a late-evening start hold.

whyPoints.title: The refusals are published
whyPoints.description: No copied board documents, no claimed approval from ADEK, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, no production of assessed work, and no paid tutoring of a student by a teacher at their own school. A page that lists what a provider will not do is more useful than one listing what it says it is.

faqs.question: What should I actually count when a tutor says they are experienced at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Five things, none of which is years. How many examination series they have prepared candidates for. Whether they have read the current specification version your child's cohort sits. Which boards they have worked, since Cambridge, Pearson and OxfordAQA structure the same subject differently. Which tiers they have taught, because Core and Extended fail in different ways. And which practical route in the sciences, because preparing alternative-to-practical candidates is not preparing anybody for a timed practical. Ask for those five and the word stops being decorative.

faqs.question: How can I tell from a marked paper whether a tutor knows what they are doing?
faqs.answer: Look at the annotation. An experienced marker names the criterion a mark was awarded or withheld against, circles the line where a calculation chain broke rather than the wrong final answer, separates a method loss from a knowledge gap, and flags where the student answered a different command word from the one printed. A less experienced one ticks, crosses and writes that more detail is needed. Ask for one six-mark answer to be re-annotated with the criteria named: a tutor who marks to the scheme can do that on the spot.

faqs.question: Does it matter if my child's tutor learned the subject from an older version of the syllabus?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the hardest staleness for a parent to spot, because nothing about the teaching sounds uncertain. Revisions move content between papers, add or withdraw topics, change component weightings and change which formulae are printed rather than memorised. A tutor working from memory will teach confidently and partly wrongly. Ask which version the cohort is examined on, what changed from the previous one, and where the document lives. The boards publish current specifications on their own sites, so there is no excuse for guessing.

faqs.question: Is a tutor experienced with UK GCSE equally experienced with IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. The qualifications are close relatives and the assessment is not identical, so a tutor who assumes equivalence will be confident about paper structures that do not apply to your child's entry. The same caution applies in reverse to post-16 experience: a tutor used to sixth-formers tends to pitch above the specification, teaching the mechanism behind a result the paper never asks for while marks continue to leak on the question that is set. Neither background disqualifies anyone. Treating the transfer as obvious is the warning sign.

faqs.question: How much does experience add to an hourly rate in this market?
faqs.answer: Published UAE figures show the spread clearly. Budget online tutoring, often by university students, is advertised from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour. Qualified subject tutors online sit at roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with one UAE agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150. IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted between about AED 200 and AED 450, with one agency publishing AED 270, and named premium tutors reach AED 650. Those are other organisations' published 2026 figures rather than IB Gram's charges; ours is agreed after the free trial.

faqs.question: Should I pay more for a tutor who says they used to mark papers for the board?
faqs.answer: Possibly, for one specific reason: applying a mark scheme professionally sharpens how someone explains why a fluent answer scored in the middle band. Test that rather than the title by asking them to mark an answer aloud, criterion by criterion. What marking experience does not confer is access to anything unreleased: no advance sight of papers, no knowledge of boundaries before they are set, no influence on a result. If the claim arrives with any hint of inside knowledge, treat it as a reason to end the conversation rather than to pay a premium.

faqs.question: When in the Abu Dhabi school year is it hardest to book an experienced tutor?
faqs.answer: From November through February, which is exactly when the evidence a tutor needs becomes available. Mocks are sat and returned in that window, so demand across the emirate concentrates at once and the specialists book out first. A family starting to look in January is usually choosing from what is left. The practical move is to arrange a single script review in September or October, when nothing is urgent, and keep the relationship open rather than beginning the search when the mock grade arrives.

faqs.question: How should tuition work around Ramadan in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Plan it in advance rather than renegotiating it in the first week. School days shorten, household routines move and evening study happens at different hours, which reliably breaks a plan built in January around a fixed afternoon slot. Three arrangements work: shifting sessions to post-Iftar timing, moving to shorter and more frequent contacts, or pausing deliberately with set work to be marked. An experienced tutor raises the question unprompted, and that is one of the easier ways to tell whether they have taught in this market before.

faqs.question: Can an experienced tutor tell me how much the grade will improve?
faqs.answer: No, and an answer to that question should lower your confidence rather than raise it. Grade thresholds are set by the board after a series has been marked, so a student near a boundary is near it in a way nobody can resolve in advance. What an experienced tutor can forecast is process: the component losing marks named after session one, a timed repeat attempt scored by session four, and method errors on a targeted question type falling within three or four attempts. Ask for those commitments in writing instead.

faqs.question: My child sits Cambridge in science and Pearson in maths. Do I need two tutors?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily two, but you do need a tutor who has prepared candidates for each board rather than one who treats them as interchangeable. The structural differences are real: grade scales, how tiering works, how practical science is assessed, how many papers a subject carries and where the assessment weight sits. Ask directly which boards they have prepared candidates for and accept a straight no on either. A tutor who declines a board they do not know is demonstrating exactly the judgement you were trying to buy.

faqs.question: Why does Cambridge's timetable zone matter when planning revision?
faqs.answer: Because the timetable your revision sequence is built from has to be the right one. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong timetable was used. For a tutor building a block backwards from paper order, using a timetable found online rather than the one for your child's centre can sequence the final sessions around the wrong paper.

faqs.question: Is an experienced tutor worth it if my child is only two grades off target?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and for a narrower purchase than families expect. A small gap is almost always technique rather than knowledge, and technique is where experience pays most: command-word discipline, method marks claimed, pacing, graph conventions. That is a short block of four to eight sessions with a clear measure, not a term of weekly slots. A less experienced tutor will cover content, which is the wrong work for this gap and will produce pleasant sessions and a flat mark. Buy a script review first and decide from what it says.

faqs.question: What questions should I ask a tutor's previous family if I get a reference?
faqs.answer: Two, both about evidence rather than satisfaction. What did you receive in writing after each session, and did it name a component. And did you ever see a repeat attempt at the same question type, marked before and after. A family who can answer both has worked with someone who diagnosed and measured. A warm reference with no documents behind it tells you the sessions were enjoyable, which is worth something and is not the thing you were asking about.

faqs.question: Does an experienced private tutor in the UAE still need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and experience makes no difference to it. Private tutoring in the UAE runs through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which introduced the private tuition work permit. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask to see it before the first paid session.

faqs.question: Can an experienced tutor improve my child's coursework draft directly?
faqs.answer: They can give written feedback on it and they must not rewrite it. Assessed work has to be the candidate's own: a tutor may teach the skills, explain the criteria, discuss a plan and question a draft, but supplying text or editing until the sentences are no longer the student's is malpractice, and the consequence lands on the candidate rather than the adult who helped. An experienced tutor states that at the first session instead of negotiating it at eleven at night in April, and says it to the student directly.

faqs.question: How long does it take to find an experienced tutor for a scarce subject like 0606?
faqs.answer: Longer than for mathematics or English, and the honest answer is that it depends on the week. Additional Mathematics, the separate sciences at the top of Extended and some language specifications have thin supply in the Gulf timezone, and mock season tightens it further. If no specialist is free we will say so rather than offer a generalist as a substitute, and we will say what the realistic wait looks like. A page in this market that never discloses a coverage limit is concealing one.

abu-dhabi/experienced-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Hand over a marked script and watch what happens
abu-dhabi/experienced-igcse-tutor.closingBody: The quickest test of an experienced IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi costs nothing and takes thirty minutes. Find the most recent marked paper, note the specification code, the tier and the practical route, and take the free trial lesson, one per family with no card details taken. Then ask three questions: what do you see in this script, what changed in the current specification version, and would you mark this answer aloud naming the criterion. The answers will tell you what years of service never could. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, anywhere in the emirate, and the rate is agreed after you have seen the teaching.

abu-dhabi/expert-ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: Each profile below states the courses that tutor teaches and the level they teach them at. Read the level, not the subject. Chemistry HL and Chemistry SL share a syllabus core and diverge completely in paper structure, and a tutor comfortable with one is not automatically useful for the other.

intro.heading: Expertise in IB tutoring is a supply problem before it is a quality problem
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi has a reasonable tutoring market and a lopsided one. For Standard Level Business Management, Economics, Biology or English, a family on the island can find three competent people within a week and choose on price. For Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Chemistry, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Computer Science, Theory of Knowledge supervision or Spanish B, the same family can spend a month asking and come back with nobody who has taught the course to completion. The word expert is doing the work of describing that second category.

This matters because it explains the AED figures you are being quoted. Market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online in the UAE run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist bands sit higher, around AED 200 to AED 450 and above in Bestimate's 2026 survey, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. None of those are our prices. The spread between them is almost entirely a scarcity spread, not a talent spread.

The practical consequence for a parent is that the question changes. Instead of asking whether a tutor is good, ask how many people could do this specific job and how quickly one of them is free. For Standard Level support the answer is many and soon, and you should negotiate. For Higher Level sciences in the weeks before a session the answer is few and not soon, and the right move is to book early rather than to pay more later.

What an expert actually does that a competent generalist does not is diagnostic rather than explanatory. Anybody who knows Chemistry can explain an enthalpy cycle. Somebody who has taught Chemistry Higher Level through several Diploma cohorts can look at a marked Paper 2, say that four of the six lost marks went to command-term handling rather than to chemistry, and name which data booklet section the student keeps forgetting exists. That difference is invisible on a website and obvious within forty minutes of a session.

The rest of this page is built around that distinction. A coverage table showing which Abu Dhabi specialisms are thin and what happens when nobody local covers them. A Higher Level against Standard Level comparison, because the hours differ as much as the content. An hours-and-cost estimate by starting point. A command-term table, which is where expertise is visible. And an honest section on when buying a specialist is the wrong purchase. IB Gram delivers all of it as one-to-one online tuition; it does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, because the whole point of the format is reaching the person who teaches your child's course rather than the person who can reach your door.

abu-dhabi/expert-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: Specialist supply inside Abu Dhabi varies by programme as sharply as it varies by subject. The Diploma draws most of the market's experienced people, the Middle Years Programme is under-served relative to its enrolment, and the Primary Years Programme is served mostly by generalists.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Three Higher Level and three Standard Level subjects, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity, service. Papers are externally marked, Internal Assessments are internally marked and externally moderated, and the core can add up to three points. Almost all genuine subject specialists in this market work here, which is why Diploma rates sit above every other programme.
programmes.countryNote: An Abu Dhabi Diploma student carrying Physics HL, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL and Chemistry HL is asking for the three scarcest specialisms in the emirate at once. Families who treat that as one search get stuck; families who treat it as three separate searches, started early, usually fill all three.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria scored 0-8, with interdisciplinary units and a Personal Project in the final year. There are no external papers for most students, so expertise here means fluency with criterion wording and with the school's own task design rather than with past papers.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years specialists are the real gap in Abu Dhabi. Plenty of tutors will take a Year 9 student and teach them the content well while marking out of a hundred, which leaves a parent no closer to knowing whether criterion C or criterion D is the weak one. Ask any prospective tutor to name the four criteria for the subject before you book.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry with no graded examinations and no external assessment. Support is almost always numeracy fluency, reading stamina, written expression or the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education strands that sit alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools.
programmes.countryNote: This is the one programme where a specialist premium is usually not worth paying in Abu Dhabi. A capable primary teacher who understands inquiry-based reporting will do more for a Year 4 student than a Diploma subject expert, and costs considerably less per hour.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Assessment blends Diploma subject grades with the career-related component's own requirements.
programmes.countryNote: Specialist cover for the Career-related Programme inside Abu Dhabi is effectively nil because so few schools in the emirate run it. Any realistic match for the reflective project or the personal and professional skills course will be an online one, and should be searched for a term ahead.

abu-dhabi/expert-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: The list below is ordered by how hard the specialism is to fill in Abu Dhabi rather than by popularity. For each, the note describes the expertise that distinguishes a specialist from a well-informed generalist.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The scarcest Higher Level specialism in the emirate. Expertise shows in extended-response marking: a specialist knows that a correct answer with no stated principle scores partially, and trains the student to name the physics before doing the algebra. HL adds the option topic and a second long paper.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium carry the Higher Level marks. A specialist steers the Internal Assessment towards a measurable, repeatable variable in the first fortnight, which is the decision that determines the eventual criterion scores more than anything done later.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level proof and calculus make this the subject where generalist tutoring fails fastest. Paper 3 is an extended investigative response and needs separate practice; a tutor who has never prepared a student for it will teach the content and leave that paper untouched.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Few Abu Dhabi tutors cover this properly. The internal solution development work needs supervision on scope and documentation, and the HL extension into abstract data structures is where students who coded confidently at Middle Years level stall.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Supervision rather than teaching: a prescribed-title essay of 1,600 words plus an exhibition of three objects. Specialist help is questioning until the knowledge question is genuinely answerable. Nobody may write any part of it, which makes an unskilled tutor actively unhelpful here.

subjects.name: Spanish B and French B
subjects.description: Group 2 cover beyond Arabic is thin in Abu Dhabi. Assessment runs through an individual oral built on a stimulus, two written papers and listening. A specialist rehearses the oral under timed conditions rather than practising conversation.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Three assessed components: the comparative study, the process portfolio and the exhibition. Expertise is in the written and curatorial parts, which carry most of the marks and which students who are strong studio practitioners routinely under-serve.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies must be deployed as evidence rather than recited. A specialist drills the structure of an answer that earns the critical-thinking marks, and knows the HL extension requirements, which are commonly taught thinly in schools short of staff.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Widely covered in Abu Dhabi, so negotiate. Expertise is in diagram precision and in the Internal Assessment commentaries, which are marked against set criteria and are routinely written as news summaries rather than as applied analysis.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The most plentiful science specialism locally. Content volume is the enemy, not difficulty. A specialist works from the syllabus understandings and the command terms rather than from a textbook chapter order, which is how students in Abu Dhabi most often meet the course.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: A separate specialism from IB subject teaching, because the stream the school placed your child in determines everything. Abu Dhabi students also sit the emirate's mandatory Arabic requirement alongside their IB course, and the two are not the same work.

abu-dhabi/expert-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: Abu Dhabi's tutoring demand is not spread evenly across the emirate. The notes below describe what families in each area most often ask for and what their week looks like, because that determines which slots are available and therefore which specialists are reachable.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Dense high-rise family housing with a young Diploma cohort. Demand concentrates on Mathematics and the sciences, and the 6pm to 8pm window fills first because so many households share the same school-bus timetable.

regions.name: Al Maryah Island
regions.note: Small residential population with a working-parent profile, which pushes requests towards later evening slots and weekend mornings. Those are the easiest slots in which to reach a specialist based outside the UAE.

regions.name: Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Long-established apartment district close to the Corniche schools. Requests skew towards Middle Years criterion support and Arabic streams rather than Diploma sciences, which locally are easier to fill here than elsewhere.

regions.name: Masdar City
regions.note: A small, technically minded community where Computer Science and Physics requests appear disproportionately often. Both are among the hardest specialisms to fill inside the emirate, so families here benefit most from booking a term ahead.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Al Zeina and Al Muneera families with a heavy after-school activity load. The practical constraint is not geography but a crowded weekday evening, which makes a fixed weekly slot more valuable than a flexible one.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Large mainland catchment with mixed curricula and comparatively few IB places nearby. Families here are often preparing a Middle Years student for a Diploma transfer, which is a planning conversation rather than a revision one.

regions.name: Al Shamkha
regions.note: Fast-growing community at the edge of the city with the thinnest local tutor supply of any area on this list. Online delivery is not a preference here; it is the difference between a subject specialist and nobody.

regions.name: Al Falah
regions.note: Villa community with a strong Arabic-stream demand alongside the international curriculum, and school-run patterns that make the 4pm hour unusable for most households.

schoolClusters.city: Corniche, Al Khalidiyah and Al Bateen
schoolClusters.note: The oldest school catchment in the city, with several long-established international schools within a few minutes of each other. Requests from this cluster lean towards Middle Years criterion work and Group 2 languages.

schoolClusters.city: Yas Island, Al Raha Beach and Al Falah
schoolClusters.note: Newer schools with newer cohorts, where Diploma science demand has grown faster than the local specialist supply. This is the cluster where families most often report a long search for Higher Level Physics or Chemistry.

schoolClusters.city: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Shakhbout City
schoolClusters.note: Mainland communities with mixed curricula and a steady flow of students transferring into IB programmes from British and Indian curriculum schools. Transition planning is the dominant request.

modes.description: One subject, one level, the same tutor every week over live video. Work is set and marked between sessions, so the hour itself is diagnostic rather than administrative. For a scarce specialism this is the format that holds a slot: the tutor's Tuesday 6pm is yours for the term rather than contested each week.

sections.heading: What Abu Dhabi is short of, and what happens when nobody local covers it
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market publishes a coverage limit. It is the most useful thing a tutoring platform can tell an Abu Dhabi parent, because the gap between plentiful and scarce is where the quoted AED figure comes from and where a month gets wasted. The table below is a working picture of availability inside the emirate, written as a disclosure rather than a sales point.

Read the fallback column carefully. When a subject has no specialist available inside the UAE, there are three honest options and one dishonest one. The honest options are to wait for a named slot to open, to work with a specialist based outside the UAE who teaches the course and schedules to Gulf Standard Time, or to narrow the brief to something a generalist can genuinely do well, such as timed practice marking. The dishonest option, common in this market, is to match the family to a near-enough tutor and let them find out.

An out-of-UAE specialist is not a compromise for a Diploma student in the way parents often assume. The course is identical worldwide, the papers are identical, the mark schemes are identical. The only real variables are the time zone, which is a scheduling question, and familiarity with the UAE's mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education strands, which matters for those subjects and not at all for Chemistry.

Match times in the table are what a family should plan around rather than promises. They are driven by how many people teach the course and what time of year it is. The same Higher Level Chemistry request that fills in a week in October can take three in late February, because every Diploma family in the emirate is making it at once.

sections.heading: Higher Level and Standard Level are different jobs at different prices
paragraphs: Parents routinely ask for a tutor in a subject. Tutors routinely quote for a subject at a level. The gap between those two sentences produces most of the mismatches reported after a first month, because the Higher Level course in any Diploma subject is not the Standard Level course with extra homework.

The content differs, obviously. Less obviously, the assessment architecture differs: Higher Level students sit additional papers, face longer extended responses, meet an option or extension topic that Standard Level students never see, and in several subjects have a different Internal Assessment weighting against a larger total. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level carries a third paper that is an extended investigation and that needs its own preparation, which is the single most common thing an unprepared tutor overlooks.

The hours differ as a direct consequence. A Standard Level student recovering from a 4 to a 5 is usually a content-gap problem solvable in a term of weekly hours. A Higher Level student aiming from a 5 to a 7 is a technique-and-depth problem that needs marked work every week over two terms, because the final marks are in the extended responses and those improve only through being marked repeatedly.

The table sets the two side by side as a tutoring brief rather than as a syllabus summary. Use it to sanity-check any quote: a tutor who prices Higher Level identically to Standard Level has either not understood the brief or is not planning to mark extended responses.

sections.heading: How many hours a subject actually needs, from where your child is now
paragraphs: The most expensive mistake in this market is buying hours by the month without an estimate of how many are needed. Monthly packages circulating in the UAE sit around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, and Bestimate's survey puts a weekly hour at AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Those are market figures, not ours. What they do not tell you is whether your child needs twelve hours or sixty.

A usable estimate starts from the marked evidence rather than from the target. A student losing marks on content has a different hour requirement from one losing them on command terms, even with the same grade on the report. The first is bounded by how much syllabus is missing. The second is bounded by how many pieces of extended writing can be marked before the examination, which is a calendar problem.

The table gives planning ranges by starting point. They assume one subject, one level, marked work between sessions, and a start early enough to use the time. Compress the same movement into six weeks and the hours per week roughly double while the total gain falls, which is the arithmetic behind the advice to book in the autumn.

Use the indicative totals as a budget sanity check, not as a quotation. Multiply your own quoted hourly figure by the session count in the row that matches your child's marked evidence. If the result is a number you would not spend, the honest options are a narrower brief, a shorter block on the single weakest component, or a conversation with the school about what it can provide first.

sections.heading: The diagnostic hour: what a specialist does in the first session
paragraphs: Expertise is easiest to recognise in the first sixty minutes, before anybody has taught anything. A specialist treats the first session as an assessment of the student rather than a demonstration of themselves, and the shape of it is fairly consistent across subjects.

They ask for marked work and read it rather than glancing at the grade. They pick a question the student got partially right, not one they got wrong, because partial credit is where the diagnosis lives. They ask the student to talk through their working aloud, which separates a conceptual gap from a communication gap faster than any question could. They check whether the student knows what the command term in that question was asking for, and whether they know which paper that question came from and what that paper is worth.

Then they say something specific and slightly uncomfortable. That the recall is fine and the writing is costing three marks a question. That the Internal Assessment topic as currently framed cannot score above the middle band no matter how well it is executed. That the realistic movement by May is one grade and not two. A tutor who leaves a first session having promised a great deal and diagnosed nothing has told you which tier of this market they belong to.

What they do not do is more revealing still. No specialist worth paying opens with a package, a guarantee, or a claim about examiner access. No specialist offers to take an Internal Assessment away and improve it. And none will quote a grade outcome, because nobody can: the honest sentence is about what will be worked on and what the evidence will look like in four weeks.

sections.heading: Command terms, where subject expertise becomes visible
paragraphs: IB mark schemes are built on command terms, and most of the marks a capable student loses are lost there rather than in the content. A student who can describe a process fluently will still score two of four on a question asking them to explain it, because explanation requires a causal link that description does not. This is learnable in a handful of sessions and it is the clearest evidence that a tutor knows the courses rather than the subject.

Abu Dhabi students arriving from British and American curriculum schools are particularly exposed here. They have been rewarded for writing a great deal and for showing method, and the Diploma rewards something narrower and more exact. The adjustment is not about effort; it is about reading the verb and answering only what it asks.

A tutor who works this way will mark a student's answer twice: once for the chemistry or the history, and once for whether the response did what the verb instructed. The second mark is the one that moves a 5 to a 6. The table below is the version worth putting on the wall above a desk.

Ask any prospective specialist to explain the difference between two of these terms in their subject. The answer takes a competent course teacher ten seconds and a generalist considerably longer, and it costs you nothing to ask before you book. It is also worth asking your child the same question about the last paper they sat, because a student who cannot say what the verb in a question required is losing marks they already know the content for, and that is the cheapest set of marks available to anybody.

sections.heading: Fitting specialist sessions into an Abu Dhabi week
paragraphs: Scheduling is where good intentions in this emirate go to die. School buses in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor get students home late enough that a 4pm start is unusable for many households, and the 5pm to 7pm window on Gulf Standard Time is consequently the most contested stretch of the week. For a scarce specialism, a flexible family gets a specialist and an inflexible one gets a generalist.

Working parents on Al Maryah and Al Reem often find later slots easier, and those later slots are precisely the ones that open up specialists based further west, who are starting their own afternoon as Abu Dhabi finishes dinner. That is a genuine advantage of the online format rather than a consolation: the time zone that makes 8pm awkward for a local tutor makes it straightforward for one several hours behind.

Ramadan reshapes the whole structure for a month. Schools shorten, afternoons go quiet and the usable study window moves to post-Iftar. Families who plan for that in advance keep continuity through a month that otherwise costs four sessions, and the students who lose the most are the DP2 cohort, for whom those weeks sit close to the examination window.

Two further habits are worth adopting. Keep the slot fixed rather than negotiating it weekly, because a named recurring slot is how you hold a specialist's time. And protect the week either side of the school's internal deadlines for coursework, which is when a student most needs the hour and is most likely to cancel it.

sections.heading: When buying a specialist is the wrong decision
paragraphs: A page about expert tutoring should say plainly when expert tutoring is not the answer, because several of the situations that bring Abu Dhabi families to this search are not subject problems at all and a specialist will not fix them.

The first is a workload problem. A Diploma student carrying three Higher Levels, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and a service commitment who is failing across four subjects does not have four subject weaknesses. They have a scheduling collapse, and buying four specialists adds four more commitments to a week that is already the cause. The intervention that works is a conversation with the school's Diploma coordinator about load and deadlines, and at most one tutor on the single subject that is furthest behind.

The second is a technique problem that is uniform across subjects. If the same student is losing marks to command terms in Biology, Economics and History alike, one specialist in one of those subjects can teach the habit transferably, and paying three specialist premiums buys the same lesson three times.

The third is the last fortnight. In the final two weeks before papers, new material is a liability and the best use of money is nothing at all, or a single session on examination-day mechanics. A provider willing to sell a family a large intensive block in the last ten days is selling comfort rather than marks. The honest answer in that window is to sleep, eat and work through past papers already marked.

sections.heading: The specialisms that are not IB subjects at all
paragraphs: Two categories of request arrive constantly from Abu Dhabi families and neither is served by an IB subject specialist. Knowing that saves a month of looking in the wrong place.

The first is the mandatory UAE strand. Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the international curriculum they are licensed to deliver. Streams differ between Arab and non-Arab students, and in Dubai the KHDA guidance goes further, requiring separate classes for the two groups and setting the language of instruction for each. Abu Dhabi families are working within the same federal baseline. A tutor for this work needs experience of the specific stream the school placed the child in, and almost no IB subject specialist has it.

The second is study skills and executive function. Note-taking that produces usable revision material, a deadline map a fifteen-year-old can actually run, revision that is testing rather than re-reading, and the discipline of attempting a question before reading the solution. These are teachable and they transfer across every subject, and for a Middle Years student they frequently matter more than any amount of subject content. A capable generalist does this better and cheaper than a Higher Level specialist.

Where both are in play, sequence them. Fix the working habits and the mandatory strand first, because they affect every subject and every term. Then buy the scarce Higher Level specialist for the one subject where depth is genuinely the constraint, and buy it early enough in the year that the slot still exists.

process.title: Name the course and the level, not the subject
process.description: Say Chemistry Higher Level, or Mathematics Applications and Interpretation Standard Level. Half the mismatches in this market come from a request for a subject being filled by somebody who teaches the other level. The level is also what determines the AED band you will be quoted.

process.title: Send marked evidence with the enquiry
process.description: A marked paper with component marks, or criterion scores task by task for a Middle Years student. This is what allows a specialist to tell you whether your child needs twelve sessions or thirty before anybody has been booked, and it is the input the hours table on this page assumes.

process.title: Hear the coverage answer honestly
process.description: You are told whether a specialist for that exact course and level is free, roughly when, and what the alternatives are if not. For the thin specialisms on this page that answer is sometimes a wait or a tutor outside the UAE. It is never a near-enough substitute presented as a match.

process.title: Use the trial as a diagnosis
process.description: The 45-minute trial over live video costs nothing and takes no card details. Judge it on whether the tutor located a specific lost mark from the evidence you sent and named what the first month would target. Comfort is not the product; diagnosis is.

process.title: Fix the slot, then review on evidence
process.description: Hold a recurring weekly time on Gulf Standard Time, and set a review four weeks out against newly marked work. If nothing has moved in the evidence, change the tutor or narrow the brief. Adding hours to an arrangement that is not working is the most common way families overspend here.

whyPoints.title: Coverage published, not implied
whyPoints.description: This page states which Abu Dhabi specialisms are thin and what happens when nobody local is free. No competitor page researched for this market discloses a coverage limit at all, and the limits are what actually determine whether a family gets a specialist or a substitute.

whyPoints.title: Quoted by level, because levels differ
whyPoints.description: Higher Level and Standard Level are priced and planned separately, because the papers, the extended-response load and the specialist scarcity are all different. A quote that treats them as one subject has not read the brief.

whyPoints.title: Hours estimated from evidence
whyPoints.description: Planning ranges on this page start from what the marked work shows rather than from the grade a family wants. That makes a budget checkable in advance and makes it obvious when a narrower brief would do the same job for less.

whyPoints.title: Market figures carry their source
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here is attributed to the provider that published it or to the 2026 UAE market survey it came from, and none is an IB Gram price. You can argue with a sourced figure, which is the point of publishing one.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what tutoring will not fix
whyPoints.description: A workload collapse, a uniform technique problem across subjects, or the last fortnight before papers are all situations where buying a specialist is the wrong call. Saying so costs us sales and saves families money they would not get back.

faqs.question: What makes an expert IB tutor in Abu Dhabi different from a strong school teacher?
faqs.answer: Diagnosis under constraint. A school teacher works with thirty students and a scheme of work; a specialist tutor works with one student, their marked scripts and a fixed number of weeks. The skill that distinguishes them is reading a partially correct answer and saying which marks went to content and which went to command-term handling, then choosing what to leave untaught because there is no time. Many excellent school teachers do this well. The relevant question is not their job title but whether they have taught that exact course at that exact level repeatedly.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are hardest to find a specialist for in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Physics and Chemistry, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Computer Science at either level, Theory of Knowledge supervision and the Group 2 languages other than Arabic. Biology, Economics and Business Management at Standard Level are comparatively plentiful, and for those you should be negotiating rather than queuing. The scarcity is what the specialist premium in the market band of roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour is actually pricing, and it tightens sharply in the weeks before an examination session.

faqs.question: How long should we expect to wait to be matched with a Higher Level specialist?
faqs.answer: It depends far more on the month than on the subject. A Higher Level Chemistry request made in October usually fills quickly because the emirate's Diploma families have not started looking yet. The same request in late February competes with every other DP2 household in Abu Dhabi and can take considerably longer. Computer Science and Theory of Knowledge supervision are the two where waiting is normal at any time of year. If a specialist is not free you are told, and the realistic alternatives are named rather than papered over.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Diploma student usually need?
faqs.answer: One per subject, with marked work in between, is the right default and covers most situations. Two becomes sensible only in a short targeted block before a session, or for a student moving from a 6 to a 7 at Higher Level where the constraint is how many extended responses can be marked. Three or more on one subject is almost always a sign of something else: a workload problem, a missing year of content, or hours being sold rather than planned. Start at one and let marked evidence argue for more.

faqs.question: Does a specialist cost more per hour or fewer hours in total?
faqs.answer: Usually both, which is why the comparison has to be done on the total rather than the rate. A specialist at the top of the market band often needs ten to fourteen sessions to fix something a generalist would work on for a term without locating, because the diagnosis is faster and the practice is better aimed. The arithmetic is worth doing explicitly: multiply your quoted rate by the session count in the planning table that matches your child's marked evidence, and compare the two totals rather than the two hourly figures.

faqs.question: My child is six weeks from examinations. Is a specialist still worth buying?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a narrowed brief. Six weeks is enough to work on the highest-yield components and the technique faults that cost marks on every paper, and not enough to close a year of missing content. Expect two or three sessions a week on a single subject, timed practice from the first session rather than the last, and a tutor who tells you which topics are being deliberately abandoned. What is not worth buying is a broad programme across four subjects in the same window; that spreads the hours too thin to move anything.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Mathematics and Physics for the same student?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and it is worth testing rather than assuming. The overlap is real at Standard Level, where a strong mathematician often handles Physics mechanics comfortably. At Higher Level the two courses diverge: Physics extended responses are marked on explanation and principle, Mathematics Paper 3 is marked on sustained investigation, and few people are genuinely strong at both. Ask the tutor directly which of the two they have taught to completion more often, and treat the other as a separate search rather than a bonus.

faqs.question: How can I tell in a trial lesson whether a tutor really knows the course?
faqs.answer: Watch what they do with your child's marked work rather than what they say about themselves. A specialist will choose a question the student half answered, ask them to think aloud, name the command term, and state where the marks went. Then they will say something specific and slightly unwelcome about the realistic ceiling. Ask them to explain the difference between explain and evaluate in their subject, or to name the four criteria for a Middle Years subject. Those answers are instant for a course teacher and laboured for a generalist.

faqs.question: Can lessons move later during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth agreeing the change before the month begins rather than during it. School days shorten, afternoons become unproductive and the usable study window shifts to after Iftar. Families who set a post-Iftar slot in advance generally keep all four sessions in the month; families who improvise lose two or three. For a DP2 student the timing matters more than for anyone else, because those weeks sit close to the examination window and cannot be made up later.

faqs.question: Will sessions work around the Abu Dhabi school run and evening traffic?
faqs.answer: Traffic is one of the stronger arguments for the online format. Nobody is driving to the lesson, so a session starting at 6.15pm starts at 6.15pm regardless of what the Sheikh Zayed bridge is doing. The constraint that remains is the family's own week: bus arrival times in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor make an early slot unusable for many households, and the 5pm to 7pm window fills first across the emirate. Later slots are both easier to get and easier to staff with a specialist.

faqs.question: Is a tutor based outside the UAE a disadvantage for an Abu Dhabi student?
faqs.answer: For most subjects, no. The IB courses, papers and mark schemes are identical worldwide, so a Chemistry Higher Level specialist in another country is teaching exactly the course your child sits. Two things genuinely differ. The time zone, which is a scheduling question and often works in your favour for later evening slots. And familiarity with the UAE's mandatory Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies strands, which matters a great deal for those subjects and not at all for the sciences.

faqs.question: What does a specialist do differently with an Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: They spend the early sessions narrowing the research question until it is answerable within the word limit, which is where most Extended Essays are won or lost, and they do it before any research is done. After that the work is reading the student's own drafts and saying which criterion is under-served, pushing on the reasoning rather than the prose, and mapping deadlines backwards from the school supervisor's dates. What they never do is write, rewrite or edit the text to completion. The essay has to be the student's own work or the diploma is at risk.

faqs.question: Does the student lose anything by not having a tutor in the room?
faqs.answer: Younger students who need somebody physically alongside them to stay on task do lose something, and that is a real consideration in the Primary Years and early Middle Years. For a Diploma student the trade runs the other way: screen sharing a marked script, annotating it live and working through a question on a shared whiteboard is at least as effective as sitting side by side, and it buys access to the person who teaches the course rather than the person who lives nearby. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, so the comparison is worth making honestly.

faqs.question: Is group tuition ever better value than one-to-one with a specialist?
faqs.answer: For content delivery to several students at a similar level, sometimes. For a Diploma student with a diagnosed weakness, rarely, because the value of the hour is in work marked against that student's own scripts and a group hour cannot do that. Groups fail outright for Internal Assessments, which must be each student's own work, and for Higher Level technique, where the marks sit in individual extended responses. If budget is the constraint, fewer one-to-one sessions on one subject beats more group hours across three.

faqs.question: What should we do if four weeks of specialist tutoring has changed nothing?
faqs.answer: Change the arrangement rather than adding hours, which is the instinct that costs Abu Dhabi families the most. Ask for the marked evidence from those four weeks and look for movement in the specific component that was targeted, not in the overall grade, which moves slowly. If the targeted component has not shifted, the likely causes are a wrong diagnosis, a brief that is too broad, or a student not doing the work between sessions. Each has a different fix, and none of them is a fifth and sixth hour.

abu-dhabi/expert-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Buy scarcity early, buy breadth never
abu-dhabi/expert-ib-tutor.closingBody: The practical summary of this page is short. Decide which of your child's subjects is genuinely a depth problem and buy a specialist for that one, early in the year while the slot still exists. Use a generalist, or the school, for the technique and habit work that transfers across everything. Name the course and the level when you ask, send the marked evidence, and judge the trial on whether somebody located a specific lost mark. The AED figures on this page belong to the market and carry their sources, so you can price any quote against them. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, the trial costs nothing, and coverage gaps are told to you rather than discovered.

abu-dhabi/hudayriyat-island.tutorsIntro: These tutors are matched to the component rather than to the subject label: the investigation, the exploration, the Paper 3 extended response, the comparative essay. Each one works from criteria and mark schemes, which is the only way to coach work that a student has to produce on their own.

intro.heading: The taught course and the unsupervised course are two different courses
paragraphs: Hudayriyat Island is residential at one end and a recreation district at the other, reached by bridge from the western side of Abu Dhabi island. No school sits on it, so every child here is schooled in Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah, Al Mushrif or further out, and comes home to a quiet, low-density neighbourhood. That combination matters more than it sounds. Island households have good conditions for independent study and very little structure imposed on it, and the Diploma and IGCSE both assume a great deal of structured independent study.

Here is the arithmetic a school prospectus never prints. A Diploma Higher Level subject is nominally 240 hours of teaching across two years. The internal assessment, the past-paper practice, the reading and the revision that convert those taught hours into a grade are not inside that figure. Across six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, a Diploma student is carrying several hundred hours of work that no teacher schedules, supervises or marks along the way. IGCSE is the same shape in miniature: content is delivered in class, and the discipline of working under timed conditions against a mark scheme is almost entirely homework.

That gap is where grades are actually decided, and it is also why strong classroom teaching and a disappointing result are perfectly compatible. A parent sees good lessons, attentive staff and a reasonable report, then a mock grade two bands below expectation. Nothing has gone wrong in the classroom. The unsupervised half has been done badly or not at all, usually because nobody wrote down what it consists of.

So this page writes it down. It separates taught time from independent time, component by component. It names the internal assessment criteria by their letters with the marks attached, because a student working alone on an investigation needs to know that research design and evaluation carry six marks each rather than being vague about quality. It publishes the word and page limits for every assessed component in one place. And it says where IGCSE marks leave the page in the gap between Year 10 content and a Year 11 paper.

What a tutor adds in this picture is supervision of work the school does not supervise, not a second delivery of the syllabus. One hour a week spent re-teaching a lesson your child already sat is an hour wasted, and parents buy it constantly because it is the easiest thing to ask for. One hour spent marking their timed paper against the real mark scheme, or interrogating their investigation method before any data is collected, changes the half of the course that was previously unobserved by anyone. Those lessons run one-to-one over live video, which happens to be the right format for work built around marked scripts, criteria and shared documents rather than around a whiteboard.

abu-dhabi/hudayriyat-island.programmesIntro: Island families are schooled across the western districts of Abu Dhabi island, which means a mix of the IB continuum and British routes. The notes below are about the independent load each programme imposes rather than about what each one covers.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each marked against four criteria lettered A to D and scored out of eight. The MYP deliberately assesses process as well as product, so a student who can do the mathematics but cannot document a method loses marks that look mysterious on a report card.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP Personal Project is the first piece of work a student has to run alone from start to finish, and it arrives in Year 10 or 11. For a Hudayriyat household it is also the first test of whether the quiet house translates into actual output. We coach the process, the goal and the reflection; the project remains the student's own throughout.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The core alone carries a 4,000-word essay and a 1,600-word Theory of Knowledge essay, both produced over months with no lesson time allocated to the writing itself.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students reaching Hudayriyat Island come from the Al Bateen and Al Mushrif school cluster, where Higher Level provision is reasonable but class sizes limit individual feedback on draft work. The component most often neglected here is the internal assessment, which at 20% of a science grade is worth more than most families realise.

programmes.name: IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both operate here, and the papers differ even where subject names match. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 runs a Core tier on papers 1 and 3 with a grade ceiling at C, and an Extended tier on papers 2 and 4 reaching A*. Pearson's 4MA1 tiers as Foundation and Higher instead.
programmes.countryNote: The independent half of IGCSE is timed practice against mark schemes, and almost no school has enough lesson time to run it properly. A Year 11 student who has never marked their own script against the published scheme is guessing at what examiners reward, which is the single commonest reason capable students underperform.

programmes.name: A Level
programmes.description: Linear A Levels with all assessment at the end of the course, which pushes the independent burden even further than the Diploma does. There is no coursework safety net in most subjects, so the entire grade rests on performance across a small number of papers sat within a few weeks.
programmes.countryNote: Families choosing between the Diploma and A Levels in the western districts should weigh the independent-work profile, not just the breadth. A Level suits a student who can self-direct deep work in three subjects; the Diploma spreads the load but adds the core, which is itself several hundred unsupervised hours.

abu-dhabi/hudayriyat-island.subjectsIntro: These are the components island students most often ask for help with, described by what each one assesses and where the marks tend to leave the page.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Papers 1 and 2 at 36% and 44%, scientific investigation at 20%. Independent practice is where fields and circuits are won; students who only ever see worked examples in class cannot produce a mechanism-level written explanation under time pressure.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same paper structure and the same 20% investigation. Organic mechanisms need handwritten repetition, not reading, and that repetition is homework. A tutor's job here is to check the drawings and the arrow placement, which is quick on a shared screen.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Built on unifying themes rather than a topic checklist, so unseen-context questions dominate Paper 2. The reliable loss point is answering a command term for explanation with a description of a trend, which only practice against mark schemes fixes.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Standard Level is two papers at 40% each plus a 20% exploration; Higher Level adds Paper 3 at 20%. Paper 3's extended investigation is unlike anything in a textbook and has to be practised deliberately rather than encountered for the first time in May.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with the graphic display calculator throughout. Marks go on interpretation: a correct statistical output followed by no sentence stating what it means in context scores the calculation and nothing else.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis in Paper 1, comparative essay in Paper 2, Individual Oral at 30% of Standard Level. Higher Level adds the HL essay at 20%. Independent reading improves the ceiling; only timed essay practice moves the actual mark.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Standard Level runs Paper 1 at 30%, Paper 2 at 40% and the portfolio at 30%, with a quantitative Paper 3 added at Higher Level. The three-commentary portfolio is the most coachable element in the course and the one students leave latest.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE)
subjects.description: Tier choice sets a hard grade ceiling, so the decision needs marked evidence behind it. Beyond that, the gains come from working past papers under genuine timed conditions and self-marking against the scheme.

subjects.name: Physics (IGCSE)
subjects.description: Electricity and waves are the predictable weak strands. The alternative-to-practical paper rewards specific experimental vocabulary that is rarely drilled in class, and it is fully learnable in a handful of focused sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry (IGCSE)
subjects.description: Moles and electrolysis separate grades at the top end. Qualitative analysis tables reward memorised observation detail, which is an independent-study task that pays for itself quickly once a student knows it exists.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title plus the exhibition with its 950-word commentary. Almost no revision time is allocated to it anywhere, and it affects the diploma total through the bonus points matrix alongside the Extended Essay.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: 4,000 words in a subject of the student's choosing, assessed against published criteria covering focus, knowledge, critical thinking, presentation and engagement. The commonest failure is a question too broad to answer inside the limit.

abu-dhabi/hudayriyat-island.regionsIntro: Hudayriyat households are schooled across the western and central districts of Abu Dhabi island. These are the areas that define the commute and, with it, when independent study actually happens.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: The nearest established school district, reached without touching the central business area. Al Bateen Academy and the American Community School sit here, and a Bateen school place gives Hudayriyat families their shortest afternoon.

regions.name: the Corniche
regions.note: The route rather than the destination for most island families, and the stretch where the afternoon is lost. A collection from a Khalidiyah or Ras Al Akhdar school realistically means being home after half past four.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: An apartment island on the far side of the city with its own school provision. Relevant to Hudayriyat households who moved west and kept a Reem school place, which converts a walk into a cross-city drive.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Cranleigh Abu Dhabi and the Saadiyat cluster, reached by crossing the city. The Diploma provision is strong, but from Hudayriyat it is the longest regular school run in this list and it pushes weekday sessions late.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach
regions.note: On the highway corridor towards the airport, with a mix of British and American provision nearby. Hudayriyat families rarely school here, but it is where several of the emirate's teaching staff live, which shapes tutor availability.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: The deepest school cluster in the emirate, including the British International School Abu Dhabi and GEMS American Academy. From Hudayriyat it is a committed drive, and families who do it usually chose a specific Higher Level combination.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Mainland district with a large Indian and Pakistani curriculum presence. It matters here mainly for students transferring from a national board into IGCSE, where the independent-study expectations change sharply.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Across the city to the east, with American and British provision. Event weekends reshape the evening traffic pattern for anyone commuting that way, which is an argument for weekend-morning study slots rather than Friday ones.

abu-dhabi/hudayriyat-island.modesIntro: The patterns below exist because the independent half of a course fails in three distinct ways: nothing gets scheduled, coursework drifts, or timed practice never happens under real conditions. Each mode targets one of those.

modes.title: Weekly supervision of independent work
modes.description: The tutor does not re-teach the lesson. The hour is spent on what the student produced since the last session: a timed question marked against the real scheme, a set of mechanisms checked, a practice essay annotated. The week's independent work is set at the end and inspected at the start of the next session.
bullets: Work set between sessions, then actually checked
Marking done against the published scheme, with the student watching
Same tutor each week so patterns of error are visible
Short written note after each session naming what was set

modes.title: Component blocks for coursework
modes.description: Three or four sessions placed at the points where an investigation, exploration or Extended Essay actually fails: the question, the method, and the criterion the draft is missing. This is the pattern for a student who is coping in class and drifting on coursework, which describes most Diploma students by February of the first year.
bullets: Session one on whether the question is answerable in the word limit
Session two on method and data quality before collection
Session three reading the draft against criteria by letter
Feedback on the student's own text only

modes.title: Timed-conditions practice
modes.description: A full paper sat under real timing, then marked and dissected. Most students have never done this outside a mock hall, which is why their first experience of real time pressure is the mock itself. Running three or four of these across a term changes performance more reliably than any amount of content revision.
bullets: Full paper under genuine timing, not a question set
Marked against the official scheme, mark by mark
A written breakdown of where time and marks were lost
Repeated on the same paper type to prove the change

sections.heading: What class time delivers, and what the student is left holding
paragraphs: Separate the course into what a teacher can and cannot do with the hours available, and the tutoring question answers itself. A teacher delivers content, models technique, sets homework and marks a limited amount of it. A teacher cannot sit with one student while they attempt a Paper 3 investigation under time pressure, cannot read four drafts of one essay, and cannot supervise the forty hours of practice that convert understanding into marks.

Hudayriyat households are unusually well placed for the independent half and unusually likely to leave it unstructured. The island is quiet, the houses are large, and there is no noisy apartment block or sibling crowding in the way. What there also is not, is a set of imposed deadlines. A student in a busy household sometimes works better because the day has edges. Here the day does not, and work slides.

The table below splits the Diploma and IGCSE workload by component. The point of it is not precision to the hour; it is the ratio. For most components the unsupervised portion is the larger portion, and for the Diploma core it is almost all of it. Once a parent sees that, the conversation changes from how many hours of tutoring to which unsupervised component is being neglected.

Read the right-hand column as a shopping list. The components with the highest independent share and the clearest published criteria are the ones where outside supervision has the largest effect per hour spent. The components that are mostly taught, and examined on content recall, are the ones to leave to the school.

sections.heading: The independent week, written down instead of assumed
paragraphs: Students do not fail to revise because they are lazy. They fail because nobody has ever told them what an hour of independent work should contain, so the hour becomes re-reading notes, which feels like study and produces nothing. The fix is prescriptive and dull: name the task, name the output, name how it will be checked.

A usable Diploma week for a Hudayriyat student looks like this. Two blocks of ninety minutes at the weekend, one on the heaviest Higher Level subject and one on coursework. Three weekday blocks of forty-five minutes, each with a single output: five examination questions marked against the scheme, one mechanism sheet, one page of an essay plan. One block for the core, which almost everyone skips, and which is where the bonus points sit. That is roughly seven hours. It is considerably less than most parents imagine and considerably more than most students actually do.

Every block needs an output that exists afterwards. A marked question with the lost marks circled is an output. A completed error log is an output. Forty minutes of reading is not, because nothing afterwards can be inspected. This single rule, applied for a term, does more than changing tutors.

The role of the weekly session in this scheme is inspection and correction. If the student arrives with nothing to inspect, the session becomes a lesson, and a lesson is the least valuable use of the hour because the school already delivered one. We say that at the first session so the expectation is set from the start.
bullets: Name the task, the output and how it will be checked
Two weekend blocks of ninety minutes, three weekday blocks of forty-five
Every block leaves something behind that can be inspected
The weekly session inspects and corrects; it does not re-teach

sections.heading: Internal assessment criteria, letter by letter, with the marks attached
paragraphs: Ask a Diploma student what their investigation is marked on and most will say quality of the science. Ask them which criterion carries six marks and almost none can answer. That is a straightforward information failure, and it is fixable in one session. A student who knows that the evaluation criterion carries the same weight as the data analysis stops writing two lines of evaluation at midnight.

In the current science guides the scientific investigation is marked out of 24 across four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each worth six marks. In Mathematics the exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The last of those carries six of the twenty marks, which is why a mathematically thin exploration cannot be rescued by beautiful presentation.

The practical use of this table is to audit a draft. Read the draft with the criteria beside it and ask, for each letter, what in this document evidences that criterion. If the honest answer for one of them is nothing, you have found where the marks are. That is a twenty-minute exercise a parent can do without any subject knowledge at all, and it identifies the problem before a tutor is even engaged.

Always confirm the current criteria and mark allocations against your child's own subject guide or their coordinator, because guides are revised on a cycle and a sibling's version may be out of date. We do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson subject guides, mark schemes or past papers; they are the boards' copyright and should be obtained through the school.

sections.heading: Word and page limits across every assessed component
paragraphs: Limits are the one part of the assessment architecture that is entirely knowable in advance, and students still breach them. A Theory of Knowledge essay at 1,900 words is not a slightly long essay; material beyond the limit is not read. An Extended Essay that runs past 4,000 words loses the end of its argument, which is usually the part that earns the critical-thinking marks.

The limits also do planning work that students rarely recognise. Four thousand words is not very much for a research question that requires three bodies of literature. Twelve pages of mathematics is not very much for an exploration involving a long derivation. If a student cannot sketch how their piece fits inside the limit before they start, the question is wrong, and that is a far cheaper discovery to make in week one than in week ten.

Collect the limits for all the components your child is carrying onto one sheet at the start of the year and put it where they work. Island households have the wall space and the quiet, and this is the single cheapest intervention available. Most students have never seen the full set in one place.

Confirm every figure against the current subject guide for your child's cohort, since limits and the treatment of appendices are revised periodically and a sibling's version of a course may be out of date. The table below reflects the long-standing limits for the components Hudayriyat students most often carry, and the right-hand column names what examiners most often see mishandled inside each one. Treat it as a planning document at the start of the year rather than a reference consulted in a panic the week before submission.

sections.heading: Training on the island and study in the same evening
paragraphs: Hudayriyat is a recreation district as much as a residential one, with cycling, skating, water sports and a sports hub on the doorstep. A high proportion of island teenagers train seriously, and that is a good thing academically until the calendar collides. Training four evenings a week plus a competition weekend removes exactly the blocks a Diploma student needs for independent work, and the collision usually becomes visible in the first mock season rather than when the schedule is set.

Athletes are often the easiest students to plan with, because they already understand periodisation. The same logic applies to study: build volume in the off-season, taper into a competition or an exam, and do not attempt both peaks at once. A student with a competition block in February should front-load coursework into November and December rather than discovering in February that an investigation is due.

Practically, that means two things. Put the heavy academic work in the mornings of non-training days, which on this island usually means a weekend morning. And treat the forty-five-minute weekday block as genuinely short and single-purpose: five marked questions, one mechanism sheet, one essay plan. A tired athlete can complete a defined forty-five-minute task after training; they cannot complete an undefined two-hour study session, and pretending otherwise produces guilt rather than marks.

The scheduling flexibility of live video matters here more than anywhere. A session can move to a morning, run from a hotel during a competition week, or shift by a day without anyone driving anywhere. A fixed in-home appointment is the arrangement that breaks first under a training calendar.
bullets: Front-load coursework into the months before a competition block
