sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks leave the page between Year 10 and the final paper
paragraphs: IGCSE students lose marks in a small number of repeatable ways, and almost none of them are about not knowing the content. The first is command-term misreading: answering describe when the question said explain, which costs the analysis marks every single time it happens. The second is unit and significant-figure discipline in the sciences and in mathematics, where the physics is right and the answer is not.

The third is the structured question with escalating mark tariffs. A six-mark question needs six distinct creditable points, and students who write a dense paragraph of three ideas score three. Teaching a student to count their own points against the tariff before moving on is a fifteen-minute intervention with a measurable effect across every paper.

The fourth is timing, which masquerades as weakness. A student who scores well on the first two-thirds of a paper and collapses in the last third has a pacing problem, not a knowledge problem, and buying content lessons for a pacing problem is throwing money at the wrong target. This is why we want to see a marked script before recommending anything: the distribution of lost marks across the paper distinguishes the two cases immediately.

The fifth, specific to the sciences, is the alternative-to-practical paper, which rewards experimental vocabulary and answer conventions that are rarely drilled anywhere. How to state a variable, how to describe a precaution, how to read an instrument to the right precision: these are conventions rather than science, and they are learnable in a handful of focused hours. It is the highest-return few hours available to an IGCSE science candidate and almost nobody spends them, because practical lesson time goes on the practical itself.
bullets: Command terms: describe and explain are not interchangeable
Count creditable points against the mark tariff before moving on

sections.heading: A home tutor on the island against a specialist on a shared screen
paragraphs: Parents here do search for a home tutor, and the reasoning is sound: a quiet villa, a large table, nobody needs to go anywhere. It is worth answering the question honestly before stating what we actually offer. An independent tutor driving to Hudayriyat Island is crossing the bridge twice, and that travel is inside the rate. Market in-home rates run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 for a comparably qualified tutor working online, on the published competitor pricing and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table. The larger cost is choice: the available pool narrows to whoever will make that drive on a weekday evening.

IB Gram does not make home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Abu Dhabi lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, and that is better said here than discovered later.

For the work this page is about, the screen is genuinely the better tool rather than a compromise. Supervising independent study means looking at documents: a marked script with the lost marks circled, a draft investigation beside its criteria, a mark scheme open in a second window, a mechanism being drawn and corrected in real time. All of that is easier shared on a screen than passed across a table, and the session recording or the annotated file still exists the following week, which a kitchen-table conversation does not.

The honest limitation is supervision of attention. A student who needs an adult physically present to stay on task is harder to hold on video, particularly below about thirteen. For those students we recommend shorter sessions and a parent within earshot rather than claiming the format solves everything.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when most of the work happens alone
paragraphs: The more of a course a student completes unsupervised, the more the honesty question matters. An internal assessment, an exploration, an Extended Essay and a Theory of Knowledge essay are all produced at home over weeks, and the rules require them to be the student's own work. A malpractice finding falls on the student and can cost the diploma, so this is their exposure rather than a tutor's.

What a tutor legitimately does with that work is substantial. Pressing on whether a research question can be answered inside the word limit. Pointing out that a planned method cannot generate data capable of supporting a conclusion, before any data exists. Reading a draft against the published criteria and naming the letter that is unevidenced. Teaching the skill the draft lacks, then returning it. Asking the student to justify a paragraph out loud, which exposes borrowed reasoning faster than any software.

What a tutor must not do is supply text, rewrite a section into something the student could not have produced, edit a draft to completion, or hand over a ready-made topic, structure or data set. One operation in this market sells finished Diploma internal assessments outright. That product is an integrity breach dressed up as a service, and the family carries the consequence, not the seller.

There is also a sourcing rule worth knowing. We do not supply or reproduce subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Those are the boards' copyright and your child's school can provide them legitimately. Anything a tutor needs to reference, we reference and link rather than redistribute.
bullets: Questions, methods and criteria coaching, as early in the process as possible
Feedback against published criteria, on the student's own text
No supplied text, no rewriting to completion, no ready-made topics or data
Board materials referenced and linked, never reproduced or handed over

sections.heading: Starting from the last marked script
paragraphs: The first thing we ask for is the most recent piece of work a teacher marked, because it answers questions that conversation cannot. The distribution of lost marks across a paper distinguishes a content gap from a technique gap from a pacing problem. Teacher comments on a draft show whether the student is being told the same thing repeatedly and not acting on it. A clean script with a disappointing total usually means marks are leaving over command terms and tariffs rather than over understanding.

The trial session is a diagnostic rather than an introduction. The tutor works through that script with your child, establishes which of the failure modes is actually operating, and writes down what a term of supervision would consist of. You keep that plan whether or not you go further. If the conclusion is that your child needs a protected study hour and an error log rather than a tutor, that is what we will say, and it has happened often enough that we mention it on the page.

Then the cadence is set against the island calendar: training days, competition blocks, the school's own coursework deadlines rather than the board's, and the Ramadan period when the school day shortens and an early afternoon slot becomes briefly available. A pattern chosen against the real calendar survives the term. A pattern chosen in optimism does not.

On availability, we are straight with you up front. Coverage for the rarer Diploma languages and some Higher Level combinations is thin in this time zone, and a specific weekday slot in a rare subject may simply not exist. When that is the case we say so and offer the nearest genuine alternative rather than putting a generalist in front of a Higher Level paper. It is also worth asking any tutor you consider, from any provider, whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years.
bullets: Send the last marked script; it distinguishes content, technique and pacing
The trial session is a diagnostic and may advise against buying lessons
Cadence is set against training, coursework deadlines and Ramadan hours
Rare subject coverage is stated honestly before you plan around it

process.title: Send the last marked piece of work
process.description: A mock script, a returned essay or a coursework draft with teacher comments. Where the marks were lost across the page tells a specialist whether the problem is content, exam technique or timing, and that distinction decides what is worth buying. Description of the problem is far less useful than the document itself.

process.title: Audit the independent half
process.description: We list the components your child is carrying that nobody supervises: the investigation, the exploration, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay, timed practice. Then we ask which of them currently has a date, an output and somebody checking it. The empty rows are the plan.

process.title: Meet the matched tutor for a diagnostic hour
process.description: The tutor works through the script and the coursework drafts with your child against the published criteria, names the criterion or technique that is unevidenced, and writes down what a term of supervision would contain. The plan is yours whether or not you continue with us.

process.title: Fix the weekly output, not just the slot
process.description: Each week has a named task and a named output that exists afterwards and can be inspected. The session begins with that output rather than with a lesson. This is the part that changes results, and it is the part students have never had described to them before.

process.title: Re-measure on external evidence
process.description: The next mock, the next criterion-marked draft, the next timed paper under real conditions. If the external evidence has not moved after a reasonable run of sessions, the plan changes or the tutor does. Sessions feeling productive is not evidence of anything.

whyPoints.title: We target the unsupervised half
whyPoints.description: The school delivers content and marks a share of the homework. We supervise the components nobody else sees: the investigation, the exploration, the core essays, the timed practice. Buying a second delivery of a lesson your child already attended is the most common waste of a tutoring budget in this market.

whyPoints.title: Criteria and marks published, not implied
whyPoints.description: This page names the internal assessment criteria by letter with their mark allocations and sets out the word limit on every assessed component. A student who knows the evaluation criterion carries six marks writes a different evaluation. The information itself is free, and almost nobody publishes it.

whyPoints.title: Every session leaves evidence
whyPoints.description: Marked questions with lost marks circled, an error log, a draft annotated against criteria. The written note after each session names what was covered and what was set, so the next week starts from something inspectable rather than from a conversation about how things are going.

whyPoints.title: Board materials referenced, never redistributed
whyPoints.description: We do not supply subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. They are the boards' copyright and your child's school can provide them. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from any board or from ADEK, and claims none.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling that survives a training calendar
whyPoints.description: Island teenagers train seriously, and a fixed appointment is the first thing a competition block destroys. Live video sessions move to a morning, run from a hotel or shift by a day without anybody driving, which is why they survive the season rather than quietly lapsing in week five.

whyPoints.title: A coursework line stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Questions, methods, criteria and feedback on the student's own text. No supplied sentences, no rewriting to completion, no ready-made topics or data sets. Operations in this market sell finished internal assessments; the student carries the malpractice risk, which is exactly why we draw the line where we do.

faqs.question: How many independent study hours does a Diploma subject actually need?
faqs.answer: A Higher Level subject is nominally around 240 taught hours across two years, and the internal assessment, past-paper practice, reading and revision that turn those hours into a grade sit outside that figure entirely. Across six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, a Diploma student carries several hundred hours that nobody schedules, supervises or marks along the way. That is why strong classroom teaching and a weak mock grade coexist so often. The useful question is not how many hours, but which of those unsupervised components currently has a deadline and somebody checking it.

faqs.question: Why is my child doing well in class and badly in mocks?
faqs.answer: Because class performance and examination performance measure different things. Class work is untimed, supported and often collaborative. A mock is a timed solo performance scored against a mark scheme, and the specific skills it requires, reading command terms correctly, matching answer length to the mark tariff and pacing across a full paper, are practised almost entirely at home. A student who has never marked their own script against the published scheme is guessing at what earns credit. Send us the mock script; where the lost marks sit across the paper usually identifies the cause within minutes.

faqs.question: What is the Diploma scientific investigation marked out of?
faqs.answer: In the current science guides it is marked out of 24 across four criteria, each worth six marks: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. It carries 20% of the final grade at both Standard and Higher Level. Most students can name the first two and treat evaluation as a closing paragraph written late, which is where six available marks quietly disappear. Confirm the allocation against your child's own subject guide, since guides are revised on a cycle, and ask their coordinator rather than relying on a sibling's older version of the course.

faqs.question: How many marks does the use of mathematics criterion carry in the exploration?
faqs.answer: Six of the twenty available marks. The Mathematics exploration is assessed across five criteria: presentation at four marks, mathematical communication at four, personal engagement at three, reflection at three, and use of mathematics at six. The practical consequence is that a mathematically thin exploration cannot be rescued by careful formatting, and a topic that does not demand mathematics at the level of the course caps the mark before any writing begins. That is why the topic conversation is the single highest-value session available, and it belongs at the start rather than near the deadline.

faqs.question: What should an hour of independent revision actually contain?
faqs.answer: A named task with an output that exists afterwards. Five examination questions attempted under time and marked against the scheme, with lost marks circled. One mechanism sheet completed by hand. One essay plan with the argument in the right order. An error log updated with this week's recurring mistakes. Re-reading notes is not an output, because nothing afterwards can be inspected, which is why it feels like work and produces nothing. Students rarely resist this once it is described; they simply have never had it described to them.

faqs.question: Is the Theory of Knowledge essay worth spending tutoring money on?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and almost nobody does. It is 1,600 words on a prescribed title, produced over months with essentially no lesson time allocated to the writing, and alongside the Extended Essay it feeds the bonus points matrix that can move a final diploma total. Students treat it as unexaminable because it does not look like a subject. Two or three sessions on title choice, argument structure and the use of real examples from their own subjects is usually enough, and it is cheap relative to its effect on the total.

faqs.question: Do tutors visit homes on Hudayriyat Island?
faqs.answer: Not through us. IB Gram does not make home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India, and Abu Dhabi lessons run one-to-one over live video. Independent in-home tutors do cross the bridge, and their rates carry that travel, which is why market in-home figures run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 online. For the work this page describes, marked scripts, drafts against criteria and mark schemes side by side, a shared screen is the better tool rather than a substitute.

faqs.question: My child trains most evenings. Can tutoring fit around that?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the planning is the same as training planning. Build academic volume in the off-season, taper into a competition block, and never attempt both peaks at once. Put heavy work in the mornings of non-training days, which here usually means a weekend. Keep weekday sessions short and single-purpose, because a tired athlete will complete a defined forty-five-minute task and will not complete an undefined two-hour one. Live video sessions move to a morning or run from a hotel during a competition week without anyone driving anywhere.

faqs.question: What is the word limit on the Extended Essay and what happens if it is exceeded?
faqs.answer: Four thousand words, covering the main body with the introduction and conclusion. Material beyond the limit is not read, which in practice means a student who overruns loses the end of their argument, and the end is usually where the critical-thinking marks are earned. Appendices are not a way around it: an argument hidden in an appendix is not assessed either. If your child cannot sketch how their essay fits inside 4,000 words before starting, the research question is too broad, and that is a cheap thing to discover in week one.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE paper gives the best return for a few hours of work?
faqs.answer: The alternative-to-practical paper in the sciences, almost every time. It rewards experimental vocabulary and answer conventions, how to state a variable, how to describe a precaution, how to read an instrument, that are rarely drilled in class because practical time is spent on the practical itself. Those conventions are learnable in a handful of focused sessions and they transfer across all three sciences. After that, command-term discipline and counting creditable points against the mark tariff are the next highest-return interventions available.

faqs.question: Can a tutor read my child's internal assessment draft?
faqs.answer: Yes, against the published criteria, and that is the single most useful thing a tutor does with coursework. The tutor names which criterion letter is currently unevidenced, teaches the skill the draft is missing and hands it back. What must not happen is text being supplied, a section being rewritten into something the student could not have produced, a draft being edited to completion, or a topic or data set being handed over ready-made. A malpractice finding falls on the student, so the boundary exists for their protection.

faqs.question: Will you send us past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No. Subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the copyright of the IB, Cambridge and Pearson, and redistributing them is not something we do. Your child's school can supply them legitimately, and the boards publish specimen material on their own sites. A tutor working with your child will reference and link official material rather than hand over copies. Any provider offering a library of board documents as a selling point is telling you something about how they treat rules generally.

faqs.question: How do I tell a content gap from a timing problem?
faqs.answer: Look at where the marks were lost across the paper rather than at the total. Marks missing evenly throughout, including on early low-tariff questions, suggests content. Strong performance across the first two-thirds followed by a collapse, blank final questions or one-line answers to six-mark items, is pacing. Marks lost on the analysis half of questions the student clearly understood is command-term misreading. Those three cases need completely different purchases, which is why we want the marked script before recommending anything at all.

faqs.question: Does the quiet of a low-density island help or hurt study?
faqs.answer: Both, and families are often surprised by the second half. The conditions are excellent: space, quiet, no competing noise. What a low-density neighbourhood does not supply is imposed structure, and students who work well in busy houses sometimes do so because the day has edges. Here the day does not. The fix is not more hours but more definition, naming the task, the output and how it will be checked, so that the quiet becomes productive rather than simply undisturbed.

faqs.question: What happens if we start supervision only six weeks before the papers?
faqs.answer: It is still worth doing, but the target changes. Six weeks is not enough for content rebuilding and it is ample for technique: command terms, mark tariffs, pacing across a full paper and self-marking against the scheme. Those are the fastest-moving variables in any grade. Coursework is a different matter, because an investigation or essay near its deadline leaves only cosmetic room, and that is exactly when families start asking for help nobody should give. Supervision bought early is both more useful and entirely safe.

abu-dhabi/hudayriyat-island.closingHeading: Audit the half nobody is watching
abu-dhabi/hudayriyat-island.closingBody: List the components your child is carrying that nobody supervises: the investigation, the exploration, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay, the timed practice that never happens outside a mock hall. abu-dhabi/hydra-village.tutorsIntro: Hydra Village requests arrive board-specific: Cambridge 0580 Extended Paper 4, Pearson 4PH1, the alternative-to-practical paper, or a Diploma subject for a student whose school changed route. The tutors below teach to one specification properly rather than to a subject in general, one-to-one over live video.

intro.heading: The first question is which paper, not which tutor
paragraphs: Hydra Village sits out towards the Dubai road, past Al Bahia and Al Shahama, built as gated villa clusters some distance from the city. There is no school inside the compound, so children travel, and families here have chosen schools in several different directions depending on the year the child started and which places were available. The practical consequence shows up in tutoring enquiries more sharply here than in districts with one obvious local school.

The consequence is board confusion. One child sits Cambridge for the sciences and Pearson Edexcel for maths. A sibling two years younger, at a different school, sits Cambridge for everything. A family moving from one school to another mid-course finds the new school enters a different specification for the same subject. Parents describe the subject - maths, physics, chemistry - and assume that is enough information to buy help with. It is not, and a tutor who accepts the subject name without asking for the code is the first warning sign.

Getting it wrong is expensive in a specific way. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 at Extended tier sits on Papers 2 and 4; the Core tier sits on Papers 1 and 3; Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 is a different syllabus again; Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 has its own paper structure and formula provision. A student drilled on the wrong set for a term has practised real mathematics and the wrong examination, and nobody notices until a mock arrives in the format they have not seen. The cost is not only the wasted hours. A student who has been told they are prepared, and then meets a paper laid out differently from everything they practised, loses confidence at exactly the point in Year 11 when confidence is doing a great deal of the work for them, and recovering it takes longer than fixing the format did.

The second thing that catches this community is examination logistics. Living a distance out, with schools in several directions, some families here end up dealing with centres and entries directly - a retake in a subject the school does not re-enter, a private candidacy, or a series the school does not sit. Those arrangements have deadlines and requirements that are published but not obvious, and missing one costs a whole series rather than a few marks.

Every lesson for a Hydra Village family runs one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. For a community at this distance that removes the problem of finding a tutor who both knows Pearson 4PH1 and is willing to drive out past Al Bahia on a weekday evening, which is a very short list in practice.

abu-dhabi/hydra-village.programmesIntro: The stages below cover what Hydra Village families ask about, with an emphasis on the specification detail that decides whether help is useful or wasted.

programmes.name: Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two boards, different codes, different paper structures and different tiering conventions. Cambridge splits Core and Extended on most syllabuses; Pearson runs mostly single tier on its International GCSE specifications. The practical rule is that everything - practice papers, mark schemes, formula provision - has to match the code on the entry.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs June and November series with a March series for some specifications, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, stating that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Pearson runs May and June and November, publishing provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official document is the only one worth planning from.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Students arriving from either IGCSE board meet the same change: content continues, assessment does not. Procedure becomes justification in maths, and recall becomes uncertainty and argument in the sciences.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools enter the May session, which loads the autumn of Year 13 with coursework drafts, the Extended Essay and predicted grades at once. Confirm every IB date with the school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org - no IB session or results date in this project has been verified from the IB's own site, so anything quoted elsewhere without a source should be treated as a guess.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight. For a Hydra Village family whose children are at different schools, the MYP's descriptors and a GCSE school's percentages are not comparable, and trying to read one as the other produces either false alarm or false comfort.
programmes.countryNote: Where a student moves from an MYP school into an IGCSE school mid-course, the content transfers reasonably well and the answer technique does not. Command words, mark allocations and the convention of writing to a mark total are new, and that is a four to six week adjustment concentrated on how answers are structured rather than on what the student knows.

abu-dhabi/hydra-village.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are listed by specification rather than by name, because for this community the code is the information that matters.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.levels: Core on Papers 1 and 3, Extended on Papers 2 and 4
subjects.description: Extended adds functions, transformations of graphs, vectors and harder trigonometry over the shared core. Marks go on the long structured questions where a student completes the difficult step and then answers a slightly different question from the one set.

subjects.name: Cambridge International Mathematics 0607
subjects.description: A separate syllabus from 0580, with a different emphasis and its own paper structure, often used by schools running an IB continuum. Families frequently assume 0580 material covers it; it does not, and the difference shows in the investigation-style questions.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1
subjects.description: Its own paper structure and formula provision, with questions phrased differently from Cambridge even where the mathematics is identical. A student moved between boards mid-course usually has the content and not the format.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity, moments and momentum account for most marks lost. The alternative-to-practical paper tests experimental reasoning in writing and rewards a student trained to criticise someone else's method rather than recite their own.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Covers much the same physics with a different paper split and its own practical-skills assessment on paper. Students who practise Cambridge papers for a Pearson entry meet unfamiliar question phrasing on the day.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Mole calculations and the qualitative analysis tables separate the middle grades from the top. Ion tests memorised as a list collapse under pressure; understood as chemistry they hold, and that distinction is most of the teaching.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: A long syllabus with precise examinable detail - named enzymes, named vessels, named stages. Students performing well in class and poorly in mocks are usually revising topics rather than practising the command words the paper uses.

subjects.name: English: First Language and as a Second Language
subjects.description: Two courses that look alike and grade differently, with consequences for later university language conditions. Reading inference under time pressure needs deliberate practice rather than more reading.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Justification carries the marks, and Paper 3 at Higher Level is an extended investigation with no IGCSE equivalent on either board. Students arriving from a strong Extended or Higher paper grade still have to learn to write reasoning.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first language and as an additional language
subjects.description: Two separate courses with different starting points, assessed in Standard Arabic for the first-language route. Written register and grammar are the recurring gaps, and they respond to short frequent sessions.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel for the same subject
paragraphs: Both boards examine International GCSE subjects to a comparable standard and both are accepted for the same purposes. They are not, however, interchangeable from the point of view of a student preparing for one of them. The content overlaps heavily; the paper structures, phrasing conventions, tiering arrangements and formula provision do not.

The most consequential difference is tiering. Cambridge splits most of its maths and science syllabuses into Core and Extended, sitting on different papers, with the Core entry capping the available grade. Pearson's International GCSE specifications are mostly single tier, which means the decision a Cambridge family agonises over in Year 10 simply does not arise for a Pearson family - and a parent who has heard about tiering from a neighbour may spend months worrying about a choice their child's school never has to make.

The second is how practical science is assessed. Cambridge offers an alternative-to-practical written paper on most science syllabuses; Pearson assesses practical skills through a written paper of its own. In both cases the examination tests experimental reasoning on paper rather than bench technique, which is genuinely good news for a student taught online: the skill being examined is reading and criticising a method, designing a fair test on paper, and spotting the flaw in a described procedure. That is teachable over video as well as anywhere.

The third is the calendar, which is covered in its own section below. The table sets out what differs, with the detail a parent needs in order to buy the right help and ignore advice that applies to the other board.

sections.heading: How practical science is handled when the lessons are online
paragraphs: This is the question a Hydra Village parent asks within the first two minutes of a conversation about physics or chemistry, and it deserves a straight answer rather than reassurance. The laboratory work itself happens at school, where the equipment and the supervision are. A tutor does not replace that and should not pretend to.

What the examinations actually test, though, is largely not bench technique. Cambridge's alternative-to-practical paper and Pearson's practical-skills paper both examine experimental reasoning in writing: read a described method and find its flaw, identify the dependent and controlled variables, say why a measurement is unreliable and what would improve it, plot and interpret data that includes error. Those are reading and reasoning skills and they are taught as well on a shared screen as in a room.

The teaching method is specific. The student is shown a method written by someone else and asked what is wrong with it, repeatedly, across different contexts, until the habit forms. They are given data with uncertainties and asked what conclusion it supports and what it does not. They write evaluation paragraphs and have them marked against the scheme's wording rather than against a general impression. Students who do this stop writing about human error, which is the single most wasted paragraph in school science.

For Diploma students the picture is similar but the stakes are higher, because the internal assessment is a full written report on an investigation the student designs and runs. The design, the uncertainty treatment, the analysis and the evaluation are all reviewable over video; the data collection is not, and should not be. Any provider offering to supply data or to produce the report itself is offering malpractice, whatever language it uses.
bullets: Laboratory work stays at school, where the equipment and supervision are

sections.heading: Series, zones and the timetable that is the candidate's own risk
paragraphs: No competing page found in this market names a single examination series or deadline, which is a remarkable gap given that the dates are the plan. For a family out at this distance, sometimes dealing with a centre directly, the dates are also where the expensive mistakes live.

Cambridge runs its International GCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with a March series for some specifications and Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. That sentence is the reason to get the zone from the school's examinations officer rather than from a timetable found online.

For the March 2027 series Cambridge publishes final entries at 27 November 2026, an examination period from 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct on 13 May 2027 and certificates in late June. Pearson Edexcel's International GCSE examinations run in May and June and in November, with the November 2026 final timetable from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

That last pair of dates carries a planning implication families miss. The gap between sitting a November paper and receiving the grade can mean a decision about re-entering has to be taken before the previous result is in hand. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which can be revised, so every plan should be built on the live official document rather than on a date restated by a third party - this page included.

sections.heading: Sitting a paper as a private candidate
paragraphs: Some families in outlying communities end up arranging an entry themselves: a retake in a subject the school will not re-enter, an extra subject the school does not offer, or a series the school does not sit. It is entirely possible and it is also full of small requirements that are published but not advertised.

The first and hardest step is finding a centre that accepts private candidates, because not every school does and policies differ by subject and by series. The second is confirming that the centre offers the specific specification the student has been studying - a centre may run Cambridge and not Pearson, or one syllabus within a board and not another. The third is checking components: some subjects include requirements a private candidate cannot easily complete, and that can rule a subject out before any study begins.

After that it is deadlines and administration. The centre submits the entry on the candidate's behalf, by the board's final entry deadline - 27 November 2026 for the Cambridge March 2027 series, for example - and charges its own fees for doing so, which vary by centre and are a question for the centre rather than for a tutor. The timetable and, for Cambridge, the administrative zone have to be confirmed as soon as the final version is published. Results reach the centre first, and any review of results window is short.

A tutor's role in this is teaching and sequencing, not administration. What can be done is building the study plan backwards from the entry deadline, making sure the practice material matches the specification the centre offers, and flagging the questions to put to the examinations officer early. What cannot be done is entering a candidate, and no tutoring provider should imply otherwise.

sections.heading: Where marks go in each board's papers
paragraphs: Once the specification is settled, the useful conversation is about which questions lose marks, and the answers differ between boards even in the same subject. That is the strongest argument for matching a tutor to the code rather than to the subject name.

On Cambridge maths at Extended tier, the recurring losses sit in transformations of graphs, vectors, harder trigonometry and the long structured questions on Paper 4, where a student completes the demanding step and then answers a question slightly different from the one asked. On Pearson 4MA1 the phrasing of the longer questions trips students who learned on Cambridge material, and the formula provision differs enough that a student can waste minutes looking for something that is not there.

In the sciences, Cambridge's alternative-to-practical paper is a distinct skill that students often meet cold, because class time goes on content. Pearson's practical-skills questions test similar reasoning in a different format. In both, electricity in physics and mole calculations in chemistry account for a disproportionate share of lost marks, and in biology it is the precision of extended written answers rather than the breadth of recall.

Across both boards there is one loss larger than any topic: questions left unanswered at the end of a paper. Twelve marks blank costs more than any single misunderstood subject area, and the cause is pacing. It is fixed by sitting whole papers to time with a visible clock, marking them against that board's own published scheme, and repeating. That is uncomfortable, unglamorous and the most reliable intervention available.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs out here, and what the distance adds
paragraphs: Distance is the part of the price that nobody publishes. The market bands for tutoring are reasonably well documented once you look, and the pattern across every source is that travel costs money and the further out a household is, the more of it.

The figures, in AED and attributed: a budget online tutor, usually a university student, sits between 45 and 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from the low thirties. A qualified subject tutor working online sits between 150 and 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from 150 and IB from 200. A tutor travelling to a home runs 180 to 500, with Bestimate quoting 180 to 350 and independent home tutors 200 to 500. An IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist sits at 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing 270, and a premium named tutor can reach 650, which BartyED states openly.

Advertised monthly packages make the travel cost unusually visible: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits at home. Half the sessions for twice the money is the clearest published statement of what a drive is worth, and for a community out past Al Bahia the real figure would sit at the top of the in-home band rather than the bottom.

There is a second cost to distance that does not appear in any rate table: the pool. A tutor who knows Pearson 4PH1 specifically, and is willing to drive out here on a Tuesday, is a very short list and may be an empty one. Online delivery converts that from a geography problem into a scheduling problem, which is a far easier thing to solve. IB Gram quotes after a consultation and a trial lesson rather than publishing a rate card, since the span between a primary reading session and Paper 3 supervision is too wide for one number.

Travelling tutors AED 180-500, with the top of the band applying to outlying communities

sections.heading: Coursework, controlled components and what a tutor may touch
paragraphs: At IGCSE the amount of internally assessed work is smaller than at Diploma level but it still exists, and families often have no clear idea what help is permitted. The principle is the same across every board and every component: the work submitted has to be the student's own, the centre confirms that it is, and the consequence of a breach falls on the candidate.

What a tutor may do is teach the skills the component needs, explain how it is marked, discuss a plan the student has drafted, and give feedback on the student's own written work. For a Diploma student the same applies with more at stake: teaching the subject content, reading each criterion descriptor in plain language, interrogating a research question that cannot be answered in the word count, and reviewing a draft the student produced.

What a tutor may not do is supply material that reaches the submission. No paragraph, no processed dataset, no rewritten conclusion, no bibliography typed out for copying. Heavy line-editing is the same breach wearing a politer name, because a sentence composed by the tutor is a sentence the student did not write. At least one site competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price; buying one puts the student at risk of sanction, not the seller.

The related point about materials is worth stating in the same breath. Examination papers, mark schemes, grade boundary tables and syllabus documents belong to the boards, so they are referenced by series and question number, linked to the official source and worked through in the lesson rather than supplied as downloads. The student keeps their own annotated attempt, which is the artefact with value in any case, and the school holds licensed access for anything else.

sections.heading: What to establish before the first lesson
paragraphs: For a Hydra Village family the pre-lesson checklist matters more than for most, because the risk of buying help for the wrong examination is genuinely high in a community where siblings sit different boards. Five facts settle it, and all five are obtainable in a single email to the school.

First, the board and the syllabus code for each subject, per child. Second, the tier where one applies - Core or Extended on a Cambridge syllabus, or the paper route on a Pearson one. Third, the series the student is entered for, since a March, June or November entry changes the whole timeline. Fourth, for Cambridge candidates, which of the six administrative zones the centre sits in. Fifth, the grading scale in use, because a mock mark on an A* to G scale and one on a 9 to 1 scale are not interpretable against each other.

With those five facts, matching takes a day and the first lesson starts on the right material. Without them, the first two sessions go on finding out, which is an avoidable cost. The school's examinations officer or the subject teacher can supply all of it, and the front page of any past paper the student has actually sat usually carries the code and the paper number as well.

The sixth thing worth establishing is not academic. What time is the household genuinely back from the school run, given the distance out here, and which evenings are already committed? A slot that ignores the real arrival time will be missed often enough to break the arrangement, and in this community that time is later than the school's timetable suggests.
bullets: Board and syllabus code, per subject and per child
Tier or paper route where the specification has one
The series the student is entered for, and for Cambridge the administrative zone
The grading scale in use, so mock marks can be interpreted
The household's real arrival time from a long school run

process.title: Get the five facts from the school
process.description: Board, syllabus code, tier, series and grading scale, per subject and per child. One email to the examinations officer or subject teacher supplies all of them, and the front page of a past paper the student has sat usually carries the code too. This is the step that prevents a term of practice on the wrong specification.

process.title: Match to the code, then trial
process.description: A tutor who works to Cambridge 0580 Extended is not automatically the right tutor for Pearson 4MA1. The trial lesson is with the matched specialist rather than a coordinator, and it uses material from the student's own board so both sides can see whether the fit is right on real work.

process.title: Set the slot against the real arrival time
process.description: Out on the Dubai-road side the journey home is longer than the school timetable implies, and a slot booked at the optimistic end gets missed. We ask what time the door actually opens, which evenings are already taken, and whether Ramadan timing will move the slot later in the year.

process.title: Build the plan backwards from the entry deadline
process.description: The entry deadline, the series window, the mock dates and any school coursework deadlines go on one sheet, and the plan runs back from them. For a private candidacy, the questions for the centre are listed at this point rather than discovered in November.

process.title: Mark against that board's own scheme
process.description: Practice papers are marked against the published scheme for the student's specification, so the mark means what it will mean on the day. Where a student has moved boards, early sessions compare the same topic across both so the student can see what has changed in the phrasing.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the specification, not the subject
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607 and Pearson 4MA1 are three different examinations, and practice does not transfer between them. Matching on the code is the single biggest protection against a term of real mathematics taught towards the wrong paper.

whyPoints.title: Board dates from the boards
whyPoints.description: Every entry deadline, examination window and results date here is attributed to Cambridge or Pearson's own publication, including the warning that the wrong zone timetable is the candidate's risk. Where a date could not be verified, as with the IB sessions, it is omitted.

whyPoints.title: Practical science taught as the paper tests it
whyPoints.description: Laboratory work stays at school. What the papers examine is experimental reasoning in writing, which is taught by repeatedly criticising other people's methods, and that works as well over a shared screen as in a room.

whyPoints.title: Honest about private candidacy
whyPoints.description: A tutor can sequence the study and flag the questions for the centre. A tutor cannot enter a candidate, cannot promise a centre will accept one, and should not imply either. The steps and their owners are set out so a family can act on them.

whyPoints.title: No travel in the rate
whyPoints.description: UAE lessons are one-to-one over live video. For a community this far out the published in-home bands would apply at their upper end, and the advertised package comparison - half the sessions for twice the money - makes the difference concrete.

whyPoints.title: Materials handled legally
whyPoints.description: Papers, mark schemes, boundary tables and syllabus documents belong to the boards. They are referenced by series and question, linked to the official source and worked through in the lesson. What the student keeps is their own annotated attempt.

faqs.question: How do I find out which exam board my child is entered with?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's examinations officer or subject teacher for the syllabus code, not the subject name. The front page of any past paper the student has actually sat usually carries the code and the paper number as well. This matters because Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607 and Pearson 4MA1 are three different mathematics examinations with different paper structures and formula provision. Practice material does not transfer between them, and a student drilled on the wrong set has practised real mathematics towards the wrong paper.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both of our children if they sit different boards?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but it should not be assumed. A teacher who works to Cambridge 0580 Extended may know Pearson 4MA1 well or barely at all, and the differences in question phrasing and formula provision are enough to matter at the top grades. Where a tutor genuinely works to both, they should be able to tell you how the long questions differ in each. Where they cannot, two tutors is the right answer, and because lessons are online that costs nothing extra in logistics.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge harder than Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Neither is harder in a way that should influence a choice, and in most cases the choice belongs to the school rather than the family. They differ in structure: Cambridge tiers most maths and science syllabuses into Core and Extended on different papers, while Pearson's International GCSE specifications are mostly single tier. They also use different grading scales on some syllabuses, so a mock mark on an A* to G scale and one on a 9 to 1 scale cannot be read against each other without checking which applies.

faqs.question: What is the alternative-to-practical paper, and can it be taught online?
faqs.answer: It is a written paper on most Cambridge science syllabuses that examines experimental reasoning rather than bench technique: read a described method and find its flaw, identify variables, say why a measurement is unreliable, interpret data with error in it. Pearson assesses practical skills through its own written paper. Because what is examined is reading and reasoning, it teaches as well over a shared screen as in a room. The laboratory work itself stays at school, where the equipment and supervision are.

faqs.question: What time can lessons start for a household out at Hydra Village?
faqs.answer: Later than the school timetable implies. The run back from the Khalifa City and Al Raha campuses, or from the islands, puts most households here home between half past four and half past five, and a child travelling by bus with a multi-stop route arrives later again. Most families settle on a slot between 17:30 and 19:00, with examination candidates sometimes later. Because every lesson is online and nobody is driving out, a slot can be moved to another evening without re-planning anyone's route.

faqs.question: My child changed schools and the papers look different. What do we do?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a format problem rather than a content problem, because that is usually what it is. A student who has moved boards mid-course generally knows the material and not the question conventions: command words, mark allocation, how the new board phrases what it wants. Four to six sessions comparing the same topic across both specifications, followed by practice on the new board's papers marked against its own scheme, closes it. It is one of the cheapest interventions available and one of the most commonly skipped.

faqs.question: When is the Cambridge March series, and who should take it?
faqs.answer: For 2027 the examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March, with final entries closing on 27 November 2026, forecast grades due on 27 February 2027 and results on Direct on 13 May 2027. It is available for some specifications rather than all, and is used by students whose school year is structured differently or who want an earlier sitting. Confirm with the school's examinations officer which of your child's subjects are even offered in that series before planning around it.

faqs.question: Can we enter our child for an IGCSE ourselves?
faqs.answer: Yes, through a centre that accepts private candidates, which not every school does. The steps are: find such a centre, confirm it offers the exact specification your child has studied, check whether any component is impractical for a private candidate, let the centre submit the entry by the board's deadline and pay its fees, confirm the timetable and the administrative zone, then collect results through the centre. A tutor can sequence the study and list the questions for the examinations officer, but cannot enter a candidate.

faqs.question: How long before the results of a November paper arrive?
faqs.answer: Longer than families expect, which affects retake planning. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and its June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day. The practical consequence is that a decision about re-entering a subject can fall due before the previous grade is in hand, so the plan has to be made on mock evidence rather than on the actual result. Confirm the current series dates on Pearson's own support pages.

faqs.question: Do you teach Pearson 4PH1 as well as Cambridge 0625 physics?
faqs.answer: Yes, but as separate matches rather than one tutor covering both by default. The physics overlaps heavily; the paper split, the question phrasing and the practical-skills assessment do not. A student entered for 4PH1 who practises 0625 papers will meet unfamiliar phrasing on the day, and at the top grades that costs marks. The first thing we establish is the code on the entry, and practice is then drawn only from that board, marked against its own published scheme.

faqs.question: Which topics cost the most marks at IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: In physics, electricity and the moments and momentum questions account for a disproportionate share across both boards. In chemistry it is mole calculations and the qualitative analysis tables, which collapse under pressure when they were memorised as a list rather than understood as chemistry. In biology it is the precision of extended written answers rather than breadth of recall. Alongside all of those sits the largest single loss, which is questions left unanswered at the end of the paper through poor pacing.

faqs.question: Will a tutor send us past papers for the right board?
faqs.answer: They will tell you exactly which papers to use - series, paper number and question numbers - and link you to the board's own site, but they will not supply them as downloads. Examination papers, mark schemes, boundary tables and syllabus documents are the copyright of Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and distributing them is infringement. The school holds licensed access, and the subject teacher is often the fastest legitimate route. In the lesson the paper is worked through on screen and the student keeps their own annotated attempt.

faqs.question: Is a tutor allowed to help with internally assessed work at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Within limits that are the same across every board. A tutor may teach the skills the component needs, explain how it is marked, discuss a plan the student has drafted and give feedback on the student's own written work. A tutor may not supply material that reaches the submission, and heavy line-editing is the same breach under a politer name. The centre confirms the work is the candidate's own, and the consequence of a breach falls on the candidate rather than on anyone who sold the help.

faqs.question: Does living this far out limit which tutors we can get?
faqs.answer: It would if a tutor had to drive. The published in-home bands run AED 180 to 500 an hour and would apply at their upper end this far from the city, and the real constraint is worse than the rate: a specialist in one specific specification who is also willing to drive out past Al Bahia on a weekday evening is a very short list. Because every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, the question becomes which hour suits rather than which tutor is nearby, which is a far easier problem.

faqs.question: What should we have ready before the first session?
faqs.answer: Five facts and one time. The board and syllabus code for the subject, the tier or paper route where the specification has one, the series the student is entered for, the administrative zone if the entry is with Cambridge, and the grading scale in use so mock marks can be interpreted. The time is when the household is genuinely back from the school run. With those in hand the first lesson starts on the right material instead of spending two sessions finding out what the right material is.

abu-dhabi/hydra-village.closingHeading: Settle the specification, then book the hour
abu-dhabi/hydra-village.closingBody: The most useful thing a Hydra Village family can do before hiring anybody is send one email to the school and come back with the syllabus code, the tier, the series and the grading scale for each subject. From there a match takes a day, practice comes from the right board marked against its own scheme, and the plan runs backwards from a published entry deadline rather than forwards from today. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, every board date on this page is attributed to Cambridge or Pearson, and the slot is set against the time your household is actually home.

abu-dhabi/ib-biology-ia-help.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach IB Biology at Standard and Higher Level and have supervised scientific investigations through to submission. Choose on the basis of what they can show you: a marked draft, a criterion breakdown, and a timetable that fits an Abu Dhabi school week.

intro.heading: What Abu Dhabi parents are really asking when they search for Biology IA help
paragraphs: Almost every enquiry that reaches us with these words attached has the same shape. A Diploma student at a school in Khalifa City, on Saadiyat, or along the Al Raha corridor has an internal deadline eight to twelve weeks away. There is a research question, some data in a spreadsheet, and a teacher comment that says the analysis needs more depth. Nobody in the house can tell whether that comment is worth two marks or nine, and nobody can tell whether another month of evenings will change it.

That is a measurement problem before it is a Biology problem. The scientific investigation in the current IB Biology guide carries 20% of the final grade at both Standard and Higher Level and is marked out of 24 across four criteria. Those criteria are published, the strands inside them are published, and the mark your child's teacher awards is defensible or it is not. A parent who cannot see the criteria is being asked to judge progress by mood, which is why the first session here produces a document rather than a feeling.

The approach on this page is deliberately evidence-first. A tutor reads the existing draft before any teaching happens, marks it against each criterion, and hands back a written breakdown with the mark bands named and the specific sentences or figures that sit behind each one. From that point every session has a target you can check: Research design was weak on the control of confounding variables, here is the revised method, here is what the tutor expects it to be worth now. You are never asked to accept that things are going well.

Abu Dhabi adds its own constraints. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and internal assessment deadlines are set by each school rather than by the regulator or by the IB, so two Diploma students living on the same street in Al Reem can be working to dates three weeks apart. Travel across the island and over the Sheikh Zayed and Mussafah bridges eats the usable part of a weekday evening. Live online sessions remove that problem rather than working around it.

Honesty about scope matters as much as the teaching. A tutor working on a scientific investigation explains biology, questions a method, teaches the statistics, and marks a draft against the criteria. A tutor does not author any sentence of the report, supply figures, or hand over a finished document. The student types every word. That line is not a marketing position; it is what keeps an IB candidate out of a malpractice investigation, and it is stated in writing before the first session runs, in plain terms, so that nobody discovers the boundary halfway through a deadline week.

abu-dhabi/ib-biology-ia-help.programmesIntro: Biology investigation work sits inside a programme, and the programme decides what a session can usefully do. These are the three IB structures Abu Dhabi families most often bring to us when the search term is Biology IA help.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two-year Diploma, where the scientific investigation lives. Biology is taken at Standard or Higher Level, and the investigation is identical in form at both levels: one student-designed piece of practical work, reported in no more than 3,000 words, marked out of 24 by the teacher and subject to IB moderation. Higher Level students carry additional syllabus content and a longer Paper 2, but they are not asked for a larger investigation.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts are concentrated in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, on Saadiyat and Yas, and in a handful of long-established island schools. Several of these schools run the investigation across the end of DP1 and the start of DP2, which means data collection often falls in the hottest months when fieldwork outside is impractical. Laboratory-based or secondary-data designs tend to be the realistic choice.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Where investigation skills are built or missed. MYP Sciences is marked against four criteria, and Criterion B, inquiring and designing, together with Criterion C, processing and evaluating, are the direct ancestors of the Diploma investigation. A student who has written variables, hypotheses and evaluations against those criteria for five years arrives in DP1 able to design. A student who has mostly followed printed method sheets does not.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has several IB continuum schools running MYP into the Diploma, alongside British-curriculum schools that place students into DP1 straight from IGCSE. Students arriving from the IGCSE route frequently meet an open-ended practical design for the first time in DP1. We treat that as a specific, teachable gap rather than a weakness, and it is usually four to six sessions of work.

programmes.name: Diploma core: Extended Essay, TOK and CAS
programmes.description: The core competes with the investigation for the same weeks. A Biology Extended Essay is a different task from the investigation, with its own word limit and its own supervisor, and students who take both on in the same term are usually the ones who run out of time. Mapping the core deadlines against the investigation deadline is often the single most useful hour a DP1 family buys, and it costs nothing in biology content.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools set their own core deadlines and most publish them to parents at the start of DP1. Bring that calendar to the first session. Where a Biology Extended Essay and the investigation share a laboratory technique, there are rules about reusing work between components, and your DP coordinator is the person who confirms what your school permits.

abu-dhabi/ib-biology-ia-help.subjectsIntro: Investigation work rarely arrives alone. These are the subjects Abu Dhabi Diploma families most often pair with Biology support, described by what the assessment actually demands rather than by topic list.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Four themes, a 36% Paper 1 split between multiple choice and data-based questions, a 44% Paper 2 of structured and extended response, and the 20% investigation. Most marks are lost not on recall but on command terms: outline, explain, suggest and evaluate each want a different shape of answer, and students who revise content without practising the verbs plateau at a 4 or 5.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The common second science in Abu Dhabi Diploma timetables, and the one whose own investigation deadline usually clashes with Biology. Chemistry rewards quantitative processing, so students often bring stronger uncertainty handling to Biology than their Biology teaching gave them. That transfer is worth naming in a session rather than discovering by accident.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Shares physiology content with Biology and runs its own investigation. Abu Dhabi students taking both often reuse a measurement technique such as heart rate or reaction time, which raises a legitimate question about overlap between components. The answer comes from the DP coordinator, and the design can be adjusted early at no cost.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary option with a different internal assessment structure from the Biology investigation. Students who switch into or out of it mid-DP1 lose the most time, because the design conventions and the mark allocations are not transferable. A mapping session before the switch is cheaper than a rescue afterwards.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Its internal assessment is an experimental study with inferential statistics, so a Biology student taking Psychology has usually met significance testing before their Biology teacher raises it. The two reports have different word limits and different criteria, and treating one as a template for the other costs marks in both.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Where the statistics in a Biology investigation are actually taught. Chi-squared tests of association, correlation coefficients and basic hypothesis testing sit in this course. A Biology student who takes Analysis and Approaches instead may have met none of them formally, which is a predictable four-session gap rather than a sign of weakness.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most Abu Dhabi students take if they are aiming at engineering or physical sciences. It is stronger on calculus and weaker on applied statistics than Applications and Interpretation, so error bars, standard deviation and test selection usually have to be taught explicitly for the investigation.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Relevant because the investigation is a written report assessed partly on clarity of communication inside each criterion. Students who write well in English A still lose marks in Biology for burying a conclusion in narrative instead of stating it against the data. The fix is structural and takes about two sessions.

subjects.name: Biology Extended Essay
subjects.description: A separate 4,000-word research task with its own supervisor, frequently running in the same term as the investigation. Support here is process coaching: question focus, source quality, argument structure and the supervisor relationship. No part of the essay is written for the student, and the reflection sessions with the school supervisor remain the student's own.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.description: The place to fix design skills before DP1 rather than during it. Criterion B asks for a testable hypothesis, variables and a method; Criterion C asks for processing, presentation and evaluation. Students who can do both against the MYP wording arrive in the Diploma needing content teaching rather than a crash course in experimental design.

abu-dhabi/ib-biology-ia-help.modesIntro: Three ways families buy investigation support, chosen by how much of the task is still open. The honest answer to which one fits is usually decided by the number of weeks left, not by budget.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the investigation
modes.description: A fixed slot from research question to submission, typically ten to fourteen weeks. Each session takes one criterion, works on the current draft, and closes with written notes. This is the version where you can see movement week by week, because each set of notes names the mark band the tutor thinks the draft now sits in and why.

Research design for a student whose variables are not controlled, or data analysis for a student whose graphs carry no uncertainty. It suits families who already have school feedback they trust and want one thing fixed rather than general supervision. The block ends with a before-and-after marked draft.

The tutor marks the complete draft against all four criteria and returns a written breakdown with the specific strands that are unevidenced. It changes nothing by itself; what it does is tell the student exactly where the remaining hours should go, in writing.

sections.heading: The evidence a first session produces, and why it comes before any teaching
paragraphs: A first session on a Biology investigation produces four things: a marked copy of the existing draft, a criterion-by-criterion note saying which mark band each criterion currently sits in, a short list of the strands with no evidence behind them at all, and a plan with dates. None of that is teaching. It is diagnosis, and it exists so that the rest of the work can be checked rather than believed.

The reason this matters in Abu Dhabi specifically is that school feedback arrives in very different formats across the emirate. One school issues a filled criterion grid with band descriptors circled. Another returns a paragraph of comments in a shared document. A third gives a predicted mark with no breakdown. A parent comparing a child at Raha International with a cousin at Brighton College is comparing two incompatible reports, which is why an independent marked draft is the only common currency.

The marked draft also settles the most common argument in the house, which is whether the problem is biology or writing. A student who can explain osmosis correctly out loud and still scores in the lowest band for conclusion does not have a content gap. They have a reporting gap, and those are fixed in different ways and in different numbers of hours. Working out which one you are paying for is worth doing before you buy ten sessions of the wrong thing, and it takes one reading of the draft rather than a term of observation.
bullets: A marked copy of the student's existing draft, annotated by criterion
A written note placing each criterion in a mark band, with reasons

A dated plan running back from the school's internal deadline

sections.heading: Week by week: what changes in the draft and how you check it
paragraphs: Progress on an investigation is not smooth and it is not visible in a mark until late. The useful measure is whether a named strand moved from unevidenced to evidenced in the student's own text. That is checkable by a parent who has never studied biology, because the tutor's note says which paragraph or figure now carries the evidence and the student can point to it.

The table below is the shape of a twelve-week run, counted forward from a first session. Dates are school-set in Abu Dhabi, so the column that matters is the one naming what comes back to you rather than the week number. A student starting later compresses the sequence rather than skipping stages, and the first thing to go is usually the second round of data collection.

Two warnings about reading a plan like this. A week where nothing appears to change is often the week the research question is being narrowed, which is the highest-value work in the whole task and produces almost no visible text. And a draft that looks finished at week six is usually a draft with a conclusion that restates the data instead of answering the research question, which is a six-mark problem hiding behind a tidy document. Read the plan as a sequence of deliverables rather than a schedule: each stage either produces a document you can hold or it has not happened, and a student who cannot show the processed data at week eight is not eight weeks in regardless of how many sessions have been paid for.

sections.heading: The research question decides most of the mark before any data exist
paragraphs: More investigation marks are lost at the research question than anywhere else, and they are lost before a single measurement is taken. A question that names no independent variable, no dependent variable and no range cannot be answered by data, so the design strands have nothing to reward and the conclusion has nothing to answer. Students arrive with questions that are really topics, and teachers often approve them because the topic is sound.

Abu Dhabi adds a practical filter that families rarely consider. Outdoor fieldwork between May and September is genuinely difficult, school laboratory access is timetabled and limited, and anything involving human participants needs consent arranged through the school. A question that would work in a temperate September does not survive an Abu Dhabi one. Secondary-data designs using published datasets are a legitimate route and are frequently the stronger choice, not a fallback.

The practical test is whether the question can be written as a sentence containing a measured variable, a changed variable, five or more levels of that change, and a stated organism, tissue or dataset. If it cannot, no amount of later work rescues the design marks. This is also the cheapest stage to fix: narrowing a question is usually one session, while rescuing a weak one after data collection means collecting data again. The table below takes five questions in the form students genuinely arrive with, says what a marker cannot reward in each, and gives the version that survives. The pattern across all five is the same: add units, add a range, name the subject, and fix the endpoint.

sections.heading: The statistics nobody budgeted for, taught on your child's own numbers
paragraphs: The single most common unbudgeted cost in a Biology investigation is statistics. A student taking Analysis and Approaches rather than Applications and Interpretation may have met no formal hypothesis testing at all, and the Biology teacher is not timetabled to teach it. The result is a draft with a mean, a bar chart and no indication of whether the difference is anything more than noise, which is the data analysis criterion losing marks quietly.

Test selection is not a matter of preference. It follows from the design: two independent groups with continuous measurements point one way, categorical counts in a contingency table point another, and two continuous variables measured on the same subjects point a third. The error that costs marks is applying a test of difference to a correlation design, or reporting a significance value without saying what the null hypothesis was.

This is taught on the student's own spreadsheet rather than a textbook example, because the thing that has to survive is their data, with their sample size and their missing values. A student who has calculated standard deviation by hand on their own five repeats, then plotted error bars that overlap, has learned something a worked example cannot deliver: that their own result may not be significant, and that saying so clearly earns marks rather than losing them. An honest null result, properly tested and properly reported, sits in a higher band than an overclaimed difference with no test behind it.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and the Abu Dhabi rule about your child's own teacher
paragraphs: The investigation must be the student's own work. A tutor may explain biology, challenge a method, teach statistics, mark a draft against the criteria and say that a conclusion does not answer the research question. A tutor may not author sentences, generate figures, supply a method, or hand back a version of the report with the problems silently repaired. The distinction is not subtle and it is not negotiable: the student's name goes on an authenticity declaration, and a breach is an IB malpractice matter for the candidate.

There is a specific Abu Dhabi dimension that families ask about constantly. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than quoted policy and verify it against the current ADEK document, but the practical advice is simple: do not arrange paid sessions with the teacher who will mark the investigation.

The same reasoning applies to the commercial offers that circulate in Abu Dhabi parent groups, where a completed investigation is sold as a package with a price attached. Buying one puts the candidate's whole Diploma at risk, not just the Biology grade, and schools detect them more often than the sellers admit. What a legitimate tutor produces is a marked copy of your child's draft with the problems named. If anyone offers a finished report instead, the offer itself tells you what you are dealing with.
