sections.heading: What investigation support costs in the Abu Dhabi market
paragraphs: Market rates here are published by providers in dirhams and vary by a factor of ten, so the number alone tells a parent almost nothing. What changes the figure is who is teaching, whether the hour includes marking a draft outside the session, and whether travel is being paid for. The table below gathers published provider bands rather than quoting a price for this service, and each band is attributed to where it was read in October 2026.

Two patterns are worth knowing before any call. In-home rates in the Abu Dhabi market carry travel inside them, which is why the same tutor's visiting rate sits above their online rate; you are buying the drive across the island as well as the teaching. And monthly packages advertised in the emirate are usually priced on session count rather than on marking, so a package that looks cheaper per hour can include no written feedback at all.

The right question to ask a prospective tutor is not the hourly figure but what arrives in writing afterwards. An hour that ends with a marked draft and a criterion note is a different product from an hour of conversation at the same price. IB Gram's own position is to start with a free trial session, with the conditions stated up front, and to quote only after a draft has been read, because quoting before that means guessing at how much work the task needs.

sections.heading: Online draft work against a visiting tutor, on the same task
paragraphs: IB Gram does not make home visits in Abu Dhabi; one-to-one tuition here is delivered live over video, and home visiting is a service offered only in India. That is a limit worth stating plainly rather than burying, because the honest comparison on investigation work favours the online format for reasons that have nothing to do with price.

Investigation work is document work. The student and the tutor need the same draft open, the same spreadsheet open, and a record of what changed between versions. Screen sharing with version history does that natively; a visiting tutor leans over a laptop and leaves no trail. The other difference is the tutor pool. A family in Al Shamkha choosing from tutors willing to drive to Al Shamkha on a Tuesday is choosing from a short list, and a Biology Higher Level specialist who can mark a scientific investigation may not be on it.

Against that, a visiting tutor is better at presence. A student who will not sit down without an adult in the room benefits from someone physically there, and no video call changes that. Where that is the real problem, the honest answer is that a visiting generalist supervising homework and an online specialist marking the investigation are different purchases, and some Abu Dhabi families buy both. sections.heading: Who sets what: ADEK, your school, and the IB
paragraphs: Parents often assume a single authority governs the investigation deadline, the mark and the appeal route. Three different bodies are involved and only one of them is reachable by a phone call. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and publishes its own inspection ratings, which tells you about the school but nothing about an individual internal assessment. The IB owns the criteria, the word ceiling and moderation. Your school owns the deadline, the draft policy and the laboratory timetable.

That division explains why answers differ between families at different Abu Dhabi schools. How many drafts a teacher may comment on, whether a submission is accepted late, and when the internal deadline falls are school decisions taken inside IB guidance. The person who can confirm all three is the DP coordinator, and the request is a short email rather than a meeting. It is worth sending before buying any support at all, because the deadline sets the plan.

Moderation is the part that surprises people most. The teacher marks the investigation and the IB moderates a sample, so a school mark can move. This is not a reason to distrust the teacher; it is a reason to keep the draft and the criterion notes, because an inflated internal mark that falls on moderation is far more painful in July than a realistic one in February. Independent marking against the published criteria is a way of finding that out early.

sections.heading: Equivalency, UAE universities and what the investigation is worth later
paragraphs: A Biology investigation mark is never read on its own by a university. It is 20% of a subject grade, and that subject grade is one of six. Families in Abu Dhabi usually ask about it in the context of medicine or health sciences applications, where the relevant question is which subjects were taken at Higher Level and what the overall points total was, not what a single internal component scored.

Certificate equivalency through the UAE Ministry of Education is a separate process from admission and is not something a tutoring service performs or guarantees. The published requirements for the British track are specific: five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count of five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. The American track sets separate English and mathematics test thresholds.

For the IB there is no points figure published here, deliberately. Secondary sources circulate numbers that could not be confirmed on the ministry's own pages, and publishing an unverified threshold would be worse than publishing nothing. Check the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority directly, and ask your school's university counsellor at the same time. What a strong investigation does contribute is a Biology grade that holds up, which is the part an admissions office actually reads, and the part that survives any later change to an equivalency rule.

process.title: Send the draft and the deadline
process.description: Share whatever exists, even if it is three paragraphs and a spreadsheet, along with the school's internal deadline and any teacher feedback already received. A tutor reads it before the first session. Nothing useful can be planned from a subject name and a year group alone, and the draft is what makes the first hour diagnostic rather than introductory.

process.title: Free trial session with a marked draft
process.description: The first session is free, limited to one session per student, and runs as a working session rather than a sales call. The tutor marks the draft against all four criteria and returns a written note placing each criterion in a band. If the fit is wrong, you keep the marked draft and the notes and owe nothing.

process.title: Agree the plan against the school's dates
process.description: The plan runs backwards from your school's deadline, not forwards from today. It names which criterion each session targets, when data collection has to be finished, and what happens if the laboratory slot moves. Where the deadline is too close for the full sequence, the plan says which stages are being dropped and what that costs in marks.

process.title: Weekly sessions with written notes
process.description: Each session works on the live draft and ends with notes naming the criterion, the change made and the next task. Notes go to the parent as well as the student. This is the record that lets you judge the work without reading biology, and it is the reason a plateau becomes visible in week four rather than in July.

process.title: Pre-submission re-mark
process.description: Before the student submits, the full draft is marked again against all four criteria and compared against the baseline from session one. The comparison is the honest answer to whether the money worked. It also catches the late problems: a word count over the ceiling, an uncited dataset, or a conclusion that still restates data instead of answering the question.

whyPoints.title: The marked draft comes before the sales conversation
whyPoints.description: The first thing produced is a criterion-marked copy of your child's existing work, not a brochure. It is yours whether or not you continue. This is also the only reliable way to find out whether the problem is biology content, experimental design or report writing, and those three cost very different numbers of hours to fix.

whyPoints.title: Progress is written down, not asserted
whyPoints.description: Every session ends with a note naming the criterion worked on and the change made in the draft. You can check it against the document. A parent who cannot read a Biology syllabus can still read a note that says Criterion C moved from unevidenced to partially evidenced and see the paragraph that did it.

whyPoints.title: Statistics taught on the student's own data
whyPoints.description: Test selection, standard deviation and error bars are taught on the spreadsheet the student actually collected, with their sample size and their gaps. Worked textbook examples do not transfer. The measure of success is that the student can redo the analysis alone, because that is what the report has to evidence.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line is stated before the first session
whyPoints.description: What a tutor will and will not do is set out in writing before any money is involved: explanation, challenge, teaching and marking, with no text, figures or methods supplied. Families who have met the completed-coursework offers circulating in Abu Dhabi tend to ask for this in writing, and it is better given unprompted.

whyPoints.description: Because sessions run over video, a Biology Higher Level specialist who can mark a scientific investigation is available to a family in Al Shamkha on the same terms as one on Saadiyat. The alternative, in practice, is choosing from whoever is willing to drive to your community on a weekday evening.

whyPoints.description: Where no Biology specialist is free in the slot you want, we say so and give the realistic wait rather than substituting a general science tutor. For a 24-mark investigation that distinction decides whether the hours are worth buying at all, and a wrong match discovered in week three has cost both money and weeks.

faqs.question: What does IB Biology IA help in Abu Dhabi actually involve week to week?
faqs.answer: It involves working on your child's own scientific investigation, one criterion at a time, in a live online session. A typical run opens with a marked baseline draft, then moves through the research question, the method, data collection, processing and statistics, the conclusion and the evaluation. Each session ends with written notes naming the criterion addressed, what changed in the draft, and the next task. Those notes go to the parent as well as the student. Nothing is written for the student at any stage; the tutor explains, questions, teaches and marks, and the student does the writing.

faqs.question: How many marks is the Biology scientific investigation worth and how are they divided?
faqs.answer: Under the current IB Biology guide the investigation carries 20% of the final grade at both Standard and Higher Level and is marked out of 24. Those 24 marks sit across four criteria, six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The practical consequence is that a student who writes a beautiful conclusion but designed a method with no controlled variables has capped themselves at eighteen before the report is read. Confirm the exact allocation against the subject guide your school issues, since guides are revised and the school's copy is the one your teacher marks from.

faqs.question: My son's research question was approved by his teacher but a tutor says it is too vague. Who is right?
faqs.answer: Both can be right, because approval and marking are different judgements. A teacher approving a topic is often confirming it is safe, ethical and achievable in the school laboratory. A marker is asking whether the question names a measured variable, a changed variable with a stated range, and a specific organism, tissue or dataset. A question can clear the first test and fail the second. The practical move is to rewrite the question to that specification and take it back to the teacher, who will almost always accept a tighter version of something already approved.

faqs.question: Is a secondary-data investigation treated as a weaker option in Abu Dhabi schools?
faqs.answer: No. The criteria do not award marks for having stood in a laboratory. A design built on a published dataset is assessed on the same four criteria as a practical one and can score at the top band if the question is sharp, the source is properly described and the processing is sound. For families in the emirate it is often the stronger route, because outdoor fieldwork between May and September is impractical and laboratory slots are timetabled and limited. What a secondary design must do is state who collected the data, when, by what method, and its limitations.

faqs.question: Our Biology class is behind the syllabus and the investigation is due. Which problem do we pay to fix first?
faqs.answer: The investigation, almost always. It is a fixed-deadline component worth 20%, and a missed or weak submission cannot be recovered by revision later. Syllabus content, by contrast, can be caught up in the months before the written papers, and a good deal of it will be retaught in revision anyway. The one exception is when the investigation itself depends on a topic the class has not reached, in which case the teaching narrows to that topic rather than to the whole backlog. A marked draft tells you which situation you are in.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether the Biology sessions are actually working before the mark comes back?
faqs.answer: Compare the written criterion notes across sessions against the draft itself. A working sequence shows named strands moving from unevidenced to evidenced, in the student's own text, with the tutor pointing at the paragraph or figure that now carries the evidence. A sequence that is not working shows the same comment repeated in different words for a month. You do not need biology to read that pattern. The pre-submission re-mark against the week-one baseline is the other check, and it is the one that answers the question in writing.

faqs.question: Does my child need statistics for the Biology investigation if they take Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and that is the most common unbudgeted cost in the task. Hypothesis testing, chi-squared tests of association and correlation sit in Applications and Interpretation rather than Analysis and Approaches, so a student on the Analysis route may have met none of them formally. The Biology teacher is not timetabled to teach them. Expect roughly four sessions, taught on the student's own spreadsheet rather than on textbook examples, covering spread, uncertainty, test selection and how to state a null hypothesis and a significance threshold in the report.

faqs.question: Can we pay my daughter's own Biology teacher at her Abu Dhabi school for extra investigation sessions?
faqs.answer: Treat that as the wrong route. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers giving paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording against the ADEK policy document yourself before relying on it. Beyond the rules, the teacher marking the work should not also be paid to improve it, which is a conflict a moderator can reasonably question.

faqs.question: Someone in a parents group is selling a finished Biology investigation. What is the actual risk?
faqs.answer: The risk is the whole Diploma, not the Biology grade. Submitted work carries an authenticity declaration in the candidate's name, and IB academic honesty rules treat submitting another person's work as malpractice, with consequences that can extend to the award of the diploma itself. Schools detect these more often than sellers suggest, because the writing does not match the student's other work and the process leaves no draft history. A legitimate tutor returns a marked copy of your child's draft with problems named, never a document to submit.

faqs.question: What does Biology investigation support cost in Abu Dhabi, and what should the hour include?
faqs.answer: Published rates in the UAE market run from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutoring, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel inside the rate, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB specialist, with premium examiner-led provision quoted higher. Those are other providers' published figures as read in October 2026, not our price. The question that matters more is what arrives in writing afterwards: an hour ending in a marked draft is a different product from an hour of conversation.

faqs.question: Why is there no in-home option in Abu Dhabi when other providers offer one?
faqs.answer: Because IB Gram delivers UAE tuition live online and runs home visiting only in India, which we would rather state than obscure. On investigation work the online format is also the better fit: both parties need the same draft and spreadsheet open with a version history, which screen sharing does natively and a laptop on a kitchen table does not. It also widens the choice of tutor from those willing to drive to your community on a weekday to any Biology Higher Level specialist who can mark a scientific investigation.

faqs.question: Three weeks to the deadline and the data are collected but nothing is processed. Is it salvageable?
faqs.answer: Usually, if the data can support any analysis at all. That is the first thing checked, because no amount of writing rescues five repeats with no variation. Where the data hold up, three weeks is enough for a pre-submission review, a statistics block on the student's own numbers, and a conclusion and evaluation rewritten against the criteria. What is not realistic in that window is redesigning the method or collecting again. The review says plainly which of those two situations you are in before any further hours are bought.

faqs.question: Does the 3,000-word ceiling on the report include tables, graphs and the bibliography?
faqs.answer: The conventional position is that the ceiling applies to the body of the report rather than to data tables, graph labels, citations or the bibliography, but the only answer that protects your child is the one in the subject guide the school is marking from, confirmed by the DP coordinator. Ask in writing and keep the reply. What is universally true is that students over the limit usually have narrative to cut rather than data: background that belongs in two sentences, and a conclusion that retells the results before answering the question.

faqs.question: Can sessions move to post-Iftar times during Ramadan without a rescheduling charge?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most Abu Dhabi families ask for it. Later evening slots after Iftar work for Diploma students who are fasting, and reduced school hours during Ramadan change what a weekday afternoon looks like in any case. The practical planning point is that Ramadan and Eid tend to fall across the weeks when DP2 students are finishing investigations and starting revision, so it is worth agreeing the shifted timetable several weeks ahead rather than in the first week. Slot changes agreed in advance carry no fee.

faqs.question: What happens if no Biology Higher Level specialist is free in the slot we want?
faqs.answer: We say so, give the realistic wait, and offer the nearest alternative explicitly labelled as such, rather than quietly substituting a general science tutor. For a 24-mark scientific investigation that distinction decides whether the hours are worth buying: a tutor who has not supervised one cannot mark a draft against the four criteria with any authority. Most families would rather wait ten days for the right match than discover in week three that the match was wrong, having spent both money and weeks they cannot get back.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with students in Abu Dhabi need a UAE permit, and how do we check?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to groups including school and government staff, private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you. Ask any tutor directly and apply through the MoHRE channels.

abu-dhabi/ib-biology-ia-help.closingHeading: Start with the draft, not with a quote
abu-dhabi/ib-biology-ia-help.closingBody: Send the scientific investigation as it stands, the school's internal deadline, and whatever feedback the teacher has already given. The first session is free, one per student, and runs as working time rather than a sales call: your child's draft comes back marked against all four criteria, with a written note placing each one in a band and listing the strands that carry no evidence yet. Keep that document whatever you decide next. If the fit is wrong, you have still learned whether the problem is biology, design or writing, which is the question most Abu Dhabi families actually arrived with.

intro.heading: What a parent in Abu Dhabi is really choosing between
paragraphs: Searches for IB classes in Abu Dhabi almost always start with a specific trigger: a report card where one subject has dropped two grades, an IA draft returned with comments nobody at home can decode, or a mock paper that came back at 3 when the predicted grade was a 5. The word "classes" is doing a lot of work in that search. It can mean a group of twelve students in a tuition centre off Al Falah Street, a pair of friends sharing a tutor, a school's own after-school subject clinic, or a single student and a single teacher working through a marked paper line by line. Those four things cost different amounts, fix different problems, and fail in different ways.

The distinction matters more in the Diploma Programme than in almost any other curriculum, because the DP spreads its marks so widely. A student sits six subjects, three of them at Higher Level, and each one carries an internal assessment worth between a fifth and a third of the final grade. On top of that sit the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, which together can move a Diploma total by up to three points. Forty-two points come from the six subjects, three from the core, and the ceiling is 45. A content-revision class does nothing for the eight or nine separate internal-assessment deadlines that run through DP1 and DP2, and those deadlines are where Abu Dhabi families most often tell us the term fell apart.

Abu Dhabi adds its own constraints. Private schools in the emirate are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools, and enrolment is spread across three very different belts: the island, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, and the newer mainland communities out towards Al Shamkha and Al Reef. A family in Al Bateen and a family in Al Reef have the same syllabus and completely different evenings. Most private schools in the emirate release students between about 14:30 and 15:30; after that, the gap between a 20-minute drive and a 45-minute drive decides whether a 16:30 class is realistic or whether the only workable slot is 19:30.

That is why IB Gram delivers to Abu Dhabi as one-to-one online classes over live video, and says so before anything else. We do not make home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. The trade is deliberate. A family in Al Reef looking for a Chemistry HL specialist who can mark energetics questions against the current criteria gets that specialist, instead of whichever tutor is willing to drive out to Al Reef at seven in the evening. Travel time is the most expensive thing in in-home tutoring and the student gets none of it.

The rest of this page is written to be used rather than admired. It sets out what each format of IB class is good at and what it costs in the Abu Dhabi market, with every rate attributed to the provider who published it. It lists where marks actually go missing, component by component. It gives the internal assessment criteria by letter with their mark allocations and word limits, which no competitor page in this market publishes. It counts the DP year backwards from the May examination session. And it says plainly what a tutor in an IB class may and may not do with work that has to be the student's own.

abu-dhabi/ib-classes.programmesIntro: The IB is four programmes, not one, and a request for IB classes in Abu Dhabi can mean any of them. The Diploma Programme is where most enquiries sit, but Middle Years students often need the groundwork more urgently, and Primary Years parents are usually asking about reading and number fluency rather than assessment. Here is what classes at each stage actually cover.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than subject syllabuses, so there is no paper to revise for and no mark scheme to work against. Classes at this stage are about fluency: reading accuracy and speed, number facts, written structure, and the habit of explaining a method rather than just giving an answer. A PYP class that promises exam preparation has misunderstood the programme.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi PYP cohorts are unusually mixed, because the emirate's IB continuum schools draw from families on two- and three-year postings alongside long-settled residents. A child arriving mid-unit from a British or American system typically needs help with the inquiry format itself before any subject content. Classes that start with the unit's central idea, rather than with worksheets, settle that transition faster.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP work is marked against four criteria per subject, each on an eight-point scale, and converted to a 1-7 grade by the school. Students who are used to percentage marks find this opaque, and so do parents. Classes at MYP level are most useful when they are built around the criteria the school is actually using: what a 7-8 descriptor demands in criterion C for Sciences, or why an investigation that reached the right conclusion still scored 4.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 4 and MYP 5 are the real pressure points in Abu Dhabi, because the personal project and the Diploma subject choices land in the same eighteen months. Families on the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor often ask for help with the personal project and the Maths route decision together. Those are two different conversations and we keep them separate; the subject choice deserves its own session with the shortlist of university courses in front of you.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Each subject carries an internal assessment, written papers at the end of DP2, and a 1-7 grade. The programme's difficulty is rarely the content; it is the number of concurrent deadlines and the fact that each subject's marks are lost in a different way. A DP class plan that treats all six subjects the same will waste half its hours.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi DP cohorts sit the May session, and the schools build their internal deadlines backwards from it. Confirm the examination window and results dates with your child's DP coordinator or on ibo.org rather than from any tutoring site, including this one; the IB sets those dates and revises them. What we can plan around with confidence is the school's own calendar, which usually puts mocks between December and February of DP2.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines at least two DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is offered by far fewer schools than the DP, and students on it usually need help with the DP courses they are carrying rather than with the career-related component, which the school's provider delivers.
programmes.countryNote: Very few Abu Dhabi schools run the CP, so most enquiries that mention it turn out to be about the DP. Where a student genuinely is on the CP, the useful classes are the DP courses inside it, taught exactly as they would be for a full Diploma candidate, plus structured help with the reflective project's planning and referencing.

abu-dhabi/ib-classes.subjectsIntro: A class is only as good as the match between the tutor's specialism and the component losing marks. Below are the DP subjects Abu Dhabi families ask about most, with what each one assesses and the place the marks tend to disappear. Levels are given because a Higher Level paper is not a longer Standard Level paper; it is a different assessment.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency, assessed over two papers at SL and three at HL, with a 20-mark exploration. HL Paper 3 is two long multi-part problems and it is where the grade is usually decided, because students treat it as a normal paper and run out of time on part (a).

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use, with a graphical display calculator or software expected throughout. Marks go missing in interpretation: a correct regression with no sentence explaining what the gradient means in context scores the method and loses the communication.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Two papers plus a 20% scientific investigation. Paper 1 covers multiple choice and data analysis; Paper 2 is extended response. The common failure is describing a trend rather than explaining it with a named relationship, and ignoring the data table printed in the question.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity across two papers plus the scientific investigation. Organic mechanisms and energetics carry the most lost marks at HL: curly arrows drawn without charges or lone pairs, and enthalpy cycles set up with the wrong sign convention.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Concept-led content with heavy command-term weighting and a 20% scientific investigation. Students lose marks by writing everything they know about a topic instead of answering the verb; "outline" and "explain" earn marks in different places.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, with diagrams expected in almost every answer and three commentaries as the internal assessment. At HL, Paper 3 rewards calculation plus evaluation; most students deliver the calculation and stop there.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis in Paper 1, comparative essay in Paper 2, an individual oral, and at HL a 1,200-1,500 word essay. The recurring problem is writing about what a text says rather than how the writer built it, which caps the analysis criterion whatever the content knowledge.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Business tools and concepts assessed through case-study papers and a research-based internal assessment. Marks are lost where a tool is named and applied mechanically without a judgement about the business in the stimulus.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: System fundamentals, computational thinking and a developed solution as the internal assessment. The solution is where grades move: students build something functional and then under-document the design decisions the criteria actually reward.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source work in Paper 1, thematic essays in Paper 2, regional depth in HL Paper 3, plus a 2,200-word investigation. Paper 1's four-part structure has a predictable mark distribution and students routinely overwrite part (a) and underwrite part (d).

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches, with an experimental study as the internal assessment. The study is marked on method and analysis rather than on results, so a tidy experiment with a weak justification of the statistical test scores poorly.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic A
subjects.description: Language acquisition at B level and literature at A level. Abu Dhabi students often carry Arabic alongside the mandatory Ministry requirement, which creates two different kinds of work in the same week, and the DP assessment is the one with the oral components to prepare.

abu-dhabi/ib-classes.regionsTitle: Where in Abu Dhabi our students live
abu-dhabi/ib-classes.regionsIntro: Online delivery means the area you live in does not change who can teach your child, but it does change when a class can start and what the school's calendar looks like. These are the Abu Dhabi communities our DP and MYP students are spread across, with the scheduling detail that matters in each.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: A dense cluster of British and American schools with a short internal commute, so 16:00 and 16:30 slots work for most families here. Khalifa City IB families more often ask for Maths and Sciences than for languages.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Ten minutes from Khalifa City and close to one of the emirate's long-established IB continuum schools. Students here frequently come to us mid-MYP, when criteria-based marking first starts to bite.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: A short causeway run to the island but a longer one to Khalifa City. Saadiyat Island IB students often sit in cohorts where the DP is one of two post-16 routes offered, which makes the subject-choice conversation more complicated.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer housing and newer schools, with a noticeable number of families arriving mid-year from other curricula. Evening slots after 18:00 are the norm because of the drive back from island schools.

regions.name: Al Reem Island and Al Maryah Island
regions.note: Apartment living with very short commutes, which makes 15:30 classes genuinely possible. Students here are often the only DP candidate in their building, so study-group effects are absent and one-to-one carries more weight.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Established island neighbourhoods with long-standing schools, including DP provision. Traffic within the island is short but parking and pickup logistics push many families to a 17:00 start.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Al Falah
regions.note: Mainland communities where the school run can be 35 minutes or more each way. Late slots dominate, and the gap between a 19:00 class and homework is the thing to plan around.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Samha
regions.note: Furthest from the island schools, and the clearest case for online delivery: the subjects these families most need help with, such as Physics HL and Economics HL, are exactly the ones with the thinnest local tutor pool.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: Large, mixed communities with a wide spread of curricula. DP enquiries here are often from students who moved into the Diploma from a national or Indian curriculum and need the assessment format explained from scratch.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and the eastern corridor
schoolClusters.note: The corridor running from Khalifa City through Al Raha Gardens to Al Raha Beach holds the heaviest concentration of international provision in the emirate, including IB continuum schools and British schools offering the DP alongside A-Levels. Students from these schools make up a large share of our Abu Dhabi DP enquiries.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi island, Saadiyat and Al Reem
schoolClusters.note: Island and near-island schools serve families with short commutes and a mix of British, American and IB routes. Several of these cohorts offer the DP as one option among several at post-16, which means subject-choice advice has to account for what the alternative route would have required.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: The mainland and the southern communities
schoolClusters.note: Schools serving Al Shamkha, Al Falah, Baniyas and Mohammed Bin Zayed City carry larger cohorts and a wider spread of prior curricula. Transition work - from a national curriculum or from Cambridge IGCSE into the Diploma - is a bigger share of what students here need.

abu-dhabi/ib-classes.modesIntro: Four ways families in Abu Dhabi use one-to-one IB classes. They are not packages so much as shapes: the same tutors, the same online delivery, organised around a different problem. Most families start with the first and add the third when an internal assessment deadline appears on the school calendar.

modes.title: Weekly subject class
modes.description: One subject, one level, one hour or ninety minutes a week, running through the term. This is the default and the only mode that reliably changes a grade, because it gives the tutor a repeated view of the same student's errors. The first three weeks are diagnostic; after that the plan is written against what the student actually gets wrong rather than against the syllabus order.
bullets: Pace set by the student, not by a cohort
A written note after each class naming what was fixed and what is still open
Past-paper questions marked against the current mark scheme

modes.title: Internal assessment clinic
modes.description: Short, intensive blocks timed to the school's own IA deadlines, working on the student's draft against the criteria by letter. The tutor reads what the student wrote, names the criterion that is capping the mark, and teaches the skill the criterion is asking for. The student then rewrites. Nothing is drafted for them and no text is supplied to paste in.

modes.title: Pre-mock and post-mock repair
modes.description: A short block before the school's mock window to rehearse paper technique under timed conditions, and a second block afterwards built entirely around the returned script. The post-mock block is the higher-value half: a marked mock is the most useful diagnostic document a DP student will produce before the real session.

modes.description: For students joining DP1 from Cambridge IGCSE, a national curriculum, an American high school programme or MYP, aimed at the specific gap rather than at general revision. The content gap is usually smaller than families fear; the assessment gap - criteria, command terms, internal deadlines - is usually larger.

sections.heading: What each format of IB class actually fixes
paragraphs: An IB class in Abu Dhabi can be any of five things, and the cheapest is not always the wrong answer. A school's own after-school subject clinic costs nothing extra and is often the right first move, because the teacher running it wrote the internal deadlines and knows exactly which topic the cohort fumbled. What a clinic cannot do is work at one student's pace, and it cannot look at one student's returned paper and say: the content is fine, you are losing marks because you answer the question you expected rather than the one printed.

Tuition-centre group classes of six to twelve sit at the other end. They are efficient at content delivery and past-paper volume, and in this market they are the cheapest paid option, with providers publishing per-student rates from around AED 45 upwards. The limitation is structural rather than a criticism of the teaching: in a group of ten, individual error patterns are invisible, so the class teaches the average student's gap. A student whose problem is time management on Paper 3, or sign conventions in energetics, will sit through content they already know.

A small group of two to four works when the students are failing in the same way, which is less common than it sounds. Two friends taking Physics HL who both struggle with extended response can share a class productively. Two friends where one has a data-analysis problem and the other has a mechanics problem will each get half a class. One-to-one is the only format that can start from the returned script, and it is the most expensive per hour precisely because nothing in it is shared.

sections.heading: The Diploma Programme a class plan has to cover
paragraphs: The DP is built as six subject groups plus a core, and a class plan that ignores the shape of it will spend hours in the wrong place. Group 1 is studies in language and literature. Group 2 is language acquisition. Group 3 is individuals and societies. Group 4 is the sciences. Group 5 is mathematics. Group 6 is the arts, which a student may swap for a second subject from groups 1 to 4. Three subjects are taken at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, or occasionally four and two.

Each of the six is graded 1 to 7, giving 42 points. The core adds up to three more: the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are graded A to E and combined on a matrix that awards between zero and three bonus points. CAS is not graded but must be completed. The ceiling is 45 and the Diploma has minimum conditions as well as a points total, which is why a student can clear 24 points and still not be awarded the Diploma if a Higher Level grade or a core grade falls below the floor.

What this structure means for classes is simple arithmetic. Every subject carries an internal assessment worth a fifth to a third of its grade, so across six subjects a DP student is managing six internal assessments plus the Extended Essay and the TOK essay and exhibition. That is eight or nine separate pieces of assessed coursework, each with its own criteria, its own word limit and its own internal school deadline. A class plan organised by subject alone will meet all of those deadlines late.

The practical version we use is to split hours three ways: content repair where a topic is genuinely missing, paper technique where the content is there but the marks are not, and process coaching for the internal assessments. The proportions change through the two years. In DP1 the internal assessments dominate. In DP2 after mocks, paper technique takes almost everything.
bullets: Six subjects at 1-7 gives 42 points; the Extended Essay and TOK add up to three more

sections.heading: Where IB marks actually go missing, component by component
paragraphs: Almost every parent who contacts us describes the problem as the subject. Almost every returned script says the problem is a component. A Chemistry HL student at 4 is rarely weak across chemistry; far more often the multiple choice is solid, the structured questions are solid, and twelve marks are vanishing in organic mechanisms and enthalpy cycles. That is a four-week fix. Treating it as "needs chemistry help" is a two-term fix that costs five times as much.

The pattern repeats across subject groups with different mechanics. In mathematics it is usually time and reading: HL Paper 3 presents two extended problems, and a student who reads the stem once and starts algebra immediately loses the later parts that depended on noticing a constraint. In the sciences it is the command term and the supplied data: "explain" answered as "describe" caps the mark however good the physics is, and a data table printed in the question is there because the examiner expects it quoted.

In the humanities and languages it is almost always the difference between content and analysis. A History Paper 1 answer that narrates the source instead of evaluating its origin and purpose will score in the lower bands with perfect factual accuracy. An English A Paper 1 that explains what a passage is about rather than how the writer built the effect does the same. These are teachable skills with a short feedback loop, which is why they respond so well to one-to-one classes and so poorly to content revision.

sections.heading: Internal assessment criteria by letter, with marks and limits
paragraphs: This is the single most useful page of information a DP parent can have and almost nobody publishes it. Every internal assessment in the Diploma is marked against named criteria with fixed mark allocations, and the criteria are public. A student who knows that the mathematics exploration carries six marks for use of mathematics and only three for personal engagement will spend their time differently from one who does not. A student who knows criterion C of the Extended Essay is worth twelve of thirty-four marks will not spend three weeks on presentation.

The limits matter as much as the criteria. The Extended Essay has a 4,000-word ceiling. The Theory of Knowledge essay has 1,600 words. The sciences investigation has 3,000. The History investigation has 2,200. The English A Higher Level essay sits in a 1,200 to 1,500 word band. Mathematics works in pages rather than words, with twelve to twenty recommended. Going over a limit does not earn extra marks and in several components the examiner stops reading.

The third column parents rarely see is which criterion is most often underscored. Across the drafts our tutors read, the pattern is consistent: evaluation and reflection criteria are where marks are routinely left on the table, because students treat them as a conclusion to be summarised rather than as a separate skill with its own descriptors. Criterion D in the sciences investigation and criterion C in the History investigation are the clearest examples.

Verify every figure below against the current subject guide your child's school is teaching, because the IB revises guides on a rolling cycle and a school may be on a different version from the one a tutoring site last checked. The subject teacher or DP coordinator can confirm which guide applies, and the official criteria sit in the school's own copy of it.

sections.heading: What IB classes cost in Abu Dhabi, with the sources named
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages we examined for this market publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, a currency Abu Dhabi families do not transact in. So here is the market in AED, with every band attributed. Treat these as the range you will be quoted, not as our price list: IB Gram quotes after a consultation, because an hour of Mathematics AA Higher Level support in DP2 and an hour of MYP 4 science are not the same product.

The pattern across the market is consistent. Budget online tutoring, often delivered by university students, runs from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Qualified subject tutors working online sit at AED 150-300, where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialists in IB, IGCSE and A-Level sit at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 rate table showing 200-450+. Premium named tutors reach AED 500-650 and higher, BartyED publishing AED 650.

In-home visits in Abu Dhabi are the band to read carefully, because the figure includes something the student does not receive. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors are advertised at AED 200-500. Part of that premium is travel time across a city where the drive from Al Reef to Al Bateen at the evening peak is not a short one. Monthly packages in the market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

For planning, Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour class are AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Whether UAE VAT applies to any quoted figure is a question for the provider; ask whether the number you are given is inclusive, and ask for it in writing.

sections.heading: Class size and what it costs you in talk time
paragraphs: The argument for one-to-one is usually made emotionally and it has a mechanical version that is more persuasive. In a sixty-minute class, the amount of time a particular student spends producing work that a teacher sees and corrects is the variable that matters. In a group of ten, that time is divided ten ways by definition, and in practice worse than that, because the teacher spends a large share of the hour on exposition that reaches everybody equally and diagnoses nobody.

This is why group classes work well for content and badly for technique. Content can be delivered to ten people simultaneously with no loss. Technique cannot, because technique is the correction of a specific error that this specific student makes. A tutor who watches one student attempt an energetics question can see that the sign convention is reversed in the second line. A teacher in front of ten cannot see anybody's second line.

There is a cost argument on the other side and it is honest. Four one-to-one hours cost roughly what twelve group hours cost in this market. If a student's problem genuinely is missing content across a whole topic, twelve hours of group teaching may be better value than four hours of one-to-one. The question to answer before paying for either is which problem you have, and the returned mock paper answers it faster than any conversation.

Our practical advice to Abu Dhabi families is to use the formats in sequence rather than choosing between them. Use the school's clinic for content the cohort missed. Use one-to-one for the components where your child's marks are going missing and for the internal assessments, where criteria-based feedback on one student's own draft cannot be delivered to a group at all.

In this market four one-to-one hours cost roughly what twelve group hours cost

sections.heading: The DP year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi DP cohorts sit the May examination session, and the school builds every internal deadline backwards from it. That is the calendar a class plan has to fit, and it is the thing no competitor page in this market lays out. The exact examination window and results dates are set by the IB and should be confirmed with your child's DP coordinator or on ibo.org; we do not publish IB dates here, because they are revised and a tutoring site is the wrong place to read them.

What can be planned with confidence is the sequence. Subject and level choices are confirmed at the end of Year 11, before DP1 starts, and that decision has a longer shadow than anything else on the list, because the Maths route in particular closes university options. Internal assessment first drafts run through DP1 and into the first term of DP2. The Extended Essay usually lands in the first term of DP2 with supervisor reflection sessions recorded along the way. The TOK exhibition sits in DP1 and the essay in DP2.

Mock examinations usually fall between December and February of DP2. This is the pivot point of the whole two years. Before mocks, the useful work is content and internal assessments. After mocks, the only work that pays is paper technique built on the returned scripts, and families who start tutoring in March of DP2 are buying far less than the same money bought in October of DP1.

For families whose children also sit Cambridge or Pearson qualifications alongside or before the Diploma, those boards publish their dates and they are worth reading as a model of how far ahead entry deadlines sit. Cambridge's March 2027 series, for example, has exams from 3 February to 4 March 2027 with final entries due on 27 November 2026 - fourteen weeks before the first paper. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used.

sections.heading: ADEK, your child's school, and who regulates what
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi are overseen by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes inspection outcomes. That is a different body from the one that oversees Dubai's schools, and parents moving between emirates are often surprised to find the inspection framework, the fee rules and the school listings all sit with a different authority.

The full map is worth knowing because Abu Dhabi families move within the country. Dubai's private schools sit with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Sharjah's sit with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education and, along with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education.

What this means for a tutoring decision is narrower than it first appears. A regulator licenses and inspects schools; it does not license or endorse tutoring providers. IB Gram is not approved by, registered with or connected to ADEK, and no tutoring company in this market should tell you otherwise. A separate permit regime exists for individual private tutors, administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and a separate educational services permit exists for institutes operating physical premises in Dubai.

Where the regulator is genuinely useful to you is verification. If a school is named to you, it should appear on the regulator's own listing, and the current inspection report should be read there rather than from a summary on a tutoring site. We do not publish inspection ratings on these pages for exactly that reason: a rating read second-hand can be years out of date, and the authority's own site is one click away.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line a tutor in an IB class does not cross
paragraphs: The IB treats authenticity as a condition of assessment, not a guideline, and the consequences of breaching it fall on the student rather than on the tutor. A Diploma candidate found to have submitted work that is not their own can lose the subject grade and, in serious cases, the Diploma. That is the context in which a market containing providers who openly sell completed internal assessments should be read, and one researched competitor in this market advertises exactly that at around AED 3,750 per piece.

The line is clear enough to state in a sentence. A tutor may teach the skill a criterion is asking for, explain what a descriptor means, read a draft the student has written and name which criterion is capping the mark, model the technique on a different question, and check referencing conventions. A tutor may not supply sentences to paste in, rewrite a paragraph into the submission, choose the research question on the student's behalf, or hand over a finished piece of work in any condition.

In practice the distinction shows up in how feedback is phrased. "Criterion D asks you to weigh your limitations against your conclusion, and at the moment you have listed three without saying which one most affects your result" is teaching. Handing back a marked-up document with replacement prose in it is not. Our tutors give the first kind and the student then rewrites in their own words, which is also the only version that produces a student who can answer questions about their own work in a viva or a reflection session.

Two related rules are worth stating because competitors breach them. Nobody should be supplying you with IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; those are the boards' copyright and the official sources are public. And no tutor can promise a specific grade. A page promising a 7 is telling you something about the page, not about the teaching.

sections.heading: After the Diploma: Ministry of Education equivalency
paragraphs: Families planning to use a UAE university place after the Diploma run into equivalency, the Ministry of Education process that recognises a foreign secondary certificate. It is worth understanding early, because the requirements sit on subjects and tests chosen years before the application, and no tutoring provider performs or guarantees any part of the process. It is the Ministry's, and the Ministry's own channels are where it is done.

The published requirements are clearest for the British track. A student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade no lower than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor in this market publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong, and inheriting that error would cost a family a subject choice.

For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB there is no points threshold we are prepared to publish, because the source we read does not state one. Check it on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority and treat any tutoring site that quotes an IB number without a government source with suspicion.

The practical consequence for a DP class plan is the Maths decision in Year 11. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are both full IB mathematics courses, and both are accepted widely, but individual university programmes - engineering and some economics degrees in particular - state a preference. That is a subject-choice conversation to have with the shortlist of courses open, before DP1 begins, not in DP2 when the choice is locked.

process.title: Send the marked paper, not just the subject
process.description: The fastest way to get a useful first class is to send a photograph of the most recent marked paper or returned IA draft along with the subject and level. A tutor can read a script in ten minutes and arrive at the first class with a hypothesis. Without it, the first class is spent finding out what the paper would have told us.

process.title: Consultation, then a specialist match
process.description: A short call establishes the subject, the level, the component losing marks and the school's deadline calendar. We then match a tutor who teaches that subject at that level, rather than a generalist who covers the subject area. If nobody suitable is free, we say so and give a date rather than filling the slot.

process.title: A free trial class before any payment
process.description: The trial is a working class, not a sales call. The tutor works on the component the paper identified and finishes by naming what they would do over the next six weeks. No payment is taken before the trial happens, and if the match is wrong after it, we change the tutor rather than defending the first choice.

process.title: A six-week plan with a written note each week
process.description: After each class the tutor writes a short note: what was covered, what was fixed, what is still open, and what the student should practise before the next one. Six weeks is long enough for a pattern to appear in a marked paper and short enough that a plan that is not working gets changed.

process.title: Reset the plan at the school's mock window
process.description: Mock examinations change what is worth doing. We rebuild the plan around the returned scripts, rank the subjects by marks available rather than by anxiety, and set an end date. Many families reduce hours after mocks in two subjects and increase them in one.

whyPoints.title: Classes are one-to-one and online, and we say so first
whyPoints.description: Every class for an Abu Dhabi family runs live over video with one tutor and one student. We do not make home visits in Abu Dhabi, and in-home tutoring is something we offer only in India. Saying that before anything else is the point: you can judge the rest of the page knowing what is actually being sold.

whyPoints.title: Specialist by subject and level, not by subject area
whyPoints.description: A Physics HL tutor and a general science tutor are different people. We match on the component, so a student losing marks on Paper 2 extended response gets a tutor who marks extended response, and a student stuck on criterion D of the scientific investigation gets one who has read a lot of criterion D.

whyPoints.title: Every rate on this page carries its source
whyPoints.description: The AED figures here are the market's, each attributed to the provider that published it and dated. Our own fee is quoted after the consultation because it depends on subject, level and session length. A page that publishes a single headline number for every subject is simplifying something that is not simple.

whyPoints.title: Assessed work stays the student's own
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach criteria, read drafts and name what is capping a mark. They do not supply prose or submit work. This is a genuine difference in this market, where completed internal assessments are openly advertised, and it protects the student from a malpractice finding that would cost far more than a grade.

whyPoints.title: Timed to Abu Dhabi, not to a time zone somewhere else
whyPoints.description: Slots are set in Gulf Standard Time against your child's actual school release time and commute, whether that is a ten-minute run on Al Reem Island or a forty-minute one from Al Reef. The same slot is held weekly, because a class that moves every week is the first thing to be dropped in a busy term.

whyPoints.title: Honest about coverage
whyPoints.description: Some subject-and-level combinations are thin everywhere, and a few are thin in this time zone. Where no suitable tutor is free, we say so, name a date, and tell you whether the specialist available sits in another time zone and what that does to the slot. The alternative is a mismatch nobody admits to for six weeks.

faqs.question: Is an IB class the same thing as IB tutoring, or something different?
faqs.answer: In this market the words are used interchangeably, which hides a real difference. A class usually means a scheduled group session covering syllabus content, often at a tuition centre, with six to twelve students. Tutoring usually means one tutor working with one student on that student's specific errors. Both are legitimate and they fix different problems: content gaps respond well to group teaching, while marks lost to command terms, timing or internal assessment criteria need individual diagnosis. IB Gram runs the one-to-one version, delivered live online. When you ring a provider in Abu Dhabi, ask how many students are in the room before you compare prices, because the per-hour figures are not comparable otherwise.

faqs.question: How many IB classes a week does a Diploma student in Abu Dhabi usually need?
faqs.answer: Most families start with one subject at one hour a week and add from there based on what the marked papers show. One weekly hour in a single subject is enough to change paper technique over a term. Two subjects at one hour each is the most common shape in DP2. Beyond three hours a week across subjects, students start losing the independent practice time that makes classes work at all, and the extra hours stop paying. The exception is a short intensive block around an internal assessment deadline or after mocks, where four to six hours over two weeks in one subject can do more than a term of weekly sessions.

faqs.question: Are your IB classes in Abu Dhabi group classes or one-to-one?
faqs.answer: One-to-one, with one tutor and one student, delivered live online over video. We do not run group classes, and we do not place a tutor in your home anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The reason for the single format is that the thing one-to-one does uniquely well is diagnose why a particular student is losing marks, which cannot be done for ten students at once. If your child's problem is genuinely a missing topic across a whole unit, a group class at a centre may be better value, and we will tell you that on the consultation call.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP 5. Should classes start before DP1 begins?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but for a narrower reason than general preparation. The content jump from MYP 5 into DP1 is smaller than most families expect. The assessment jump is larger: criteria-based marking becomes component weightings, command terms become decisive, and eight or nine pieces of assessed coursework appear on a calendar. Six to ten weeks of work over the summer on command terms, on the shape of the papers, and on the Maths route decision pays better than content revision. The Maths choice in particular deserves its own session with the shortlist of university courses in front of you, because Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation close different doors.

faqs.question: Which IB subject groups do your classes cover for Abu Dhabi students?
faqs.answer: All six groups, with the depth varying by group. Mathematics, the sciences and individuals and societies are where most Abu Dhabi enquiries sit and where the specialist pool is deepest at both levels. Studies in language and literature and language acquisition are well covered, including Arabic and Arabic B. The arts are the thinnest group everywhere, and for a Visual Arts or Music candidate we will tell you honestly whether a suitable specialist is free before you plan around it. Match requests are made by subject and level together, because a Higher Level paper is a different assessment from the Standard Level one, not a longer version of it.

faqs.question: How long is one class and can it fit after Abu Dhabi school pickup?
faqs.answer: Sixty or ninety minutes are the two standard lengths, and ninety suits Higher Level work in DP2 where a full paper section needs sitting and then marking in the same session. Most private schools in the emirate release students between about 14:30 and 15:30. Inside the island or on Al Reem, a 15:30 or 16:00 start is realistic. From Khalifa City or Al Raha, 16:30 works. From Al Reef, Al Samha or Al Shamkha, where the run home can be forty minutes, families usually settle on 18:30 or 19:00. Because delivery is online, no travel time is added at the tutor's end.

faqs.question: Do your classes cover internal assessment as well as the written papers?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most DP students the internal assessments are where the available marks sit. Each subject's internal assessment is worth between a fifth and a third of the grade, and across six subjects plus the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay there are eight or nine pieces to manage. Classes work on the criteria by letter: what criterion D of the sciences investigation is actually asking for, why criterion C of the Extended Essay carries twelve of thirty-four marks, what the word limits are. The tutor reads what the student has written and names what is capping the mark. The student then rewrites it themselves.

faqs.question: What happens in the first class, and how is it different from a sales call?
faqs.answer: The first class is a working lesson. If you have sent a marked paper or a returned draft in advance, the tutor will have read it and arrives with a hypothesis about where the marks are going. The session tests that hypothesis by having the student attempt something similar while the tutor watches the method rather than the answer. It finishes with the tutor naming, in plain words, what they would work on over the next six weeks and in what order. No payment is taken before that trial class happens, and if the match turns out to be wrong we change the tutor.

faqs.question: Can two siblings share a class, and does that halve the cost?
faqs.answer: Two siblings can share a session if they are taking the same subject at the same level and are losing marks in similar places, which is less common than families hope. Where it works, it is good value. Where one sibling has a data-analysis problem and the other a mechanics problem, each gets half a lesson and both make half the progress, and separate shorter sessions do more. Siblings in different year groups or different subjects should always have separate sessions. We will say which applies after looking at both children's recent marked work rather than agreeing to a shared booking because it is cheaper.

faqs.question: Are classes available for the November examination session as well as May?
faqs.answer: Yes. Abu Dhabi schools sit the May session, so most of our Diploma work follows that calendar, but students retaking a subject or transferring from a southern-hemisphere school may sit in November, and we schedule to whichever session applies. Confirm the actual examination window and the entry deadline with your child's DP coordinator or on ibo.org rather than from any tutoring site, including this one: the IB sets those dates and revises them. For a retake, the useful planning conversation is which single component is worth the hours, because a retake usually turns on one paper rather than on the whole subject.

faqs.question: How do online classes handle practical and data-analysis skills in the sciences?
faqs.answer: The practical work itself belongs to the school, which runs the laboratory programme and supervises the scientific investigation. What online classes handle well is the part of science that carries the marks: processing data, propagating uncertainties, drawing and interpreting graphs, and justifying a research design against criterion A. Those are shared-screen activities, and a tutor annotating the student's own spreadsheet or graph is closer to how the work is actually assessed than a demonstration would be. Paper 1 data-analysis questions and Paper 2 extended response are both worked the same way: the student attempts it live and the tutor marks the method as it appears.

faqs.question: Does my child's school in Abu Dhabi need to approve outside classes?
faqs.answer: No approval is needed for a family to arrange private tuition, but telling the school is usually worth doing. Subject teachers can say which component they think is costing marks, and they set the internal deadlines a class plan has to fit around. Where schools do have a policy that matters is on their own staff: Abu Dhabi professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document, and do not ask a teacher to tutor your child privately if they teach at your child's school.

faqs.question: Can a teacher from my child's own Abu Dhabi school run private classes for them?
faqs.answer: They should not, and asking puts the teacher in a difficult position. Reported Abu Dhabi professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat both as press-reported and check the current policy documents directly. The practical answer is to look outside the school, where the tutor has no stake in the grades they are helping to produce, which is better for everyone including the student.

faqs.question: Do you need a permit to teach private IB classes in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, under the service named Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so do not accept a quoted figure.

faqs.question: What does an hour of IB class cost in Abu Dhabi at the moment?
faqs.answer: The market in 2026 runs in bands. Budget online tutoring sits at roughly AED 45-150, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150-300, where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. IB and IGCSE specialists sit at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home visits run AED 180-500 because travel is inside the fee. Premium named tutors reach AED 500-650, BartyED publishing AED 650. Our own fee depends on subject, level and session length and is quoted after a consultation rather than advertised as one number.

faqs.question: Do classes help with the Maths Analysis and Approaches or Applications decision?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the highest-value single sessions available in Year 11. Both are full IB mathematics courses and both are accepted widely, but individual university programmes state preferences, and engineering and some economics degrees are the ones to check first. The useful session puts the shortlist of courses and their stated entry requirements next to the student's actual performance in algebra and in statistics, then looks at what Higher Level in either route would demand across two years. It is a decision with a long shadow, and it is far cheaper to get right in Year 11 than to work around in DP2.

abu-dhabi/ib-classes.closingBody: If you are weighing up IB classes in Abu Dhabi, the most useful thing you can do before speaking to anybody is find the most recent marked paper or returned internal assessment draft. It will tell you in ten minutes what a term of general revision would take months to find: whether the problem is missing content, paper technique, or an assessment criterion nobody has explained. Send it with the subject and level, and a specialist tutor will read it before the free trial class. Classes run one-to-one, live online, in Gulf Standard Time, around your child's actual school release time - and no payment is taken before the trial happens.

abu-dhabi/ib-coaching.tutorsIntro: The coaches below work on Diploma and Middle Years papers rather than on general study skills. Each one marks to the published criteria for the subject they coach, returns the annotated script, and tells you in plain words which habit is costing the most marks this month.

intro.heading: Coaching and tutoring are not the same purchase
paragraphs: Most Abu Dhabi families who search for IB coaching have already tried something. There has usually been a school teacher who gave up a lunchtime, a relative who is good at maths, or a group revision class in a centre off Airport Road. The grade moved a little, then stopped. That pattern is diagnostic in itself. A student stuck between a 4 and a 5 is rarely short of content. They are losing marks the same three or four ways on every paper, and nobody has sat down with their actual script and shown them where.

IB coaching, as IB Gram runs it, is one-to-one and delivered over live video. A coach does not re-teach the syllabus from page one. The coach takes the most recent real piece of work - a mock paper, a returned Internal Assessment draft, a timed essay - reads it against the published markscheme or the assessment criteria for that subject, and names the specific habits costing marks. The hour after that is spent drilling those habits until they survive a clock.

The distinction matters because the two products have different price tags and different failure modes. Content tutoring is the right purchase when a student genuinely has not met a topic: a Diploma student who moved into Abu Dhabi in October and arrived three chapters behind in Physics needs teaching, not technique. Coaching is the right purchase when the content is in the student's head but does not reach the page in the form the examiner rewards. Buying the first when you need the second is the most common waste of money in this market, and it is why a term of weekly sessions sometimes produces nothing.

Abu Dhabi has its own shape as a market. Private schools in the emirate are supervised by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which handles the licensing and accreditation of private schools and publishes its own inspection outcomes. Enrolment is spread across three bands: the older island schools around Al Bateen and Al Mushrif, the Saadiyat and Al Reem Island intake, and the large Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor that pulls families out towards the airport. A coach working the island at 4pm and the Khalifa City corridor at 6pm by car loses an hour of the evening to the Sheikh Zayed bridge crossing. Over video, that hour goes to the student instead.

This page sets out what IB assessment actually rewards, which command terms the markschemes treat as different instructions, where the six subject groups leak marks, what an eight-week coaching block looks like counted backwards from the paper, what the Abu Dhabi market charges, and where coaching legally and academically has to stop. It does not publish IB session dates, because the IB's own site could not be verified for this project, and it does not promise a grade.
bullets: Coaching works on technique and timing; content tutoring works on syllabus gaps. Buy the one your child's script shows you.
Every session starts from a real marked script, not a textbook chapter.
