abu-dhabi/ib-coaching.programmesIntro: Coaching looks different at each stage of the IB continuum, because what is assessed changes. In the Primary Years there is no external paper to coach towards; by the Diploma there are six subjects, three internal assessments to supervise and a core that carries its own points.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examination, so coaching here is not exam coaching. It is the habit layer: reading a question twice, showing method on paper, estimating before calculating, and writing a sentence that answers what was asked. Sessions are short and usually weekly. The most useful work is often in English reading comprehension and in the written explanation of a maths method, because both are the foundations the Middle Years criteria later mark explicitly.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi primaries run the PYP alongside the Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies requirements that apply to private schools across the UAE under the Ministry of Education's general regulations. Families moving from a British primary in Al Bateen into a PYP school on Saadiyat often find the transition is in the reporting language rather than the content, and a term of coaching on how to read a PYP report is sometimes worth more than extra maths.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP is criterion-marked, which makes it the first stage where coaching has real leverage. Each subject has four criteria, usually A to D, each scored on an eight-point scale with published descriptors. Students lose marks by writing a good answer that does not address the criterion being assessed. Coaching here means reading the task sheet with the student, identifying which criterion each part of the task feeds, and rewriting one paragraph until it matches the descriptor wording.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi MYP students in Year 11 face a decision point that coaching can genuinely inform: continue to the Diploma, or move to an A-Level route at one of the British schools in the emirate. The honest answer depends on whether the student can carry six subjects plus the core. A coach who has read two terms of the student's criterion marks is better placed to answer that than a brochure.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is where coaching earns its fee. Six subjects, each with external papers and an internal assessment, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Marks are lost to command-term misreading, to answers that describe when the paper asked for evaluation, to data-based questions answered without reference to the data, and to timing collapse in the final twenty minutes. All four are coachable and none of them require re-teaching the syllabus.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma students sit the May session, in common with the rest of the northern-hemisphere IB world. No IB session or results date is published on this page: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so the only reliable source is your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org directly. Plan a coaching block backwards from the date your coordinator gives you, not from a date you read online.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs a career-related study with two or more Diploma courses, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Coaching for a CP student concentrates on the Diploma courses they do carry and on the reflective project, which is marked against its own criteria and is the component most often started too late. The written reflection carries more weight than students expect.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is offered by a small number of schools in the UAE and by very few in Abu Dhabi, so CP families often need a coach who has read the subject guide rather than one who has taught a full cohort. We will say so when that is the case, and we will say when the honest answer is that no coach on the platform currently covers a CP career-related study.

abu-dhabi/ib-coaching.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is listed with what the assessment actually measures and where the marks go missing. A coaching block is built around the second column, not the first, because that is the part a weekly hour can change inside a term.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which is where most of the damage happens: students who can do the algebra on a graphing display cannot do it by hand under time pressure. Marks also go to unjustified steps. The markscheme rewards shown reasoning, so coaching drills writing the line that earns the method mark even when the final answer is wrong.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI is calculator-active throughout and heavier on modelling, statistics and interpretation in context. The classic loss is a correct calculation followed by no sentence interpreting it. Coaching here is largely about the final line of every answer: what the number means for the situation in the question, in the units the question used.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 multiple choice punishes unit slips and sign errors; Paper 2 extended response punishes explanations that restate the phenomenon instead of applying a principle. The experimental component needs uncertainty handling that is almost never taught twice. Coaching focuses on structured explanation chains and on uncertainty arithmetic.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics generate the most repeat errors, and the data booklet is under-used by students who have not practised finding values quickly. Coaching works on mechanism notation, on where the booklet saves time, and on writing full ionic equations under exam conditions rather than from memory.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Biology marks are lost in command-term drift: an answer that describes a process when the question asked for an explanation of a trend scores a fraction of what it could. The data-based questions reward reading the axes before the stem. Coaching is mostly question dissection and precision of biological vocabulary.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram-led answers that omit the diagram, and evaluation paragraphs that list both sides without reaching a judgement, cost the most. The HL quantitative questions reward method marks. Coaching trains the diagram-first habit and a closing judgement sentence that references the stimulus material.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Business answers fail when the tool is applied in general instead of to the named organisation in the case study. The HL extension paper rewards candidates who annotate the pre-released case before the exam. Coaching builds that annotation discipline and tool selection under time limits.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis rewards a line of argument about how a text produces meaning, not a feature hunt. The individual oral needs a global issue narrow enough to sustain ten minutes. Coaching works on thesis construction and on cutting the summary that eats the first page.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode trace questions and the HL abstract data structures section generate the most lost marks. Students who can code in Python often cannot hand-trace a loop. Coaching drills trace tables, dry-running by hand, and the algorithm description style the markscheme expects.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic A
subjects.description: Private schools in the UAE carry Arabic alongside their licensed curriculum under the Ministry of Education's general regulations, so most Abu Dhabi students sit an Arabic course whether or not it is one of their six Diploma subjects. Coaching concentrates on the productive skills - the written task and the oral - where structure and register are marked explicitly.

regions.note: Island families near the Al Bateen schools usually finish the school run by 3.15pm, so a 4pm start works on weekdays. Al Bateen is one of the few areas where a 4pm slot is genuinely open rather than theoretical.

regions.note: Dense apartment living with short school commutes but heavy late-afternoon street traffic. Most Al Khalidiyah students settle into a 5pm or 5.30pm session and prefer two shorter midweek slots to one long weekend block.

regions.name: Al Mushrif
regions.note: Al Mushrif villas feed several of the older island schools, and after-school sport runs late here. Families in Al Mushrif often ask for a 6.30pm start, which suits coaches working from India and the wider Gulf.

regions.name: Al Nahyan
regions.note: A mixed community with students spread across British, American and IB schools, so a household can have two children on different assessment calendars. Staggered 5pm and 6.15pm slots in the same evening are common in Al Nahyan.

regions.note: Al Karamah sits close to the main hospital corridor, and shift-working parents here value a recorded session they can review later. Weekend morning coaching is more popular in Al Karamah than anywhere else on the island.

regions.note: Short walks to school and long evenings; students in the Corniche and Al Zahiyah blocks tend to be available early. A 4.30pm paper-marking session followed by homework works well here.

regions.note: Mostly working parents in apartments, with children bussed off-island to school. Al Maryah households usually want a fixed weekly slot in writing, and a session note the parent can read on the commute home.

schoolClusters.note: The island carries the emirate's oldest international schools and the widest curriculum mix in the smallest area. abu-dhabi/ib-coaching.modesIntro: Three coaching shapes cover almost every request we get from Abu Dhabi families. All three run one-to-one over live video, and all three start from a marked script rather than a syllabus.

modes.title: Weekly technique coaching
modes.description: One 60-minute session a week through the term, built around whatever the school set most recently. The pattern is fixed: twenty minutes on the returned script, twenty-five on a drill targeting the error class it exposed, fifteen on a timed question done live. The error list carries over week to week until each item is retired.

modes.title: Eight-week block before a paper
modes.description: A counted-backwards block for students with a date in sight: a mock, a school internal examination, or the May session. Week one is diagnostic, weeks two to six target the error classes in order of mark value, week seven is a full paper under exam conditions, week eight is the debrief. The block ends on purpose rather than drifting.

modes.title: Internal assessment supervision
modes.description: Scheduled around the school's own draft deadlines rather than weekly. The coach reads the student's draft against the assessment criteria, asks the questions an examiner would ask, and hands the draft back with criterion-referenced comments. The student makes every change themselves, and the school supervisor remains the authority on the task.

sections.heading: What a parent is actually asking for when they search IB coaching in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: IB coaching in Abu Dhabi, in the sense parents mean it, is one-to-one work on how a student converts what they know into marks. It is not a revision class and it is not a second syllabus run-through. The hour is spent on a specific script, a specific error class and a specific drill, and it is delivered over live video on Gulf Standard Time so the specialist is chosen for the subject rather than for the drive.

The three products in this market look similar in an advert and behave completely differently in practice. A tuition centre revision class puts eighteen students in a room with a worked past paper, which is useful for a student who needs structure and useless for a student whose problem is a personal habit nobody has named. Content tutoring re-teaches topics, which is exactly right for a genuine gap and exactly wrong for a student who already knows the material. Coaching reads the student's own output and changes the output.

Working out which one you need is a ten-minute job if you have the last marked paper in front of you. If the lost marks sit on topics the student has not studied, buy teaching. If the lost marks are spread across topics the student can explain verbally, buy coaching. If the paper came back with a grade and no annotations at all, the first useful purchase is someone marking it properly, which is what a diagnostic session does.
The table below is the version we would give a parent on the phone. It is not flattering to coaching in every row, because coaching is the wrong purchase in two of them.

sections.heading: The command terms that decide the mark, not the content
paragraphs: IB papers are written in a controlled vocabulary. Each command term is an instruction with a defined expectation, and markschemes are built so that an answer which meets a different instruction cannot score full marks however good it is. This is the single most coachable thing in the Diploma, and almost no commercial page in this market mentions it.

The failure is rarely ignorance. Ask a Diploma student the difference between describe and explain and most will tell you correctly. Give them a Paper 2 question under time pressure and a large proportion will describe, because describing is what the brain does when it is anxious and knows the content. Coaching fixes this with repetition on short answers rather than with a definition sheet: ten eight-mark questions in a fortnight, each one re-marked against the term that was actually used.

The second half of the problem is the mark allocation. A four-mark explain question wants four linked statements, not a paragraph. A six-mark evaluate question that reaches no judgement caps itself somewhere in the middle band regardless of content quality. Students who learn to read the term and the mark total together before writing anything gain marks without learning a single new fact.

The terms below appear across the sciences, individuals and societies, and mathematics. Definitions vary slightly by subject guide, so a coach always checks the student's own guide rather than a generic list.

One warning about how this gets taught badly. Handing a student a printed glossary of command terms achieves almost nothing, because the problem is not vocabulary but behaviour under pressure. The drill that works is narrow and repetitive: a short question, four minutes on the clock, then marking it together against the term that was printed and asking what the answer would have needed to score the last two marks. Done ten or twelve times across a fortnight, on questions from the student's own subject guide, the habit starts to hold. Done once as a lecture about command terms, it changes nothing by the following week, and both the student and the parent conclude that coaching does not work.

sections.heading: Where Diploma marks go missing, subject group by subject group
paragraphs: Marks leak in patterns, and the patterns are group-specific. A coach who has marked a few hundred scripts in one subject group can usually predict a student's error class from two pages. That is what makes a diagnostic session worth an hour: it converts a vague sense that the grade is stuck into a named list of three or four habits.

Across the sciences, the dominant losses are explanation chains that break after one link, uncertainty and significant-figure handling in the experimental work, and graph questions answered without reading the axes. In mathematics, the dominant losses are unshown method on calculator-active papers and arithmetic collapse on the non-calculator paper. In individuals and societies, the dominant loss is evaluation without judgement. In language A, it is summary crowding out analysis.

None of these require new content. All of them require a student to do something different with the same knowledge, which is why they respond to drilling inside a term rather than needing a year. The table pairs each group with the habit a coaching block targets first, chosen by mark value rather than by how easy it is to fix.

Ranking the error classes by mark value, rather than by how annoying they are, is the part families get wrong on their own. A parent reading a Physics script notices the spelling and the handwriting. An examiner's markscheme does not award anything for either. Meanwhile the same script loses four marks across two questions because every explanation stops at the first link, and nobody has pointed at that. Ordering the list properly also decides how long the block needs to be: two high-value habits can be moved inside six weeks, while a list of twelve small irritations cannot be moved at all and usually means the diagnosis was done without reading the script closely.

Group 6 deserves a note of its own, because it is the group families most often assume cannot be coached. The arts components are documented rather than examined in the conventional sense, and the documentation is marked. A process portfolio that records what the student did, without recording why they chose it over the alternative, is a portfolio that has thrown away marks that were available for free. Reflective writing of that kind is a teachable form, and it is one of the clearest examples of a Diploma component where technique rather than talent decides the grade band.

sections.heading: Criterion-referenced marking, and why a good essay is not the unit of measurement
paragraphs: Internal assessments and most Middle Years tasks are marked against criteria, each with descriptors at several levels, and the examiner works by best fit rather than by adding up good qualities. A student can write a genuinely impressive piece of work and land in a middle band because the descriptor for the top band asks for something the piece never attempts. This is not unfair marking. It is the system working as published, and it is invisible unless somebody shows the student the descriptors.

The practical consequence is that redrafting without the criteria open is close to useless. A student who improves the prose of a Biology internal assessment while leaving the evaluation of the method thin has improved the part that is not being marked. A coach's first move on any draft is to put the criterion descriptors beside the draft and mark the gap, criterion by criterion, in the language the descriptors use.

There is a discipline question inside this too. Criterion-referenced marking rewards explicit signalling: saying what you are doing, in the words of the descriptor, so the examiner does not have to infer it. Students often resist this because it feels mechanical compared with the essays they wrote in Year 10. It is mechanical, and it is what the published descriptors ask for.

The honest limit: a coach reads, questions and marks. The student makes every change and every word on the page remains theirs. We put that in writing before any internal assessment work starts, because the alternative is an academic-honesty problem that lands on the student rather than on us.

sections.heading: An eight-week coaching block, counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Most families arrive with a date and a vague plan. Reversing the order fixes more than any individual session: start from the date, work backwards, and decide what has to be true in each of the preceding weeks. The schedule below is the one we use for a mock or an internal school examination, and it is also the shape of a run-in to the May session.

The structural points matter more than the specific weeks. The diagnostic has to come first and has to use real work, because a block planned without one is a guess. The full timed paper has to come before the last week, not in it, so there is still time to act on what it shows. And the final week is for consolidation and sleep, not for new material, which is the hardest part of the plan to hold when a student is anxious.

Two sessions a week in the last fortnight is common and sensible. Four is not: the limiting factor by that stage is how much independent practice the student is doing between sessions, and more contact hours crowd that out. A coach who agrees to five sessions a week in the final month is selling hours rather than giving advice.

Dates in the table are expressed in weeks before the paper rather than as calendar dates. For IB sessions, take the actual dates from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org: this project could not verify IB dates from the IB itself, so none are published here.

sections.heading: Is your coach legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and the regulation is more specific than most families realise. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. The eligible categories are set out on the federal portal and include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount appears on this page.

There is an Abu Dhabi layer on top of that. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's own code of conduct has been reported as barring the same thing. Treat that as press-reported rather than as ADEK's exact wording, and check the current policy document if it matters to your decision. The practical advice is simple: do not arrange for your child to be tutored privately, for a fee, by a teacher at their own school.

A tutoring business with premises and staff is a different legal animal again. In Dubai that means a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; the Abu Dhabi equivalent sits with ADEK. IB Gram operates as an online tutor-matching platform and holds no such permit, no licence from ADEK, and no office in the UAE. We say so plainly because two pages ranking for these searches imply otherwise.

What you can do as a parent is ask. A UAE-based tutor who holds the permit can show you the permit; one who cannot should be able to explain why not. We ask UAE-based tutors on the platform for their permit number before matching.

sections.heading: What IB coaching costs in the Abu Dhabi market
paragraphs: Nobody ranking for these searches publishes an AED rate table, which is strange given it is the first question every parent asks. The figures below are market rates collected from providers' own published pages in October 2026 and from a published Dubai rate survey, with the source named in each row. They are not IB Gram's price list. Our own answer to the price question starts with a free trial lesson and a conversation about how many sessions the error list actually needs.

Two patterns are worth knowing before you compare quotes. First, in-home rates carry travel inside them whether or not the invoice says so: a tutor crossing from the island to Khalifa City for a single hour is pricing a two-hour commitment. Second, rates rise as a session date approaches, which is a market reality rather than a complaint. A block agreed in October costs less per hour than the same block agreed in March.

The third pattern is the one families miss. Price per hour is the wrong unit. A cheaper tutor who needs three sessions to diagnose what a specialist names in one has not saved you anything, and a specialist who sells twenty sessions where eight would do has not earned the premium. Ask any provider how many sessions they expect to need and what evidence they will produce. A provider who cannot answer that is selling hours.

Dubai's KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in that emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year. Abu Dhabi fee decisions sit with ADEK and follow their own timetable. Either way, tutoring is a discretionary cost on top of a fee that is already the largest line in most family budgets, which is a reason to buy the smallest block that does the job.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: exactly where coaching stops
paragraphs: The IB treats work submitted for assessment as the student's own, and a breach is an academic-misconduct matter that falls on the student. This is the part of the market with the worst behaviour in it: one page researched for this project sells finished Internal Assessments at a fixed AED price. That is not tutoring and a family who buys it is buying a malpractice risk that attaches to their child's candidature, not to the seller.

The boundary is workable and we state it before any coursework session. A coach may teach the method, explain the assessment criteria, ask the questions an examiner would ask, mark a draft against the descriptors, point at a paragraph and say that the reasoning does not follow, and show a published exemplar. A coach may not supply text, rework a passage into its final form, invent data, choose the research question on the student's behalf, or hand back a draft with sentences in it that the student did not produce.

The practical test we give coaches is the attribution test: if the student were asked in a viva to explain why a particular sentence is in their work, could they? If the answer is no, the help went too far. That test is more useful than a word count of how much was changed, and it is the one an IB coordinator will effectively apply if a question is ever raised.

There is a second honesty point about materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, markschemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson. We reference them and link to the official sites. We do not host them, supply them as downloads, or reproduce them on these pages.
bullets: A coach marks a draft and questions it; the student writes every word of it.
Nobody on the platform supplies finished coursework, at any price, for any component.
Official syllabus and paper material is linked, never reproduced or sent as a file.
If the student could not defend a sentence in a viva, the help went too far.

sections.heading: Why coaching for Abu Dhabi families runs over video, and what that changes
paragraphs: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Every Abu Dhabi session is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We are direct about this because it is the first thing a family needs to know and because the alternative - a page that implies a doorbell and delivers a video link - wastes everybody's evening.

For coaching specifically, video is not a compromise. The working surface of a coaching session is a document: a marked script, a markscheme, a draft with criterion comments in the margin. Screen sharing puts that document in front of both people at full size, with the annotation visible as it is made, which is better than two people leaning over one printed page. The session can be recorded, so a student revising in April can watch the February explanation again. A tutor sitting in a living room in Khalifa City can do none of that.

The larger effect is on who your child can actually work with. Driving radius is a brutal filter: it selects for proximity and against specialism. A family in Al Reem Island looking for a Chemistry HL coach who has supervised internal assessments gets whoever is within a reasonable drive at 5pm on a Tuesday. Over video the same family gets the person who has read a hundred Chemistry internal assessments, whether they are in Abu Dhabi, Dubai or Mumbai, and the 6pm slot that was impossible by car opens up.

What stays with the school is also clear. Laboratory work, the recorded oral components, CAS and the formal supervision of the Extended Essay belong to your child's teachers and coordinator. A coach works alongside those people and around their deadlines. We ask for the school's assessment calendar at the start precisely so that coaching does not pull against it.

process.title: Send the last marked script
process.description: Before any call, send the most recent piece of marked work: a mock paper, a timed essay, an internal assessment draft with the teacher's comments. One real script tells a coach more than a half-hour conversation about how the term has gone, and it means the first session starts with a diagnosis rather than with questions.

process.title: A free 45-minute diagnostic lesson
process.description: The trial lesson is a working session, not a sales call. The coach marks part of the script with your child, names the error classes they can see, and tests one of them live. There is no charge and no card details are taken. If the diagnosis is that coaching is not what your child needs, we say so and tell you what is.

process.title: A named error list and a fixed block
process.description: You receive a written list of the error classes in order of mark value, with a proposed number of sessions attached. The number is fixed before the block starts, so it is a plan rather than an open tab. If the list is short, the block is short; we would rather run six useful sessions than sell twenty.

process.title: Weekly coaching with the script on screen
process.description: Sessions run one-to-one over live video in your slot, with screen sharing on the student's own work. The annotated script comes back within a day. Every session opens by checking what happened to last week's error class, which is how items get retired rather than merely discussed.

process.title: A timed paper, then a written handover
process.description: Near the end of the block your child sits a full paper under exam conditions and it is marked against the published criteria. The handover sets out what moved, what did not, and what is still weak going into the exam. If a second block is genuinely not needed, the handover says that too.

whyPoints.title: The coach is chosen for the paper, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: Because sessions run over video, the matching question is which component your child is losing marks on, not who can reach Al Mushrif by 5pm. For a Physics HL student struggling with uncertainty handling, that difference is the whole value of the arrangement.

whyPoints.title: Technique is written down, not implied
whyPoints.description: Every block produces an error list, annotated scripts, and a handover document. You can read what is being worked on and check whether the list is shrinking. Progress you cannot see is indistinguishable from progress that is not happening.

whyPoints.title: The markscheme is the authority
whyPoints.description: Coaching decisions are made against the published criteria and the subject guide your child's school uses, not against a tutor's opinion of good work. Where the two conflict, the criteria win, and the student is shown the descriptor rather than told the verdict.

whyPoints.title: Permit and regulator questions get a straight answer
whyPoints.description: We will tell you where a tutor is resident, whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and that IB Gram holds no ADEK licence, no KHDA permit and no UAE office. Ambiguity on these points is common in this market and it is never accidental.

whyPoints.title: We say when coaching is the wrong purchase
whyPoints.description: If the diagnostic shows a syllabus gap rather than a technique problem, we will say the honest thing: buy teaching, not coaching. If no coach on the platform covers your child's subject at the level needed, we will say that too rather than matching somebody approximate.

whyPoints.title: The student's work stays the student's work
whyPoints.description: On internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay, a coach questions and marks and nothing else. Nobody supplies text or reworks a passage into its final form. That line is stated in writing before the first coursework session.

faqs.question: Is IB coaching in Abu Dhabi different from ordinary IB tutoring?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the difference decides whether the money works. Coaching takes the student's own marked script and changes how they convert knowledge into marks: command terms, method lines, timing, criterion-referenced drafting. Tutoring re-teaches topics from the subject guide. A student who can explain photosynthesis out loud but loses half the marks on a six-mark explain question needs coaching. A student who joined a Diploma class in October three chapters behind needs teaching. Bring the last marked paper and the answer is usually obvious within ten minutes. Buying the wrong one is the most common waste in this market.

faqs.question: Which command terms cost Abu Dhabi Diploma students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Explain and evaluate, consistently. Explain asks for linked reasons; under time pressure students describe instead, because describing is what the brain reaches for when it is anxious and knows the content. Evaluate asks for both sides weighed and then a judgement; a large share of answers list both sides and stop, which caps the mark in the middle band whatever the content quality. Determine and calculate cost marks differently: the answer is right and the method is invisible, so method marks are unavailable. All three are fixed by repetition on short questions, re-marked against the term that was actually printed.

faqs.question: How many sessions does an eight-week coaching block need?
faqs.answer: Usually eight to twelve. One session a week through the block, plus a second session in each of the last two weeks when the calendar is tight. We fix the number before the block starts so it is a plan rather than an open tab. More than two sessions a week in the run-in is usually counterproductive, because by that stage the limiting factor is how much independent practice the student does between sessions, and extra contact hours crowd that out. A provider proposing five sessions a week in the final month is selling hours.

faqs.question: Can an IB coach work on my child's Internal Assessment draft?
faqs.answer: A coach can read the draft against the published assessment criteria, mark the gap criterion by criterion, ask the questions an examiner would ask, point at reasoning that does not follow, and show a published exemplar. A coach cannot supply text, rework a passage into its final form, invent data or choose the research question. The test we apply is the attribution test: if your child were asked in a viva why a particular sentence is in their work, could they explain it? If not, the help went too far. The school supervisor remains the authority on the task.

faqs.question: Should my child stop their school support to start coaching?
faqs.answer: No. School support and coaching do different jobs and the school's version is free. Keep the subject teacher for the syllabus, the laboratory work, the recorded oral components and the formal supervision of coursework. A coach works around that calendar, which is why we ask for the school's assessment dates at the start. Where the two genuinely conflict, the school wins: a coach who encourages a student to deprioritise a school deadline in favour of a coaching plan has misunderstood the arrangement. The useful coach is the one your child's teacher would recognise as helping.

faqs.question: What does IB coaching cost per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Market rates for one-to-one IB support in the UAE, from providers' own published pages in October 2026, run from roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200 to AED 450 for an IB specialist, and AED 180 to AED 500 for an in-home visit with travel priced into the hour. A premium named tutor is published at AED 650. Those are market figures with the source named, not our price list. Our answer begins with a free trial lesson and a conversation about how many sessions the error list actually needs.

faqs.question: Do private IB coaches in Abu Dhabi need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: A UAE resident giving private lessons does. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. People tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure appears here. Ask any UAE-based tutor for their permit before the first paid session.

faqs.question: Can my child's own school teacher coach them privately in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: You should assume not. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct has been reported as barring the same arrangement. Treat both as press-reported rather than as the authority's exact wording, and check the current policy document if the decision matters. The practical position is straightforward: a paid private arrangement with your child's own classroom teacher is the one arrangement to avoid, however convenient it looks.

faqs.question: How do you coach a timed paper over live video?
faqs.answer: The student sits the paper offline under real conditions, photographs or scans it, and sends it in. The coach marks it against the published criteria before the session, with timings noted question by question where the student recorded them. In the session the marked script is on screen for both people, annotated live as the conversation goes. Timing data is usually the surprise: students discover they spent nineteen minutes on a six-mark question. Screen sharing a document at full size, with annotation visible as it is made, works better than two people leaning over one printed page.

faqs.question: Is coaching worth it for a student already scoring a 6?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the work looks different. A student at 6 has the content and is losing a narrow band of marks to specific habits: a thesis that arrives in the third paragraph, an evaluation that implies a judgement instead of stating it, a method line omitted because the answer felt obvious. Those are precise fixes and a short block can address them. We will not promise a 7, and any provider who does is selling something we are not. What a block can promise is a named list of what is costing marks and evidence of whether it changed.

faqs.question: When in the Diploma should coaching start?
faqs.answer: The most useful entry point is early in DP2, after the first real internal examinations have produced marked scripts worth diagnosing. Starting in DP1 is reasonable when a student has moved into the IB from a different system and needs the assessment conventions rather than the content. Starting six weeks before the May session is late but not pointless: a focused block on the two highest-value error classes still moves marks. What does not work is starting late and trying to cover everything, which produces a tour of the syllabus and no change in technique.

faqs.question: Can coaching sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most Abu Dhabi families ask for it. School hours shorten during Ramadan and evenings reorganise around Iftar, so the standard 5pm slot stops working. We move sessions to a post-Iftar window, usually between 8.30pm and 10pm Gulf Standard Time, and keep them shorter: forty-five minutes of focused marking review works better than a tired hour. Coaches working from India are an hour and a half behind Gulf Standard Time, which makes late Abu Dhabi slots straightforward rather than a favour. The slot reverts after Eid unless you prefer to keep it.

faqs.question: What should I send before the first coaching lesson?
faqs.answer: Four things, and none of them take long. The most recent marked script with the teacher's comments on it. Your child's subject list with levels, so a coach knows whether this is HL or SL. The school's assessment calendar for the term, including internal draft deadlines. And a sentence from you about what you think is going wrong, which is useful precisely because it often differs from what the script shows. If you have a report with criterion marks on it, send that as well; criterion marks over two terms are the fastest read available.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram coach the Theory of Knowledge essay?
faqs.answer: Coaching for the Theory of Knowledge essay is available and it stays strictly inside the honesty boundary. A coach works on what the prescribed title is actually asking, on whether the chosen areas of knowledge can carry the argument, on the quality of the real-life examples, and on marking a draft against the assessment instrument. The student writes it. Nobody on the platform produces text for a TOK essay, at any price. The exhibition is handled the same way: the coach questions the choice of objects and the link to the prompt, and the student makes every change.

faqs.question: What happens if no coach is free for my child's subject?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than matching somebody approximate. Niche Diploma subjects and the less common language acquisition options are the usual gaps, and so is a specific combination such as Visual Arts process portfolio supervision at HL. When that happens you get three honest options: wait for a named coach to free up with a date attached, take a different but genuinely qualified coach with the limitation stated, or go elsewhere with our suggestion of what to ask for. Concealing a coverage gap wastes a term, which is worse than losing an enquiry.

abu-dhabi/ib-coaching.closingHeading: Start with the script, not the schedule
abu-dhabi/ib-coaching.closingBody: If your child's grade has stalled, the next useful step costs nothing: send the last marked paper and book the free 45-minute diagnostic lesson. The coach will mark part of it with your child, name the error classes, and test one of them live. You will get a written error list in order of mark value and a proposed number of sessions, fixed before anything starts. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which means the coach is chosen for the component your child is losing marks on rather than for a driving radius across Abu Dhabi. If the honest answer is that coaching is not what your child needs, we will tell you that instead.

abu-dhabi/ib-crash-course.tutorsIntro: The tutors below run intensive Diploma blocks for Abu Dhabi students over live video. Each profile names the subject, the level and the components they work on, because an intensive block only earns its price when it is pointed at something specific.

intro.heading: Time pressure is the worst condition for buying tutoring, so start with what is still reachable
paragraphs: Nearly every enquiry for an IB crash course in Abu Dhabi arrives in one of two windows: late October of Diploma Year 12, when the first Higher Level assessments come back worse than expected, or February and March of Year 13, when mock results land and the May papers are suddenly close. Both are moments of genuine urgency, and urgency is the condition under which families buy the most tutoring and get the least out of it. The reason is not the tutors. It is that nobody has separated the parts of the grade that are still open from the parts that have closed.

The Diploma is unusual in this respect. A grade in each subject is assembled from external papers plus an internally assessed component worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the total, and the core adds up to three further points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. Those internal pieces have school deadlines that fall months before the examinations. Once a draft is submitted and the supervisor's declaration is made, no amount of intensive tutoring reaches it. A family spending a crash-course budget in April on a subject whose exploration was the actual problem is spending money on the wrong quarter of the grade.

What remains open in the final weeks is narrower than most marketing suggests and more valuable than most families expect. Timing is open: a candidate who routinely leaves the last question unattempted can be taught to finish, and that is worth real marks in every subject at once. Command-term discipline is open: the gap between "outline" and "explain" is a mark allocation, and correcting it affects every paper simultaneously. Accuracy, units, significant figures and method-shown are open. Paper-specific technique is open, including the long investigative components that almost nobody practises. Content, in the sense of learning a topic from nothing, is mostly closed, and pretending otherwise is the central dishonesty of crash-course advertising.

There is also a question of how many hours a student can absorb. An intensive block is limited by the student's capacity rather than by the family's budget. Two hours a day for a fortnight, with real practice between sessions, is a genuine intervention. Five hours a day for a week is a way of converting money into exhaustion in the fortnight when rest has the highest marginal value it will ever have. A tutor who agrees to the second arrangement without saying so is selling hours rather than teaching.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition as one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For an intensive block that matters practically: a compressed run needs the right specialist for a named component, and in Abu Dhabi the resident pool for a given Higher Level subject is small. Being able to draw on specialists regardless of distance is what makes a short block worth running at all.
bullets: Still open late: timing, command terms, accuracy, method shown, paper-specific technique
Closed once submitted: the exploration or investigation, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge
Mostly closed: learning a Higher Level topic from nothing in the final weeks
Market rate for an IB specialist: AED 200-450+ per hour (Bestimate 2026; TutorChase AED 270)
Capacity, not budget, sets the ceiling: about two focused hours a day is the practical limit
No tutor at any intensity can promise a grade; treat a page that does as a warning

abu-dhabi/ib-crash-course.programmesIntro: Intensive blocks get bought at four different points, and they behave differently at each. The same number of hours is worth several times more at the first than at the last.

programmes.name: Diploma Year 12
programmes.description: The most productive moment for an intensive block and the least common. A short run of hours in the first year can fix command-term habits, settle a research question for the internally assessed component, and repair the subject-choice error that becomes expensive later. Nothing has closed yet, so every hour has the full remaining course to act on.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi enquiries in this window usually follow a first-term report rather than an exam. A block of six to eight hours in November of Year 12, aimed at one Higher Level subject, is the best-value intensive tutoring a Diploma family can buy in this emirate.

programmes.name: Diploma Year 13, before the mocks
programmes.description: The last point at which an intensive block can still include new content with any realism. Internal components are in draft rather than submitted, so feedback on the student's own work still reaches something, and the mock papers that follow give immediate evidence of whether the hours did anything.
programmes.countryNote: This is when weekend and holiday blocks fill in Abu Dhabi, particularly over the winter break. Specialist availability in Higher Level Chemistry, Physics and Mathematics narrows sharply from January, so a block booked in November runs with the tutor you chose rather than the one who was free.

programmes.name: The final run to the May papers
programmes.description: An intensive block here is a technique and timing intervention, not a content one. Full papers sat to time, marked against the scheme in the same session, with each lost mark attributed to a cause. Done narrowly it moves marks. Done as a sweep across six subjects it produces a tired candidate with a lighter bank account.
programmes.countryNote: The honest advice to an Abu Dhabi family arriving in April is usually fewer hours than they came for, concentrated on one or two subjects nearest a boundary, finishing a week before the first paper rather than running into it.

programmes.name: Retakes and the later session
programmes.description: A candidate improving one or two subjects in a later session is the ideal crash-course case, because the diagnosis already exists in the form of a result, the component list is known, and the hours can be aimed with precision. This is the one scenario where an intensive block reliably outperforms a term of weekly sessions.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session as their main series. Retake planning should be confirmed with the school's Diploma coordinator, since availability and registration are handled through the school rather than by a tutor, and we do not publish International Baccalaureate session dates that have not been verified at source.

abu-dhabi/ib-crash-course.subjectsIntro: For each subject, the component that an intensive block can realistically move and the one it cannot. Use this to choose where a fixed number of hours goes.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Movable late: Paper 1 algebraic fluency without a calculator, and Higher Level Paper 3 approach, which most candidates have attempted once or twice. Not movable late: a missing foundation in calculus, which needs months. An intensive block here is best spent on two full Paper 3 attempts with the mark scheme.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Movable late: calculator discipline, statistical interpretation phrasing, and the habit of answering in context rather than in numbers. Not movable late: comfort with modelling from scratch. Intensive sessions work well on full statistics questions, which are slow and rarely practised to completion.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Movable late: organic mechanism conventions, energetics calculation layout, and data-analysis questions with uncertainty. Not movable late: the exploration once submitted, which is where the problem often actually was. Check which it is before buying hours.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Movable late: reasoning from a named principle in writing, uncertainty treatment, and graph work with gradients. Not movable late: a shaky mathematical base, which shows up as an inability to rearrange under time pressure. Intensive blocks suit full data-analysis tasks.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Movable late: command-term discipline and long-answer construction, which are the largest avoidable losses in the subject. Not movable late: the full content load if large parts are genuinely unlearnt. A block of six hours writing marked long answers outperforms twelve hours of reading.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Movable late: diagram accuracy, axis labelling and application to the named context, all of which are mechanical and high-yield. Not movable late: the internally assessed commentaries once submitted. Intensive sessions should audit diagram marks across a full past paper.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Movable late: Paper 1 approach to an unseen non-literary text and essay structure under time. Not movable late: the individual oral once recorded. An intensive block is best spent writing two full Paper 1 responses and reworking the weaker one.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Movable late: argument structure and source evaluation technique, where most losses are shape rather than knowledge. Not movable late: the historical investigation after submission. Sessions should produce one full essay marked and one paragraph rewritten.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Movable late: applying tools to the stimulus rather than generically, and time allocation across a case-study paper. Not movable late: the Higher Level research project once submitted. Full papers to time are the right use of intensive hours.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Movable late: naming specific studies with findings instead of writing generic evaluation, which is the difference between most grades in this subject. Not movable late: the experimental study write-up after submission.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Movable late: pseudocode conventions, trace tables and the written paper's algorithmic questions. Not movable late: the internally assessed solution, including its design documentation, once handed in.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first language
subjects.description: A Ministry-mandated subject in UAE private schools, examined on its own terms and frequently the one a family tries to address in a late block. Supply is thin and overlaps little with the subject-tutor pool, so an intensive block here needs booking earlier than the others.

abu-dhabi/ib-crash-course.regionsTitle: Where intensive blocks run from across Abu Dhabi
abu-dhabi/ib-crash-course.regionsIntro: Intensive blocks are scheduled in daily or near-daily runs, which makes family logistics the binding constraint rather than distance. These are the communities we run blocks for most.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Blocks here are usually run over the winter or spring break rather than in term, because weekday evenings are already full. Higher Level sciences dominate the requests.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha
regions.note: The largest source of intensive enquiries in the emirate, and the most likely to involve two children at different stages, which makes a shared daily window the practical arrangement.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Apartment households where a daily scheduled block provides structure as much as teaching. Morning slots during holidays work best; evening slots compete with everything else.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Dense activity schedules and effectively no resident specialist pool, so blocks here are built around what the family can hold for ten consecutive days rather than around a preferred time.

regions.name: Al Bateen and the western island
regions.note: Bilingual households where an intensive block often has to accommodate Arabic as a first language alongside a Diploma subject, which usually means two separate short runs rather than one.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Karamah
regions.note: Close to several large schools that run their own revision programmes, so private intensive hours here should target what the school programme explicitly skips.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Al Falah
regions.note: Long distances from the island's tutor supply mean a daily in-home block is not a realistic arrangement at all. Online delivery is what makes an intensive run possible in these communities.

regions.name: Masdar City and Al Ghadeer
regions.note: Small school-age populations with no local specialist pool to draw on. Blocks are scheduled purely around family routine, and travel stops being a variable in the plan.

schoolClusters.city: The islands: Saadiyat, Al Reem and Yas
schoolClusters.note: Small Diploma subject cohorts, which means a Higher Level subject may have only a few dozen candidates in the emirate and the specialist pool for an intensive block is correspondingly thin.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and the eastern mainland
schoolClusters.note: Diploma, British and American routes within a few kilometres of each other, so intensive blocks here often have to run alongside a sibling studying an entirely different system.

schoolClusters.city: The central island and Al Mushrif
schoolClusters.note: Established schools with their own revision provision over the breaks, which is worth auditing before buying intensive hours so the block covers the gaps rather than repeating the programme.

abu-dhabi/ib-crash-course.modesIntro: Three shapes an intensive block can take. The right one is decided by how specific the diagnosis is and how much time is left, not by how worried anyone is.

modes.title: The holiday block
modes.description: Daily or near-daily sessions across a school break, typically eight to fourteen sessions over two or three weeks. The most effective intensive format, because a full day is available rather than an evening carved out of a tired week, and because consecutive days let a correction be practised before it is forgotten.

One named component per session, not a subject sweep
Practice set between sessions and reviewed at the next
Finishes before term restarts rather than trailing into it

modes.title: The targeted short run
modes.description: Four to eight sessions over two to four weeks aimed at one subject and one or two components, usually after a marked mock has identified exactly where the marks went. The cheapest intensive format and the one with the clearest evidence of whether it worked.
bullets: Begins from a marked script, not a topic list
One subject, one or two named components
Measurable against the next assessment
Stops when the named losses stop recurring

modes.title: The paper-practice run
modes.description: A sequence of sessions in the final weeks, each built around one complete paper sat to time and marked in the same session. No new content, no syllabus coverage, no notes. Suited to a candidate whose problem is timing, accuracy or command terms rather than knowledge.
bullets: One full paper per session, sat under timed conditions
Marked against the scheme while the reasoning is fresh
Each lost mark attributed to timing, method or vocabulary
Ends a week before the first paper, by design

sections.heading: What is still open, and what closed months ago
paragraphs: This is the section that should decide whether you buy anything at all. A Diploma grade is not one thing arriving in May; it is a set of components with staggered deadlines, and an intensive block can only act on the ones still open. Families who skip this step reliably spend money on the wrong quarter of the grade, and no tutor can give that money back.

The internally assessed components are the clearest case. Each subject's exploration, investigation, commentary or project is worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the subject grade. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge together contribute up to three points to the diploma total. All of these have school deadlines that fall well before the examination period, and all of them are declared by a supervisor. After submission they are finished. If your child's problem in Chemistry was a weak exploration, an April crash course in Chemistry papers does not touch it, however good the teaching is.

What remains open is technique that generalises. Timing is the biggest single item: a candidate who consistently runs out of time is losing marks they could already have earned, in every subject at once, and it is correctable in a fortnight with timed practice and a per-question clock. Command-term discipline is next. Accuracy conventions, units and significant figures are next. Method-shown comes after that, since step marks are available even where the final answer goes wrong. These four, taken together, are worth more in a short window than any amount of content revision.

Content occupies a middle position that deserves honesty. Consolidating a topic the student has met and half-forgotten is realistic in a short block. Teaching a Higher Level topic the student has never understood is not, and the appearance of progress in such a session is usually recognition rather than competence. A tutor should say which category your child's gap falls into after one diagnostic session, and should be willing to say the second out loud.

sections.heading: Rationing a fixed number of hours across six subjects
paragraphs: A Diploma candidate studies six subjects. A crash course buys perhaps ten, twenty or thirty hours. The arithmetic is brutal and most families resolve it badly, by dividing the hours evenly or by giving them to whichever subject feels most frightening. Both approaches reliably waste the budget.

The better method is to rank by marks available rather than by distress. For each subject, ask three things: how far is the current level from the next grade boundary, how much of the remaining assessment is still ahead, and how mechanical is the identified weakness? A subject two marks below a boundary with a timing problem is the best possible use of hours. A subject fifteen marks below with a conceptual gap is the worst, because the hours will produce visible improvement and no grade change.

Then apply the Higher Level weighting. Higher Level subjects carry the same 1 to 7 scale but typically have more assessment ahead and a harder final paper, so the same hour often returns more there. Against that, Higher Level content is harder to repair late, which pushes in the opposite direction. The resolution is usually to put intensive hours into one Higher Level subject where the weakness is technique, and leave a Higher Level subject with a conceptual gap to school provision and the student's own work.

Finally, protect the general items. Two or three hours spent on timing and command terms, using scripts from several subjects at once, affect all six grades. Families almost never buy this because it does not feel like a subject, and it is consistently the highest-yield purchase in a short window. sections.heading: What an intensive block costs in this market
paragraphs: Intensive hours are priced from the same bands as weekly ones, with two adjustments that pull in opposite directions. A named IB specialist in the UAE market runs from about AED 200 to AED 450 an hour and beyond; TutorChase publishes AED 270, Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts specialists at 200 to 450 plus, and a premium named tutor has been advertised in the Gulf at AED 650. Those are other providers' published figures, quoted here because three of the six competitor pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all.

The first adjustment is downward: a booked run of sessions prices below the same number of ad hoc hours, because the tutor plans once and holds a sequence of slots rather than negotiating each one. Families generally see that discount in the ten to twenty per cent range. The second adjustment is upward and larger: demand for specialist hours in Abu Dhabi concentrates from February onwards, when every Year 13 household in the emirate wants the same subjects in the same weeks. A block booked in November runs with the tutor you chose; a block booked in March runs with whoever is left.

Monthly package shapes in the UAE market give a second reference point. Around AED 799 a month is advertised for eight online sessions, against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four in-home double sessions, which works out at roughly double per hour of teaching once travel is accounted for. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, 600 to 1,200 mid-range and 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. An intensive block compresses a comparable total into weeks rather than months.

IB Gram publishes no rate card on these pages, and the reason is that the right number depends entirely on subject, level and availability. What we do commit to is that the rate is confirmed before any paid session, that the first lesson is free and takes no card, and that no package is required to start. Anyone asking for commitment before a diagnostic lesson is asking you to buy a service nobody has yet established you need.

sections.heading: The diagnostic hour that decides the rest
paragraphs: An intensive block should open with a diagnosis rather than with teaching, and the diagnosis should be specific enough to change the plan. This is the single biggest difference between a block that works and one that feels busy. A session that begins "what would you like to go over?" has already wasted the most valuable hour in the sequence.

The raw material is a marked script. A mock paper with the examiner's or teacher's marks on it, read against the mark scheme, tells a specialist more in forty minutes than a week of conversation: where the time ran out, which command terms were misread, whether method was shown, whether the losses cluster in one topic or scatter across the paper. A report with grades on it is a poor substitute, because it records the outcome rather than the mechanism.

What the diagnostic hour should produce is a short written list: the three or four specific losses, each attributed to a cause, with an estimate of how many marks each is worth and whether it is reachable in the time available. That list is what the rest of the block spends its hours on, and it is what a parent should ask to see. If no such list emerges, the block has no plan, and the sessions will default to content coverage because content coverage is the easiest thing to fill an hour with.

The same hour should also produce an honest statement of what the block will not attempt. A tutor who tells you that the Chemistry exploration is submitted and therefore out of reach, or that the Higher Level calculus gap is too wide to close by May, is giving you the most useful information in the whole arrangement. We make that first lesson free precisely because a family deserves that answer before paying for anything, and sometimes the answer is that fewer hours are needed than they came for.

sections.heading: Intensity, sleep and the limits of a compressed week
paragraphs: The constraint on an intensive block is not money and not tutor availability. It is how much teaching a seventeen-year-old can convert into performance in a day, and the honest figure is lower than families want to hear. Roughly two hours of focused one-to-one work, plus independent practice on what that session corrected, is a full day's academic load for most candidates in the final weeks.

Beyond that, the returns do not merely diminish, they reverse. A student who has had five hours of tutoring has had three hours in which nothing was retained and has lost the evening in which the first two hours might have been consolidated. Practice is where the correction becomes permanent, and practice requires time the block has consumed. This is why a well-designed intensive run sets work between sessions and reviews it at the start of the next one, rather than filling the gap with more teaching.

Sleep is the other item nobody includes in the plan. In the fortnight before examinations, rest has a higher marginal value than any additional hour of instruction, and a block that encroaches on it is converting money into a worse result. A tutor should be willing to recommend a shorter block for this reason, and a family should be suspicious of one who recommends the opposite without having seen the student's schedule.

Timing within the day matters in Abu Dhabi specifically. Holiday blocks work best in the morning, when a student is rested and the day has not fragmented. Term-time blocks have to sit in the evening and should be shorter accordingly. During Ramadan, sessions shift to post-Iftar timing, and the sensible adjustment is shorter blocks at the same weekly total rather than the same blocks later, because sustained concentration while fasting is genuinely harder. We schedule around that rather than treating it as an exception.

sections.heading: Academic honesty under time pressure
paragraphs: A compressed block in the weeks before a deadline is the point at which the academic-honesty boundary comes under the most pressure, which is why it belongs on a crash-course page rather than in a footnote. One of the sites competing for Diploma searches in this market sells completed internal assessments. That is not an expedited form of tutoring; it is malpractice, and under International Baccalaureate rules the consequence falls on the candidate rather than on the seller.

What a tutor may properly do is extensive and covers nearly everything a student under pressure actually needs. They can teach the method a component assesses. They can question a research question until it is answerable within the word limit. They can explain in plain language what each criterion descriptor is asking for. They can read a student's own draft and identify, criterion by criterion, where the mark is not yet earned and why. They can teach referencing and explain what counts as a student's own work.

What a tutor must not do is produce any part of a submission. Not a paragraph, not a rewritten conclusion, not an edit that substitutes the tutor's sentences for the student's. The student produces every word submitted, and the school supervisor declares the support the candidate received. A tutor who raises this boundary unprompted in the first session, and is willing to put it in writing, is protecting your child. One who treats a deadline as a reason to be flexible about it is not.

Material is subject to the same rule. Subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables belong to the International Baccalaureate and the examination boards; a tutor references them and links the official source rather than distributing copies. Nobody outside an examination centre has lawful access to unreleased material, and any suggestion of such access in the weeks before a session should end the arrangement immediately, whatever has already been paid.

sections.heading: Who may lawfully run a tutoring block in the UAE
paragraphs: An intensive block is subject to the same rules as a weekly session, and the rules here are clearer than most of this market. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services system.

Eligibility is broader than parents assume: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount appears here, and any page quoting one is quoting something unverified.

Abu Dhabi adds a restriction that becomes relevant in exactly this scenario, because a family under pressure often thinks first of a teacher who already knows the child. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document here, so check the current ADEK publication before relying on the exact wording. The practical rule is to look outside your child's own school.

A centre with premises and staff requires an educational services permit from the emirate regulator, which is a different instrument from an individual tutor's permit and is not a quality rating. IB Gram holds no such permit and claims none. It is an independent tutor-matching platform, delivery is online and one-to-one, and no tutor here is described as approved, accredited or licensed by ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the International Baccalaureate or any examination board.

sections.heading: When the honest answer is fewer hours, or none
paragraphs: A crash course is the easiest tutoring to sell and the hardest to sell honestly, because the buyer is anxious and the clock is visible. There are several situations in which the right recommendation is to buy less than the family came for, and a tutor unwilling to make that recommendation is worth avoiding whatever their rate.

The first is when the problem is a closed component. If the subject grade was damaged by an exploration already submitted, hours spent on papers cannot recover it, and the family should be told so rather than sold a block that produces a slightly better paper and the same grade. The second is when the gap is too wide. A Higher Level subject fifteen marks below the next boundary with a conceptual rather than mechanical weakness will show visible improvement under intensive teaching and will not change grade, and spending the budget elsewhere protects marks that are genuinely reachable.

The third is capacity. A candidate already working six hours a day in the final fortnight does not have room for five hours of tutoring, and adding them trades rest for instruction at precisely the wrong exchange rate. The fourth is specialist availability: if no UAE-based specialist is free in the subject and level needed, we say so rather than putting a generalist into a specialist-priced block. A generalist running an intensive course is worse value than a short run with the right person and considerably worse than two sessions a week with someone who knows the component.

The positive version of this is that a correctly scoped block often costs less than the one a family imagined. Three hours on timing and command terms plus six hours on the subject nearest a boundary is a smaller purchase than twenty hours spread evenly, and in most cases it is the one that changes a result. The diagnostic lesson is free and takes no card precisely so that this conversation can happen before any money moves.
