process.title: Say how much time is left and what is already submitted
process.description: The first two facts that matter are the date of the next assessment and which internally assessed components have gone in. Together they decide whether an intensive block is worth buying at all, and they take one sentence to establish.

process.title: Send the marked script
process.description: A mock paper with marks on it, not a report and not a topic list. It is the raw material for the diagnosis, and without it the first session becomes a conversation about feelings rather than an audit of where the marks went.

process.title: Take the free diagnostic lesson
process.description: A full lesson, no payment and no card held. It should end with three or four named losses, each attributed to a cause, with an estimate of marks available and an explicit list of what the block will not attempt. Ask for that list in writing.

process.title: Agree the hours, the shape and the finish date
process.description: How many sessions, over how many days, on which components, ending when. An intensive block should have a planned end rather than a rolling continuation, and the finish date should sit before the first paper rather than during the series.

process.title: Review after a third of the hours
process.description: A third of the way in, read the session notes and ask whether the named losses are recurring less. If they are, continue. If they are not, the diagnosis was wrong and the remaining hours should be redirected rather than spent on the same plan.

whyPoints.title: A stated list of what we will not attempt
whyPoints.description: Every intensive block opens with an explicit account of which components are closed and which gaps are too wide to close in the time left. That list is the most useful thing a family under pressure can be given, and it is the thing crash-course advertising omits.

whyPoints.title: Hours aimed at components, not spread across subjects
whyPoints.description: An even split across six subjects is the commonest way an intensive budget is wasted. We rank by marks available and mechanical fixability, and we fund the general items such as timing and command terms first because they affect every subject at once.

whyPoints.title: Specialists reachable regardless of distance
whyPoints.description: Delivery is online and one-to-one, so a daily block for a family in Al Shamkha or Al Ghadeer draws on the same specialists as one on Saadiyat. For a compressed run that is the difference between the right tutor and the available one.

whyPoints.title: A planned finish date
whyPoints.description: Blocks are scoped with an end, normally a week before the first paper. A tutoring arrangement that rolls on into the examination fortnight is taking time from rest when rest has its highest value of the year.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary stated before the deadline pressure
whyPoints.description: On any assessed component the tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work, and produces no part of a submission. Raised in the first session and recorded, because a compressed timetable is when this matters most.

whyPoints.title: Nothing claimed that cannot be checked
whyPoints.description: No board or regulator approval, no self-published ratings, no statistics without a count and a method, and no promise about a grade at any intensity. Every rate on this page is another provider's published figure, named and dated.

faqs.question: What is actually in an IB crash course, and what is marketing?
faqs.answer: The substance is a short sequence of sessions aimed at named components, opened by a diagnosis from a marked script and closed on a planned date. The marketing is the implication that a compressed block can cover a syllabus. It cannot. What it can genuinely reach late is timing, command-term discipline, accuracy conventions, method shown and paper-specific technique, all of which generalise across subjects. What it cannot reach is any internally assessed component already submitted, or a Higher Level topic the student has never understood. A provider who will not say that second part is selling hours.

faqs.question: How many hours does a useful IB crash course run to?
faqs.answer: Usually between eight and twenty-four, and the number is set by what the diagnosis found rather than by the time remaining. A targeted run on one subject after a marked mock is often four to eight sessions. A holiday block covering one Higher Level subject plus the general timing and command-term work runs twelve to eighteen. Beyond about two focused hours a day the returns reverse, because practice and rest are where corrections become permanent. A plan that proposes five hours a day has been designed around a budget rather than a student.

faqs.question: We have eight weeks until the papers. What can a crash course still change?
faqs.answer: Quite a lot, provided you target the generalising items. Timing is the biggest: a candidate who regularly leaves the last question unattempted is losing marks already earned, and timed practice with a per-question clock fixes it inside a fortnight. Command-term discipline is next, and it affects every paper at once. Accuracy, units and method shown follow. Paper-specific technique, including the long investigative components most candidates have barely attempted, is reachable. What eight weeks will not do is teach a Higher Level topic from nothing or recover a submitted internal assessment.

faqs.question: Which Diploma components are already closed by the time a crash course starts?
faqs.answer: Anything submitted and declared. Each subject's internally assessed component, worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the subject grade, closes at the school's internal deadline. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, which together contribute up to three points, close earlier still. Recorded orals in the language subjects are closed once recorded. This is why the first question to ask before buying intensive hours is which components have gone in, because a block aimed at papers cannot repair a grade that was damaged by an exploration submitted in February.

faqs.question: How much does an intensive IB block cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Intensive hours price from the same bands as weekly ones. Published market rates for an IB specialist run from about AED 200 to AED 450 an hour and above: TutorChase lists AED 270, Bestimate's 2026 table puts specialists at 200 to 450 plus, and a premium named tutor has been advertised in the Gulf at AED 650. A booked run typically prices ten to twenty per cent below the same hours bought ad hoc, though that discount narrows from February as specialist demand concentrates. Those are other providers' figures; our rate is confirmed before any paid session and the first lesson is free.

faqs.question: Does a crash course across six Diploma subjects ever work?
faqs.answer: Not as six separate courses, no. Twenty hours divided evenly is three hours a subject, which is enough to look busy and not enough to change anything. What does work across all six at once is the general layer: timing, command terms, accuracy and method shown, taught using scripts drawn from several subjects, because those losses recur identically everywhere. Three hours there plus concentrated hours in one or two subjects nearest a grade boundary is a far better use of the same budget than an even split.

faqs.question: Is a crash course worth it for a predicted-grade problem rather than an exam one?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the timing is different. Predicted grades are set by the school from its own evidence, which usually means mock papers and coursework performance, so the intervention has to land before those assessments rather than before the final papers. That makes a short block in the autumn of Year 13 the relevant purchase, aimed at whatever the next internal assessment will measure. Speak to the school about what evidence it uses first; buying hours without knowing that is aiming at a target nobody has described.

faqs.question: How do we choose which two subjects get the crash course hours?
faqs.answer: Rank by marks available, not by anxiety. For each subject ask how far the current level sits from the next boundary, how much assessment is still ahead, and whether the identified weakness is mechanical or conceptual. A subject two marks below a boundary with a timing problem is the best possible use of hours. A subject fifteen marks below with a conceptual gap is the worst, because the hours produce visible improvement and no grade change. Higher Level subjects usually have more assessment ahead, which tilts the decision towards them when the weakness is technique.

faqs.question: Can a crash course fix a Higher Level subject my child is failing?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on why. If the marks are being lost to timing, misread command terms, unshown method or an unpractised paper format, then yes, and sometimes substantially. If the student has never understood a major strand of the course, then no: intensive teaching will produce recognition rather than competence, and the exam will not reward recognition. One diagnostic session reading a marked script against the mark scheme distinguishes the two cases, and an honest tutor will tell you which one you are in before you buy a block.

faqs.question: What does an intensive block look like during the Abu Dhabi school holidays?
faqs.answer: Morning sessions, near-daily, typically eight to fourteen across two or three weeks, with practice set between them and reviewed at the start of the next. Holidays are the best window for intensity because a rested student in the morning absorbs more than a tired one in the evening, and consecutive days let a correction be practised before it fades. The caution is that intensity without a target is just volume: four long sessions on named components beats fourteen sessions of general revision, and costs less.

faqs.question: Is a crash course useful before the November session rather than May?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the planning is the same but the calendar differs. UAE schools sit the May session as their main series, so a November candidate is usually a retake or a student on a different school calendar, which means the diagnosis already exists in the form of a result. That makes the hours easier to aim. We do not publish International Baccalaureate session dates on these pages because we have not verified them at source; confirm the window and the registration route with your school's Diploma coordinator, and plan the block backwards from what they tell you.

faqs.question: My child is retaking one Diploma subject. Is an intensive block the right shape?
faqs.answer: This is the clearest case for one. A retake comes with a result, which is a precise diagnosis: you know the component breakdown, you know where the marks went, and you are working on one subject rather than six. An intensive block of eight to sixteen sessions aimed at the two weakest components will usually outperform a term of weekly general sessions. Confirm the registration route and the available session with the school first, since both are handled through the school rather than by a tutor, then build the block backwards from that date.

faqs.question: What should come out of the diagnostic session that opens an intensive block?
faqs.answer: A short written list: three or four specific losses, each attributed to a cause, with an estimate of how many marks each is worth and whether it is reachable in the time left. Alongside it, an explicit statement of what the block will not attempt, naming any submitted component and any gap too wide to close. Ask to see both. If no list emerges, the block has no plan, and the sessions will drift into content coverage because content coverage is the easiest way to fill an hour.

faqs.question: Can a crash course help with Theory of Knowledge this late?
faqs.answer: Only if it has not yet been submitted. Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title, both with school deadlines that fall well before the examination period, and both contributing to the three core points available with the Extended Essay. Before submission, a tutor can teach the method, question whether a chosen title can actually be argued, explain what the criteria ask for, and give feedback on the student's own draft. After submission it is closed, and the hours are better spent on the external papers.

faqs.question: How do we stop a crash course turning into last-minute coursework help?
faqs.answer: State the boundary at the first session and get it in writing. A tutor may teach method, question a research question, explain criterion descriptors and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not produce any part of a submission, including a rewritten paragraph or an edit that replaces the student's sentences. The student writes every word submitted and the school supervisor declares the support received. A deadline is not a reason to soften that, and any provider who treats it as one is exposing your child rather than helping.

abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: Profiles below name the course and level each tutor teaches, and whether they supervise coursework in that subject. Supervision is a distinct skill from teaching: it is questioning, criterion reading and deadline discipline, and a tutor who is excellent at timed paper technique is not automatically good at it.

intro.heading: The home in home tutoring is where the Diploma is actually written
paragraphs: The Diploma is unusual among school qualifications in how much of it is produced outside a classroom. An Extended Essay of up to 4,000 words, a Theory of Knowledge essay of 1,600, an Internal Assessment in every one of six subjects, and a service record all have to be made somewhere, and that somewhere is a bedroom or a dining table in Khalifa City or Al Mushrif. The examinations get the attention. The coursework decides as much and is produced at home with almost no supervision.

This is why the phrase home tutor is the one Abu Dhabi families type. What they usually want is not a visitor; it is somebody who takes responsibility for the part of the Diploma that happens at home. Somebody who knows when the school's internal deadline for the scientific investigation really is, who has read the criteria the student is being marked against, and who will notice in October that an Extended Essay question cannot be answered in the word limit, rather than in February when it cannot be changed.

Two things should be said plainly before anything else. First, independent tutors in Abu Dhabi do travel to homes and charge for it, and market in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to AED 350 an hour in Bestimate's 2026 survey, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to AED 500. Those are market figures, not ours. Second, IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India, and UAE tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video.

For coursework specifically, the online format is not a compromise. Supervision work is reading, questioning and annotating, and a shared screen with the student's own document open is a better instrument for that than two people looking at one laptop across a table. The student keeps control of their file, the annotation is visible, and nothing physical changes hands, which also happens to be the cleanest position to be in on academic honesty.

What follows is the practical version of a DP2 year at home. A comparison of who should do which part of the coursework job, because most coursework disasters come from the school supervisor, the tutor and the parent each doing somebody else's task. A week-by-week map of the autumn and winter, with the collision point named in advance rather than discovered. Twelve scenarios with the honesty line marked on each, because the vague version of that rule is what gets students into trouble and the fearful version deprives them of teaching they are entitled to. The physical and behavioural things at home that measurably change output and cost almost nothing to change. And what a parent should and should not do at the table, which is a shorter list than most parents expect and a more useful one.

The volume of independent writing is the structural difference from every other post-16 route, and it is produced at home.
programmes.countryNote: An Abu Dhabi DP2 student sitting the May session meets their heaviest coursework collision in the winter months, when school internal deadlines, mock papers and university application work overlap. That fortnight is predictable a year ahead, and planning for it is the cheapest intervention available to a family here.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-assessed work across eight subject groups, with an interdisciplinary element and a Personal Project in the final year. The Personal Project is the first genuinely independent long piece a student produces, and it is the rehearsal for the Extended Essay whether anybody says so or not.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi students who took the Personal Project seriously arrive in DP1 with the habits the Extended Essay needs: a question, a timeline and a supervisor relationship. Those who treated it as a formality meet all three for the first time under far higher stakes.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. The reflective project is the home-produced centrepiece and carries the same honesty rules as any Diploma coursework.
programmes.countryNote: Local supervision for the reflective project is almost non-existent in Abu Dhabi because so few schools run the programme. Families usually need an online supervisor and should arrange it well before the project starts rather than once it has stalled.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-based units with no graded examinations and no formal coursework. The relevant thread to the Diploma is writing stamina and the ability to work on something for more than one sitting.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Abu Dhabi with both a DP2 student and a primary child frequently find the primary child's homework displaced entirely during coursework weeks. Naming that in advance and protecting a separate slot for the younger child is worth more than it sounds.

abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Every Diploma subject has work that is produced at home, and the thing a session actually fixes differs by subject. The notes below name that specifically rather than describing the course.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: A session fixes the investigation design before the data exists: one measurable variable, a trial run, and enough repeats to say something. After the data is collected, the only thing left to fix is the evaluation section, which is where the remaining accessible marks sit.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A session fixes the gap between a biological question and an investigable one. Students choose topics they find interesting and cannot measure. The second thing it fixes is command-term handling in extended responses, which transfers to every other paper the student sits.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: A session fixes working presentation: stating the principle before the algebra, carrying units through, and not over-rounding. For the investigation, it fixes uncertainty handling, which is the part students treat as decoration and markers treat as substance.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: A session fixes an Exploration topic that has no mathematics to develop, which is the most common fault in the whole component. It also fixes the Higher Level investigative paper, which schools cover last and students meet cold.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: A session fixes modelling vocabulary and calculator technique, then the Exploration's statistical choices. Students often run a test whose assumptions their data does not meet, which costs criterion marks regardless of how well it is written up.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A session fixes article choice for the commentaries. An article that is too old, too general or too long cannot be analysed within the word limit, and no amount of good writing recovers it. After that, the fix is evaluation rather than description.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: A session fixes a historical investigation question narrow enough for real source work, and then the source-evaluation section, which is written last and thinly. The 2,200-word limit punishes a broad question more than a difficult one.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: A session fixes the experimental report: a replicable study, correct ethical handling and a discussion that engages with the original research rather than summarising it. Students frequently choose a study they cannot replicate within a school setting.

subjects.name: English A: Literature
subjects.description: A session fixes the individual oral pairing, where a weak choice of extracts caps the mark, and the habit of listing techniques instead of arguing about meaning. The learner portfolio is the under-used tool that makes the rest easier.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: A session fixes register and text-type conventions rather than vocabulary, and rehearses the individual oral under timed conditions. Abu Dhabi students also carry the emirate's mandatory Arabic requirement alongside this, which is separate work.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: A session fixes the comparative study and the process portfolio, which carry marks that strong studio students leave on the table. The written rationale is the component most often produced in the final week and most visibly rushed.

abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Home study conditions vary enormously across Abu Dhabi and they affect Diploma output more than most families expect. These notes describe each area in terms of what a student's working week at home actually looks like there.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Villa living with space for a dedicated desk, and the common problem is the opposite of cramped: a student working in a large family area with constant movement through it. A door that closes is worth more than a bigger room.

regions.name: Golf Gardens
regions.note: Quiet, low-density and well suited to long study blocks, which makes it one of the easier areas in the emirate for Extended Essay work. The risk here is isolation rather than noise, and a fixed weekly check-in matters more.

regions.name: Al Mushrif
regions.note: Established villa district with large households and frequent guests, where the majlis rhythm competes with evening study. Families who agree a protected two-hour window in advance lose far fewer coursework hours in a term.

regions.name: Al Karamah
regions.note: Mixed apartments and villas close to the city centre, where students often share a room with a sibling. A shared room is workable for revision and poor for drafting, which argues for a library or school study hall for long writing.

regions.name: Al Muroor
regions.note: Dense residential streets with short school commutes, which gives students more usable afternoon time than most of the emirate. The practical advantage is that an early evening slot is genuinely available here.

regions.name: Al Manaseer
regions.note: Apartment living near the centre with limited desk space in many flats. Students here commonly work on a laptop on a bed, which measurably reduces output on long writing tasks and is a cheap thing to change.

regions.name: Al Rawdah
regions.note: Settled residential area with a steady school-run pattern and predictable evenings, which makes a fixed recurring tutoring slot easy to keep. Predictability is the single biggest advantage a coursework year can have.

regions.name: Al Maqtaa
regions.note: Between the bridges, with long commutes to island schools that eat the late afternoon. Students here benefit from doing coursework in the morning at weekends rather than attempting it after a late bus arrival.

schoolClusters.city: Al Mushrif, Al Karamah and Al Muroor
schoolClusters.note: Central districts feeding long-established schools with mature Diploma cohorts. Requests from these households are dominated by coursework supervision in the DP2 autumn rather than by subject remediation.

schoolClusters.city: Al Raha Gardens, Golf Gardens and Al Maqtaa
schoolClusters.note: Villa communities whose students travel to the Khalifa City and Al Raha school corridor. Extended Essay and scientific investigation supervision is the dominant request, often starting late in DP1.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi

abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-home-tutor.schoolDisclaimer: Schools appear here only to describe the Abu Dhabi education map. No affiliation, partnership, endorsement or client relationship with any named school or group is implied.
abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-home-tutor.modesIntro: Coursework work has three natural patterns and they are not interchangeable. All are delivered one-to-one over live video, with the student's own document on screen and nothing handed over in either direction.

modes.title: Fortnightly supervision with a written note
modes.description: Ninety minutes every two weeks through the drafting period, with a short written summary afterwards naming the criterion to work on next. The gap between sessions is deliberate: the student has to produce something before the next one is useful, and a weekly rhythm often means a session spent discussing work that does not yet exist.

modes.title: The framing block, bought early
modes.description: Two or three sessions at the very start of a coursework piece, spent entirely on the question, the variable or the article choice. This is the highest-return purchase in the Diploma and the least popular, because at that stage nothing feels wrong yet. By the time it does feel wrong, the decision is no longer changeable.
bullets: Two or three sessions before any research or data collection

modes.title: Deadline triage
modes.description: A single session when three deadlines land in one fortnight, used to decide the order and what gets a minimum viable version. The outcome is a written plan with hours allocated, not teaching. It is the session most likely to save a DP2 winter and the one families least often think to ask for.

sections.heading: Who should actually do each part of the coursework job
paragraphs: A Diploma student with a piece of coursework has three potential sources of help and they are not substitutes for each other. The school supervisor holds authority over the process and is the only person who can approve a question or confirm a deadline. A private tutor can question, read drafts and give criterion-level feedback. The parent can protect time and ask questions nobody else will ask. Most coursework disasters come from one of the three doing another's job.

The school supervisor is the one families under-use. They are assigned, they are obliged to meet the student, and their judgement is the one the board recognises. A student who arrives at those meetings with a written question and a plan gets far more from them than one who arrives empty handed, and a tutor's most useful contribution is often preparing the student for the supervisor meeting rather than replacing it.

A private tutor's value is in the questioning that a busy teacher with a full cohort cannot do in fifteen-minute slots. Is this question answerable in the word limit. Can this variable be measured more than once. Does this article contain enough specificity to analyse. Those conversations take an hour each and they decide the outcome.

The table sets out the division explicitly, including the parts a parent should take and the parts nobody outside the student should touch. It is worth reading as a boundary document rather than a service description.

sections.heading: The DP2 autumn and winter, week by week
paragraphs: A DP2 year has a shape and almost every Abu Dhabi family discovers it one term too late. The table below is a generic map rather than a calendar: the real dates belong to your school's own deadline list, which is the single most useful document a Diploma parent can obtain and which most never ask for.

On board dates, this page publishes none for the IB, because specific session, upload and results dates have not been confirmed from the IB directly for this project. Confirm each with your school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org. What can be said is the pattern: Abu Dhabi schools sit the May session, so internal coursework deadlines fall through the autumn and winter and the papers follow in the spring term.

The collision point is predictable. In most schools the scientific investigation, the Extended Essay final draft and the mock examination window land within about six weeks of each other, and university application deadlines sit on top. That fortnight is visible a year in advance and it is where the year is won or lost. Families who buy the framing block in September rather than weekly hours in January arrive at it with two of the three pieces finished.

The weekly expectation at home is worth stating because it is routinely underestimated. A Diploma student is generally carrying homework for six courses, Theory of Knowledge reading, a service commitment and a long coursework piece. The honest arithmetic is that coursework needs a protected block rather than the gaps between other work, and the block has to be in the calendar before the week starts or it will not happen.

sections.heading: Twelve scenarios, and where the honesty line falls on each
paragraphs: The academic-honesty rule is simple to state and hard to apply in the moment. Every piece of assessed work must be the student's own. The difficulty is that real situations are specific, a student at 11pm with a deadline tomorrow is not consulting a policy document, and the consequence of getting it wrong can be the loss of the whole diploma rather than one grade.

So here is the line drawn on twelve situations that actually arise in Abu Dhabi households. Most of them are more permissive than nervous parents expect, which matters: a family that believes all help is forbidden deprives a student of legitimate teaching, and a family that believes anything goes is risking the qualification.

The pattern across all twelve is worth internalising. Help that develops the student's own capability is permitted. Help that substitutes for it is not. A question is almost always fine. A sentence written for the student almost never is. The practical test is whether, after the help, the student could produce something comparable unaided; if not, the line has been crossed.

Where there is genuine doubt, the correct destination is the school, not a tutoring website. The school's own academic-honesty policy governs, the Diploma coordinator interprets it, and a student who asks is treated very differently from a student who is found out. A tutor who discourages that conversation is not acting in the student's interest. It is also worth knowing that policies differ between schools on points such as third-party proofreading, so the answer your neighbour's child was given may not be the answer that applies to yours.

sections.heading: The desk, the door and the phone
paragraphs: Three physical facts about a home affect Diploma output more than any study technique, and all three are cheap to change. They are worth naming because families spend thousands of dirhams on tutoring while leaving them unaddressed.

The first is the writing surface. A student drafting 4,000 words on a laptop on a bed produces measurably less and worse work than the same student at a desk with the screen at eye level and room for a second document. This is not a comfort point; it is about being able to see the criteria and the draft at the same time, which is how criterion-led writing actually works.

The second is the door. Long-form writing requires uninterrupted blocks, and an interruption costs far more than the minute it takes. In Abu Dhabi households with guests, siblings and a majlis rhythm, the protected block has to be agreed with the whole family rather than assumed by the student. Two protected hours twice a week beats seven interrupted ones.

The third is the phone, and the honest version of this advice is not about willpower. A phone in the room with notifications enabled fragments attention even when it is not touched. The arrangement that works is the device in a different room for a fixed block, agreed in advance, with a stated end time. Students accept this far more readily when it is bounded than when it is presented as a rule about character.

sections.heading: What a session fixes, component by component
paragraphs: Families often buy sessions without a clear picture of what one hour can change. For coursework the answer is specific and it varies enormously by when the session happens, which is the whole argument for buying early.

At the start of a piece, an hour can change the entire ceiling. A question narrowed from a general theme to something answerable, a variable chosen so that it can be measured ten times rather than once, an article swapped for one specific enough to analyse: each of those takes under an hour and each raises the maximum achievable mark. Nothing later in the process has that leverage.

In the middle of a piece, an hour changes a criterion. The tutor reads what exists, identifies that the analysis is description, and the student rewrites that section with a clearer target. Repeat over three or four sessions and the draft improves in a directed way rather than generally. This is the standard useful pattern and it accounts for most legitimate coursework support.

At the end of a piece, an hour changes very little about the content and can still be worth having, because the evaluation and reflection sections are typically the weakest part and the most mark-dense per word. What an hour cannot do at that stage is rescue a framing decision, which is the request that arrives most often and the one an honest tutor declines rather than taking the fee for. The same arithmetic applies to the sciences: once the data exists, the investigation is what it is, and a session can only improve how clearly it is analysed.

sections.heading: Parents at the table: three useful moves and two to avoid
paragraphs: Parents of Diploma students in Abu Dhabi occupy an awkward position: close enough to see the work falling behind and not qualified to intervene in it. There are, however, three things a parent can do that nobody else can, and they are worth more than any attempt at subject help.

The first is obtaining the school's internal deadline list and putting it somewhere visible. Not the board's dates, the school's own, which are earlier and which actually govern the year. Most students cannot produce this document on request, and most parents have never asked for it. The second is protecting time: agreeing the two-hour block, defending it against family logistics, and holding it even in weeks when nothing is due. The third is asking one specific question weekly, which is what did your supervisor say, rather than the general one, which is how is the essay going.

The two moves to avoid are both well intentioned. Do not get involved in the content of assessed work. Beyond reading for sense, where the school's policy allows it, a parent's hand in a draft is both an honesty risk and a competence risk, because a parent's instinct for what reads well is usually not what the criteria reward. And do not buy breadth in response to panic: four subjects of weekly tutoring commissioned in a bad week adds four commitments to a timetable that was already the problem.

One further thing that genuinely helps and costs nothing: ask the student to explain their coursework question to you, out loud, in two minutes. A student who can do that has a workable question. A student who cannot has the diagnosis in front of them, and so do you.

sections.heading: When the student is the problem, and when the plan is
paragraphs: Not every DP2 crisis is a tutoring problem, and buying tutoring for the wrong one is how families in this emirate spend heavily and change nothing. There are three distinguishable situations and they need different responses.

The first is a capability gap in one subject: the student works, understands most of it, and loses marks in identifiable places. This is what tutoring is for, and a single subject with weekly marked work is the right purchase.

The second is a plan problem. The student is capable, is working, and the week does not contain the work. Three Higher Levels, two languages, a service commitment, an Extended Essay and a university application cannot all be done well in the same fortnight, and the solution is triage with the Diploma coordinator rather than more hours. A tutor who will not say this is selling into the problem.

The third is a motivation or wellbeing problem, and it needs naming honestly because tutoring frequently gets bought as a substitute for addressing it. A student who has stopped working, is sleeping badly or has disengaged entirely will not be reached by a subject specialist, and the hours will be paid for and not used. That conversation belongs with the school's pastoral team and, where appropriate, with professional support. A tutor's honest contribution at that point is to say so and to stand down.

Telling the three apart is easier than it sounds and does not require a professional. Look at the marked work rather than the grades. Identifiable losses in named places point to the first. Work that is good where it exists and absent where it does not points to the second. Work that has simply stopped arriving points to the third. Spending on the wrong one of those three is the most common way a DP2 budget disappears without anything changing.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and the strand that runs alongside
paragraphs: One Abu Dhabi-specific feature of a Diploma student's home workload is routinely left out of tutoring conversations: the mandatory UAE subject strand that runs alongside the international curriculum.

Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. In Dubai, KHDA's published guidance on mandatory subjects goes into considerable detail: separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, with combined classes for the two groups prohibited because of different curriculum expectations and language of instruction, Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, and instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit with a recommended minimum of 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson. Abu Dhabi schools work within the same federal baseline under ADEK's licensing.

For a DP2 family this matters in a practical way. Those lessons occupy real timetable space and real homework time, and they do not appear in the Diploma's own 45 points. A student planning their week around six Diploma courses and the core has underestimated the week. A tutor planning a revision schedule without knowing which stream the school has placed the child in will schedule over it.

If support is needed for the strand itself, it is a separate specialism. A tutor must have taught the specific stream the school assigned, and for mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so material choices are constrained in a way they are not for IB subjects. Ask about the stream before anything else.

process.title: Get the school's deadline list first
process.description: Before any tutoring decision, obtain the school's own internal deadline list for coursework. It is earlier than the board's dates, it governs the DP2 year, and almost no family asks for it. Everything else on this page is planned backwards from that document.

process.title: Say which piece of work this is about
process.description: A scientific investigation at the design stage and a Theory of Knowledge essay in third draft need different people and different session lengths. Name the component, the subject, the level and the stage, and send what exists so far, however rough.

process.title: Buy the framing block early
process.description: Two or three sessions on the question, variable or article choice before any research begins. It is the highest-return purchase in the Diploma, it costs a fraction of a term of weekly hours, and it is the only thing that raises the achievable ceiling rather than the mark.

process.title: Use the trial on the actual draft
process.description: Forty-five minutes over live video, free, no card details. Put the real document on screen and watch what the tutor does with it. A supervisor names a criterion and asks a question that the student cannot immediately answer; a generalist comments on the writing style.

process.title: Keep the fortnightly rhythm with a written note
process.description: Sessions every two weeks so the student has to produce something in between, each one followed by a short written note naming the next criterion. Then a review against the school's feedback rather than against how the sessions felt.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line drawn on real situations
whyPoints.description: Twelve specific scenarios with the line marked on each, rather than a general statement about integrity. Most of them are more permissive than families expect, which matters as much as the prohibitions do, because a family that fears all help deprives a student of legitimate teaching.

whyPoints.title: A map of the year, not a description of it
whyPoints.description: The DP2 autumn and winter laid out period by period, with the school's internal deadlines separated from the board's and no unverified IB dates published. Nothing else in this market gives a family that shape in advance.

whyPoints.title: Supervision treated as its own skill
whyPoints.description: Questioning, criterion reading and deadline discipline are not the same as teaching timed paper technique, and tutors are matched accordingly. A superb examiner-style tutor can be the wrong person for an Extended Essay.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the home conditions
whyPoints.description: A desk, a door and a phone placement change Diploma output measurably and cost almost nothing. Saying so loses us billable hours and is the first thing a family should fix before spending on anything else.

whyPoints.title: Online because it suits the work
whyPoints.description: Supervision is reading, questioning and annotating a document the student controls. A shared screen does that better than two people at one laptop. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, and for coursework that is the right instrument rather than a limitation.

faqs.question: Do IB Diploma tutors travel to homes in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Independent tutors in the emirate do, and market rates reflect it: Bestimate's 2026 survey puts in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to AED 350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to AED 500, largely because a round trip across the city costs them more time than the lesson. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. UAE tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video, which for coursework supervision is the better instrument anyway.

faqs.question: Is online supervision good enough for an Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: For this particular job it is better than sitting side by side. Extended Essay supervision is reading a document, asking questions the student cannot immediately answer, and annotating against criteria. With screen sharing the student keeps control of their own file, the annotations are visible to both, and nothing is handed over in either direction, which is also the cleanest position on academic honesty. What matters far more than the medium is that the question was stress-tested before any research began.

faqs.question: How do we set up a workable study space for a Diploma student at home?
faqs.answer: Three things, none expensive. A desk with the screen at eye level and room for a printed copy of the assessment criteria beside it, because criterion-led writing requires seeing both at once. A door that closes, with a two-hour block agreed with the whole household rather than assumed by the student. And the phone in a different room for that bounded block with a stated end time. In Abu Dhabi villas the usual problem is not space but traffic through the room.

faqs.question: Where exactly does feedback on a coursework draft stop being allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes. Reading the student's own draft and saying which criterion it under-serves is legitimate and is the core of useful coursework support. What a tutor must not do is rewrite sentences into their own prose, edit the draft to completion, supply data the student did not collect or assemble a bibliography of unread sources. The practical test is whether the student could produce something comparable unaided afterwards. Your school's own academic-honesty policy governs, and the Diploma coordinator interprets it; check it if there is any doubt.

faqs.question: How many drafts of a coursework piece is a student allowed to have reviewed?
faqs.answer: The school's policy sets this, not a tutoring provider, and policies differ on how much formal feedback a supervisor may give and at what stage. Many schools allow one substantive round of written feedback from the supervisor, which is why a student should arrive at that round with their best effort rather than a sketch. A private tutor's feedback is governed by the same principle rather than the same count: it must be commentary on the student's own work, not production of it. Ask the coordinator for the written policy.

faqs.question: Should a parent sit in on Diploma tutoring sessions?
faqs.answer: Occasionally at the start, rarely after that. Sitting in on a first session tells you whether the tutor diagnoses or reassures, which is worth knowing. After that, a sixteen or seventeen-year-old generally works less honestly with a parent present, and the sessions where real weakness is admitted are the useful ones. A better arrangement is a short written note after each session naming what was worked on and what comes next, which gives you the information without changing the room.

faqs.question: What does the school supervisor do that a private tutor should not?
faqs.answer: Approve the research question, set and confirm the real deadline, give the formal feedback the school's policy permits, and approve method and ethics where data collection is involved. Those are authoritative acts and the board recognises them. A private tutor questions, translates criteria into plain language and gives commentary on drafts. The most useful thing a tutor often does is prepare the student for the supervisor meeting, because a student arriving with a written question and a plan gets far more out of fifteen minutes than one arriving empty handed.

faqs.question: Three deadlines land in the same fortnight. What should we drop?
faqs.answer: Nothing entirely, but something gets a floor rather than a ceiling. The triage logic is to protect whatever has the largest irreversible consequence: a coursework submission that cannot be resubmitted outranks a mock paper that will be repeated, and a framing decision outranks a polish. Then give the lowest-stakes item a deliberate minimum viable version rather than letting it quietly fail. One session spent building that plan hour by hour, with sleep treated as a constraint, is usually the best money spent in a DP2 winter.

faqs.question: How do we stop a phone from eating a two-hour study block?
faqs.answer: Bound it rather than ban it. A phone in the room with notifications on fragments attention even when untouched, which matters most for drafting and analysis, the two most interruption-sensitive Diploma tasks. The arrangement students actually accept is the device in another room for a fixed block with a stated end time and the phone returned at that time without negotiation. Presented as a rule about character it fails; presented as a two-hour arrangement with a clear finish it generally holds.

faqs.question: Is it worth hiring a tutor for Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the useful kind looks nothing like subject tutoring. Theory of Knowledge marks come from handling knowledge questions precisely, and the work is somebody asking a student why they believe a claim and refusing to accept the first answer. That is coachable. What a tutor may not do is write, rewrite or plan the 1,600-word essay to the point where the thinking is theirs rather than the student's. Buy it early in the drafting period; a tutor arriving a week before submission can do very little honestly.

faqs.question: What should a Diploma student be doing at home each week per subject?
faqs.answer: Realistically, set homework plus one piece of independent practice that gets marked by somebody, plus a protected coursework block that does not move. The last of those is the one that disappears, because coursework loses every competition with homework due tomorrow. Six courses, Theory of Knowledge reading and a service commitment is already a full week, which is why the coursework block has to be in the calendar before the week starts rather than found in the gaps that never appear.

faqs.question: Can a tutor check referencing before submission?
faqs.answer: A tutor can and should teach the referencing convention the subject requires and show the student how to check their own work against it. That is a transferable academic skill. What a tutor should not do is correct the references themselves or compile a bibliography, because that converts a student skill into somebody else's output and, if sources were not actually read, misrepresents the research. The student does the checking; the tutor teaches the method and then verifies that the student can apply it.

faqs.question: Does the Arabic requirement continue through the Diploma years?
faqs.answer: Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed curriculum, and must follow the Ministry's general regulations. Dubai's KHDA guidance is the most detailed published version, requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, setting the language of instruction for each stream and calculating instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit. Abu Dhabi schools sit within the same federal baseline under ADEK. For a DP2 family the practical point is that those lessons take real timetable and homework time outside the 45 points.

faqs.question: My child works better with somebody physically in the room. What do we do?
faqs.answer: Take that seriously and solve it separately from the subject question. Presence is a focus problem, and the cheaper fixes are a study hall at school, a library, a parent working quietly in the same room on their own task, or a scheduled block with a sibling studying alongside. Then buy the subject specialist online, where the choice is everyone who teaches your child's exact course rather than everyone who will drive to your road. Conflating the two usually produces a nearby generalist, which solves the focus problem and not the Chemistry one.

faqs.question: If we only buy one thing in the DP2 autumn, what should it be?
faqs.answer: Two or three sessions on the framing of whichever coursework piece is least settled, bought before any more data is collected or writing is done. A question narrowed until it is answerable, a variable that can be measured repeatedly, an article specific enough to analyse: each takes under an hour and each raises the maximum mark the piece can reach. Everything bought later improves execution within a ceiling that is already fixed. It is the cheapest high-leverage purchase in the programme and the least popular, because at that stage nothing feels wrong yet.

abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-home-tutor.closingHeading: The year is won at the dining table in October
abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-home-tutor.closingBody: Most of what decides a Diploma happens at home, unsupervised, in the autumn and winter of DP2. So get the school's internal deadline list and put it on a wall. Fix the desk, the door and the phone before spending anything on tuition. Buy two or three sessions on the framing of the least settled coursework piece before more work goes into it, and keep a fortnightly rhythm with a written note afterwards. Ask your child to explain their question out loud in two minutes; if they cannot, you have the diagnosis. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, the first forty-five minutes cost nothing, and the writing stays the student's throughout.

abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-online-tutor.heroSubtitle: Hiring an IB diploma online tutor in Abu Dhabi should leave a paper trail. After four weeks a family ought to be holding marked scripts with the same fault named each time, a draft history on the coursework piece, and a short written note per session saying what comes next. This page sets out what that evidence looks like week by week, how to read a marked script yourself, why component marks move before grades do, and when the evidence says stop paying. Sessions are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: Each profile states the Diploma course and level that tutor teaches. Ask any of them what their marking of a past paper looks like before you book: a tutor who marks to the published scheme and names the category of each lost mark produces evidence, and one who writes a grade at the top does not.

intro.heading: If nothing was written down, nothing can be reviewed
paragraphs: The hardest question in private tutoring is whether it is working, and most families in Abu Dhabi answer it with an impression. The sessions feel productive. The student seems more confident. The tutor is encouraging. None of that is evidence, and every one of those impressions is compatible with a grade that does not move. Evidence is a marked script from week one and a marked script from week five with the same fault named on both and a different number beside it.

This page is about that trail. What should exist after four weeks, what it looks like, how a parent reads it without being a subject teacher, and what it means when the component has moved and the grade has not. It is written for the Diploma specifically because the Diploma is unusually measurable: almost every subject produces timed scripts with component breakdowns, the coursework is marked against published criteria, and the school issues predicted grades from documented evidence. There is more to look at here than in almost any other school qualification.

The reason the format is online is partly practical and partly evidential. Screen sharing a marked script, annotating it live and saving the annotated version produces an artefact. A visiting tutor working on paper across a table produces a conversation. Both can be good teaching; only one leaves something a parent can read in four weeks and compare with week one. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, and this is one of the places where the format is an advantage rather than a constraint.

The second reason is subject access. An Abu Dhabi family choosing a tutor online chooses from everybody who teaches their child's exact course and level, rather than from those who can reach Al Reem or Masdar City by six. For Higher Level sciences, Computer Science and the smaller languages, that difference is the difference between a specialist and a willing generalist, and it shows up in the marking quality from the first week.

What follows is the week-by-week record, a method for reading a marked script that takes a parent twenty minutes to learn and requires no subject knowledge, the lag between component movement and grade movement, the draft history that should exist on a coursework piece, what mock papers are actually worth as a diagnostic and how little they are worth as a prediction, how schools build predicted grades and what that means for when to spend, and the circumstances in which the honest reading of the evidence is to stop paying. Market rates are included where they belong, attributed to the providers who published them, and none of them is an IB Gram price list or anything close to one.

abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Each IB programme produces a different kind of evidence, and the difference matters for anybody trying to judge whether support is working. The Diploma is the most measurable; the Primary Years Programme is the least.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six courses with externally marked papers, internally assessed work moderated by the board, and school-issued predicted grades. Every one of those produces documentation: component breakdowns, criterion scores, mock scripts and draft histories. A Diploma student is the easiest case in school education for evidence-led tutoring.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools sit the May session, so a DP2 student has mock scripts from the winter available as a baseline and roughly a term in which movement is still achievable. That makes the winter mocks the single most useful document an Abu Dhabi family can hand a tutor.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment across eight subject groups, each criterion scored 0 to 8 per task. There are no external papers for most students, so evidence of progress is the criterion score trend task by task rather than a percentage or a grade.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi families with a Middle Years student are often told their child is doing fine and shown an averaged grade. Asking for the criterion scores by task instead turns a vague reassurance into a diagnosis, and it is a request the school can meet.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma subject courses alongside a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. The Diploma components produce the same evidence as a full Diploma; the career-related elements are documented differently and vary by provider.
programmes.countryNote: Because the programme is rare in Abu Dhabi, a family supporting a student on it should agree with any tutor at the outset what evidence will be produced, since the usual past-paper trail does not exist for the career-related components.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-based units with no graded examinations. Evidence is qualitative: reading fluency, written output length and quality, and whether a child can sustain work across more than one sitting.
programmes.countryNote: Evidence-led support still applies at this stage in Abu Dhabi, just in a different currency. Timed reading, a word count on a piece of independent writing, and the number of minutes a child works before stopping are all measurable and all more useful than a comment on a report.

abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Below are the Diploma courses Abu Dhabi families most often ask about, with the specific evidence that shows support is working in each. Generic improvement is not evidence; these are.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Evidence is structured-question marks on topics previously failed, and extended responses where the student now states the principle before calculating. For the investigation, evidence is a trial run with repeat measurements before the real data collection, which is visible in the lab book.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Evidence is units carried through multi-step problems and uncertainty handled rather than ignored. On a marked script this shows as marks recovered in the working lines rather than in the final answer, which is the clearest single signal of real progress in this subject.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Evidence is command-term discipline: an answer to an explain question that contains a causal link, where the week-one script contained a fluent description. This change transfers across subjects, so it should be visible in History or Economics scripts too.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Evidence is method marks collected on questions still answered incorrectly, which proves working presentation has improved before accuracy has. At Higher Level, evidence also means an attempted extended investigative paper rather than an untouched one.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Evidence is correct choice of statistical test with its assumptions checked, and calculator output interpreted rather than copied. On the Exploration, evidence is a documented reason for the model chosen rather than a model presented without justification.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Evidence is diagrams labelled completely and evaluation paragraphs that reach a judgement. In the commentaries, evidence is an article chosen early with a note explaining why it can be analysed, which is a document that either exists or does not.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Evidence is source questions where provenance is used rather than described, and essays with a line of argument stated in the first paragraph. For the investigation, evidence is a source-evaluation section drafted before the narrative rather than after it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Evidence is tools applied to the specific case rather than defined, visible as marks in the application and evaluation bands of a marked script. A week-one script full of correct definitions scoring in the middle band is the classic starting profile here.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Evidence is a thesis present in the opening paragraph and techniques used as support rather than listed. For the individual oral, evidence is a recorded rehearsal marked against the criteria, which most students never produce before the real thing.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Evidence is documented design decisions and a test plan on the solution development work, and at Higher Level correct handling of abstract data structures in written answers. Code that runs is not evidence; documentation that explains why it is built that way is.

abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-online-tutor.regionsIntro: Online delivery removes travel from the equation and leaves scheduling and connection quality as the variables. These notes describe each area in terms of what actually affects an online session there.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer housing with good connectivity and a heavy co-curricular culture, which is the real constraint on slots rather than bandwidth. Families here do better with a later fixed slot than with a flexible early one.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: High-rise apartments where the practical issue is a quiet room rather than a connection. A student working at a dining table in a shared flat loses more to interruption than to any technical problem.

regions.name: Masdar City
regions.note: Small, well-connected community with an unusual concentration of Physics and Computer Science requests, both among the scarcest specialisms locally. Online delivery is what makes those matches possible at all here.

regions.name: Al Falah
regions.note: Villa community with long school commutes, so the usable window starts later than families expect. An 11am weekend session frequently produces better work than a 5pm weekday one.

regions.name: Al Rahba
regions.note: Northern community a long way from the island tutor pool, where in-home arrangements are rare and expensive. For a Diploma student here the online option is the practical route to a subject specialist.

regions.name: Al Bahia
regions.note: Coastal residential area with a mixed-curriculum population and a steady flow of students entering the Diploma from other systems. Baseline evidence is often thin for those students, which makes the first diagnostic session more important.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Dense Diploma population and the most contested evening slots in the emirate. A family that can take a weekend morning has a materially better choice of specialist than one that can only take 5pm.

regions.name: Al Shawamekh
regions.note: Outer mainland community with very little local tutoring supply of any kind. Evidence-led support is particularly valuable here because the alternative is usually no specialist contact at all.

schoolClusters.city: Yas Island, Al Raha and Al Bahia
schoolClusters.note: Students we support in this cluster come from schools with established Diploma cohorts and well-documented internal assessment. Winter mock scripts are usually available here, which makes a baseline straightforward to set.

schoolClusters.city: Al Reem Island, Masdar City and the mainland
schoolClusters.note: Newer and mixed-curriculum provision where students more often transfer into the Diploma mid-course. The first task with these families is usually constructing a baseline rather than reading an existing one.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City and the Al Raha corridor
schoolClusters.note: The emirate's densest IB continuum provision, with Group 4 sciences and Mathematics the dominant requests. Families here commonly have criterion data from Middle Years years as well, which makes trend reading easier.

abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-online-tutor.modesIntro: Three patterns of online Diploma support, distinguished by what evidence each one produces. All are one-to-one over live video; none involves a tutor travelling to a UAE address.

modes.title: Weekly marked-work cycle
modes.description: Questions set after each session, marked before the next one, with the category of each lost mark named rather than just a total. The artefact is a growing folder of annotated scripts in which the same fault appears and then stops appearing. This is the pattern that makes progress visible rather than felt.

Each lost mark categorised rather than simply totalled

modes.title: Coursework draft history
modes.description: Fortnightly supervision in which each version of the student's own document is kept, with feedback recorded against criteria. The draft history is both the evidence of progress and the honest audit trail showing the writing was the student's throughout, which matters if anybody ever asks.

modes.description: A diagnostic session that produces a written baseline, then a review session four weeks later against newly marked work. Suitable for families who want a decision rather than a term. Many conclude that one subject needs support rather than three, which is usually the cheapest outcome available.

sections.heading: The four-week record: what should exist, week by week
paragraphs: A month of weekly sessions is long enough to produce a documented change in one component and too short to produce a grade change in most subjects. Knowing that in advance stops a family from either giving up too early or continuing on faith for a year. The table below is what should be sitting in a folder at the end of four weeks.

The first session is a baseline, and it is the document everything else is measured against. It should name the category of each lost mark on a real script rather than describe the subject generally. A baseline that says the student needs to work on exam technique is useless; one that says eleven of the nineteen lost marks on this paper were command-term failures, four were unstated method and four were content gaps in two named topics is a measuring instrument.

Weeks two to four then work on the largest category, with questions set, marked and returned each week. The key artefact is not the teaching but the marking: the same fault named in week two, named again in week three, and then absent in week four. That sequence is what progress looks like on paper. A folder of scripts with totals and no categorisation cannot show it.

The written note after each session matters more than families assume, and it takes a tutor three minutes. It records what was worked on, what was set, and what the next target is. Four of those notes side by side are a narrative a parent can read without knowing any chemistry, and they make the four-week review a factual conversation rather than a negotiation about feelings.

sections.heading: How to read a marked Diploma script without being a subject teacher
paragraphs: A parent can learn to read a marked script in about twenty minutes, and it is the most useful twenty minutes available in this whole process. The trick is not to look at the marks lost but to sort them into categories, because the categories have completely different costs to fix.

There are five, and almost every lost mark in the Diploma belongs to one of them. A command-term failure, where the student knew the material and answered a different question from the one asked. An unstated method, where the thinking was right and nothing credit-worthy was written down. A presentation loss, where units, rounding or labelling cost marks that were earned. A timing loss, visible as blank or scrambled answers at the end of a paper. And a genuine content gap, where the student did not know the material.

Sorting a script this way takes a highlighter and no subject knowledge. Count how many lost marks fall into each category. Whichever category is largest is what the first month of tutoring should target, and that is a conversation a parent can have with a tutor on equal terms. It also immediately exposes the mismatch that wastes the most money: a student with eleven command-term failures and four content gaps being taught content for a term.

The table below gives the categories with how to spot each, how quickly each responds and what the evidence looks like when it has been fixed. The last column is the important one, because it tells you what to ask for at the four-week review.

sections.heading: Component marks move before grades do
paragraphs: This is the single most common source of disappointment in Diploma tutoring and it is entirely avoidable with one explanation at the start. A subject grade is a coarse instrument. It aggregates several components, each with its own weighting, and a grade boundary can sit anywhere. A student can improve substantially and stay on the same grade for a term.

What moves first is the component. A student whose structured-question marks rise by several marks has genuinely improved, and that improvement may not cross a boundary yet. If a family is watching only the reported grade, they will conclude that a month of work achieved nothing and stop at exactly the point where continuing would pay.

The practical answer is to agree at the outset which component is being targeted and to review that component rather than the grade. The tutor should state this in the baseline: we are working on structured-question marks in topics six and seven, and here is the current figure. Four weeks later there is a number to compare. Grade movement is then a consequence rather than a monthly expectation.

The table gives rough lags from component movement to visible grade change. They are planning estimates rather than promises, and they vary by subject, by how close the student started to a boundary and by how the school's reporting works. Nobody can promise a grade, and a provider who does is describing something no tutor controls.

sections.heading: What online delivery produces that a visiting tutor usually does not
paragraphs: This is not an argument that online teaching is better teaching. It is an argument that online teaching leaves a trail, and in a two-year qualification where a family is spending real money, the trail is worth having.

A screen-shared script can be annotated and the annotated version saved. A document worked on live keeps its revision history. Set work arrives and returns in writing, so there is a record of what was asked and what came back. Session notes are typed rather than remembered. None of this is impossible on paper across a table; all of it tends not to happen, because the natural medium of an in-home session is conversation and conversation leaves nothing behind.

The second thing the format produces is subject access. Market rates for specialist cover in the UAE run roughly AED 200 to AED 450 and above per Bestimate's 2026 survey, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and in-home rates sit at AED 180 to AED 350 or AED 200 to AED 500 from independent home tutors, largely because of travel. Removing travel does not just reduce cost; it widens the pool to everyone who teaches the course rather than everyone within a drive of Al Rahba. For Higher Level Physics or Computer Science in Abu Dhabi that is decisive.

What the format does not solve is focus for a student who needs somebody physically present to start working. That is a real limitation and it should be addressed directly rather than argued away: a study hall, a library, a parent working quietly in the same room on their own task. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, so a family for whom presence is the binding constraint should solve presence separately and buy the subject specialist online.
