sections.heading: Draft history: evidence of progress and of authorship
paragraphs: On a coursework piece, the draft history does two jobs at once and both matter. It shows whether the work is improving in a directed way, and it shows whose work it is. Keeping it costs nothing and a family should insist on it.

The progress job works like this. Version one is read and one criterion is named as the weakest. Version two addresses that criterion and a different one becomes the weakest. Version three addresses that. A student whose drafts move in that pattern is being supervised properly. A student whose draft three is a tidier version of draft one is receiving comments on style rather than feedback against criteria, and that is a different and much less valuable product.

The authorship job is the one nobody thinks about until it matters. Every piece of assessed work must be the student's own, and a dated sequence of the student's own drafts with a tutor's questions recorded alongside is the clearest possible demonstration that it was. A piece that appears fully formed with no history is harder to account for, even when it is entirely legitimate. Keeping the history is in the student's interest.

The boundary stays exactly where it always is. The tutor asks questions, reads the student's text, names the under-served criterion, explains in plain language what that criterion rewards and teaches referencing conventions. The tutor does not write, rewrite, edit to completion, supply data the student did not collect or build a bibliography of unread sources. Providers selling finished Internal Assessments operate in this market at prices around AED 3,750, and the malpractice finding from buying one lands on the student.

sections.heading: What a mock paper is actually worth
paragraphs: Mock examinations are the most useful and most misread document in a DP2 year. Their value is almost entirely diagnostic and almost not at all predictive, and families in Abu Dhabi routinely treat them the other way round.

As a diagnostic they are excellent. A full paper sat under time, marked to a scheme, produces exactly the data that the five categories in the earlier table need. It samples topics across the whole course, it exposes timing problems that short practice never reveals, and it generates a script that can be compared with another one in eight weeks. The winter mocks are the best baseline an Abu Dhabi DP2 family will ever hold, and they are free.

As a prediction they are weak, for a reason worth understanding: a mock is usually sat before the course is finished and before any consolidated revision. A student who has not yet been taught two topics will lose those marks regardless of ability. This is why a mock grade that is two below the target is often alarming and not meaningful, and why the useful question is which categories the lost marks fall into rather than what the grade was.

So the right use of a mock is to extract the categories, target the largest, and then design a second timed paper eight weeks later as the measuring instrument. Any tutor who looks at a mock script, names a grade and moves on has wasted the most informative document of the year. Ask for the categorisation instead.

sections.heading: Predicted grades and the evidence behind them
paragraphs: Predicted grades are produced by the school in DP2 for university applications, before any final paper is sat, and they are a professional judgement based on documented evidence. Understanding what that evidence is tells a family where tutoring can and cannot affect the outcome.

Schools generally build a prediction from internal assessments through DP1 and DP2, mock performance, coursework quality and the teacher's judgement of trajectory. All of that is work done before the prediction is issued, which means tutoring affects predictions only by changing that body of work. Support purchased after predictions have gone out can change the final result and cannot change the prediction.

This has a clear planning implication for Abu Dhabi families, and it is one of the strongest arguments for spending in DP1 rather than DP2. A student whose DP1 evidence is strong receives a prediction that opens options. A student whose DP1 evidence is weak may be predicted conservatively and then outperform it in May, which is a better outcome than the reverse but a worse set of university offers.

A tutor cannot negotiate a predicted grade and should never imply they can. The judgement belongs to the teachers who hold the evidence. What a tutor can legitimately do is help a student produce stronger evidence before the prediction is made, and help them understand what the school is looking at. If the prediction seems inconsistent with the evidence, that is a conversation with the Diploma coordinator, conducted with the marked work in hand.

sections.heading: When the evidence says stop
paragraphs: A page about evidence has to include the readings that mean stop paying, because a provider who never recommends ending an arrangement is not running an evidence-led service.

The clearest signal is a targeted component that has not moved after four to six weeks of properly marked work. That is not a reason to add hours. It means one of three things: the diagnosis was wrong and the largest category was misidentified, the brief is too broad to make progress on anything, or the student is not doing the work between sessions. Each has a different fix and none of them is a second weekly hour.

The second signal is a folder with nothing in it. Four weeks of sessions and no marked scripts, no written notes and no draft history is not an evidence problem, it is a service problem, and the honest conclusion is that the family cannot assess what they are buying. Ask once for the documentation. If it does not arrive, change tutor rather than continuing.

The third is the end of usefulness, which is a good outcome and rarely announced. A student who can read a command term, show working, complete a paper in time and frame their own coursework question does not need a weekly tutor any more. The honest tutor says so and offers an occasional check-in instead. Continuing a weekly arrangement past that point is comfortable for everybody and useful to nobody, and in the final fortnight before papers it is actively counterproductive: new material at that stage is a liability and the best use of the hour is sleep.
bullets: Targeted component flat after four to six weeks: re-diagnose, do not add hours
No marked scripts or notes after a month: change tutor, not frequency
Student not completing set work: the fix is not more sessions
Skills now independent: move to occasional check-ins
Final fortnight: consolidation only, nothing new

process.title: Send the winter mock, or the most recent full paper
process.description: A complete marked script with component marks is worth more than a term of reports. If a mock exists, send it; if not, send the most recent full assessment. For a Middle Years student send criterion scores task by task rather than an averaged grade.

process.title: Ask for a categorised baseline in writing
process.description: Not a plan for the subject but a count: how many lost marks were command-term failures, unstated method, presentation, timing or content. That document is the measuring instrument for everything that follows, and it should arrive after the first session.

process.title: Agree the component and the review date
process.description: Name the single component being targeted and fix a date four weeks ahead. Reviewing a grade monthly produces false disappointment, because grades lag components by weeks. Reviewing the component produces a number that either moved or did not.

process.title: Insist on the paper trail
process.description: Marked scripts with lost marks categorised, a three-line written note after each session, and for coursework a dated draft history. All of it is a by-product of working properly, so a tutor who finds it burdensome is telling you how they work.

process.title: Act on the four-week reading
process.description: If the component moved, continue. If it did not, re-diagnose rather than adding hours: the likely causes are a wrong baseline, too broad a brief, or work not being done between sessions. If the skills are now independent, move to occasional check-ins and stop paying weekly.

whyPoints.title: Progress stated as a number, not a feeling
whyPoints.description: The targeted component is named at the start and compared at four weeks. That makes a continuation decision factual, and it protects a family from both of the usual errors: stopping just as something starts working, and continuing for a year on reassurance.

whyPoints.title: Lost marks categorised, not totalled
whyPoints.description: A script marked with a total tells you how it went. A script with every lost mark sorted into command term, method, presentation, timing or content tells you what to do, and lets a parent judge the plan without knowing the subject.

whyPoints.title: The lag explained in advance
whyPoints.description: Component marks move before grades do, and saying so at the outset prevents the most common disappointment in Diploma tutoring. No grade is promised, because no tutor controls one.

whyPoints.title: A draft history that shows authorship
whyPoints.description: Dated versions of the student's own drafts with criterion feedback alongside demonstrate both improvement and whose work it is. That record protects the student, and it is a by-product of supervising properly rather than an administrative extra.

whyPoints.title: Clear about when to stop
whyPoints.description: A flat component after six weeks of marked work means re-diagnose, not buy more hours. Independent skills mean occasional check-ins rather than a weekly slot. Saying this costs billable hours and is what evidence-led actually means.

faqs.question: What should we have in writing after a month of online Diploma tutoring?
faqs.answer: A categorised baseline from the first session, marked scripts from each week with the category of every lost mark named, a three-line note after each session saying what was worked on and what comes next, and a short four-week comparison between the week-one script and a fresh attempt at a similar question. If coursework is in play, add a dated draft history. All of it is a by-product of working properly rather than extra administration, so its absence tells you something about how the sessions are being run.

faqs.question: How quickly should a Diploma grade actually move?
faqs.answer: Slower than the component does, which is the thing to understand before the first session. A grade aggregates several weighted components and a boundary can sit anywhere, so a student can improve genuinely and report the same grade for a term. Command-term fixes often show as a grade within four to eight weeks; content gaps take a full assessment cycle that samples the missing topics; coursework quality does not show until the piece is marked. Watch the targeted component monthly and let the grade follow.

faqs.question: What does proper marking of a past paper look like?
faqs.answer: Each lost mark attributed to a category rather than a total written at the top. On a good script you can see which marks went to answering a different question from the one asked, which to method that was never written down, which to units or rounding, which to running out of time, and which to genuinely not knowing the material. That is the document a tutoring plan is built from. Ask a prospective tutor to show you a sample of their marking, with the student's details removed, before you book.

faqs.question: How can we tell the tutoring is working rather than just pleasant?
faqs.answer: Compare two marked scripts on the same question type, four or five weeks apart, and look at whether the targeted category of lost marks has shrunk. Impressions are not evidence: a student can feel more confident, enjoy the sessions and lose the same marks. The useful test is whether a fault named in week two is still being named in week five. If the folder contains no marked work to compare, that is the first problem to solve, before any question about the teaching.

faqs.question: Can we see the tutor's notes after each session?
faqs.answer: You should, and three lines is enough: what was worked on, what was set, and what the next target is. Four of those side by side are a narrative a parent can read without knowing the subject, and they turn a four-week review into a factual conversation. What is not useful is a lengthy report written to look thorough. For a student over sixteen, a short factual note to the parent plus the marked work is the right balance between information and the student's own space.

faqs.question: How does marking a Diploma script work over video?
faqs.answer: The script is shared on screen, annotated live while the student explains their thinking, and the annotated version is saved. That sequence is more useful than it sounds, because hearing a student narrate their working separates a conceptual gap from a communication gap in seconds. The saved annotation is then comparable with the next one. It is the part of online delivery that most clearly produces something an in-home session usually does not, which is an artefact rather than a conversation.

faqs.question: What technology does an online Diploma session actually need?
faqs.answer: Less than families expect. A laptop with a working camera, a stable connection, and ideally a way to get the student's handwritten working onto the screen: a phone photograph of a page is sufficient. A graphics tablet helps in Mathematics and the sciences but is not necessary. What matters far more is the environment: a quiet room, a desk rather than a bed, the assessment criteria printed and to hand, and the phone in another room for the duration of the session.

faqs.question: Does the tutor keep a record of coursework draft versions?
faqs.answer: They should, and so should the student. A dated sequence of the student's own drafts with criterion feedback recorded alongside does two jobs: it shows whether the work is improving in a directed way, and it demonstrates whose work it is. A piece that appears fully formed with no history is harder to account for even when it is completely legitimate. Keeping the history is in the student's interest, costs nothing, and is a natural by-product of being supervised properly rather than edited.

faqs.question: How many timed papers should a DP2 student have sat by the winter?
faqs.answer: Enough that a full paper under time is familiar rather than novel, which in practice means several per examined subject rather than one. The school's mock window supplies some of them; the rest come from set work. The purpose is not practice for its own sake but the generation of comparable scripts: a paper sat in October and a paper sat in January, both marked the same way, is the clearest evidence a family will get. Short practice questions never reveal timing problems, which is why full papers matter.

faqs.question: What evidence does a school use to set a predicted grade?
faqs.answer: Typically internal assessments across DP1 and DP2, mock performance, coursework quality and the teacher's judgement of trajectory. Every one of those is produced before the prediction is issued, which is why support bought in DP1 affects predictions and support bought after they go out affects only the final result. A tutor cannot negotiate a prediction and should never imply they can. If a prediction looks inconsistent with the evidence, take the marked work to the Diploma coordinator and ask.

faqs.question: Our child says the sessions are going well but the marks have not moved. What now?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a diagnosis problem rather than an effort problem. Three causes account for almost all of these cases. The baseline identified the wrong largest category, so the work has been aimed at something that was not costing many marks. The brief is too broad, so nothing receives enough attention to shift. Or the work between sessions is not being done, which no amount of session time fixes. Ask for the marked scripts from the past four weeks and look at which category is still being named.

faqs.question: Is recording a session useful?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and less often than people assume. A recording of a worked solution that a student will revisit is genuinely useful; a recording of a whole session rarely gets watched. The better artefacts are the annotated script and the written note, because they are short and searchable. If recording is wanted, agree it explicitly with the student and the tutor first, be clear where the file is stored and who can see it, and remember that a session about a sixteen-year-old's weaknesses is a sensitive document.

faqs.question: Can the tutor speak to the school directly?
faqs.answer: Only with your consent and the school's agreement, and usually it is not necessary. The information that matters flows through documents rather than conversations: the school's internal deadline list, the marked assessments, the criterion feedback from a coursework supervisor. A tutor who has those does not need a meeting. Where a genuine conflict exists, for instance over a coursework question that the tutor thinks is unanswerable, the right route is the student and parent raising it with the coordinator, with the evidence in hand.

faqs.question: What does evidence look like for a Middle Years student with no exam marks?
faqs.answer: Criterion scores task by task, which the school can supply and which most parents never request. A Middle Years subject is assessed against four criteria scored 0 to 8, so a trend showing criterion C rising from 3 to 5 across three tasks is real evidence, while an averaged grade of 5 tells you nothing about what to work on. Ask for the criterion data, pick the lowest criterion, and make that the four-week target. It is the same method as the Diploma in a different currency.

faqs.question: When should we stop paying for tutoring altogether?
faqs.answer: When the student can do the things the tutoring was buying: read a command term and answer it, show method, complete a paper in time, frame their own coursework question and act on criterion feedback. At that point a weekly slot is comfortable and no longer useful, and an occasional check-in is the honest replacement. Stop also when a targeted component has not moved after six weeks of properly marked work, because the answer then is re-diagnosis rather than more hours. And in the final fortnight, stop adding anything new.

abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-online-tutor.closingHeading: Ask for the folder, then read it
abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-online-tutor.closingBody: Evidence-led tutoring is not a slogan; it is a folder. A categorised baseline, marked scripts where every lost mark is sorted rather than totalled, a three-line note after each session, and for coursework a dated draft history. With those, a parent in Abu Dhabi can judge a Diploma tutor without knowing any chemistry, and can tell the difference between a month that worked and a month that felt good. Agree which component is being targeted, fix a review date four weeks out, and act on what the comparison shows, including stopping. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time and the first forty-five minutes cost nothing.

abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-tutor.heroSubtitle: An IB diploma tutor in Abu Dhabi is hired for a structure, not a subject. The Diploma is six courses, three of them at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity, service, and the final number is assembled from parts that are marked in different places by different people. This page sets out what each part assesses, which marks are the school's and which the board's, where the losses concentrate, and what two years looks like counted backwards. Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-tutor.tutorsIntro: Profiles state the Diploma course and the level each tutor teaches. The level is the part to read: Higher Level courses carry an additional paper and a larger extended-response load, and a tutor who has only prepared Standard Level students will teach the content competently and leave the hardest paper untouched.

intro.heading: The final number is assembled, not earned in one place
paragraphs: Parents of Abu Dhabi Diploma students usually arrive at tutoring with a grade problem: a 4 in Chemistry that should be a 6, a Mathematics mark that fell between October and January. The useful reframing is that no Diploma grade is a single thing. Each subject grade from 1 to 7 is assembled from externally marked papers and from an Internal Assessment that the school marks and the board moderates. Six subject grades then sit alongside up to three bonus points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, and the total runs to a ceiling of 45.

That architecture decides where tutoring money does and does not work. Marks inside an externally marked paper respond to technique, timed practice and command-term discipline, and they can move fairly quickly. Marks inside an Internal Assessment respond almost entirely to decisions made at the planning stage, and once the data is collected and the framing is fixed, very little can be done. Bonus points from the core respond to a kind of thinking that cannot be taught in the final term at all. A family who understands which of those three they are dealing with spends a third of what a family who does not spends.

The second structural fact that matters is that the Diploma is a two-year single attempt. There is no module to resit in the spring of DP1 and no averaging across years. The work done in DP1 shows up as a predicted grade that goes to universities before any examination is sat, and the coursework drafted in DP1 is frequently submitted in DP2 with limited scope for revision. This is why the same amount of tutoring produces very different results depending on when it is bought, and it is the single most expensive thing Abu Dhabi families learn late.

Third, the Diploma punishes breadth badly handled. A student carrying three Higher Levels, two languages, Theory of Knowledge, a 4,000-word essay and a service commitment is not usually failing four subjects because of four content weaknesses. They are failing because the week does not contain the work. A good tutor says that out loud and recommends one subject and a conversation with the Diploma coordinator, rather than selling four sets of hours into a week that is already the cause of the problem.

What follows is the structure in detail: what each of the six groups assesses and where its marks leak, which components the school marks and which the board marks, the Internal Assessments group by group, the losses ranked by size, and the two years mapped backwards from the examination window. IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one online tuition into Abu Dhabi, matched by course and level; it does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, because a Diploma student needs the person who teaches their exact course rather than the person who can reach their road by six.
bullets: Each subject grade combines externally marked papers with a school-marked Internal Assessment
Technique marks move quickly; coursework marks are decided at the planning stage
Predicted grades go to universities before any paper is sat
Three Higher Levels plus the core is a timetable problem as often as a subject one
Ask your school's Diploma coordinator for the current points and failing conditions

abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-tutor.programmesIntro: The Diploma does not stand alone in an Abu Dhabi school. Most students reach it through the Middle Years Programme or from a British or American curriculum, and the preparation gap differs sharply by route. These are the programmes a Diploma tutor is most often asked about alongside it.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six courses drawn from six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity, service. Subject grades run 1 to 7, the core contributes up to three further points and the total ceiling is 45. Most components are externally marked; each subject also carries internally marked work that the board moderates.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts sit the May session, which places the coursework crunch in the winter months and the examination window in the spring term. The practical effect for a family here is that DP2 autumn is the last point at which a decision about Internal Assessment framing can still change an outcome.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each on a 0 to 8 scale, with interdisciplinary units and a Personal Project in the final year. There are no external papers for most students. The criterion habits built here are the ones the Diploma then assumes.
programmes.countryNote: Students arriving in DP1 from an Abu Dhabi Middle Years cohort usually handle criterion-referenced coursework comfortably and find the timed external papers unfamiliar. Students arriving from a British curriculum have the reverse profile. Knowing which one your child is saves a term of mis-aimed tutoring.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A combination of Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Grading mixes Diploma subject grades with the career-related component's own requirements rather than producing a 45-point total.
programmes.countryNote: Few Abu Dhabi schools run this route, so a student on it who needs support for a Diploma subject component is usually looking at the same specialist pool as a full Diploma student, while the reflective project needs somebody sourced online.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry with no graded examinations. Relevant to a Diploma conversation mainly because the habits it builds, particularly extended writing and independent research, are the ones the Extended Essay later demands.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi families with a Diploma student and a younger child often ask whether to start support early. For the younger child the honest answer is reading volume and writing stamina rather than subject tutoring, and it costs a fraction of a Diploma hour.

abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-tutor.subjectsIntro: Below are the Diploma courses Abu Dhabi families most often seek support for, with what each actually assesses and where its marks tend to leak. Group membership matters because every student takes one course from most groups, which constrains the choices available.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Group 1. Assessed through an individual oral built on a global issue, a guided analysis of an unseen text, and a comparative essay at both levels with an additional written assignment at Higher Level. Marks leak when students identify techniques without building an argument about meaning.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Group 2. An individual oral based on a stimulus, productive writing to a specified text type, and receptive papers. Abu Dhabi students frequently speak fluently and lose marks on register and text-type conventions, which is a short, well-defined fix.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Group 3. Source-based paper, thematic essays, and at Higher Level an additional regional-option paper. The Internal Assessment is a 2,200-word investigation with a distinct source-evaluation section. Narrative in place of argument is the dominant loss.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Group 3. Diagram accuracy, real-world application and, at Higher Level, additional quantitative demands. The Internal Assessment is a set of commentaries built on news articles, and they fail when written as summaries rather than as applied analysis.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Group 4. Multiple-choice, structured and extended-response papers plus a scientific investigation. Content volume is the enemy. Marks leak to command-term handling: a fluent description scores partially on a question that asked for an explanation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Group 4. Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the Higher Level marks, and the data booklet is both a resource and a trap for students who have not learned what it contains. The investigation's criterion scores are decided by the variable chosen in the first fortnight.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Group 4. Multi-step problems where units and unstated principles cost marks the student had earned, plus extended responses that reward naming the physics before the algebra. The scarcest Higher Level specialism in the Abu Dhabi market.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Group 5. Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency, with an additional extended investigative paper at Higher Level that needs its own preparation. The Exploration is marked against criteria rather than out of a hundred, which surprises students every year.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Group 5. Statistics, modelling and technology-assisted work, with calculator fluency genuinely assessable. Students from American middle schools in Abu Dhabi commonly meet the modelling vocabulary here for the first time.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Group 6. A comparative study, a process portfolio and an exhibition. Most of the available marks sit in the written and curatorial work, which strong studio practitioners routinely under-serve while producing excellent pieces.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition of three objects. Marks come from handling knowledge questions precisely. A tutor questions and gives feedback on the student's own thinking; writing any part of it is malpractice.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: An independent research essay of up to 4,000 words in a subject, supervised by a teacher at the school. Almost every weak Extended Essay is a well-executed answer to a question that was too broad to answer, which is why the early sessions matter most.

abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-tutor.regionsIntro: Diploma cohorts are not spread evenly across Abu Dhabi, and the shape of the local cohort affects what support a family can find nearby. These notes describe each area in terms of its Diploma population rather than its amenities.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: A concentrated Diploma population within a small geography, which means local tutors fill up quickly and families compete for the same evening slots. Higher Level sciences are the requests that go unfilled here most often.

regions.name: Hidd Al Saadiyat
regions.note: Low-density villa community whose students travel to schools elsewhere on the island. The long school day leaves a narrow usable window, and a fixed later slot is worth more here than flexibility.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Al Zeina and Al Muneera households with a dense Diploma cohort and heavy co-curricular commitments, which matters because creativity, activity, service competes directly with coursework weeks.

regions.name: Al Qurm
regions.note: Small residential pocket close to the island schools, where families often have two children in different programmes at once. Diploma and Middle Years support are frequently needed in the same week and should be sequenced rather than stacked.

regions.name: Al Nahyan
regions.note: Central district feeding several long-established schools, with a Diploma population that skews towards humanities and languages. Group 3 and Group 2 support is easier to find locally here than Group 4.

regions.name: Al Zahiyah
regions.note: Dense apartment living near the city centre with mixed-curriculum households. Students transferring into DP1 from other systems are more common here, which makes transition planning the dominant first conversation.

regions.name: Al Jubail Island
regions.note: New and still filling, with very few local tutors of any kind. For a Diploma student here the realistic choice is an online specialist or nobody, which makes the format decision straightforward.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: Established Diploma cohorts and the shortest travel times in the emirate, which makes it the one area where local in-home arrangements are logistically easy. Higher Level science scarcity still applies.

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat, Al Qurm and the island schools
schoolClusters.note: Students we support in this cluster come from schools offering the Diploma alongside other post-16 routes, so families here frequently ask for help comparing the Diploma with A Levels before DP1 rather than after it.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.note: The corridor with the emirate's densest IB continuum provision. Requests from these schools concentrate on Group 4 sciences, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, and Internal Assessment supervision in the DP2 autumn.

schoolClusters.note: Mixed-curriculum catchment with a steady flow of students entering the Diploma from British and Indian curriculum backgrounds. The dominant need is bridging a Year 11 to DP1 gap rather than remediation.

abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-tutor.modesIntro: Diploma support divides naturally into three jobs, and they need different patterns of contact. All three are delivered one-to-one over live video; none involves a tutor travelling to a UAE address.

modes.title: Weekly subject work with marking
modes.description: The standard pattern for an externally examined course: one session a week on a fixed slot, with past-paper questions set, marked and returned before the next session. This is where technique marks are recovered, and it only works if the marking happens, because the recovery comes from seeing the same fault named repeatedly.
bullets: One subject, one level, the same tutor each week
Questions marked between sessions with the fault named each time
Timed conditions introduced early rather than in the final term
Specialist matched to the course, not to the subject name

modes.title: Coursework supervision cycles
modes.description: Fortnightly ninety-minute sessions around an Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay or the Theory of Knowledge essay, timed to the school's own deadlines. The tutor questions the plan, reads the student's own draft and names the criterion being under-served. The writing stays the student's throughout, without exception.
bullets: Research question narrowed before any data is collected
Criterion-level feedback on the student's own draft
School supervisor deadlines mapped backwards
No writing, rewriting, editing to completion or supplied data

modes.title: Diagnostic and transition sessions
modes.description: One-off or short-run sessions for a specific decision: whether a student should move a subject between levels, how to close a Year 11 to DP1 gap, which of four struggling subjects to support, or what the realistic ceiling is by May. The output is a written conclusion rather than a term of hours.

Useful before committing to a term of weekly sessions

sections.heading: The six groups and the core, and what each one actually assesses
paragraphs: A Diploma student takes one course from each of five groups and a sixth from either the arts group or a second course from one of the others. Three are taken at Higher Level and three at Standard Level. Every group has a distinctive assessment shape, and knowing the shape tells you what a tutor should be doing in the hour.

The language groups are oral-heavy in a way parents consistently underestimate. Both Group 1 and Group 2 include an individual oral assessment that is recorded and marked, and it is the component students practise least because it does not look like revision. For an Abu Dhabi student who speaks a language fluently at home, the Group 2 oral is frequently the easiest set of marks on their whole timetable and the ones they prepare for last.

The sciences and mathematics carry an additional Higher Level paper and, in the sciences, a scientific investigation. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level carries an extended investigative paper that requires separate practice. The arts group replaces timed papers with portfolio and exhibition work, which means the deadline discipline matters more than examination technique.

The core sits outside all of it. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together contribute up to three additional points, and creativity, activity, service is a requirement rather than a graded component. Because the core points are capped and the subject grades are not, families sometimes dismiss the core; that is a mistake when a student is near a university offer boundary, where two points decide the outcome.

sections.heading: Who marks what, and why that changes how you buy tutoring
paragraphs: A Diploma grade is produced by two different machines and a parent should know which one is affecting their child. Externally marked components are sent away and marked by examiners against a published scheme the student never sees. Internally marked components are marked by the student's own teacher at school and then moderated by the board, which can move the whole cohort's marks up or down.

The distinction has a direct consequence for tutoring. For externally marked work, the tutor's job is to make the student's response match what a scheme rewards: name the command term, state the principle, show the working, answer only what was asked. This is teachable, it is measurable through marked practice, and progress shows up within a few weeks.

For internally marked work, the tutor's job is almost entirely preventative. Once the investigation has been run, the commentary written or the portfolio assembled, the criterion scores are largely determined. A tutor arriving in month four can improve the presentation of a piece whose framing caps it in the middle band, and that is the most common disappointment Abu Dhabi families report about coursework support.

Moderation is the piece nobody explains to parents. Because internally marked components are moderated, a school's marks can be adjusted, which means the mark your child saw in school is not necessarily the mark that counts. Nobody can predict the adjustment, and any tutor who claims to know how moderation will fall is inventing it.

sections.heading: The Internal Assessments, group by group
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject has internally assessed work and no two are the same, which is why generic coursework help is close to useless. The table sets out what each actually is, because the single largest preventable loss in the whole Diploma is a student discovering in February what their Internal Assessment was supposed to be.

There is a pattern worth naming across all of them. In every subject, the mark is substantially decided by a choice made before the work begins: a variable that can be measured repeatedly, a research question narrow enough to answer, a news article recent and specific enough to analyse, an artwork comparison with genuine common ground. Execution matters, but execution cannot rescue a bad choice.

The second pattern is that students consistently under-serve the reflective and evaluative sections. In the sciences that is the evaluation of method and sources of error. In History it is the source-evaluation section. In the arts it is the written commentary. These sections are where the easiest available marks sit and they are written last, in a hurry, after the interesting part is finished.

A tutor working on coursework properly spends their early hours on the choice and their later hours on the evaluative sections, and reads the student's own drafts in between. They do not write, rewrite, edit to completion, supply data the student did not collect or produce a bibliography the student did not read. That boundary is absolute and the consequence of crossing it falls on the student.

sections.heading: Where Diploma marks actually leak, in order of size
paragraphs: If the losses were ranked by how many marks they cost across a whole cohort, the order would surprise most parents. Content ignorance is not at the top. The largest pool of recoverable marks in the Diploma is answering a different question from the one asked, and it belongs to students who know the material well.

Second comes working presentation in the quantitative subjects: units omitted, answers unrounded or over-rounded, method unstated so no credit can be given for an approach that was correct. These are marks the student earned and did not collect, and they take two or three sessions to fix permanently.

Third is coursework framing, which is not recoverable at all once the window closes. Fourth is timing: students who can answer every question but not within the paper's time, which is a strategy problem rather than a knowledge problem and responds to practice under real conditions rather than to more teaching. Content gaps come fifth, and they are the most expensive to fix because the syllabus is large and the work is slow.

The ranking is also a spending order. Fix the question-reading, then the presentation, then protect the coursework, then practise against the clock, and only then buy content coverage. Abu Dhabi families who buy in that order routinely spend a fraction of what families who start with a general monthly package across three subjects spend, and move further. The order holds across subjects too, which is why one tutor working on question-reading in Biology often lifts History and Economics without being paid for either.

sections.heading: Two Diploma years counted backwards
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market publishes a calendar. It is the most useful thing a Diploma family can be given, because almost every expensive mistake in the programme is a timing mistake rather than an ability one. The table below runs the two years backwards from the examination window, with the caveat that matters most: the dates belong to your school and to the board, not to a tutoring site.

On dates specifically. Abu Dhabi schools sit the May session. Specific IB session, upload and results dates in this project have not been confirmed from the IB itself, so none are published here; confirm every one with your school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org before you plan around it. For comparison, the other boards do publish, and their pattern shows why entry deadlines sit months before papers: Cambridge's March 2027 series has an examination period of 3 February to 4 March 2027 with final entries due 27 November 2026, and Pearson's International GCSE November 2026 final timetable runs to 19 November 2026.

The internal deadlines are the ones that actually govern a DP2 year, and they are set by your school rather than by the board. A school will typically want a scientific investigation drafted well before the board's submission window, because the teacher has to mark it and the department has to internally standardise. Ask for that list in the first week of DP1 and put it on a wall.

The habit that saves the most money is simple: identify the two months in which three deadlines collide, and buy tutoring in the two months before them rather than during them. For most Abu Dhabi Diploma students that collision point is the DP2 winter, which is also when every other family in the emirate is trying to book the same specialists.

sections.heading: Higher Level choices and what universities actually read
paragraphs: The three Higher Level choices are the most consequential decisions in the Diploma and they are usually made at sixteen with incomplete information. They determine the workload for two years, the predicted grades that go to universities, and in several fields whether an application is eligible at all.

The pattern worth understanding is that prerequisites are usually expressed as Higher Level subjects rather than as total points. Engineering and the physical sciences generally expect Mathematics and Physics at Higher Level; medicine generally expects Chemistry and a second science; economics degrees at many universities expect Mathematics, and are increasingly specific about which mathematics route. That last point is the one that catches Abu Dhabi families: the choice between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation is made in Year 11 and can quietly close doors in Year 13.

Check the requirement on the university's own admissions page rather than taking a tutor's word for it, including for UAE institutions, and check it for the specific programme rather than the faculty. Requirements change between admission cycles and between campuses of the same institution. Where a student intends to study in the UAE, the Ministry of Education equivalency process also applies, and it is described on our Abu Dhabi certified tutor page in detail.

Where the Higher Level choice turns out to be wrong, a change is sometimes possible early in DP1 and becomes progressively harder. The conversation is with the Diploma coordinator rather than with a tutor, and it should happen the moment the mismatch is clear rather than after a term of paid support trying to make an unsuitable choice work.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the boundary that does not move
paragraphs: Every piece of assessed work in the Diploma must be the student's own. This is not a policy preference; it is the condition on which the qualification is awarded, and a finding of malpractice can cost a student the entire diploma rather than one subject grade. A parent buying coursework support in Abu Dhabi should know exactly where the line sits, because several providers in this market cross it for a fee.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial. Teach the content. Question a research plan until the student can explain why it is answerable. Explain in plain language what a criterion rewards and what a command term demands. Read the student's own draft and say which criterion it under-serves and why. Model the approach to a different question. Build a timetable backwards from the school's deadlines. Teach referencing conventions and how to check them.

What a tutor may not do is narrow and absolute. Write any part of the work. Rewrite the student's sentences into their own prose. Edit a draft to completion. Supply data the student did not collect, or a bibliography of sources the student has not read. Hand over a model answer so close to the task that copying is the obvious next step. Services advertising completed Internal Assessments operate in this market at prices around AED 3,750, and buying one puts the student's name on the malpractice finding, not the seller's.

There is a related line on materials. Nobody should be sending you folders of board syllabus documents, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those are the boards' published material, your child's school has legitimate access to them, and a tutor distributing them is telling you something about how they operate.
bullets: Permitted: teaching, questioning, criterion-level feedback on the student's own draft
Permitted: deadline mapping and teaching referencing conventions properly
Prohibited: writing, rewriting, editing to completion or supplying data
Prohibited: a model answer close enough that copying is the next step
Reference board documents by link; do not accept them as files

sections.heading: When DP1 has gone badly, and what the autumn of DP2 is for
paragraphs: The most common moment an Abu Dhabi family reaches for a Diploma tutor is the start of DP2, after a DP1 report that was worse than expected. It is a good moment to act and a bad moment to panic, and the difference between those two is what gets bought in the next fortnight.

The first step is an honest read of the evidence rather than the grades. Pull every marked paper from DP1 and look for the pattern. If the same fault appears across three subjects, one tutor can teach it transferably and the other two subjects will improve without being paid for. If one subject is genuinely behind on content while the others are fine, that is a single-subject purchase. If everything is behind and nothing is specifically wrong, the problem is the week and the conversation is with the Diploma coordinator about load.

The second step is to protect the coursework, because the DP2 autumn is the last window in which framing decisions can still be changed. Two ninety-minute sessions on an investigation design or an Extended Essay question, bought in September, are worth more than a term of weekly hours bought in February. This is the single highest-return purchase in the entire programme and almost nobody makes it.

The third step is to resist the instinct to buy breadth. A family that commissions four subjects of weekly tutoring in September has added four commitments to a week that was already overloaded, and the usual result is four sets of missed homework and a worse winter. One subject, one coursework block, and a review against marked evidence at four weeks is a plan. Four subjects is a reaction.

process.title: Bring the DP1 evidence, not the report
process.description: Marked papers with component breakdowns, the coursework drafts as they stand, and the school's internal deadline list. A Diploma diagnosis is made from marked scripts; a report card averages away the information that would tell a tutor what to do first.

process.title: Separate the three jobs
process.description: Technique recovery on externally marked papers, supervision on internally assessed work, and the honest question of whether the week contains the work. These need different patterns and different amounts of time, and treating them as one request is how families end up paying for the wrong one.

process.title: Match by course and level
process.description: Chemistry Higher Level, not Chemistry. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, not maths. You are told before anything is agreed whether a specialist for that exact course and level is free, and if they are not, what the realistic alternatives are.

process.title: Use the trial on the hardest piece of evidence
process.description: Forty-five minutes over live video, free, no card details. Put the worst marked paper or the weakest coursework draft in front of the tutor and watch what they do. A specialist names a criterion or a command term within ten minutes; a generalist talks about the subject.

process.title: Review at four weeks against new marks
process.description: Not against how sessions felt. Compare newly marked work on the specific component that was targeted. If it has moved, keep going. If it has not, change the tutor or narrow the brief rather than adding a second weekly hour.

whyPoints.title: Built on the assessment structure
whyPoints.description: This page is organised by what the Diploma actually assesses, group by group, and by who marks each component. That distinction determines what tutoring can and cannot change, and almost no competitor page in this market makes it at all.

whyPoints.title: A calendar, counted backwards
whyPoints.description: Most expensive Diploma mistakes are timing mistakes. The milestone table exists so a family can see which decisions are cheap now and impossible later, with the school's internal deadlines separated from the board's.

whyPoints.title: Honest about unverified dates
whyPoints.description: Specific IB session and results dates are not published here because they have not been confirmed from the IB directly. Cambridge and Pearson dates that are sourced are cited with their framing. Confirm every IB date with your Diploma coordinator.

whyPoints.title: A stated coursework boundary
whyPoints.description: Teaching, questioning and criterion-level feedback on the student's own draft; never writing, rewriting or supplying data. The line is published because several providers in this market sell the other side of it and the consequence lands on the student.

whyPoints.title: Specialist by course and level
whyPoints.description: An Abu Dhabi family matched online chooses from everyone who teaches their child's exact course, not from those who can reach their road by six. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, and for a Higher Level science that is an advantage rather than a limitation.

faqs.question: What does an IB diploma tutor in Abu Dhabi do that the school teacher cannot?
faqs.answer: Work from one student's marked scripts rather than from a scheme of work for thirty. A school teacher has to cover the syllabus for the whole class at a pace set by the department; a tutor can decide that two topics will be abandoned because the marks are not there, and spend the time on the command-term fault costing three marks a question. The best Diploma tutoring is a triage decision followed by repeated marking, and that is a service a classroom cannot provide to one student.

faqs.question: How is the Diploma total of 45 points actually put together?
faqs.answer: Six subject grades of 1 to 7 give a maximum of 42, and Theory of Knowledge together with the Extended Essay contribute up to three further points, for a ceiling of 45. Subject grades combine externally marked papers with internally assessed work that the school marks and the board moderates. There are also conditions beyond the total that must be met for the diploma to be awarded, and the current list belongs to your school's Diploma coordinator rather than to a tutoring website. Ask them for it in writing at the start of DP1.

faqs.question: Can Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay really change the final total?
faqs.answer: Yes, by up to three points, and those points matter most exactly where families pay least attention to them: at a university offer boundary, where the difference between 34 and 36 decides an outcome. The core is also the part that cannot be rescued late, because the Extended Essay question is set in DP1 and the thinking the Theory of Knowledge essay rewards is not something a term of tutoring in the spring produces. Treat the core as an early investment rather than a late one.

faqs.question: Which Diploma components does the school mark and which does the board mark?
faqs.answer: Timed written papers, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Extended Essay are externally marked. Scientific investigations, written coursework in the humanities, individual oral assessments and arts portfolios are marked by the school and then moderated by the board, which can adjust a cohort's marks. That distinction is the one that should shape your spending: externally marked components respond to technique practice right up to the papers, while internally assessed work is largely decided when it is designed.

faqs.question: How much does the Internal Assessment count towards a subject grade?
faqs.answer: Enough to decide a grade boundary in most subjects, which is why it deserves more attention than it gets. The exact weighting differs by subject and level and is published in each subject guide, which your child's school holds; ask the teacher for the figure for their specific course rather than taking a number from a tutoring site. What is consistent across subjects is that the mark is substantially determined by the design decision made at the start, not by the quality of the write-up at the end.

faqs.question: When should a DP1 student start the Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Earlier than the school's deadline implies and later than panic suggests. The genuinely useful early work is narrowing the question or the variable until it can be investigated properly, and that can happen as soon as the topic is taught. In the sciences a trial run before the real data collection is the single most valuable hour in the whole process, because it reveals whether the chosen variable actually produces measurable results. Students who do that in DP1 rarely need expensive coursework support in DP2.

faqs.question: Does the choice between Mathematics Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation matter later?
faqs.answer: It can close doors, which is why it should not be made purely on which looks easier. Analysis and Approaches is proof, calculus and algebraic fluency; Applications and Interpretation is statistics, modelling and technology-assisted work. Several engineering, physics, economics and computer science programmes specify the route they expect, and the specification varies by institution and by admission cycle. Check the requirement on the university's own admissions page for the specific programme, and do it in Year 11 while the choice is still open.

faqs.question: Can a student move a subject from Higher Level to Standard Level partway through?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the window narrows as the two years progress. It is an administrative decision made by the school rather than by a tutor, and it becomes considerably harder once final entries for the examination session are made. If the mismatch is clear, raise it with the Diploma coordinator immediately rather than spending a term of paid tutoring trying to make an unsuitable level work. A tutor can tell you honestly whether the gap is closeable; the school decides whether the change is possible.

faqs.question: What are the most common Internal Assessment mistakes UAE students make?
faqs.answer: Four recur constantly. A research question or variable too broad to investigate within the limits. A design that cannot produce measurable, repeatable results, discovered only after the data is collected. An evaluation section written last and thinly, when it holds some of the most accessible marks. And a late start, which converts every other problem into an unfixable one. All four are prevented by two early sessions on the plan and none of them is fixed by a term of weekly hours in the spring.

faqs.question: How do predicted grades work, and can tutoring change them?
faqs.answer: Predicted grades are the school's professional judgement of what a student will achieve, issued in DP2 for university applications before any final paper is sat. They are based on DP1 evidence: marked assessments, mock papers and coursework quality. Tutoring can change them, but only by changing that evidence, which means the work has to happen in DP1 rather than after the predictions are issued. A tutor cannot negotiate a prediction and should never suggest they can; the judgement belongs to the teachers who have the evidence.

faqs.question: Is the Diploma a better route than A Levels for an Abu Dhabi student?
faqs.answer: It depends on the student rather than on the qualification. The Diploma keeps six subjects, two languages and a research requirement going for two years, which suits a broad student with good time management and punishes a narrow one. A Levels allow depth in three or four subjects and suit a student who already knows their direction. Both are recognised by UAE and overseas universities, and both require the Ministry of Education equivalency process if the certificate will be used here. Ask the school which cohort your child resembles.

faqs.question: How big is the jump from IGCSE or Middle Years into DP1?
faqs.answer: The content jump is smaller than the independence jump. Most students cope with the material and struggle with the volume of self-directed work: an Extended Essay, an Internal Assessment in every subject, Theory of Knowledge and a service commitment all running alongside six courses. Students from a Middle Years background usually find the coursework familiar and the timed papers strange; students from IGCSE find the reverse. Identifying which profile your child has in the first term is worth more than any amount of content tutoring.

faqs.question: What if my child's school has no specialist teacher for a Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: It happens in this emirate, particularly in Higher Level Physics, Computer Science and the smaller languages, and it is a legitimate reason to buy external support rather than a reflection on the school. The honest approach is to raise it with the Diploma coordinator first, because the school may have a plan you do not know about. If external support is needed, specify the course and level precisely, expect a wait for the scarcer specialisms, and start looking a term before you think you need to.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with creativity, activity, service?
faqs.answer: Only in a limited and honest way. Creativity, activity, service is a requirement rather than a graded component, and its value is in the student's own initiative and reflection. A tutor can help a student plan a realistic schedule so that it does not collide with coursework weeks, and can discuss what reflective writing looks like. Nobody should be writing reflections, inventing activities or producing a service record, and a provider offering to tidy up a portfolio has misunderstood what the requirement is for.

faqs.question: Do Abu Dhabi students sit the May session or the November one?
faqs.answer: Abu Dhabi schools follow the northern academic year and their candidates sit the May session. A November session exists and is used by schools on a southern-hemisphere calendar and occasionally by individual retake candidates. This page deliberately publishes no specific IB session or results dates, because they have not been confirmed from the IB directly for this project; confirm them with your school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org. What you can plan around is the shape: coursework deadlines in the DP2 winter, papers in the spring.

abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-tutor.closingHeading: Know which machine you are dealing with
abu-dhabi/ib-diploma-tutor.closingBody: The useful question about a Diploma grade is not whether it can improve but which part of it is movable. Technique marks on externally examined papers respond to weekly marked practice, and they move fairly quickly. Coursework marks are decided when the work is designed, so protect those decisions early and expect little from late help. Core points come from thinking built over two years. Bring the marked scripts and the deadline list, match by course and level, and review at four weeks against new marks rather than against how the sessions felt. Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the first forty-five minutes cost nothing.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-arabic-a-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work on Diploma Arabic A at Standard and Higher Level, across both the Literature and the Language and Literature route. Each session produces a marked piece of work, so the evidence of progress arrives with the lesson rather than at the end of term.

intro.heading: Start with the marked script, not the grade
paragraphs: An Arabic A grade on an Abu Dhabi school report tells you almost nothing about what to fix. A 4 can come from a student who analyses beautifully and writes shapeless essays, from a student who organises an argument perfectly and never leaves the plot summary, or from a bilingual student whose spoken Arabic is excellent and whose formal written register collapses the moment the task becomes a comparative essay. Three different problems, one number. The first thing a useful tutor does is ask for the actual script and read the examiner's marks.

Arabic A is assessed against four criteria, each with its own mark allocation, and almost every Diploma Arabic A student is losing marks in one or two of them rather than across the board. Criterion A covers understanding and interpretation. Criterion B covers analysis and evaluation. Criterion C covers focus and organisation. Criterion D covers language. On Paper 1 each is worth 5 marks out of 20. On Paper 2, knowledge and understanding and analysis are worth 10 each and organisation and language 5 each, out of 30. On the individual oral, all four carry 10 marks apiece, out of 40. Those numbers are the diagnostic. A student stuck on 11 out of 20 with 4 for understanding and 1 for analysis needs a completely different term's work from one scoring 2 and 4 the other way round.

This page is built around evidence rather than reassurance. It sets out what each Arabic A component is worth, what a marked script looks like once you know which letter maps to which skill, how an HL essay should accumulate a visible draft history, and what a parent in Abu Dhabi should expect to see change in the first eight weeks. It also covers the mandatory Arabic stream that ADEK-regulated schools run alongside the Diploma, which is a separate subject with separate expectations and is frequently confused with Arabic A at parents' evening.

On delivery, we are direct: IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in Abu Dhabi. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Arabic A support for an Abu Dhabi family is one-to-one live video, screen-shared with the student's own text in front of both of them, annotated live and saved. For this subject that is an advantage rather than a compromise. The pool of people who can teach Arabic A Literature at Higher Level, who know how a comparative essay on two Arabic literary works is marked, is small in any single emirate. Choosing by expertise rather than by driving distance from Al Mushrif is the difference between a tutor who can read your child's script and one who can only practise conversation.

Rates below are market figures from published UAE sources, given so you can judge any quote you receive, including ours. They are not our price list. Every figure carries the band it came from. Where a date is unverified, the page says so instead of inventing one.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-arabic-a-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Arabic A sits at the top of a language pathway that starts years earlier. Abu Dhabi families usually arrive at the Diploma course having already made two or three decisions about Arabic in PYP and MYP, and those decisions are what determine whether Arabic A is comfortable or brutal in DP1.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: In the PYP, Arabic is a language of instruction and inquiry rather than an examined subject. Schools stream children by whether Arabic is a first or an additional language, and the stream a child is placed in at Year 2 often follows them for a decade. Transdisciplinary units mean Arabic reading is practised inside science and social-studies inquiry rather than in isolated grammar drills, which builds comprehension but can leave formal writing thin.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools regulated by ADEK run Arabic to the Ministry of Education requirement from the first year of primary, in separate groups for Arab and non-Arab children. For an Arabic-speaking family in Al Bateen or Al Mushrif, the practical question in PYP is whether the child is reading unvocalised text independently by Year 5, because that single skill decides whether Arabic A is realistic later.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Language and Literature is where Arabic A is won or lost. The MYP criteria — analysing, organising, producing text, using language — are the direct ancestors of the Diploma's four criteria, and a student who finishes MYP5 with a 5 in Arabic Language and Literature is usually comfortable in DP Arabic A. Students who sat MYP Language Acquisition Arabic instead are being asked to jump two courses in one summer.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi IB schools offer both MYP Language and Literature Arabic and MYP Language Acquisition Arabic, and the choice made in Year 9 narrows the Diploma options sharply. Families in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor often discover in Year 11 that the Arabic stream their child has been in for three years does not lead where they assumed it did.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Arabic A is a Group 1 studies in language and literature course, available as Literature or as Language and Literature, each at SL and HL. It is a literary-analysis qualification sat in Arabic, not a language course. Students read set works, write guided analyses of unseen passages, compare works in an essay under timed conditions, and deliver a 15-minute individual oral built around a global issue.
programmes.countryNote: Taking Arabic A alongside an English A course is the usual route to the bilingual diploma for Abu Dhabi students, which requires grade 3 or above in both Language A courses. Confirm the exact award conditions with your school's IB coordinator before building a subject choice around it, because the regulations are set by the IB and reviewed periodically.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme includes a language development component rather than a full Language A course. Arabic appears there as a developing competency with a portfolio, which suits a student heading into a UAE workplace but does not carry the literary analysis load of Arabic A. A handful of UAE schools run it alongside the Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: CP is uncommon in Abu Dhabi compared with the Diploma, and a student moving from CP language development into Arabic A mid-course is taking on an unfamiliar assessment model. Where that transfer is being considered, the honest answer is usually a term of catch-up on literary terminology in Arabic before the set works begin.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-arabic-a-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Arabic A students in Abu Dhabi rarely need one tutor. The pattern we see is Arabic A plus one science or maths course where the English-language technical register is the real obstacle. These are the Diploma subjects most often requested alongside it.

subjects.name: Arabic A: Literature
subjects.description: Entirely literary: set works read in Arabic, a guided analysis of an unseen literary passage in Paper 1, and a comparative essay in Paper 2. At HL it adds the 1,200-1,500 word HL essay on one work studied. Marks are lost on criterion B, analysis and evaluation, where students describe what a text says instead of how it works.

subjects.name: Arabic A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Half literary works, half non-literary texts — advertisements, speeches, opinion columns, social-media posts in Arabic. Paper 1 is a guided analysis of an unseen non-literary text, two of them at HL. Students who read literature well often struggle here because analysing a newspaper column needs a different vocabulary of techniques.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: The Group 2 language acquisition course, for students with some prior Arabic. Frequently confused with Arabic A at subject-choice evenings. A heritage speaker misplaced in Arabic B tends to score well without learning much; a student placed in Arabic A too early loses marks on written register for two years.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The usual partner course for Arabic A students pursuing the bilingual diploma. The criteria are identical in structure, which means analytical skills transfer directly between the two. A tutor working on Arabic A criterion B can often fix the same habit in the English A essays at no extra cost in hours.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most Abu Dhabi universities and engineering faculties expect. Paper 3 at HL is a 55-minute extended-response paper worth 20% of the grade and is where HL candidates concede the most. Arabic-first students sometimes lose marks decoding English command terms rather than on the mathematics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling led, with a graphical-calculator requirement throughout. Suits students heading into business, social science or design. The exploration is 20% of the grade at both levels and is marked on the same criterion-letter model that Arabic A uses, so the planning habits transfer.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Heavy on precise terminology and command-term discipline. Students who learn biology in English while thinking in Arabic typically lose marks on 'explain' and 'evaluate' questions where the content is known but the answer structure is not. The internal assessment is 20% of the final grade.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic chemistry and energetics are the two topics Abu Dhabi students ask for most. Paper 2 extended response rewards method shown step by step. The scientific investigation is internally assessed and externally moderated, and the common failure is an insufficiently narrow research question.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries marks that students regularly leave on the table — axes labelled, curves shifted, equilibria marked. The internal assessment is three commentaries on published news articles, and UAE students have strong local material available in both Arabic and English for them.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Paper 1 is a source-based paper with a four-question structure whose mark allocations reward a disciplined approach. Students taking History alongside Arabic A find the source-analysis skill overlaps closely with Arabic A Paper 1, since both ask what a text does rather than what it says.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The TOK exhibition and the 1,600-word essay sit outside subject grades but contribute up to 3 points with the Extended Essay. Bilingual students often write unusually well on TOK's language and knowledge themes because they have lived the question.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay. An Arabic A student may write it in Arabic in a Group 1 category, which is rarer and often well received, but it needs a supervisor comfortable reading academic Arabic. Support here is process coaching and feedback on the student's own drafts.

modes.title: Weekly criterion clinic
modes.description: A standing weekly hour built around one piece of written work. The student submits a timed Paper 1 or Paper 2 response before the session; the tutor marks it against the four criteria, and the hour is spent on the single criterion losing the most marks. The marked script is returned with the mark breakdown so you can track it across weeks.

modes.description: A short block of sessions across the HL essay cycle: choosing a work and a line of inquiry, narrowing the question, structuring the argument, and reading the student's own draft. The tutor gives feedback and asks questions. The tutor does not supply sentences, paragraphs or an outline the student has not reasoned through themselves.

modes.description: The oral carries 40 marks and 20-30% of the grade depending on level, and it is the component most students prepare least. Sessions are recorded rehearsals: a global issue, an extract, 10 minutes of analysis, 5 minutes of questions, then the recording reviewed against the criteria with the student listening to their own evidence.

sections.heading: What a search for an Arabic A home tutor in Abu Dhabi usually means
paragraphs: An IB DP Arabic A home tutor in Abu Dhabi is, in practice, a specialist in Arabic literary analysis who can read a marked Diploma script and say which of four criteria is costing the grade. The phrase families type into Google describes a delivery method, but the thing they need is diagnostic skill. We deliver that one-to-one over live video across the emirate rather than by sending anyone to an address, and the reason is supply rather than convenience.

Count the people in Abu Dhabi who have taught Arabic A Literature at Higher Level, marked comparative essays on two Arabic works to the Diploma criteria, and supervised HL essays through a full cycle. It is a short list in any emirate. Now restrict that list to people who live within a reasonable drive of your area and are free at 17:00 on a Tuesday. The list gets shorter still, and the usual outcome is a tutor chosen for their postcode who turns the hour into conversation practice because that is what they can do. A bilingual student does not need conversation practice. They need someone who can explain why their analysis paragraph scored 2 out of 5.

The second reason is evidence. Online sessions produce artefacts by default. The script sits on a shared screen, gets annotated during the hour, and is saved when the lesson ends. Three weeks later you can put the three scripts side by side and see whether criterion B moved. A session at a kitchen table leaves a verbal report and a parent's impression. For a subject where the whole problem is that a grade hides four separate skills, the artefact is the point.

To be plain about it: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE, and no tutor will arrive at an Abu Dhabi address. In-home tutoring is a real market here, it has real advantages for younger children, and the comparison table below sets out honestly what it costs and what it buys. For Diploma Arabic A specifically, the trade is expertise against travel, and expertise wins.
