sections.heading: Availability, and what happens when nobody covers Business Management
paragraphs: Business Management is taught in fewer Abu Dhabi schools than Economics and by fewer specialists, and that shows up in availability rather than in price. The brief that actually matters is narrow: the current syllabus, comfort with the quantitative unit, experience supervising research projects, and familiarity with the pre-released case study for the live session.

For a weekday evening slot in DP1, matching is usually straightforward. For a 17:00 slot in the DP2 spring, when the case study and the project deadlines are both live across the emirate, it is not. At that point there are three honest answers, and a provider that always says yes is giving none of them.

A different time is the cheapest and most effective concession: a 20:00 slot or a weekend morning widens the pool substantially in exam term. A different tutor profile is the second: an Economics specialist who also teaches Business Management can handle the discursive units and marked-paper work competently while being weaker on the research project, and that trade-off should be stated rather than concealed. The third is waiting with a date attached.

Where no UAE-resident specialist is free, a matched tutor may be based elsewhere and teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and that is disclosed before any commitment. Two providers ranking for UAE searches route parents to contact numbers outside the country without saying where delivery happens. On a subject with a fixed case study cycle, discovering that late is particularly costly.

process.title: Say which of the three things you need
process.description: The pre-released case study, the research project, or finance and accounts. Those three cover most Business Management requests in this emirate, and naming one narrows the plan and the cost immediately. If more than one applies, say so, because the order they are bought in changes the total.

process.title: Send one marked answer or the project brief
process.description: A returned Paper 2 question, a marked quantitative section, or the school's research project brief with its internal deadlines. Any of those tells a specialist in minutes whether the job is technique, arithmetic or question design, which is the whole of the diagnosis.

process.title: Take the first session at no charge
process.description: A full session online with the matched tutor, with no payment and no card held. It should end with a written view: which component is costing marks, how many sessions that repair realistically takes, and whether any part of it could sensibly be shared with another student to reduce the cost.

process.title: Buy the blocks in the order that pays
process.description: Finance and accounts first, because it is mechanical and affects every paper. Research project question design next, because it expires. Case study preparation across the whole lead time rather than in the last six weeks. Paper 2 evaluation habits last, since they take a term rather than a block.

process.title: Review against marked work every six weeks
process.description: Compare marks by component against where they started. If the block you bought has not moved anything, change the diagnosis, the mode or the tutor rather than buying more of the same. A provider should be willing to tell you that the problem is revision habits rather than teaching, where that is what the evidence says.

whyPoints.title: Priced by component, with the sources named
whyPoints.description: Three of the six competitor pages measured for this cluster publish no price at all, and the two that do quote dollars. Every AED range here is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it and tied to the specific component a family would be buying.

whyPoints.title: Shared sessions offered where they genuinely help
whyPoints.description: The pre-released case study is identical for every candidate, so a shared session with two or three students produces better analysis at a lower cost per family. Saying so costs us revenue and it is the honest answer, and individual mark repair still happens one-to-one.

whyPoints.title: The research project boundary is written down
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches research method, explains what the criteria reward, and comments on drafts the student has written. Supplying text, choosing the organisation and question outright, or revising a draft into a submission is malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the candidate.

whyPoints.title: Quotes made comparable before you commit
whyPoints.description: Session length, specialist against generalist, unused-session rules, whether the quoted AED figure is inclusive, and whether the tutor holds a current MoHRE permit. Five questions that make two Abu Dhabi quotes comparable, and a provider should answer all five plainly.

whyPoints.title: No accreditation claimed, because none is held
whyPoints.description: ADEK oversees Abu Dhabi private schools and KHDA oversees Dubai's, including the Educational Services Permit a training institute with premises requires. IB Gram holds no permit, approval, accreditation or partnership from any regulator, board, school or school group, and occupies no premises in the UAE.

whyPoints.title: Built around the Abu Dhabi calendar
whyPoints.description: Slots run 16:30 to 20:00 Gulf Standard Time and move after Iftar during Ramadan. Plans count backwards from the school's own research project milestones and the arrival of the pre-released case study, both of which fall earlier than families expect.

faqs.question: What does a Diploma Business Management tutor charge an hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Market rates for IB specialist tutoring in the UAE run roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour, the band published in Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. TutorChase publishes AED 270, Unitors lists IB tuition from AED 200, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for an examiner tier. Rates from AED 33 to AED 65 advertised by Tutopiya and EdFlik are university-student or group formats rather than Diploma specialists. The more useful question is how many hours your specific component needs, since the rate varies little and the hours vary a great deal.

faqs.question: Does the pre-released case study change what we should be paying for?
faqs.answer: Completely. Because the case is issued to schools ahead of the examination, a family has months of lead time rather than weeks, and nothing about the case changes in that period. Starting preparation when it arrives buys the same hours at the same rate and achieves far more than starting six weeks out. It also makes a shared session defensible, because every candidate in the world sits the same case and much of the groundwork is common analysis rather than individual diagnosis.

faqs.question: Is a shared class good value for preparing the pre-seen case?
faqs.answer: For that component, yes, and this is the one place in the subject where we will say so. The analysis of the organisation, its context, the units the case touches and the toolkit techniques it invites is identical for every candidate, and two or three students working through it together argue better than one student working alone. What a shared session cannot do is repair your own child's habit of asserting rather than justifying, or their specific timing problem. Keep that part one-to-one.

faqs.question: How many hours does supporting the 1,800-word research project take?
faqs.answer: Six to eight for most students, and they are front-loaded. Roughly one hour establishing whether a workable organisation with real information access actually exists, one or two framing a question narrow enough to answer in 1,800 words, one or two on methodology and which analytical tools the question genuinely needs, two on criterion-referenced feedback on the student's first full draft, and one on reallocating the word budget so the evaluation is not what gets cut. Bought after a question has been approved and found unanswerable, the same hours achieve much less.

faqs.question: Which analytical tools take the most teaching time?
faqs.answer: The quantitative ones and the ones students apply mechanically without interpretation. Investment appraisal and ratio analysis take real teaching because the marks are for what the figure means in a specific context rather than for the calculation. Decision trees and critical path analysis take practice because the arithmetic is easy and the errors are careless. The strategic frameworks are quicker to teach and more often misused: applied because they are familiar rather than because the question needs them, which earns nothing.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level Business Management cost more to support than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Usually, and the reason is a specific component rather than a higher rate. Higher Level adds a third paper built on an unseen case about a social enterprise, which asks for a justified recommendation rather than a balanced evaluation. Students who write strong Paper 2 answers often write weak Paper 3 ones, because a good evaluation weighs and declines to choose while this paper requires a choice. That is a separate block of four to six sessions, and it is the main difference between the two levels on an invoice.

faqs.question: Why does finance and accounts drive up a Business Management bill?
faqs.answer: Because it is the only unit in the subject where an answer can be plainly wrong. A weak response on motivation theory still scores something; a cash flow forecast with an arithmetic error scores nothing for that item, and a ratio interpreted backwards is worse than no interpretation. Students who are fluent on the discursive units find that fluency does not transfer. The content is bounded, so four to six sessions normally covers it, and buying it when the unit is taught costs the same as buying it in a panic a year later.

faqs.question: How do we compare two tutoring quotes for Business Management in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Five questions make them comparable. How long is a session, since forty-five and ninety minutes are both called a session in this market. Is the tutor a Business Management specialist or a generalist across Group 3, and which did they teach most recently at Diploma level. What happens to unused sessions in a package. Is the quoted AED figure inclusive of value added tax. And does the tutor hold a current MoHRE private tuition work permit. A provider who answers all five plainly is usually the safer choice.

faqs.question: Are monthly Business Management packages cheaper than paying hourly?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the comparison needs the questions above. Packages circulating in this market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Check the real session length, the carry-over rule for unused sessions, and whether the package tutor is a specialist. For Business Management there is a further consideration: most families spend in three concentrated blocks rather than evenly across two years, and a monthly package assumes a steady pattern they may not want.

faqs.question: Do you send a Business Management tutor to our house in Al Raha Gardens?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. All Abu Dhabi lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. On rate the two options overlap anyway, with Bestimate putting in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 against AED 200 to AED 450 for an online specialist. What differs is reach: a Business Management specialist with research project experience is a narrow brief, and restricting it to a short evening drive narrows it much further.

faqs.question: Does my daughter need a real organisation for the research project?
faqs.answer: Yes, and settling that before anything else is the cheapest hour you will spend on the project. A student with access to someone willing to answer questions, share figures or describe a decision has a project. A student who has picked a large multinational online and hopes public material will answer their question usually discovers in the second draft that it does not. In Abu Dhabi this is most often solved through a parent's own workplace, and families near the central business district tend to have the easiest time of it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help choose the research question without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach what makes a question answerable, test a student's proposed question against the information actually available, and explain why a question is too broad for 1,800 words. What a tutor cannot do is choose the organisation and the question on the student's behalf, supply text, or revise a draft into something submittable. The distinction is between teaching judgement and exercising it for them. The school supervisor keeps the authenticity record, and the IB treats a breach as malpractice by the candidate.

faqs.question: What does it cost to add a second subject to a Business Management plan?
faqs.answer: Less than two separate plans if the subjects share content, and the same as two plans if they do not. Digital Society shares technology adoption and organisational change with Business Management, and the research habits transfer, so one tutor across both can cut total hours. Economics shares much less than families assume: market structures and some demand analysis, with completely different assessment instincts. Two specialists is usually the honest answer for Business and Economics, and that doubles the weekly spend rather than reducing it.

faqs.question: Does a Business Management tutor in Abu Dhabi need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years to a defined list including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so distrust any figure quoted. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK ethics rules additionally bar school staff from paid tutoring of their own enrolled students.

faqs.question: We only want help for the final six weeks before the papers. What does that look like?
faqs.answer: It looks like the most expensive hours per mark on the whole course, and it is still worth doing if nothing earlier was possible. At six weeks the research project is submitted and those marks are fixed, so the money goes entirely into the papers. Expect two sessions a week, which sits in Bestimate's AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above monthly band for specialist exam-year support. The highest return in that window is finance and accounts technique and shown working, because both are mechanical. Evaluation habits rarely change in six weeks.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-business-management-tuto.closingHeading: Start by naming which of the three you need
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-business-management-tuto.closingBody: Business Management support in Abu Dhabi is bought for the pre-released case study, the 1,800-word research project, or finance and accounts, and the three cost very different amounts because they take very different numbers of hours. The case study rewards lead time and can be shared. The project rewards one early hour on the question more than any amount of later rewriting. Finance and accounts is mechanical and recoverable. Send one marked answer or the school's project brief, take the first session at no charge, and buy the blocks in the order the diagnosis gives you.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-cas-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The mentors below work on the Creativity, Activity, Service requirement rather than on a subject syllabus. That means portfolio structure, evidence of the learning outcomes, interview preparation and the writing that holds it together. Ask for the stage your child is at — unstarted, under-evidenced, or unwritten — and the match is made on that.

intro.heading: The cost question, answered before the explanation
paragraphs: CAS carries no marks. It contributes nothing to the 45 points. And a Diploma candidate who has not satisfied it does not receive the Diploma. That combination is why it produces a particular kind of late panic in Abu Dhabi households, and why the market for paid CAS help exists at all. So the honest starting point for a page targeting an IB DP CAS home tutor in Abu Dhabi is not a description of the requirement. It is a price, a range, and a frank statement of how often the right amount to spend is nothing.

Here is the range. Published one-to-one tutoring rates in the UAE run from roughly AED 33-65 an hour at the budget online end, through AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, to AED 200-450 and beyond for IB specialists, with a named premium provider publishing AED 650. Visiting tutors sit at AED 180-350 according to Bestimate's 2026 rate work, and some home tutors advertise up to AED 500 once travel is loaded in. Nothing in that spread is specific to CAS, which is the first useful piece of information: nobody prices CAS separately, so you are buying generic mentoring hours at generic rates.

The second useful piece of information is that CAS has fewer purchasable problems than families assume. Four things typically go wrong. A student has done nothing, in which case what is needed is an opportunity rather than a tutor. A student has done plenty and recorded none of it, which is a writing and structuring problem and genuinely purchasable. A student has an unviable CAS project, which needs one conversation, not a term of hours. Or a student is two weeks from a sign-off deadline with an empty portfolio, which is the expensive version of the second problem and the one most families arrive with.

Four things move the number in Abu Dhabi specifically. Travel is the largest: a visiting mentor crossing from the island to Al Falah or Al Shamkha prices that journey into the hour, and the rate difference between an online and an in-home hour in the published data is substantial. Timing is the second: demand concentrates in the weeks before each school's internal sign-off, and anyone buying in that window is buying from a thinner pool. Cohort size is the third, because a thin DP cohort in a newer mainland school often means an overstretched CAS coordinator and therefore more that a family ends up paying for. The fourth is simply which of the four problems above you actually have.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For CAS that costs a family nothing at all, because CAS mentoring is conversation and document work. There is no laboratory, no equipment, no whiteboard that needs to be in the room. What online delivery removes is the travel loading in the rate and the rigidity in the slot, which matters in a household where the student's service commitment is itself an evening activity.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-cas-home-tutor.programmesIntro: CAS belongs to the Diploma Programme, but the service and activity habits it tests are built much earlier in an IB school, and the Career-related Programme has its own version of the same requirement. Knowing where your child sits changes whether the right purchase is mentoring, writing support, or nothing.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: CAS runs alongside the six subjects for roughly eighteen months, assessed by nobody and required by everybody. It is evidenced through a portfolio, three formal interviews with a CAS coordinator or adviser, and a CAS project of at least one month. Satisfying it is a condition of the Diploma award, which is why an empty portfolio is a serious problem rather than an administrative one.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts cluster in a small number of schools on the island, along the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor and on Yas Island. Established schools usually run structured service partnerships that make CAS straightforward and cheap. Newer mainland cohorts often do not yet, and those are the households that end up paying for what a settled programme provides free.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Service as action is the MYP's equivalent, logged across the five years and culminating in the Personal Project. A student who has kept a usable record through MYP arrives in DP1 already able to write a reflection that says something. One who has treated service as a box to tick arrives with the writing problem that later costs money to fix.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi families moving in from British or American systems mid-MYP often meet logged service for the first time. The practical consequence shows up two years later: a DP1 student who has never written a reflection in their life, facing seven learning outcomes and an interview.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Carries service learning rather than CAS, with a reflective project, personal and professional skills and a language portfolio alongside DP courses. The service learning component is evidenced in a similar way and runs into the same recording problem, but the cohort is far smaller so a local mentor pool rarely exists.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision in the UAE is concentrated in a handful of schools, so a CP student needing help with service learning is often the only candidate in the building on that pathway. Online matching is the practical answer when the cohort is one.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Action is built into the inquiry cycle and the Year 6 exhibition, with no portfolio and no interviews. Nothing here needs paying for. What it establishes is whether a child is used to being asked what they learned from doing something, which is precisely the question CAS asks a sixteen-year-old.
programmes.countryNote: PYP provision is spread across community schools in Khalifa City, Al Reef and the newer mainland developments. Families at this stage are not CAS customers and should not be sold to as though they were.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-cas-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: CAS is not a subject, so there is no syllabus to list. What there is instead is a set of experience types that reliably evidence the learning outcomes in an Abu Dhabi context, each with its own practical constraint. The grid below is what the strands actually look like in this emirate.

subjects.name: Instrumental or vocal performance
subjects.description: Strong for the outcome about developing a new skill and for commitment over time, provided there is a record of progression rather than a certificate. The weakness is that lessons a student already took before DP1 do not evidence new growth unless the repertoire or the goal visibly changes.

subjects.name: Visual art, film or design outside the classroom
subjects.description: Works well because the artefacts are self-documenting. The usual failure is overlap with an assessed Visual Arts component, which is not permitted to double count. Keep a clear separation between what belongs to the portfolio and what belongs to the subject.

subjects.name: Club or school team sport
subjects.description: The easiest strand to accumulate and the hardest to reflect on, because a student who has played football since they were seven cannot claim a new skill. The fix is a defined goal inside the season: a position change, a fitness target, a coaching role for younger players.

subjects.name: Individual fitness or endurance goal
subjects.description: Abu Dhabi's climate makes outdoor training a seasonal project, which is actually useful: planning around the heat demonstrates the perseverance and planning outcomes clearly. A logged twelve-week programme with setbacks recorded evidences more than a gym membership ever will.

subjects.name: Tutoring or coaching younger students
subjects.description: Among the most reliable service options in a school with a large primary section, and it evidences collaboration and ethical engagement naturally. It needs supervision arranged through the school rather than privately, and the beneficiary's perspective has to appear in the reflection.

subjects.name: Volunteering with a licensed charity or community body
subjects.description: The strongest evidence for engagement with issues of global significance, because the need is real and documented. In the UAE, work has to go through a properly licensed organisation, and arrangements are best made via the school's existing partnerships rather than informally.

subjects.name: Environmental or sustainability work
subjects.description: Abu Dhabi offers genuine subject matter here: water consumption, cooling loads, mangrove and coastal habitats, waste in large villa communities. A measured project with before-and-after data evidences several outcomes at once and reads far better than a single clean-up morning.

subjects.name: Language or cultural exchange
subjects.description: Learning Arabic beyond the school requirement, or running a conversation group, evidences new skills and global engagement in a way an examiner-facing component never asks about. It requires sustained attendance to be worth anything in the portfolio.

subjects.name: Student-led initiative or society
subjects.description: Founding something is strong evidence for initiative and planning, and it is the most common basis for a CAS project. The requirement that catches students out is collaboration: an initiative run alone does not satisfy the project's collaborative dimension.

subjects.name: Paid work or a family business
subjects.description: Employment does not count as CAS by itself, which surprises families every year. An unpaid, structured extension of the activity with a defined learning goal and supervision can sometimes be shaped into something that does, but this needs checking with the CAS coordinator before any hours are logged.

subjects.name: The CAS project
subjects.description: At least one month in duration, collaborative, planned through to reflection, and the one element with a hard structural requirement. Students most often fail it on duration or on collaboration, having run a single fundraising day alone and logged it as the project.

subjects.name: The portfolio and three interviews
subjects.description: What the coordinator actually sees. Three formal conversations across the programme, with a record of the seven learning outcomes against evidence. The portfolio is where good CAS goes to die undocumented, and it is the only part of CAS a paid mentor can meaningfully help with.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-cas-home-tutor.regionsTitle: What CAS costs by where you live in Abu Dhabi
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-cas-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Geography changes the CAS bill in two ways: whether a visiting mentor would price travel into the hour, and whether the service opportunities near you are already organised by someone else. Both are local questions and neither is answered by a generic rate card.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Established schools with structured service partnerships, so most families here need no paid mentoring at all. Where money is spent it is on portfolio writing in DP2, not on finding opportunities. Short commutes keep any visiting-tutor travel loading low, which is why local rates here sit nearer the published middle.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Apartment living with limited scope for activity-strand projects at home, so club and school provision does the work. The practical cost here is scheduling: a student whose activity commitment is already an evening slot has little room left, which pushes mentoring to weekend mornings.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Buses from island schools often arrive after 4.30pm, so a visiting mentor's slot and a club commitment compete for the same hour. Families here typically settle on an online weekend block, which removes the travel loading that Bestimate's 2026 figures attach to in-home hours.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: A dense DP population feeding a small number of schools, which means CAS sign-off deadlines hit many households in the same fortnight. Buying mentoring in that window costs more and offers less choice than booking in the term before it.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Older island neighbourhoods with long-established schools and a mix of curricula. Service opportunities here are frequently arranged through the school's own partners, which is the cheapest route available and the one families most often overlook.

regions.name: Yas Island and West Yas
regions.note: Newer cohorts where the CAS programme is still maturing, so coordinators are stretched and more falls to the family. This is where paid portfolio support most often earns its fee, because the structural scaffolding a settled programme provides is not yet there.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: Mainland villa communities with long drives to island schools and multiple children per household. Travel loading on a visiting mentor would be the highest in the emirate here, which makes the online rate difference most visible to these families.

regions.name: Al Shamkha, Al Falah and Al Reef
regions.note: Distance from the island is the governing cost factor, both for a visiting mentor and for any service placement that is not local. Projects built around the immediate community cost nothing in travel and usually evidence the outcomes better than something organised downtown.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-cas-home-tutor.modesIntro: There are three honest shapes of paid CAS help and one shape families should refuse to buy. The difference between them is roughly a factor of ten in total cost, so picking the right one matters more here than negotiating an hourly rate.

modes.title: One diagnostic conversation
modes.description: A single session that establishes which of the four CAS problems a student actually has, checks the portfolio against the seven learning outcomes, and produces a written list of what is missing. For a student who has been active and simply has not recorded it, this is often the entire intervention needed. It is the cheapest useful thing available and the one families skip.

modes.title: Portfolio and reflection writing support
modes.description: The genuinely purchasable problem. A student with eighteen months of real activity and an empty record needs to learn how to write a reflection that says something: what was attempted, what went wrong, what changed as a result. Three or four sessions normally covers it, with the student writing between them. This is teaching, not transcription.
bullets: What separates a usable reflection from "I learned a lot"
Mapping existing experiences onto outcomes the student has already met

modes.title: CAS project troubleshooting
modes.description: Usually one session, occasionally two. The project is where a student fails on structure rather than effort: too short, not collaborative, or planned without a reflection stage. A single conversation that tests the plan against the requirements before it starts saves a term of wasted activity, and is far cheaper than rebuilding afterwards.

modes.title: What we will not sell you
modes.description: Ongoing weekly CAS mentoring across a term is almost always the wrong product. CAS has no syllabus to teach and no marks to improve, so a weekly hour fills with conversation. Anyone selling a term-length CAS package to an Abu Dhabi family should be asked precisely what the second half of it contains.
bullets: No weekly retainer for a requirement that carries no marks
No writing of reflections, under any framing
No invented service placements the student did not attend

sections.heading: What CAS help actually costs in the Abu Dhabi market, with sources
paragraphs: Nobody publishes a CAS rate, because nobody treats CAS as a separate product. What you are quoted is a general one-to-one mentoring rate, so the honest way to price this is to show the market spread and then show how many hours each of the four CAS problems really consumes. Total cost is hours multiplied by rate, and the hours figure is where families lose money, not the rate.

Every number in the table below was published by the provider named, at the date given. They are market rates and none of them is an IB Gram price. Our own figure comes from a consultation after a free first conversation, for the plain reason that quoting before anyone has looked at the portfolio would be a guess. The useful column is the right-hand one: what the realistic hour count is for each problem, because that is what turns an hourly rate into a bill.

Read the arithmetic rather than the rate. A diagnostic conversation plus three writing sessions at AED 250 is around a thousand dirhams and solves the commonest CAS problem completely. A weekly hour from October to April at the same rate is roughly seven thousand dirhams for a requirement that carries no marks. The gap between those two outcomes has nothing to do with negotiating and everything to do with buying the right shape. Ask any provider for an hour estimate in writing before you discuss a rate at all, because a quote per hour tells you nothing about what the term will cost and a provider who will not estimate hours is telling you something about how they intend to bill you.

sections.heading: The four things that change the number in this emirate
paragraphs: Travel is the first and largest. The published gap between an online hour and an in-home hour in the UAE market is wide enough to notice across a term, and in Abu Dhabi the distances are real: the island to Al Shamkha, Al Falah or Al Samha is a serious evening journey. A mentor who drives that prices it in, and a mentor who does not drive it can be selected from a far larger pool. For a requirement that is entirely conversation and document work, paying a travel loading buys nothing.

Timing is the second. Demand for CAS help in Abu Dhabi spikes in the weeks before each school's internal sign-off, and because the big cohorts in the Al Raha and Khalifa City corridor run on similar calendars, those spikes land together. A family buying in that fortnight is choosing from whoever is left and paying whatever that person asks. The same help bought a term earlier costs less and takes fewer hours, because there is time for the student to do the work between sessions rather than alongside a mentor.

Cohort maturity is the third, and it is the one nobody mentions. A settled Diploma programme with a full-time coordinator and existing service partnerships supplies most of what CAS needs for free: placements, supervision, interview scheduling, a template for the portfolio. A newer cohort in a growing mainland school may have a coordinator teaching a full timetable as well, and the shortfall quietly becomes a household expense. Before paying anyone, ask the school precisely what it provides. The fourth factor is simply which problem you have, which the next section takes apart.

sections.heading: Which CAS problems money can solve, and which it cannot
paragraphs: This is the section competitors in this search result never write, because it reduces the size of the sale. CAS failures fall into four kinds and only two of them respond to paid help. Knowing which one you have is worth more than any rate comparison, and it takes one honest conversation to establish.

An inactivity problem is not purchasable. If a student has genuinely done nothing for a year, what is missing is a placement, a team, a commitment and time — none of which a mentor supplies. The right calls are to the school's CAS coordinator and to whatever licensed community organisations the school already works with. A recording problem, by contrast, is highly purchasable and is the one most Abu Dhabi families actually have: eighteen months of real activity, no portfolio, no reflections, an interview approaching. Three or four sessions of writing teaching usually resolves it.

A structural problem with the CAS project is purchasable but cheap: one conversation testing the plan against duration, collaboration and the reflection stage. Buying a term of mentoring for this is overpaying by a factor of ten. A motivation problem is the fourth, and it is the one that quietly consumes the most money. A student who does not want to engage will sit through paid sessions politely and produce nothing, and selling more hours into that is indefensible. Saying so is the useful thing a provider can do, and it is a conversation better had with the school's pastoral team than with anyone charging by the hour.

sections.heading: The free substitutes most Abu Dhabi households have not exhausted
paragraphs: Before any payment, four free resources exist and families routinely use none of them. The first is the school's CAS coordinator, whose job this is. A coordinator can confirm the sign-off deadline, say which outcomes the portfolio is missing, and in many cases hand over a template. That conversation costs an email and removes the need for a diagnostic session entirely.

The second is the school's existing partnerships. Established Abu Dhabi schools maintain relationships with licensed community organisations precisely so that students are not arranging placements informally, which in the UAE is also the legally cleaner route. The third is the cohort. CAS projects have to be collaborative, so a student with no project and a classmate with a half-built one is a free solution to both problems. Coordinators can broker that and often will if asked.

The fourth is the published guidance itself. The IB's CAS material sets out the seven learning outcomes and the project requirements in plain language, and reading it with your child for an hour is a legitimate substitute for a paid diagnostic. Note that the hours figure families repeat to each other — a round number somewhere near a hundred and fifty — is a legacy of older guidance rather than a current requirement, though individual schools do set their own internal expectations. Ask your school what its policy is instead of assuming the number is universal. An hour of reading the guidance together, with the sign-off date written at the top of the page, will often tell a family more than the first paid session they were about to book.

sections.heading: Reflection is a writing problem, and writing can be taught
paragraphs: The purchasable part of CAS is almost entirely writing. A reflection that says "I learned a lot and it was a great experience" evidences nothing, and a student who writes twelve of those has a full portfolio and an empty one at the same time. What a coordinator is looking for is far more specific: what was attempted, what obstacle appeared, what the student did differently afterwards, and what they now think about the issue the activity touched.

That is a teachable structure rather than a talent. The method we use is to start from what the student actually remembers, in speech, and then teach them to convert it into evidence against a named outcome. A student who can tell you that the under-twelve football session fell apart because they had planned for fifteen children and twenty-eight arrived is already describing planning, perseverance and collaboration. They simply have not written it down in a form that names those things.

The boundary matters here more than anywhere else on this page. A mentor teaches the structure, questions the student until the specifics surface, and then stops. The sentences in the portfolio are the student's. A portfolio written by somebody else is detectable in a five-minute interview, because the interview asks the student to talk about what they wrote, and that is the whole purpose of the three formal conversations. Buying written reflections buys the student a conversation they cannot survive, and the coordinator who conducts it has heard enough portfolios described aloud to know the difference within a couple of questions.

sections.heading: The Abu Dhabi service calendar, and what it does to the bill
paragraphs: CAS runs for about eighteen months and the Abu Dhabi year has three stretches in which outdoor and community activity is genuinely difficult. Planning around them is free; failing to plan around them produces the compressed, expensive catch-up that families pay for in DP2. This is a local operational fact that no competing page in this cluster mentions.

The summer is the longest interruption, both because of the heat and because a large share of Abu Dhabi families travel for six to eight weeks. A commitment that depends on weekly attendance will break, and a student who has not arranged a continuation returns in September with a visible gap in the record. The usable answer is to shift strands seasonally: a creativity or online service commitment that travels, and the activity strand loaded into the cooler months.

Ramadan is the second stretch, and it changes timing rather than stopping anything. Activity moves to after Iftar, service demand in the community rises, and schools often run their own initiatives, which makes it one of the better months for evidencing service if planned rather than endured. The third is the examination run-in, when a student should be nowhere near a new CAS commitment. Anything left for that window will be bought at a premium, in hours and in stress. The practical upshot of all three is that the cheap period for CAS is DP1, when the school's own provision is available and nothing competes with it, and the expensive period is the second half of DP2, when everything competes with everything.

sections.heading: What a paid CAS mentor may not touch
paragraphs: At least one operation in this search result sells completed assessed work, so the boundary needs stating rather than implying. CAS is unmarked, which makes some people assume the honesty rules are looser here. They are not. The portfolio is a record of what a student did and thought, and the three formal interviews exist to test that the record is theirs. A mentor who supplies reflections is handing a student a document they cannot discuss.

So the line is simple and it is written here so you can hold us to it. A mentor may ask questions until the specifics surface, teach the structure of a reflective entry, explain what an outcome statement means, rehearse interview questions, and read a draft and say what is missing. A mentor may not write an entry, invent an experience, log hours that did not happen, or describe a placement the student did not attend. Nor may a mentor produce any part of the Personal Project, an Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay, which are separate requirements with their own rules.

There is a second boundary that is specific to Abu Dhabi. Press reporting of ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document. The practical point stands regardless: the person who signs off your child's CAS should not be paid by you to help them pass it.

sections.heading: Online mentoring against a visiting mentor, priced side by side
paragraphs: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. On a CAS page that limitation is close to costless, and it is worth setting out why in money terms rather than as a reassurance. A visiting mentor's hour contains a journey. Bestimate's 2026 rate work puts in-home tutoring at AED 180-350 with some home tutors advertising to AED 500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified online hour, and the difference is the car.

The second cost is rigidity, which does not appear on an invoice. A visiting mentor runs a route, so the slot cannot move. CAS students are the ones most likely to need it to move, because their activity and service commitments are themselves evening fixtures and they shift week to week. An online slot that can be rebooked at short notice is not a convenience here; it is the difference between a session happening and a session being paid for and missed.

The third is selection. CAS mentoring needs someone who has actually read a portfolio against the outcomes and sat on the other side of an interview. The number of such people in Abu Dhabi who will also drive to Al Shamkha on a Thursday evening is small. Removing the driving radius from the match is not a compromise; it is how a mainland family gets the same person a Saadiyat family would get. That single fact does more for a household in Al Falah or Al Samha than any discount on an hourly rate ever could.

sections.heading: ADEK, the permit, and what you are actually buying
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi's private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge. The UAE government's own portal describes ADEK as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and ADEK publishes an inspection record for each one. None of that touches CAS directly, because CAS is signed off by the school against IB requirements, but it matters for a cost question: a school with a well-run Diploma programme supplies more of CAS for free, and its inspection report is a better guide to that than anything a tutoring provider tells you.

The permit question is the one a parent can check. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which introduced private tuition work permits. The UAE government portal states that the permit is granted free of charge for two years and that eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, any specific amount quoted to you should be disregarded.

IB Gram holds no accreditation from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and does not operate premises in the UAE. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai would need a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific authorisation issued to specific organisations. What you are buying from us is one-to-one teaching time delivered online, and the only claims on this page are ones you can check: the rates belong to the providers named, the regulatory facts come from the government portals cited, and the delivery model is stated rather than implied.

process.title: Email your school before you email us
process.description: Ask the CAS coordinator for the internal sign-off date, which outcomes the portfolio is currently missing, and which organisations the school already partners with. That costs nothing and frequently answers the whole question. If it does, there is no reason to buy anything, and we would rather say that than sell into it.

process.title: Tell us which of the four problems you have
process.description: Nothing done, plenty done but unrecorded, a project that fails the requirements, or a disengaged student. The bill differs by a factor of ten across those four. If you are not sure which one applies, say so, and the first conversation will establish it before anything is quoted.

process.title: A free first conversation that ends in a number
process.description: The first session reads the portfolio against the seven outcomes and produces a written list of gaps plus an honest hour estimate. Where the right answer is one session and nothing further, that is what you will be told. Where it is three or four, you get the number before you commit.

process.title: Buy the shape, not a retainer
process.description: A diagnostic, writing support, project troubleshooting or interview rehearsal are separate products with separate hour counts. Weekly CAS mentoring across a term is not something we offer, because there is no syllabus to fill it with and no marks for it to move.

process.title: Check the portfolio, then stop
process.description: When the outcomes are evidenced and the student can discuss the record aloud, the work is finished and the sessions end. A provider proposing further hours at that point is selling comfort. The review point is agreed in writing at the start so that the stopping condition is not a negotiation.

whyPoints.title: The price conversation happens first
whyPoints.description: A rate, an hour count and a total before you commit, with every market figure attributed to whoever published it. Three of the six pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all and two quote United States dollars. An Abu Dhabi family transacts in dirhams and should be shown dirhams.

whyPoints.title: We name the problems not worth paying for
whyPoints.description: Two of the four common CAS failures do not respond to purchased hours, and we say which. That shrinks the sale and it is the single most useful thing a provider can tell a family three weeks before a sign-off deadline.

whyPoints.title: No travel loading on a conversation
whyPoints.description: CAS mentoring is talk and documents. Paying an in-home premium for that buys a car journey. Lessons are online and one-to-one, which also means the slot moves around a service commitment instead of around a mentor's route.

whyPoints.title: The authorship line is published
whyPoints.description: A mentor questions, teaches structure and rehearses interviews. The entries in the portfolio are written by the student. The three formal interviews exist precisely to test that, so anything else leaves your child holding a document they cannot defend.

whyPoints.title: The delivery model is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one and online on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE and holds no accreditation from ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board. Saying so is less comfortable than staying vague and considerably more useful.

whyPoints.title: Coverage and timing disclosed up front
whyPoints.description: Demand concentrates before each school's sign-off window, and availability in that fortnight is genuinely tighter. You hear the match time before you commit rather than after, including when the honest answer is that booking a term earlier would have cost you less.

faqs.question: What should CAS support cost in Abu Dhabi, if we need any at all?
faqs.answer: Nobody prices CAS separately, so you pay a general one-to-one rate. Published UAE figures run from AED 33-65 at the budget online end, AED 150-300 for a qualified online tutor, AED 200-450 and above for IB specialists, and AED 180-500 for a visiting tutor once travel is loaded in; one named provider publishes AED 650. The number that matters is hours, not rate. The commonest CAS problem — plenty done, nothing written — takes a diagnostic plus three or four sessions. At mid-market rates that is roughly a thousand dirhams, not a term-length package.

faqs.question: Is paying for a CAS mentor ever simply a waste of money?
faqs.answer: Yes, in two situations. If your child has genuinely done nothing, what is missing is a placement and a term of commitment, and no mentor supplies either; the school's coordinator and its existing partnerships are the right calls. If your child is disengaged, paid sessions become polite attendance with nothing produced between them, and buying more hours into that is indefensible. The two situations where money does work are an unwritten portfolio and a CAS project that fails on structure. One of those takes a few sessions and the other takes one conversation.

faqs.question: Why do quotes for CAS help in Abu Dhabi range from AED 150 to AED 650 an hour?
faqs.answer: Because the quotes are not for the same thing. The lower end is a general online tutor; the upper end is a premium provider trading on claimed examiner experience. Four local factors widen the gap further: whether the mentor travels to you, whether you are buying inside the pre-sign-off rush, how mature your school's CAS programme is, and which of the four CAS problems you actually have. For an unmarked requirement that is mostly conversation and writing, paying at the top of that range is difficult to justify on any reading.

faqs.question: Does our school's CAS coordinator already do what I am about to pay for?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, and this is the cheapest check available. A coordinator can give you the internal sign-off date, tell you which of the seven learning outcomes the portfolio still lacks, hand over a template, broker a collaboration with a classmate who needs a project partner, and point you at licensed organisations the school already works with. In established Abu Dhabi schools that covers most of what a paid diagnostic would produce. Where it does not — typically in newer cohorts with a stretched coordinator — the shortfall is real and is where paid help earns its fee.

faqs.question: My son has eighteen months of real activity and an empty portfolio. How many paid hours does that take?
faqs.answer: Usually four or five in total, spread over three or four weeks, with the student writing between sessions. The first establishes which outcomes his existing experiences already evidence, which is normally more than he thinks. The next two or three teach what a usable reflective entry contains: the specific obstacle, the decision taken, what changed afterwards. A final session rehearses the interview. At AED 200-300 an hour that is roughly a thousand to fifteen hundred dirhams. Anyone quoting a term-long package for this problem is selling hours rather than solving it.

faqs.question: Is the hours figure everyone quotes for CAS an actual IB requirement?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a school policy question rather than an IB rule. The round number that circulates between parents comes from older guidance; current CAS material emphasises a reasonable balance across the three strands over roughly eighteen months rather than a total to be accumulated. Individual schools do set their own internal expectations, and your school's figure is the one that governs your child. Ask the coordinator in writing. Chasing an invented total is one of the commonest ways students waste a year on activity that evidences nothing.

faqs.question: Can CAS actually stop my daughter receiving her Diploma?
faqs.answer: Satisfying CAS is a condition of the Diploma award, so an unsatisfied requirement is a serious matter rather than an administrative one, even though CAS contributes no points. In practice schools work hard to avoid that outcome, which is why the three formal interviews exist: they are checkpoints, not formalities. The risk is highest for a student who has drifted through DP1 with no project and an unrecorded year. If that describes your daughter, the conversation to have this week is with the coordinator, not with a tutoring provider.

faqs.question: Is there any legitimate paid help with CAS reflections?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is teaching rather than transcription. A mentor can ask questions until the specifics surface, show what separates an evidenced entry from "I learned a lot", explain what each outcome statement is asking for, and read a draft and name what is missing. What a mentor cannot do is supply the entry. The three formal interviews ask the student to talk about what they wrote, so a portfolio in somebody else's voice hands your child a conversation they cannot survive. The sentences have to be theirs.

faqs.question: We are out of the UAE for the whole summer. Does that cost us later?
faqs.answer: It can, and it is the most predictable expense in the whole CAS window. A commitment that depends on weekly local attendance breaks over a six to eight week absence, and the gap is visible in the record. The free fix is seasonal planning: put a portable creativity commitment or an online service role into the summer, and load the activity strand into the cooler months. The expensive version is returning in September to rebuild a broken commitment while DP2 coursework starts, which is exactly the scenario that produces compressed, premium-rate catch-up in the spring.

faqs.question: Which CAS strand is hardest to evidence in Abu Dhabi, and can money solve it?
faqs.answer: Service, consistently, and money solves it poorly. Placements in the UAE should go through properly licensed organisations, which means the practical route is the school's existing partnerships rather than an informal arrangement a family finds. A mentor cannot create a placement. What a mentor can do is help shape a service idea around something genuinely local — water use, cooling loads, coastal habitats, support for younger students — so that the evidence is real and measurable. That shaping is one conversation, not a term of hours.

faqs.question: What does the CAS project have to be, and can paying for help shorten it?
faqs.answer: It has to run for at least one month, be collaborative, and move through planning, action and reflection rather than being a single event. No payment shortens the month, which is the point families most often want to buy around. What one conversation can do is stop a student spending a term on something that will not satisfy the requirement: a fundraising day run alone is the classic failure, strong on effort and wrong on both duration and collaboration. Testing the plan before the effort goes in is the cheapest intervention on this page.

faqs.question: Our adviser has signed off two interviews. Is the third one a formality?
faqs.answer: No, and treating it as one is a mistake. The final interview is where the record as a whole is reviewed against all seven learning outcomes, and it is the point at which a portfolio that looked adequate in instalments can turn out to have gaps. It also asks the student to talk about the project and about what changed over the eighteen months, which is a harder conversation than describing a single activity. One rehearsal session against the actual outcome statements is usually enough, and it is a good use of a single paid hour.

faqs.question: Would a visiting CAS mentor in Abu Dhabi be worth the travel loading?
faqs.answer: For CAS specifically, it is hard to argue. The work is conversation and document review, so nothing in it requires someone physically present. Bestimate's 2026 figures put in-home tutoring at AED 180-350, with some home tutors advertising to AED 500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified online hour; the gap is the car. Travel also fixes the slot, which is the wrong trade for a student whose service and activity commitments move week to week. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE in any case; our delivery is one-to-one and online.

faqs.question: Does anyone outside the school ever look at a CAS portfolio?
faqs.answer: Rarely in the sense parents imagine. The portfolio is reviewed internally and CAS completion is reported as satisfied or not, with no mark and no grade attached. Universities do not read it. What they may read is a reference, and what a student says about an eighteen-month commitment in an interview or a personal statement is often drawn from exactly this material. So the portfolio has a quiet downstream value, which is an argument for doing it properly rather than for paying someone to make it look impressive.

faqs.question: Two weeks to sign-off and the portfolio is empty. What does that cost?
faqs.answer: More than the same problem bought a term earlier, in both rate and hours. Realistically six to ten compressed hours, at the top of whatever band is available, because demand in Abu Dhabi concentrates in exactly that fortnight and the pool thins. Before paying it, do two free things: email the coordinator to confirm what is genuinely outstanding, and sit with your child to list what they actually did over eighteen months. Most students in this position have done the activity. If that is true, the work is writing, and writing can be done quickly once the raw material is on the table.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor working with students in Abu Dhabi need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which introduced private tuition work permits. The government portal states the permit is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen and university students. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so disregard any amount quoted to you. Ask any mentor directly before you pay them.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-cas-home-tutor.closingHeading: Ask the school first, then ask us for a number
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-cas-home-tutor.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB DP CAS home tutor in Abu Dhabi, the sequence that saves the most money is simple. Email the CAS coordinator for the sign-off date and the outstanding learning outcomes. Then tell us which of the four problems you have, and take a free first conversation that ends in an hour count rather than a package. Where the answer is that you need one session, you will be told that. Where it is nothing at all, you will be told that too. Mentoring, when it is worth buying, is one-to-one and online on Gulf Standard Time, for families from Saadiyat Island to Al Shamkha, with the reflections written by your child.

intro.heading: CAS costs nothing to pass and plenty to mishandle
paragraphs: Creativity, Activity, Service is the only part of the IB Diploma that cannot be improved by spending money, and it is one of the parts families in Abu Dhabi spend most readily on. There is no grade, no mark scheme and no examiner. There are seven learning outcomes, a portfolio of evidence and reflections, a project of at least one month, and three documented interviews with the school's CAS coordinator. Completion is required for the diploma to be awarded. Quality, in the sense a marker would recognise, is not assessed at all.

That combination produces a strange market. Because CAS is compulsory and unmarked, it generates anxiety without generating anything to work on, and a service industry has grown in the Gulf to absorb that anxiety: paid volunteering placements with certificates attached, portfolio formatting help, reflection writing, and bundles of experiences sold as a package that will satisfy the outcomes. Almost none of it addresses what a CAS coordinator actually signs off.

The coordinator is the key fact. CAS is already somebody's job at your child's school, that person's time is inside your fees, and they are the only person who can confirm the outcomes have been met. Before any family pays anyone externally, the cheaper step is an email to the coordinator asking which outcomes are currently unevidenced. Most of the time the answer is two or three, each of which the student can address in a fortnight without help.

It is worth being precise about why that works, because it is the opposite of how the rest of the diploma behaves. In an examined subject, a tutor can teach content the student does not have, and the marks move. In CAS there is no content and no marks. What exists is a record of things the student did, and the only question is whether that record shows all seven outcomes. Nobody outside the student can generate the experiences, and nobody outside the school can confirm them, which leaves a narrow strip of genuinely useful external work and a wide market selling everything else.

There are genuine exceptions, and this page names three rather than pretending there are none. A student with real executive-function difficulties who cannot sustain an eighteen-month commitment without structure. A student who joined the diploma late, mid-DP1 or later, and has to compress the whole thing. A student whose CAS project has collapsed and who needs to rebuild one that meets the month-minimum requirement in the time available. In those cases a handful of mentoring hours earns its keep, and the hourly figures on this page are the market bands to judge a quote against.

Where we do work, the rules are strict. The reflections and portfolio entries are written by the student, in their own words, about things they actually did. We do not supply reflections, we do not arrange or sell volunteering placements, and we do not issue certificates. Sessions are delivered one-to-one over live video; IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and for CAS that is beside the point anyway, because the work happens in the student's own community rather than at a desk.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-cas-tutor.programmesIntro: Service and activity requirements appear across the IB continuum in different forms, and a student who met them properly earlier arrives at CAS needing nothing. This is how each programme touches it in Abu Dhabi.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: CAS runs across at least eighteen months from the start of DP1, built from experiences in the three strands plus a project lasting at least one month. Evidence and reflections go into a portfolio, and the student has three documented interviews with the coordinator. No grade is issued; completion is required for the award of the diploma.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools differ sharply in how much they organise and how much they leave to the student. Some run structured service partnerships and sports programmes that fill the strands almost automatically; others hand over a portfolio template in week one and expect initiative. Which of those your child's school does is the single best predictor of whether any external support is worth buying.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Service as action runs through the MYP, with students expected to take initiative and reflect on the outcomes, and the Personal Project adds a sustained independent commitment with a process journal. Both rehearse exactly the habits CAS asks for, including writing about a setback honestly.
programmes.countryNote: An Abu Dhabi continuum student who kept a genuine service-as-action record arrives at CAS already fluent in it and needs no paid help whatsoever. A student transferring in for DP1 from a system with no service requirement is the one most likely to stall, which is why late arrivals form one of the three legitimate cases for mentoring on this page.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Action is part of the PYP's inquiry cycle, usually as class or year-group initiatives rather than individual commitments. There is nothing to document formally and nothing to buy, but the idea that noticing a problem is followed by doing something about it starts here.
programmes.countryNote: Worth mentioning only to make a point about sequencing: families sometimes try to build a CAS portfolio retrospectively from primary-school activities. It does not work, because CAS requires experiences undertaken during the programme with reflections written at the time. The portfolio is a record of the eighteen months, not a curriculum vitae.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: CP students do not do CAS. The CP core includes service learning alongside personal and professional skills, a reflective project and language development, assessed and recorded differently. The requirements overlap in spirit and differ in documentation.
programmes.countryNote: This is a live source of confusion in Abu Dhabi, where CP and DP students share corridors and advice. A CP student being coached against CAS learning outcomes, or buying a CAS portfolio service, is paying for the wrong framework entirely. Confirm with the coordinator which core your child is registered for before spending anything.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-cas-tutor.subjectsIntro: CAS has no subjects. What it has are strands and the kinds of experience that sit inside them. These are the categories Abu Dhabi students actually use, with what each one is good for and where it goes wrong.

subjects.name: Creativity — performing arts
subjects.description: Music ensembles, drama productions, dance groups. Strong for sustained commitment and for collaboration outcomes because rehearsal schedules are fixed and attendance is visible. Weak as a source of challenge evidence if the student has been doing it since Year 4 and faces nothing new.

subjects.name: Creativity — visual and digital making
subjects.description: Film, photography, design, illustration, coding something for a real user. Good for initiative and planning outcomes. The common failure is a project with no audience and no deadline, which produces no evidence of commitment because nothing ever had to be finished.

subjects.name: Activity — team sport
subjects.description: School teams and community clubs. The easiest strand to fill in Abu Dhabi and the easiest to over-rely on. Fixtures and training provide reliable commitment evidence; they rarely provide the new-skill or challenge evidence the outcomes also want.

subjects.name: Activity — individual physical challenge
subjects.description: Running, swimming, cycling, climbing, martial arts taken up deliberately at a level that is genuinely hard. The best single source of evidence for developing a new skill and for perseverance, because progress and setbacks are both measurable.

subjects.name: Service — direct community work
subjects.description: Working with people: tutoring younger students, care-home or hospital visiting arranged through the school, coaching children at a community club. The richest source of ethical-implications evidence and the strand schools most often broker, because access and safeguarding need an adult arrangement.

subjects.name: Service — indirect and advocacy
subjects.description: Work that benefits a community without direct contact: fundraising with a plan behind it, translating materials, building something a group needs, campaigning on an issue the student can explain. Suits students whose timetables make regular placements impossible.

subjects.name: Service — environmental
subjects.description: Coastal and mangrove clean-ups, water and waste audits at school, planting and habitat work. Abundant in this emirate and easily reduced to a single morning with a photograph, which evidences nothing. Done as a sustained commitment with data it is one of the strongest options available.

subjects.name: The CAS project
subjects.description: A collaborative undertaking of at least one month involving one or more strands, with planning, action and reflection. The piece most likely to fail, usually because the group was chosen for friendship rather than for reliability and nobody owned the schedule.

subjects.name: Dual-strand experiences
subjects.levels: Creativity and service, or activity and service
subjects.description: Coaching a younger team, running a music programme at a community centre, organising a charity sports event. Efficient, because one sustained commitment generates evidence across two strands, and the reflection usually improves because the student has to think about both purposes.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-cas-tutor.regionsTitle: What CAS actually looks like across Abu Dhabi
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-cas-tutor.regionsIntro: CAS is the one part of the diploma that depends on where a family lives, because the experiences are local. These are the areas our enquiries come from and what is realistically available in each.

regions.name: The Corniche and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Coastal clean-up and water-related environmental work is accessible on foot or by a short drive, and community sports facilities are dense. Good for sustained service commitments that do not require a parent to drive across the emirate twice a week.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Proximity to the cultural district makes arts-related creativity and service genuinely workable, including visitor-facing volunteering arranged through a school. The strongest area in the emirate for creativity evidence that is not simply continuing an existing hobby.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Large community centres, sports clubs and compound-level initiatives, plus the biggest pool of younger students to coach or tutor. Dual-strand experiences are easiest to construct here because everything is within a short drive.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Villa and apartment communities with active resident groups, which makes an organised project with a real community audience straightforward. The risk is a project that never leaves the compound and produces thin ethical-implications evidence.

regions.name: Eastern Mangroves and the eastern corniche
regions.note: Mangrove and coastal habitat work is available and genuinely interesting, which makes it attractive for environmental service. It only counts as a commitment if it recurs; a single kayak clean-up with photographs evidences nothing at all.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Shamkha
regions.note: Longer drives to central facilities, so school-brokered placements and school-based projects matter more here. Indirect service and advocacy work often suit these families better than placements requiring twice-weekly travel.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Dense residential population with strong community and sporting networks, and a large number of younger children to coach or tutor. Among the easiest areas in the emirate to build a sustained direct-service commitment.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Significant sports and entertainment infrastructure, which produces plentiful activity options and plentiful one-off event volunteering. The second category is where portfolios go wrong, because events produce certificates rather than commitment evidence.

schoolClusters.city: Schools with structured CAS programmes
schoolClusters.note: Where a school runs its own service partnerships, sports programme and project framework, students generally complete CAS without external help. Families from this cluster who contact us usually need one conversation, not a block of sessions.

schoolClusters.city: Schools where CAS is largely student-led
schoolClusters.note: Where a portfolio template is issued and initiative is expected, the students who stall are those with weak planning habits or a late entry into the programme. This is where the three legitimate cases for mentoring are concentrated.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Newer campuses with CAS practice still forming
schoolClusters.note: Diploma cohorts still growing and coordinator capacity still being established, which can mean inconsistent guidance on what the portfolio should contain. Students here benefit most from learning to read the seven outcomes themselves.

sections.heading: What CAS support should cost, and why the honest answer is usually nothing
paragraphs: Market rates for one-to-one tutoring in the UAE, surveyed in October 2026, run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the university-student end to AED 650 and above for a premium named tutor, with agency start rates around AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts the subject-specialist band at AED 200 to 450 plus and in-home visits at AED 180 to 350. Those are market figures with sources attached, not our prices.

Applied to CAS, almost all of that is irrelevant, because CAS has no content to teach and no marks to recover. What a mentor can usefully do is audit a portfolio against the seven outcomes, build a sustainable structure for a student who cannot hold one, or help rebuild a failed project. Those are one to four hours of work in total, and no student needs all three.

The table below sets out what families in this emirate actually pay for in CAS, what each item should cost, and what the school already provides at no extra charge. Read the last column first. Several of the items most readily sold have a free equivalent sitting in the school office, and one of them cannot be bought legitimately at all.

Our own position is deliberately narrow. One free consultation per family, no card details taken, at the end of which we will often say that the coordinator can cover it and that there is nothing worth buying. That is not modesty: a block of CAS sessions sold to a student whose coordinator would have handled it is the clearest waste of money available in the diploma core.
