sections.heading: Spectroscopy: the Higher Level topic schools run out of time for
paragraphs: Spectroscopic identification is Higher Level content, it is reliably examined, and it is reliably taught in the last weeks available. The pattern is structural rather than anyone's fault: it sits late in the Structure themes, it arrives in DP2 when the investigation and mocks are competing for time, and it looks like a small topic in a contents list. Students consequently meet mass spectrometry, infrared spectroscopy and proton nuclear magnetic resonance once, quickly, and then face a question that asks them to combine all three.

The good news is that it is among the most teachable topics in the course, because it is a procedure rather than a body of knowledge. Spectroscopic questions are solved by elimination in a fixed order, and a student who has internalised the order answers them reliably. Molecular formula and fragmentation evidence first, from the mass spectrum. Functional group next, from characteristic infrared absorptions. Then the carbon skeleton and the position of groups, from the number of proton environments, the chemical shifts and the relative areas in the nuclear magnetic resonance spectrum.

The data booklet carries the reference values, which is the fact students most often fail to use. Characteristic infrared absorption ranges and proton chemical shift ranges are supplied, so these questions are not memory tests; they are reading-and-reasoning tests with the reference table open. Practising with the booklet at hand, under time, converts the topic from frightening to routine in perhaps four sessions.

The marks lost when it goes wrong are concentrated in two places. One is counting proton environments, where students count hydrogens rather than environments and get the wrong number of signals. The other is jumping to a structure from one piece of evidence and then defending it against the rest, rather than letting all three spectra narrow the possibilities. Both are habits of approach, and both are fixable without any additional chemistry.

sections.heading: Energetics, equilibrium and electrochemistry: where HL marks concentrate
paragraphs: If the Higher Level additions were ranked by marks at risk, the quantitative cluster would sit at the top. Energy cycles, entropy and spontaneity, equilibrium constants, weak acid and base calculations with buffers, and electrode potentials with electrolysis arithmetic between them account for a very large share of the Paper 2 marks that separate a 5 from a 7. They also share a single underlying requirement: a student has to be comfortable with signs, logarithms and ratios.

Sign conventions cause more loss here than conceptual misunderstanding. An enthalpy change is negative when energy is released; an entropy change is positive when disorder increases; a Gibbs energy change is negative for a spontaneous process; a cell potential is positive for a feasible reaction. Each of those is simple in isolation and easy to confuse under time pressure, particularly when a question supplies values for two of three quantities and asks for the third. A student who writes the relationship out and substitutes carefully loses nothing; a student who works from memory of which way round it goes loses a mark per question.

Logarithms are the second recurring obstacle, and they are not a chemistry problem. Calculating a pH from a hydrogen ion concentration, going back the other way, handling pKa and Ka, and understanding why a change of one pH unit is a tenfold change in concentration all require logarithm fluency. Students taking Analysis and Approaches usually have it. Students taking Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level often do not, and in that case the logarithm work belongs inside the chemistry sessions rather than being left to a mathematics course that may not reach it.

Equilibrium is the third, and it fails for a conceptual reason that a formula cannot repair. An equilibrium constant is a ratio of concentrations at equilibrium, not a property that behaves like a rate. Students who treat it as a formula to fill in get the arithmetic right and the reasoning questions wrong — which way a system shifts, why a catalyst does not change the constant, why temperature does. Teaching the meaning before the calculation is slower in week one and faster by week six.

sections.heading: Mole discipline: the arithmetic that quietly costs grades
paragraphs: A striking share of Higher Level chemistry mark loss has nothing to do with Higher Level chemistry. It sits in the mole, and in the family of calculations built on it: mass to moles, moles to concentration, gas volumes, limiting reagent, percentage yield, atom economy, titration, and back-titration. A student who can discuss orbital hybridisation and then mis-scales a dilution is losing marks that are entirely recoverable, and recovering them is the cheapest grade movement available in the subject.

The fix is a single method used every time rather than a different improvisation per question. Write what is given with units. Convert to moles. Use the balanced equation's ratio, explicitly. Convert back to what is asked, with units. Students who adopt that four-step layout stop losing marks to the two commonest errors, which are using an unbalanced ratio and dividing where they should have multiplied. The layout also makes partial credit possible, because an examiner can see the method even when the arithmetic slips.

Titration and back-titration deserve separate treatment, because they are where a confused layout does most damage. A back-titration asks a student to find the amount of a substance by reacting it with an excess and then titrating what is left, which involves a subtraction in the middle. Done in a consistent layout it is routine. Done by improvisation it produces an answer that looks plausible and is wrong by exactly the amount of the excess, and the student has no way to notice.

Significant figures and units are the last piece, and they are examined in both papers and again in the investigation. An answer should carry the precision the data justifies, not the precision the calculator offered, and every final answer needs its unit. These are habits, they are boring, and six weeks of strict marking changes them permanently. A tutor who lets them pass because the chemistry was right is training a student to lose marks politely.

sections.heading: The chemistry investigation: choosing something that can actually be measured
paragraphs: The scientific investigation carries 20% of the grade, is marked out of twenty-four across four equally weighted criteria, is limited to 3,000 words, and has around ten hours of class time allocated to it. In chemistry the criterion that decides the mark is usually research design, and it is decided before any measurement happens. A question that cannot be measured quantitatively with school equipment, in the time available, with enough repeats to say anything, has already lost marks that no amount of careful writing recovers.

The investigations that score well in a school laboratory tend to be unglamorous and quantitative. A rate of reaction against concentration or temperature. An enthalpy change by calorimetry. A titration to find the concentration of something in a consumer product. The effect of a variable on the yield of a simple preparation. Each produces a continuous independent variable, a measurable dependent variable, repeatable readings, and enough uncertainty to discuss honestly. Each is also safe enough that a school will actually permit it, which is not a trivial consideration.

Safety and feasibility are where chemistry differs from the other sciences in this assessment. A student may design an elegant investigation that the school cannot approve, or that requires a reagent the laboratory does not stock, or that needs an instrument it does not have. Checking approval and availability before investing in the design is practical advice that saves weeks, and it is the kind of thing a tutor should raise in the first investigation conversation rather than after a proposal has been written.

The limit on tutor involvement is fixed by IB academic honesty rules and should be given to the family in writing before any investigation session. A tutor may discuss whether a question is measurable and safe, point at a criterion and say which descriptor a current version meets, comment on uncertainty treatment and presentation conventions, and ask the questions that make a student notice a gap. A tutor may not supply text, supply data, or return a rewritten report. The student signs an authenticity declaration and the work must be theirs.

sections.heading: From memorising to reasoning: changing a study method mid-course
paragraphs: The hardest part of Chemistry HL for a student arriving from IGCSE is not a topic. It is that the study method which produced a grade 8 at sixteen produces a 4 at seventeen, and nobody tells them that is what has happened. They respond by doing more of what worked: more flashcards, more re-reading, more highlighted notes. Effort rises, the grade does not move, and the student concludes they are no longer good at chemistry. That diagnosis is wrong and it is demoralising, which makes correcting it the first useful thing a tutor does.

The replacement method has three parts and none of them is glamorous. The first is explaining out loud. A student who can state why a property behaves as it does, in sentences, to another person, has understanding that will survive an unfamiliar question. A student who recognises the right answer in a list does not. Twenty minutes of a session spent making the student do the talking is worth more than an hour of a tutor explaining well, and it is uncomfortable for exactly the first three weeks.

The second is working from the model rather than the memory. Almost every Higher Level reasoning question can be answered from a small number of models: electrons are attracted to nuclei and shielded by other electrons, bonds form where electron density can be shared or transferred, systems move towards lower energy and higher disorder, reactions go where electron density meets electron deficiency. A student who returns to those models under pressure can construct an answer. A student who searches memory for a matching fact finds nothing when the question is new.

The third is spacing and retrieval rather than review. Chemistry content from the first term of DP1 is examined eighteen months later, so anything learned and never retrieved is gone. A short weekly return to old material, in the form of questions rather than re-reading, costs ten minutes and is the difference between a syllabus that accumulates and one that leaks. It is also the habit students abandon first when a deadline arrives, and the one worth protecting in a session plan.

sections.heading: Costs, permits and delivery for Abu Dhabi families
paragraphs: Published rates in this market are scarce, so the figures below come from providers that publish their own prices and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost survey. They are market rates from those named sources rather than IB Gram's own fee, and Abu Dhabi tracks Dubai closely, with in-home visits at the upper end because the emirate's distances make an evening of house calls expensive for the tutor.

Higher Level sciences sit at the specialist end of the market, and the reason is supply rather than prestige. A tutor who teaches the current Chemistry guide at Higher Level, is confident with organic mechanisms and the quantitative Reactivity content, and is available in a Gulf evening slot is a small population. Providers that publish a level split price it accordingly. The final term before the May session is when both the price and the availability tighten, which argues for booking a final-term block in the autumn rather than in March.

On the legal position, two bodies do different jobs and the distinction matters. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain and publishes inspection ratings. Individual private tutors fall under the federal private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023; u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page for private tutor licensing lists a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without the permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule, so no figure should be quoted to a parent.

Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff may not provide paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, which should be verified against ADEK's current policy document. Delivery here is stated the same way on every UAE page: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the Emirates, holds no ADEK, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation and claims none, and delivers every UAE lesson one-to-one over live video with screen sharing and a recording.

process.title: Name the content, not the subject
process.description: A message that says Chemistry Higher Level and names the problem — organic mechanisms, energy cycles, equilibrium calculations, spectroscopy — produces a shortlist of people who have taught exactly that. 'Needs chemistry help' produces a generalist.

process.title: Send a marked paper and a calculation
process.description: One marked assessment plus one worked calculation shows whether the losses are conceptual, mechanistic, arithmetic or command-term. Those four have four different plans, and the arithmetic one is the fastest and cheapest to fix.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One 45-minute lesson over live video with the proposed tutor, no card details and no obligation. It runs on a real question from the student's own work and ends with the tutor stating what the first month would target and in what order.

process.title: Check what the student is revising from
process.description: If the material was written for the previous syllabus, the plan starts by replacing it. Topics have moved between themes and the option units are no longer examined, so an old guide sends a student to the wrong content.

process.title: Read the record at week four and week twelve
process.description: Two scheduled checkpoints where a parent looks at the mark log and session notes and decides. A flat log on the areas being attacked, with no explanation, means changing the plan or the tutor rather than extending on faith.

whyPoints.title: Mechanisms taught as reasoning
whyPoints.description: Organic mechanisms are built from where electron density sits and where it is lacking, so a student can handle a substrate they have never seen. Memorised mechanisms fail the moment a question changes the molecule, which is what examiners do.

whyPoints.title: The current guide, properly mapped
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach the three Structure and three Reactivity themes with Higher Level content in the places it actually sits. A student revising from older material over-prepares on deleted topics and under-prepares on Reactivity.

whyPoints.title: The data booklet used as a tool
whyPoints.description: Spectroscopy, constants and reference values are supplied in the examination, so sessions practise finding and choosing rather than memorising. Students who treat the booklet as a safety net have never learned to use it under time pressure.

whyPoints.title: Arithmetic discipline enforced
whyPoints.description: Mole, titration, dilution and logarithm work is drilled into one reliable layout, with significant figures and units marked strictly. These are the cheapest marks in the subject and the ones most often surrendered.

whyPoints.title: Investigation help with a written boundary
whyPoints.description: Support is discussion, criterion feedback and process coaching on the student's own work, including whether a design is measurable and whether a school will approve it. No text and no data are ever supplied.

whyPoints.title: Rates attributed, fees confirmed in writing
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names the provider or survey that published it and the year. IB Gram's own fee follows a free trial lesson and is confirmed in writing rather than advertised as a headline number.

faqs.question: How is IB Chemistry organised now that the core and options have gone?
faqs.answer: Into six themes in two groups. The three Structure themes cover models of the particulate nature of matter, models of bonding and structure, and the classification of matter. The three Reactivity themes cover what drives chemical reactions, how much and how fast and how far a reaction goes, and the mechanisms of chemical change. Higher Level content sits inside those themes rather than in a separate section, and the optional units are no longer examined. Revision material written for the previous arrangement sends a student to topics that have moved or disappeared.

faqs.question: Which Chemistry topics are Higher Level only?
faqs.answer: The Higher Level additions cluster in identifiable places rather than spreading evenly. Energy cycles and entropy and spontaneity are Higher Level work in Reactivity 1. Quantitative treatment of the extent of reaction, including equilibrium constants, is Higher Level in Reactivity 2. Weak acid and buffer calculations, electrode potentials, electrolysis arithmetic and the organic reaction mechanisms are Higher Level in Reactivity 3. Spectroscopic identification and stereoisomerism are Higher Level additions in the Structure themes. Confirm the exact markings in the current subject guide through the school, since the guide is the authoritative document.

faqs.question: My daughter finds organic mechanisms impossible. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Usually, and quite quickly, because the problem is almost always method rather than ability. Students learn mechanisms as pictures and then meet a question with a different substrate, where the memorised picture gives the wrong answer. Teaching them as reasoning fixes it: ask where electron density sits and where it is lacking, label the structure as primary, secondary, tertiary, chiral or aromatic before drawing anything, and start every arrow at a lone pair or pi bond. Students who genuinely adopt that order stop treating nucleophilic substitution and electrophilic addition as separate memory items.

faqs.question: What is in the Chemistry data booklet and is it supplied in the exam?
faqs.answer: It is supplied, with the periodic table, and it carries constants, relationships and reference data including characteristic infrared absorption ranges and proton chemical shift ranges. That changes what the papers test: recall marks are scarce and selection marks are everywhere. The examinable skill becomes choosing the right relationship for the situation and justifying it, under time pressure, with the booklet open. Students who treat it as a safety net rather than a working tool lose marks because they have never practised finding things in it or deciding between two similar entries.

faqs.question: How much mathematics does Chemistry HL actually need?
faqs.answer: More than students expect and less than they fear. The requirements are confident rearrangement, ratio reasoning, unit conversion across prefixes, indices, and logarithms for pH, Ka and pKa work. Nothing requires calculus. A student taking Analysis and Approaches generally has all of it already. A student taking Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level often lacks the logarithm fluency, and in that case the logarithm work belongs inside the chemistry sessions rather than waiting for a mathematics course that may not cover it in the required form.

faqs.question: Why do mole calculations keep going wrong when the chemistry is understood?
faqs.answer: Because the student improvises a different approach each time instead of using one layout. The reliable method has four steps: write what is given with units, convert to moles, apply the balanced equation's ratio explicitly, convert back to what was asked with units. Students who adopt that stop losing marks to the two commonest errors, which are using an unbalanced ratio and dividing where they should multiply. The layout also protects partial credit, because an examiner can see a correct method even when the arithmetic slips.

faqs.question: What is in Paper 1B for Chemistry, and how should it be practised?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries 36% and comes in two parts. Paper 1A is multiple choice. Paper 1B is a set of data-based questions built on experimental material, where candidates process supplied data, handle uncertainties, interpret a graph or a spectrum and reach a conclusion. The two halves reward opposite habits — speed and elimination in 1A, careful recorded processing in 1B — so they are best practised separately rather than as one paper. Strong chemists frequently lose more marks in 1B than they anticipate, because it is a processing test rather than a knowledge test.

faqs.question: Is Chemistry HL required for medicine or pharmacy?
faqs.answer: Chemistry is specified by a large number of medical and pharmacy programmes, frequently at Higher Level, but requirements vary by country and by institution and change between application cycles. The only reliable method is to read the published entry requirements for each specific course on the shortlist, on the university's own admissions pages, in the year of application. Some programmes name chemistry plus one other science; some name chemistry and biology; some specify mathematics as well. Nobody should summarise this for a family, and nobody should suggest tutoring changes a prerequisite.

faqs.question: How should a Higher Level student approach a spectroscopy question?
faqs.answer: By elimination in a fixed order, with the data booklet open. Take the molecular formula and fragmentation evidence from the mass spectrum first. Identify the functional group next from characteristic infrared absorptions. Then establish the carbon skeleton and the position of groups from the number of proton environments, the chemical shifts and the relative areas in the proton nuclear magnetic resonance spectrum. The two commonest errors are counting hydrogens rather than environments, and committing to a structure from one spectrum and then defending it against the other two instead of letting all three narrow the field.

faqs.question: What makes a good chemistry investigation topic at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Something measurable, quantitative, repeatable and permitted. Rate of reaction against concentration or temperature, an enthalpy change by calorimetry, a titration to find the concentration of something in a consumer product, or the effect of a variable on the yield of a simple preparation all score well because each gives a continuous independent variable, a measurable dependent variable, enough repeats to say something, and honest uncertainty to discuss. Check the school will approve the design and stocks the reagents before investing weeks in it, because feasibility is where chemistry differs from the other sciences here.

faqs.question: Does my son need to memorise periodic trends and solubility rules?
faqs.answer: He needs to be able to explain trends, which is different from reciting them. Higher Level questions ask why first ionisation energy behaves as it does across a period, or why atomic radius changes down a group, and those marks are awarded for reasoning about nuclear charge, shielding and electron removal. A memorised trend with no explanation collects nothing. The periodic table is supplied, so the examinable skill is reading a position and reasoning from it. Memorising descriptive lists is the study method that stops working at exactly this point in a chemistry education.

faqs.question: How many weekly sessions do Abu Dhabi Chemistry HL families usually start with?
faqs.answer: One, with a second added in the final term. For a Higher Level science the weekly hour works best as maintenance plus targeted repair: keeping step with school teaching, closing the method gap left by an IGCSE memorisation habit, and keeping the investigation off the critical path. Families who start with two sessions a week in DP1 often find the second one under-used, because the work that moves marks happens between lessons. The exception is a student who is genuinely behind on content, where a short intensive block early is better value than a long thin one.

faqs.question: What does Chemistry HL tuition cost for an Abu Dhabi family?
faqs.answer: Providers that publish rates put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and specialists higher: Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai survey puts IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. In-home visits in that survey are AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors quoted to AED 500, because driving sits inside the hourly rate. Higher Level sciences sit at the specialist end because supply is thin. IB Gram confirms its own fee in writing after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Where does a chemistry tutor's input on the investigation have to stop?
faqs.answer: At anything that produces the work itself. A tutor may discuss whether a research question is measurable, safe and permitted by the school, point at a criterion and say which descriptor a current version meets, comment on uncertainty treatment and presentation conventions, and ask the questions that make a student notice a gap in their own reasoning. A tutor may not supply text, supply data, or return a rewritten report. The student signs an authenticity declaration for the school, and the document has to be theirs throughout. The boundary should be given to the family in writing before the first session.

faqs.question: Will a Higher Level chemistry tutor come to our villa, or is this online only?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, Al Ain or anywhere else in the UAE; a tutor travelling to a family's address is a service available only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard that suits mechanism arrows well, screen sharing of the student's own calculations, and a recording available afterwards. For Higher Level chemistry the trade favours the family: a tutor chosen for mechanisms and quantitative Reactivity rather than for living near Al Raha, with no travel premium inside the rate.

intro.heading: What Standard Level Chemistry actually asks of a student
paragraphs: Standard Level Chemistry is a 150-hour course examined through two written papers and one internal investigation. Paper 1 is worth 36 per cent and arrives in two halves that test different things: multiple-choice items, then a data-based section. Paper 2 is worth 44 per cent and is where structured and extended written answers live. The investigation accounts for the remaining 20 per cent, is marked by the school against published criteria, and is moderated externally on a sample. Almost every decision about where to spend paid hours follows from those three figures.

The course content is organised under two themes, structure and reactivity, with the Standard Level material forming the spine and Higher Level extensions layered on top for students taking the deeper option. That design has a consequence most Abu Dhabi families discover late: a topic is not finished when the class moves on from it, because the same ideas return in a different theme later. Bonding returns inside energetics. Moles return inside every calculation in the course. A gap left open in the first term is not a missing topic; it is a recurring tax on every paper afterwards.

What a Standard Level student struggles with is rarely the chemistry as a body of knowledge. It is the translation step. They know that a reaction releases heat and cannot write it as a sign convention. They understand that a rate depends on collisions and cannot deduce an order from a table of data. They can describe a titration and lose the marks because the question said justify. This is why re-explaining a topic, which is what most well-meaning support does, produces so little movement in a score.

This page is therefore structured around the examination rather than around the service. The sections below work through the components, the layout of the two themes, how the two halves of Paper 1 differ, what Paper 2 rewards, the command terms with their usual tariffs, a topic-to-paper map, the investigation criteria where Standard Level marks are commonly dropped, and the honest limits of what a single session can repair. Where market prices appear they are published bands with their source attributed, not a fee list.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time slots. For this subject that is a practical advantage rather than a compromise: Standard Level chemistry is written and calculated work, produced on a shared screen where the tutor can correct a sign convention or a significant figure as it is written and save the annotated page afterwards. Families in Abu Dhabi who began by searching for a home tutor usually find the scheduling is the part they value most, because a fixed evening slot survives traffic, fixtures and a late school bus.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme

programmes.description: Assessed against four science criteria that weight investigation design, data processing and evaluation heavily. programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 and Edexcel 4CH1 both cover bonding, stoichiometry, acids, rates and organic families, assessed through shorter and more directive questions. Standard Level Paper 2 asks exactly that, which is why strong IGCSE grades do not reliably predict a strong first Diploma report.

Tutors working with these students spend early sessions on command terms rather than content, because the content is largely present and the response style is not. Mark loss concentrates in quantitative accuracy, sign conventions in energetics, order deduction from rate data, and command-term mismatch on the longer written items.

subjects.name: Chemistry

subjects.description: Four themes with a heavier recall load and the same investigation weighting. Students taking Chemistry and Biology at Standard Level frequently schedule both investigations in the same fortnight by accident, which is a planning problem rather than a chemistry one and is easily avoided.

subjects.description: A frequent sixth subject for Standard Level chemists heading to commerce or health-management routes. Its written-response demands are closer to Paper 2 chemistry than students expect, so command-term work done for one subject tends to pay in the other.

sections.heading: The three components, and what each one is really testing
paragraphs: Standard Level Chemistry is assessed by two written papers and one internal investigation, and each of the three rewards a different capability. Treating them as one subject called chemistry is the main reason revision time gets spent badly. A student can be well prepared for the multiple-choice half of Paper 1 and badly prepared for the data-based half sitting in the same booklet, and nothing in a school grade distinguishes the two.

Paper 1 carries 36 per cent of the grade. Its first part is multiple-choice, which rewards breadth of recall and fast elimination. Its second part is data-based and rewards something quite different: reading a table or graph, extracting the relationship and justifying a conclusion. Paper 2 carries 44 per cent and is where structured and extended responses live, with marks allocated against specific markscheme lines rather than general correctness. The investigation carries 20 per cent and is the only component with no clock on it and no second attempt.

The weightings should drive the hours. A student two grades short with ten weeks left should be working on Paper 2 technique and the data-based half of Paper 1, because that is where 60 per cent of the available marks sit in the parts most responsive to short-term work. A DP1 student with the investigation ahead of them is in a different position entirely, since 20 per cent of the final grade can be secured calmly in term time rather than defended under exam pressure. The table below sets out what each component asks and where Standard Level students commonly lose it.

Describing the data instead of explaining it; conclusions stated without reference to the figures given

sections.heading: Two themes, and why a finished topic is never finished
paragraphs: The chemistry guide organises everything under two themes. Structure deals with the nature of matter: particles, bonding, the periodic trends and the models used to describe them. Reactivity deals with what happens and why: energetics, rates, equilibrium, acids and bases, oxidation and reduction, and the organic families. Standard Level content forms the spine of both, and the deeper material is layered onto the same structure for Higher Level students rather than taught as separate units.

The design has a practical implication that catches Abu Dhabi families out every year. Topics are not sealed. Bonding reappears inside energetics when bond enthalpies are used. Moles reappear in every quantitative question in the course, in both themes, until the final paper. Periodic trends reappear in reactivity when oxidation states are assigned. A student who did not consolidate moles in the first term is not missing one topic; they are paying a small tax on nearly every calculation for two years.

This is why the sequence of paid sessions should follow the student rather than the school's scheme of work. If the class is on organic chemistry and the student cannot reliably convert concentration units, the organic lesson will go in and come straight back out, because the questions in that topic are quantitative too. Repairing the foundation first looks like falling further behind for a fortnight and then stops looking like that. Any tutor who agrees to simply follow the class without checking the foundation is agreeing to the comfortable version of the job.

sections.heading: Paper 1A and Paper 1B are two different exams in one booklet
paragraphs: The most common misreading of the Standard Level assessment is treating Paper 1 as a single multiple-choice test. It has two parts and they reward different skills. The multiple-choice section tests recall and elimination across the whole syllabus, with no credit for working and no partial marks. The data-based section gives the student information they have not seen before and asks them to process it, draw a relationship out of it and justify a conclusion in writing.

Students who revise by content list prepare well for the first and not at all for the second, because you cannot revise unfamiliar data. What you can practise is the procedure: read the axes and the units before the question, state the trend in terms of the quantities given, identify the one anomalous point if there is one, then answer the question actually asked. Done repeatedly on past items, that routine is worth several marks to a mid-band student within a few weeks.

The multiple-choice half has its own technique, and it is mostly about the data booklet and about elimination. Students lose marks hunting for a constant they could have located in seconds, or taking a value from the wrong table under time pressure. Others answer every question as a calculation when two of the four options could have been discarded on a units check alone. Neither failing is a chemistry failing, which is why both respond quickly to drilling and why neither is addressed by re-teaching topics.

sections.heading: Paper 2: the forty-four per cent that decides the grade
paragraphs: Paper 2 is the largest single component of the Standard Level grade and the one where the gap between knowing chemistry and scoring in chemistry is widest. Marks are awarded against specific markscheme lines. A student can write a chemically sound paragraph that collects nothing because the markscheme wanted a comparison and received a description, or wanted a justification referencing given data and received a general explanation.

The structured questions reward disciplined working. Units carried through every line, intermediates left unrounded until the final answer, significant figures matched to the data given, and the final conversion actually performed rather than assumed obvious. Experienced markers see the same three losses in Abu Dhabi scripts as everywhere else: a correct method abandoned one step early, an answer quoted to a precision the data cannot support, and a missing unit on an otherwise perfect calculation.

The extended responses reward structure. Three developed points scoring three marks beat one point explained three ways, which is the single most useful thing a student can be told about this paper. Practising that means writing answers under time and then comparing them line by line with the published markscheme, out loud, until the student can predict where the marks were going to be. It is slow work and it moves grades, which is the opposite of how most revision time gets allocated. A student who has never compared one of their own answers with a markscheme line has no idea what the paper is rewarding, however much chemistry they know.

sections.heading: Command terms and what they are worth
paragraphs: Every IB chemistry question is built on a command term, and the term tells the student what kind of answer collects the marks. State wants a short answer with no reasoning. Explain wants a causal chain. Deduce wants a conclusion drawn from information provided in the question. Justify wants a conclusion supported by explicit reference to that information. Compare wants both sides addressed in the same sentence structure. These are not synonyms, and the markscheme does not treat them as such.

Command-term mismatch is the most expensive habit a Standard Level student can carry into Paper 2, because it costs marks on questions where the chemistry was known. It is also one of the most fixable, since the repair is procedural: circle the command term before writing, say what that term requires, then write to it. Most students need three to four weeks of corrected practice before the habit sticks, and the improvement shows on a marked script rather than in how confident they feel.

The table below sets out the terms that appear most often in Standard Level chemistry papers, what the markscheme is looking for, the usual mark tariff and the failure that recurs. It is worth printing and keeping next to the student while they attempt past papers, because the point is not to memorise definitions but to interrupt the reflex of writing everything known about the topic. Students who keep it visible for a fortnight usually stop needing it, which is the sign that the habit has transferred.

sections.heading: Topic to paper: where each Standard Level topic actually gets examined
paragraphs: Revision plans usually run through the syllabus in order, which treats every topic as equally likely to appear in every component. The examinations do not work that way. Some topics turn up overwhelmingly as multiple-choice recall, some are the standard material for data-based questions, and some are the reliable homes of extended written responses. Knowing which is which changes how a topic should be revised, not merely when.

The map below is drawn from the pattern of past papers rather than from the guide's ordering. It is a planning tool, not a prediction: anything in the syllabus can be examined anywhere, and a student should not skip a component for a topic because the map is thin there. What it does is stop a student from preparing a topic in the wrong register, for example learning periodicity as a set of facts when the questions ask them to justify a trend from supplied radii and electronegativity values.

Used properly, the map also exposes where investigation material overlaps with examined material. Students who choose a kinetics or energetics investigation are practising, over several weeks, exactly the data processing that the Paper 1 data-based section rewards. Those who pick an unusual context get less of that spillover. Neither choice is wrong, but a family deciding how to spend limited hours should know which investigation topics are doing double duty. In a term where the budget covers eight sessions rather than twenty, that overlap is the difference between covering one component and covering two.

sections.heading: Where Standard Level students drop investigation marks
paragraphs: The investigation carries the same 20 per cent at Standard Level as at Higher Level, and the published criteria are the same. What differs is scale: a Standard Level student has less taught content to draw on and usually less laboratory time, so the realistic ambition is a well-executed narrow question rather than an original one. The marks are lost in predictable places, and almost all of them are decided before any data are collected.

The first and largest loss is a research question too broad to answer with the data a school laboratory can produce. A question about the factors affecting reaction rate cannot be answered; a question about the effect of a specified concentration range on the rate of one named reaction can. The second loss is uncertainty treated as a closing paragraph rather than as part of the method, so instrument precision is quoted without being propagated into the processed values. The third is an evaluation that lists weaknesses without weighting them, when the criteria reward judging which weakness actually mattered.

A tutor's legitimate role here is teaching the criteria, the uncertainty treatment and the evaluation structure, then giving feedback on the student's own dated drafts in the form of questions. The report stays the student's work from first version to last. Finished investigations are openly sold in this market, and the risk of submitting one falls on the candidate, as a malpractice matter handled by the IB rather than a disagreement with a provider. The school supervisor remains the authority on scope and approval throughout.

sections.heading: What one session can close, and what takes six
paragraphs: It is a fair question and it is rarely answered honestly. Some things genuinely move in a single session. Data-booklet navigation does. A specific calculation procedure, like converting between concentration units or constructing an energy cycle, does. So does the command-term routine, in the sense that a student can learn to identify the term and name what it requires within an hour, although making it automatic under exam pressure takes longer.

Other things do not. A topic a student has never understood takes two or three sessions, because the first produces comprehension, the second produces unassisted recall and the third produces it under time. Quantitative accuracy as a habit takes about a month of corrected practice, since it is a behaviour rather than a piece of knowledge. Extended-response structure on Paper 2 takes four to six weeks because it requires writing, marking and rewriting several times. An investigation needs a block spread across the school's own deadlines and cannot be compressed into a weekend.

The practical consequence for an Abu Dhabi family with a limited budget is to buy in the right order. Procedural fixes first, since they are cheap and show quickly. Then the topic gaps that recur across the syllabus, which is almost always moles and energetics. Then written technique, which is slow and worth the most. Buying in the reverse order is the most common way a family spends a term of fees and ends it with the same grade and the belief that chemistry is simply hard.

sections.heading: Why there is no in-home option, and what replaces it
paragraphs: Parents searching for a home tutor in Abu Dhabi deserve a direct answer rather than a redirection. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. Standard Level chemistry teaching for Abu Dhabi families is delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time slots. The in-home market here is genuine, with published bands of roughly AED 180-350 an hour in the Bestimate 2026 rate survey, and higher where travel is long or the subject is scarce.

What the online format changes is the shortlist. In an in-home arrangement the pool is whoever will travel to Al Shamkha or Al Falah at 17:30 on a Tuesday, which is a small set and not sorted by chemistry. Online, the shortlist is chemists, and a student losing marks on rate order deduction can be matched with someone who marks that question type regularly rather than with a generalist scientist who will prepare the topic the night before.

The second change is the artefact. Standard Level chemistry is written and calculated work, so sessions happen on a shared screen where the sign convention is corrected as it is written and the annotated page is saved. Families who began by searching for home tuition usually end up valuing the scheduling most: a fixed evening slot that survives traffic on the Mussafah road, a late bus from the island, or a change of plan at 16:00. Nothing is promised at your address, because nothing needs to be.

sections.heading: ADEK, the practical scheme of work, and what the laboratory notebook is for
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi are overseen by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes inspection outcomes. That is useful background on a school, and it says nothing about whether your child can deduce a rate order. The documents that matter for chemistry are the ones your school produces: the scheme of work, the practical programme and the internal deadline calendar for the investigation.

Ask for the practical schedule specifically. Standard Level chemistry students are expected to have hands-on laboratory experience across the course, and the practical programme is where investigation skills are built long before the assessed investigation begins. A student who has been passive in the laboratory and attentive in theory lessons tends to produce a weak methodology section, and that is visible months ahead if anyone is looking at the notebook.

Abu Dhabi also has a rule worth knowing before you hire anyone. ADEK's professional-ethics expectations for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and a teacher tutoring privately is required to hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Confirm the current wording with the school or on ADEK's policy pages, and treat an offer from your child's own chemistry teacher with that in mind.

process.title: Name the component, not the subject
process.description: The most useful opening message says which paper the marks were lost on and, if possible, which questions. Chemistry is going badly is a starting point; a mid-band Paper 2 with blank extended responses is a brief. Where a marked script exists, a photograph of one question shortens the diagnosis by an entire session.

process.description: A working session rather than a sales call, with no card details required. The student attempts items across the components and the tutor identifies whether the problem is coverage, procedure, command terms or arithmetic. You are told which of those it looks like and roughly how many sessions each would take to close.

process.title: Scope the block, with an end to it
process.description: Topic repair blocks are scoped to named topics and end when a cold mixed set on those topics scores. Technique work runs weekly because it is a habit change. Investigation support follows the school's internal deadlines. Agreeing the shape before the first paid hour prevents an open-ended arrangement that nobody reviews.

process.title: Fix the weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Sessions are booked at a fixed weekly time chosen around the school run. Families in Al Mushrif and Al Khalidiyah commonly take 16:30; families in Al Shamkha, Al Falah and Mussafah usually need 18:00 or later. During Ramadan most slots move to post-Iftar evenings or weekend mornings without a rescheduling charge.

process.title: Review against the component, not the mood
process.description: Progress is checked against the thing that was wrong. If the diagnosis was command terms, the test is whether marked extended responses now collect the available marks. If it was coverage, the test is a cold set on those topics. A review that asks only whether the student enjoys the sessions is not a review.

whyPoints.description: Sessions are planned from the component weightings and the error pattern rather than from the school's current topic. A student ten weeks out with a weak Paper 2 is working on extended responses even if the class is on organic chemistry, because that is where the available marks are.

whyPoints.description: Answers are compared line by line with published markscheme wording, read aloud, until the student can predict where the marks sit. This is the least popular part of the work and the part that most reliably moves a Standard Level grade on the paper worth 44 per cent.

faqs.question: How is IB Chemistry Standard Level assessed, and what is each paper worth?
faqs.answer: Three components. Paper 1 is 36 per cent and contains a multiple-choice section plus a data-based section, which test different skills despite arriving in one booklet. Paper 2 is 44 per cent and carries structured questions and extended written responses marked against specific markscheme lines. The scientific investigation is 20 per cent, marked internally by the school against published criteria and moderated externally on a sample. Those weightings should drive how paid hours are allocated: Paper 2 holds the largest share of the marks and responds well to technique work.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the two parts of Paper 1 in Standard Level chemistry?
faqs.answer: The multiple-choice section tests breadth of recall and elimination, with no credit for working and no partial marks. The data-based section supplies information the student has not seen before and asks them to process it and justify a conclusion. Students who revise by content list prepare well for the first and not at all for the second, because unfamiliar data cannot be revised. What can be practised is the procedure: axes and units first, trend stated in the given quantities, anomaly identified, then the actual question answered.

faqs.question: Which Standard Level chemistry topics carry the most weight in Paper 2?
faqs.answer: Stoichiometry, energetics, rates and the acid-base and redox material account for the bulk of the structured and extended items, because each one supports multi-step calculation and causal explanation. Organic chemistry appears steadily, usually as pathway and naming questions. Periodicity and bonding surface more often as trend-justification items than as calculations. None of this means a topic can be skipped, but it does mean a student with ten weeks left should not be spending equal time on every heading in the guide.

faqs.question: Our son revises by rereading his notes and still scores 4. What should he do instead?
faqs.answer: Write chemistry under correction. Rereading produces recognition, which feels like knowledge and collapses under an unfamiliar question. The replacement is attempting past-paper items cold, marking them against the published markscheme, and keeping a short list of the errors that recur. For most mid-band Standard Level students the list is short and consistent: command-term mismatch, unrounded intermediates, missing units and conclusions stated without reference to given data. Three to four weeks of corrected written practice changes a marked script more than a term of rereading.

faqs.question: How many marks do command terms cost a Standard Level chemistry student?
faqs.answer: On a typical Paper 2 a student who answers the chemistry rather than the command term loses several marks on questions where the content was known, which is the most frustrating category of loss available. The terms are not synonyms: state wants a word, deduce wants a conclusion from supplied data, explain wants a causal chain, justify wants explicit reference to the evidence, and compare wants both items addressed together. The repair is procedural rather than academic, and it usually takes three to four weeks of corrected practice to become automatic under time.

faqs.question: Is Standard Level chemistry enough for a pharmacy or health-science application?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the university and the country, and the only reliable source is the admissions page of each programme your child is considering. Some health-science and pharmacy routes accept chemistry at Standard Level; many medical and some pharmacy programmes require it at Higher Level. Check before DP1 subject choices are finalised, because a change later is disruptive and sometimes impossible. A tutor can help your child cope with either level, but nobody should advise you to assume a requirement that the university itself states clearly.

faqs.question: Which investigation criterion do Standard Level students lose most marks on?
faqs.answer: The losses cluster at the start and the end. At the start, a research question too broad for a school laboratory to answer caps the mark before any data exist: the effect of concentration on rate is answerable, the factors affecting reaction rate is not. At the end, evaluations list weaknesses without judging which one actually mattered, and uncertainty is quoted rather than propagated into the processed values. Both are planning failures rather than knowledge failures, and both are far cheaper to fix in advance than afterwards.

faqs.question: Does a Standard Level chemistry student need to learn the organic mechanisms?
faqs.answer: The formal curly-arrow mechanism work with lone pairs and formal charges belongs to the Higher Level extension. Standard Level students need the reaction pathways, the functional group transformations, naming and the conditions, which are examined steadily in both papers. A student who has been copying mechanism notation from a Higher Level classmate's notes is spending time on material that will not be rewarded in their paper, and that is worth checking early in the second year rather than late.

faqs.question: Can one session fix a topic my daughter has never understood?
faqs.answer: One session produces comprehension, which is not the same as marks. Expect two or three: the first to understand it, the second to recall it unassisted, the third to produce it under time on an unfamiliar question. Procedural things genuinely do move in one session, including data-booklet navigation, a specific calculation route or the command-term routine. Habits such as quantitative accuracy take about a month of corrected practice, and extended-response structure takes four to six weeks because it requires writing, marking and rewriting several times.

faqs.question: Will a tutor visit our villa in Abu Dhabi for Standard Level chemistry lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. Teaching for Abu Dhabi families is one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time slots. The local in-home market is real and charges roughly AED 180-350 an hour on published 2026 survey bands, with more where travel is long. Online delivery trades the person in the room for a chemistry specialist matched to the question types your child drops, and for a slot that traffic cannot cancel.

faqs.question: What does Standard Level chemistry leave out that Higher Level includes?
faqs.answer: The main omissions are entropy and Gibbs energy, electrode potentials and electrochemical cell calculations, buffer and pH-curve work, and a substantially extended organic section including mechanism notation and stereochemistry. The two themes and the investigation requirement are shared. Knowing the boundary matters for two reasons: a Standard Level student should not be revising Higher Level extension material, and a student considering moving up should understand that the added content is mathematical in character rather than simply more of the same.

faqs.question: How do school practical lessons connect to the written papers?
faqs.answer: More directly than most students realise. The data-based section of Paper 1 and the quantitative parts of Paper 2 both test exactly what a careful practical programme builds: reading instruments to their precision, recording units, noticing anomalies and explaining a trend from numbers. A student who is passive in the laboratory and attentive in theory lessons tends to produce weak methodology in the investigation and loses marks on data questions in the papers. Asking to see the practical schedule and the laboratory notebook is worth doing well before the investigation begins.

faqs.question: Is it worth moving from Chemistry Standard Level to another science in DP1?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the decision should be made on where the marks are being lost rather than on how the subject feels. A student losing marks to arithmetic and units will lose them in physics too, so the move solves nothing. A student who finds the quantitative load genuinely unmanageable may do better in a more descriptive science or in environmental systems and societies. Check the university requirements first, then speak to the school, since the transfer window and the catch-up involved are both set by them rather than by a tutor.

faqs.question: How much does Standard Level chemistry tuition cost per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market bands put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150-300 an hour and IB specialists higher, while in-home one-to-one sits at about AED 180-350 on the Bestimate 2026 survey, rising for scarce subjects. Unitors advertises IB tuition from AED 200 and TutorChase publishes AED 270 for its specialist tier. Those are other providers' published figures, quoted as market context rather than as our price. Ask what the hour includes, because marked work, written notes and draft feedback are often billed separately.

faqs.question: What happens if the class has moved on and my daughter has not?
faqs.answer: This is the most common reason Abu Dhabi families start paying, and the answer is to repair the foundation before chasing the class. If moles and unit conversion are shaky, lessons on the current topic will not hold, because the current topic is quantitative too. That means two or three sessions that look like falling further behind, followed by faster progress than before. A tutor who simply follows the class each week without checking the foundation has chosen the comfortable version of the job rather than the useful one.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-chemistry-sl-home-tutor.closingHeading: Work out which component is losing the marks first
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-chemistry-sl-home-tutor.closingBody: Before booking a term of chemistry sessions, find out what is actually wrong. Send the last paper your child sat, or a photograph of one question from it, and say which grade it produced. The free 45-minute diagnostic session identifies whether the problem is coverage, procedure, command terms or arithmetic, and says roughly how many sessions each of those would take to close. No card details are needed to book it. If the answer turns out to be two topics and a habit rather than a subject, you will have saved most of the budget you were about to commit.

intro.heading: Chemistry SL goes wrong quietly, which is why it needs a record
paragraphs: A Chemistry Standard Level grade rarely collapses. It drifts. A 6 in the first DP1 assessment becomes a 5 at the end of the year and a 4 in the January mock, and at no point is there a single event a family can point at. School reports describe effort and participation honestly and usefully, but they are not designed to tell a parent that eleven marks on the last paper went to unit conversion and command terms rather than to chemistry. Without that information, a family cannot tell whether the problem is serious or trivial.

This page is built around fixing that specific gap. Everything a tutor does with a Standard Level chemistry student here produces a document: a script from the student's own school assessment re-marked with every lost mark attributed to a cause, a running mark log organised by theme, a dated version history of the scientific investigation, and a two-line note after each session saying what was worked on and what comes next. A parent should never have to ask whether tutoring is working. They should be able to open a folder and read the answer.

That approach suits Standard Level chemistry particularly well, because the subject's recoverable marks are unusually visible once someone looks for them. Standard Level is 150 teaching hours across three Structure themes and three Reactivity themes, without the Higher Level content. A great deal of what separates a 4 from a 6 is not chemistry knowledge at all: it is mole arithmetic done without a consistent layout, answers given to a precision the data does not support, questions answered at the wrong length for their command term, and graphs read correctly then described wrongly.

Those four things are diagnosable from one marked script, and they are fixable in weeks rather than terms. Which is why the first month of any sensible arrangement is diagnostic rather than instructional: find out where the marks are going, sort the losses into unlearned content on one side and habit on the other, and attack the habit side first because it returns more marks per hour of a student's time.

Abu Dhabi contributes its usual constraint, which is timing rather than distance. Students here come home from school across the island and the mainland corridor at different times, and a Standard Level chemistry session needs a student with concentration left. Because lessons run over live video, the family in Al Reef and the family in Al Mushrif can hold the same weekly slot with the same tutor. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; a tutor travelling to a family's address is a service available only in India.

What follows is the detail: what sits in the evidence file and what each part is for, which content Standard Level students should stop revising, how a baseline diagnosis is built, what movement looks like week by week, the three mark clusters worth attacking first, how the investigation's version history protects both the student and the family, how to read a mock result, and what a parent should refuse to accept from anybody selling tutoring.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher and three Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Chemistry at Standard Level runs 150 teaching hours and is assessed by Paper 1 at 36%, in a multiple-choice part and a data-based part, Paper 2 at 44%, and the scientific investigation at 20%, with a data booklet supplied in the examinations.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi cohorts the Standard Level chemistry set often contains students who moved down from Higher Level during DP1. Those students carry a particular evidence problem: their old marked work was against a harder syllabus, so a mark log has to be restarted rather than continued, or the trend line is meaningless.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Integrated sciences assessed against four criteria rather than by percentage. The criterion reports are more informative than a percentage would have been, because they separate knowledge from inquiry from processing, which is exactly the separation a Diploma diagnosis needs.
programmes.countryNote: Where an Abu Dhabi student has come through the same school's MYP, five years of criterion reports sit in the parent portal unread. They usually predict the Diploma difficulty accurately: weak processing and evaluating in MYP tends to become weak data handling in the Diploma, and it is visible years earlier.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 and Pearson International GCSE 4CH1 are the usual routes in. Both cover particles, bonding, the periodic table, acids and bases, rates and introductory organic chemistry, and both reward a memorisation study method that the Diploma then stops rewarding.
programmes.countryNote: An IGCSE transcript is useful evidence for a different reason than families assume. A strong grade achieved by memorising predicts a Standard Level chemistry drift in DP1, because the method does not transfer. Knowing that in September rather than January is worth a term.

programmes.name: Course certificates and the Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Some Abu Dhabi schools offer individual course certificates or the Career-related Programme alongside the full Diploma. A student can sit Chemistry SL within either, with identical papers and an identical investigation, but with a different surrounding workload.
programmes.countryNote: Where there is no Extended Essay competing for DP2 weeks, the investigation can and should be finished early. That single scheduling decision removes the commonest cause of a lost revision term, and it shows up in the evidence file as a completed report in the autumn rather than a draft in February.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-chemistry-sl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Abu Dhabi families often book two or three Diploma subjects at once, and the evidence approach works the same way in each. These are the courses most frequently requested alongside Chemistry SL.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Three Structure and three Reactivity themes, assessed by Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and one scientific investigation at 20%. Standard Level omits the Higher Level content, which concentrates in energy cycles, entropy, quantitative equilibrium, weak acids, electrochemistry and organic mechanisms.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Four organising themes plus the investigation. The most common partner for Chemistry SL in Abu Dhabi, and the pairing that most often puts two internal assessments into the same DP2 term, which a shared calendar prevents and an unshared one does not.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes with Higher Level extensions. Shares the uncertainty, significant-figure and graph conventions with chemistry, so a single data-handling block visibly moves the mark log in both subjects at once.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling with technology assumed. The usual mathematics pairing for a Standard Level chemistry student, and the reason rearrangement and index work sometimes has to be built inside the chemistry hour.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra and calculus, with one paper sat without a calculator. Students in AA generally find the mole and concentration arithmetic routine, which means the chemistry sessions can stay on chemistry.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Anatomy, physiology, energy systems and training, plus an investigation. A common Group 4 companion for Abu Dhabi students aiming at physiotherapy, and it reuses the metabolic chemistry content directly.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisation, human resources, finance, marketing and operations. A frequent Diploma companion for students taking chemistry to keep a science route open rather than because it is the plan.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches with research methods throughout. Shares chemistry's demand for precise use of evidence, and the research-methods content rewards the same data literacy.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary course satisfying either Group 3 or Group 4. Students weighing a lighter science route against Chemistry SL compare these two most often, and the honest comparison is about assessment style.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay. Chemistry gives a student usable knowledge questions about models known to be simplifications and about what counts as evidence in a laboratory.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-chemistry-sl-tutor.regionsTitle: Abu Dhabi communities and the slot a Standard Level session can actually use
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-chemistry-sl-tutor.regionsIntro: The evidence file shows something families rarely expect: sessions booked too early in the afternoon produce less movement in the mark log than sessions booked an hour later. Attention is the variable, and in this emirate attention is decided by the school run.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Buses from island and corridor schools arrive between about 3.15pm and 4pm. Mark logs from 5pm slots in this community consistently move faster than those from 4pm slots, which is an argument for the later booking rather than a preference.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Tower housing behind a single causeway, with an unpredictable afternoon. Evening online slots are the standard pattern here, and their consistency is what makes a weekly record possible at all.

regions.name: Al Mushrif
regions.note: Minutes from several established island schools, with students frequently home by 3.30pm. One of the few Abu Dhabi communities where a 4pm session genuinely works, and therefore the easiest hour of the week to secure.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Villa living inside the mainland school corridor. Families here commonly run two siblings in consecutive slots, and the shared calendar is what stops two internal assessments landing in the same fortnight.

regions.name: Al Reef
regions.note: A peripheral community with a long bus run and almost no local Diploma-level science provision. Sessions start at 6pm or later, and the realistic local alternative is a general tutor rather than a chemistry specialist.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Long internal distances and a well-known Diploma cohort. Evening slots dominate, and requests from this area are most often about the investigation timeline rather than about content.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: A large mainland community with a long, variable commute. Consistency of timing matters most here, because a moved session usually becomes a missing week in the record rather than a rescheduled one.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Under the same regulator as the capital, with its own international schools and very few resident chemistry specialists. Remote delivery is the practical default, and it makes a weekly written record easier to keep than a travelling arrangement ever did.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi island and Saadiyat
schoolClusters.note: The island's established private schools and the Saadiyat campuses hold a large share of the emirate's Diploma science entries. Reporting cycles differ between them, which matters for a mark log: the baseline has to come from the student's own assessments, not from a comparison across schools.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City and the Al Raha corridor
schoolClusters.note: The mainland corridor carries the emirate's densest group of international schools, and most Standard Level chemistry enquiries come from here. Internal assessment deadlines vary by school, so the first session's job is to write those dates down.

schoolClusters.city: Al Ain and the outer emirate
schoolClusters.note: Al Ain falls under the same regulator as Abu Dhabi city and runs its own IB and British-curriculum schools. With almost no local specialist supply, families there rely on a written record more heavily, because there is no informal network to check a tutor against.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-chemistry-sl-tutor.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named only as context for the Abu Dhabi schooling environment families ask about. No affiliation, endorsement or commercial relationship with any school is implied, and current subject offerings should be verified on ADEK's own school listing.
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-chemistry-sl-tutor.modesIntro: Three arrangements cover almost every Standard Level chemistry request. All run over live video, none involves travel to a UAE address, and each produces the same written record; what differs is how long the record runs for.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one with a running record
modes.description: The default: a fixed slot through DP1 and DP2 with work marked between sessions, a mark log by theme, and a short note after each hour. The record is the point. It makes the four-week and twelve-week reviews real decisions rather than conversations, and it gives a student something to look at other than a grade.
bullets: A fixed weekly slot held for the same student
Marked work returned between sessions rather than read aloud in them
A mark log by theme and by cause of loss
A two-line written note after every session

modes.title: A four-week diagnostic block
modes.description: For families who want the diagnosis before committing to a term. Four sessions, in which old scripts are re-marked, a baseline log is built from the student's own school work, the three biggest mark clusters are identified, and the investigation position is assessed. It ends with a written document whether or not anything else is booked.
bullets: Old assessments re-marked against published command terms
A ranked list of topics by marks lost, not by syllabus order
An honest read on the investigation timeline
A written diagnosis that belongs to the family either way

modes.title: An investigation support block
modes.description: A short series timed to the school's own internal deadlines rather than to the examination, covering whether a research question is measurable, safe and permitted, and giving criterion feedback on the student's own drafts. Each draft is dated and kept, which protects the student if authenticity is ever questioned.
bullets: Design checked before laboratory time is committed
Criterion-by-criterion feedback with a mark estimate
Dated draft history retained by the student
The academic-honesty boundary given to the family in writing

sections.heading: What the evidence file contains, and what each part is for
paragraphs: The file has four parts and none of them is elaborate. The first is a mark log: a simple table of every assessed piece of work with its date, its mark, and the theme it covered. It exists so that a trend can be seen rather than inferred, and so that a parent reading it in January can tell whether the December mock was an outlier or a pattern. Baselines come from the student's own school assessments, not from an entry test designed to flatter.

The second part is re-marked scripts. A tutor takes the student's own assessment and marks it again, with every lost mark attributed to one of four causes: content not learned, arithmetic or unit error, command-term mismatch, or data and graph interpretation. The attribution is the useful bit. A total of 28 out of 45 tells a family almost nothing; the same script showing nine marks lost to units and command terms tells them the problem is weeks away from being fixed rather than years.

The third is the investigation version history. Every draft the student produces is dated and kept, along with the feedback given on it. That serves two purposes: it shows a parent the work developing rather than appearing, and it provides a record of what help was given, which matters if a school ever asks about authenticity. A student who can show six dated drafts with comments about criteria is in a very strong position.

The fourth is the session note, which is two lines written after every hour: what was worked on, and what the next session will fix. It is the cheapest part of the file and the one that most reliably exposes a drifting arrangement. Four consecutive notes saying 'revision of Reactivity 2' mean nobody has a plan, and a parent reading them will see that long before a report card confirms it.
bullets: A mark log by date, mark and theme, baselined on the student's own work
Re-marked scripts with every lost mark attributed to a cause
A dated investigation draft history, kept by the student

sections.heading: The Standard Level boundary: content to stop revising
paragraphs: The first entry in many evidence files is a deletion. Standard Level chemistry students regularly revise Higher Level content, because it appears in videos, in second-hand books and in notes shared by friends who sit the harder course. Every hour spent there is an hour that cannot be examined, and over a term it adds up to a meaningful amount of a student's finite revision time.

The Higher Level content sits inside the same six themes, which is why it is easy to encounter by accident. Energy cycles and entropy and spontaneity in Reactivity 1 are Higher Level. Quantitative treatment of the extent of reaction, including equilibrium constants, is Higher Level in Reactivity 2. Weak acid and buffer calculations, electrode potentials, electrolysis arithmetic and the organic reaction mechanisms are Higher Level in Reactivity 3. Spectroscopic identification and stereoisomerism are Higher Level additions in the Structure themes.

A Standard Level student still meets the ideas in a qualitative form in several of those places, which is where the confusion comes from. Standard Level chemistry covers enthalpy change and its measurement, rate of reaction and the factors that affect it, the position of equilibrium and how it responds to change, and acids and bases including pH as a scale. What it does not require is the quantitative machinery: no equilibrium constant calculations, no buffer arithmetic, no Born-Haber style cycles, no mechanism diagrams with curly arrows.

The practical step is to confirm the Higher Level markings in the current subject guide through the school and then physically remove those chapters from the revision plan. Students find this hard to do, because deleting material feels like cutting corners. Framing it as reallocating hours to examinable content usually helps, and the mark log makes the benefit visible within a month.
