sections.heading: Building the baseline in the first four weeks
paragraphs: The first four sessions produce a diagnosis, not progress, and saying so in advance prevents a specific disappointment. A family that expects a grade to move in week three will conclude the arrangement has failed; a family that expects a written diagnosis in week four can judge it fairly. The diagnosis is the thing being paid for in the first month, and it should be good enough to be useful even if nothing else is ever booked.

It is built from the student's own material. Two school assessments, a mock if one exists, any returned laboratory work, and whatever exists of the investigation. A tutor re-marks a selection against the published command terms and the mark scheme conventions rather than for general correctness, because the gap between what a student knows and what they score is usually sitting in the wording. Then the losses are attributed, counted and ranked.

The ranking is where the plan comes from, and it is ranked by marks per hour of work rather than by syllabus order. Unit and mole errors come first because they are numerous and quick. Command-term mismatches come second for the same reason. Data and graph interpretation comes third. Unlearned content comes last, not because it matters least but because it takes longest, and a student who has gained eight marks of confidence from the quick wins learns the hard content better than one who started with it.

By the end of week four the file should contain a baseline log with at least two or three honest figures, three or four re-marked scripts, a ranked topic list, a note on the investigation position relative to the school's deadlines, and a plan for the next eight weeks. If a tutor cannot produce that, the right response is to stop rather than to continue and hope, and a family should say so at the outset so the expectation is mutual.

sections.heading: What movement looks like, week by week
paragraphs: Progress in Standard Level chemistry is not smooth and does not need to be. It arrives in distinct phases with different shapes, and knowing the shape in advance is what stops a family panicking in week seven or relaxing too early in week five. The phases are predictable enough to put in a table, and the table is the most useful single thing in the file during DP1.

The first phase, roughly weeks one to four, shows no movement in the mark log at all and should not. It fills with diagnosis. The second phase, weeks five to ten, usually shows a quick gain as unit, mole and command-term losses are closed, and that gain can look dramatic: five to ten marks on a paper recovered without learning any new chemistry. Families sometimes over-read this as a transformation. It is the easy marks arriving, and it stops.

The third phase, roughly weeks eleven to twenty, is the flat one, and it is where arrangements get abandoned unnecessarily. The quick wins are banked, the remaining losses are content and reasoning, and content moves slowly. A log that plateaus here with session notes showing specific themes being worked through is functioning normally. A log that plateaus here with session notes saying 'general revision' is not, and that is the distinction the record exists to make visible.

The fourth phase is DP2, where the log changes character. Topic exercises are replaced by timed full papers, the investigation closes, and the numbers become noisier because a full paper tests everything at once. The useful read in this phase is the breakdown rather than the total: whether the marks lost are still clustered where they were in October, and whether the clusters are shrinking. A family looking at that table in February can make a genuine decision about the final term.

sections.heading: The three mark clusters worth attacking first
paragraphs: Across Standard Level chemistry scripts the recoverable losses concentrate in three places, and a tutor who attacks them in order produces visible movement in the log inside six weeks. The first is the mole and its family: mass to moles, concentration and dilution, gas volumes, limiting reagent, percentage yield and titration. The errors are rarely conceptual. They are an unbalanced ratio used without checking, a division where a multiplication was needed, a volume left in cubic centimetres, or a molar mass taken without the water of crystallisation.

The repair is a single layout used every time: write what is given with units, convert to moles, apply the balanced equation's ratio explicitly, convert back to what the question asked with units. Students resist this because it feels slower, and it is slower for about two weeks. Then it is faster and more accurate, and it protects partial credit because an examiner can follow a correct method through a slipped calculation.

The second cluster is command-term mismatch. 'State' wants one line. 'Outline' wants a brief account. 'Explain' wants reasons, and the mark scheme awards each link in the chain, so a correct one-line answer to a three-mark 'explain' collects one mark. 'Deduce' wants a conclusion from given information. 'Compare' wants both sides addressed explicitly. There are not many of these terms, they are published, and matching answer length to term is mechanical. It is also worth several marks a paper and almost never practised.

The third cluster is data and graph work, which appears in Paper 1B, in Paper 2 and again in the investigation. Reading a value from a graph, finding a gradient and saying what it physically represents with units, deciding on an appropriate number of significant figures from the raw data, and spotting an anomalous result and saying what to do about it are all examined. Students get the number and lose the sentence. Practising the sentence is the fix, and it transfers straight into the investigation's data analysis criterion.

sections.heading: The investigation, and why the draft history matters twice
paragraphs: The scientific investigation carries 20% of the Standard Level grade, is marked out of twenty-four across four equally weighted criteria, is limited to 3,000 words, and has around ten hours of class time allocated. In the evidence approach it is treated as a sequence of dated drafts rather than as a single deliverable, and that choice does two separate jobs.

The first job is quality. Research design is the criterion that decides most chemistry investigation marks, and it is decided before measurement begins. A dated first version containing only a research question, the independent and dependent variables, the controlled variables and a proposed method lets a tutor say whether the question is measurable, whether the school is likely to approve it, and whether the reagents and equipment exist, while there is still time to change it. Students who skip this stage lose design marks that no later writing recovers.

The second job is protection. A student who can produce six dated drafts, each with a record of the feedback received, is in a strong position if a school ever asks how the work developed. A student who submits a polished report with no history is not accused of anything, but has nothing to show either. The boundary on help should be given to the family in writing at the start: a tutor may discuss whether a question is measurable and safe, point at a criterion and say which descriptor a version meets, comment on uncertainty treatment and presentation conventions, and ask questions that expose a gap. A tutor may not supply text or data, and may not return a rewritten report.

The timing advice is unglamorous and worth repeating. Finish the investigation early. A report still in progress in the final term consumes revision weeks that cannot be replaced, and it does so at exactly the point where the mark log needs timed papers rather than laboratory work. Families who book an investigation block in DP2 autumn almost never need a crisis block in spring.

sections.heading: Reading a mock result without over-reacting to it
paragraphs: A DP2 mock grade is the moment most families decide something, and it is the moment they are most likely to decide the wrong thing. A single mock is one data point, sat under unfamiliar conditions, often covering content taught unevenly, and marked to a boundary a school has chosen rather than one the IB has published. Treating it as a prediction is a mistake in both directions: a good mock can produce complacency, and a bad one can produce a panic that costs a term of sensible work.

The useful output of a mock is the breakdown, and it is usually available for the asking. Which themes lost marks. How many marks went to arithmetic, units and command terms rather than to chemistry. Whether the paper was finished. Whether the data-based questions were stronger or weaker than the recall ones. That information is a plan; the grade on the front is a mood. A tutor should be able to produce the breakdown from the script within one session, and it should go into the file next to the log.

Where a mock does carry real signal is in clock management and in stamina, because those are the two things a short assessment cannot test. A student who ran out of time has a fixable, mechanical problem and should sit two more timed papers before anyone discusses content. A student who finished comfortably and lost marks evenly across the paper has a content problem, and the plan should look completely different.

The comparison that actually matters is the mock against the student's own earlier log, not against the cohort or against a target. A student who has gone from losing eleven marks on units and command terms to losing four, while total marks rose only slightly because new content was examined, is progressing well and looks stalled on a grade. Only the file shows that, which is the entire argument for keeping one.

sections.heading: What a parent should refuse to accept
paragraphs: Because this page argues for evidence, it should also be specific about what counts as the absence of it. Four claims are worth refusing outright, from any tutoring service in this market including this one, and a family that holds that line will avoid most of the ways tutoring money gets wasted in the UAE.

The first is a promised outcome. No tutor can promise a 6, a specific mark gain or a university place, because the examination is marked by the IB and the work is done by the student. Anyone promising one is either describing a refund policy they should publish in full on the same page or making a claim they cannot honour. The second is a statistic without its arithmetic: a satisfaction percentage, an average score gain or a proportion of students achieving something, quoted without the number of students, the dates and the method. Those numbers are unverifiable by design.

The third is a regulatory claim. No tutoring service should describe itself as approved, accredited or licensed by ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson unless it holds that specific permit and can show the number. A KHDA educational services permit is a particular thing issued to training institutes with premises; a MoHRE private tuition work permit belongs to an individual tutor. Neither makes an agency accredited by a board. IB Gram holds no such accreditation and claims none.

The fourth is an offer to produce assessed work. Any service that will supply a finished investigation, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay is selling a student an academic honesty investigation with a report attached. A tutor teaches, discusses, gives criterion feedback and coaches process. Everything submitted must be the student's own, and a service that blurs that line is not a cheaper option; it is a different and much worse product.

No statistic without its n, its date and its method
No claim of approval or accreditation from a regulator or an examination board
No offer to supply a finished investigation, essay or coursework

sections.heading: Costs, permits and delivery in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Market figures here come from providers that publish their own prices and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost survey, and they describe the market rather than IB Gram's fee. Qualified online subject tutors run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour: Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and Bestimate puts IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. In-home visits in the same survey sit at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors quoted to AED 500, because the driving is inside the rate.

Standard Level generally sits below Higher Level across providers that publish a split, which makes the arithmetic a family should do straightforward. Four to six sessions aimed at mole arithmetic and command terms will usually move a Standard Level grade further than twenty sessions of additional content, and will cost a fraction as much. That is the practical value of a diagnosis: it tells a family which of those two things to buy.

On the legal position, two bodies do different jobs. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain and publishes inspection ratings. Individual tutors fall under the federal private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023; u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years to applicants including registered school teachers, public and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule, so no figure should be quoted to a parent.

Delivery is stated the same way on every UAE page here. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, Al Ain or anywhere in the Emirates; a tutor travelling to a family's address is an India-only service. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video with screen sharing and a recording, which has one incidental advantage for the approach on this page: the written record is easier to keep, share and read when every piece of work is already a file rather than a page in a bag.

process.title: Send the last two marked assessments
process.description: Not a description of the problem — the scripts. A re-marked script is the only thing that distinguishes a chemistry gap from an arithmetic habit, and the two have completely different timelines and completely different costs to fix.

process.title: Say what the school's next three deadlines are
process.description: Internal assessment dates, mock windows and reporting dates. A plan built against the school's calendar works; a plan built against a generic two-year timeline collides with the school's and loses.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One 45-minute lesson over live video with the proposed tutor, no card details and no obligation. It runs on a real question from the student's own work and ends with a first read on where the marks are going.

process.title: Agree that week four produces a document
process.description: A written diagnosis: baseline log, re-marked scripts, a ranked topic list, and the investigation position. Agreeing this at the start makes the four-week review a decision rather than a conversation about feelings.

process.title: Review the file, not the impression, at week twelve
process.description: Read the log and the session notes together. A plateau with specific themes named is normal; a plateau with notes saying 'general revision' is a drifting arrangement, and the right response is to change it.

whyPoints.title: A record a parent can read without help
whyPoints.description: A mark log, re-marked scripts, dated investigation drafts and a two-line note per session. Nothing in the file needs interpreting by the person who wrote it, which is the whole point of keeping it.

whyPoints.title: Losses attributed to a cause
whyPoints.description: Every lost mark is sorted into content, arithmetic, command term or data interpretation. A total tells a family nothing; an attribution tells them whether the fix is four weeks or two terms, and what it will cost.

whyPoints.title: The Standard Level boundary enforced
whyPoints.description: Higher Level chemistry is removed from the revision plan explicitly, so no evening goes on equilibrium constants, buffers, electrode arithmetic or mechanism diagrams that cannot be examined at this level.

whyPoints.title: An honest account of the flat phase
whyPoints.description: The gain from habit losses closing arrives early and then stops. Families are told that in advance, so the normal plateau at weeks eleven to twenty is not mistaken for failure and a working arrangement is not abandoned.

whyPoints.title: Investigation drafts dated and kept
whyPoints.description: A version history improves the work and protects the student, because a dated sequence of drafts with recorded feedback shows how a report developed. No text and no data are ever supplied by a tutor.

whyPoints.title: Claims a family should refuse, named
whyPoints.description: No promised grades, no statistics without n and method, no regulator accreditation, no offer to produce assessed work, and every AED figure attributed to the source that published it.

faqs.question: What should a Chemistry SL parent be able to read after four weeks?
faqs.answer: Four things. A baseline mark log with two or three honest figures taken from the student's own school assessments rather than from an entry test. Three or four re-marked scripts with every lost mark attributed to content, arithmetic, command term or data interpretation. A topic list ranked by marks lost rather than by syllabus order. And a note on where the investigation stands relative to the school's own deadlines. Agreeing in advance that week four produces that document turns the first review into a decision rather than a conversation about whether everyone feels positive.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topics should a Standard Level student stop revising?
faqs.answer: The Higher Level content inside the same themes, which is easy to meet by accident in videos and shared notes. That means energy cycles and entropy and spontaneity, quantitative equilibrium constant work, weak acid and buffer calculations, electrode potentials and electrolysis arithmetic, organic mechanisms with curly arrows, stereoisomerism, and spectroscopic identification by mass spectrometry, infrared and proton NMR. Standard Level still meets several of those ideas qualitatively, which is where the confusion comes from. Confirm the markings in the current subject guide through the school and then remove those chapters from the plan.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a 4 is a content problem or a technique problem?
faqs.answer: From a marked script rather than from a grade. If the setup is right, the correct approach was chosen, and the error appears in the arithmetic, the units, the rounding or the length of the answer, it is technique and it moves in four to six weeks of strict marking. If questions were left blank, or the student could not say what was being asked, it is content and it takes a term or more. The two produce identical grades and need completely different plans, which is why no tutor should quote a session count before seeing the work.

faqs.question: Does the Standard Level investigation carry fewer marks than the Higher Level one?
faqs.answer: No, and this surprises most families. The scientific investigation is worth 20% of the grade at both levels, is marked out of twenty-four across four criteria of six marks each — research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation — is limited to 3,000 words, and has around ten hours of class time allocated at both levels. Proportionally that makes it a larger opportunity for a Standard Level student, particularly one who finds examinations difficult, because it is the one component where time and care rather than speed under pressure determine the mark.

faqs.question: How should we use the DP2 mock chemistry result?
faqs.answer: As a breakdown, not a grade. Ask for the script and look at which themes lost marks, how many marks went to arithmetic, units and command terms rather than to chemistry, whether the paper was finished, and whether the data-based questions were stronger than the recall ones. A student who ran out of time has a mechanical problem fixable with two more timed papers. A student who finished and lost marks evenly has a content problem needing a different plan. The number on the front is a mood; the breakdown is a plan.

faqs.question: Is Chemistry SL enough for a biology, nursing or nutrition degree?
faqs.answer: Frequently yes, but the requirement is set by each programme and has to be read on that university's own admissions pages in the year of application. Many life-science, nursing and allied-health courses ask for a science at Standard Level or for biology specifically, with chemistry desirable rather than required. Others name chemistry at Higher Level, particularly in medicine, pharmacy and some biochemistry routes. Two courses at the same institution can differ. Nobody should summarise this for a family, and nobody should suggest that tutoring changes a published prerequisite.

faqs.question: What does a re-marked script show that a school report does not?
faqs.answer: Where the marks went, and why. A report describes effort, participation and attainment honestly and is not designed to tell a parent that eleven marks on the last paper were lost to unit conversion and answer length rather than to chemistry. A re-marked script attributes every lost mark to a cause, which converts an anxious conversation into an arithmetic one: nine marks of habit is a six-week problem, nine marks of unlearned content is a two-term problem, and the family can decide what to spend on which.

faqs.question: How long before the grade actually moves?
faqs.answer: Expect no movement in the first four weeks, because that period is diagnosis. A visible gain usually arrives between weeks five and ten as unit, mole and command-term losses close, and it can be five to ten marks on a paper without any new chemistry being learned. Then a plateau from roughly week eleven to week twenty, because the remaining losses are content and content moves slowly. A family told this in advance does not abandon a working arrangement during the flat phase, which is when most arrangements are abandoned.

faqs.question: My son understands it in the lesson and has forgotten it by the test. Why?
faqs.answer: Because understanding in the presence of an explanation is not the same as retrieving without one, and because chemistry taught in the first term of DP1 is examined eighteen months later. The remedy is retrieval rather than review: short weekly returns to older material in question form, with the notes closed. Ten minutes a week is enough, and it is the first habit students drop when a deadline arrives. In a session, the practical version is making the student do the talking, which is uncomfortable for about three weeks and then works.

faqs.question: Should we book two sessions a week in DP1 for Chemistry SL?
faqs.answer: Usually not. One well-used hour closes the habit clusters, keeps pace with school teaching and keeps the investigation off the critical path, and the work that actually moves marks happens between sessions rather than inside them. A second weekly hour in DP1 often goes under-used, because the student has not had time to attempt the work the hour would be built on. The exception is a student genuinely behind on content, where a short intensive block early is better value than a long thin arrangement across a year.

faqs.question: What claims should I refuse to believe from a tutoring service?
faqs.answer: Four. A promised grade, mark gain or university place, because the IB marks the examination and the student does the work. A statistic without its number of students, its dates and its method, because such figures are unverifiable by design. A claim of approval, accreditation or licensing by ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson without a permit number to show. And any offer to produce a finished investigation, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay, which sells a student an academic honesty investigation rather than a grade.

faqs.question: What does Chemistry SL tuition cost in Abu Dhabi, and what moves the figure?
faqs.answer: Providers that publish rates put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more in Bestimate's 2026 Dubai survey; Unitors publishes IB from AED 200 and TutorChase publishes AED 270. In-home visits in that survey are AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors are quoted to AED 500, because travel sits inside the rate. Level moves the figure, format moves it more, and the final term before the session moves both price and availability. IB Gram confirms its own fee in writing after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Can my daughter still reach a 6 in Chemistry SL if we start in DP2?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what a marked script shows, which is why the honest answer follows a diagnosis rather than a sales conversation. A DP2 student whose content is broadly in place and who is losing marks to arithmetic, units and command terms has real room, because those clusters move in weeks. A DP2 student who has not learned two of the six themes and has no investigation has a different problem, and should be told the number of hours it would genuinely take rather than given an encouraging number and a weekly slot.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor about permits before booking in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and whether they currently teach at the school your child attends. The permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, so there is no cost reason for a tutor not to hold one; anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. On the second question, press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates Abu Dhabi school staff may not take paid private students from their own school.

faqs.question: Does the data booklet change how a Standard Level student should revise?
faqs.answer: Substantially. It is supplied in the examinations along with the periodic table, and it carries constants, relationships and reference data. That means time spent memorising what is printed in it is wasted, and time spent practising with it open is not. The examinable skill becomes selecting the right relationship for a situation and justifying the choice under time pressure. Students who treat it as a safety net rather than a working tool lose marks because they have never had to find anything in it quickly or decide between two similar-looking entries.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-chemistry-sl-tutor.closingHeading: Two marked scripts, and a diagnosis you can read
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-chemistry-sl-tutor.closingBody: If your child sits Chemistry at Standard Level in an Abu Dhabi school, send the evidence rather than the worry: the last two marked assessments, the school's next three internal deadlines, and two workable weekly slots on Gulf Standard Time. A free 45-minute trial lesson with the proposed tutor follows, with no card details taken. Four weeks later there should be a document — a baseline log, re-marked scripts with every lost mark attributed, a ranked topic list and an honest read on the investigation — whether or not anything further is booked.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-computer-science-home-tu.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here teach Diploma Computer Science at Standard and Higher Level, and each profile names the option topic and the programming language they work in. That matters more than it sounds: a tutor strong in one option topic can be no use at all for a cohort sitting another, and the option is what the second written paper is built on.

intro.heading: The problem is almost never the programming
paragraphs: A pattern repeats across Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts. A student who builds things at home, who has shipped a working app, who can debug faster than the teacher, comes back with a 4 in Computer Science and nobody can explain it. The family assumes the content is too hard and buys content revision. The content was never the problem. The problem is that this subject is examined on paper in a notation the student does not use, on a design process they skip because they do not need it, and through documentation that is marked more heavily than the code it describes.

Start with the structure. The first written paper tests computational thinking and program design: abstraction, algorithm construction, and the ability to express and trace an algorithm in the IB's own approved pseudocode notation rather than in Python or Java. The second written paper is drawn from one option topic, chosen by the school from a small set, which is why a tutor who has taught one option fluently may be worth nothing to a cohort sitting another. At Higher Level there is a third paper built on a case study the IB releases ahead of the examination, requiring independent research into technology the course has not taught. The internal assessment is a solution developed for a real client, submitted as a documentation folder with a short functionality video attached.

Each of those components has a characteristic failure, and the failures are diagnosable from one marked script and one look at a draft folder. Pseudocode written in Python syntax. Trace tables abandoned halfway because the student can see the answer. A design section that describes the finished product rather than the decisions behind it. A record of tasks assembled the week before submission and therefore fictional. A functionality video that shows the application working but never demonstrates the success criteria it was supposed to meet. None of these are intelligence problems and none of them are fixed by more content.

Abu Dhabi adds one practical factor. Diploma Computer Science cohorts in this emirate are small, often a handful of students, frequently taught by one teacher who also carries another subject. That teacher may be excellent and still have no second opinion available on a borderline internal assessment, no colleague who has marked the option topic before, and no time to run the paper technique drills the subject needs. That gap is what external support is actually for here, and it is why the match has to be on the option topic rather than on the subject name. Lessons run online, one to one, over live video; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, because home visits are a service we provide only in India.

Paper 2: one option topic, chosen by the school from a small set
Paper 3 at Higher Level: a pre-released case study needing independent research
Internal assessment: a solution for a real client, submitted as a documentation folder
The functionality video has a seven-minute ceiling and must demonstrate the success criteria
Confirm which guide and which option your child's cohort is sitting before booking anything

These are the stages that matter for a student in this emirate, and what support looks like at each.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years, three assessed papers at Higher Level and two at Standard Level, plus the internally assessed solution. The written papers are sat on paper, in pseudocode, under time pressure, which is a different task from building software. Higher Level adds abstract data structures, resource management and control, and the case-study paper.

Ask the Diploma coordinator which option the cohort sits and which guide version applies, then brief any tutor on both before the first session rather than discovering the mismatch in week three.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Design in the Middle Years Programme is where the documentation habit either forms or does not. Students are assessed on inquiry, development of ideas, creating the solution and evaluation, which is recognisably the same shape as the Diploma internal assessment. A student who learned to write up decisions here has a large head start.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run Design rather than a computing course in the middle years, so a student can arrive in DP1 having written a lot of documentation and very little code, or the reverse. Establishing which of the two gaps you are dealing with is the first useful hour of support.

programmes.name: The Diploma core: IA, EE and TOK
programmes.description: The Computer Science solution, an Extended Essay where the student chooses the subject, and Theory of Knowledge all compete for the same evenings. The solution is the one with a client attached, which means its timeline depends on somebody outside the school being available, and that is what slips.

A solution that depends on a client interview needs that interview booked around those breaks rather than during them, and a tutor can be useful simply by making a student plan the dependency early.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-computer-science-home-tu.subjectsIntro: Computer Science is usually chosen alongside a mathematics route and at least one science, and the combination decides what university doors stay open. These are the pairings seen most often in Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Computational thinking and program design on the first paper, one option topic on the second, a pre-released case study at Higher Level, and a client solution submitted as documentation with a functionality video. Marks are lost in notation, tracing and design justification far more often than in logic.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebra, proof and calculus route. Many competitive overseas computing courses specify mathematics at Higher Level, and this is usually the version they mean. Check the individual course page rather than the institution's homepage, because requirements vary within the same university.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-permitted assessment. Accepted for many data, analytics and information-systems degrees and rejected by some pure computer science courses. The exploration is marked against the same criteria set as the other route, so the workload difference is smaller than students assume.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields, waves and an internally assessed investigation with uncertainty analysis. Pairs with Computer Science for engineering routes, and the two share a specific weakness: students who can produce a correct result but cannot justify the method they chose to get there.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Design cycle thinking, materials and a design project assessed against criteria that reward justified decisions over finished appearance. The closest subject in the Diploma to the Computer Science internal assessment in the way it is marked, and a useful comparison when teaching documentation.

subjects.name: Digital Society
subjects.description: Concepts, content and contexts around digital systems, with an inquiry project rather than a built solution. Chosen by students who want the subject matter without the programming examination. Confirm with the school whether it is offered, since availability in the emirate varies by campus.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure, reactivity and an internally assessed investigation. Required or strongly preferred for several UAE engineering and health-science routes, and often the third science in a Computer Science student's block. Marks concentrate in data handling and in the evaluation section.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Five content units, two written papers and a research project worth a quarter of the grade. Paired with Computer Science by students aiming at information systems or product roles. The two subjects fail the same way: a tool applied without a specific context attached.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Micro, macro and global economy with a portfolio of commentaries on published articles. Diagram accuracy earns marks but explanation earns more, and students who are strong at the quantitative side still lose the evaluation marks at the end of each long answer.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis, an individual oral and, at Higher Level, an essay on studied works. Relevant to Computer Science students in one concrete way: the documentation folder is a piece of technical writing, and students who cannot structure a paragraph cannot structure a design justification.

sections.heading: What this search means, and the two facts to establish before booking anything
paragraphs: A parent searching for an IB DP computer science home tutor in Abu Dhabi is asking for one-to-one help with a Diploma subject. Two facts decide whether any given tutor can provide it, and both are obtainable in a single email to the school's Diploma coordinator. The first is which guide version the cohort is being assessed against, because the subject has been revised and material written for one version misleads a student sitting the other. The second is which option topic the school has chosen for the second written paper.

The option matters more than anything else on a tutor's profile. A tutor who has taught databases through several cohorts and a tutor who has taught object-oriented programming are not interchangeable for a student sitting one of them, and the difference is invisible in a subject listing that says only Computer Science. Ask the question before the trial lesson. A tutor who cannot name the option topics is not the tutor for this subject.

The third thing worth establishing, though it is not strictly a fact about the course, is what language the class codes in. The written papers are language-agnostic and are answered in pseudocode, but the internal assessment is built in something real, and a student working in Java with a tutor who thinks in Python will spend session time on translation rather than on marks. None of this is complicated. It is simply the information that makes the difference between a useful first session and a wasted one.

Once those are settled, the diagnosis is quick. Send one marked written paper and the current state of the internal assessment folder. The six failure patterns set out in the next section are visible in those two documents within about twenty minutes, and the first block of sessions should be aimed at whichever two of them are costing the most marks rather than at the syllabus in order.

sections.heading: Six ways a capable programmer loses Computer Science marks
paragraphs: These are the patterns that show up most often in Abu Dhabi cohorts, and they are worth naming precisely because each has a different fix with a different cost. A student losing marks to notation needs drilling, which is cheap and fast. A student losing marks to a weak client relationship in the internal assessment needs a decision made early, which is cheap if caught in DP1 and very expensive if caught in DP2.

The most common by a distance is pseudocode written in the syntax of a real language. The IB publishes an approved notation for developing pseudocode, with its own conventions for loops, selection, output and collection handling. An answer written in fluent Python is answering a question nobody asked, and an examiner cannot award marks for correctness in a notation the mark scheme does not use. Students resist this because it feels like being marked down for knowing more. They are being marked on a specified skill.

The second is the abandoned trace table. Asked to trace an algorithm, a strong programmer reads it, sees the output, writes the answer and skips the table. The marks are in the table. Each row is a mark or part of one, and the final answer alone attracts a fraction of the available credit. This is the single highest marks-per-hour fix in the subject, because the skill is mechanical and improves within two sessions.

The remaining four are design justification replaced by description, a record of tasks reconstructed near the deadline rather than kept as the work happened, a functionality video that demonstrates features instead of the stated success criteria, and extended written answers that explain how something works without ever evaluating it against an alternative. The table below pairs each symptom with what the examiner actually saw and what a session does about it.

sections.heading: The IB's pseudocode is a dialect, and the dialect is examinable
paragraphs: This deserves its own section because it is the clearest example of a mark loss that has nothing to do with ability. The IB publishes an approved notation for developing pseudocode, and the written papers both set and expect answers in it. The notation has its own conventions for assignment, for selection and iteration, for output, and for the collection and array handling that the questions lean on heavily. It is not a programming language, it has no compiler, and nothing a student has built outside school will have used it.

The practical consequence is that a student can write an algorithm that is logically perfect and still be unable to claim the marks. Mark schemes in this subject are notation-aware. An examiner reading an answer in Python is not permitted to invent credit for an intention correctly expressed in the wrong dialect, and a question asking the student to construct an algorithm using the approved notation has made the notation part of the assessment objective.

The fix is drilling, and it is dull in the way that effective drilling usually is. The student writes the same half-dozen algorithm shapes in the notation until it is faster than thinking about it: linear search, counting with a condition, finding a maximum, reversing a sequence, iterating a collection with the specified methods, and nested iteration over a two-dimensional array. Two or three sessions of this is normally enough, and it is the most reliable mark movement available in the subject.

Two warnings. First, material circulating online is not consistent about this notation, and some of it predates the current conventions, so work from the school's own copy of the guidance rather than from a search result. Second, do not reproduce or distribute official syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes; reference them and ask the school for its licensed copies. We cite the official sources and link out rather than hosting anything.

sections.heading: Trace tables and dry runs: the best marks-per-hour in the subject
paragraphs: A trace table asks a student to record the state of every relevant variable at every step of an algorithm's execution. It is tedious, it is mechanical, and it is where a disproportionate share of the first paper's marks live. The reason it is such reliable mark territory is that it cannot be bluffed and it does not depend on recall: a student who follows the procedure correctly gets the marks, every time, regardless of how well they slept.

Strong programmers are the worst at it. A student who can read an algorithm and predict its output has no felt need for the table, so they write the output, leave the grid half-empty, and lose most of the available credit to a shortcut that would be entirely sensible anywhere except in an examination. Teaching this is a matter of making the procedure non-negotiable rather than explaining anything.

The drill that works is narrow. Take an algorithm with a loop and a condition, trace it in full, then trace it again with an input that exercises the edge case, then do a third with an off-by-one error deliberately introduced so the student sees the table catch what reading could not. By the third repetition most students stop resisting the table, because it has just found something they had missed.

The same habit pays twice. Dry-running an algorithm on paper is also how a student debugs the internal assessment when the code misbehaves in a way the debugger does not explain, and the record of that reasoning is legitimate material for the development section of the folder. The skill earns marks in two components, which makes it the cheapest hours a family will buy in this subject.

sections.heading: The internal assessment is a documentation exercise with code attached
paragraphs: Students routinely misread the weight of this component. The code matters, but what is submitted and marked is a documentation folder: the planning that establishes a client and a set of success criteria, a design section that justifies decisions, a record of tasks kept across the development, the product itself, a functionality video, and an evaluation measured against the criteria that were agreed at the beginning. A technically impressive product with a thin folder scores below a modest product with a rigorous one.

The client is the dependency that causes the most damage when it is handled casually. The brief requires a real client or adviser with a genuine need, interviewed, with the resulting requirements recorded. A student who nominates a family member and invents the requirements has built a project with no evidence trail, and every criterion downstream weakens: success criteria that were never negotiated, design decisions that cannot be justified against a need, and an evaluation with nothing to evaluate against.

The record of tasks is the second common failure, and it is entirely avoidable. It is supposed to be a contemporaneous log of what was planned and done. Written in the fortnight before submission, it reads as what it is, and it stops being evidence of a process. Five minutes at the end of each working session for the whole development period produces a document that does its job, and a tutor who does nothing but enforce that habit has earned their fee.

The functionality video is the last trap. It has a ceiling of seven minutes, and its purpose is to demonstrate that the success criteria have been met, not to tour the application's features. A video planned from the criteria list, in criteria order, with the student narrating which criterion each sequence satisfies, is a different and better document from one recorded by clicking around the finished product.

sections.heading: Higher Level: abstract data structures, recursion and the case study
paragraphs: Higher Level adds content that is conceptually harder than anything at Standard Level and a third paper that behaves unlike the other two. The additional content covers abstract data structures, including linked lists and trees, together with resource management and control. Students who have only ever used the collections their language provides meet, for the first time, the question of how such a structure is built and what it costs to traverse.

Recursion is where most Higher Level students stall, and the stall has a specific shape. They understand the definition, they can read a recursive function and say what it does, and they cannot write one for a problem they have not seen. The gap is that recursion has to be approached from the base case outward rather than from the top down, and that is a habit rather than an insight. Tracing recursive calls on paper, with the call stack drawn explicitly, converts it from mystery to procedure in a handful of sessions.

The third paper is built on a case study the IB releases to schools ahead of the examination. It covers technology the taught course does not, and it expects the student to have researched it independently, understood the vocabulary, and formed views about trade-offs they can defend in extended writing. Students who treat it as revision reading score what reading earns. Students who build a glossary, follow the primary sources behind the material and practise extended answers on it score considerably better.

Dates are the one thing to be careful about here. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no exam-session or release date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly. Treat the May session as the one Abu Dhabi schools sit, and get every specific date from the school's Diploma coordinator or from the IB's own assessment pages rather than from any tutoring site, including this one.

sections.heading: Diploma Computer Science in Abu Dhabi schools, and the singly-staffed class
paragraphs: ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in this emirate and publishes its own inspection ratings. That is useful context for choosing a school and almost no help at all for choosing a Computer Science class, because inspection ratings are awarded to schools rather than to departments, and a strong school can have a small, newly established computing cohort.

What a parent should actually ask the school is narrower. How many students are in the Diploma Computer Science group this year. Whether both Standard and Higher Level are taught in the same room. Which option topic the cohort sits, and for how many cohorts the department has taught it. Whether the teacher has marked internal assessments in this subject before, or whether this will be their first submission. And whether anonymised past student folders at different mark bands can be shown.

Those answers predict where external support is needed better than any rating does. A group of four students with both levels in one room and a teacher new to the subject is not a failing arrangement, but it is one where a second opinion on a borderline folder has real value, and where the paper technique drills will not happen in class because there is no time for them.

The regulator picture across the country is worth knowing in outline, because families move between emirates. Dubai's private schools sit with KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain with ADEK, Sharjah with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from any of them and claims none; they are named here to explain who governs what.

sections.heading: Where the subject leads, and the mathematics question behind it
paragraphs: Families choose Computer Science expecting it to be required for a computing degree. Usually it is not. Mathematics is the subject that gates admission to most computer science courses, frequently at Higher Level, and Computer Science itself is treated as useful rather than essential. That makes the mathematics route choice the consequential decision in a Diploma block, and it is often made in DP1 on the basis of which course looks easier.

The pattern across admissions pages is that the algebra-and-proof route is specified more often by competitive overseas computer science courses, while the statistics-and-modelling route is widely accepted for data, analytics and information-systems degrees. There are exceptions in both directions, within the same institution. The only reliable method is to read the individual course page for each destination on the list, and to do it before the level choices are locked rather than after.

For students staying in the region, the relevant institutions include Khalifa University, New York University Abu Dhabi, Zayed University, United Arab Emirates University and Sorbonne University Abu Dhabi, each with its own published entry profile. Certificate equivalency through the Ministry of Education is a separate process from university admission, and the published British-track requirements are clear: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. No equivalent IB points figure appears in the source we verified, so check moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority directly rather than accepting a number from a tutoring page.

One more honest note. Tutoring is not required for equivalency, for university admission or for progression through the Diploma. Any page that suggests otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process. What tutoring can do is move marks on specific components, and the table below is about checking requirements rather than about buying hours.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the assessed work is code
paragraphs: This subject has honesty questions the other sciences do not, because reusing existing code is normal professional practice and because generative tools will produce a working solution on request. The IB's position is that assessed work must be the student's own, with sources acknowledged. The practical translation for a Computer Science folder is attribution: a library used is named, a tutorial followed is cited, a code fragment adapted from elsewhere is marked as adapted and its origin given.

A tutor's role has a hard boundary here, and the boundary is drawn around keystrokes. A tutor may explain a concept, read the student's code and ask why a construction was chosen, point at the line where behaviour diverges from intent, teach a debugging method, explain what a criterion is asking for, and challenge a design decision until the student can defend it or change it. That is teaching and it is what the specialist rate buys.

A tutor may not supply code for the solution, restructure a section into its final form, perform the analysis the student is assessed on, or hand over text for the folder. Nobody should produce assessed work on a student's behalf, and no provider offering that is offering anything other than a malpractice risk carried entirely by the student. We say this on every page in this set because the market around it is real: one site in the competitor research sells completed internal assessments outright.

On generative tools specifically, the safe position is to assume the school's policy is the binding one and to ask for it in writing. Where such tools are permitted at all, their use has to be declared and the output has to be understood well enough to defend in a conversation with the teacher. A student who cannot explain their own submitted code line by line has a problem that no amount of tutoring will solve after the fact.

sections.heading: What Computer Science support costs in this emirate, and how the lessons run
paragraphs: Market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online in the UAE run roughly AED 150-300 an hour, and IB specialists are quoted from about AED 200 to AED 450 and upwards. In-home visits sit higher, roughly AED 180-500, because travel is inside the hour. Those bands come from published provider pages and from Bestimate's Dubai rate table, read in October 2026; they describe the market and are not an IB Gram price list. Computer Science sits at the upper end of whatever band a provider operates in, because the teaching population is small and the option topics fragment it further.

Delivery for this subject is a genuine argument rather than a compromise. The work happens on a screen. A shared screen with the student driving, the tutor watching the code appear and asking questions about it, is closer to how the subject is actually practised than two people looking at a laptop across a kitchen table. Nothing is lost in translation to video because there was no physical artefact to lose.

To state the delivery position plainly: every UAE lesson is one-to-one and online, over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in this emirate. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and no sentence here should be read as offering them in the UAE. The gain, rather than the concession, is that a family in Al Reef chooses from the same pool of option-topic specialists as a family on Saadiyat.

On availability, the honest version. In a given week there may be no UAE-based Diploma Computer Science specialist free for the option your cohort sits at the hour you need. Where that happens we say so and offer the slot with a tutor based elsewhere teaching the same specification at the same rate, or give a date rather than a maybe. Where a component genuinely cannot be covered at the level needed, saying the slot is unavailable is a better answer than substituting a generalist at specialist money.

faqs.question: Why does my child write working code and still score a 4 in Computer Science?
faqs.answer: Because the written papers assess things building software does not. The first paper wants algorithms expressed in the IB's approved pseudocode notation, trace tables completed in full, and extended answers that evaluate rather than explain. A student who codes fluently in Python writes pseudocode in Python syntax, abandons trace tables because they can see the answer, and describes how something works without weighing it against an alternative. All three are specified skills with marks attached. None of them is intelligence, and all three improve inside a handful of focused sessions once they are named.

faqs.question: What is the IB's approved pseudocode notation, and is it really examinable?
faqs.answer: It is a specified notation with its own conventions for assignment, selection, iteration, output and collection handling, published by the IB and used by the mark schemes. Yes, it is examinable: a question that asks for an algorithm in the approved notation has made the notation part of what is being assessed, and an examiner cannot award credit for a correct idea expressed in Python or Java syntax. The fix is drilling roughly six algorithm shapes until the notation is faster than thinking about it. Work from your school's own copy of the guidance rather than from search results, which are inconsistent.

faqs.question: How do trace tables actually earn marks in the written papers?
faqs.answer: Row by row. A trace table records the state of each relevant variable at each step of execution, and the credit is distributed across those rows rather than concentrated in the final answer. A student who reads the algorithm, writes the correct output and leaves the grid half-empty claims a fraction of what was available. This is the highest marks-per-hour fix in the subject because the skill is mechanical: trace an algorithm in full, trace it again on an edge-case input, then trace one with a deliberate off-by-one error so the table catches what reading could not.

faqs.question: Which Computer Science option topic is my child's Abu Dhabi school teaching?
faqs.answer: Ask the Diploma coordinator, because it is a school-level decision and it determines tutor fit completely. The second written paper is drawn from a single option chosen by the school from a small set, and a tutor who has taught one option through several cohorts may be no use for another. This is the question to put before the trial lesson rather than after it. A tutor who cannot name the available option topics is not a specialist in this subject, whatever the profile says.

faqs.question: What has to be in the Computer Science internal assessment folder?
faqs.answer: Planning that identifies a real client or adviser and records negotiated success criteria, a design section that justifies decisions rather than describing the product, a record of tasks kept while the work happened, the product itself, a functionality video inside the seven-minute ceiling that evidences each success criterion, and an evaluation measured against the criteria agreed at the start. The code matters, but the folder is what is marked. A technically impressive product with a thin folder scores below a modest product documented rigorously. Confirm the current requirements with your school's coordinator.

faqs.question: How should the internal assessment client be chosen, and can it be a relative?
faqs.answer: The brief needs a real client or adviser with a genuine need, interviewed, with the resulting requirements recorded. A relative can in principle serve if the need is real and the interview genuinely happens, but the common failure is a nominated family member whose requirements were invented afterwards to fit a product the student already wanted to build. That weakens every criterion downstream: success criteria nobody negotiated, design decisions with no need to justify them against, and an evaluation with no benchmark. Settle the client early in DP1, not late in DP2.

faqs.question: What are the rules on using libraries and AI coding tools in this subject?
faqs.answer: Assessed work must be the student's own with sources acknowledged, so a library used is named, a tutorial followed is cited, and an adapted fragment is marked as adapted with its origin given. For generative tools, treat your school's written policy as binding and ask for it rather than assuming. Where such tools are permitted at all, the use has to be declared and the output understood well enough to defend line by line in conversation with the teacher. A student who cannot explain their own submitted code has a problem that no later tutoring can repair.

faqs.question: What extra content do Higher Level Computer Science students sit?
faqs.answer: Higher Level adds abstract data structures, including linked lists and trees, together with resource management and control, and it adds a third written paper built on a case study the IB releases to schools ahead of the examination. The conceptual step up is real: students who have only ever used the collections their language provides now have to build and traverse such structures and reason about the cost of doing so. Recursion is where most stall, and it yields to tracing recursive calls on paper with the call stack drawn explicitly.

faqs.question: How should a student prepare for the Higher Level case study paper?
faqs.answer: Not by reading it. The case study covers technology the taught course does not, and the paper expects independent research, command of the vocabulary and defensible views on trade-offs. The approach that works is a glossary built from the material, reading of the primary sources the material points at, and timed extended answers practised on it. Treat it as a research project with an examination at the end. Get the release timing from your school's Diploma coordinator, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and no date in this project is confirmed from the IB directly.

faqs.question: Does my child need Mathematics Analysis and Approaches for a computing degree?
faqs.answer: Often, but it depends on the course rather than the university. Competitive overseas computer science courses specify mathematics at Higher Level more often than not, and the algebra-and-proof route is the version they usually mean. Data, analytics and information-systems degrees widely accept the statistics-and-modelling route. Computer Science itself is frequently useful rather than required. Read the individual course page for every destination on your child's list before the level choices lock, because requirements vary within the same institution and a homepage will not tell you.

faqs.question: Which Abu Dhabi schools run Diploma Computer Science, and how big are the classes?
faqs.answer: Several schools across the island, Saadiyat and the Khalifa City corridor offer it, and the groups are frequently in single figures with Standard and Higher Level taught in the same room. ADEK licenses and inspects private schools in this emirate and publishes inspection ratings, but those are awarded to schools rather than departments, so a strong school can have a newly established computing cohort. Ask the school directly how many students are in the group, which option is sat, how many cohorts have sat it, and whether anonymised past folders can be shown.

faqs.question: Is Computer Science a sensible choice for a student who has never programmed?
faqs.answer: It can be, but go in with the real picture. The course teaches programming from the beginning, and the written papers are answered in pseudocode rather than in a language, which levels the field more than families expect. The harder adjustment is the design process and the documentation, which reward recorded reasoning over working output. A student with no prior coding who writes carefully often outperforms a self-taught programmer who skips the design section. Ask the school what prior experience the class assumes, since that varies by department rather than by syllabus.

faqs.question: Can Computer Science lessons really work online when the work is practical?
faqs.answer: This is the subject where online delivery is the stronger option rather than the compromise. The work lives on a screen already. With the student sharing their screen and driving, the tutor watches code appear, asks why a construction was chosen at the moment it is written, and points at the line where behaviour diverges from intent. Nothing physical is lost in translation. The gain is the tutor pool: a family in Al Reef or Al Shamkha chooses from every available specialist in their option topic rather than from whoever is willing to drive out there.

faqs.question: What does Diploma Computer Science support cost in the Abu Dhabi market?
faqs.answer: Market rates for a qualified online subject tutor across the UAE run roughly AED 150-300 an hour, with IB specialists quoted from about AED 200 to AED 450 and upwards, and in-home visits at roughly AED 180-500 because travel sits inside the hour. Those figures come from published provider pages and Bestimate's Dubai rate table, read in October 2026, and they describe the market rather than our prices. Computer Science sits at the upper end of any provider's band because the teaching population is small and the option topics divide it further.

faqs.question: How long does it take to match a Computer Science tutor in this emirate?
faqs.answer: For Standard Level content and paper technique, usually a few days. For a specific option topic at Higher Level, it can take a week in term time, and for internal assessment feedback near an internal deadline it can take longer because demand across the emirate peaks in the same fortnight. Where nobody is free at your hour we say so and offer a tutor based elsewhere teaching the same specification at the same rate, or give you a date. No researched competitor in this cluster discloses a coverage limit at all.

intro.heading: Why Computer Science is the most scarcity-priced subject in this emirate
paragraphs: Every other Diploma subject in Abu Dhabi has a tutor market. Computer Science has a short list. The reason is structural rather than academic: comparatively few schools in the emirate run the Diploma course at all, so comparatively few teachers have taught it, and the people who can code professionally mostly have better-paid work than tutoring sixteen-year-olds on a Tuesday evening. Scarcity, not difficulty, is what sits behind the rate.

The market bands are the same ones that apply across IB tutoring: roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour for a specialist, per Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, Unitors listing IB tuition from AED 200, and BartyED publishing AED 650 for an examiner tier. Computer Science reliably sits in the upper half of the specialist band and sometimes above it, and a family comparing it with a Mathematics quote is comparing two very different supply situations rather than two levels of greed.

The second thing that moves the number is which half of the subject is broken, because this course has two halves that barely resemble each other. One half is a written theory examination covering system fundamentals, computer organisation, networks and computational thinking, with abstract data structures and resource management added at Higher Level. The other half is a built artefact: a computational solution designed, implemented, documented and defended by the student. A tutor who is strong at one is frequently weak at the other, and a family paying for the wrong strength is spending at the top of the market for something that does not help.

The third is the credential problem, and it is specific to this subject. In Biology a tutor who knows biology is probably useful. In Computer Science a tutor who knows programming may be of very little use, because the written papers examine things working developers rarely think about: tracing pseudocode by hand, describing a specific sorting behaviour in examiner language, explaining why a particular data structure suits a particular access pattern. Capable engineers lose marks on these papers too. What you are buying is examination literacy, and it is worth asking directly how recently a tutor taught this course rather than how long they have been coding.

The fourth input is local and legal. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of Abu Dhabi private schools, and Gulf News reported that its professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. The MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years and carries a code of conduct saying the same. In a subject where the resident specialist pool is already short, those rules shorten it further. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service we run only in India, and every Abu Dhabi lesson runs online over live video.
